A pharmacy grad, Patel joined the firm in 1976 and took charge in 1995 after a formal separation between the two founding families.
The $2.75 billion (revenue) pharmaceutical company is headquartered in Ahmedabad.
His son Sharvil Patel has been the company's managing director since 2017.
In August 2025, consumer arm Zydus Wellness acquired U.K.-based vitamins and minerals firm Comfort Click for about $325 million.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Gujarat University; Master of Science, Gujarat University

did_you_know_facts: Patel chairs the board of governors of the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad and is chairman of the board of governors of the Institute of Management Udaipur.
Fellow billionaire Bhadresh Shah and Upasana Konidela, the granddaughter of healthcare billionaire Prathap Reddy, have board seats at Zydus Lifesciences.
quote: What we do tomorrow is more important than what we did yesterday.

name: Guillaume Pousaz
about: Guillaume Pousaz founded Checkout.com in 2012 to solve the problem of online payment processing for shops and shoppers around the world.
In January 2022, Checkout.com raised $1 billion from private investors, valuing the company at $40 billion.

In December 2022, Checkout.com marked down its internal valuation to $11 billion, as fintech valuations tumbled during the year; a year later it was lowered to $9.35 billion. In 2025, it rose to $12 billion, according to the company.
Pousaz, who is CEO of Checkout.com, owns an estimated nearly two-thirds of the London-based company.
The Swiss citizen dropped out of college to go surfing in California before working in fintech and payments.
He is known for his obsession with endurance athletics and lives in London with his family.

name: Marc Benioff
about: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff owns about 2% of the cloud computing software firm he cofounded in 1999.
Before Salesforce, he spent 13 years at database software giant Oracle as a protege of Larry Ellison.
Salesforce was a pioneer in hosting its software online, rather than installing it in clients' computer systems.
He's an angel investor in dozens of tech startups and a prolific philanthropist.
Benioff and his wife Lynne have pledged $350 million to University of California, San Francisco, for its children's hospitals and research.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Southern California

did_you_know_facts: At 17, Benioff developed and sold Atari video games, and earned enough to pay his way to USC.
Benioff spoke out against laws permitting discrimination against LGBT people in North Carolina, Georgia and Indiana.
In May 2018, Benioff celebrated construction of the 1,070-foot tall Salesforce Tower in San Francisco.
quote: When I get something in my head, it's hard for me to just let it go.

name: Judy Faulkner
about: Judy Faulkner founded medical-record software provider Epic Systems in a Wisconsin basement in 1979.
Faulkner, a computer programmer, is CEO of the $5.7 billion (2024 sales) company, of which she owns an estimated 43%.
Epic supports the medical records of over 250 million patients and is used by top medical centers such as Johns Hopkins and Mayo Clinic.
The company has never raised venture capital or made an acquisition, and develops all its software in-house.
Faulkner signed the Giving Pledge in 2015 and has agreed to eventually give 99% of her assets to a private charitable foundation.
In 2024 she told Forbes that she was regularly selling around $100 million of her Epic shares a year back to the company, with proceeds going to her charitable foundation, Roots & Wings.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Dickinson College; Master of Science, University of Wisconsin

did_you_know_facts: Faulkner started Epic, originally named Human Services Computing, with $70,000; she wrote the original code on a Data General Eclipse 16-bit minicomputer.
Perks at her Epic's headquarters in Verona, Wisconsin include a tree house and an Indiana Jones-inspired cave walkway.
quote: "I always liked making things out of clay. And the computer was clay of the mind. Instead of physical, it was mental."

name: Vyacheslav Kim
about: Vyacheslav Kim is chairman of Kaspi Bank, Kazakhstan's largest payments and fintech company.
Kaspi's 2020 IPO was celebrated as London's largest international tech public offering that year .
Kaspi generated revenues of $2.5 billion in 2024.
Kim's partner at Kaspi is Georgian billionaire Mikhail Lomtadze, a former private equity investor at Russian-focused fund Baring Vostock.

name: Tony Tamer
about: Tony Tamer is the cofounder and co-executive chairman of H.I.G. Capital, a private equity firm with $70 billion under management.
Tamer launched H.I.G. Capital in 1993 with Sami Mnaymneh; the duo have been masters of middle-market private equity deals.
In addition to operations in Europe and Latin America, H.I.G. also runs a large credit business.
Prior to founding H.I.G. Capital, Tamer was a partner at Bain & Company.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School; Master of Science in Engineering, Stanford University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Rutgers University

did_you_know_facts: Tamer fundraised for his former Bain colleague Mitt Romney's 2012 presidential campaign as a co-chair of his Florida finance team.

name: Sami Mnaymneh
about: Sami Mnaymneh is cofounder, CEO and co-executive chairman of H.I.G. Capital, a private equity firm with $70 billion under management.
Mnaymneh launched H.I.G. in 1993 with Tony Tamer and the duo became known for being the masters of middle-market deals.
In addition to operations in Europe and Latin America, H.I.G. has a large credit business.
Prior to starting H.I.G., Mnaymneh was a managing director at Blackstone and a vice president of mergers and acquisitions at Morgan Stanley.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School; Doctor of Jurisprudence, Harvard University; Bachelor of Arts/Economics, Columbia University

did_you_know_facts: Mnaymneh was the valedictorian of his graduating class at Columbia University in 1981.

name: Maria Fernanda Amorim & family
about: Maria Fernanda Amorim is the widow of Americo Amorim, who died in 2017. She and her three daughters inherited his fortune.
Americo Amorim spent six decades in his family's cork business, Corticeira Amorim, and invested in an energy company and banks in several countries.
His grandfather started Corticeira Amorim in 1870; the company has dominated the cork industry ever since.
Amorim's biggest asset is an approximate 20% stake in Portuguese oil and gas company Galp Energia, which is chaired by her eldest daughter Paula.
did_you_know_facts: She has founded 2 museums: one is dedicated to Porto wines, and the other, located in Grij?, is focused on arts and crafts.

name: Scott Farquhar
about: Scott Farquhar is cofounder of collaboration software company Atlassian, based in Sydney, Australia.
He and CEO Mike Cannon-Brookes started the company soon after graduating from college, funding it with credit cards.
Atlassian's marquee customer list includes retailing giant Costco and American airline Delta.
Atlassian is a cofounder of Pledge 1%, which urges companies to donate at least 1% of equity, employee time or products to charity.
He stepped down as co-CEO in September 2024 to spend more time with his family and to pursue philanthropic activities. He continues as a board member and an advisor.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of New South Wales

did_you_know_facts: In November 2025, he completed the Ironman triathlon which included a 26.2 mile marathon; a 2.4 mile swim and a 112-mile bicycle ride.
quote: We were always cash flow positive from the very early days, but that's largely because we were still eating ramen noodles.

name: Tench Coxe
about: Tench Coxe has served on the board of chip designer Nvidia since 1993, accumulating enough stock (as compensation) to become a billionaire.
Coxe is the third largest individual shareholder of Nvidia, behind founder and CEO Jensen Huang and board member Mark Stevens.
Coxe spent more than three decades at venture capital firm Sutter Hill Ventures, serving as a managing director from 1989 to 2020.
As of late 2021 owned about 1% of software firm Snowflake, in which Sutter Hill was the earliest investor.
He also serves on the board of money management firm Artisan Partners Asset Management.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Dartmouth College; Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School

name: Stanley Druckenmiller
about: Stanley Druckenmiller made it big as a hedge fund manager for 30 years. He now manages his money through a family office.
Until 2000, he worked for George Soros. The duo famously bet against the British pound in 1992 and made massive profits.
He shut down his $12 billion hedge fund Duquesne Capital Management in 2010, returning funds to clients.
did_you_know_facts: At Bowdoin College, Druckenmiller reportedly ran a hot dog stand for extra cash and graduated magna cum laude.
A major donor to his alma mater, he has given more than $40 million to higher education institutions like Bowdoin, Brown and Stanford since 2014.
quote: I love being around kids. I couldn't figure out why all these 70-year-olds wanted to hang out with me when I was 27. Now I understand, and I'm trying to steal their energy.

name: Rinat Akhmetov
about: Ukraine's richest person, Rinat Akhmetov has vowed to stay in Ukraine and support his country in its fight against Russia.

Russian forces destroyed plants owned by his mining and steel firm Metinvest and ravaged substations of his power generation firm DTEK. More than 1,400 of his employees have died as a result of the war.

He says his companies, which still operate, have donated $368 million in goods and have invested around $4 billion in restoring infrastructure destroyed by Russia, building new facilities and modernizing production.
The son of a coal miner, Akhmetov got his start buying up mining assets during the 1990s privatization era.
Akhmetov is believed to own a 476-foot yacht, named Luminance, that cost him $500 million. He also owns a French villa and a London apartment.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Economics, Donetsk National University

did_you_know_facts: Akhmetov grew up in Russian-backed Donetsk but has not been back since Russia's invasion in 2014.
quote: I am in Ukraine and I am not going to leave the country. I share the same feelings with all Ukrainians: I am sincerely waiting for the victory of Ukraine in this war.

name: Zong Fuli
about: Zong Fuli, also known as Kelly, is the daughter of beverage giant Hangzhou Wahaha Group's late founder Zong Qinghou.
Her wealth is based on a company stake inherited in 2024, after the elder Zong passed away earlier in the year.
Once Wahaha's chairman and CEO, Kelly stepped down in September 2025.
She already stepped down once in 2024, before being reinstated months later after resolving an unspecified shareholder dispute at the time.
In 2025, she was sued in Hong Kong over $2.1 billion worth of trust assets by three plaintiffs who claim to be her half siblings.
did_you_know_facts: Started in Hangzhou in 1987, the company's name Wahaha mimics the sound of a laughing child.

name: Koon Poh Keong
about: When Koon Poh Keong returned home to Malaysia from the U.S. after graduation, he found no jobs on offer and Malaysia was in a recession.
Poh Keong started his company by rallying his four brothers, who pooled $50,000 and began an aluminum-extruding outfit.
Poh Keong is group CEO of aluminum company Press Metal while his brother Poh Ming is the executive vice chairman.
He founded the company with his brothers by renting a factory in Puchong, Selangor, a state on the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia.
Press Metal is Southeast Asia's largest integrated aluminum producer. It competes with the likes of Rio Tinto and China's Aluminum Corp.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, University of Oklahoma

name: Jim Kavanaugh
about: Jim Kavanaugh is the CEO of IT provider World Wide Technology.
With David Steward, he started the St. Louis-based company in 1990 by selling computers and printers to telecom companies like AT&T.
Kavanaugh personally fulfilled one of the company's first orders by renting a truck and driving 500 PCs to Omaha.
WWT is now a $20 billion (sales) company that sells software and hardware to customers including Citi, Verizon and the federal government.
Before starting WWT, Kavanaugh was a professional soccer player and was on the 1984 Olympic team.
Kavanaugh was appointed to the board of St. Louis-based Stifel Financial in 2022.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, St. Louis University

did_you_know_facts: Kavanaugh is part owner of the St. Louis Blues NHL team and a new Major League Soccer expansion team in St. Louis, announced in August 2019.

name: Marc Rowan
about: Marc Rowan is the CEO and a cofounder of Apollo Global Management, one of the biggest U.S. private equity firms, with $785 billion in assets.
Rowan met Apollo cofounders Leon Black and Joshua Harris while working at investment bank Drexel Burnham Lambert's M&A division.
The trio founded Apollo in 1990, after Drexel filed for bankruptcy following a cash shortage caused by turmoil in the junk bond market.
Rowan and his cofounders took Apollo Global public in 2011.
Rowan replaced Black as Apollo's CEO in 2021, after the latter stepped amid controversy surrounding his longtime relationship with sexual predator Jeffrey Epstein.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: Rowan owns several restaurants in the Hamptons, including Lulu Kitchen and Bar in Sag Harbor
Rowan was an investor in headphones firm Beats Electronics, which was acquired by Apple in a $3 billion deal in 2014.

name: Mikhail Gutseriev
about: Mikhail Gutseriev is a founder and the main shareholder of Safmar Group, a conglomerate with interests in oil, coal, real estate and retail.
Between 2015 and 2017, he spent $2 billion acquiring banks, pension funds, oil fields, factories, warehouses, real estate and retail companies.
In 2017 Binbank, which was headed by his nephew, former billionaire Mikail Shishkhanov, was nationalized by Russian Central Bank.
His son Said is a shareholder of Safmar. His father gave him his financial business and a big appliance store chain.
Gutseriev was sanctioned by the U.K. and EU in 2021 for being a "longtime friend" of Belarusian dictator Alexander Lukashenko. In 2022 he transferred assets to Kazakhstani Salman Gutsariyev.

personal_stats.label: Source of Wealth
personal_stats.value: Oil, coal, real estate, Self Made

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Kazakh Technological Institute

did_you_know_facts: Gutseriev is an owner of Hotel National, the hotel in Moscow where Donald Trump stayed during his first visit to Russia in 1987.
He has eight Russian radio stations, including the popular Radio Shanson, and writes lyrics for songs performed by famous Russian singers.
quote: In Russia there will never be a family business because of the lack of culture. In Russia, the family business is seen as a mafia clan.

name: Dennis Washington
about: Dennis Washington parlayed an early love of machinery into a diversified business group called Washington Companies.
Washington owns copper mining, marine transportation and heavy equipment businesses.
After working for his uncle's construction business, he struck out on his own with a $30,000 loan to start Washington Construction.
Montana's richest person, Washington also has an investment in Seaspan Corp., cofounded by son Kyle, which now operates more than 220 container ships.

forbes_list.list: The Richest Person In Every State (2025)

did_you_know_facts: Washington got polio at age 8 and spent 8 months in a hospital and rehab clinic. He then spent time in government housing and shined shoes for pocket money.
The day after high school graduation, in 1952, Washington headed to Alaska where he started out greasing equipment, then became a heavy-crane operator.
quote: People always ask me for my secret. There isn't one. You've just got to keep a level head and stay away from greed. I just think in my life I relied on my instincts and had good intuition, and things just kind of fell into place.

name: Jeffrey Lurie
about: Jeffrey Lurie, a former professor of social policy, is the outspoken owner of the Philadelphia Eagles NFL team.
In 1994, Lurie took out a loan to buy the Eagles for $185 million. The team is now worth more than $8 billion.
Lurie took an executive role at General Cinema Corporation, the film company founded by his grandfather, in 1983.
Two years later, he founded Chestnut Hill Productions, where he produced a string of mostly forgettable movies.
Lurie has since won two Academy Awards for producing documentaries: "Inside Job," about the 2008 economic crisis, and "Inocente," about an undocumented homeless American teen.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Clark University; Doctorate, Brandeis University

did_you_know_facts: Lurie flipped burgers at a Massachusetts drive-in theater before becoming an adjunct assistant social-policy professor at Boston University.

name: Alain Bouchard
about: Alain Bouchard cofounded convenience store conglomerate Alimentation Couche-Tard with a single Quebec shop in 1980.
As executive chairman, Bouchard still oversees the $73 billion (sales) company, which boasts more than 17,000 owned or franchised stores worldwide.
Bouchard, who grew the business rapidly by snatching up competitors, retired as president and CEO in September 2014.
Couche-Tard acquired the Circle K chain in 2003 and the Holiday Stationstores and CST Brands chains in 2017.
Couche-Tard made a $20 billion bid for French food retailer Carrefour in early 2021, but the French government nixed the deal.
did_you_know_facts: Bouchard got his start stocking shelves at his brother's franchised Perrette store and, after climbing the ladder at two chains, struck out on his own.
quote: I've learned that when you stick to it and you focus, you win.

name: Michael Kadoorie
about: Michael Kadoorie chairs CLP Holdings, the publicly traded power company his family cofounded in 1901.
CLP Holdings now serves 80% of Hong Kong's population.
Kadoorie is also chairman of the Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels, the global luxury chain that includes the Peninsula Hotels.
The company celebrated its 150th anniversary in 2016.
Michael's son Philip sits on the board at both CLP Holdings and the Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels.
did_you_know_facts: Kadoorie is the scion of a family of Iraqi Jews who settled in Asia decades ago.

name: Daniel Nadler
about: Daniel Nadler cofounded OpenEvidence in 2022 to use AI to help doctors make sense of the voluminous amount of medical research.
OpenEvidence has reached a valuation of $12 billion after an early 2026 funding round. Nadler owns nearly 60% of the company.
Before founding OpenEvidence, Nadler cofounded Kensho, which used AI for financial intelligence. He sold that company to S&P for $550 million in 2018.
OpenEvidence has signed up more than 758,000 doctors, and is adding them at a rate of 55,000 per month. It's free for verified doctors, and makes its money from advertising.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Ph.D, Harvard; Bachelor of Arts, University of Toronto

did_you_know_facts: Nadler wrote his Harvard Ph.D. thesis on the pricing mechanisms of credit derivatives. He also studied poetry under Pulitzer Prize-winner Jorie Graham.
quote: We talk about the golden age of biotechnology where there are new drugs and better drugs developed all the time. But it is like the dark ages for physicians because of burnout.

name: Hasmukh Chudgar & family
about: Low profile Hasmukh Chudgar founded generics maker Intas Pharmaceuticals in 1977.
Chudgar has long handed over operations to his sons Nimish and Binish, who run the $3.5 billion (revenue) company.
In August 2025, Intas Pharma acquired biosimilar company Udenyca from California-based Coherus Life Sciences for $558 million.
The company's portfolio includes an affordable drug to treat breast cancer called Eleftha, which is similar to Roche's Herceptin.
In 2022, the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority bought a 3% stake in Intas from Temasek.
did_you_know_facts: Chudgar's third son Urmish heads the company's biopharma business and is a haematologist-oncologist.
The company's biggest markets are Europe and India.

name: Ty Warner
about: Ty Warner is the creator of Beanie Babies, the plush toy fad of the 1990s.
Warner used the profits from selling Beanie Babies to assemble a high-end hotel portfolio, including the Four Seasons in New York.
Ty Inc. still sells Beanie Babies but has expanded its offerings to include toys like Beanie Boos and Beanie Bellies.
His Las Ventanas al Paraiso resort in Mexico rents its Ty Warner Mansion for $35,000 a night.
Warner has donated $100 million in cash and toys to the Children's Hunger Fund since 2005.

personal_stats.label: Source of Wealth
personal_stats.value: Plush toys, real estate, Self Made

did_you_know_facts: A onetime bellman, car valet and fruit market vendor, Warner found his calling as a salesman, peddling encyclopedias and later stuffed animals at toymaker Dakin.
Warner was convicted of tax evasion and paid a $53 million fine in 2013 for stashing money in a Swiss bank, but avoided jail time.
Zach Galifianakis played Warner in the 2023 fictionalized drama film "The Beanie Bubble."

name: Zhang Daocai
about: Zhang Daocai is the chairman of Sanhua Holding Group, whose interests include refrigeration, air conditioning and automotive thermal management components as well as finance.
He founded Sanhua in 1984 and listed the refrigeration and air conditioning parts arm, Zhejiang Sanhua Intelligent Controls, on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2005.
It had a dual listing on the Hong Kong stock exchange in June 2025.
His son Zhang Yabo is the chairman of the listed arm, younger son Zhang Shaobo serves as its director.
The group's 48 factories across the globe supply to international brands such as BMW and Panasonic.

name: Cliff Obrecht
about: Cliff Obrecht is cofounder and chief operating officer of design software maker Canva, which was valued by private investors at $42 billion in August 2025.
Canva was launched in 2013 by Obrecht, now-wife Melanie Perkins and Cameron Adams in Sydney, Australia, but was met by investor skepticism due to its location.
Like Perkins, Obrecht owns an estimated 18% stake. The couple has pledged to transfer more than 80% of their stake to the Canva Foundation for charitable causes.
Defying the doubts, Canva has attracted 240 million monthly users to its freemium software, with 6 million teams from companies like Zoom paying for it.
Canva's software enables the creation of attractive visuals for menus, resumes and Instagram graphics.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Western Australia

did_you_know_facts: Obrecht proposed to cofounder Perkins in Turkey's Cappadocia region with a $30 engagement ring.

name: Melanie Perkins
about: Melanie Perkins is cofounder and CEO of design software maker Canva, which was valued by private investors at $42 billion in August 2025.
Canva was launched in 2013 by Perkins, now-husband Cliff Obrecht and Cameron Adams in Sydney, Australia, but was met by investor skepticism due to its location.
Like Obrecht, Perkins owns an estimated 18% stake. The couple has pledged to transfer more than 80% of their stake to the Canva Foundation for charitable causes.
Defying the doubts, Canva has attracted 240 million monthly users to its freemium software, with 6 million teams from companies like Zoom paying for it.
Canva's software enables the creation of attractive visuals for menus, resumes and Instagram graphics.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Drop Out, University of Western Australia

did_you_know_facts: Perkins learned kitesurfing in an effort to receive an investment from a group of kiteboard enthusiast venture capitalists, including angel investor Bill Tai.
quote: If the whole thing was about building wealth, that would be the most uninspiring thing I could possibly imagine.

name: Robin Li
about: Robin Li is the cofounder, chairman and CEO of search engine operator Baidu, which is dual-listed on the Nasdaq and in Hong Kong.
The company counts online advertising as its bread-and-butter business. It is also expanding aggressively in AI.
Baidu in 2023 rolled out a chatbot rival to ChatGPT called Ernie.
It also operates driverless robotaxi services in mainland China, and secured trial permits for such services in Dubai and Hong Kong.
The company's semiconductor design unit, Kunlunxin, counts customers that include Chinese telecom giant China Mobile.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts, University at Buffalo; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Peking University

name: Yang Chang-Chih
about: Yang Chang-Chih is the founder of Gold Circuit Electronics, a maker of printed circuit boards for servers and networking equipment.
He handed over the chairman position to his son Chen-Tse in 2017. The older Yang still serves as a director.
Gold Circuit Electronics listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in 1998.
The company opened its first Thai plant in 2025 with $40 million investment and is pumping another $40 million into its expansion project.
His daughter Chen-Jung also sits on the board.

name: Juergen Blickle
about: Juergen Blickle and his brother Rainer own SEW-Eurodrive, a manufacturer specializing in drive-automation and power-transmission solutions.
The company, acquired by his father, Ernst, in 1945, now employs more than 19,000 people and generates around $3.7 billion in annual revenue.
Its motor, gear and electronic components power conveyors, lifts and other applications in contexts ranging from auto assembly to commercial baking.
In the U.S., it operates a manufacturing plant in Lyman, South Carolina, and has five regional assembly centers and dozens of technical sales offices.
did_you_know_facts: Juergen owns 50% of the company and Rainer, 44.9%. Just over 5% is held by Rainer's charitable foundation.
The brothers shun all publicity; not much is known about them.

name: Quek Leng Chan
about: Quek Leng Chan is the executive chairman of privately held Hong Leong Co. (Malaysia), which has interests in finance, food and property.
He inherited part of his fortune from his father, one of three brothers who started a banking group in the 1920s.
His cousin, Kwek Leng Beng, is also a billionaire and serves as chairman of Hong Leong Group in Singapore.
did_you_know_facts: Quek is a British-trained lawyer.

name: George Soros
about: George Soros is a hedge fund tycoon who managed client money in New York from 1969 to 2011.
In 1992, Soros shorted the British pound and reportedly made a profit of $1 billion. He became known as the man who broke the Bank of England.
Soros shifted $18 billion from his family office to his Open Society Foundations as of 2018.
Soros was born in Hungary; at 17 he left the country and put himself through the London School of Economics working as a railway porter and waiter.
Long one of the Democratic Party's biggest donors, he has given more than $200 million to candidates and PACs over the past decade.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, London School of Economics

did_you_know_facts: Soros' father was a lawyer. During the Nazi occupation he bought his family forged papers and bribed an official who then claimed Soros was his Christian godson.
quote: I occupy an exceptional position. My success in the financial markets has given me a greater degree of independence than most other people. This allows me to take a stand on controversial issues: in fact it obliges me to do so.

name: Maria Angelicoussis
about: Maria Angelicoussis is the CEO and owner of Angelicoussis Group, a shipping company based in Athens, Greece.
Founded in 1947 by her grandfather, Antonis, Maria took the reins of the group after the death of her father, John, in April 2021.
The Angelicoussis Group owns 158 ships, including oil tankers, liquid natural gas carriers and dry bulk vessels.
Angelicoussis obtained a medical degree from Cambridge University and worked as a junior doctor in the British National Health Service for two years.
She first joined the family business in 2008, when she returned to Greece from the U.K. to work as the group's vice president.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: University College London; Medical Doctor, Cambridge

name: John Grayken
about: John Grayken is the founder and owner of Lone Star Funds, a private equity firm based in Dallas, Texas, that focuses on corporate equity, real estate, credit, and other financial assets.
Since 1995, Grayken has raised 25 funds with approximately $95 billion in committed capital.
The assets Lone Star buys are managed by Hudson Advisors, a firm based in Dallas that Grayken owns with over 800 employees and more than $260 billion in cumulative assets managed.
Grayken is from a suburb south of Boston, but he renounced his U.S. citizenship for tax purposes in the 1990s and took Irish citizenship.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: He bought Boston's most expensive condo for $33 million in 2016.
While attending the University of Pennsylvania, Grayken played on the ice hockey team as a defenseman.

name: Wang Xing
about: Wang Xing is the chairman and CEO of Hong Kong-listed Meituan, which was created through a 2015 merger of Groupon-like group buying site Meituan and Yelp-like Dianping.com.
Wang cofounded China's first college social network xiaonei.com, which was sold to Oak Pacific Interactive in 2006.
After growing Meituan into a food-delivery heavyweight in mainland China, Wang is also expanding in locations including Hong Kong, Qatar and Saudi Arabia.
Wang in 2021 transferred shares at the time worth more than $2 billion to his foundation amid a China antitrust investigation.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Masters in Computer Engineering, University of Delaware; Bachelor of Engineering, Tsinghua University

name: Oleg Deripaska
about: Oleg Deripaska is the founder of Basic Element, a Russian industrial group with interests in aluminum, energy, construction, agriculture and more.
In April 2018, the U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control imposed sanctions against Deripaska and some of his companies.
In 2000, he merged his Siberian Aluminum with the aluminum assets of Roman Abramovich's Millhouse Capital to form UC Rusal.
In January 2019, OFAC lifted sanctions on En+ Group, UC Rusal and Eurosibenergo, and Deripaska agreed to permanently reduce his stake to 44.95%.
He was the richest person in Russia and the 9th richest in the world in 2008 before nearly losing it all due to crashing markets and heavy debts.
In an IPO in November 2017, En+ Group, which combined Deripaka's stake in UC Rusal and assets in the electric power industry, raised $1.5 billion.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Economics, Plekhanov Russian University of Economics; Master of Science, Moscow State University

did_you_know_facts: Deripaska was married to the daughter of Valentin Umashev, former chief of staff and current son-in-law of Russia's first president, Boris Yeltsin.
He is a subject in a tell-all book written by Nastya Rybka, an alleged escort who calls herself "Deripaska's mistress" on her social media accounts.
He sued in American courts to challenge the sanctions in March 2019; in June 2021, a District Court judge in Washington, D.C., dismissed his lawsuit.
quote: I started my business in a unique time - one country was gone, and the other had not yet appeared. The first gave me the opportunity to get a wonderful education, the second, to succeed.

name: Michael Milken
about: Mike Milken joined what became investment bank Drexel Burnham Lambert in 1969 and expanded the market for high-yield junk bonds.
He was banned from the securities industry after pleading guilty to securities fraud in 1990. In February 2020, President Trump pardoned him.
Milken chairs the Milken Institute think tank, which produces the annual Milken Global Conference in Los Angeles, the Davos of the West Coast.
His investments include private equity, hedge funds, venture capital and more than one asset management firm.
He's donated $500 million of his fortune on the Center For Advancing The American Dream in Washington DC, which including outside funding is expected to cost $1 billion.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of California, Berkeley; Master of Business Administration, University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School

did_you_know_facts: Milken founded what is now called the Prostate Cancer Foundation in 1993 after his own battle with prostate cancer.
Milken switched majors at U.C. Berkeley from math and science to business after the 1965 Watts riots in Los Angeles, determined to democratize capital access.
quote: Finance can change the world and create millions of jobs by empowering people with ability.

name: Xu Shihui
about: Xu Shihui is the chairman of Chinese snack and beverage maker Dali Foods Group.
Xu started out in the cookie business and took the food empire public in 2015. Today it is best known for its Copico potato chips, Heqizheng herbal tea and Haochidian soda crackers.
Citing reasons including unsatisfactory share performance, Xu took Hong Kong-listed Dali private in 2023 in a deal that values it at $6.6 billion.
Xu's daughter Xu Yangyang is a Dali vice president and executive director.
did_you_know_facts: Xu works seven days a week and hopes his work style inspires other managers. (He met Forbes Asia in his office in 2016 during a national holiday.)
Xu is the son of a laborer who worked at Dali when it was a collective and amassed shares by turning the business around.

name: Marcos Galperin
about: Marcos Galperin is founder of e-commerce platform MercadoLibre, the eBay of Latin America.
MercadoLibre, which operates in 18 Latin American countries and Portugal, went public in 2007 on the Nasdaq.
In 2026, after 26 years at the helm, Galperin stepped down as CEO and became executive chairman of the company.
He worked at Argentine oil company YPF for three years and as a summer intern at JPMorgan before starting MercadoLibre in 1999.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Stanford Graduate School of Business; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School

did_you_know_facts: eBay, once MercadoLibre's largest shareholder with 18%, sold its stake in 2016 for more than $1 billion.
Galperin helped organize Argentina's first-ever presidential debate ahead of the country's 2015 elections.
Galperin hails from Argentine business royalty. His grandfather started Sadesa, a tannery that has grown into one of the country's largest leather manufacturers.
quote: Successful entrepreneurs are typically stubborn contrarians, since creating a new reality that most people believe cannot exist will typically take a lot of time and several failures along the way.

name: Dona Bertarelli
about: The bulk of Dona Bertarelli's wealth comes from the 2007 sale of her family's biotech business Serono for over $13 billion.
In the 1990s Dona was Serono's executive director of public and professional affairs.
Her brother Ernesto is the richest man in Switzerland. They split ownership of most family assets.
She now focuses her time on marine conservation efforts and is a special adviser to the United Nations.
did_you_know_facts: Bertarelli became the fastest woman to sail around the world when her team raced for the Jules Verne Trophy in 2016.
She owns the Park Gstaad hotel, Five Seas Hotel in Cannes and Country Club Geneva.

name: James Clark
about: Jim Clark cofounded the Netscape browser and has since multiplied his wealth through timely tech investments.
The former Stanford professor got in early on Apple, Facebook, Twitter and Palantir.
Clark is married to Kristy Hinze, a former Victoria's Secret and Sports Illustrated model.
An ocean lover, his yachts include the 300-foot sailing yacht Athena and the 138-foot sloop Hanuman.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of New Orleans; Master of Science, University of New Orleans; Ph.D, University of Utah

did_you_know_facts: Clark was the key financial backer of the Japanese dolphin hunting documentary "The Cove."
Clark collects wine and art, including works by Monet and Matisse and a 30,000-bottle Burgundy collection he calls his "liquid asset."

name: Charles Simonyi
about: Early Microsoft employee Charles Simonyi is the man behind some of the company's most successful software, including Word and Excel.
The developer has a Ph.D. in computer science from Stanford and worked on one of the first personal computers at Xerox.
He joined Microsoft, then a fledgling firm, as employee No. 40 in 1981 and spent two decades in application development.
A native of Hungary, he left Microsoft in 2002 and founded Intentional Software, which develops platforms for productivity apps.
Microsoft acquired Intentional Software in 2017 for an undisclosed price, bringing Simonyi back to the Redmond, Washington giant.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of California, Berkeley; Doctorate, Stanford University

did_you_know_facts: Simonyi paid $60 million to jet to the International Space Station on a Russian rocket in 2007 and 2009, making him the first tourist to have visited space twice.
Simonyi worked as a night watchman in a computer lab as a teenager, which allowed him to use the machines after everyone had left.

name: Matthew Prince
about: Matthew Prince cofounded the web infrastructure and security company Cloudflare in 2009.
Prince owns about 8% of the company, which he took public in 2019, and serves as CEO.
Pre-IPO, its investors included Google's venture firm CapitalG, Microsoft, Baidu and Qualcomm Ventures.
Before Cloudflare, Prince was a law professor and cofounded Unspam Technologies, which helped block spam content for clients.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctor of Jurisprudence, University of Chicago; Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Trinity College Connecticut

did_you_know_facts: Prince worked as a ski instructor for six months in Park City, Utah when he was in his early twenties.

name: Jorge Moll Filho & family
about: Jorge Neval Moll Filho is a cardiologist and entrepreneur who founded Rede D'Or, one of Brazil's largest hospital and lab operators.
Moll started his business with a health diagnostics imaging laboratory in 1977.
Rede D'Or owns more than 30 hospitals. In 2010 Moll sold subsidiary Labs D'Or to publicly-traded Fleury SA for over $750 million.
In 2015, private equity firm Carlyle Group and Singapore's sovereign-wealth fund GIC bought stakes in Rede D'Or, spending over $500 million.
Moll lives in Rio de Janeiro and is the president of the board of directors of Rede D'Or.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Masters of Public Health, Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

did_you_know_facts: Every year, over 220,000 surgeries are performed and 24,000 babies are born in the hospitals managed by Rede D'Or.
quote: Study a lot about a topic before starting a business...First dedicate yourself to one thing. Then, become an entrepreneur on that topic.

name: Roger Penske
about: Former race car driver Roger Penske is the founder, chairman and CEO of Penske Corporation, a transportation services company with over $43 billion in revenue.
The company's publicly traded subsidiary Penske Automotive Group is best known for its auto dealerships, which sell new and used cars, and its iconic yellow rental trucks.
Penske started his career as a race car driver before opening one car dealership in 1965 with a $75,000 loan from his father.
In 2020, Penske Corporation acquired the Indianapolis Motor Speedway, host of the Indianapolis 500 Mile Race.
In 2019, Donald Trump Penske was awarded Penske the Presidential Medal of Freedom, the highest civilian honor in the U.S., for his accomplishments in racing and in business.
did_you_know_facts: He was named Sports Illustrated's race car driver of the year in 1961.
Penske Corporation's subsidiary, Penske Transportation Solutions, has nearly 500,000 trucks in its fleet bringing in around $13 billion in revenue.
quote: Without a little risk in your life every day, you start to get sloppy, and that is something I don't want to be. I want to be on the leading edge with our people and the company.

name: Yan Junjie
about: Yan Junjie is the chairman and CEO of Chinese AI model company MiniMax Group.
The company sells products such as audio- and video- generating models to enterprises as well as individual developers.
The mogul took the firm public in Hong Kong in January 2026, raising $618 million. It previously raised funding from investors including Alibaba, Tencent and Chinese gaming firm miHoYo.
Liu Wei, billionaire cofounder of miHoYo, is a board director at MiniMax.
Yan worked at fellow Hong Kong-listed Chinese AI company SenseTime for over six years before founding MiniMax in 2021.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Southeast University; Ph.D, Chinese Academy of Sciences

name: Steven Rales
about: Steven Rales and his brother Mitchell acquired a REIT in 1983 and merged it into their firm Danaher, named after a Montana creek.
Focused on tax avoidance and cash flow, they acquired more than three dozen companies and turned Danaher into a diversified firm.
Rales serves as chairman of the board at Danaher, which had around $24 billion in sales in 2024.
In 2021, he and his brother each transferred Danaher shares worth more than $1.5 billion to their charitable foundations.
In 2023, Rales purchased an additional 15% stake in the NBA's Indiana Pacers; he now owns 20% of the franchise.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, DePauw University; Law Degree, American University

did_you_know_facts: His production company Indian Paintbrush funded some of Wes Anderson's movies, such as "Isle of Dogs", "Moonrise Kingdom" and "The Grand Budapest Hotel."
His brother Mitchell Rales showcases his extensive art collection in a state of the art museum in Maryland.

name: Gary Rollins & family
about: Gary Rollins is executive chairman emeritus of $3.4 billion (2024 sales) Rollins Inc., the biggest pest control company by revenues in North America.
He ran the company with his brother, Randall Rollins, until Randall's death in 2020.
The company was founded by Rollins' father Wayne (d. 1991) and uncle John (d. 2000), who made an early fortune with regional radio stations and bought bug-killing giant Orkin for $62 million in 1964.
In 2023, the Rollins family unloaded a 9% stake in Rollins Inc. for more than $1.5 billion pretax. They still own about 40% of the publicly traded company.
In 2010, Gary Rollins' children sued their father and uncle, alleging the two were blocking access to trusts and denying them their rightful cash allocations. The family settled the matter in 2019.

personal_stats.label: Giving as a percentage of net worth
Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Tennessee Chattanooga

name: Min Kao & family
about: Min Kao cofounded GPS maker Garmin with the late Gary Burrell in 1989, after the duo led development of the first GPS navigator at Allied Signal.
Kao is executive chairman of the navigation firm, which has annual revenue of about $6 billion and makes everything from GPS for cars to weather radar for airplanes.
Garmin has brought GPS navigation and wearable technology to the automotive, outdoor, fitness, aviation, and marine markets.
Kao stepped down as CEO in 2012 but remains executive chairman and a member of the board.
Kao came to the U.S. from Taiwan in the 1970s and got a master's and a Ph.D. in engineering at the University of Tennessee.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctorate, University of Tennessee Knoxville; Bachelor of Arts/Science, National Taiwan University; Master of Science, University of Tennessee Knoxville

did_you_know_facts: Garmin is a mix of the first names of cofounders Gary Burrell and Min Kao.
While pursuing his Ph.D at the University of Tennessee, Kao worked as a researcher for NASA and the U.S. Army.
Kao's son, Ken Kao, is a Hollywood producer who has backed films including "The Favourite" and "The Nice Guys."

name: Max Van Hoegaerden Herrmann Telles
about: Max Van Hoegaerden Herrmann Telles is the son of Marcel Hermann Telles, a founding partner in Brazilian investing firm 3G Capital.
3G is best known for its investments in Anheuser-Busch InBev and Restaurant Brands International, parent of Burger King and Canadian coffee chain Tim Hortons.
Telles inherited shares in ABinBev through an inter vivos donation in 2024. His brother, Christian, also received an inheritance, but is not a billionaire.
Their father and his spouse, Bianka van Hoegaerden, divorced in 2009.
The brothers have been shareholders of São Carlos Empreendimentos e Participações since 2017.

name: Howard Lutnick & family
about: Donald Trump tapped Howard Lutnick to co-chair his transition team, then named him America's 41st secretary of commerce.
Lutnick lost both parents as a teenager, leaving him and his two siblings to take care of each other.
After graduating from Haverford College, he got a job at the Wall Street firm of Cantor Fitzgerald, where he became a favorite of founder Bernie Cantor and eventually took control of the firm.
The September 11, 2001 attack on the World Trade Center killed 658 of Cantor Fitzgerald's 960 New York employees, including Lutnick's younger brother, Gary.
Thanks to an electronic trading business and savvy dealmaking, Lutnick rebuilt his empire, which employed more than 14,000 people by the time he joined the Trump administration in 2025.
did_you_know_facts: Lutnick's rise to power at Cantor Fitzgerald sparked a fight with the family of his mentor, Bernie Cantor, whose widow barred Lutnick from her husband's cemetery.
Lutnick lived in a Trump Palace penthouse before purchasing a townhouse next door to Jeffrey Epstein, with whom a Lutnick spokesperson says he had no association.
quote: People think you need to be really smart to be successful. And what I say is you just need to be really clever.

name: Florentino Perez
about: Florentino Perez splits his time running Spain's largest construction company Grupo ACS and popular Spanish soccer team Real Madrid.
Perez, president of Real Madrid, boosted advertising and merchandise revenues in his first tenure as president (2000-2006).
He was re-elected president of Real Madrid in 2009. The team, owned by its fans, is worth more than $6 billion according to Forbes.
Florentino has been CEO of Grupo ACS since 1997; he owns about a 14% stake in the publicly-traded construction company.
did_you_know_facts: Perez briefly worked for the Madrid city council, then moved to Spain's Ministry of Public Works and Transport, before landing in the private sector in 1983.
Perez is credited with creating the Galacticios, Real Madrid's star-studded team in the early 2000s, with players including Ronaldo, Figo, Beckham and Zidane.

name: Frederik Paulsen
about: Frederick Paulsen inherited small drugmaker Ferring Pharmaceuticals, founded by his father in 1950.
When he took over running the business in 1983, it generated $15 million in annual revenue.
Today the biotech outfit, which makes infertility, obstetrics, urology, gastroenterology and endocrinology drugs, has estimated sales of $2.2 billion.
Ferring employs more than 6,500 people and has subsidiaries in nearly 60 countries.
Board members include H?l?ne Ploix, former director of the IMF, and Alexandra, the Countess of Frederiksborg, a former Danish princess.
did_you_know_facts: Paulsen enjoys extreme adventure travel: he was the first person to cross the Bering Strait from Alaska to Russia in an ultralight aircraft.
Paulsen's father named the company Ferring after the name for inhabitants of F?hr, his native island off the coast of Germany.

name: Kjeld Kirk Kristiansen
about: Third-generation owner of Lego, Kjeld Kirk Kristiansen led the toy company known for its interlocking plastic bricks from 1979 to 2004.
He and his three grown children together evenly split ownership of a 75% stake in the $7.2 billion (sales) business.
He stepped down from Lego's board in 2019. His son Thomas, Lego's deputy chairman, will replace him as chair of family holding company Kirkbi in 2023.
His grandfather Ole, a carpenter, started making wooden toys in his workshop in 1932 before moving into plastic in the 1940s.
The family also owns about half of theme park operator Merlin Entertainments, which it took private with a consortium in 2019.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Aarhus Business School; Master of Business Administration, International Institute for Management and Development

did_you_know_facts: The original Legoland, built in 1968 in Kristiansen's hometown of Billund, is made up of over 20 million Lego bricks.
The word "Lego" comes from the Danish words "LEg GOdt" ("play well").
quote: When children play games or build their own creations in the physical world, they actively challenge both the laws of nature and intellectual and physical limits.

name: Liu Hanyuan
about: Liu Hanyuan is the chairman of China's Tongwei Group, one of the world's largest in two different industries -- aquafeed and new energy.
Liu worked at a government job in the hydropower bureau in Sichuan province before he took the plunge as an entrepreneur in the fish food business.
Liu's daughter Shuqi became chairman and CEO of Tongwei Group's main listed business, Tongwei Co., in 2023.

name: Janice McNair & family
about: Janice McNair, widow of Bob McNair (d. 2018), inherited her late husband's 80% stake in the NFL's Houston Texans.
The couple met at Columbia College in South Carolina in the late 1950s and moved to Houston. Together they had four children and 16 grandchildren.
Bob made his first fortune selling his power generator company Cogen Technologies to Enron for $1.5 billion in 1999.
With the proceeds of Cogen's sale, he paid $700 million that year for the NFL's 32nd franchise.
Her son Cal McNair was named the team's principal owner in 2024.
did_you_know_facts: The Houston Texans, the youngest franchise in the NFL, was worth $2.8 billion when Bob McNair died in 2018, more than four times what he paid in 1999.

name: Xu Gaoming
about: Xu Gaoming is the founder and chairman of Chinese jewelry maker Laopu Gold.
Dubbed by consumers as "Hermes of gold jewelry," the luxury brand features traditional Chinese design and craftsmanship.
Xu worked with a local fishery bureau and a tourism investment firm before officially launching Laopu in 2016.
He took the company public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2024. His son, Xu Dongbo, is also a major shareholder.

name: Mark Walter
about: Mark Walter is CEO of investment firm Guggenheim Partners, which has more than $300 billion in assets under management.
Walter helped found the firm in the late 1990s after he folded his Chicago-based company, Liberty Hampshire, into the Guggenheim family office.
A yearlong SEC probe into Guggenheim over controversial real estate deals linked to Walter reportedly ended in 2019 with no penalty.
Walter's personal investments include stakes in plant-based food maker Beyond Meat and online car vendor Carvana.
In June, Walter agreed to buy a majority stake in the Los Angeles Lakers from the Buss family, in a deal valuing the team at approximately $10 billion.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctor of Jurisprudence, Northwestern University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Creighton University

did_you_know_facts: Walter, who earned a law degree from Northwestern University before going into finance, gave $40 million to the school in 2014.
Walter and his wife, Kimbra, own a wildlife preserve in Florida that has a mix of threatened and endangered species.

name: Thomas Pritzker
about: Tom Pritzker is one of 13 billionaire heirs in the Pritzker clan behind hotel giant Hyatt.

He stepped down as Hyatt's executive chairman in February 2026 amid scrutiny over his friendly relationship with Jeffrey Epstein. "There is no excuse for failing to distance myself sooner," he said at the time.
Hyatt Hotels dates back to 1957 when Tom's father, Jay Pritzker (d. 1999), purchased the first Hyatt House motel near Los Angeles International Airport.
Tom's father Jay and uncle Robert acquired manufacturing firm Marmon in the 1950s and expanded it; Tom led Marmon's 2008 sale to Berkshire Hathaway.
Pritzker stepped down from the board of Royal Caribbean Cruises in 2020 after two decades as a director.
He founded the Pritzker Neuropsychiatric Disorders Research Consortium, a research effort into the genetic basis of psychiatric disorders.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Claremont McKenna College; Doctor of Jurisprudence, University of Chicago; Master of Business Administration, University of Chicago

did_you_know_facts: Pritzker is an Honorary Professor of History at Sichuan University in Chengdu, China.
Pritzker leads archeological expeditions in the Western Himalayas.

name: Peggy Cherng
about: Peggy Cherng is cofounder and co-CEO of Panda Express, the $6.2 billion (est. sales) Chinese fast-food chain with some 2,500 locations.
Born in Myanmar, Cherng got a Ph.D. in electrical engineering in the U.S., then went to work for 3M and McDonnell Douglas, where she helped design battlefield simulators for the U.S. Navy.
She left her engineering career to help her husband, Andrew Cherng, open Panda Express' first location in a Glendale, California, shopping mall in 1983.
She implemented the company's sales and analytics software, earlier than many other restaurants, helping make Panda Express the dominant player among Asian limited-service chains in America.
In 2018, the Cherngs invested in a group that bought the Mandarin Oriental hotel, now the Waldorf Astoria, in Las Vegas for $214 million.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, University of Missouri; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Oregon State University; Ph.D, University of Missouri

did_you_know_facts: The Cherngs' Panda Restaurant Group is also the sole U.S. franchisee of Japanese cheesecake chain Uncle Tetsu and runs all the Raising Cane's in Hawaii and Alaska.
For her 1974 doctoral thesis, Cherng developed a computer program that used an algorithm to scan digitized chest X-rays for signs of congenital heart disease.
quote: A lot of people in the restaurant business aren't educated as engineers. I have an advantage.

name: Andrew Cherng
about: Andrew Cherng cofounded Chinese fast-food chain Panda Express, alongside his wife Peggy Cherng.
Born in China, his family moved to Taiwan and Japan before he immigrated to the U.S., where he met Peggy as a freshman at Baker University in Kansas.
The couple launched Panda Express in 1983 in a Glendale, California mall.
Today the 2,500-location chain stretches from the U.S. to Canada, Mexico, Dubai and South Korea. The Cherngs are co-CEOs.
In 2018, the couple invested in a group that bought the Mandarin Oriental hotel, now the Waldorf Astoria, in Las Vegas for $214 million.
did_you_know_facts: Andrew Cherng has a master's degree in applied mathematics; he first got into the food business with his father, opening a sit-down restaurant in Pasadena in 1973.

name: Karen Pritzker
about: Karen Pritzker is one of 13 billionaire Pritzker heirs. Her grandfather, A.N. Pritzker (d. 1986), built industrial conglomerate Marmon and Hyatt hotels.
She has invested in public companies like Apple, as well as hundreds of private biotech and medical device firms.
Pritzker and her late husband Michael Vlock donated to Yale, Teach for America and the Michael J. Fox Foundation for Parkinson's Research.
Her Seedlings Foundation supports the physical and mental health of children, and is one of the top-giving foundations in Connecticut.
did_you_know_facts: Pritzker's KPJR Films produced a documentary about "Joy Luck Club" author Amy Tan that was directed by Robert Redford's late son and featured at Sundance this year.

name: Daryl Katz
about: Daryl Katz amassed a fortune in the pharmacy business, buying the Canadian rights to U.S. franchise Medicine Shoppe in 1991.
A few years later he snatched up struggling Canadian drugstore chain Rexall, then expanded to the U.S. market.
Katz, the son of a drug store owner, has since sold off all of his pharmacy operations, pivoting his Katz Group to real estate and entertainment.
He has been co-developing a $2 billion, 25-acre complex in Edmonton's downtown that will include offices, condos and retail, among others.
Katz also owns his native city's NHL team, the Edmonton Oilers.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctor of Jurisprudence, University of Alberta; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Alberta

did_you_know_facts: Katz started off his career as a lawyer, then ran a chain of frozen yogurt stands after buying the Alberta franchise rights to Yogen Früz with other investors.
Katz is the majority owner of conservative news website LifeZette, founded by Fox News host Laura Ingraham.

name: Cen Junda
about: Cen Junda's fortune stems from his stakes in Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals and Hansoh Pharmaceutical Group.
China-based Hansoh operates a research center in the U.S. state of Maryland.
He holds degrees from Zhejiang University and the China State Institute of Pharmaceutical Industry.

name: Dirk Ziff
about: Dirk Ziff and his brothers Robert and Daniel inherited a fortune from their grandfather, who cofounded publishing company Ziff Davis in 1927.
The brothers' late father built up Ziff Davis, publisher of PC Magazine and Car and Driver, and sold the company for $1.4 billion in 1994.
Through their Ziff Brothers Investments, which had hedge funds in the U.S. and in London, the brothers greatly expanded their inheritance.
Ziff Brothers Investments ceased operations in 2014. In 2015, Dirk Ziff formed his own family office, Ziff Capital Partners.
The brothers are also reportedly investing with former employees of their hedge funds.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Columbia University; Master of Business Administration, Harvard University

did_you_know_facts: In 2021, the Ziffs sold their late father's estate in Manalapan, Florida for $94 million. It was originally listed in 2015 for $200 million.
Dirk is married to a former Forbes Magazine reporter.

name: Robert Ziff
about: Like his billionaire brothers Dirk and Daniel, Robert Ziff owes his fortune to his grandfather's publishing company, Ziff Davis.
The brothers' late father, William Jr., built up Ziff Davis, publisher of PC Magazine and Car and Driver, and sold the company for $1.4 billion in 1994.
The brothers created Ziff Brothers Investments and grew their inheritance with hedge funds in the U.S. and in London.
Ziff Brothers Investments ceased operations in 2014; the brothers are reportedly investing with former employees of their hedge funds.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Harvard University; Doctor of Jurisprudence, Cornell University

did_you_know_facts: Robert graduated magna cum laude from Harvard University and ranked first in his class at Cornell Law School.
His older brother Dirk is married to a former Forbes Magazine reporter.

name: Daniel Ziff
about: Daniel Ziff and brothers Robert and Dirk inherited a fortune that dates back to 1927 when their grandfather cofounded publishing company Ziff Davis.
Daniel's late father, William Jr., built up Ziff Davis, which became best known for such trade publications as PC Magazine and Car and Driver.
The publishing business was sold for $1.4 billion in 1994.
The brothers created Ziff Brothers Investments and greatly expanded their inheritance with hedge funds in the U.S. and in London.
Ziff Brothers Investments ceased operations in 2014; the brothers are reportedly investing with former employees of their hedge funds.

name: Kerry Stokes
about: Kerry Stokes took a winding path en route to earning a fortune with his SGH (formerly Seven Group Holdings), which has media, construction and mining assets.
He started his career selling Caterpillar tractors and trucks in Australia and eventually China, before moving into media with Seven Group.
In 2021 he retired as chairman of Seven Group Holdings.
In 2024, SGH acquired ASX-listed concrete and asphalt maker Boral for A$4.4 billion.
His son Ryan Stokes is the CEO and managing director of SGH.
did_you_know_facts: Early in his life his mother gave him up for adoption, and he later dropped out of school at age 14.
Stokes employs a team of people to manage his vast collection of paintings, sculptures and historic artifacts, many of which are on loan to art galleries worldwide.

name: Albert Avdolyan
about: Albert Avdolyan owns Far East and Siberian coal mining and gas companies.
Avdolyan got the investment capital from selling stakes in the Russian telecommunications companies Megafon and Yota.
Two billion tons of coking are proven reserves of the largest in Russia basin Elga. Avdolyan is the major shareholder of the company that keeps the license on extracting coal there.
In 2022 he started construction of a private railroad from coal deposits in Yakutia to the future port on the Sea of Okhotsk, the Pacific railway. Its length is about 500 kilometers.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Laws, Irkutsk State University

name: Radovan Vitek
about: Real estate mogul Radovan Vitek got his start during Slovakia's voucher privatization in the 1990s.
He moved to the Czech Republic in 1997, where he took over a cooperative and turned the headquarters into a luxury hotel.
His CPI Property Group owns 1 million square meters of lucrative real estate in Berlin, Germany.
CPI also has property in Budapest, Croatia, the Cote d'Azure and Poland including shopping centers.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Law Degree, University of West Bohemia

did_you_know_facts: Vitek owns a 260-acre estate in Surrey, England that formerly belonged to ex-Beatle Ringo Starr.

name: Philip Ng
about: Philip Ng and his brother Robert control Far East Organization, Singapore's largest private landlord and property developer.
The group was founded by their father Ng Teng Fong, who moved from China to Singapore in 1934 and came to be known as "The King of Orchard Road."
Their Hong Kong arm, Sino Group, is run by older sibling Robert and his son Daryl, while Philip oversees the Singapore interests.
Singapore-listed Far East Orchard repurposed the century-old former Westminster Fire Station in London into a luxury development with 17 apartments and put it on sale in 2022.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Kings College London; Masters of Science in Technology, Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)

did_you_know_facts: The brothers are staunch Christians and refer to Far East as a Christian enterprise.
Founder Ng Teng Fong spurned his family's grocery store and got into real estate in 1960 against his father's wishes.

name: Vincent Viola
about: The son of a truck driver from Brooklyn, Vincent Viola started electronic-trading firm Virtu Financial in 2008 and took the company public in 2015.
Market-maker Virtu completed a series of secondary offerings in May 2019 to help repurchase more than $500 million in stock from Viola.
Viola splurged on real estate with stock sale proceeds, buying a beachfront Florida condo and spending $108 million on Arizona's tallest skyscraper.
Viola is the owner of the NHL's Florida Panthers. He graduated from West Point in 1977 and New York Law School in 1983.
In 2003 he founded the Combating Terrorism Center at West Point to provide education and research about global terrorism.

personal_stats.label: Giving as a percentage of net worth
Education
personal_stats.value: Doctor of Jurisprudence, New York Law School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, United States Military Academy

did_you_know_facts: Donald Trump appointed Viola to be Secretary of the Army in December 2016 but Viola withdrew his nomination two months later citing business conflicts.
Viola was a former infantry officer who served in the 101st Airborne Division.
quote: "From the first day at West Point, my focus and purpose was about selfless leadership, putting others before yourself and being ready to sacrifice for others so that the mission and the goal would be accomplished."

name: Tse Ping & family
about: Tse Ping is a member of the billionaire Chearavanont clan from Thailand and the guiding hand behind Hong Kong-listed Sino Biopharmaceutical.
He stepped down as chairman of Sino Biopharmaceutical in 2015 and ceded the role to his daughter Theresa, while staying on as senior vice chairman.
Ping's son Eric rose to CEO in 2022 and is the company's largest individual shareholder.
Trapped in China during the turbulent Mao-era Cultural Revolution, Tse was shipped off to the countryside from the southern city of Shantou and lost the opportunity to attend college.

name: Teddy Sagi
about: Teddy Sagi founded gambling software developer Playtech in 1999. It has revenue of more than $1 billion and is traded on London's stock exchange.
Sagi sold a 12% slice of Playtech for almost $400 million in 2016; he sold the rest for $88 million in November 2018.
He has taken 4 companies public on London's AIM: Playtech, Market Tech, online payments processor SafeCharge and cybersecurity company Kape.
Sagi took Market Tech (now Labtech London) private in July 2017; it owns a portfolio of London property including tourist hot spot Camden Market.
In 2019, he sold SafeCharge to Canadian company, Nuvei for $889 million. His other investments include co-working spaces and technology startups.
did_you_know_facts: Sagi plans to rejuvenate Camden Market by introducing technology and high-tech operations.
He has six children with his partner Yael Nizri, the 2006 Miss Israel.
quote: The way the world is going, people like to have engagement and entertainment. People want to connect with each other, to see each other.

name: Chase Coleman III
about: Chase Coleman III started out as a hedge fund investor, but his Tiger Global Management has evolved into a broader investment firm.
Tiger Global Management oversees $50 billion in assets. Its venture capital arm is now its biggest unit.
Prior to starting Tiger Global in 2001, Coleman worked for hedge fund legend Julian Robertson.
His longtime partner Scott Shleifer joined Tiger Global in 2002 and cofounded its venture business, which he led until the start of 2024.
Tiger Global's hedge fund fell more than 50% in 2022 after an impressive first two decades. It rebounded 20% in 2023 and 2024.
did_you_know_facts: Coleman is a descendant of Peter Stuyvesant, the last Dutch governor of New York.

name: Miguel Krigsner
about: Bolivian-born Miguel Krigsner founded Grupo Boticario, Brazil's second-largest cosmetics company behind number one, Natura.
Grupo Boticario operates in more than 50 countries; Krigsner individually owns approximately 80% of the business.
His brother-in-law Artur Grynbaum joined as a financial assistant and worked his way up to president of the group by 2008. He owns about 20% of the group.
In 1990 Krigsner created the Boticario Group Foundation dedicated to environmental protection, which receives about 1% of Grupo Boticario's net income annually.
Today, Krigsner and Grynbaum serve as president and vice president, respectively, of the Grupo Boticario advisory board.
did_you_know_facts: His parents fled Nazi Germany to settle in Bolivia in the 1940s. Krigsner was born in Bolivia and moved to Brazil in 1961.
quote: Everything will make sense when you look back. From the moment I was born, I was never able to separate my personal life from my professional life.

name: Steven Spielberg
about: The films of Steven Spielberg, a three-time Academy Award-winning director, have grossed more than $10 billion worldwide.
Spielberg became a household name directing movies like 'Jaws' and 'Jurassic Park.'
In 1994, he cofounded DreamWorks studios with Jeffrey Katzenberg and David Geffen.
Today, a slice of the cash from every ticket at Universal theme parks goes directly into his pocket thanks to blockbuster hits like 'Indiana Jones.'
His recent turns in the director's chair include 'West Side Story' and 'The Fablemans,' a semi-biographical tale about his entry into moviemaking.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, California State Long Beach

did_you_know_facts: After failing to get into USC film school, Spielberg got his start as an unpaid intern in the editing department of Universal.
Spielberg did not take a salary for his Oscar-winning 'Schindler's List' in 1993.

name: Stephen Smith
about: Stephen Smith is a Canadian financial services magnate.
Smith cofounded mortgage lender First National Financial in 1988, just four years after being personally bankrupt.
He also owns about half of Canada Guaranty Mortgage Insurance Company and a stake in publicly traded Canadian bank EQB.
He acquired lender Home Trust for more than $1.2 billion in 2023 and merged it with Fairstone Bank of Canada in early 2025.
Smith has donated more than $100 million to Queen's University, where the business school is named after him.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Queens University

did_you_know_facts: Smith has passed his love of heli-skiing onto his three adult children.
An electrical engineer by education, Smith programmed code that is still used today by First National's mortgage approval and tracking system, Merlin.

name: Tom Brown
about: Tom Brown is cofounder and chief compute officer of startup Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI employees.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $380 billion in February 2026, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
While working at OpenAI, Brown served as lead author of the white paper that introduced the GPT-3 language model.
Brown studied computer science and cognitive science at MIT. He cofounded his first company, social club Grouper, in 2011.

name: Jack Clark
about: Jack Clark is cofounder and head of policy at Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six ex-OpenAI researchers.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $380 billion in February 2026, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
Clark previously worked as a technology journalist at Bloomberg, before leaving for OpenAI in 2016.
He writes a newsletter about AI research called Import AI. It has more than 69,000 subscribers.

name: Jared Kaplan
about: Jared Kaplan is cofounder and chief science officer of Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI employees.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $380 billion in February 2026, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
Kaplan is a theoretical physicist with a PhD from Harvard. His research has been focused on quantum gravity and machine learning.
He became a professor at Johns Hopkins University in 2012 but is currently on leave.

name: Dario Amodei
about: Dario Amodei is cofounder and CEO of Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other former OpenAI employees, including his sister Daniela Amodei, who is president.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $380 billion in February 2026, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
Amodei previously served as vice president of research at OpenAI, where he co-invented reinforcement learning from human feedback.
Amodei has a PhD in biophysics from Princeton University.

name: Daniela Amodei
about: Daniela Amodei is cofounder and president of Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
She cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other former OpenAI employees, including her brother Dario Amodei, who is CEO.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $380 billion in February 2026, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
Amodei worked at OpenAI for about three years as an engineering manager and vice president.
Amodei studied English literature at the University of California, Santa Cruz, then joined fintech unicorn Stripe in 2013 as a founding recruiter.

name: Sam McCandlish
about: Sam McCandlish is cofounder and chief technology officer of Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI employees.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $380 billion in February 2026, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
McCandlish previously worked for three years as a member of the technical staff at OpenAI.
He has a PhD in theoretical physics from Stanford.

name: Christopher Olah
about: Chris Olah is cofounder and interpretability research lead at Anthropic, which builds large-scale artificial intelligence systems.
He cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI employees.
Anthropic, which private investors valued at $380 billion in February 2026, has partnerships with Google's parent company Alphabet and Amazon.
Olah previously worked in a similar role at OpenAI and was a researcher at Google Brain.
Olah skipped college and was named a Thiel Fellow in 2012, when he was 19. In 2020, he wrote a blog post to help others decide if they should follow a similar path.

name: Edythe Broad & family
about: Edythe Broad is an American art collector and philanthropist.
She was married to billionaire businessman Eli Broad from 1954 until his death in April 2021.
Known for their philanthropy, Edythe and Eli established two foundations that support medical research, public education and the visual and performing arts.
The foundations, which have been awarding grants for over 50 years, have pledged or given away more than $4 billion to date.

name: Robert Ng
about: Robert Ng and his brother Philip control Far East Organization, Singapore's largest private landlord and property developer.
The group was founded by their father Ng Teng Fong, who moved from China to Singapore in 1934 and came to be known as "The King of Orchard Road."
Their Hong Kong arm, Sino Group, is run by older sibling Robert's son Daryl, while Philip oversees the Singapore interests.
Singapore-listed Far East Orchard repurposed the century-old former Westminster Fire Station in London into a luxury development with 17 apartments and put it on sale in 2022.
did_you_know_facts: The brothers are staunch Christians and refer to Far East as a Christian enterprise.
Founder Ng Teng Fong spurned his family's grocery store and got into real estate in 1960 against his father's wishes.

name: Zhang Congyuan
about: Zhang Congyuan founded Huali Industrial, a shoe manufacturer, in 2004; the company now has factories in China, Indonesia, Vietnam, Dominica and Myanmar.
Huali supplies to dozens of brands including Nike, Puma, UGG and Vans.
Zhang also cofounded Hong Kong-listed shoemaker Symphony Holdings, but sold his stake and is no longer with the company.
He shares the fortune with his wife and children.

name: Bruce Flatt
about: Bruce Flatt is the CEO of Brookfield Corp., a $1 trillion (assets) alternative investment firm with real estate, infrastructure and private equity operations.
Brookfield spun off its asset management business in 2022, and Flatt named protégé Connor Teskey CEO of this entity in 2026.
A Winnipeg native, he joined an accounting firm out of college, then took a job at Canadian conglomerate Brascan, which soon nearly collapsed.
He helped revive Brascan through a series of savvy real estate deals and became CEO in 2002, refashioning the firm into Brookfield Asset Management.
His winning deals include buying Olympia & York in 1996 and London's Canary Wharf in 2015, and recapitalizing General Growth Properties in 2010.
did_you_know_facts: Flatt lives in a quiet Toronto neighborhood and often commutes by subway.
quote: Never put yourself in a situation where you have to sell something in an environment where you should be buying.

name: Ronda Stryker
about: Ronda Stryker is a director of Stryker Corp., the medical equipment company founded by her grandfather, Homer Stryker (d. 1980).
She owns about 5% of Stryker Corp. which she inherited from her parents; she is the only one of her siblings to serve on the board.
In 2011, she and her husband gave $100 million to create the Homer Stryker medical school at Western Michigan University.
In 2016 the couple pledged $20 million to the Harvard Medical School Department of Global Health and Social Medicine to support equitable health care.
Stryker and her husband donated $30 million to Spelman College in 2018, the largest gift from living donors in the institution's history.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Northern Colorado; Master of Arts, Western Michigan University

did_you_know_facts: Stryker taught special education at Kalamazoo, Michigan public schools.
Stryker received a lifetime achievement award from the YWCA in 2013 for her work as a role model for women.
quote: I believe that, in my lifetime, we can create a movement and affect real change in billions of people's lives around the world, particularly women and children who often bear the brunt of the lack of access to health care.

name: Ding Shizhong
about: Ding Shizhong is the chairman of Anta Sports, one of China's largest homegrown sportswear makers.
It sells under a range of brands such as Anta, Fila, Descente and Kolon Sport.
In 2019 the company led a consortium to acquire Finnish group Amer Sports, with brands including Arc'teryx, Wilson and Salomon, for $5.2 billion.
Amer Sports went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2024, raising $1.4 billion.
