The Getty family faced many tragedies: The wife of Gordon's brother J. Paul Jr. died of a heroin overdose and J. Paul Jr.'s son was kidnapped by Italian gangsters.
Getty has publicly acknowledged the fact that he has two families: four sons with his late wife Ann, and three daughters with Cynthia Beck.

name: Jerzy Starak
about: Jerzy Starak is the owner of Polpharma, one of Poland's largest drug manufacturers.
Polpharma specializes in pharmaceuticals used in cardiology, neurology and gastroenterology.
Starak also founded and owns Polpharma Biologics, an arm of his company that focuses on developing biosimilar drugs.
A diversified investor, Starak also holds a stake in herbal product producer Herbapol.
Starak started out with chemical company Comindex in the 1970s.
did_you_know_facts: Starak and his wife Anna Woźniak-Starak exhibit their collection of 20th and 21st century Polish art at a gallery space that they founded in Warsaw.

name: Jeff Skoll
about: Jeff Skoll built his fortune as eBay's first full-time hire and president in 1995; he left eBay in 2001, three years after its IPO.
His Skoll Foundation has put on the Skoll World Forum since 2004, bringing together business, government, philanthropy and civil society leaders focused on social change.
His charitable Skoll Foundation and Skoll Global Threats Fund have distributed some $1.2 billion globally over more than 20 years.
In 2024, Skoll announced that after 2 decades he was shutting down his movie production company Participant Media, which produced An Inconvenient Truth and many other films.
Skoll founded millennial-focused cable TV channel Pivot TV in 2013 but shut it down in late 2016.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Stanford Graduate School of Business; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Toronto

did_you_know_facts: Skoll was born and raised in Canada and pumped gas to pay his way through the University of Toronto. He became a U.S. citizen in 2007.
He met eBay founder Pierre Omidyar while he was an MBA student at Stanford University.
quote: When my friend Pierre Omidyar approached me with his idea for eBay, I was very sure of what to do. With my newly minted [MBA] degree in hand, I said 'Pierre, what a stupid idea!' Luckily, I soon realized that Pierre was onto something.

name: Ruan Xueping
about: Ruan Xueping is the vice chairman of Shanghai-listed power strip supplier Goneo Group.
It's formerly known as Gongniu Group, which means bull in Chinese.
Ruan cofounded Gongniu with his elder brother Ruan Liping, also a billionaire, in 1995.
Both brothers hold Hong Kong citizenship.

name: Peter Spuhler
about: Peter Spuhler, former CEO of Stadler Rail, built a fortune buying up railcar makers across eastern Europe.
In 2019, Spuhler took Stadler Rail public through an IPO that valued the company at $3.8 billion.
His wife's grandfather had started Stadler five decades earlier, and in 1989, he bought the company from her grandmother for $6 million.
Today, Spuhler owns a variety of shareholdings through his holding company PCS Holding.

His portfolio also includes Swiss textile machine manufacturer Rieter, car supplier Autoneum and Aebi Schmidt, a manufacturer of specialty vehicles that went public in 2025 and trades on the NASDAQ exchange.
did_you_know_facts: Spuhler, a former Swiss Army officer, served for 13 years in parliament where he advocated a pro-business agenda.

name: Jon Yarbrough
about: Jon Yarbrough started Video Gaming Technologies, which produced casino games, in 1991.
The business grew due to the proliferation of tribal casinos; Yarbrough says he's worked with around 35 tribes in 100-plus locations over the years.
Yarbrough sold his company to Australian firm Aristocrat Leisure in 2014 for about $1.3 billion.
These days he manages his investments, which include real estate and tech stocks, through his family office Yarbrough Capital.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Tennessee Technological University

did_you_know_facts: As a college student, Yarbrough loaned his foosball table to a local arcade in exchange for 50% of its profits; now he keeps the table in his office.
During college, Yarbrough interned at NASA, where he designed a mini supersonic wind tunnel and sent instructions to the Mars lander.

name: Jeremy Jacobs Sr & family
about: Jeremy Jacobs is chairman of concessions juggernaut Delaware North, a private company that serves 500 million people per year across four continents.
The business was founded in 1915 by his father, who began by selling popcorn and peanuts
The New York-based company is currently considered a global leader in hospitality management & food service management.
Jacobs is also the owner of the NHL's Boston Bruins ice hockey team, and he was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2017.
In early 2019, Jacobs began handing control of the Boston Bruins team and Delaware North to his six children.
did_you_know_facts: Jacobs owns a Florida restaurant with legendary golfer Jack Nicklaus, with whom he shares a birthday.
Jacobs pledged $30 million in 2015 to the University at Buffalo, his alma mater, which renamed its medical school after him.

name: Ruan Liping
about: Ruan Liping is the chairman of power strip supplier Goneo Group, which went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2020.
Previously known as Gongniu Group, the company changed its English name to Goneo in 2023.
Ruan, a basketball fan, named the firm in honor of NBA Chicago Bulls former star Michael Jordan - with Gongniu translating to "bulls."
He cofounded Gongniu in 1995 with his younger brother Ruan Xueping, who is the company's vice chairman and also a billionaire.
Ruan started his career as an engineer in a local mechanical factory. He quit his job about a decade later to launch Gongniu.

name: Linda Campbell
about: Linda Campbell is one of six billionaire heirs to the media and publishing empire founded by her grandfather Roy Thomson (d. 1976).
The family's biggest holding: more than 310 million shares of Thomson Reuters.
Thomson owns around 14% of the business through the family's investment firm, Woodbridge.
The family's other assets include the Toronto-based Global and Mail newspaper, and the Montreal Canadiens and Winnipeg Jets sports teams.

name: Gaye Farncombe
about: Gaye Farncombe is one of six billionaire heirs to the media and publishing empire founded by her grandfather Roy Thomson (d. 1976).
The family's biggest holding: more than 310 million shares of Thomson Reuters.
Thomson owns around 11% of the business through the family's investment firm, Woodbridge.
The family's other assets include the Toronto-based Global and Mail newspaper, and the Montreal Canadiens and Winnipeg Jets sports teams.

name: Mangal Prabhat Lodha
about: Politician and property magnate Mangal Prabhat Lodha founded developer Lodha group in Mumbai in 1980, now known as Macrotech Developers.
A native of the desert state of Rajasthan, Lodha started off by building middle-class homes in Mumbai's far-flung suburbs.
After his sons Abhishek and Abhinandan joined the business in 2003, the firm went on an expansion binge picking up prime land parcels. Abhinandan has since left the business.
Lodha built Mumbai's Trump Tower, a 78-story luxury skyscraper, located in a complex called The Park, in midtown Mumbai.
In 2021, Lodha completed Macrotech's long-delayed IPO. The company has since changed its name to Lodha Developers.
did_you_know_facts: Lodha was the Mumbai president of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party until 2022.
He successfully lobbied for a law to ban the slaughter of cows, a key electoral plank for his political party, in his home state of Maharashtra.
Lodha's sons ended a 50 billion rupees ($571 million) trademark feud in April 2025.
Abhishek now has rights to use 'Lodha' and 'Lodha Group' brands and Abhinandan has rights to use 'House of Abhinandan Lodha' brand.

name: Russell Savage
about: Russ Savage founded energy drink company Rockstar in 2001.
Savage sold Rockstar to PepsiCo in 2020, in a deal worth more than $4 billion.
Formerly known as Russ Weiner, he changed his name in 2025 to Russ Savage in honor of his father, right-wing talk-radio star Michael Savage.

He got his start in the late 1990s, when he ran for California State Assembly. Though he lost the race, he caught the eye of his father's friend, Skyy Vodka founder Maurice Kanbar, who quickly hired him.
When Kanbar rejected Savage's idea for an energy drink, he quit and launched Rockstar using a $50,000 mortgage on his Sausalito, Calif. condo.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, San Diego State University

did_you_know_facts: Savage started a yard service company in his Northern California neighborhood at age 8 and worked the drive-thru at Wendy's at 15.
Savage once owned a 161-foot yacht named 'Rockstar' that was damaged by a Miami drawbridge.
When the first Rockstar cans hit stores and bars, Savage drove around San Francisco in an old limo painted with the Rockstar logo to promote it.

name: Bulat Utemuratov
about: Bulat Utemuratov is a Kazakhstani investor whose investment portfolio includes holdings in the hotel sector and mobile phone companies Kar-tel and Kyrgyzstan's Sky Mobile.
In 2012, he led the sale of mineral company Kazzinc to commodities firm Glencore for $1.4 billion in cash and shares, which he sold in 2021.
Utemuratov purchased 88% of Kazakhstan's Forte Bank for $400 million in 2014.

In 2025, the businessman sold The Ritz-Carlton Vienna hotel, the gold mining company RG Gold in Kazakhstan, the Burger King franchise in Kazakhstan, and Sky Mobile LLP in Kyrgyzstan (a mobile operator).
One of his biggest transactions was the 2007 sale of Kazakhstan's ATF Bank to Italian bank UniCredit for a reported $2.2 billion

name: Lynda Resnick
about: From almonds & oranges in California's Central Valley to seedless lemons in South Texas, Lynda Resnick and her husband Stewart are worth billions from farming as the world's leading grower of tree nuts and America's largest citrus grower.
They cofounded and co-own the Wonderful Company, among the largest farming operations in America. As a couple, they share a fortune worth an estimated $10.8 billion.
Lynda dropped out of college at 19 to start her own ad agency. Stewart came to her looking for marketing help.
Both previously divorced, they met in the 1970s when she provided marketing help for a burgeoning janitorial business.
Lynda focuses on philanthropy; the Resnicks have pledged more than $2 billion to charitable causes, including climate change research.
did_you_know_facts: A former child actress, Resnick dropped out of community college and started her own advertising agency at 19 years old.
Resnick was an unindicted co-conspirator in the Pentagon Papers investigation. The leaks were copied on her ad agency's Xerox machine. The case was later dropped.
quote: It takes a nut to sell a nut.

name: Stewart Resnick
about: From almonds & oranges in California's Central Valley to grapefruits in South Texas, Stewart Resnick and his wife Lynda owe their billions to nature's bounties.
They cofounded and continue to co-own the Wonderful Company, among the largest farming operations in America. As a couple, they share a fortune worth an estimated $10.8 billion.
Nearly half of all Americans purchase one of their products, including pistachios, almonds, Halos oranges, POM Wonderful and Fiji Water.
Stewart bought his first piece of California farmland in 1978 as a hedge against inflation.
They own a majority stake in the Kern Water Bank, one of the country's largest underground water storage facilities.
did_you_know_facts: Stewart is a prostate cancer survivor and drinks 8 ounces of POM wonderful and a pomegranate pill a day. He claims he hasn't had a cold in a decade.
Stewart is the son of a New Jersey bar owner who drank and gambled his money away.
quote: You have to be an optimist to be a farmer. Fortunately, with our management team, we have some optimists and some pessimists.

name: Lachhman Das Mittal
about: Lachhman Das Mittal started his business career in 1990 at age 60 after retiring from the state-owned Life Insurance Corporation of India.
Today his Sonalika Group is India's third-largest tractor maker by market share.
Japanese firm Yanmar has a 30% stake in his tractor outfit International Tractors.
Mittal has handed over operations to his sons Amrit Sagar and Deepak and grandsons Raman, Sushant and Rahul, but remains keenly interested in the business.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Punjab University; Master of Arts, Punjab University

did_you_know_facts: Sonalika, which means "lines of gold" in Hindi, was named after a wheat seed that fueled India's Green Revolution.
His daughter Usha Sangwan was the first woman managing director of the Life Insurance Corporation of India, the state-owned life insurer. She has since retired.
quote: I can convince anyone to purchase my tractors.

name: Venu Srinivasan
about: Venu Srinivasan is chairman emeritus of TVS Motor Company, India's third-largest maker of two-wheelers.
TVS Motor is the flagship of the TVS Group, which was founded in 1911 by T. V. Sundaram Iyengar. Srinivasan belongs to the third generation.
The Chennai company has three factories in India and one each in Indonesia and the U.K.
His son Sudarshan Venu, who was managing director, took over as chairman of TVS Motor in August 2025.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, Anna University, Chennai, India; Master of Business Administration, Purdue University

did_you_know_facts: He was awarded the Padma Bhushan, India's third-highest civilian award, in 2020.
TVS Motor Company has invested in Formula One driver Narain Karthikeyan's venture DriveX, which sells refurbished, pre-owned two-wheelers.
Sudarshan is a motorcycle enthusiast, who has raced in four continents.
His daughter Lakshmi Venu, who is managing director of auto components maker Sundaram-Clayton, was appointed vice-chair of tractor maker TAFE in March 2025.

name: Michael Saylor
about: Michael Saylor founded business analytics software firm MicroStrategy and ran it as CEO until early August 2022, when he moved into the chairman's role.
One of the best-known executives of the Internet bubble, Saylor was a multibillionaire in the late 1990s thanks to his stake in MicroStrategy.
He fell from the billionaire ranks after questionable accounting led to a restatement of financial results and the dot-com bust crashed the stock.
He's a billionaire again thanks to timely bitcoin investments. In October 2020, he disclosed he personally bought 17,732 bitcoins for $175 million.
He has steered MicroStrategy's corporate coffers into bitcoin, spending billions to accumulate 214,400 bitcoins.
A former rocket scientist, Saylor studied aeronautics and astronautics at MIT on an Air Force scholarship before founding MicroStrategy in 1989.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

did_you_know_facts: Saylor helped trigger the institutional bitcoin boom in December 2020, when MicroStrategy's bitcoin ownership crossed the $1 billion milestone.

name: Michael Xie
about: Michael Xie is the cofounder and chief technology officer of Fortinet, which provides cybersecurity services to businesses like Panasonic and Siemens.
The Chinese native moved to North America in the 1990s to study engineering at the University of Manitoba in Canada.
After graduating, Xie worked at several network security companies before cofounding Fortinet with brother Ken Xie in 2000.
The siblings took the California-based firm public in an IPO nine years later; Michael owns more than 7% of the company.
Fortinet had $5.3 billion in 2023 revenue and offers services like enterprise firewalls, cloud security and network security.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Tsinghua University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Tsinghua University; Master of Science, University of Manitoba

name: Ivan Tavrin
about: Ivan Tavrin is the founder of Kismet Capital Group, which has interests in technology and consumer companies in Russia.
From 2012 to 2016 Tavrin was CEO of Megafon, a large Russian telecommunication operator owned by fellow billionaire Alisher Usmanov and his partners.

He bought one of Russia's largest internet companies, Avito, from South African conglomerate Naspers for $2.4 billion in 2022, selling 50% to state-owned Rosselkhozbank (or Russian Agricultural Bank) in 2025.
During his university years, Tavrin started an advertising agency selling TV ads and eventually invested in regional TV and radio stations which were later acquired by The Walt Disney Company.
He was shareholder in Disney Channel Russia until 2023.
Since the 2022 Ukraine-Russia war, Tavrin has been snapping up Russian assets of foreign companies, including those held by German consumer goods giant Henkel and U.S. payments company Fleetcor

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master, Moscow State Institute of International Relations

name: Torbjorn Tornqvist
about: Torbjörn Törnqvist is the Swedish cofounder of Gunvor, a global energy and commodities group.
Gunvor has a diverse portfolio that includes refineries, pipelines, terminals, LNG carriers, and biofuel and hydrogen plants.
Törnqvist got his start at British Petroleum in 1977, and launched Gunvor in 2000.
He bought out his cofounder Gennady Timchenko in 2014, following the Russian invasion of Crimea.
Törnqvist owned more than 80% of Gunvor until December 2025, when he sold his stake to a group of employees and stepped back from the company.
did_you_know_facts: Törnqvist is an avid sailor; his Artemis Racing team has raced in the America's Cup and now develops tech to cut emissions in maritime trade.
In 2015, Tornqvist paid himself a $1 billion dividend, one of the biggest payments ever in the commodity-trading industry.

name: George Economou
about: George Economou is a Greek shipping tycoon who owns several privately-held firms under his TMS Group.
He took one of those firms, Dryships, public on the Nasdaq in 2005 before ultimately taking it private again in 2019 at a $456 million valuation.
In 2018, he sold offshore drilling firm Ocean Rig to publicly traded TransOcean at a $2.7 billion valuation, just 18 months after the firm filed for bankruptcy.
Between August and December 2023, Economou bought large positions in several publicly-traded shipping firms in the U.S.
Outside of shipping, he owns an estimated $250 million art collection including works by Pablo Picasso. Part of it is on display in his private museum in Athens.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Master of Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

did_you_know_facts: Dryships made headlines due to volatile trading and several reverse stock splits in 2016 and 2017 that saw its stock price rise by 1,500% before plunging by 99%.
Economou also owns homes in Connecticut, Greece, London, New York, St. Barts and Saint-Tropez, plus the luxury Armonia Residences south of Athens.

name: Zhang Jianzhong
about: Zhang Jianzhong is the chairman and CEO of Moore Threads Technology, a semiconductor maker that is vying to be the Nvidia of China.
He took the company public in Shanghai in December 2025, raising $1.1 billion.
Before founding Beijing-based Moore Threads in 2020, Zhang once led Nvidia's China business.
Moore Threads was added in 2023 to a U.S. trade blacklist, which prevents it from accessing advanced American chipmaking technologies.

name: Rakesh Gangwal
about: Airline veteran Rakesh Gangwal owes his fortune to InterGlobe Aviation, the parent outfit of budget airline IndiGo, India's largest by market share.
Gangwal started his airline career with United Airlines in 1984 and went on to run US Airways Group as its chief executive and chairman.
Gangwal cofounded IndiGo, headquartered outside Delhi, with Rahul Bhatia (also a billionaire) in 2006 with one aircraft.
The Miami resident resigned from the company's board in 2022 and said he would gradually sell his stock over the next five years.
Gangwal was named chairman of Southwest Airlines in November 2024. He resigned from that role in August 2025 but remains on the board.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School; Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology

did_you_know_facts: The Indian-born mechanical engineer studied at the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur before getting his M.B.A. at Wharton.
He and his wife paid $30 million for a Miami mansion that previously belonged to billionaire Charles Johnson.
Gangwal and IndiGo cofounder Bhatia had a bitter falling out in 2019 over corporate governance issues. Their dispute reached courts in London, Florida and Maryland.

name: Jeffrey Cheah
about: Jeffrey Cheah is the executive chairman of Malaysia's Sunway group. Over five decades, he transformed his obscure tin-mining company into a group with interests in property, healthcare, education and infrastructure.
Sunway Healthcare raised $736 million from its March 2026 IPO. It currently operates five hospitals, with three more in the pipeline.
In 2020, Sunway expanded into fintech, acquiring a 51% stake in credit reporting agency Credit Bureau Malaysia.
In February 2025, the group announced its plan to build a $578 million mixed-use project, along with Malaysia's state-owned commuter rail operator MTR, near the Singapore border.
His daughter, Sarena, and sons, Adrian and Evan, work in the family business.
did_you_know_facts: He is an avid philanthropist and has disbursed thousands of scholarships in Malaysia over the years.
He started his career as an accountant for an auto assembly plant.
Cheah received the ASEAN Entrepreneurial Excellence Award from EY for 2023.
quote: I believe that education is an extremely powerful tool, and we should never stop pursuing knowledge at all ages.

name: Richard Livingstone
about: Richard Livingstone, with his billionaire brother Ian, own properties throughout London including high-end shops, swanky hotels and tony apartments.
Among their signature projects is Panama Pacifico, a master planned city they're developing in Panama with Colombian billionaire Jaime Gilinski Bacal.
When finished, Panama Pacifico will include 20,000 residential properties, industrial parks and retail and commercial space.
Their real estate firm London & Regional operates hotels in L.A., Las Vegas and Miami.
The firm is also tapped to revitalize Albert Island, a 25-acre site between London's Royal Docks and the Thames River, into a mixed-use development.
did_you_know_facts: Their Panama Pacifico project sits on the former Howard Air Force Base -- the site where U.S. DEA agents arrested narco-dictator Manuel Noriega in 1990.
The sons of a dentist, Ian was a former optometrist and Richard, a chartered surveyor.

name: Ian Livingstone
about: Ian Livingstone, with his billionaire brother Richard, own properties throughout London including high-end shops, swanky hotels and tony apartments.
Among their signature projects is Panama Pacifico, a master planned city they're developing in Panama with Colombian billionaire Jaime Gilinski Bacal.
When finished, Panama Pacifico will include 20,000 residential properties, industrial parks and retail and commercial space.

The sons of a dentist, Ian was a former optometrist and Richard, a chartered surveyor.

name: Forrest Li
about: Stanford grad Forrest Li founded and runs online gaming and e-commerce firm Sea, which also has interests in e-payments and financial services.
Li entered the ranks of Singapore's richest after listing Sea on the New York Stock Exchange in 2017.
Sea has attracted investors such as Tencent, the Norwegian sovereign wealth fund, private equity firm General Atlantic and Malaysian billionaire Robert Kuok's son Kuok Khoon Hua.
In 2023, Sea booked its first-ever annual net profit since its IPO.
Sea has rolled out digital banking services in Southeast Asia, Taiwan and Brazil.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Stanford Graduate School of Business; Bachelor of Engineering, Shanghai Jiaotong University

did_you_know_facts: When a college tutor couldn't pronounce his Chinese name Xiaodong, Li adopted the name Forrest after watching the movie Forrest Gump.
Li used to work as a recruiter for Motorola in Shanghai.
In 2022, Sea shut down its Indian e-commerce unit, citing market uncertainties.
quote: We want to continually push the boundaries.

name: Thomas Tull
about: Former film financier and founder of production company Legendary Entertainment, Thomas Tull's biggest hits came from backing blockbusters.
In 2015, Tull inked a deal with Chinese billionaire Wang Jianlin's Wanda Group to sell Legendary for up to $3.5 billion in cash, stock and debt.
Tull stepped down as CEO of Legendary in 2016 to concentrate on his Tull Investment Group, which has invested in the likes of Magic Leap.
He rolled his firms Tulco, Acrisure, Teton Ridge, and both arms of USIT into a new joint venture, TWG Global, and owns shares in publicly-traded scrubs maker Figs and high-tech makeup company Oddity.
A sports fan, Tull owns minority stakes in the Pittsburgh Steelers and the New York Yankees along with a collection of baseball memorabilia.

personal_stats.label: Giving as a percentage of net worth

did_you_know_facts: Tull was born to a single mother in Binghamton, New York and grew up poor.
After attending Hamilton College on a football scholarship, Tull started a chain of laundries.

name: Park Hyeon-joo
about: Park Hyeon-joo founded Mirae Asset Global Investments (formerly called Mirae Asset Investment Advisory) and a venture capital affiliate in 1997.
He is known as the father of South Korea's mutual fund industry and launched the country's first closed-end mutual fund in 1998.
Now operating in 16 markets, his firm has approximately $272 billion in assets under management.
did_you_know_facts: The Mirae Asset Park Hyeon Joo Foundation provides scholarships to academically promising students from disadvantaged families.
In 2010, the Harvard Business School selected Mirae for a case study for its M.B.A. program.

name: Arkady Rotenberg
about: A friend of President Vladimir Putin, Arkady Rotenberg was once his judo sparring partner.
In the late 2000s Rotenberg became an owner of SGM Group and Mostotrest, now two of Russia's biggest construction contractors.
Both companies were targeted by EU sanctions in 2018 due to their participation in the construction of the Crimean bridge.
Rotenberg was also the target of U.S. and European sanctions in 2014.
In 2019 he sold SGM Group to a Gazprom subsidiary and agreed to transfer his shares of Mostotrest to a joint venture with state-owned Vnesheconombank.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts/Science, Leningrad Institute of Physical Culture

did_you_know_facts: An ice hockey fan, Rotenberg apparently still plays with Putin and is chairman of the executive board of Russian Ice Hockey Federation.
Rotenberg holds an indirect stake in Sheremetyevo Airport, near Moscow.
In 2021 Rotenberg called himself the owner of huge complex of buildings on the Black Sea coast, which Russian oppositionist Alexei Navalny called "Putin's palace."

name: Joao Moreira Salles
about: Joao Moreira Salles is a Brazilian documentary filmmaker and member of one of Brazil's oldest banking families.
His late father, Walther Moreira Salles, was the founder of Unibanco and a former ambassador to the United States.
In 2008 Unibanco merged with Itau, then Brazil's second-largest commercial bank, creating Itau-Unibanco, the largest bank in Latin America.
Moreira Salles and his three brothers, all billionaires, also own stakes in CBMM, the world's leading supplier of the mineral niobium.
did_you_know_facts: Moreira Salles' 2006 documentary Santiago won the Knight Grand Jury Prize for Documentary Features at the Miami International Film Festival.

name: Walther Moreira Salles Junior
about: Walther Moreira Salles Junior (also known as Walter Salles) is a Brazilian filmmaker and member of one of Brazil's oldest banking families.
His late father, Walther Moreira Salles, was the founder of Unibanco and a former ambassador to the United States.
In 2008 Unibanco merged with Itau, then Brazil's second-largest commercial bank, creating Itau-Unibanco, the largest bank in Latin America.
Moreira Salles and his three brothers, all billionaires, also own stakes in CBMM, the world's leading supplier of the mineral niobium.
Moreira Salles directed more than 20 films, including 'The Motorcycle Diaries' and 1998 Academy Award nominee 'Central Station.'

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Southern California

did_you_know_facts: His screenplay adaptation of Jack Kerouac's book On the Road, with Francis Ford Coppola producing, was nominated for the Palme d'Or at the 2012 Cannes Film Festival.

name: Murat Ulker
about: Murat Ulker owns 63% of Yildiz Holding, which produces a wide range of food products and non-alcoholic beverages.
Yildiz spent $850 million to buy Belgian chocolatier Godiva in 2007 and $3.2 billion to buy United Biscuits of the U.K. in 2014.
To establish a more global structure, he merged United Biscuit, Ulker Biscuit and DeMet's Candy under the roof of London-based Pladis Foods.
In early 2019, Godiva announced the sale of parts of its Asia-Pacific business, along with a production facility in Belgium, to PE firm MBK Partners.
Yildiz is using some of the proceeds from the sale to expand Godiva's cafe business from 20 stores to more than 2,000 globally by 2025.
did_you_know_facts: In 2020, Ulker handed over the chairmanship of Yildiz, which he'd held for 20 years, to his nephew Ali Ulker.
In 2014, Ulker donated $24 million to Harvard University. A research facility focused on genetic diseases is named after his father, Sabri Ulker.
quote: My name is Murat; I don't need any other title.

name: Sanjiv Bajaj
about: Sanjiv Bajaj is the son of the late Rahul Bajaj, who was chairman emeritus of the storied Bajaj Group until his death in February 2022.
The group was founded by their great-grandfather Jamnalal Bajaj, who set it up in 1926 and was a follower of Mahatma Gandhi.
Today, the Bajaj Group is a conglomerate of 40 companies in sectors such as two-wheelers, financial services and electrical appliances.
Sanjiv oversees the group's financial services business, which includes insurance.
In 2025, the family agreed to buy out Germant giant Allianz's stake In their two Indian Insurance joint ventures for $2.8 billion.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, Pune University; Master of Science in Engineering, The University of Warwick; Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School

did_you_know_facts: His older brother Rajiv is also a billionaire.
Sanjiv is keen about tennis and basketball.

name: Rajiv Bajaj
about: Rajiv Bajaj is the son of the late Rahul Bajaj, who was chairman emeritus of the storied Bajaj Group until his death in February 2022.
The group was founded by his great-grandfather Jamnalal Bajaj, who set it up in 1926 and was a follower of Mahatma Gandhi.
Today, the Bajaj Group is a conglomerate of 40 companies in sectors such as two-wheelers, financial services and electrical appliances.
Rajiv runs two-wheeler flagship Bajaj Auto.
In 2025, the family agreed to buy out Germant giant Allianz's stake In their two insurance joint ventures for $2.8 billion.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, Pune University; Master of Science in Engineering, The University of Warwick

did_you_know_facts: Rajiv is passionate about yoga and homeopathy.
His younger brother Sanjiv is also a billionaire.

name: Barry Diller
about: Barry Diller founded internet and media conglomerate IAC in 1995. He remains senior executive and chairman.
IAC owns print and digital publisher People Inc., website Care.com, The Daily Beast and equity stakes in companies such as MGM Resorts International and Turo.
Diller is also chairman of online travel giant Expedia, which acquired its holding company, Liberty Expedia, in a $2.6 billion deal in 2019.
Prior to founding IAC, he worked at ABC, Paramount and Fox and oversaw launches of hit TV shows including "Cheers" and "The Simpsons."
He built Pier 55 -- named "Little Island" -- a park and performance venue in the Hudson River that opened in spring of 2021.
He is married to designer Diane Von Furstenberg and owns an estimated third of her eponymous fashion company.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Drop Out, University of California, Los Angeles

did_you_know_facts: Diller never graduated from college and got a job in the mail room at William Morris talent agency.
Diller is the owner of the EOS yacht, one of the largest private sailing yachts in the world.
quote: What I really do think it takes [to have a successful communication tool, is] rolling out new product, and if that new product is good and appealing, then you'll more than likely survive and probably thrive.

name: Joesley Batista
about: Joesley Batista is one of two billionaire brothers who control publicly traded JBS S.A., one of the world's largest meat processing companies.
Their father, Jose Batista Sobrinho, started the business with a small butcher shop in Anapolis, in central Brazil. It grew by acquiring slaughterhouses in the region.
Joesley and his brother Wesley took control of JBS in the 2000s, leading to its 2007 acquisition of U.S. pork and beef processor Swift & Co. for $225 million.
He led the international expansion of JBS and and its main agricultural business, which became one of the biggest in Brazil.
In 2017 Joesley was arrested as part of a large Brazilian bribery probe and reportedly held for six months.
In May 2017, the brothers agreed to pay a $3.2 billion fine to Brazilian authorities because of their role in a large corruption scandal.

name: Wesley Batista
about: Wesley Batista is one of two billionaire brothers who control publicly traded JBS S.A., one of the world's largest meat processing companies.
Their father, Jose Batista Sobrinho, founded a small butcher shop in central Brazil in 1953. It grew by acquiring slaughterhouses in the region.
Wesley and his brother Joesley took control in the 2000s, leading JBS's 2007 acquisition of U.S. pork and beef processor Swift & Co. for $225 million.
His son, Wesley Batista Filho, became a director in the company's U.S. division in May 2023.
In 2017 Wesley was arrested as part of a large Brazilian bribery probe and reportedly held for six months.
In May 2017, the brothers agreed to pay a $3.2 billion fine to Brazilian authorities to atone for their role in a large corruption scandal.

name: Scott Cook
about: Scott Cook is the cofounder of financial software giant Intuit, known for products like QuickBooks, TurboTax and Mint.
The Harvard Business School grad worked for Procter & Gamble and Bain before launching Intuit in 1983.
He stepped down as CEO in 1994, but remains chairman of the $16.3 billion (fiscal 2024 sales) company and has a 2.7% stake.
Cook and his wife are big supporters of education and have donated millions to universities and are impact investors in several ed-tech funds.
Cook was planning to get a Ph.D. in economics but decided to pursue business after successfully turning his defunct college ski club into the biggest in the state.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Southern California; Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School

did_you_know_facts: Cook was an early investor in Snapchat. He met cofounder Evan Spiegel after giving a guest lecture at Stanford.
Scott's son Karl Cook is a professional equestrian.
quote: Dig for feedback on yourself. I did not do this. When I started work I waited for my boss to give me feedback -- which is the moral equivalent of taking the steering wheel for your life and handing it to someone else.

name: Michel Leclercq & family
about: Michel Leclercq set up a small sporting goods store called Decathlon in 1976.
It's now one of the world's largest athletic retailers with more than $16.5 billion in sales from more than 1,700 stores in 60 countries.
Leclercq is cousin of Gerard Mulliez, the patriarch of the famed French retail dynasty behind Auchan department stores.
Leclerq and his immediate family own approximately 40% of the company; the extended Mulliez family own about 40% as well.

name: Joseph Grendys
about: Joseph Grendys runs Koch Foods, a poultry processor that slaughters, ships and sells chicken under its own brands and through private label products.
The $5 billion (estimated revenues) business makes buffalo wings and chicken strips for Walmart and nuggets for Burger King.
Grendys joined Koch in the mid-1980s after graduating from Loyola University, lured by a 50% equity offer from original owner Fred Koch.
At the time it was just a one-room shop with 13 employees, and its main business was taking bones out of chicken and cutting up the meat.
Grendys bought out his former boss in 1992 and vertically integrated the company by gobbling up smaller feed mills and slaughterhouses.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Loyola University Chicago

did_you_know_facts: Grendys still lives in the modest Chicago split-level home where he grew up.
Its Morton, Mississippi, plant was one of five poultry processors targeted by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in August 2019.
In 2019, ICE arrested 234 Koch Foods workers, who the company said had passed the government's E-Verify program, for potentially working without legal documentation.

name: Nicolas D'Ieteren
about: Nicolas D'Ieteren chairs the Belgium-based D'Ieteren Group.
The Group's portfolio includes five businesses ranging from automobile distribution to real estate and glass repair.
The Group owns D'Ieteren Auto, which exclusively distributes Volkswagen, Audi, Lamborghini, Bugatti and Porsche in Belgium.
The business has been in the family for six generations; it was founded in 1805 by Jean-Joseph D'Ieteren.
did_you_know_facts: The D'Ieteren Gallery in Belgium showcases 200 years of vehicles with D'Ieteren parts, ranging from horse carriages to modern luxury cars.
In 2016, the Group acquired the lifestyle brand, Moleskine, in a deal that valued the notebook-focused brand at around $572 million.

name: Josh Kushner
about: Josh Kushner founded and runs VC firm Thrive Capital, which has backed some of the past decade's most notable startups, including Instagram, Spotify, Stripe and OpenAI.
Thrive was valued at $5.3 billion in a $175 million funding round in January 2023; Kushner is estimated to own a 66% stake.
Thrive's investors include Disney CEO Bob Iger and a handful of billionaires: Henry Kravis, Mukesh Ambani, Jorge Paulo Lemann and Xavier Niel.
Thrive raised $5 billion for its ninth fund in August 2024; the firm now manages approximately $25 billion in assets.
The liberal Kushner cofounded a health insurance company built around Obamacare before his brother Jared's father-in-law Donald Trump became president.
He is the son of real estate tycoon Charles Kushner, who became Trump's ambassador to France in May 2025.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Harvard; Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School

did_you_know_facts: Kushner purchased a 2.5% stake in the NBA's Memphis Grizzlies in 2019.
Thrive's headquarters are in NYC's Puck Building, owned by the Kushner family, where Josh and his wife, model Karlie Kloss, also live in a penthouse.
quote: There are three ways to make a return. You can create something no one else has created. You can discover something before anyone else. Or access something that very few can.

name: Saban Cemil Kazanci
about: Saban Cemil Kazanci is the largest shareholder of Kazancı Holding, one of Turkey's largest energy companies.
The $3.6 billion (revenue) company operates across the energy industry, including electricity generation and distribution, natural gas distribution and generator production.
His billionaire father, Ali Metin Kazanci, started the energy business in 1968 with the Watt Electric Motor Factory and serves as its chariman.
Kazancı Holding expanded its tourism business in the city of Bodrum, in 2022, with the 5-star Mirada Exclusive Hotel. It currently owns four hotels.

name: Andrei Kozitsyn
about: Until 2022 Andrei Kozitsyn was CEO of Ural Mining Metallurgical Company (UMMC), one of the top Russian producers of such commodities as copper, zinc, coal and gold.
Kozitsyn grew up in the Urals, where he studied metallurgy and later went to work as a mechanic at Uralelectromed, now UMMC's main factory.
Kozitsyn cofounded UMMC with Iskander Makhmudov, who was the group's president and his longtime partner.
In January 2019, UMMC opened the Korova (Cow) restaurant in the elite district of Yekaterinburg.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Ural Polytechnic Institute

did_you_know_facts: President and sponsor of KHL hockey club named Avtomobilist, Kozitsyn plans to build an ice arena with 15,000 seats in Ekaterinburg in 2024.
Kozitsyn founded Military Equipment Museum, which has tanks and armored vehicles and planes.

name: Hortensia Herrero
about: Hortensia Herrero owns nearly 28% of Mercadona, the Spanish supermarket chain she helped build with her husband Juan Roig (also a billionaire).
Herrero, who serves as vice president, was part of the group that bought the company from Roig's father back in 1981, when it had 8 small stores.
Herrero and Roig's four daughters are board members of Mercadona; Roig's brother Fernando is also a shareholder and billionaire.
Mercadona, which is privately owned, has about 1,700 stores, mostly in Spain, and employs 110,000 people.
The company shares 25% of its pretax profit with employees.
did_you_know_facts: She met Juan Roig at the University of Valencia, where both studied economics.
Herrero has spent at least $10 million to restore historic Valencia, Spain, where she and Roig live.

name: Shaul Shani
about: Shaul Shani is an Israeli investor who sold Brazilian firm Global Village Telecom to Vivendi for $4.5 billion in 2009; his take was $1.4 billion.
He has since increased his fortune via mezzanine lending and investments in emerging economies.
Starting in the 1980s, he cofounded three companies; two of them, Oshap Technologies and Tecnomatix, were acquired for $210 million and $228 million.
In 2014, Shani took control of Israeli communications equipment maker ECI Telecom; he agreed to sell to publicly traded Ribbon Communications in 2019.
In 2021, Shani became chairman of Rashi, one of Israel's largest charities.

name: Isaac Perlmutter
about: Isaac "Ike" Perlmutter beat out fellow billionaire Carl Icahn for control of bankrupt comic book firm Marvel in 1998.
He revived the company's stock by producing action-hero movies like 'Spiderman,' 'Daredevil,' 'Hulk' and 'Iron Man.'
In 2009, he sold a majority of Marvel to Disney for $4 billion in cash and stock; he served as chairman until Disney laid him off in 2023.
Perlmutter immigrated to the U.S. from Israel with just $250 in 1967 and sold toys on the streets of Brooklyn, where he was introduced to Marvel.
He and his wife have donated over $50 million to cancer research at NYU Langone Medical Center.
did_you_know_facts: Perlmutter is a veteran of the Six-Day War in 1967 between Israel and neighboring states Egypt, Jordan and Syria.
The reclusive billionaire is rarely spotted in public and reportedly went to the 2008 premiere of the movie 'Iron Man' disguised in glasses and a mustache.

name: Dan Kurzius
about: Dan Kurzius founded what later became Mailchimp with Ben Chestnut in 2001 as a side project to their web design company.
Mailchimp's email marketing software for small businesses garnered enough customers that in 2007 they committed to it full time.
Wary of giving up control to outside investors, Kurzius and Chestnut bootstrapped growth from profits and took no outside money.
In September 2021, Intuit announced it would acquire Mailchimp in a $12 billion cash and stock acquisition.
At the time of announcement, Chestnut and Kurzius each owned 50% of the Atlanta-based company, which had $800 million in 2020 revenue.
did_you_know_facts: Kurzius was a part-time DJ and competitive skateboarder before getting into web design.
The two cofounders met when Chestnut hired Kurzius to work at Cox Interactive Media's dot-com era MP3 music service.

name: Wen-Ta Hsieh
about: Wen-Ta Hsieh is the chairman of Hon. Precision, a maker of testing equipment for advanced chips.
The company takes up a third of the market for IC test handlers, which sort and move integrated circuits during final testing.
It supplies global semiconductor heavyweights such as TSMC and Nvidia.
Hsieh set up Hon. Precision's predecessor in 1999. He took the company public on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in November 2025.

name: Lim Hariyanto Wijaya Sarwono
about: Lim and his family own a majority stake in Singapore-listed palm oil producer Bumitama Agri; its plantations are located in Indonesia.
His son Lim Gunawan Hariyanto is CEO of the family's Harita Group.
Harita Group also owns the majority of listed bauxite mining firm Cita Mineral Investindo. Lim's integrated nickel processing company Trimegah Bangun Persada raised $650 million in a 2023 IPO.
Lim's father emigrated from China to East Kalimantan and reportedly opened a grocery store in 1915.
His daughter Christina is executive director of Bumitama Agri.

personal_stats.label: Source of Wealth
personal_stats.value: Palm oil, nickel mining, Self Made

did_you_know_facts: The family group's name Harita comes from Lim Hariyanto and wife Rita.
Lim started pursuing higher education in his late 60s, and obtained a doctoral degree in business administration from Shanghai Jiao Tong University in 2005 at age 77.

name: Jiang Rensheng & family
about: Jiang Rensheng is the chairman of Shenzhen-listed vaccine firm Chongqing Zhifei Biological Products.
A longtime distribution partner of Merck, Zhifei won the Chinese sales rights to the U.S. pharma's HPV drug in 2018.
In 2023, Jiang took his antibody drug maker Chongqing Genrix Biopharmaceutical public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.
Prior to striking out on his own, he worked as a primary school teacher and a government health official.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Associate in Arts/Science, Guilin Medical University

name: Miao Hangen
about: Miao Hangen chairs Eastern Shenghong, a Shenzhen-listed petrochemical and new material firm.
Its parent Shenghong Group, which also has interests in textile and new energy, was founded in 1992.
The group broke ground on a $4.2 billion plant for energy storage system batteries in Zhangjiagang, Jiangsu in July 2023.

name: Jamshyd Godrej
about: Jamshyd Godrej is chairman of the Godrej Enterprises Group, a conglomerate in Mumbai, which he controls with his sister, Smita Crishna-Godrej, also a billionaire.
The flagship of the Godrej Enterprises Group is privately held consumer goods giant Godrej & Boyce, which makes everything from locks to refrigerators.
His niece Nyrika Holkar is an executive director.at Godrej & Boyce and tipped to succeed him.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Illinois Institute of Technology

did_you_know_facts: He is the cousin of the Godrej clan's billionaire patriarch Adi Godrej.
A U.S.-trained mechanical engineer, Jamshyd is a keen sailor.

name: Smita Crishna Godrej
about: Smita Crishna-Godrej hails from the storied Godrej clan and controls the Godrej Enterprises Group, along with her brother Jamshyd Godrej.
In 2024, the siblings and their cousins Adi and Nadir Godrej divided the family's business empire into two separate business groups.
The flagship of the Godrej Enterprises Group is privately held consumer goods giant Godrej & Boyce, which makes everything from locks to refrigerators.
Their biggest asset is a 3,400-acre land parcel in suburban Mumbai.
While Jamshyd Godrej is chairperson of the newly carved group, her daughter Nyrika Holkar is tipped to succeed him.

name: Markus Blocher
about: Markus Blocher is a billionaire thanks to two Swiss chemical companies, EMS-Chemie and Dottikon ES Holding.
Blocher got his start working at EMS-Chemie, the Swiss polymer and chemical manufacturer that his family has run for decades.
He received a stake in the firm when his father, Christoph Blocher, sold his shares to his children to take a seat on the Swiss federal council.
Markus eventually sold his shares in EMS-Chemie and took over Dottikon, its spinoff.

name: George Lucas
about: 'Star Wars' creator George Lucas has largely retired from filmmaking since he sold his Lucasfilm to Disney in 2012 for $4.1 billion in stock and cash.
Lucas is now focused on philanthropy: his charitable family foundation has more than $1 billion in assets.
Lucas attended junior college in his hometown of Modesto, California where his parents ran a stationary store, before attending USC.
He founded Lucasfilm, his production company, in 1971 and built his fortune through his movies and their merchandise.
The Lucas Museum of Narrative Art will open in Los Angeles in 2026 and is entirely funded by Lucas and his wife, Mellody Hobson.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Southern California

did_you_know_facts: Lucas worked as a production assistant on Francis Ford Coppola's 1968 film 'Finian's Rainbow.'
When Lucas needed special effects for 'Star Wars,' he started his own special effects company, Industrial Light & Magic, in 1975.

name: Anthony von Mandl
about: Anthony von Mandl created the ready-to-drink alcoholic beverages White Claw Hard Seltzer and Mike's Hard Lemonade through his Mark Anthony Brands.
Forbes estimates von Mandl's U.S. business generated around $3.6 billion in revenue in 2025, based on analyst estimates.
He began his career in the Canadian wine business as an importer in the 1970s at age 22.
He currently owns six wineries in Canada, including Mission Hill Winery in British Columbia's Okanagan Valley.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of British Columbia

did_you_know_facts: Von Mandl's spirits portfolio includes Ireland's top end Glendalough Whiskey & Gin Distillery.
In 2016, von Mandl was appointed as an Officer of the Order of Canada, the country's highest civilian honor.
Von Mandl got his start selling wine out of his car's trunk in Vancouver.

name: Georg Nemetschek & family
about: Georg Nemetschek is the founder and deputy chairman of publicly traded German software company Nemetschek Group.
He started using design software in his own engineering office in the late 1960s, long before computers became available for personal use.
The company, which serves the architecture, engineering and construction industries, went public in 1999 and has annual revenue of about 1 billion euros.
Nemetschek Group expanded into 3D animation and motion design, securing access to the media industry. Its software has around six million users.
In 2020, Georg launched the Nemetschek Innovation Foundation to support scientific research and artificial intelligence in the construction industry.
did_you_know_facts: In 1971, he was appointed as a professor at the Munich University of Applied Sciences. He served as dean of the Civil Engineering department from 1977 to 1996.
His son Ralf is chairman of the family's Nemetschek foundation, founded in 2007 to strengthen democracy in Germany.
quote: The success of Nemetschek SE cannot only be credited to our personal performance, but also to the competence of our staff and the political and social environment in the German Federal Republic, which has safeguarded a framework of entrepreneurship.

name: Zarakh Iliev
about: Zarakh Iliev and his longtime partner God Nisanov are building trade centers, hotels and residential property in Moscow.
The pair, who moved to Moscow from Azerbaijan, own roughly 14 million of square feet of real estate in Moscow.
The partners developed a 225-acre wholesale distribution center, Food City, in Moscow and also several shopping centers on Moscow's outskirts.
Ililev is co-owner of 5- star Moscow Royal Radisson hotel, which served as FIFA's headquarters during the World Cup 2018 in Russia.
In September 2022 a real estate mogul Iliev was hit with U.K. sanctions in the wake of Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
did_you_know_facts: The son of a shoemaker, Iliev helped make shoes as a child.
Iliev and his partner God Nisanov were born and grew up in Krasnaya Sloboda village in Azerbaijan.

name: God Nisanov
about: God Nisanov and his partner Zarakh Iliev, who came to Moscow from Azerbaijan, own roughly 14 million of square feet of real estate in Moscow.
The partners developed a 225-acre wholesale distribution center, Food City, in Moscow and also several shopping centers on Moscow's outskirts.
In 2022 a real estate mogul Nisanov was hit with U.S. and U.K. sanctions in the wake of Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
did_you_know_facts: Nisanov knows six foreign languages, including Arabic, Turkish and Farsi.
Vladimir Putin's classmate Ilgam Ragimov, who was a minority shareholder in several projects, transferred his shares to his son-in-law Araz Mekhdiev.
quote: We never stood in the way of somebody's business and we do not like it if someone stands in the way of our business. We can help. And this we do quite often.

name: Pyotr Aven
about: Pyotr Aven is a co-owner of Alfa Bank and LetterOne along with Mikhail Fridman, Khan and fellow billionaires Alexei Kuzmichev and Andrei Kosogov.
Aven and his partners were all sanctioned by the EU and U.K. in February and March 2022; Aven stepped down from LetterOne's board in March.
He grew up in Moscow, graduated from Moscow State University, and worked at the Institute for Systems Studies at the Soviet Academy of Sciences.
In 1989 he went to work at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; two years later he was tapped to be Putin's minister of foreign economic relations.
Aven was president of Russia's largest privately held bank, Alfa-Bank, which was hit with sanctions in April 2022, from 1994 to 2011.
did_you_know_facts: Aven now owns the largest private collection of Russian art.
quote: In the early 90s, it was crucial to be able to be friends, to build relationships. The role of informal relationships is very important in Russia in general, it definitely means much more here than in the West.

name: Fernand Huts
about: Fernand Huts controls Katoen Natie, an Antwerp-based logistics business with more than 350 companies worldwide that employs 20,000 People.
Huts, who collects archeological textiles, is also involved in politics and was elected to the Belgian parliament in 1995.
Over time, Huts bought out 19 partners to assume control of the company.
In 2005, Huts grouped all its activities under Luxembourg-based KN Holding.
did_you_know_facts: He once paid more than five million euros for the skeleton of a Tyrannosaurus Rex.

name: Rupert Johnson Jr
about: Rupert Johnson Jr. is the vice chairman of Franklin Resources, a global investment management firm also called Franklin Templeton Investments.
He is the largest shareholder in the firm with 20%. His half brother Charles, who chaired the company until 2013, is a close second.
Their father, Rupert Sr., founded Franklin Distributors in 1947; the business grew and went public in 1983.
Rupert Jr. joined in 1965 and has been vice chairman since 1999. His nephew Gregory Johnson now serves as chairman.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Washington & Lee University

did_you_know_facts: His father Rupert named the company after Benjamin Franklin who he believed epitomized the ideas of frugality and prudence in regard to saving and investing.
Rupert pledged $100 million to his alma mater, Washington and Lee University, in 2007, $85 million of which has been designated for scholarships.

name: Cui Lixin
about: Cui Lixin is the chairman of aluminum smelter Chuangxin Industries Holdings.
He took the Inner Mongolia-based firm public in Hong Kong in November 2025, raising $706 million.
Cui is also the chairman of Shanghai-listed Innovation New Material Technology, an aluminum product maker that counts Foxconn as one of its customers.
The mogul worked for almost two decades at various government-affiliated companies before striking out on his own.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts/Science, Central South University

name: Frank Wang
about: The world's first drone billionaire, Frank Wang is the founder and chairman of DJI, China's biggest seller of civil drones with over two-thirds market share.
Wang founded DJI in 2006 and ran it out of his dorm room at Hong Kong University of Science & Technology.
DJI is best known for its Phantom Drones, which retail for around $1,000.
DJI made a list of "Chinese military companies operating in the United States" published by the U.S. Department of Defense in 2022.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology; Master of Science, Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

did_you_know_facts: The son of a teacher turned small-business owner, Wang spent most of his childhood reading about model airplanes.
When he was 16, Wang got a remote-controlled helicopter after getting high marks on an exam. He promptly crashed it and had to wait months for replacement parts.

name: Tim Sweeney
about: Tim Sweeney is cofounder and CEO of Epic Games, the developer behind Fortnite, one of the world's most popular video games.
Epic raised $2 billion in 2022 from Sony and the family office of the clan behind Lego in a funding round that valued the company at $31.5 billion.
In 2024, Epic raised $1.5 billion from Disney in a funding round that valued the company at $22.5 billion.
Epic had been battling Apple in court over app store fees since 2020, when Sweeney conceded defeat in 2024 in what he called "a sad outcome for all developers."
Epic Games paid $520 million to settle FTC allegations of privacy violations and unwanted charges in 2022.
The company is the creator of the Unreal Engine, one of the most used game development tool kits for other studios.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Maryland, College Park

did_you_know_facts: Sweeney is an active land conservationist in North Carolina, where he has purchased about 60,000 acres of forest land to keep it from being developed.
In 2021, Sweeney pledged 7,500 acres in North Carolina's Roan Highlands to the Southern Appalachian Highlands Conservancy.

name: Reinhold Schmieding
about: Michigan native Reinhold Schmieding started Arthrex, an orthopedic surgical tools company, in 1981 in Munich, Germany.
Arthrex is now headquartered in Naples, Florida and has developed over 13,000 products used in shoulder, hip and other orthopedic surgeries.
Privately-held Arthrex has estimated revenues of $3.2 billion; Schmieding owns an estimated 95% of the company.
Schmieding is the son of German immigrants who moved to the U.S. just before he was born. His father, a dentist, wanted him to be a doctor.
The notoriously press-shy founder has kept his $50 drafting table where he designed his first operating instruments.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Michigan State University

did_you_know_facts: The company logo, an "X" formed by a tiny arthroscope and a grasper, was originally sketched by Schmieding.
Schmieding is an avid fisherman, and was recruited to Michigan State to play golf.

name: Qiu Jianping & family
about: Qiu Jianping is the chairman of Hangzhou GreatStar Industrial, one of Asia's largest hand tool manufacturers.
Qiu took the plunge as an entrepreneur at age 30 after he was dissatisfied with his wage at a state-owned company.
He founded GreatStar Holding Group in 1993, which today also has interests in tires, forklifts, diesel engines and robotics.
The Group's subsidiary Zhongce Rubber Group, China's largest tire maker by sales, went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in June 2025.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Xi'an Jiaotong University

name: Cho Tak Wong
about: Cho Tak Wong is the founder of Fuyao Glass Industry Group, one of Asia's largest manufacturers of auto glass that counts Audi, Fiat and Ford among its customers.
He stepped down as chairman in October 2025, citing reasons including the need to sustainably develop the company's governance structure.
His son, Tso Fai, is the new chairman.
Cho is also known for his philanthropic causes. His Heren Charitable Foundation pledged in 2021 $1.6 billion to build the Fuyao University of Science and Technology in China.
The university plans to enroll students in late 2025.
did_you_know_facts: Cho's hobbies include golfing and collecting art.

name: Ryan Cohen
about: Ryan Cohen is the former CEO of online pets supplies store Chewy, which he cofounded in 2011.
Cohen grew the business to $3.5 billion in annual revenues and stepped down in 2018 after selling it to PetSmart for $3.4 billion in 2017.
At the end of 2020, Cohen spent about $76 million buying a 13% stake in GameStop while urging management to restructure the ailing brick-and-mortar.
He joined GameStop's board in January 2021 and his fortune surged that month after Reddit traders coordinated a massive surge in the stock's price.
The son of a teacher and a glassware importer, Cohen started his first business at the age of 15, collecting fees off referrals to e-commerce sites.
did_you_know_facts: Cohen owns around seven million shares in the embattled Chinese tech firm Alibaba.
In 2022, Cohen bought?and then quickly sold?Bed Bath & Beyond stock for a $70 million profit.

name: Eric Lefkofsky
about: Eric Lefkofsky made his fortune from the daily deals site Groupon, which he founded in 2008 with Andrew Mason and longtime business partner Brad Keywell.
Lefkofsky founded and now runs healthcare startup Tempus, which uses data to improve cancer treatment.
Tempus went public at a $6 billion valuation in 2024, his fourth IPO.
Together Lefkofsky and Keywell also founded VC firm Lightbank, which has made investments in over 100 companies, including social media firm Sprout Social.
Lefkofsky grew up outside of Detroit and went to the University of Michigan for his undergraduate and law degrees.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctor of Jurisprudence, University of Michigan; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Michigan

did_you_know_facts: Lefkofsky and Keywell owned stakes in the Wrigley Building located on Chicago's Magnificent Mile but sold them in 2018.
After a girlfriend dumped him in college, Lefkofsky started his first business, selling carpets. He estimates he generated hundreds of thousands of dollars in sales.
quote: In my adult life, I've started five companies. I've basically had five good ideas in 20 years.

name: Robert Faith
about: Bob Faith is the founder, chairman and CEO of global real estate firm Greystar, active in property and investment management and development services.
Based in Charleston, South Carolina, the firm manages and operates $320 billion in real estate across five continents.
Greystar also has an investment management platform with more than $78 billion of assets under management.
After studying petroleum engineering at the University of Oklahoma and an MBA at Harvard, Faith got a job at real estate developer Trammell Crow Co.
He became a partner in 1988 before leaving in 1991 to start investment firm Starwood Capital Partners with his Harvard classmate Barry Sternlicht.
Faith then ventured out on his own in 1993, when he founded Greystar in Houston, Texas.

forbes_list.list: The Richest Person In Every State (2025)

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, University of Oklahoma; Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School

did_you_know_facts: Faith served as the South Carolina Secretary of Commerce from 2002 to 2006.

name: Ion Stoica
about: Ion Stoica is cofounder and executive chairman of software startup Databricks, which private investors valued at $134 billion in February.
He served as the original CEO from its inception in 2013 until early 2016, when he ceded the position to cofounder Ali Ghodsi.
Prior to Databricks, Stoica cofounded video streaming startup Conviva. He is also a UC Berkeley computer science professor.
Stoica cofounded Databricks alongside six UC Berkeley academics who had built the popular data analytics engine Apache Spark.
Databricks is built on top of the Apache Spark framework and uses AI to help companies store and utilize their data.

name: Matei Zaharia
about: Matei Zaharia is cofounder and chief technology officer of software startup Databricks, which private investors valued at $134 billion in February.
He is the mastermind behind popular analytics engine Apache Spark, which was conceived when he was a 24-year-old Ph.D. student at UC Berkeley.
Spark set a world record for speed of data sorting in 2014 and won Zaharia an award for the year's best computer science dissertation.
In 2013, Zaharia and six UC Berkeley collaborators cofounded Databricks, whose software is built on top of Spark.
He has led development on multiple new, AI-powered features beyond Spark.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Ph.D, University of California, Berkeley; Bachelor of Science, University of Waterloo

quote: Our group was one of the first to look at how to make it easy to work with very large data sets for people whose main interest in life is not software engineering.

name: Catherine Commisso & family
about: Catherine Commisso is the owner of Mediacom, a New York-based cable company founded by her husband Rocco Commisso. He died in January 2026 at age 76.
Rocco Commisso founded Mediacom to focus on smaller, underserved communities, and grew it into America's fifth-largest cable TV provider.
Catherine is also the owner of Italian Serie A soccer team Fiorentina.

name: Haryanto Tjiptodihardjo
about: Haryanto Tjiptodihardjo runs listed Impack Pratama Industri, founded in 1981 by his father Handojo.
Headquartered in Jakarta, the company is the country's largest maker of polymer-based roofs by market share and produces other construction materials such as floorboard and pipes.
It also operates manufacturing sites in Australia, Malaysia, New Zealand and Vietnam.
Haryanto joined the company in 1986 after graduating with an MBA degree from Woodbury University in the U.S.
Haryanto sold his privately held Mulford Holdings, an Australia-based plastic sheets maker, to Impack Pratama Industri for 808 billion rupiah ($53 million) in June 2024 to boost the latter's revenue.

name: Arturo Moreno
about: Arturo Moreno is the owner of the Los Angeles Angels baseball team, which he bought in 2003 for $184 million. It is now worth about $2.75 billion.
Moreno's initial fortune came from billboard advertising company Outdoor Systems, which he sold to Infinity Broadcasting in 1999 for $8.3 billion.
He has stakes in other billboard advertising companies, as well as commercial real estate holdings throughout Phoenix.
Moreno's $325 million plan to develop a new Angels baseball stadium was scuttled in 2022, by Anaheim's City Council.
A few months later, Moreno announced he intended to sell the Angels to the highest bidder but later changed his mind.

forbes_list.list: The Richest Person In Every State (2023)

personal_stats.label: Source of Wealth
personal_stats.value: Billboards, Los Angeles Angels, Self Made

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Arizona

did_you_know_facts: The oldest of 11 children, Moreno was drafted into the Vietnam War before attending the University of Arizona on the G.I. Bill.
When Moreno bought the Angels, he became the first Mexican-American to own a major league sports team.
quote: There's two types of education. One where you learn by a book, and you're taught, and the other one is a baseball bat. Every time you make a mistake somebody comes and hits you in the back of the head.

name: Joy Alukkas
about: Son of a jewelry store owner and school dropout, Joy Alukkas went to the Middle East to open the family's first overseas store in 1987 in Abu Dhabi.
He broke off to launch his own jewellery chain, which now has 100 outlets spread across India and 60 overseas.
His other interests include a money exchange outfit, malls and real estate.
Alukkas' son John Paul is managing director of the international jewelry business.
Alukkas decided to postpone the public listing of the jewelry business in 2023 citing a tepid IPO market.
did_you_know_facts: In 1956, Alukkas' father, Varghese Alukkas, opened the first jewellery store in the family's home town of Thrissur.
Joyalukkas uses Bollywood stars as brand ambassadors.
Joy Alukkas's wife Jolly Joy heads the Joyalukkas Foundation.
Joy Alukkas' autobiography, "Spreading Joy," was released in 2023.
quote: Mobile phones and motorbikes have no resale value, but jewelry is worth it.

name: Lee Yeow Chor
about: Lee Yeow Chor inherited stakes in IOI group, a palm oil and property empire built by his father Lee Sin Cheng.
He and his brother Lee Yeow Seng run the group.
Lee Yeow Chor is group managing director and chief executive of IOI Corporation, the main listed arm.
He holds a law degree from King's College, London.
His brother Lee Yeow Seng, who also studied law, is the CEO of IOI Properties.
did_you_know_facts: The late Lee grew up on a rubber plantation where his father ran a Chinese food shop.

name: Stephen Feinberg
about: Stephen Feinberg cofounded private equity firm Cerberus Capital Management in 1992.
Under Feinberg's leadership, Cerberus has generated some excellent returns, and some abysmal PR.
The firm attracted negative attention in 2013 for its stake in Freedom Group, which manufactured the rifle used in the Sandy Hook massacre.
Cerberus has recently achieved more success with its investment in grocery chain Albertsons and its global real estate funds.
Feinberg was sworn in as President Trump's deputy secretary of defense in March 2025.

name: Chandru Raheja
about: One of four brothers of a property family, Chandru Raheja ventured out on his own in 1996.
Today his privately held K. Raheja Corp. is one of Mumbai's leading developers and is run by his sons Neel and Ravi.
Raheja is known for its IT parks, hotels, malls and department store chain, Shoppers Stop.
His Chalet Hotels, which owns a string of hotels such as the J.W. Marriott in Mumbai and the Westin in Hyderabad, was listed in 2019.
In 2020, Raheja listed part of his commercial properties, co-owned with private equity firm Blackstone, under the Mindspace Business Parks REIT.

name: Mike Brown & family
about: Mike Brown and his family own the NFL's Cincinnati Bengals, which Forbes valued at more than $5 billion in 2025.
He helped his father, Paul, found the team in 1967 after the elder Brown was fired as the Cleveland Browns coach in 1963.
Several members of the Brown family are involved with the team today, including Mike's daughter Katie, who was the first woman to be named to the NFL's Competition Committee.

name: Bert Beveridge
about: Bert "Tito" Beveridge is the founder of Tito's Vodka, one of the fastest growing spirits brands in America.
Beveridge started the company in 1997 with $90,000 borrowed using 19 credit cards. He slept on floors and couches while he built the business.
Tito's got its first big break after winning the 2001 World Spirits Competition in San Francisco against 72 vodkas from around the world.
The company is estimated to have sold more than 12 million cases of vodka in 2024.
Tito's says it donates the net proceeds from its online store to nonprofits.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Texas at Austin

did_you_know_facts: Beveridge grew up comfortably in San Antonio, where he played polo. As a youngster he wanted to pursue a career training horses.
After graduating from college with degrees in geology and geophysics, Beveridge started working in the oil and gas business.
quote: If someone tells me my brand isn't a craft-distilled spirit because it's too big, I just say, 'I make it the same way I've always made it. I just have a lot more stills.'

name: Stephen Mandel Jr
about: One of Julian Robertson's "Tiger Cubs," Stephen Mandel started his hedge fund firm, Lone Pine Capital, in 1997.
Mandel stepped back from managing investments for Lone Pine Capital in January 2019 but remains a managing director.
Mandel built up a reputation as one of the hedge fund industry's best when it comes to fundamental analysis and bottom-up stock picking.
Mandel has poured hundreds of millions into his Zoom Foundation. The hedge fund also has its Lone Pine Foundation.
He is a big donor to charter schools and sits on the national board of directors of Teach for America.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Dartmouth College; Diploma, Phillips Academy Exeter; Master of Business Administration, Harvard University

did_you_know_facts: Mandel donates to the Environmental Defense Fund, of which he is a board trustee.
Mandel named Lone Pine Capital after a pine tree that, legend has it, survived a lightning strike on the campus of Dartmouth College in 1887.
quote: If you can manage a classroom and inspire kids, it's going to be a hard thing for you to do, but it's just unbelievable preparation for anything you're going to do in life.

name: Lorinc Meszaros
about: Lőrinc Meszaros founded a small gas-fitting company in Felcsut, the hometown of Prime Minister Viktor Orban, in 1990.
Orban, who founded the Ferenc Puskas Football Academy, tapped Meszaros to be its president.
Meszaros' gas-fitting company, Meszaros & Meszaros, is now a big player in the construction market thanks to contracts from the government.
quote: That I have been able to come so far, God, luck and the person of Viktor Orb?n have certainly played a role.

name: Nikolai Buinov
about: Nikolay Buinov is the main shareholder of Irkutsk oil company, the largest independent private oil company in Russia.
Buinov got his start with a timber company in the early 1990s.
In 1995, Buinov and his father founded Bodaibo energy company, which supplied fuel and lubricants to gold miners in the north of Irkutsk in Siberia.
Buinov purchased the license for an oil field in 1997, which was the start of what would become Irkutsk Oil Company.
Buinov sold a stake in IOC to the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) in 2008; EBRD later sold part of its stake to Goldman Sachs.
In 2022 Goldman Sachs sold its stake in IOC to Buinov and his partners.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Leningrad Institute of Railway Engineers

name: Shen Guojun
about: Shen Guojun is the founder and chairman of Yintai Group, whose interests cover retail, real estate and investment.
Yintai's department store chain Intime was taken private from the Hong Kong Stock Exchange by Shen and Alibaba in 2017, in a deal that valued it at $2.6 billion.
Shen worked in a state-run bank before he started his own business.
The tycoon has divested sizable stakes in gold, property and other businesses amid China's slower growth.
In 2024, Alibaba sold its 99% stake in Intime to a consortium led by China's textile heavyweight Youngor Group for $1 billion, registering $1.3 billion loss.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts, Zhongnan University of Economics and Law

name: Reed Hastings
about: Reed Hastings, cofounder and chairman of Netflix, revolutionized how the world is entertained.
Hastings cofounded Netflix in 1997, the same year he sold his first company, Pure Software. He took Netflix public in 2002.
Netflix originally operated as a DVD-by-mail subscription service, but began streaming content in 2007.
Hastings stepped down as co-CEO in 2023 and has been reducing his shareholding; he now owns less than 1% of Netflix shares.
In 2020, he and his wife Patty donated $120 million to two historically Black colleges and the United Negro College Fund. Their lifetime giving surpasses $2 billion.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Stanford University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Bowdoin College

did_you_know_facts: The son of a Nixon administration lawyer, Hastings studied math at Bowdoin College and served in the Peace Corps in Swaziland.
Hastings holds a graduate degree in artificial intelligence from Stanford.
quote: Incredible people don't want to be micromanaged. We manage through setting context and letting people run.

name: Peter Cancro
about: Peter Cancro is the owner and chairman of popular sandwich chain Jersey Mike's.
The Manasquan, New Jersey-based business recorded $3.3 billion in systemwide sales from more than 2,800 stores in 2023.
It all started in 1972 when Cancro, then 14, got a job at Mike's Subs in his hometown of Point Pleasant, New Jersey.
Three years later, the store came up for sale and Cancro borrowed $125,000 from his football coach to buy it.
In 1981, Cancro changed the name to Jersey Mike's and began franchising across the U.S.
Cancro agreed to sell a majority stake in Jersey Mike's to Blackstone at a reported $8 billion valuation, including debt, in November 2024.
did_you_know_facts: Only 1% of people who apply to own a Jersey Mike's franchise get one, according to the company, making it more competitive than getting into Harvard
Cancro has no desk at Jersey Mike's HQ and instead spends about 80% of the year traveling to see franchisees.
quote: I've worked my whole life to be right where we are right now, and things have just started to grow, believe it or not.

name: Takao Yasuda
about: Takao Yasuda founded discount retailer Don Quijote, now Pan Pacific International Holdings, in 1980.
The retailer has nearly 750 stores and is publicly traded. It sells a wide range of products, from Rolexes to snacks to adult toys.
He returned as a board director in 2019, after having stepped down as CEO and chairman in 2015. Yasuda's title at Pan Pacific is now founding chairman and supreme advisor.
Supermarket UNY, formerly a part of retail and convenience-store operator FamilyMart UNY, is a 100% subsidiary.
In September 2024, his 23-year-old son Yusaku was appointed to the company's board.
did_you_know_facts: In 2017, the company opened up its first store in Singapore, called Don Don Donki, part of an expansion in Southeast Asia.
Yasuda's first retail venture was a discount store in Tokyo called Thieves' Market, which he opened in 1978.

name: Stephen Cohen
about: Stephen Cohen cofounded data mining firm Palantir around the time he finished college in 2003 and is currently president and secretary.
