He went on to acquire a stake in the Chemist Warehouse pharmacy chain that Jack cofounded with Mario Verrocchi in 1995 with five pharmacies.
Today Chemist Warehouse has annual revenue of A$3.3 billion and over 600 outlets across Australia, China, Dubai, Ireland and New Zealand.
Chemist Warehouse dropped its plan for an IPO opting for a merger with ASX-listed Sigma Healthcare, which was completed in February 2025.
did_you_know_facts: In 1976, the brothers established a successful sunglasses, perfume and suntan lotion company-Le Specs and Le Tan-which they sold in 1991.

name: Ramon Ang
about: Ramon Ang is the chairman of San Miguel, one of the oldest conglomerates in the Philippines.
Originally a brewer, San Miguel is now a leader in food and beverages; but the bulk of its revenue comes from power and infrastructure businesses.
San Miguel is building a $15 billion airport and city complex at a 2,500-hectare site in Bulacan. It also started a $3 billion project to revamp Manila's international airport in 2024.
In 2023, Ang's Bulacan-based cement maker Eagle Cement delisted following the sale to San Miguel.
In 2024, Ramon's son John Paul was elevated from San Miguel's board director to president and chief operating officer to assist him in running the company.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, Far Eastern University

did_you_know_facts: Ang started out by fixing and selling used Japanese car and truck engines; subsequently with the late Eduardo Cojuangco he sold aluminum wheels.
Late billionaire Eduardo Cojuangco and Ramon Ang were good friends; they bonded through a common passion for collecting and restoring vintage cars.

name: Richard Peery
about: Early Silicon Valley property baron Richard "Dick" Peery partnered with John Arrillaga, buying farmland in the 1960s and turning it into office parks.
Peery's longtime business partner since the 1960s, Arrillaga died in early 2022.
In 2006 Peery and Arrillaga sold many of their buildings for $1.1 billion.
Peery, who dropped out of the Stanford MBA program, had gained early experience managing his father's small property portfolio.
His son Dave runs the Peery Foundation, whose grantees include both Bay Area and international nonprofit groups.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Brigham Young University

did_you_know_facts: He and his sister endowed Brigham Young University with $3 million to establish the H. Taylor Peery Institute of Financial Services, named after their late father.
Peery owned every gum ball machine on the Stanford campus when he was in middle school and went on to launch a miniature golf course in his teens.

name: Ankur Jain
about: Ankur Jain founded and runs home rental rewards startup Bilt Rewards, which raised $250 million from private investors at a $10.75 billion valuation in July 2025.
Bilt Rewards processes rent payments and enables renters to earn and redeem points with airlines, hotels, gyms and restaurants.
Jain, who is CEO, owns 32% of Bilt Rewards, which is based in New York City.
Jain previously cofounded Humin, an app that combined contacts, calendars and more and was acquired by Tinder; he made the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in 2015.
Jain's father, former Microsoft executive Naveen Jain, was briefly a billionaire in 2000 when shares of InfoSpace, the Internet content firm he founded, peaked.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, The Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: Longtime NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell joined Bilt Rewards' board as an independent director in 2024.
Ken Chenault, former chairman of American Express, became chairman of Bilt Rewards in 2024 after venture capital firm General Catalyst, where Chenault now works, invested in Bilt.
quote: We're helping you understand what you can afford. We're helping you build your credit.

name: Oprah Winfrey
about: Oprah Winfrey transitioned her hit talk show, which ran for 25 years until 2011, into a media and business empire.
Reinvested, the profits from her show, plus profits from films like The Color Purple, Beloved and Selma (which her Harpo Productions coproduced) add up to an estimated more than $2.5 billion.
In 2011, Winfrey launched cable channel OWN. She sold most of her stake in the network to owner Warner Bros. Discovery in 2020 in exchange for shares in the company.
Her sprawling real estate portfolio includes homes in California and over a dozen properties including 2,100 acres of land in Hawaii.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Tennessee State University

did_you_know_facts: Winfrey overcame a tough childhood, born to a teen mother in rural Mississippi and raised without indoor plumbing.
Winfrey has focused her philanthropy on education, including supporting a girls' school in South Africa.
quote: What I learned in all of those thousands of interviews is that there is a common denominator in our human experience. Everybody wants to know did you hear me and did what I say matter?

name: Feng Hailiang
about: Feng Hailiang chairs Zhejiang-based Hailiang Group, whose interests include copper smelting, real estate, education and agribusiness.
Feng started a trading company in 1985, followed by a copper products factory in 1989; the latter was the predecessor to Hailiang Group.
Feng's son Feng Luming is an executive director of Hong Kong-listed Hailiang International Holding.
Liming holds undergraduate and graduate degrees in business from the University of San Francisco.
Hailang Group donated more than $100 million of stock to the Hailiang Charitable Foundation in 2020.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Zhejiang University

name: Waleed Mohammad Al Zaabi
about: Waleed Mohammad Al Zaabi is the founder and owner of Tiger Group, a United Arab Emirates-based real estate developer with offices in Dubai and Sharjah.
A civil engineer by training, Al Zaabi founded Tiger Group in 1976 as a construction firm and then moved into real estate development in 1996.
He later expanded into hospitality, manufacturing, agriculture and education in 2006. By 2014, Tiger Group had become a leading developer in Dubai and Sharjah.
Tiger Group has developed 50,000 apartments since 1976 and is building another 20,000 units, plus office and retail space, across the United Arab Emirates.
In 2024, Tiger Group launched Sky Tower, set to be the tallest residential tower in the world at 1,745 feet when it's completed in late 2029.

name: Jim Breyer
about: One of Facebook's first venture investors, Jim Breyer made much of his fortune investing in the social network.
After 28 years at venture firm Accel Partners, Breyer started his own firm, Breyer Capital, in 2006 and has bet on artificial intelligence and cryptocurrency.
He has invested in over 40 companies that have had successful IPOs or mergers, and is the second largest individual shareholder of stablecoin firm Circle, which went public in June 2025.
Breyer is a trustee of the American Film Institute in Los Angeles and SFMOMA in San Francisco and a board member of investment firm Blackstone.
Breyer's second wife Angela Chao, a sister-in-law of U.S. Senator Mitch McConnell, died in a car accident in February 2024.

forbes_list.list: The Midas List: Top Tech Investors (2018)

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Stanford University

did_you_know_facts: Breyer, whose parents fled Hungary, spent his early years living in a funeral home in New Haven because it was the cheapest place to live while his dad went to Yale.
In 1982, Breyer sent his resume to Steve Jobs, who forwarded it to the director of marketing. He was hired for the summer and part-time while he was at Stanford.

name: Parker Conrad
about: Parker Conrad is the cofounder and CEO of human resources software startup Rippling.
Conrad owns an estimated 20% of the company, which private investors valued at $16.8 billion in May 2025.
Conrad cofounded the company in 2016 after resigning under pressure as CEO of Zenefits, the HR startup he founded in 2013.
Zenefits, worth $4.5 billion at its peak, slashed its valuation by more than half in 2016 amid compliance investigations related to its insurance sales.
Conrad worked at biopharma company Amgen and in 2007 moved to San Francisco to start Wikinvest, now called SigFig, with a college friend, who eventually forced him out of the company.
A battle with testicular cancer led Conrad to become an expert on the U.S. healthcare system. He founded Zenefits with $20,000 in savings.

name: Gwynne Shotwell
about: Gwynne Shotwell is SpaceX's president and COO, and manages the operations of the commercial space exploration company founded by Elon Musk.
It's grown from a futuristic idea of enabling people to live on other planets to a company with over 13,000 employees and a valuation of $350 billion.
As of March 2024, SpaceX has transported astronauts to the International Space Station nine times on behalf of NASA and three times for private company customer Axiom Space.
Shotwell was the 11th employee of SpaceX, joining the company in 2002. Before that, she was at spacecraft developer Microcosm as its space systems director.
Shotwell owns an estimated stake in SpaceX of less than 1%.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Northwestern University; Master of Science, Northwestern University

did_you_know_facts: NASA has selected SpaceX to be one of the companies that will transport astronauts to the Moon's surface as part of the Artemis program.

name: Eva Maria Bucher-Haefner
about: Eva Maria Bucher-Haefner's fortune mostly stems from her former stake in IT management software maker CA Technologies, acquired by Broadcom in 2020.
She inherited half of her father Walter's stake in the business when he died in June 2012, then the world's oldest billionaire at 101.
She and her brother, Martin Haefner, also inherited equal stakes in car dealer AMAG.
Bucher-Haefner sold her stake in AMAG to Martin, who is also a billionaire, in late 2018.
She runs Moyglare, a 500-acre horse farm in Ireland that was purchased by her father in 1962, home to around 100 horses today.

name: Chung Mong-joon
about: Chung Mong-joon is the largest shareholder of shipbuilder HD Hyundai Heavy Industries.
He is the sixth son of the late Hyundai group founder Chung Ju-yung, who got his start repairing trucks for the U.S. Army after the Korean War.
Chung ran HD Hyundai Heavy Industries until he entered politics in 1988; he served seven terms in the National Assembly.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Ph.D, Johns Hopkins University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Seoul National University

did_you_know_facts: In 2014, he ran for mayor of Seoul but lost.
He is a former vice president of international soccer body FIFA.

name: Wilhelm Beier & family
about: Wilhelm Beier is the chairman of the supervisory board of Dermapharm, a pharmaceutical company he founded in 1991.
Dermapharm, based in Gruenwald near Munich, manufacturers generic drugs for maladies ranging from insect bites to fungal diseases and osteoporosis.
Nearly half of its revenues come from the so-called "parallel trade'': arbitraging price differences for drugs between countries.
Dermapharm, which went public in 2018, is expanding into the business of medical marijuana. Beier and his family still own more than 70% of the company.
The company holds over 40% of one Germany's most popular home shopping television channels.
did_you_know_facts: Wilhelm's wife Elisabeth runs the company's international business, while son Michael runs online perfume shop Point Rouge.
Known as "Willi" in Munich, Beier has reportedly hosted parties with celebrity guests at his estate in Kitzbuehel, Austria, one of the world's top ski resorts.

name: Peter Sondakh
about: Peter Sondakh is head of Rajawali Corpora, an investment firm founded in 1984 whose portfolio includes hotels, media and mining.
His Rajawali Property group, founded in 1989, owns the marquee Four Seasons in Jakarta and the St. Regis in Jakarta and Bali.
Other assets include internet service provider Velo Networks and TV network Rajawali Televisi.
Sondakh sold his nearly 84% stake in Indonesian coal mining outfit Golden Eagle Energy to Singapore-listed Geo Energy in 2023 for about $200 million.
Sondakh is expanding into geothermal powerplant through his gold mining company Archi Indonesia.
did_you_know_facts: Sondakh's father was an entrepreneur, exporting wood and coconut oil since Sondakh was just a baby.
A devout Christian, Sondakh is known to read the Bible everyday.
During a holiday in the U.S., he paid a George Washington University psychology professor to assess his strengths and weaknesses.
quote: I want to know what's wrong with me. Unless you know your weaknesses, how can you improve?

name: Alexis Lê-Quôc
about: Alexis Le-Quoc is the chief technology officer of Datadog, a cloud monitoring company he founded in 2010 with Olivier Pomel, the firm's CEO.
Datadog listed on the Nasdaq in 2019, raising nearly $650 million and nabbing a $10.9 billion market cap on its first day of trading.
Le-Quoc and Pomel became billionaires in 2020; Le-Quoc owns some 3% of Datadog shares.
The French natives met while undergraduates at Ecole Centrale Paris, where both received a master's in computer science.
Before launching Datadog, the duo worked together at New York-based firm Wireless Generation, which was acquired by News Corp in 2010.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Ecole Centrale Paris

name: Felix Baker
about: Felix Baker is the cofounder of Baker Brothers Advisors, a New York hedge fund firm that specializes in biotechnology stocks.
Baker started his hedge fund firm with his brother, Julian Baker, in 2000. As of March 2025, the firm was managing $18 billion in assets.
The two brothers started their fund-management careers in 1994 with a biotechnology investing partnership with the Tisch Family.

name: Julian Baker
about: Julian Baker is a cofounder of Baker Brothers Advisors, a New York hedge fund that specializes in biotechnology stocks.
Baker started his hedge fund him with his brother, Felix, and as of March 2025 was managing about $18 billion.
The brothers started their fund-management careers in 1994 with a biotechnology investing partnership with the Tisch Family.

name: Vincent McMahon
about: Vince McMahon grew World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) from a regional operation into a global phenomenon.
A third-generation wrestling promoter, McMahon grew up in a trailer park in North Carolina and joined his father's small wrestling company in 1972.
He purchased the business 10 years later and turned it into a giant. He took WWE (then named WWF) public in 1999.
In 2023, McMahon agreed to merge WWE with UFC to form TKO Group Holdings.
He stepped down as executive chairman of TKO in 2024 amid sexual misconduct allegations, which he has denied.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, East Carolina University

did_you_know_facts: Donald Trump picked McMahon's wife, Linda, to lead the Small Business Administration during his first term and to run the Department of Education in his second term.
McMahon's daughter, Stephanie, is married to professional wrestler Paul Levesque, better known as Triple H. She resigned as WWE's chief brand officer in 2023.

name: Keith Dunleavy & family
about: Keith Dunleavy is the founder of Inovalon, a cloud-based software and healthcare analytics firm.
He took Inovalon public on the Nasdaq in 2015 and sold it to a consortium of private equity firms in 2021 for $7.3 billion.
In 2025 he retired after 26 years as Inovalon's CEO. He still owns a roughly 15% stake and serves on the board.
He also founded Apandion, an investment firm backed solely by his funds, with an emphasis on founder-led tech firms. Among its investments: SpaceX and Shield AI.
In 2020 Dunleavy and his wife created the Dunleavy Foundation, which has supported education, social entrepreneurship and U.S. service members and veterans.
Dunleavy graduated from Dartmouth College with a focus on biology and engineering and got an MD from Harvard Medical School.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Dartmouth College; Medical Doctor, Harvard University

name: Xie Weitong
about: Xie Weitong was the largest shareholder of Huayou Cobalt, a mainland Chinese supplier of cobalt and lithium battery chemicals. He sold all his stakes in 2021.
The company also operates cobalt and copper mining businesses in the Congo, and acquired a $422 million lithium mine in Zimbabwe in 2022.
Xie resigned in 2019 after serving as the company's vice chairman for 17 years since its inception.

name: Prathap Reddy
about: Cardiologist Prathap Reddy founded Apollo Hospitals Enterprise in 1983 after he returned from the U.S. in the 1970s.
The Chennai-based company operates a network of more than 70 hospitals and over 6,000 pharmacies.
His four daughters run the company. Eldest Preetha Reddy and third daughter Shobana are executive vice chairperson and executive chairperson respectively.
Second daughter Suneeta Reddy is managing director and the youngest, Sangita Reddy is joint managing director.
did_you_know_facts: His granddaughter Upasana is married to popular Telugu actor Ram Charan, who featured in the picturization of the Oscar-winning song Naatu Naatu in the movie RRR.
In 2022, Apollo Hospitals Group set up a hospital in Nairobi in partnership with Balmer Healthcare of Kenya, offering 20 specialties.

name: August Troendle
about: August Troendle is the CEO of Medpace, a clinical research company he founded in Cincinnati, Ohio in 1992; he owns nearly 20% of the stock.
Medpace conducts clinical trials for pharmaceutical companies seeking to bring drugs, vaccines or medical devices to market.
Before starting Medpace, Troendle spent five years as a director at Swiss pharma company Sandoz, now known as Novartis.
He also briefly worked as a medical review officer at the FDA's division of metabolic and endocrine drug products from 1986 to 1987.
A doctor with an M.D. from the University of Maryland, Troendle has also served on the boards of several public and private healthcare companies.

name: Fernando Chico Pardo
about: Fernando Chico Pardo started his first company in Mexico City at age 27, a stock brokerage called Acciones y Asesoría Bursátil.
That brokerage later became part of Grupo Financiero Inbursa, a banking and financial group controlled by Mexican billionaire Carlos Slim.
After he left Inbursa in 2003, Chico Pardo became a controlling shareholder in Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste (Asur), which operates nine airports in Mexico and one in San Juan, Puerto Rico.
He also runs private equity fund Promecap, which has acquired interests in or provided funding for a variety of Mexican companies.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Kellogg School of Management; Bachelor of Business Administration, Universidad Iberoamericana

name: Karsanbhai Patel
about: Low-profile founder of Nirma, Karsanbhai Patel, started out mixing detergents in his backyard and selling them door-to-door on his bicycle.
His low-price Nirma brand sparked a detergents war with bigger rivals such as Unilever and Procter & Gamble.
Today Nirma is one of the largest producers of soda ash in the world by volume.
Patel has long handed over operations to the next generation and took the company private in 2012. His cement unit Nuvoco Vistas was listed in 2021.
In 2024, Nirma completed the $680 million acquisition of a 75% stake in Glenmark Life Sciences, a maker of pharmaceutical ingredients, since renamed as Alivus Life Sciences.
did_you_know_facts: Patel was born into a farmer's family in Gujarat and started his career as a lab assistant.
Nirma is named after Patel's late daughter Nirupama.

name: Marc Fielmann
about: Marc Fielmann is the CEO of Fielmann Group AG, Europe's leading optical company that operates stores and online shops across the continent and also in the United States.

Guenther Fielmann handed over the company to his son Marc as the market leader in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland in 2018 with approximately 700 stores. As of now Fielmann operates around 1,300 stores.
With revenues exceeding EUR 2 billion and some 24,000 employees, Fielmann serves more than 28 million customers.
Fielmann holds a BSc from the London School of Economics and Poltical Science (LSE).
He began working at the company in 2012 and took over the reigns from his father in 2019.

name: Ted Alfond
about: Ted Alfond is one of three living heirs who are billionaires thanks to Warren Buffett's purchase of the Dexter Shoe Company.
Ted's father, Harold Alfond, bought an old mill in Maine in 1958 and turned it into a shoemaker that sold millions of boots and casual shoes a year.
In 1993 Harold sold the company to Buffett for about $420 million in Berkshire Hathaway stock, now worth billions due to the rising share price.
Ted and his brother Bill are minority investors in Fenway Sports Group, which owns the Boston Red Sox, Liverpool FC and the Pittsburgh Penguins.
Ted's youngest sibling, Peter, died in 2017 at age 65 from malaria, which he contracted during a trip to Africa.

name: Susan Alfond
about: Susan Alfond and her three siblings inherited a fortune created by their father, who started Dexter Shoe Company.
Her father, Harold Alfond, bought an old mill in Maine in 1958 and turned it into a shoemaker that sold millions of boots and casual shoes.
In 1993 Harold sold the company to Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway for $420 million of stock; the shares are worth billions of dollars now.
Susan's youngest sibling, Peter, died in 2017 at age 65 from malaria, which he contracted during a trip to Africa.

forbes_list.list: The Richest Person In Every State (2025)

name: Bill Alfond
about: Bill Alfond is one of three living heirs who are billionaires thanks to Warren Buffett's purchase of the Dexter Shoe Company.
Bill's father, Harold Alfond, bought an old mill in Maine in 1958 and turned it into a shoemaker that sold millions of boots and casual shoes a year.
In 1993 Harold sold the company to Buffett for about $420 million in Berkshire Hathaway stock, now worth billions due to the rising share price.
Bill and his brother Ted are minority investors in Fenway Sports Group, which owns the Boston Red Sox, Liverpool FC and the Pittsburgh Penguins.
Bill's youngest sibling, Peter, died in July at age 65 from malaria, which he contracted during a trip to Africa.

name: P.V. Ramprasad Reddy
about: P.V. Ramprasad Reddy sits on the board of generics maker Aurobindo Pharma, which he cofounded in 1986.
Aurobindo Pharma makes drugs to treat a range of diseases such as diabetes and cardiac ailments.
The company gets nearly three-fourths of its revenue from the U.S. and Europe.
Starting with a single manufacturing plant, Aurobindo expanded into a global company with 35 manufacturing plants and 9 R&D Centers that serve more than 150 countries.
In July 2025, Aurobindo struck a $250 million deal to acquire U.S. drugmaker Lannett to expand its American manufacturing footprint.
did_you_know_facts: The wife of Aurobindo's cofounder Nityananda Reddy is a cousin of P.V. Ramprasad Reddy.

name: John Tyson & family
about: John Tyson is chairman of Tyson Foods, the processor that breeds, slaughters and sells meat that ends up in grocery stores across America
The conglomerate owns beloved brands like Hillshire Farms, Jimmy Dean and Aidells sausages.
Tyson is known for its chicken, but the company also produces approximately 20% of the beef and pork in the U.S.
In 2019, Tyson Foods debuted its own alternative meat line Raised & Rooted, including plant-based nuggets.
Tyson Foods was originally founded by John's grandfather in 1935. John served as CEO of the company from 2000 to 2006.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Southern Methodist University

did_you_know_facts: Following in the footsteps of his late father, John Tyson is an avid art collector whose collection includes the likes of Warhol, Lichtenstein and de Kooning.
Tyson began working at Tyson Foods at 13, transferring eggs to incubators in the hatchery and vaccinating chickens on the farm.
quote: You strive every day to try to do the right thing. It goes back to my granddad, to my dad and the people he had around him and it's reflected in today's company and leadership. We care about our folks, our communities, our farmer relationships.

name: Balkrishan Goenka
about: Balkrishan Goenka controls and runs the Welspun Group in Mumbai, with interests in textiles and pipes.
Spurning his family's trading business, Goenka borrowed $100,000 from his father, took a bank loan and started Welspun in 1985 to make polyester yarn.
He expanded into home linen, focusing on the export market, with customers such as Walmart and Macy's.
His Welspun Corp is one of the largest pipe companies in the world.
His wife Dipali runs listed home textiles maker Welspun India.
did_you_know_facts: Goenka has a passion for vintage cars.
His older daughter, Radhika, founded and runs The Lingerie Shop.
In 2023, he bought a luxury penthouse in Mumbai for $30 million.

name: Warren Stephens
about: Warren Stephens is an investing billionaire and the current United State ambassador to the United Kingdom.
His uncle Witt founded Little Rock-based investment bank Stephens Inc. in 1933; his father Jackson joined in 1946.
The outfit underwrote Walmart's public offering in 1970.
The two brothers plowed their earnings into private equity, hewing to the investment criteria, "whim and caprice."
Stephens grew up in the business, became CEO in 1986 and bought out his cousins in 2006.
Stephens sold a group of newspaper holdings, including the Las Vegas Review Journal, for $400 million in 2015.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Washington & Lee University; Master of Business Administration, Wake Forest University School of Business

did_you_know_facts: A golf nut, Stephens built the Alotian Club outside Little Rock; it's ranked one of the nation's best.

name: Sean Parker
about: Sean Parker's fortune stems from his brief tenure, at age 24, as Facebook's president. Parker is now a venture capital investor and philanthropist.
Parker was a teenage hacker and famously founded filesharing site Napster in 1999.
His interest in music led him to invest in Spotify in 2010. He served on the company's board until 2017.
He launched his Parker Foundation in 2015 with $600 million earmarked for science, global health and civic engagement.
In 2016, his foundation announced a $250 million grant to establish the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy.
Parker became chairman of image-generation startup Stability AI in 2024.
did_you_know_facts: Parker, who has asthma and allergies to certain foods, also founded the Sean N. Parker Center for Allergy & Asthma Research at Stanford in 2014.
Parker bought Brody House in Los Angeles from Ellen DeGeneres for approximately $55 million in 2014.
quote: Your biggest challenge as an entrepreneur is not concealing your idea from others or keeping your idea secret. It's actually convincing people that you're not crazy and that you can pull [it] off.

name: Chen Qiongxiang
about: Chen Qiongxiang's fortune arises from her stake in Contemporary Amperex Technology, a supplier of batteries for electric vehicles founded in 2011.
Contemporary Amperex, also known as CATL, listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in June 2018.
CATL is headquartered in the southeast Chinese city of Ningbo.

name: Segolene Gallienne
about: Segolene Gallienne is the daughter of the late Albert Frere, the billionaire industrialist who died in 2018 at age 92.
Albert Frere, who was the richest person in Belgium, turned his family's scrap-metal business into a media, utilities and oil empire
Albert Frere' s business interests included Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL bank), insurer Royale Belge, Petrofina and Tractebel before he began slowly selling off assets later in his career.
Gallienne is not involved in the management of her holding company but her husband Ian Gallienne is the CEO of key participation GBL.
did_you_know_facts: Galliene sits on board of the Cheval Blanc winery, which is partly owned by the family and Bernard Arnault's Christian Dior..

name: Gang Ye
about: Gang Ye cofounded online gaming and e-commerce firm, Sea, with Forrest Li and David Chen.
He's been the company's chief operating officer since 2017, following his previous role as chief technology officer.
Sea has attracted investors such as Tencent, the Norwegian sovereign wealth fund, private equity firm General Atlantic and Malaysian billionaire Robert Kuok's son Kuok Khoon Hua.
In 2023, Sea booked its first-ever annual net profit since its IPO in 2017.
Sea has rolled out digital banking services in Southeast Asia, Taiwan and Brazil.
did_you_know_facts: Ye previously worked at the Economic Development Board of Singapore and palm oil major Wilmar International.

name: Wu Yingming
about: Wu Yingming is chairman of the board of supervisors at Contemporary Amperex Technology, a supplier of lithium-ion batteries also known as CATL.
Wu holds an undergraduate degree from Northeastern University in China.
CATL is headquartered in the city of Ningde in China's Fujian Province.

name: William Hockey
about: In 2012, William Hockey cofounded payments company Plaid, which helps other fintechs connect to customers' bank accounts.
He met his cofounder Zach Perret while they were both working as junior consultants at Bain & Company.
He stepped down as Plaid's chief technology officer in 2019, but he remains a board member.

In 2022, he launched Column, a chartered bank based in San Francisco that helps other businesses (including Mercury and Brex) offer banking services. Hockey self-funded Column and owns the vast majority of it.
Hockey studied history and business at Emory University in Atlanta, Georgia.

name: Ma Yunsheng
about: Ma Yunsheng chairs Chambroad Holding, a supplier of petrochemicals, fine chemicals and agribusiness products.
Ma worked as a government official before he joined Chambroad in 1982 when it was a collective.
Chambroad strives for "progress to better serve the country and contribute to society," according to the company website.

name: Susan Ocampo & family
about: Susan Ocampo is a board member and the largest individual shareholder of semiconductor firm Macom Technology Solutions.
She cofounded semiconductor and components supplier Sirenza Microdevices in 1984 with her late husband, John Ocampo (d. 2023).
The couple also cofounded technology investment firm GaAs Labs in 2008. Susan is vice president, secretary and treasurer.
She owns around 15% of the shares of Macom, which John Ocampo led as chairman and took public on the Nasdaq in 2012.

name: Zhang Tao
about: Zhang Tao was the CEO of restaurant review site Dianping when it merged with Groupon-like Meituan in 2015.
Meituan went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2018.
Zhang received an MBA from Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania in 2002, and returned to China in 2003, when he set up Dianping.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania

name: Pierre Karl Péladeau
about: The son of Quebecor's founder, Pierre Karl Peladeau is the largest individual shareholder in the media company, which prints Le Journal de Montreal.
Peladeau has spent more than two decades as CEO, with a three year break between 2014 and 2017, and expanded the company into telecom, sports and entertainment.
In 2015, he was elected to lead the separatist Parti Québécois, before resigning in May 2016.
In February 2017, he returned as CEO of a very healthy Quebecor, as shares rose 70% during his political stint.
Sister Anne-Marie Peladeau sued Pierre Karl Peladeau and his brother Erik over a 20-year-old agreement to buy back her shares, and a judge awarded her $36 million in 2020.
did_you_know_facts: A lifelong fan, Peladeau bought the Canadian Football League's Montreal Alouettes in 2023.

name: Mark Davis
about: Mark Davis owns the Las Vegas Raiders, the NFL team he inherited from his father, Al Davis (d. 2011).
Davis' only jobs have ever been with the team. He worked first in the equipment room, then in team retail, where he is said to have invented the muff-style hand warmer that is now used league-wide.
Davis moved the Raiders from Oakland to Las Vegas in 2020 after a failed attempt to relocate to Los Angeles.
When Davis took over, Forbes valued the team at $761 million. Now, it's worth more than $7 billion.
He also owns the Las Vegas Aces WNBA team.

name: Michiel Le Roux
about: Michiel Le Roux of South Africa founded Capitec Bank in 2001 and owns about 11% of the company's shares.
The bank, which trades on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, targets South Africa's emerging middle class.
He served as chairman of the board of Capitec from 2007 to 2016 and still sits on the company's board.
Le Roux previously ran Boland Bank, a small regional bank in Cape Town's hinterland.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: LLB, University of Stellenbosch; Bachelor of Commerce, University of Stellenbosch

did_you_know_facts: Capitec Bank has more than 800 branches and over 15,000 employees.
Le Roux was the largest donor to the Democratic Alliance, a liberal South African political party, during its 2023-2024 financial year.

name: Cai Dongchen
about: Cai Dongchen is the chairman and CEO of CSPC Pharmaceutical Group.
CSPC's bulk drug products include vitamin C, antibiotics and caffeine.
The company's manufacturing facilities are located mainly in the eastern Chinese city of Shijiazhuang.
Cai holds a MBA degree from Nankai University.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Nankai University; Master, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences

name: Augusto Perfetti
about: Augusto Perfetti and his brother Giorgio Perfetti own candy and gum giant Perfetti Van Melle, a company with more than $4.8 billion in revenues in 2024.
Their father Ambrogio and uncle Egidio started the company in 1946 as a chewing gum business in a small town near Milan.
In 2022, the company announced it would acquire Mondelez International's developed market gum business, adding brands such as Trident, Dentyne and Bubbalicious.
Augusto Perfetti named his yacht and his private jet after Mentos mints and Airheads taffy, the company's top-selling brands.
Perfetti once sold a 300-foot yacht under construction to fellow billionaire Suleiman Kerimov.
did_you_know_facts: Perfetti's father and uncle were inspired to start the company after seeing American soldiers bring gum to Europe during World War II.

name: David Zalik
about: David Zalik is the cofounder and former CEO of financial technology company GreenSky, which Goldman Sachs acquired in an all-stock transaction worth about $2.2 billion in 2022.
Goldman sold GreenSky to a consortium of investors in 2024, and Zalik left the company.
The Atlanta-based GreenSky has facilitated billions of dollars in loans for home improvement projects via a network of banks and thousands of contractors.
The business also helps with financing for doctor, dentist and veterinary visits.
Zalik immigrated to the U.S. from Israel at age four when his father, a mathematics professor, got a job at the University of Rhode Island.
did_you_know_facts: Zalik started his first business at the age of 14, buying computer parts from distributors and assembling them himself.
Zalik didn't attend high school and never graduated from college.
quote: We've kept a truly maniacal focus on the product. And maniacal is the right word.

name: Naomi Azrieli
about: Naomi Azrieli is an heir to the Azrieli Group real estate fortune.
She and her two sisters, Danna and Sharon Azrieli, own about 46% of the publicly traded company.
She sits on the board and inherited her stake after her father, David Azrieli, died in 2014.
Noami also chairs the family's Azrieli Foundation, which supports a number of causes, including science, music and Holocaust education.

name: Sharon Azrieli
about: Sharon Azrieli is an heir to the Azrieli Group real estate fortune.
She and her two sisters, Danna and Naomi Azrieli, own about 46% of the publicly traded company.
She sits on the board and inherited her stake after her father, David Azrieli, died in 2014.
Sharon is also on the board of the family's Azrieli Foundation, which supports a number of causes, including science, music and Holocaust education.

name: Danna Azrieli
about: Danna Azrieli is an heir to the Azrieli Group real estate fortune.
She and her two sisters, Naomi and Sharon Azrieli, own about 46% of the publicly traded company.
She inherited her stake after her father, David Azrieli, died in 2014.
Danna chairs Azrieli Group, which builds shopping malls and office buildings in Israel.

name: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
about: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw, one of India's richest self-made women, founded biopharmaceutical firm Biocon, in 1978. The firm has successfully forayed into the lucrative U.S. market, and it also has one of Asia's largest insulin factories in Malaysia's Johor region.

In December 2025, Biocon announced that it is buying the rest of privately held subsidiary Biocon Biologics to consolidate its biosimilars and generics drug businesses. The deal values Biocon Biologics at $5.5 billion, it said.
Biocon Biologics acquired the biosimilars business of U.S. drugmaker Viatris in 2022 for $3.3 billion.
In 2022, the Central Bureau of Investigation arrested a Biocon Biologics executive and four others in an alleged bribery case. The company denied any wrongdoing.
Biocon-backed cancer therapy company Bicara Therapeutics raised $362 million in an IPO on the Nasdaq in September 2024.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Melbourne University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Bangalore University

did_you_know_facts: Mazumdar-Shaw wanted to be a doctor but couldn't get into medical school.
In 2019, she and late husband John Shaw, donated $7.5 million to the University of Glasgow to create a research hub and a professorial chair of precision oncology.
In 2024, she was bestowed the Jamsetji Tata Award by the Indian Society for Quality for pioneering biosciences movement in India.
Her philanthropic initiative, Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center, aims to create a sustainable, affordable cancer care model.
quote: My legacy is going to be in affordable healthcare. I am willing to invest in developing that model and the policies around it.

name: E. Joe Shoen
about: Joe Shoen is the president and chairman of U-Haul's parent company Amerco. He owns around 20%.
His parents, L.S. and Anna Mary Shoen, cofounded the truck and trailer rental company in 1945.
Worried that his father was wrecking the company, Joe led a coup in 1986, forcing his dad into retirement and alienating most of his 12 siblings.
Brother Mark Shoen, also a billionaire, reportedly remains on good terms with Joe.
Despite his problems working with his own dad, Joe's son Sam is an executive at Amerco.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, College of the Holy Cross

did_you_know_facts: Shoen wrote his thesis at Harvard Business School on the self-storage business.
Shoen is known for his frugality, insisting employees stay in cheap motels, two to a room.

name: Alan Howard
about: Alan Howard cofounded Brevan Howard Asset Management, a European hedge fund specializing in macro trading, in 2002.
The firm was once one of the world's top macro hedge funds, with assets under management peaking at $40 billion in 2013.
A streak of uninspiring returns led to billions in investor withdrawals, but assets have rebounded to $36 billion after solid returns in recent years.
In 2019, Howard stepped down as CEO to focus solely on investing and to give portfolio managers more autonomy.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Imperial College London

name: Shiv Kishan Agrawal
about: Shiv Kishan Agrawal, who was running Nagpur-based Haldiram Foods International, merged his company with Delhi-based Haldiram Foods in 2023 to create Haldiram Snacks Food.
A consortium of investors led by Singapore's Temasek, acquired a 20% stake in the merged company in 2025 at an estimated valuation of $10 billion.
Agrawal is the grandson of the founder Ganga Bishan Agarwal, who started selling snacks from a tiny shop in Bikaner in Rajasthan and went on to create the popular Haldiram brand.
The business was eventually divided among the patriarch's grandsons into three separate companies, operating out of Nagpur, Delhi and Kolkata.

name: Masahiro Noda
about: Masahiro Noda is the chairman and CEO of publicly traded computer-system integrator and custom software maker Obic.
Obic is known for its accounting software and its television ads featuring a Kabuki actor.
In the fiscal year through March 2025, the company posted $452 million in net profit on $848 million in revenue.
Noda launched the business with his wife's savings in 1968.

name: Ren Yuanlin
about: Ren Yuanlin chairs Yangzijiang Shipbuilding, one of China's largest shipyards.
Ren joined the company in the1970s, then called Jiangyin Shipbuilding Factory, and headed its ship body workshop. He worked his way up to a factory supervisor and eventually became chairman in 1997.
In 2022, Yangzijiang Financial Holding, a former subsidiary, spun off from the group and went public in Singapore.
Apart from Yangzijiang Shipbuilding, Ren's wealth also includes his stake in Yangzijiang Financial and debt investments.

name: Gerry Harvey
about: Gerry Harvey is cofounder and executive chairman of furniture and electrical goods chain Harvey Norman.
He also controls a property portfolio and owns the Magic Millions racehorse auction market.
He describes his wife Katie Page, who runs Harvey Norman, as "the mastermind" of the operation.
Page also holds shares in the company.
Harvey Norman has more than 100 company operated stores overseas, in countries like New Zealand, Singapore, Malaysia, Slovenia and the UK.
did_you_know_facts: Harvey plans to open five Harvey Norman stores in Britain across England's West Midlands.

name: Yao Liangsong
about: Yao Liangsong is the chairman of Guangzhou-headquartered Oppein Home Group, one of China's largest makers of custom kitchen cabinets and home furniture.
Yao set up Oppein in 1994, which has prospered amid a rise in home ownership and growth in the middle class.
The company has opened 7,400 stores in more than 100 countries.
His brother Yao Liangbo is a director at Oppein.
did_you_know_facts: Yao holds a bachelor's degree in machinery manufacturing from Beihang University.

name: Miriam Baumann-Blocher
about: Miriam Baumann-Blocher's fortune stems from her stake in Ems-Chemie, her family's Swiss polymer and chemical manufacturing giant.
She received her stake in 2004 when her father, Christoph Blocher, sold his shares to his children to take a seat on the Swiss federal council.
Over the years Miriam and her brother Markus sold most of their shares to their sisters, Magdalena and Rahel, to run businesses of their own.
In 2007 Miriam purchased Läckerli-Huus, a Swiss confectionery and baked goods company that she still manages today.

name: Jay Paul
about: Silicon Valley real estate developer Jay Paul builds and leases office space to big tech firms, including Hewlett-Packard, Amazon and Apple.
His privately held Jay Paul Co. has developed more than 14 million square feet of office space in California and Texas.
His first project in San Francisco-proper was 181 Fremont, a 70-story tower with offices and 67 luxury condos up top, which opened in 2018.
Paul is developing about 4 million square feet of office space in downtown San Jose, with plans for a new office campus and several high-rises.
He also owns properties in Santa Cruz, San Diego and Austin, Texas.
did_you_know_facts: Paul lives in San Francisco's affluent Pacific Heights neighborhood. He owns two yachts and at least one Picasso painting.
Google leases more than a million square feet of office space from Jay Paul Co.

name: Deng Wen
about: Deng Wen is the chairman and president of Sichuan Teway Food Group, a supplier of hot-pot condiments, which he founded in 2007.
He got his start in the food and beverage industry in 1993 and once worked for China Oil and Foodstuffs, the state-owned food processing company known primarily for its flour.
Sichuan Teway went public in Shanghai in 2019 and raised $70 million to fund expansion.

name: Ryan Smith
about: Ryan Smith is the owner of the Utah Jazz and the cofounder of Utah-based cloud computing company Qualtrics.
He cofounded Qualtrics, known for its feedback surveys of customers and staff, in 2002 with his brother, Jared, and father, Scott.
Three days before its scheduled IPO in January 2019, Qualtrics was acquired by German software firm SAP for $8 billion in cash.
SAP spun out Qualtrics as a stand alone public company in 2021. It was taken bought by private equity giant Silver Lake in 2023.
In 2020, news broke that Smith was leading a group to buy the Utah Jazz NBA team for $1.66 billion. The deal closed in December 2020.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, Brigham Young University

name: Lawrence Golub
about: Lawrence Golub is the CEO of Golub Capital, a private credit firm he founded in 1994 that has $75 billion in capital under management.
Golub Capital started as a buyout firm, but after the 2000 dotcom bust, Golub shifted its strategy to lending.
In 2003, Golub recruited his younger brother, David, who now serves as CEO of the firm's publicly traded business development company.
Since the 2008 financial crisis, Golub Capital has grown dramatically to become a major player in financing middle-market private equity deals.
Golub is an active philanthropist who supports Parkinson's research, the American Repertory Theater, and hospitals in New York and Boston.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Harvard College; Doctor of Jurisprudence, Harvard Law School

did_you_know_facts: Golub took a year off of Wall Street to be a White House Fellow from 1992 to 1993, first working under the George H.W. Bush administration and then Clinton.

name: Anu Aga
about: Anu Aga derives her wealth from a majority stake in listed engineering firm Thermax.
Aga started working at Thermax in 1985 when it was run by her husband and took the helm in 1996 after he died of a heart attack.
She stepped down as chairman in 2004, ceding the spot to her daughter Meher, a U.K.-trained chemical engineer, who lets hired executives manage the firm.
Consumer goods billionaire Harsh Mariwala has a board seat in the company.
Thermax has partnered with Australian billionaire Andrew Forrest's Fortescue Future Industries to set up a green hydrogen venture in India.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Mumbai

did_you_know_facts: Aga cofounded Teach for India in 2008, a non-profit that recruits young people to teach for two years in schools for low-income kids.
Aga was a nominated member of parliament for six years.

name: B. Partha Saradhi Reddy
about: B.Partha Saradhi Reddy is chairman of Hetero Group, which he founded in 1993.
Hetero produces a range of anti-retroviral drugs for a host of diseases including AIDS.
It has a portfolio of more than 200 products across therapies ranging from cancer to immunology to diabetes.
Hetero makes branded and non-branded generic medicines.
He is a member of the Rajya Sabha, upper house of the Indian Parliament.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Osmania University; Ph.D, Osmania University

did_you_know_facts: Reddy has a Ph.D in synthetic organic chemistry from Hyderabad's Osmania University.
Son Vamsi Krishna is managing director of the Hetero Group.

name: Haim Saban
about: Haim Saban turned his success with children's TV show "Mighty Morphin Power Rangers" into Fox Family Channel, a joint venture with News Corp.
Saban, who repurchased Power Rangers back in 2010, sold it for a second time in 2018, this time to Hasbro in a $522 million deal.
Saban and a group of private equity investors purchased Spanish language TV Network Univision Communications for $13.7 billion in 2007.
In February 2020, Univision agreed to sell a majority stake for an undisclosed price to two firms: Searchlight Capital Partners and ForgeLight LLC.
The Sabans, who have given $230 million to various organizations and initiatives, pledged $50 million to the forthcoming Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in 2017.
did_you_know_facts: Born in Egypt to Jewish parents, Saban moved with his family to Tel Aviv when he was a child and lived in a one-room flat.
While serving in the Israeli army, Saban landed a booking for his band, but he didn't have a band or play an instrument, so he founded a band on the spot.
quote: Huggable lamb that I am, people tell me I'm a tough negotiator.

name: David Baszucki
about: David Baszucki is cofounder and CEO of Roblox, a social gaming platform that allows kids and teens to play games that are made by fellow gamers.
Roblox's 83 million daily active users spent more than 73 billion hours using the platform in 2024.
Players on the platform can buy a digital currency, Robux, which lets them purchase special items within games.
Robux purchases allow tween developers of games to earn money for their efforts. The company paid Roblox creators nearly $1 billion in 2024.

name: Zhang Gongyun
about: Zhang Gongyun is the former chairman and controlling shareholder of Shenzhen-listed Himile Mechanical Science and Technology (Shandong), a supplier of tire molds.
Himile's customers include Yokohama, Continental, Michelin and Bridgestone.
The company went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2011.

name: Kwon Hyuk-bin
about: Kwon Hyuk-bin founded Smilegate in 2002 and has built it into one of the most successful gaming companies in South Korea.
Following a 2008 partnership with Chinese internet giant Tencent, it released its most popular title, CrossFire.
Through his Smilegate Foundation, Kwon has established schools in China and Vietnam, providing education in IT, among other subjects.
did_you_know_facts: Kwon's first venture in business was an ill-fated educational software company that he founded but soon tanked.
While in college, Kwon was selected into Samsung's prestigious software program for students.
quote: We do not ask for profit share because I think it's my responsibility to return the favor that the society had offered me.

name: Surender Saluja
about: Surender Saluja is the founder and chairman of Premier Energies, a manufacturer of solar cells and solar modules.
The 30-year-old company has five manufacturing units in Hyderabad, in the southern Indian state of Telangana.
His son Chiranjeevi is the managing director of Premier Energies.
Premier Energies debuted on the Indian bourses in September 2024 at a 120% premium to the issue price.

name: Theo Roussis
about: Theo Roussis controls Ravago, a plastics recycling and compounds producer and distributor.
Roussis is the son-in-law of Raf Van Gorp, who founded Ravago in 1961 as a recycler of plastic waste.
Under Roussis, Ravago grew into an empire with revenue 13 billion euros and 9.000 employees.
Together with his wife, Gunhilde Van Gorp, Roussis controls Ravago through Luxembourg-based holding company, Plastiche.
did_you_know_facts: Roussis is of Greek descent and has never given an interview.

name: Martin Hetzner
about: Martin Hetzner is CEO of Hetzner, a German technology company he founded in 1997.
He is the sole owner of the business, which offers data-center management and IT services in Germany.
Hetzner had sales of more than 500 million euros in 2023, its most recent financial disclosures.
Hetzner is private and avoids public appearances.

name: Xue Min
about: Xue Min controls Shanghai United Imaging Healthcare, a supplier of medical equipment for imaging and radiation therapy.
The company sells to 50 countries, including the U.S., Italy, Japan and New Zealand.
It went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange's Sci-Tech Innovation Board in 2022.
Earlier, in 1998, Xue founded Shenzhen Mindit Instruments, which was later acquired by Siemens Medical Solutions.

name: Qiu Guanghe & family
about: Qiu Guanghe is chairman and founder of Semir Group, the parent of Zhejiang Semir Garment, which makes and sells apparel.
Semir Garment was founded in 2002, focusing on casual wear and children's clothing and now boasts nearly 8,000 stores across China (including franchises).
Qiu founded the fashion retailing group in 1996 in his hometown of Wenzhou, a trading mecca in Zhejiang Province.
Qiu Jianqiang, Qiu's son, chairs Zhejiang Semir Garment.

name: Maritsa Lazari & family
about: Maritsa Lazari is the widow of late billionaire Christos Lazari, who died in 2015, a few months shy of their 50th wedding anniversary.
The couple, who met in London, married in 1965.
Christos eventually created a successful fashion line called Drendie Girl. The couple used the profits from that business to buy up property.
Lazari Investments owns more than 3 million square feet of commercial real estate in London, mostly office space that it rents out.
Maritsa was a cofounder of the real estate business and serves as a director. Her three children are also involved in the company.
did_you_know_facts: In 2017, the family established a charity foundation in honor of Christos, donating an initial $4.9 million with plans to invest more in the future.

name: Yu Zhuyun
about: Yu Zhuyun is the chairman and CEO of Central New Energy Holding Group, a business whose diverse interests span new energy, real estate and wellness.
Central New Energy went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2018.
Yu holds an MBA from Hong Kong Baptist University and an EMBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.

name: Stephen Lansdown
about: Stephen Lansdown cofounded Hargreaves Lansdown, a British financial services firm.
The company manages over $100 billion in assets and boasts more than 1.7 million clients.
Lansdown stepped down as chairman of the firm in 2009 and left its board in 2012.
In 2010 he relocated to Guernsey, where he was a non-executive director of Ravenscroft Group, an investment services firm based on the island. He retired as chairman in 2021.
Lansdown cofounded Earth Capital, a private equity firm focused on sustainable and impact investing, in 2008. It shut down in 2024.
did_you_know_facts: Lansdown owns Bristol Sport, which oversees the commercial operations of Bristol City F.C., Bristol Rugby Club, Bristol City W.F.C., Bristol Flyers and DZ Racing.

name: Gilles Martin
about: Gilles Martin is the executive chairman of Eurofins Scientific, a Luxembourg-based laboratory services company listed on the French stock exchange.
Martin, who founded the original lab in 1987, owns an estimated 22% of the company through the family's holding company Analytical Bioventures.
His brother Yves-Loic owns an estimated 10% stake. He served as CTO from 1998 until 2015 and now is a board member.
Eurofins has 900 labs in 61 countries and is prominent in food and pharmaceutical products testing.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Ph.D, Syracuse University; Master, Syracuse University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Ecole centrale de Paris

name: Alexandr Wang
about: Alex Wang cofounded Scale AI in 2016 to help companies put their raw data to work for AI and machine learning.
He served as CEO of Scale AI until June 2025, when Meta acquired 49% of the company in a deal that valued Scale at around $29 billion and Wang left Scale to become Meta's chief AI officer.
Wang was the world's youngest self-made billionaire until October 2025, when he was overtaken by Polymarket founder Shayne Coplan.
A New Mexico native, Wang landed full time engineering jobs in Silicon Valley at age 17 with fintech Addepar and then question-and-answer site Quora.
At age 19, after a brief stint at MIT to study machine learning, Wang dropped out to attend the Y Combinator accelerator and launch Scale.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Drop Out, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

did_you_know_facts: Wang, the son of weapons physicists, grew up in Los Alamos, New Mexico, the sleepy town where the U.S. developed its first atomic bomb during World War II.
He entered his first math contest in 6th grade intent on winning a trip to Disney. He did - and later competed in physics Olympiads and science bowls.

name: John Pritzker
about: John Pritzker learned the hotel business at his family's Hyatt Hotel chain; he sold his shares in Hyatt to relatives in 2010.
Pritzker went on to build Commune Hotels and Resorts, a boutique hotel management company, which after a merger in 2016 became Two Roads Hospitality.
In November 2018, Hyatt Hotels purchased Two Roads Hospitality for $408 million.
John's brother Tom Pritzker is the chairman of Hyatt and his sister Gigi Pritzker is a film producer.
A photography buff, he gave $25 million to create the Pritzker Center for Photography at the SFMOMA in San Francisco.
John's father Jay, uncle Robert and grandfather A.N. Pritzker built a diverse fortune that included manufacturing and service group Marmon Holdings.
did_you_know_facts: Pritzker, a former Dead Head, took time off between high school and college to be part of the emerging counterculture in San Francisco.
To support himself after high school, Pritzker got a union job pulling cables for cable TV in an apartment complex south of San Francisco.
quote: Three years ago I gave the commencement speech at Menlo College and received an honorary degree in Rocket Science (true story). Whenever my team doubt the veracity of my assertions I remind them I'm a Rocket Scientist.

name: John Dorrance III
about: John Dorrance is an heir to the Campbell's Soup fortune; his grandfather invented the Campbell's formula for condensed soup.
His relatives are still the company's largest shareholders, but he sold his stake in the mid-1990's and emigrated to Ireland.
His move was presumably timed to avoid capital gains taxes when he sold his Campbell's stake.
The Irish government reportedly gave Dorrance citizenship in 1995 when he spent $1.5 million planting trees.

name: Henry Laufer
about: Laufer joined legendary quantitative hedge fund Renaissance Technologies, founded by Jim Simons, in 1992.
He was its chief scientist and vice president of research until retiring in 2009.
Laufer still has a stake in Renaissance, which now manages about $55 billion.
Prior to Renaissance, Laufer was a math professor at Stony Brook University for two decades.
Laufer and Simons worked together at Stony Brook where Simons was chairman of the Department of Mathematics.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, City College of New York; Doctorate, Princeton University

did_you_know_facts: Laufer and his wife Marsha gave nearly $1 million to Joe Biden's 2020 presidential campaign.

name: Stephen Butt & family
about: Stephen Butt is Texas grocery chain H-E-B's President of Shareholder Relations and its Central Market Division, a brand focused on specialty foods from around the world, and serves on the board.
His brother, Howard Butt III, is H-E-B's CEO and his uncle, Charles Butt, is chairman.
Based in San Antonio, H-E-B has 455 stores in Texas and Mexico and does $50 billion in annual revenue.
Butt's great-grandmother, Florence Butt, started the company in 1905.
did_you_know_facts: H-E-B gives 5% of pretax profits to charity.

name: Howard Butt III & family
about: Howard Butt III is CEO of Texas grocery store chain H-E-B and serves on the board.
His uncle Charles Butt is the company's chairman.
His brother, Stephen Butt, is H-E-B's President of Shareholder Relations and its Central Market division, focused on specialty foods, and serves on the board.
The Butt family owns a majority of the $50 billion (sales) company.
H-E-B has 455 stores in Texas and Mexico and employs 160,000 people.
did_you_know_facts: H-E-B gives 5% of pretax profits to charity each year.
Butt's great-grandmother, Florence Butt, started the company in 1905.

name: Glen Taylor
about: Glen Taylor bought a wedding service business for $2 million in 1975 and turned it into Taylor Corp., a printing firm with over $2 billion in sales.
Taylor, who worked at the wedding business throughout college, stepped down as CEO of Taylor Corp. in 2015; he remains chairman.
A Minnesotan, Taylor owns stakes in the state's NBA team, the Timberwolves; WNBA team, the Lynx; and the United FC soccer team.
In 2016, he sold 5% of his stake in both basketball teams to Lizhang Jiang, the NBA's first Chinese minority owner.
Taylor also owns farmland in Minnesota and Iowa, as well as the Minneapolis Star Tribune, which he bought in 2014 for nearly $100 million.

forbes_list.list: The Richest Person In Every State (2025)

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Minnesota State University

did_you_know_facts: Taylor grew up poor on a farm in southern Minnesota.
As a kid he worked on his neighbors' farms for $1 an hour.
quote: I like the garden and the farm stuff because I'm by myself, and it's the opposite of what I do all day long: sit in meetings, solve problems, listen to people, hear complaints and deal with bad things. That's my job.

name: Pier Silvio Berlusconi
about: Pier Silvio Berlusconi is the son of Silvio Berlusconi, the media mogul and longest-serving Italian prime minister in the post-war era. He died at age 86 in June 2023.
He is one of five heirs and, with his older sister Marina, inherited the majority of his father's empire which includes stakes in media, publishing and banking firms.
Pier Silvio has been the CEO of publicly traded media conglomerate MediaForEurope since 2015 and also sits on the board of the family's investment company, Fininvest.
Fininvest owns stakes in MediaForEurope plus publicly traded Italian bank Banca Mediolanum and publisher Mondadori.
Like his sister Marina, he never completed a college degree.
did_you_know_facts: He was made an honorary citizen of Portofino in 2019.

name: Marina Berlusconi
about: Marina Berlusconi is the eldest daughter of Silvio Berlusconi, the media mogul and longest-serving Italian prime minister in the post-war era, who died at age 86 in June 2023.
She is the president of media group Fininvest, which her father started in the late 1970s and built into a national force, importing American shows like 'Baywatch' to Italy.
She is one of five heirs and, with her brother Pier Silvio, inherited the majority of her father's empire which includes stakes in media, publishing and banking firms.
She is married to Maurizio Vanadia, an Italian ballet dancer and vice-director of the ballet school of Milan's Teatro alla Scala.
Berlusconi never finished her university studies and instead joined her father's Fininvest in 1996.
did_you_know_facts: Her younger son and her father, both named Silvio, share the same birthday, September 29.

name: Wang Junshi & family
about: Wang Junshi cofounded Ginlong Technologies, a manufacturer of solar inverters, with wife Lin Yibei and son Wang Yiming in 2005.
He stepped down as director and deputy general manager in 2021. Yiming now chairs the firm.
Wang was a high school teacher earlier in his career.

name: Ben Navarro
about: The former Citigroup banker cofounded Sherman Financial Group in 1998 with fellow billionaire Brett Hildebrand and built it into a credit card and debt collection empire.
One of Sherman's key assets is the Las Vegas-based lender Credit One, which says it has doled out more than 18 million credit cards to date.
Despite a nearly identical name and logo to the better known Capital One Bank, Navarro's firm is entirely separate and caters mainly to low-credit borrowers.
Since 2021, the Charleston-based billionaire has spent more than $350 million buying up property around the city, including a stadium and historic hotel.
Navarro's daughter, Emma Navarro, is one of the top-ranked tennis players in the U.S.
Navarro has spent over $300 million to buy two professional tennis tournaments, in Cincinnati and Charleston; Credit One now sponsors both.
did_you_know_facts: Navarro tried to buy the Carolina Panthers in 2018, but lost out to hedge fund mogul David Tepper.
His late father Frank Navarro (d. 2021) was an Ivy League football coach and the star of the Norman Rockwell painting, "The Recruit."

name: Frank VanderSloot
about: Frank VanderSloot founded and runs Melaleuca, which makes more than 450 products ranging from health supplements to eco-friendly household cleaners.
Melaleuca sells direct from the factory to more than one million consumers every month through its online store.
Born into a poor farming family, VanderSloot ran the farm while his father worked a railroad job, then lived in a laundromat to pay his way through school.
He is a major landowner -- with an estimated 148,000 acres across Idaho, Utah and Montana -- and he runs a leading purebred angus cattle operation.
He is also an active political donor, giving millions to Republicans. He was a national finance co-chair for Mitt Romney's two presidential bids.

forbes_list.list: The Richest Person In Every State (2025)

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Brigham Young University

did_you_know_facts: VanderSloot is an avid indoor rower and holds six world records.
In 2019, VanderSloot started what is now a $1 million fund to help Idahoans defend themselves from aggressive medical debt collection tactics.

name: Daniel Pritzker
about: Daniel Pritzker is one of 13 billionaire heirs in the Chicago-based Pritzker family, whose best known creation is Hyatt Hotels.
A filmmaker, in 2019 Pritzker released Bolden, a biographical drama about New Orleans trumpeter Buddy Bolden, after over a decade working on it.
He made a silent film, Louis, about the life of Louis Armstrong, which was released to critical praise in 2010.
Daniel's brother Tom is the chairman of Hyatt Hotels; his sister Gigi is a film producer.
Daniel's charitable foundation, named after his father and Hyatt founder Jay Pritzker, pledged $100 million to California community colleges in 2020.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctor of Jurisprudence, Northwestern University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Tufts University

did_you_know_facts: Pritzker used to own Jerry Garcia's guitar; he auctioned it and donated the proceeds, $3.2 million, to the Southern Poverty Law Center.
Pritzker is also a guitarist and the primary songwriter for Sonia Dada, a fusion rock and soul band.

name: Huang Xiaofen & family
about: Huang Xiaofen is a major shareholder and a director of Shenzhen Kinwong Electronics.
Her husband, Liu Shaobo, heads the company. He previously worked for a state-owned company in Shenzhen early in his career.
Kinwong grew out of a joint venture backed by that government business.

name: Martin Lau
about: Martin Lau is the president of Chinese internet giant Tencent.
He became a billionaire for the first time in 2017 after Tencent shares jumped by a third over the previous year.
Beijing-born Lau grew up in Hong Kong and was educated in the U.S. He left Goldman Sachs to join Tencent as chief strategy and investment officer in 2005.
Tencent's growth was hit amid China's crackdown on tech companies in 2021, but it managed to make a comeback by introducing new games and selling more ads on the popular WeChat messaging app.
He sits on the board of several Hong Kong- and overseas-listed companies, such as online discount retailer Vipshop.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Stanford University; Bachelor of Science in Engineering, University of Michigan; Master of Business Administration, Kellogg School of Management

did_you_know_facts: Lau was once nicknamed the "Salary King" for making his fortune as an employee rather than a founder.
After dominating the Chinese instant-messaging sector with its WeChat app, Tencent grew to become one of the world's largest purveyors of online gaming.

name: William Stone
about: Bill Stone started financial-software firm SS&C Technologies in 1986 with the $20,000 he had saved from his days as a KPMG executive.
His product became popular among asset managers, bankers and insurers who wanted to electronically manage their books.
He guided the firm to an IPO in 1996, but the dot-com crash nearly crippled the company in 2001.
Stone refocused and added services such as data centers, then took the company private in 2005.
In 2011, a resurgent SS&C went public again; Stone remains the firm's largest individual shareholder, with a 15% stake.
did_you_know_facts: Between June 1999 and December 2001, SS&C went from 610 to 250 employees, as the markets crashed.
The Evansville, Indiana native was the captain of his high school football team.

name: William Chisholm
about: William "Bill" Chisholm, a private equity executive, is leading a group of investors to buy the Boston Celtics NBA team for $6.1 billion.
Chisholm is the managing partner of STG Partners, a software-focused Silicon Valley private equity firm with about $12 billion in assets under management.
He cofounded Symphony Technology Group, the predecessor to STG, in 2002 with software billionaire Romesh Wadhwani.
Chisholm has worked in Silicon Valley for decades but grew up near Boston and has been a lifelong Celtics fan.
The Celtics' current CEO and governor, Wyc Grousbeck, will stay in his roles through the 2027-2028 season.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Dartmouth College; Master of Business Administration, The Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: Prior to Symphony Technology Group, Chisholm worked in venture capital and as a management consultant at Bain & Co.
Chisholm was a member of the varsity soccer team at Dartmouth College that won Ivy League titles in 1988 and 1990.

name: Tung Chee Hwa
about: Tung Chee Hwa is the eldest son of shipping magnate Tung Chao Yung, who founded what became one of Hong Kong's largest shipping companies.
After running Orient Overseas for 14 years, Chee Hwa handed over the reins to younger brother Chee Chen in order to serve as Hong Kong's first chief executive.
In 2018 the two brothers sold their entire 68.7% stake to China shipping giant COSCO, pocketing $4.3 billion.
His two sons, Alan and Andrew, were both executives at Orient Overseas.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, University of Liverpool

name: Chen Jiancheng
about: Chen Jiancheng is group chairman of Wolong Group, a manufacturer of motors, generators and drive controls; the multinational company also has interests in renewable energy and related resources.
The group's subsidiaries include three public companies, Wolong Electric Drive Group, Wolong New Energy Group and Brook Crompton Holdings.
Chen's daughter Yanni is chairman and CEO of Wolong Holding Group; his son-in-law, Pang Xinyuan, chairs Wolong Electric Drive Group and Brook Crompton.

name: Han Tao
about: Han Tao chairs Goldenmax International Group, a supplier of laminate products used to make printed circuit boards.
Han worked at a watch parts factory in Hangzhou from 1977-83, attended university and later worked for the company that became Goldenmax.
Goldenmax International Group listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2011.

name: Rajan Raheja & family
about: Low-profile Rajan Raheja hails from the sprawling Raheja property clan in Mumbai.
After a family split he went on to build a separate diversified empire that includes interests in cement, batteries and cable television.
Raheja's biggest asset is listed auto battery maker Exide Industries.
He also owns listed cable television unit Hathway Cable Datacom, in which Mukesh Ambani's Reliance Industries has a majority stake.
His son, Akshay Raheja, sits on the board of Raheja QBE General Insurance, a joint venture between his listed Prism Johnson and Australia's QBE Insurance.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Mumbai

name: Jenny Love Meyer
about: Jenny Love Meyer is chief culture officer and EVP at Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores, a truck stop and convenience store chains with over 600 locations in 42 states.
Her parents, Tom and Judy Love, founded the company in 1964 using a $5,000 loan from Tom's parents.
Brothers Frank and Greg Love are co-CEOs of the $21.6 billion (est. sales) company.
She is on the board of trustees for the Children's Miracle Network, a nonprofit that raises fund for children's hospitals in the U.S. and Canada.

name: Greg Love
about: Greg Love and brother Frank are co-CEOs of Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores, a truck stop and convenience store chains with over 600 locations in 42 states.
Love started working for the company in high school.
The $21.6 billion (est. sales) company was founded by his parents, Tom and Judy Love, in 1964.
Sister Jenny Love Meyer is chief culture officer and EVP; sister Laura has no role at the company.

name: Laura Love
about: Laura Love and her three siblings own Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores, a truck stop and convenience store chains with over 600 locations in 42 states.
Her parents, Tom and Judy Love, founded the company in 1964 using a $5,000 loan from Tom's parents.
Brothers Frank and Greg Love are co-CEOs of the $21.6 billion (est. sales) company.
Sister Jenny Love Meyers is chief culture officer and EVP.

name: Frank Love
about: Frank Love and his brother Greg are co-CEOs of Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores, a truck stop and convenience store chains with over 600 locations in 42 states.
The $21.6 billion (est. sales) company was founded by his parents, Tom and Judy Love, in 1964.
Sister Jenny Love Meyer is chief culture officer and EVP; sister Laura has no role at the company.

name: Selina Stihl
about: Selina Stihl is a granddaughter Andreas Stihl, the German founder of the famous chainsaw company which bears his name.
She joined the family business in 2011 in Brazil as vice president of Finance and Administration and eventually became the CFO there.
Back in Germany, she's now deputy chair of the advisory board at Stihl, which saw $5.8 billion in sales in 2023.
Prior to joining the family business, she worked as an accountant for Deloitte in London.
The company was founded in 1926 and now employs 19,805 people.

name: Jin Xin
about: Jin Xin chairs Dajin Heavy Industry, a supplier of offshore wind power equipment.

name: Zhou Xiaoping
about: Zhou Xiaoping is the chairman and CEO of Changzhou Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems.
Zhou and her late father Zhou Bajin cofounded the company in 1993.
Its customers include Volkswagen, Daimler, Mercedes-Benz, BMW, and General Motors.

name: Zhuo Jun
about: Zhuo Jun took over a substantial stake of Shenzhen Kinwong Electronic in 2013 when her husband, Shen Jitang, passed away.
Founded in 1993, the Shanghai-listed company is one of China's largest printed circuit board makers. It announced its plan for a dual listing in Hong Kong in 2025.
Zhuo sits on the board of Kinwong; her younger brother Zhuo Yong serves as vice chairman.
She was a clerk at Heung Yee Kuk, a statutory advisory body representing interests in the New Territories, Hong Kong, for 4 years after high school.
Kinwong is building a printed circuit board manufacturing base in Thailand, its first overseas site, slated to come onstream in 2026.

name: Tang Jie
about: Tang Jie is a cofounder of Chinese AI firm Knowledge Atlas Technology.
The company, also known as Z.ai, went public in Hong Kong in January 2026.
Tang launched the company in 2019 with fellow billionaire Liu Debing, who serves as Z.ai's chairman.
Tang is a professor at Beijing's Tsinghua University and a leading researcher in the fields of artificial general intelligence, data mining, social networks and knowledge graphs.
Z.ai was added to the U.S. government's Entity List in March 2025, barring it from acquiring advanced American technology.

name: John Coates
about: John Coates is the co-CEO of U.K. company Bet365, one of the world's largest online gambling businesses.
He joined his billionaire sister and co-CEO, Denise, in 2001 to launch Bet365 after she sold some of their father's betting shops.
Bet365 has since become a global player, with over 53 million customers across 200 countries; John owns a quarter of the firm.
In July 2015, he became the vice chairman of English Premier League's Stoke City Football Club, in which Bet365 has a majority stake.
did_you_know_facts: Coates studied law at Bristol University and started his career as an attorney.
Bet365 handles more than $65 billion of bets a year.

name: Harish Ahuja
about: Harish Ahuja is chairman of Shahi Exports, an Indian apparel manufacturer and exporter operating across eight Indian states, including Karnataka and Haryana.
It has 50 manufacturing units and three processing mills across eight Indian states.
The company is a big employer of women, who account for 70% of its workforce of 100,000 people.
The company's marquee list of clients includes international brands such Calvin Klein, Gap and H&M.
did_you_know_facts: His son Anand is married to Bollywood actress Sonam Kapoor.
Shahi Exports was founded in 1974 by his mother Sarla Ahuja.
In September 2024, he bought a home in London's Notting Hill for $27 million.

name: Alfred Gantner
about: Alfred Gantner is the cofounder of Partners Group, a Swiss private equity firm that manages more than $131 billion.
Gantner started Partners Group in 1996 after stints at UBS and Goldman Sachs, where he met cofounders Marcel Erni and Urs Wietlisbach.
The firm went public in Switzerland in 2006 and the trio each own roughly 5% of the stock.
Gantner earned his MBA from the Brigham Young University Marriott School of Management, Utah.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Brigham Young University

did_you_know_facts: In 2021, Partners Group banned its staff from using the word "deal," asking them to think more like founders and less like short-term investors.

name: Urs Wietlisbach
about: Urs Wietlisbach is the cofounder of Partners Group, a Swiss private equity firm that has more than $131 billion in assets under management.
Wietlisbach started Partners Group in 1996 with Marcel Erni and Alfred Gantner, both of whom he met while working at Goldman Sach's Zurich office.
The trio took their firm public a decade later; Wietlisbach currently owns roughly 5% of the company's stock.
Wietlisbach is a member of the board of trustees of Blue Earth Foundation, which focuses on impact investing globally.
