did_you_know_facts: Edens began construction on Brightline West, his second railway, in 2024. The $12 billion project line will be the first true high-speed train in the U.S.

name: Igor Rotenberg
about: Igor Rotenberg is the son of billionaire Arkady Rotenberg, a close friend of Russian President Vladimir Putin.

Rotenberg, once a junior partner in his father's business, used to control drilling company Gazprom Burenie and collected dividends from the company worth almost $560 million from 2017 until 2021, when he sold his shares.
He was also a shareholder in Platon Electronic Toll Collection system, which processes the collections of tolls for vehicles over 12 tons, and Aviapark, one of Europe's biggest shopping malls.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master, Higher School of Privatization and Business

did_you_know_facts: After US Treasury Department imposed sanctions against his father in 2014, Rotenberg bought his father's stakes in some assets.
Rotenberg was once a top-manager of state-owned Russian Railways.

name: Alessandra Garavoglia
about: Alessandra Garavoglia is a director of the board of Campari Group, one of the world's largest alcoholic beverage companies.
Campari's brands includes Skyy Vodka, Wild Turkey, Aperol and Campari.
Garavoglia inherited her stake in the company from her parents. Her mother, Rosa Anna Magno Garavoglia, died in 2016.
She now owns an estimated 25% of the company, which listed on the Milan Stock Exchange in 2001.
Her late father, Domenico, was a long-time employee before the last remaining heir of the Campari family passed the company to him.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Social Sciences, University of Milan

did_you_know_facts: Garavoglia wrote her college dissertation on domestic life in Louisa May Alcott's American classic, "Little Women."
Garavoglia speaks English, French and Italian.

name: Katharina Otto-Bernstein
about: Writer and filmmaker Katharina Otto-Bernstein is the daughter of late Werner Otto, who turned his mail-order business in Hamburg into a global empire.
She inherited a minority stake in Otto Group and its more than 40 companies in retail (Crate and Barrel), real estate and financial services.
She's also a shareholder of ECE, the family's commercial real estate company focused on shopping centers. Her brother Alexander is CEO.
She, her mother Maren and brother Alexander share a 15% stake in Paramount Group, which owns and manages office properties in the U.S.
did_you_know_facts: Katharina is a member of the board of directors of the Metropolitan Opera as well as the International Council of the Guggenheim Museum.
She produced a 2016 documentary on controversial photographer Robert Mapplethorpe.

name: Xue Jiping
about: Xue Jiping is chairman of Jiangsu Zhongtian Technology, a supplier of optical fiber communication products.
Zhongtian's predecessor business was a small collective factory that made bricks and tiles.
ZTT Group, Xue's listed arm, entered the field of optical fiber communication in the early 1990s.
ZTT went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange on Oct 24, 2002.

name: Dwight Schar
about: Dwight Schar is the chairman of Virginia-based NVR, one of the largest homebuilders in the United States, with nearly $9 billion in annual revenue.
He founded NVHomes in 1980 and borrowed big to acquire his former employer and competitor, Ryan Homes, in 1987. The combined company was called NVR.
NVR declared bankruptcy in 1992, but reorganized and recovered the next year. Today, the company builds homes in 15 states.
Schar bought a minority stake in the NFL's Washington Redskins (now called Washington Commanders) in 2003 for $200 million.
He sold it in 2021 for approximately $320 million amid a court battle with majority owner Daniel Snyder.
did_you_know_facts: Schar has sold over $1 billion of NVR stock since 2003.
A former junior high school teacher, Schar has donated millions to his alma mater, Ashland University, and to his children's colleges.

name: Ana Lucia de Mattos Barretto Villela
about: Ana Lucia de Mattos Barretto Villela is a member of one of Brazil's oldest banking families.
Her great-grandfather founded the bank Itau, which merged with Unibanco in 2008 to form Itau-Unibanco, Latin America's biggest private sector bank.
She is one of the largest individual shareholders of Itausa, the bank's holding company, and is vice chairwoman of their board of directors.
Her grandfather founded Duratex, a publicly-traded Brazilian maker of wood paneling and bathroom fixtures; she is a shareholder.
She became a shareholder of the bank when she was 8 years old as her parents died in a plane crash in 1982.
did_you_know_facts: Villela was named the first female board member of Itau Unibanco, Latin America's largest bank by market value, when she was 44.
She and her husband co-founded the nonprofit Alana, which focuses on promoting the welfare of children.
quote: It is so obvious that children need nature as much as nature needs children. However, we forgot this obvious fact and swept it under the carpet.

name: Michael Polsky
about: Ukrainian immigrant Michael Polsky founded Chicago-based Invenergy, one of the nation's biggest developers of renewable energy projects, 33 gigawatts so far.
Invenergy is seeking to build the $11 billion, 800-mile transmission line across Kansas and Missouri called Grain Belt Expresss.
Polsky made an early fortune selling natural gas generator SkyGen to Calpine for $450 million in 2001.
Polsky has sold big multi-billion-dollar stakes in Invenergy to Blackstone and Canadian pension fund Caisse de Depot et Placement du Quebec.
In 2006 an Illinois divorce court ordered him to pay wife Maya $180 million.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of Chicago Booth School of Business

did_you_know_facts: Polsky has given and pledged more than $150 million to the University of Chicago.
quote: "When you have a mission, a conviction, you perform on a completely different level. You believe so strongly, you don't take no for an answer."

name: Yvonne Bauer
about: Yvonne Bauer runs Bauer Media Group, which has been in her family for five generations since its founding as a small printing company in 1875. Today, its business lines include print publishing, audio and online media.
Europe's largest magazine company, it focuses on women's content and counts over 600 titles worldwide, including InTouch and Grazia.
Yvonne Bauer is the second-youngest child of Heinz Heinrich Bauer. She received 85% of the company, while her three sisters each received 5%.
In 2020, Bauer expanded its reach in the German newspaper industry with the acquisition of Mitteldeutsche Zeitung in Halle for an undisclosed sum.
Prior to joining her family's company in 2005, Bauer apprenticed at publishing House Hoffmann und Campe.
did_you_know_facts: In the digital sphere, Bauer Group runs over 400 websites and apps, including The Debrief and Lecker.de.
In 2014, she married Enno Koch, a German television journalist and producer; the couple has twins born in 2015.

name: Alain Taravella
about: Alain Taravella is chairman and CEO of Altarea Cogedim, France's third-largest real estate development firm.
Headquartered in Paris, the firm also operates in Spain and Italy and boasts a shopping center portfolio and revenue of about $3 billion.
Taravella co-founded the firm as Altarea SA in 1994 and retains 45% ownership of the group.
Taravella took the firm public in 2004 and three years later acquired Cogedim to form Altarea Cogedim Group.

name: Zeng Chaoyi
about: Zeng Chaoyi is a director of Tianshan Aluminum Group, a Chinese supplier of aluminum products.
Tianshan's shares trade at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange; it's headquartered in Xinjiang.
Shimge Pump Industry Group acquired Tianshan Aluminum Group in 2020 in a backdoor listing and changed its name to Tianshan Aluminum Group.
Brother Zeng Chaoyi's brother Zeng Chaolin is Tianshan's chairman and also a billionaire.

name: Chen Tei-fu
about: Chen Tei-Fu and his wife, Oi-Lin Chen, cofounded herbal-products maker Sunrider, which is now led by their five children.
Sunrider products are distributed in nearly 50 countries through a mix of franchises and company-owned stores.
He owns Sunworld-branded hotels in Beijing; the SLS Hotel in Beverly Hills, California; and St. Ermin's Hotel in London.
Chen's vast collection of Chinese art is on display at Sunrider headquarters in Torrance, California, near Los Angeles.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Drop Out, Brigham Young University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Kaohsiung Medical University

did_you_know_facts: In 1975 he was a starving college student in Utah, buying 20-cent hamburgers by the bunch at a weekly promotion so he could freeze them to eat later on.
His given name, Tei-Fu, means "receiving a fortune." He says his 19 grandchildren are his biggest fortune.
quote: Doing business is like playing chess. While making a move, plan ahead your next move.

name: Kenneth Feld & family
about: Kenneth Feld owns live entertainment company Feld Entertainment, the parent company of Disney on Ice, Monster Jam and other shows.
Feld Entertainment grew out of Ringling Bros. circus, which was shut down in 2017 due to falling ticket sales.
His father, Irvin, bought Ringling Bros. circus in 1967 for $8 million.
Kenneth Feld took over in 1984 following his father's death.
Since then, he has worked to diversify beyond the Big Top. A Disney on Ice version of the hit movie Frozen has been particularly popular.
did_you_know_facts: While Feld remains CEO, he's preparing his three daughters to succeed him as ringmaster.
Feld has donated $1 million to Florida State University, which boasts one of the only two college circuses in the U.S.
quote: My goal was to grow, and that wasn't always consistent with what everyone else in the company wanted to do.

name: Li Gaiteng
about: Li Gaiteng is the founder and chairman of Shanghai Flyco Electrical Appliance, a maker of personal care appliances such as electric razors and hair dryers.
His wife Lin Yu'e is an executive director at Flyco, which is majority owned by Li.
Li started the business after working as a motorcycle repairman.

name: Henry Sy Jr
about: Henry Sy Jr. is co-vice chairman of SM Investments, a conglomerate founded by his late father, Henry Sy Sr.
He also serves as chairman of SM Prime, the group's property arm with interests in malls, residences, offices, hotels and convention centers.
He is the eldest son of the founder; his older sisters and three younger brothers are also all involved in the business.
In 2017 he set up Big Boss Cement, entering an industry that benefitted from former President Duterte's massive infrastructure push.
In 2022, SM Investments agreed to acquire Philippine Geothermal Production in a $304 million all-share deal in a bid to lower its carbon footprint.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, De La Salle University

did_you_know_facts: Sy was CEO of the National Grid Corporation of the Philippines, a private power operator; he stepped down in 2016 and is now the vice chairman.
He is a devout Christian and is nicknamed "Big Boy" among business circles from being the eldest son of the founder.
Data Lake, a data company cofounded by Henry, partnered with Elon Musk's Starlink in 2022 to bring the satellite internet provider's services to the Philippines.

name: Lam Kong
about: Lam Kong chairs Hong Kong-listed China Medical System, which distributes drugs to thousands of hospitals around the country.
Lam founded the company in 1995, almost a decade after graduating from Zhanjiang Medical College.
China Medical went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2010.
China Medical System is the largest shareholder of Shanghai-listed Tibet Rhodiola Pharmaceutical.
China Medical System is headquartered in Shenzhen.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Guangdong Medical College

name: Julio Bozano
about: Julio Bozano made a fortune in banking. In 2000, he sold Banco Bozano, Simonsen to Spain's Banco Santander Central Hispano for a reported $550 million.
His investments include a coffee plantation, shopping centers and a stake in a jet engine maker.
Octogenarian Bozano controls Bozano Investimentos, a large and diversified Brazilian private equity firm.
He invested in low-cost Brazilian airline, Azul Linhas Aereas, which was founded by JetBlue founder David Neeleman and went public in April 2017.
A thoroughbred horse owner, Bozano owns more than 300 mares in farms around the world.
did_you_know_facts: Bozano is an art collector and owns paintings by artists including Picasso and contemporary Brazilian painter Beatriz Milhares.

name: Pierre van der Mersch & family
about: Pierre van der Mersch, dubbed the Belgian Warren Buffett, controls investment company Brederode.
He began his career as a bank clerk in 1958, and in the 1980s began building his fortune by taking control of a series of publicly-traded shell companies.
His asset management style focuses on taking long positions in undervalued companies.

name: Jim Crane
about: Jim Crane led an investment group that paid $615 million in 2011 for MLB's Houston Astros and a minority stake in a regional sports network.
The value of the team has quadrupled since Crane's acquisition. Crane owns an estimated 40% stake.
Crane pocketed more than $300 million when he sold his freight logistics firm Eagle Global Logistics to Apollo Global Management in 2007.
Crane launched another logistics business, Crane Worldwide, in 2008; annual revenue is more than $900 million.
Crane owns the Floridian National Golf Club, whose members include former presidents Barack Obama and George Bush.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Central Missouri State University

name: Charles Bronfman
about: In 2000, Charles Bronfman and his nephew Edgar Bronfman Jr. sold their family's spirits and alcohol giant Seagram to Vivendi for $30 billion.
His father Samuel Bronfman, a Russian immigrant to Canada, started a small distillery in 1924 and eventually bought out competitor Seagram.
Since the sale, Charles, who once co-chaired Seagram, has turned toward philanthropy, authoring two books on the matter and signing The Giving Pledge.
Bronfman has given away or pledged at least $350 million, mostly toward promotion of Canadian culture and the Jewish community's connection to Israel.
Bronfman's son, Stephen, runs Claridge, the Montreal-based private investment firm that Charles founded in 1987.
did_you_know_facts: Bronfman is one of the main benefactors of Taglit-Birthright Israel, which sends Jewish youth from North America on free educational tours of Israel.
Bronfman's daughter Ellen and her husband Andrew Hauptman own the major league soccer team the Chicago Fire.

name: Bennett Dorrance
about: The grandson of John T. Dorrance, the inventor of condensed soup, Bennett Dorrance owns a 15% stake in Campbell Soup.
Dorrance retired from the Campbell's board in 2022, ending a 33 year stint.
Dorrance is a founding partner of DMB Associates, a real estate development firm with projects in Arizona, California and Hawaii.
A licensed pilot, Dorrance owns a private hangar in Scottsdale, Arizona that sometimes houses his vintage car collection.
The Dorrance Scholarship, established by Bennett and Jacquelynn Dorrance in 1999, has supported 150-plus first-generation college students in Arizona.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Arizona

name: Jack Cogen
about: Jack Cogen is a director and early investor in cloud computing company CoreWeave.
CoreWeave went public in 2025 at an approximately $23 billion valuation; Cogen owns approximately 5%.
CoreWeave was founded in 2017 as a crypto firm; it now sells computing power for AI to companies including Microsoft and OpenAI.
Cogen is a private investor in early-stage companies; before that he was founder and CEO of greenhouse gas asset manager Natsource.
He was also a director at natural gas hedge fund Hudson Ridge Asset Management, where two of CoreWeave's cofounders worked.

name: Sergei Gordeev
about: Sergei Gordeev is an investor in startups including Hyperloop One, a U.S. highspeed-travel startup.
In 2022 Gordeev resigned as CEO of PIK SZ, the biggest Russian real estate developer where he has about 60% shares.
In 1995, he founded Rosbuilding, which bought shares of different plants.
He bought a 20% stake in home builder PIK from billionaire Suleiman Kerimov in 2013, and eventually became the controlling shareholder.
He made his fortune buying up shares of industrial companies in Moscow and then turning factories into office complexes.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Togliatti Academy of Management

did_you_know_facts: Gordeev, who is interested in architecture, designed his own house in a London suburb.
Gordeev bought a factory once owned by a theater director, founded a theater there and for many years sponsored its troupe.
quote: We set ourselves a goal to become something like Apple in residential construction. We pay great attention to product and design.

name: Kenneth Hao
about: Kenneth Hao is chairman of Silver Lake, a private equity firm specializing in making technology investments.
Silver Lake is based in Silicon Valley and oversees about $100 billion.
Hao joined Silver Lake in 2000. He previously worked as a managing director at Hambrecht & Quist.
Hao led Silver Lake's expansion into Asia, opening offices in China and Japan and leading Silver Lake's profitable investment in Alibaba Group.
Hao is a director of ServiceMax, SMART Global Holdings, SolarWinds and Symantec, and previously served on the board of Broadcom.

name: Greg Mondre
about: Greg Mondre is co-CEO of Silver Lake, a private equity firm specializing in making technology investments.
Silver Lake is based in Silicon Valley and oversees about $100 billion.
Mondre joined Silver Lake in 1999 after stints at Goldman Sachs and private equity firm TPG.
Mondre has worked on deals for Motorola Solutions, Red Ventures, WP Engine, GoodRx and GoDaddy.

name: Egon Durban
about: Egon Durban is co-CEO of Silver Lake, a private equity firm that specializes in technology investments.
Durban joined Silver Lake in 1999 as a founding principal; prior to that he worked in Morgan Stanley's investment banking division.
Durban, who owns an estimated 17% of Silver Lake, is known for orchestrating the firm's wildly successful investments in Dell Technologies and Skype.
Silver Lake manages about $100 billion of assets.
Durban is a board member of multiple companies including Dell Technologies, Twitter, self-driving car firm Waymo and mixed martial arts promoter UFC.

name: Chu Lam Yiu
about: Chu Lam Yiu is co-chairman of fragrances and tobacco flavoring supplier Huabao International Holdings.
She founded the company in 1996 and took it public on Hong Kong through a "backdoor listing" a decade later.
Chu's son Lam Ka Yu became co-chairman in June 2021.

name: David Teoh
about: David Teoh is the founder of Australia's TPG Telecom. He emigrated from Malaysia in 1986.
A series of smart acquisitions transformed the company from a computer retailer into a major internet service provider in Australia.
Teoh's listed internet service provider TPG merged with Vodafone Hutchison Australia in 2020 and was relisted as TPG Telecom.
He resigned as executive chairman in 2021.
His Simba Telecom (formerly TPG Singapore) is looking to buy Singapore telecoms outfit M1 In a $1.1 billion deal, pending regulatory approval.
did_you_know_facts: Famously publicity-shy, Teoh managed to avoid all media photographers until one staked out his Sydney home for three days in 2015.
His wife Vicky and their four sons have launched more than a dozen startups. They've also started a property investment company.

name: Mike Repole
about: Mike Repole cofounded sports drink BodyArmor in 2011.
Coca-Cola bought 15% of BodyArmor in 2018, then purchased the rest in 2021 for $5.6 billion, the company's largest acquisition of a brand.
BodyArmor's investors included tennis star Naomi Osaka and the late Kobe Bryant, who discovered the brand while rehabbing from a torn Achilles tendon.
The son of a waiter and a seamstress, Repole studied sports management at St. John's before working in sales for a small company, Mistic Beverage.
Repole also cofounded Glaceau, maker of the popular brands Vitaminwater and Smartwater, which he also sold to Coca-Cola, in 2007.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, St. John's University

name: Alec Gores
about: Private equity mogul Alec Gores cofounded the Gores Group and has sponsored more than a dozen SPACs since 2015 as an early adopter of the blank-check frenzy that exploded in 2020.
His SPACs have orchestrated mergers to take companies like Luminar Technologies, United Wholesale Mortgage and Twinkie-maker Hostess Brands public.
Gores and his younger brother Tom, also a billionaire, immigrated to America from Israel with their parents and four other siblings in 1968.
The brothers worked together at the beginning of their careers but went their separate ways in 1995 and have occasionally competed for buyout deals.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Western Michigan University

did_you_know_facts: Gores' first job after immigrating to the United States at age 15 was bagging groceries for 25 cents an hour at his uncle's store in Flint, Michigan.
Alec's and Tom's brother Sam is the chairman of the Paradigm Talent Agency, which lists Coldplay and Ed Sheeran among its clients.
quote: "I love this country. I love what it brings. When you come from a different place, and you get to see the freedom that we have, the opportunity that we have -- it's insane."

name: Riaz Valani
about: Riaz Valani was a general partner at Global Asset Capital, LLC and the first person to invest in electronic cigarette manufacturer Juul.
Valani invested a few million dollars in Juul during its early years, giving him an estimated 20% stake in the company.
When tobacco giant Altria bought a 35% stake in Juul in 2018, Valani reportedly got a pre-tax $2.6 billion dividend payout, according to a book about Juul.
In November 2020, Valani spent $40 million on a Malibu estate formerly owned by Johnny Carson.

name: Zhang Xingang
about: Zhang Xingang is the chairman and CEO of Shanghai-listed semiconductor maker Yuanjie Semiconductor Technology.
He founded the company in 2013, and took it public almost a decade later in 2022, raising $219 million.
Zhang, a U.S. citizen, worked as a researcher for fiber optic components maker Luminent and telecommunications product company Source Photonics before striking out on his own.
The company plans to list its shares in Hong Kong as well.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Ph.D, University of Southern California; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Tsinghua Univeristy

name: Haluk Bayraktar
about: Haluk Bayraktar owns 47.5% of Turkish unmanned military drone manufacturer Baykar. He co-owns it with his brother Selçuk and serves as the CEO.
The company was founded by his father Özdemir in 1984 to make parts for the Turkish auto industry and began making unmanned aerial vehicles in the 2000s.
Baykar recorded sales of $1.9 billion in 2023 and its exports rose to $1.8 billion in 2024, thanks to contracts with militaries in Europe, Africa and the Middle East.
Baykar's most famous export, the Bayraktar drone, has been used so successfully by Ukrainian troops that it inspired a popular folk song.

name: Kalanithi Maran
about: Politician's son Kalanithi Maran dabbled in his family's modest publishing business before launching Sun TV Network in 1993.
Sun is now a regional television heavyweight with 37 channels reaching more than 140 million households in India.
In June 2024 it launched a Hindi entertainment channel called Sun Neo.
Maran's other interests include newspapers, radio and direct-to-home television.
His wife, Kavery, is an executive director at Sun TV Network and oversees content.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of Scranton

did_you_know_facts: Maran and his brother Dayanidhi, a former telecom minister, were embroiled in a telecom corruption case but were cleared of all charges.
Sun owns Sunrisers Hyderabad, an Indian Premier League cricket team.
In August 2025 Sun TV Network said that the legal notice served in June by his younger brother Dayanidhi, alleging share transfer disputes in 2003, was withdrawn.
quote: I don't take competition lightly. Big or small, we nail them down before they can grow in size.

name: Bent Jensen & Family
about: Bent Jensen is the owner and CEO of Linak, a $680 million (revenue) Danish company that manufactures and sells linear actuators.
Linear actuators are devices that convert power into linear motion and are used in industrial equipment, furniture and hospital beds.
Jensen's grandfather founded the company in 1907; it originally made pulleys, grinding mills and forges.
Jensen, who received a mechanical engineering degree, joined the firm in 1976 -- with an idea for a new product: the linear actuator.
Today the company has factories in Denmark, the U.S., China and Slovakia.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Southern Denmark

did_you_know_facts: Jensen came up with the idea for linear actuators while talking with a friend from school, who had a disability, about ways to improve his wheelchair.

name: T. Denny Sanford
about: T. Denny Sanford owns First Premier Bank, which specializes in offering credit cards to high-risk borrowers.
The Sioux Falls, South Dakota, bank has just 18 branches, but is one of the largest issuers of Mastercards - many with steep rates and low limits.
An active philanthropist, Sanford says he wants to die broke. To do that he'd have to give away his most valuable asset, First Premier.
Sanford was previously investigated for child pornography after photos of nude underage girls were discovered in his email.
The investigation was closed and charges were never brought. Sanford said his email was hacked.

forbes_list.list: The Richest Person In Every State (2025)

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Minnesota

did_you_know_facts: Sanford has given more than $1 billion to Sanford Health, a group of 43 nonprofit hospitals formerly called the Sioux Valley Health System.
Sanford's children's education initiatives include one for young boys and girls which he hopes will cut America's divorce rate by 50% in the next 50 years.

name: Alexander Skorobogatko
about: Alexander Skorobogatko and partner Alexander Ponomarenko started out with sea ports and banking and then moved into airport construction.
In 2013 the two, with Arkady Rotenberg, a judo partner of President Vladimir Putin, won a tender to develop Sheremetyevo, the state-owned airport.
The partners and Rotenberg also founded TPS Real Estate, which owns more than half of the real estate in Ocean Plaza, Kiev's biggest shopping center.
In 2023 the center was seized by Ukrainian government.
The two Alexanders first set up a small perfume factory in the Ukraine and then founded a bank in Moscow.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Plekhanov Russian University of Economics

did_you_know_facts: Skorobogatko is a candidate to become a master of sports in judo and sambo.

name: Manuel Puig Rocha
about: Manuel Puig Rocha is the largest individual shareholder of Puig Brands, a fashion and beauty conglomerate which owns Nina Ricci, Carolina Herrera and Charlotte Tilbury.
The company was founded by his grandfather Antonio Puig in 1914, who got his big break with the Milady Lipstick in 1922.
Rocha has been vice president of Puig Brands since 2007, responsible for overseeing its international subsidiaries.
Rocha's father, Antonio, along with his three uncles Mariano, José María and Enrique joined the company in 1950 and helped bolster its growth.
Today at least 14 family members control Puig Brands.

name: Nicola Bulgari
about: Nicola Bulgari is vice chairman of luxury goods brand Bulgari, which was founded by his great-grandfather.
Bulgari established itself as a global luxury brand in jewelry, watches, fragrances, apparel, hotels and resorts.
In 2011, the Bulgari family sold its controlling stake to luxury goods conglomerate LVMH for $5.2 billion in cash and stock.
Nicola Bulgari is well known for his car collection, which includes mostly American cars from 1920s to the 1940s.
did_you_know_facts: He once turned down an offer from Andy Warhol to exchange a painting for Bulgari jewels. "It was the worst deal of my life," he said.
Bulgari built a 21-acre complex in Allentown, Pennsylvania with 7 warehouses and 4 restoration shops, home to roughly 125 cars.

name: Rolf Gerling
about: Rolf Gerling inherited insurer Gerling Konzern, showed little interest in managing it and saw the legacy plunge into turmoil.
His grandfather Robert founded the business in 1904 and his father, Hans, expanded it into a global insurance group. Hans died in 1992.
Mismanagement, losses from the September 11 attacks and costly asbestos claims led Rolf to sell the company for an estimated $1 billion in 2005.
His portfolio includes real estate through companies like DufourIm AG, which is headed by long-time Gerling confidant Heino von Have.
A passionate environmentalist, Gerling leads a withdrawn life in Switzerland.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Zurich

did_you_know_facts: In the 1990s, Gerling was instrumental in getting 50 insurance companies to sign a UN pledge to consider environmental problems in their business practices.
He attended a Montessori school as a child and studied analytical psychology at the C.G. Jung Institute in Zurich.

name: Brett Blundy
about: Brett Blundy is the founder of BBRC, a private investment company which has expanded from its retail roots into property, fund management, agriculture and technology.
He sold some property and retail interests in three IPOs. He's now building a beef cattle empire in northern Australia to feed Asian demand.
He has joined with cattle-station owners in Australia's Northern Territory to fund water supply, enabling properties to carry larger herds.
Fast fashion jewelry retailer Lovisa, which he cofounded in 2010 and boasts 900 stores worldwide, is embroiled in a lawsuit amid allegations of underpayment of staff dating back to 2019.
In 2021 Blundy sold key assets, including property fund Aventus, the listed Universal Store as well as the unlisted lingerie chain Honey Birdette to the Playboy Group.
did_you_know_facts: Blundy's interest in business started early. He grew up on a small farm near Melbourne where he and his four siblings would pick mushrooms to sell from a roadside stall for five cents a pound.
His career dream was to be a pilot, but that was thwarted when he failed the final year of school.
At age 20, Blundy bought a run-down record store in a suburb called Packenham with a friend. The business failed, and they had to take on day jobs to support it.
quote: I'm biased towards using your own energy, your own activity, taking care of yourself, making your own decisions.

name: Thomas Steyer
about: Tom Steyer spent 26 years running hedge fund Farallon Capital; he sold his stake in 2012 and switched his focus to politics and the environment.
The San Francisco resident has spent over $320 million in federal elections since 2010?plus another $340 million on his own presidential campaign in 2020.
He announced a campaign for governor of California in Nov. 2025.
Steyer and his wife, Kat Taylor, have donated tens of millions of dollars to alma maters Stanford and Yale for "advanced energy" research.
Steyer is a passionate advocate of clean energy and founder of the environmental group NextGen Climate and the green-focused investment firm Galvanize.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Stanford University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Yale University

did_you_know_facts: Steyer was captain of the soccer team at Yale University.
For years, Steyer wore the same dated red wool plaid tie nearly every work day; he told Forbes he had 8 ties of the same design.

name: Ma Bin & family
about: Ma Bin is the founder of Jiangsu Shemar Electric, a manufacturer of power equipment used in transmission substations and distribution systems. He stepped down as chairman in July 2025 and was succeeded by his daughter, Ma Cheng.
Ma, who founded the company in 1996, took it public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2019.
In 2023, Shemar expanded into the U.S. and established its first subsidiary in Memphis, Tennessee.
Today the company's products are used in 100 countries and regions through manufacturers including Hitachi ABB, GE and Siemens.

name: Devi Shetty
about: Cardiac surgeon Devi Shetty founded and runs Bangalore-based hospital chain Narayana Health.
It has 47 healthcare facilities including a hospital in the Cayman Islands.
U.K.-trained Shetty founded Narayana Health as Narayana Hrudayalaya in the year 2000.
Shetty took the company public in 2015. Biopharma billionaire Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw has a small stake in the company.
An ardent advocate of affordable healthcare, Shetty helped design the Yeshasvini scheme, a micro-insurance program in his home state of Karnataka.
did_you_know_facts: He's often seen in his trademark blue surgeon's outfit.
Shetty was Mother Teresa's personal physician.
In November 2025, Narayana Health, inked a deal to acquire UK's Practice Plus Group Hospitals for $248 million.

name: Ni Zugen
about: Ni Zugen is chairman of home appliance maker Kingclean Electronic, which sells wares under the Lexy brand.
Ni worked for a Suzhou-base vacuum cleaner factory before founding his own business in 1994.
Kingclean Electronic listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2015.

name: Dan Wilks
about: Dan and his brother Farris got a combined $3.5 billion (pretax) in 2011 selling their fracking company to a group led by Singapore-based firm Temasek.
The brothers have acquired more than 672,000 acres of land in six different states across the West, becoming America's 12th-largest landowners.
They first founded Wilks Masonry in 1995, following in their stone mason father's footsteps.
In 2002 they went into fracking, launching Frac Tech and growing it into an oil and natural gas giant before cashing out less than a decade later.
The brothers are also investing in oil and gas businesses, including fracking company U.S. Well Services and data provider Dawson Geophysical Company.
did_you_know_facts: Dan Wilks and his brother are active Republican donors.
The brothers reportedly spend four months a year in Montana, working on building homes on their large ranches.

name: Alexandre Grendene Bartelle
about: Alexandre Grendene Bartelle and his twin brother Pedro Grendene Bartelle cofounded Grendene, one of the world's largest sandal makers.
In 2013, he stepped down as Grendene's CEO, but has remained as the company's chairman.
He owns 41% of Grendene, which trades on the Sao Paulo exchange.
Alexandre Grendene Bartelle has investments in various industries, from steel to ethanol production and petrochemicals.
He owns real estate in various states in Brazil as well as in Uruguay.

name: Florian Rehm
about: Florian Rehm is majority owner and chairman of the supervisory board of Mast-Jägermeister SE, a German liquor company known for its herbal ingredients.
The company, founded in 1878 as a vinegar producer, created the famous (and secretive) herbal liquor recipe in 1934.
In 1975, Sidney Frank became the U.S. distributor of Jägermeister, which gained popularity with college students.
In 2015 Mast-Jägermeister acquired Sidney Frank, and through the deal established its U.S. subsidiary.
Privately-held Mast-Jägermeister is now owned by fifth-generation family members.

name: Alexey Repik
about: Alexey Repik is founder of R-Pharm, one of Russia's largest pharmaceutical companies and one of the biggest state contractors.
In 2017 Mitsui & Co., Ltd. acquired 10% shares of R-Pharm for $200 million.
Repik started R-Pharm in 2001 with $40,000 in startup capital, half of which came from his mother.
Repik got his first job in healthcare in 1995.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, The National Research University Higher School of Economics

did_you_know_facts: Repik is president of the Russian Business Association 'Delovaya Rossiya' ('Business Russia'), which unites more than 7,000 entrepreneurs.
He is donating for construction of a large shelter for 1,500 dogs per year in Yaroslavl, a city 250 kilometers from Moscow.
quote: "I have no plane; I have no yacht; not even an island, that's what is the most pity."

name: Wee Ee Lim
about: Wee Ee Lim chairs Singapore property development company UOL Group.
He was appointed UOL chairman in 2024 after the death of his father Wee Cho Yaw.
He Joined Haw Par, maker of the popular Tiger Balm ointment, in 1986, and has been serving as its president and CEO since 2003.
In March 2025, the estate of his father, the late Wee Chow Yaw, was transferred to him, his mother and siblings, completing a process that happened over many months.

name: Reinfried Pohl Jr
about: Reinfried Pohl Jr. is chief representative of DVAG, the leading German company offering mutual funds, consumer insurance and annuities.
His brother Andreas and he inherited the DVAG empire from their father, Reinfried Pohl Sr., who died in 2014.
The family's holding company, owned 50/50 by the brothers, holds 60% of DVAG, with the remaining 40% held by Generali Deutschland Holding AG.
Reinfried grew up in the company, attended openings of new branches with his father as a teenager, then sold insurance and later helped manage DVAG.
did_you_know_facts: The DVAG founder supported a range of schools and organizations in his home city of Marburg, which has led some to refer to it as "Pohl City."
Reinfried's wife, Ana, a physician, is a member of DVAG's supervisory board, as is Andreas's wife, Jaqueline.

name: Zhou Hongyi
about: Zhou Hongyi is the cofounder, CEO and chairman of Beijing-based Internet security software provider and search company 360 Security Technology, also known as Qihoo 360.
Zhou previously founded 3721.com, an online search company that was purchased by Yahoo.
Qihoo delisted from the New York Stock Exchange in 2016 then relisted in China in 2018.
Zhou also chairs Nasdaq-listed 360 DigiTech, a credit information service.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, Xi'an Jiaotong University; Master of Science, Xi'an Jiaotong University

name: Chris Lin
about: Chris Lin is the chairman and president of Aspeed Technology, a fabless integrated circuit (IC) designer.
He worked with Taiwan's IC designer Silicon Integrated Systems before founding Aspeed in 2004.
The company listed on the Taipei Exchange in 2013.

name: Tong Yongsheng & family
about: Tong Yongsheng leads Shenzhen Megmeet Electrica, which specializes in energy conversion technologies.
The company is a renowned domestic supplier across multiple sectors, including smart home appliances, power supply products, green energy and rail transit components.
In 2024, the company announced that it participated in the designing of NVIDIA's Blackwell system, making it one of NVIDIA's more than 40 equipment suppliers that serve its data centers.
The company has set up R&D centers in the U.S. and Germany, and plans to build manufacturing plants in Thailand, India and the U.S.
Tong Yongsheng holds Postdoctoral Fellow in Power Electronics at Zhejiang University. He worked for Huawei from 1996 to 2001 and Emerson later.
Tong assumed leadership of Megmeet in 2005 amid financial losses and has since served as chairman and CEO; the company has been profitable under his helm.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Ph.D, Nanjing University of Aeronautics & Astronautics

name: Zhu Gongshan & family
about: Zhu Gongshan chairs GCL-Poly Energy Holdings, a producer of polysilicon used to make solar panels.
Zhu is active in business groups, including the Global Green Energy Council and Asian Photovoltaic Industry Association.
Son Zhu Yufeng is a member of GCL-Poly's board of directors.
Chu also chairs GCL System Integration Technology, whose shares trade at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange.
Zhu graduated from Nanjing Electric Power College in July 1981 and obtained a diploma in electrical automation.

name: David Adelman
about: David Adelman is a real estate, alternative investments and sports mogul.
His Campus Apartments is one of the largest providers of on- and off-campus housing in America, with some $2 billion of properties across 80 schools in 23 states.
He is also cofounded Future Standard, an alternative investments firm that manages $86 billion across mutual funds, REITs and other vehicles. He's vice chairman.
He has a 7% stake in Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment, which owns the NHL's New Jersey Devils and the NBA's Philadelphia 76ers. He's spearheading a plan to build the Sixers a $1.3 billion arena.
A Philadelphia native, Adelman got his start using $2,000 of bar mitzvah money to invest with student housing entrepreneur and family friend Alan Horwitz.
He then went to work for Horwitz, rising to CEO at age 25, and began taking more and more of the equity as he expanded Campus Apartments nationwide.

personal_stats.label: Source of Wealth
personal_stats.value: Real estate, asset management, Self Made

did_you_know_facts: Adelman first invested in a building at the corner of 45th and Pine streets, which he still owns today. He chose it at age 13 because it was the tallest one he saw.
Through his Darco Capital, Adelman has invested in everything from soccer club Crystal Palace F.C. to private jet charter company WheelsUp, where he's on the board.

name: John Stanton
about: John Stanton is the chairman of the Seattle Mariners baseball team, serving as managing partner of a group of investors that has owned the franchise since 2016.
He made his fortune as an executive in the wireless telecommunications industry, helming four of the top wireless operators in the United States.
He formed Western Wireless Corporation in 1994; its spun-off subsidiary VoiceStream Wireless later became T-Mobile USA after a sale to Deutsche Telekom.
Stanton is currently a managing director of Bellevue, Washington-based venture capital firm Trilogy Equity Partners, which he founded in 2006.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Whitman College

did_you_know_facts: Other than during his time at university, Stanton has lived in the Seattle area for almost his whole life.

name: Ioannis Papalekas
about: Ioannis Papalekas is a Greek real estate investor and the largest shareholder of publicly traded investment conglomerate Yoda Group.
Yoda invests in shipping, healthcare, technology and real estate in Cyprus and Greece.
He founded Yoda as a private investment firm in 2019 and took it public on the Cyprus Stock Exchange in 2022; he owns 66% of the shares.
Prior to starting Yoda, he founded office real estate firm Globalworth and took it public on the London Stock Exchange in 2013.
He sold his 13.5% stake in Globalworth, which owns offices in central Europe, for $315 million in early 2020.
did_you_know_facts: Before starting Globalworth, he developed commercial real estate in Romania, achieving a 175% rate of return for himself and his investors.

name: Arnout Schuijff
about: Arnout Schuijff is the cofounder and former chief technology officer of Adyen, an Amsterdam-based payment processing company.
He stepped down from the company's management board in 2021.
Schuijff became a billionaire when Adyen went public in 2018. He sold 15% of his stake in 2019.
Schuijff started the company in 2006 with Pieter van der Does, who is the company's CEO.
Schuijff and van der Does first worked together in 2000 at another e-commerce platform, Bibit.

name: James Dinan
about: James Dinan founded York Capital Management in 1991 and is the former chairman and CEO of the money management firm.
York Capital had $1.6 billion of assets under management as of March 2025, down from $19 billion in 2019.
In 2014 Dinan purchased a minority stake in the NBA's Milwaukee Bucks, alongside fellow finance tycoons Marc Lasry and Wes Edens.
Dinan obtained his B.S. degree in economics from the Wharton School and his M.B.A from Harvard Business School.
Dinan, who stopped serving as chairman of York Capital in late 2023, now spends his time managing his family office, according to a filing from York Capital.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School; Master of Business Administration, Harvard University

did_you_know_facts: Dinan lost much of his savings in the 1987 Black Monday stock market crash. Four years later, he founded York Capital Management.
Dinan sits on numerous boards, including that of the Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts and the Museum of the City of New York.

name: T.S. Kalyanaraman
about: T.S. Kalyanaraman is the managing director of Kalyan Jewellers, a gold jewelry chain with over 368 stores in India, 36 in the Middle East, and two in the U.S.
The business has its origins in a century-old textile store established in south India by his grandfather, who hailed from a family of Hindu priests.
Kalyanaraman worked in the family's textile trade from age 12 until 1993 when he started the jewelry chain.
Warburg Pincus invested in Kalyan Jewellers in 2014 and exited fully in 2024. The company got listed in 2021.
His sons Rajesh and Ramesh are executive directors on the company's board.
did_you_know_facts: In August 2024, T.S. Kalyanarman bought an additional 2.4% stake in the company from Warburg Pincus.
He contributed $3 million to Habitat For Humanity India to build 2,000 homes for low-income families.

name: Song Chi-hyung
about: Song Chi-hyung is cofounder and chairman of Dunamu, which operates Upbit, South Korea's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volume.
In November 2025, South Korean search engine behemoth Naver said its payment arm, Naver Financial, will acquire Dunamu in a stock swap that values the combined entity at $13.6 billion.
Dunamu's previous investors include Kakao Ventures, Silicon Valley-based venture capital firm Altos Ventures and Hybe, the agency behind K-pop powerhouse BTS.
Before starting Dunamu with Kim Hyoung-nyon, who is also a billionaire, Song worked at local mobile payment company Danal.

name: Shigenobu Nagamori
about: Shigenobu Nagamori is the founder and chairman of motor manufacturer Nidec.
Nidec bills itself as the world's largest manufacturer of motors for hard-disk drives and optical drives, by units sold.
Nagamori has said publicly that his goal is to hit ¥10 trillion ($91 billion) in revenue by 2030, partly by focusing on drivetrains for electric vehicles.
In 2024, Mitsuya Kishida, one of five executive vice presidents, became the new president and CEO.

Nidec was removed from Nikkei 225 and Topix indexes in November 2025. The exchange marks it a "security on special alert" due partly to lax internal controls and an ongoing investigation over accounting scandal at one of its subsidiaries.

name: Kie Chie Wong
about: Malaysian investor Kie Chie Wong, who has lived in Australia since the 1980s, gets the bulk of his wealth from a minority stake in Fortescue Metals Group.
A longtime backer of billionaire Andrew Forrest, Wong once held a 26.5% stake in Fortescue, for which he paid about $1 million in 2003.
Wong was part of a Malaysian consortium, which bought an Australian realtor in 1988.
He reportedly hails from a Sarawak timber family in Malaysia.
Wong and his wife, Ann Pin Lim, also own a farm south of Sydney.

name: Mika Anttonen
about: Mika Anttonen heads and owns a majority stake in the nearly $8 billion (sales) Scandinavian fuel distributor St1 Group.
Anttonen uses profits to finance projects he hopes will combat climate change and eventually replace oil, such as developing bioethanol from trash.
He got his start as an oil trader working for Finland-based oil refiner and marketer, Neste Oyj, in the early 1990s.
He founded his own company, Greenergy Baltic, in 1995. He renamed it St1 in 2005.
did_you_know_facts: Anttonen plays hockey in his spare time and is a fan of the New York Rangers.
St1 is running a pilot program in Finland in which it drills four miles beneath the surface to extract heat, which can then be turned into energy.

name: Solina Chau
about: Solina Chau, also known as Chau Hoi Shuen, runs Horizons Ventures, a venture capital firm that backs disruptive tech startups.
It was among the earliest investors in Facebook, Spotify, Zoom and U.S. energy drink maker Celsius Holdings.
Chau cofounded Horizons in 2002 with her longtime business partner, Debbie Chang Pui Vee, who is a cousin of Hong Kong shipping tycoon Tung Chee Hwa.
Chau has amassed a fortune from her stakes such as in Celsius Holdings, Zoom and Canada's Well Health Technologies.
The long-time companion of Hong Kong billionaire Li Ka-shing, Chau invests some of Li's fortune and is a director at his Li Ka Shing Foundation. She also runs her own H.S. Chau Foundation.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of New South Wales

did_you_know_facts: Prior to Horizons, Chau started China-focused online media company Tom Group and took it public in Hong Kong in 2000, sparking a dot-com buying frenzy.

name: Yusuf Hamied
about: Yusuf Hamied is the non-executive chairman of Mumbai-based generics maker Cipla.
Cipla was founded in 1935 by his father Khwaja Abdul Hamied, a disciple of Mahatma Gandhi.
After the patriarch passed away in 1972, Cambridge-educated Hamied and his brother Mustafa inherited the business.
Hamied took on big pharmaceutical companies, offering low-cost generic drugs for diseases such as AIDS, earning the label of drug pirate.
At the annual shareholders' meeting in 2023, Hamied called reports of a potential stake sale in Cipla by the family to a private equity firm as "speculative."
did_you_know_facts: His niece Samina Hamied was Cipla's executive vice-chairman until March 2024.
Renowned music conductor Zubin Mehta is Hamied's childhood pal.
Cambridge University has named a building after him, making him the first Indian to get that honor.
quote: I've done more humanitarian work than Bill Gates and Warren Buffett put together.

name: Shlomo Kramer
about: Shlomo Kramer is cofounder and CEO of Cato Networks, a cloud security startup last valued by investors in 2021 at $2.5 billion.
He cofounded Check Point Software, a firewall security pioneer, with fellow Israelis Gil Shwed and Marius Nacht in 1993. Check Point went public in 1996.
Kramer cofounded data security company Imperva in 2002; it went public in 2011 and was acquired by Thoma Bravo in 2019 for about $2.1 billion.
Kramer was an early investor and board member at cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks, founded by former Check Point employee Nir Zuk.
He has also invested in sales software maker Gong, cybersecurity company Exabeam and cloud data company Sumo Logic.

name: Li Zhiyuan
about: Li Zhiyuan chairs Hainan Jinpan Smart Technology, a supplier of energy equipment.
Jinpan went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2021.
Li worked for most of the 1980s as an engineer at a electric power design institute.

name: Zhang Jian
about: Zhang Jian chairs AIMA Technology, a maker of electric bikes and scooters.
AIMA was founded in 1999.
AIMA listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2021.

name: Chi Yufeng
about: Chi Yufeng chairs Shenzhen-listed online games firm Perfect World.
Chi holds an undergraduate degree in chemistry from prestigious Tsinghua University and a MBA from CEIBS.
He is also known as Michael Chi.

name: Arne Alexander Wilhelmsen
about: Arne Alexander Wilhelmsen is heir to the family that co-founded and remains one of the largest shareholder in Royal Caribbean Cruise Line.
He sits on Royal Caribbean's board and co-owns the family business, inherited after his father Arne Wilhelmsen's death in 2020.
He chairs Awas Holding, a family-owned investment group focused on cruise, real estate, offshore and financial assets.
The group owns Linstow, a real estate company developing major projects in Norway and the Baltics.
Wilhelmsen has led the diversification of the family fortune, expanding into finance, hospitality and industrial holdings.

name: Bent Wilhelmsen
about: Bent Christian Wilhelmsen is heir to the family that co-founded and remains one of the largest shareholder in Royal Caribbean Cruise Line.
He co-owns the family business through Awas Holding, inherited after his father Arne Wilhelmsen's death in 2020.
He is a principal in Awas Holding, a private investment group focused on cruise, real estate, offshore and financial assets.
The group owns Linstow, a real estate company developing major projects in Norway and the Baltics.
Wilhelmsen is involved in steering the family's diversified holdings with a focus on long-term value creation.

name: Peter Preben Wilhelmsen
about: Peter Preben Wilhelmsen is heir to the family that co-founded and remains one of the largest shareholders in Royal Caribbean Cruise Line.
He co-owns the family business through Awas Holding, inherited after his father Arne Wilhelmsen's death in 2020.
He is a principal in Awas Holding, a private investment group focused on cruise, real estate, offshore and financial assets.
The group owns Linstow, a real estate company developing major projects in Norway and the Baltics.
Wilhelmsen plays a key role in managing and growing the family's diversified investment portfolio.

name: Yoo Jung-hyun
about: Yoo Jung-hyun owns a minority stake in online gaming giant Nexon through NXC.
Her husband Kim Jung-ju built up Nexon and then retired from management in 2006; he died in 2022 at age 54.
She joined NXC in 1995 and became its chairman in 2024.
did_you_know_facts: Yoo Jung-hyun met her future husband at a ski resort when he was a freshman.

name: Steven Schonfeld
about: Schonfeld is the founder of Schonfeld Strategic Advisors, a hedge fund with $17.5 billion in assets under management.
He first launched his business in 1988 as a proprietary trading firm specializing in short-term trading and converted it into a family office around 2009.
Schonfeld evolved into a multi-strategy hedge fund that opened to outside investors in 2016. Its flagship fund has never had a losing year.
He built a private nine-hole golf course on 44 acres in the backyard of his Old Westbury, New York home.

name: Bhadresh Shah
about: Bhadresh Shah founded and runs AIA Engineering, a niche metallurgical company in Ahmedabad city.
Shah started a small foundry in 1978 and parlayed it into a $490 million (revenue) company.
AIA is the world's second largest manufacturer of high chromium grinding parts (by sales) for the cement, mining and power industries.
Shah is a metallurgy engineer from the premier Indian Institute of Technology (Kanpur).
Shah also sits on the Board of Zydus Lifesciences, controlled by pharma billionaire Pankaj Patel.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology

did_you_know_facts: Shah hails from a family of doctors but chose to study engineering rather than medicine.
Shah is a wine connoisseur.

name: Igor Makarov
about: Igor Makarov is the founder of Itera, Russia's first independent gas company.
In the late 1990s, Itera was Russia's main exporter of gas from Turkmenistan, where Makarov was born.
In 2012 Itera entered into a joint venture with Rosneft, the state-controlled oil company; the next year, Rosneft bought out Itera for $2.9 billion.
Makarov was appointed as an energy adviser to the president of Turkmenistan in 2019.
Makarov renounced his Russian citizenship in 2023 and is a citizen of Cyprus

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Turkmen State University

did_you_know_facts: Makarov, who was once a member of the USSR cycling team, is the honorable president of the Russian Cycling Federation.

name: Leo Huang
about: Leo Huang is chairman and CEO of Chroma ATE, a supplier of automatic testing equipment for sectors such as automotive and semiconductors.
The company's power testing equipment is finding increasing uses worldwide amid exponential electricity usage due to the AI boom.
He cofounded Chroma in 1984 with alumni of Taiwan's National Chiao Tung University, including Warren Chen who is also a billionaire.
The company went public in Taiwan in 1996.
Leo's son, David, sits on Chroma's board.

name: John de Mol
about: Dutch entertainment mogul John de Mol is one of the biggest names in reality TV.
With Joop van den Ende, he founded Endemol, the company responsible for international hits "Deal or No Deal," "Fear Factor" and "Big Brother."
De Mol sold Endemol for $5.3 billion to Spanish telecom giant Telefonica in 2000.
In 2015, he sold most of his Talpa Media, creator of hit shows like "The Voice," to British ITV for an initial cash payment of $545 million.
did_you_know_facts: Endemol is the world's largest independent producer, with more than 800 productions in 76 territories airing on 295 channels around the world.
John de Mol's sister, Linda de Mol, is an actress and the host of the Dutch version of "Deal or No Deal".

name: Hans Jakob Limbach
about: Hans Jakob Limbach is the founder of Limbach group, one of Europe's largest operators of laboratories for medical testing and research.
He started the company with a single laboratory in Heidelberg and later acquired 30 independent laboratories.
Headquartered in Heidelberg, the Limbach group now boasts 300 clinical specialists and has more than 6,000 employees.

name: Sulaiman Al Muhaidib
about: Sulaiman Al Muhaidib is the chairman of Al Muhaidib Group, a Dammam, Saudi Arabia-based family-owned conglomerate.
Al Muhaidib Group invests in companies across consumer products, infrastructure, construction, real estate and finance; Sulaiman owns 28% of the company.
The group was founded in 1943 by his father Abdulkadir, who started out as a food trader before expanding into building materials and real estate.
Sulaiman and his brothers Essam and Emad took over after Abdulkadir's death in 1996; they share ownership of the group with 4 other family members.
Al Muhaidib Group owns shares in at least 16 publicly traded companies in Saudi Arabia and Egypt.

name: Essam Al Muhaidib
about: Essam Al Muhaidib is the CEO of Al Muhaidib Group, a Dammam, Saudi Arabia-based family-owned conglomerate.
Al Muhaidib Group invests in companies across consumer products, infrastructure, construction, real estate and finance; Essam owns 28% of the company.
The group was founded in 1943 by his father Abdulkadir, who started out as a food trader before expanding into building materials and real estate.
Essam and his brothers Emad and Sulaiman took over after Abdulkadir's death in 1996; they share ownership with 4 other family members.
Al Muhaidib Group owns shares in at least 16 publicly traded companies in Saudi Arabia and Egypt.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, King Saud University

name: Sheryl Sandberg
about: Sheryl Sandberg served as chief operating officer of Facebook, now Meta, from 2008 until the fall of 2022.
Sandberg and her husband, Tom Bernthal, launched Sandberg Bernthal Venture Partners in 2021 to invest their own capital in startups.
Sandberg is the author of the bestselling books "Lean In: Women, Work, and the Will to Lead" and "Lean In for Graduates."
The Harvard MBA was previously an economist at the World Bank and chief of staff to then U.S. Treasury Secretary Larry Summers.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Harvard University; Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School

did_you_know_facts: Sandberg was previously vice president of online sales and operations at Google and a management consultant at McKinsey & Co.
Sandberg married Tom Bernthal, who was CEO of a consulting agency, in 2022.
quote: The seeds of resilience are planted in the way we process the negative events in our lives.

name: Sylvia Stroeher
about: In 2003, Sylvia Stroeher netted over $1 billion when her family sold 80% of hair-care group Wella AG to Procter & Gamble.
In 1927, her great-grandfather Franz bought the rights to a process that used hot curlers and chemicals to put long-lasting waves into women's hair.
Sylvia and her husband, a former nurse, have a renowned collection of contemporary German art that includes works by Baselitz, Immendorff and Kiefer.
Part of the collection is housed in the Museum Kueppersmuehle in Duisburg, Germany.
An extension to the museum by star architect Pierre de Meuron opened in 2020.
did_you_know_facts: In 2013, Sylvia helped struggling German publishing house Suhrkamp by paying writers' remuneration for some time; she now sits on its supervisory board.

name: Gu Wei
about: Gu Wei chairs Shenzhen MTC, which makes consumer electronics products, including TVs, for brands such as Philips.
Shenzhen MTC trades on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange; Gu owns about half the company.
Gu holds a MBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.

name: Anand Deshpande
about: Anand Deshpande is chairman and managing director of software firm Persistent Systems, headquartered in Pune.
He started the company in 1990 as a database firm, pooling $21,000 from his savings and borrowings from his father and some friends.
Persistent gets the bulk of its revenue from North America and the remaining from India; Europe and the rest of the world.
It provides digital engineering and data and artificial intelligence products to the software, banking, financial services and healthcare sectors.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Technology, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur, India; Ph.D, Indiana University - Bloomington

did_you_know_facts: He loves reading non-fiction books, mostly biographies and tech books.

name: Abhay Soi
about: Former finance professional Abhay Soi is chairman and managing director of Max Healthcare Institute, India's second-largest listed hospital chain by revenue.
Soi started his career at the erstwhile Arthur Andersen and later worked for EY and KPMG.
Soi got his entrepreneurial break in 2010 when he took over a struggling 650-bed hospital in Delhi and set up Radiant Life Care.
Radiant was merged with Max in June 2020 and listed two months later.
He's looking to double the number of hospital beds by 2029.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, European University; Bachelor of Arts/Economics, St Stephen's College (India)

name: Ajay Bhardwaj
about: Chairman and managing director of biotech company Anthem Biosciences which he cofounded in 2006 in Bangalore.
Anthem Biosciences is involved in drug discovery and development as well as contract manufacturing of specialised ingredients such as enzymes and peptides for pharma and biotech companies.
Anthem went public in Juiy 2025 and its stock was listed at a 27% premium to the issue price.
Bhardwaj has four decades of experience in the life sciences sector, including a long stint as president at fellow billionaire Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw's Biocon.
His son Ishaan works at the company as a vice president.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Technology, IIT Delhi; Master, Louisiana State University

did_you_know_facts: Bhardwaj has a B.Tech in chemical engineering from IIT Madras and a masters in chemical engineering from Louisiana State University.

name: Sandeep Engineer
about: Chemical engineer Sandeep Engineer, started out working in the pharma industry before launching his own pharma venture in 1987.
A decade later, he latched on to making plastic pipes, convincing India's plumbers about their superiority to metal pipes.
Astral Pipes enlists popular actors as its brand ambassadors.
The Ahmedabad firm also makes adhesives and sealants.

name: Yao Kuizhang
about: Yao Kuizhang chairs Hebei Yangyuan Zhihui Beverage, a supplier of walnut drinks.
Yao owns 30% of the company.
Yao worked for Hebei Hengshui Laobaigan Liquor as a technician early in his career.

name: Dong Jinggui
about: Dong Jinggui is the cofounder and chairman of Yadea Group, a maker of electric scooters and bicycles.
His wife, Qian Jinghong, is cofounder and vice chairman.
Yadea was set up in 2001 in Jiangsu province.

name: Vivek Ramaswamy
about: Vivek Ramaswamy is a biotech entrepreneur, author and Republican politician who ran for president in 2024.
A Harvard and Yale Law graduate, Ramaswamy began his career on Wall Street trading biotech stocks for the hedge fund QVT.
In 2015, he took public a speculative Alzheimer's drug (which later failed) in a $3 billion IPO that formed the basis of Roivant Sciences, a drug discovery and investment firm.

In the years since, Roivant has helped bring multiple successful drug candidates to market; positive Phase 3 trial results for brepocitinib, which targets an autoimmune disease, sent its stock soaring in late 2025.
Ramaswamy left Roivant in 2020 to write Woke, Inc., a best seller, and found Strive, an asset manager that provides anti-woke investment funds.
Ramaswamy helped Elon Musk found DOGE as its co-head, but departed after a few weeks amid reports of butting heads with Musk.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Harvard University; Doctor of Jurisprudence, Yale University

did_you_know_facts: Ramaswamy graduated as valedictorian from St. Xavier High School in Cincinnati, Ohio.
quote: I don't do well as a number two. I am at my best when I am leading, not following.

name: Nan Cunhui
about: Nan Cunhui chairs Zhejiang Chint Electrics, a supplier of meters and power transmission equipment.
Nan is a standing committee member of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce and chairman of Zhejiang Federation of Industry and Commerce.
He is also the president of Zhejiang Chamber of Commerce.

name: Wang Wenjing
about: China's software industry pioneer Wang Wenjing chairs Yonyou Network Technology, once known as UFIDA.
Wang began his undergraduate studies at age 15 and founded Yonyou at age 24.
Outside of the office, Wang's interests include wine, golf and tennis.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Jiangxi University of Finance & Economics

name: Inder Jaisinghani
about: Inder Jaisinghani runs Polycab India, which makes electrical wires and cables. He started the company as a trading firm in 1986.
International Finance Corporation, the private equity arm of the World Bank, picked up a stake in the company in 2008.
In 2014, Polycab expanded into making products such as electric fans, LED lighting, switches and switchgear.
The company went public in 2019.
Polycab operates 28 manufacturing plants across India and exports its products to 79 countries.

name: Fan Xiulian
about: Fan Xiulian is the CEO of Haisco Pharmaceutical Group.
The company is known for a range of specialty pharmaceuticals, including those for anesthesia, oncology antiemetics, digestive care, antibiotics, and cardiovascular treatments.
With billionaire Wang Junmin and Zheng Wei, an entrepreneur, the trio acquired the predecessor of Haisco in 2007 and took the company public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2012.

name: Luciano Hang
about: Brazil's Luciano Hang has found success with department store chain Havan by focusing heavily on physical stores rather than online sales.
Hang cofounded Havan in 1986; today it employs approximately 20,000 people in over 150 locations.
Hang bought out his cofounder early on and today owns nearly all of Havan, which had about $1.9 billion in 2020 revenues.
Hang has many followers on social media; he regularly live streams about politics on Facebook and gets up to 1 million views.
Hang is a vocal supporter of Brazil's President Jair Bolsonaro, a right-wing candidate who was elected in October 2018.

name: Jannie Mouton & family
about: Johannes "Jannie" Mouton, also known as "Buddha Buffett," is the founder of PSG Group, a listed investment holding firm.
PSG has interests in financial services, banking, private equity, agriculture and education.
Both of his sons serve on PSG Group's board, and his son Piet Mouton is the CEO.
The 2011 book, "And Then They Fired Me," details how Mouton started PSG Group after getting fired at age 48.
He had been fired by his fellow partners at stockbroking firm Senekal, Mouton & Kitshoff, which he cofounded.

name: Vasily Shikin
about: Vasily Shikin is chief technology officer of AI-powered advertising technology company AppLovin, which went public on the Nasdaq in 2021.
He served as AppLovin's vice president of engineering for eight years before being tapped as CTO in 2020.
Shikin is one of eight billionaires from AppLovin, including the company's cofounder and CEO Adam Foroughi.
Prior to joining AppLovin in 2012, Shikin worked for four years as a software engineer at Device Anywhere, a cloud-based platform for testing and monitoring mobile websites and apps.
Born in Russia, Shikin has a master's in mathematics from Saint-Petersburg State University.

name: Sunil Vachani
about: Sunil Vachani is the founder and chairman of India-listed Dixon Technologies.
Vachani borrowed two million rupees ($27,600) from his father to set up the company in 1993 to manufacture TV sets.
The company makes products such as smartphones, washing machines and TVs for a range of clients including Samsung, Panasonic and Xiaomi.
The Noida-based company was listed in 2017.

name: Steve Case
about: Steve Case cofounded investment firm Revolution, which has invested in over 200 companies.
His Rise of the Rest tour funds startups from non-coastal states, stopping in cities to a host pitch competition for a $100,000 investment.
Revolution has also invested in restaurant chain Sweetgreen, fantasy sports firm Draft Kings and wine retailer Vinfolio.
In 1985 Case helped found Quantum Computer Services. He became CEO in 1991 and changed its name to America Online (AOL).
AOL merged with Time Warner in 2001 in a $164 billion deal that was eventually deemed one of the worst mergers in history.
did_you_know_facts: Born and raised in Hawaii, Case attended Punahou School, where Barack Obama went to high school. He later served on Obama's Council on Jobs and Competitiveness.
The Steve and Jean Case Foundation foundation created the Impact Investing Network Map to track transactions between investors and socially-conscious startup.

name: Michael Ying
about: Michael Ying is the former chairman of Hong Kong-listed fashion retailer Esprit.
He has kept a low profile and sold most of his stake in the company after stepping down in 2006.
In 2017 Ying transferred the rest of his Esprit shares to his daughters, who then sold all in 2021.
Ying joined Esprit in the 1970s and played a key role in building it into a global brand.
did_you_know_facts: Ying's Yan Ai Foundation has been supporting education and health care for poor children on the mainland.

name: Zhang Fan
about: Zhang Fan is founder and chairman of Shenzhen Goodix Technology, a touch-screen maker.
Goodix clients include Huawei, Lenovo, OPPO, vivo, ZTE, Meizu and Xiaomi.
In 2016 Goodix went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.
Zhang is a graduate of the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China.

name: David Fattal & family
about: David Fattal founded Fattal Hotels, Israel's largest hotel organization.
Fattal got his start as a waiter and bellboy and rose through management ranks before starting Fattal Hotels in 1998 at age 41.
He took the chain's parent company, Fattal Holdings 1998, public on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange in 2018.
The company owns 47 hotels in Israel with 9,000 rooms, and manages 255 hotels with a total of more than 50,000 rooms across Israel, Europe and the Mediterranean region.
Fattal owns about 51% of Fattal Holdings and nearly 9% of Mediterranean Towers, which is also listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Social Sciences, University of Haifa

name: Joe Lacob
about: Joe Lacob led an ownership group that in 2010 paid $450 million for the Golden State Warriors NBA team.
The value of the team is nearly 15 times more since then, and his 25% stake is worth nearly $2 billion, net of debt.
The Warriors have won four titles since 2010, and posted the best record in NBA history during the 2015-16 season, with 73 wins.
Lacob was a minority owner of the NBA's Boston Celtics for five years before selling to buy the Warriors.
Lacob joined venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins in 1987 and led investments in over 50 startup companies; he is no longer with the firm.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Masters of Public Health, UCLA; Master of Business Administration, Stanford University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of California, Irvine

name: Bill Malhotra
about: Bill Malhotra is the founder and CEO of Claridge Homes, one of the largest real estate developers in Ottawa, Canada.
Malhotra founded Claridge in 1986 and the company has since built more than 14,000 properties, including condos, houses and retirement homes.
He was born in India and studied civil engineering in college before moving to Canada in 1971 at age 22, where he worked at an engineering firm.
From 1977 to 1986, Malhotra was the chief structural engineer for the city of Ottawa, before leaving to start Claridge.
One of the company's residential projects, the 469-foot Claridge Icon, is the tallest building in Ottawa.
His sons Neil and Shawn are minority owners of Claridge Homes.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, Birla Institute of Technology and Science (BITS) - Pilani

did_you_know_facts: Malhotra's company is named after The Claridges, a luxury hotel in New Delhi that he used to visit as a child with his father.
In 2008, Malhotra built a 17-story condo tower in Pompano Beach, Florida; he is now developing multiple new projects in the Fort Lauderdale area.

name: Phillip Frost
about: A long-time health care investor, inventor and founder, Phillip Frost now runs diagnostics-maker Opko Health.
Frost joined Key Pharmaceuticals in 1972, reformulated its asthma drug and sold the company in 1986 for $836 million.
Frost founded Ivax, a generic drugmaker, in 1987. He sold it to Teva Pharmaceuticals for $7.6 billion in 2005.
In 2018, the SEC accused him of participating in a "pump-and-dump" scheme that generated over $27 million from unlawful stock sales.
Frost denied the allegations in a personal statement. He settled with the SEC in 2018 without admitting or denying the allegations.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Medical Doctor, Yeshiva U Albert Einstein College of Medicine; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: Born during the Great Depression, Frost is the third son of a shoe-store owner from South Philadelphia.
Frost and his wife, who have no children, have signed the Giving Pledge and have donated more than $130 million to the University of Miami.
quote: I was interested in a specialty that would permit me the time to reflect...I knew that surgery could never be for me because you're tied up in operating rooms most of the time. And I needed the freedom to do things.

name: Yair Hamburger
about: Yair Hamburger is a controlling shareholder of Harel Insurance, an Israeli insurance and financial services company.
He is one of three siblings - alongside Gideon Hamburger and Nurit Manor - who control Harel through G.Y.N Consulting, the family's privately held company.
Harel, now one of Israel's biggest institutional financial firms, was founded in 1939 and has remained under family control.
Harel manages assets valued at NIS 571 billion ($176 billion) and operates across health, motor, life insurance, pensions and asset management.

name: Nurit Manor
about: Nurit Manor is a controlling shareholder of Harel Insurance, an Israeli insurance and financial services company.
She is one of three siblings - alongside Gideon and Yair Hamburger - who control Harel through G.Y.N Consulting, the family's privately held company.
Harel, now one of Israel's biggest institutional financial firms, was founded in 1939 and has remained under family control.
Harel manages assets valued at NIS 571 billion ($176 billion) and operates across health, motor, life insurance, pensions and asset management.

name: Gideon Hamburger
about: Gideon Hamburger is the president of Harel Insurance, an Israeli insurance and financial services company.
He is one of three siblings - alongside Yair Hamburger and Nurit Manor - who control Harel through G.Y.N Consulting, the family's privately held company.
Harel, now one of Israel's biggest institutional financial firms, was founded in 1939 and has remained under family control.
Harel manages assets valued at NIS 571 billion ($176 billion) and operates across health, motor, life insurance, pensions and asset management.

name: Evan Spiegel
about: Evan Spiegel, CEO of Snap Inc., became the world's youngest billionaire at the age of 24 in 2015.
Snap, known for its disappearing photo and video app Snapchat, went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2017.
Spiegel launched the company with Bobby Murphy, a Stanford University fraternity brother, in 2011.
Spiegel and Murphy jointly own just over 20% of Snap but have special voting shares that give them control of the company.
Spiegel graduated from Stanford with a B.S. in product design in 2018, after dropping out to start Snapchat nearly seven years earlier.
did_you_know_facts: Spiegel grew up in the Los Angeles area and married supermodel Miranda Kerr in the summer of 2017.

name: Karl Knauf
about: Karl Knauf is an heir to one of the world's leading producers of building materials and systems, Knauf Gips KG.
Based in Iphofen, Germany, the company employs more than 35,000 people around the world and has annual revenue of over $11 billion.
Its product line includes plasterboards, cement boards and insulating materials.
Knauf Gips traces its roots to 1932, when brothers and mining engineers Alfons and Karl Knauf obtained rights to gypsum deposits in Schengen, Germany.
Their original gypsum factory, on the Moselle River in the border region of Luxembourg, Germany and France, is still the company's production nucleus.
did_you_know_facts: The family's Knauf Museum, on the premises of a historical inn built in 1688 on Iphofen's market square, houses a renowned collection or ancient relief art.

name: Christiane Knauf
about: Christine Brigitte Knauf is an heir to one of the world's leading producers of building materials and systems, Knauf Gips KG.
Based in Iphofen, Germany, the company employs more than 35,000 people around the world and has annual revenue of over $11 billion.
Its product line includes plasterboards, cement boards and insulating materials.
