Knauf Gips dates to 1932, when brothers and mining engineers Alfons and Karl Knauf obtained rights to gypsum deposits in Schengen, Germany.
Their original gypsum factory, on the Moselle River in the border region of Luxembourg, Germany and France, is still the company's production nucleus.
did_you_know_facts: The family's Knauf Museum, on the premises of a historical inn built in 1688 on Iphofen's market square, houses a renowned collection or ancient relief art.

name: Christine Knauf
about: Christine Brigitte Knauf is an heir to one of the world's leading producers of building materials and systems, Knauf Gips KG.
Based in Iphofen, Germany, the company employs more than 35,000 people around the world and has annual revenue of over $11 billion.
Its product line includes plasterboards, cement boards and insulating materials.
Knauf Gips dates to 1932, when brothers and mining engineers Alfons and Karl Knauf obtained rights to gypsum deposits in Schengen, Germany.
Their original gypsum factory, on the Moselle River in the border region of Luxembourg, Germany and France, is still the company's production nucleus.
did_you_know_facts: The family's Knauf Museum, on the premises of a historical inn built in 1688 on Iphofen's market square, houses a renowned collection or ancient relief art.

name: Luis Enrique Yarur Rey
about: Luis Enrique Yarur Rey is the chairman of Banco de Credito e Inversiones (BCI), a Chilean retail and commercial bank.
BCI has nearly 200 branches throughout Chile, Peru and Florida.
The bank was founded by the Yarur family in 1937. Today, it is one of Chile's largest banking institutions, with more than $80 billion in assets.
In 2015, BCI purchased City National Bank of Florida for $947 million; it was the first time a Chilean bank purchased a U.S. financial institution.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, IESE Business School

name: Chen Wenyuan & family
about: Chen Wenyuan chairs HYC Technology, a supplier of testing equipment for LCD, semiconductor and new energy electronics businesses.
HYC listed on China's new STAR market for innovative companies on the Shanghai Stock Exchange on July 22, 2019
His wife Zhang Qian cofounded the predecessor business of HYC in 2005.

name: Christopher Kwok
about: Christopher Kwok is the younger son of property mogul Raymond Kwok, chairman of Sun Hung Kai Properties, one of the largest developers in Hong Kong.
He's served as an executive director at Sun Hung Kai since 2016, taking charge of sales, project management and the leasing of major projects.
He's also a member of the Beijing Municipal Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference.
In 2012, his father and his uncle Thomas became involved in a bribery investigation. Raymond was acquitted but Thomas was found guilty and sentenced to five years in prison in 2014.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Harvard University; Master of Business Administration, Stanford Graduate School of Business

did_you_know_facts: Christopher's brother, Edward, and three of his cousins are also billionaires.
Christopher and his wife, Rachel Zhao, a former news anchor for China's Phoenix TV, met while they studied at Stanford University in 2013.

name: Wu Lanlan & family
about: Wu Lanlan is the vice chairman of Shenzhen Yuto Packaging.
Shenzhen Yuto went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2016.
Wu holds a MBA from Tongji University.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Tongji University

name: Bob Ell
about: Bob Ell is the founder and executive chairman of Leda Holdings, which owns three shopping malls in Queensland and a fourth in Canberra.
He also has large-scale residential land developments in Queensland and New South Wales.
He started out in Sydney commercial and industrial real estate in the 1970s.
Ell briefly listed Leda Holdings before taking it private in 1990. He has developed more than $3 billion worth of property projects.

name: Todd Wagner
about: With business partner Mark Cuban, Todd Wagner joined the billionaire ranks after selling video portal Broadcast.com to Yahoo in 1999.
The $5.7 billion sale didn't just benefit Wagner and Cuban: their 300 employees became millionaires.
Wagner safeguarded his shares against the dot-com bubble's epic burst with put options.
Since then, Wagner and Cuban have continued to invest together in ventures such as Magnolia Pictures, AXS TV and the Dallas Mavericks.
He also founded and runs online fundraising platform Charity Network, which has raised over $650 million for charity since it was started in 2014.
Wagner sold his stake in the Dallas Mavericks in December 2023.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Indiana University; Doctor of Jurisprudence, University of Virginia

did_you_know_facts: Wagner had a cameo role in the 2006 movie "Akeelah and the Bee," which he also produced.
quote: What Mark [Cuban] and I did was lightning in a bottle. A unicorn doesn't happen often, and it happened to me at a very young age. I felt success was something to be proud of, but I had a lot of advantages that other folks don't.

name: Edward Kwok
about: Edward Kwok is the older son of property mogul Raymond Kwok, chairman of Sun Hung Kai Properties, one of the largest developers in Hong Kong.
He's served as an alternate company director to his father since 2012, when Raymond and his uncle Thomas became involved in a bribery investigation.
His father was acquitted but Thomas was found guilty of bribing a government official and sentenced to five years in prison in 2014.
He joined Sun Hung Kai in 2010 and is a sales and project manager, responsible for planning and marketing the group's Hong Kong residential projects.
A certified accountant, he worked for international audit firm Deloitte before joining the family business.
did_you_know_facts: Edward's brother, Christopher, and three of his cousins are also billionaires.
Edward is often seen carrying a white cane because he's visually impaired.

name: Enrique Coppel Luken
about: Enrique Coppel Luken and his four brothers own Grupo Coppel, a retail and banking business in Mexico with over $8 billion in sales.
Their father and grandfather founded the first shop in Sinaloa, where they sold radios and watches.
The group's retail arm has grown from a single shop in 1941 to over 1,700 stores across Mexico.
The stores are known for providing credit to customers, allowing them to finance their purchases over multiple payments.
Enrique was chairman and CEO until Agustín, the youngest of the bunch, took over in 2008.
did_you_know_facts: The brothers also have two sisters who don't have active roles in the business.

name: Leslie Alexander
about: Leslie Alexander sold the NBA's Houston Rockets to billionaire Tilman Fertitta for $2.2 billion in 2017.
Alexander paid $85 million for the Rockets in 1993, just before Hakeem Olajuwon led the team to NBA titles the next two seasons.
Alexander first made Forbes? billionaires list in 2006, thanks to his stake in student loans securitizer First Marblehead, though the Rockets proved to be a better investment.
He started building his fortune by trading bonds after dropping out of Brooklyn Law School.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctor of Jurisprudence, Western State University College of Law; Bachelor of Arts/Science, New York University

did_you_know_facts: Alexander dropped out of Brooklyn Law School at age 21 after his father died and headed to Wall Street to help provide for his mother.
Outside of business, Alexander is an animal lover; he has funded a horse sanctuary in Middleburg,Virginia named after his mother, Evelyn.

name: Dermot Desmond
about: Dermot Desmond started his career in finance at Citibank, and later worked for the Investment Bank of Ireland and PricewaterhouseCoopers.
In 1981 he founded NCB Stockbrokers, which became Ireland's largest independent brokerage; he sold it for $39 million in 1994.
With the proceeds, Desmond started his own private equity firm, International Investment & Underwriting.
IIU now has stakes in travel software firm Datalex, Mountain Province Diamonds, Barchester Healthcare and Glasgow soccer club Celtic PLC.
did_you_know_facts: An avid golfer, he's known as "The Kaiser" for his distinctive mustache.
He also owns stakes in two luxury hotels in the Caribbean, the Pink Sands Club and the Sandy Lane Hotel.

name: Ion Tiriac
about: Ion Tiriac is a former professional athlete who heads Tiriac Group, which has interests in real estate, auto, financial services and more.
After he retired as a tennis player in the 1970s, Tiriac coached and managed top players like Guillermo Vilas, Marat Safin and Boris Becker.
He began his investment career after the fall of communism in Romania, and eventually founded the Tiriac Group.
He owns a car and motorcycle collection of more than 400 models, including cars previously owned by Al Capone, Sammy Davis Jr. and Elton John.
Tiriac has also represented Romania internationally in ice hockey, including an appearance in the 1964 Winter Olympics and three Davis Cup finals.
did_you_know_facts: Known as Count Dracula in his tennis years, Tiriac is one of the richest former athletes of all time.
He formed a formidable doubles team with Ilie Nastase and captured a Grand Slam doubles title and a runners-up finish as well.

name: David Fong
about: David Fong is the managing director and co-chairman of Hip Shing Hong Group, one of Hong Kong's largest private real estate investment companies.
His late father Fong Yun Wah served as chairman of the group until 2022. His uncle is now co-chairman.
The family had an early sesame-seed-processing business, which eventually gave way to property investment and Hip Shing Hong started in 1948.
Today the group's businesses span across residential, commercial and hospitality.
David's son Jonathan is deputy managing director of the group; younger son Vincent runs his own business in healthtech.
did_you_know_facts: The company's roots date back to 1927, when Fong Yun Wah arrived in Hong Kong with his father from Guangdong province.

name: Daniel Lubetzky
about: Daniel Lubetzky founded snack bar company Kind Healthy Snacks in 2004 and sold the majority of it to candy and pet food giant Mars in 2020.
Mars initially bought a minority stake in Kind in 2017 for an undisclosed amount; the 2020 deal reportedly valued Kind at $5 billion.
Lubetzky retains a financial stake in Kind, the size of which is undisclosed. Kind is known for its bars made with nuts and other ingredients.
Prior to Kind, Lubetzky started PeaceWorks, a marketing, consulting and distribution company, in 1994.
PeaceWorks specialized in selling items produced by groups in conflict, such as chocolates from Arabs and Israelis.
While traveling for PeaceWorks, Lubetzky found a bar with whole nuts and fruit in Australia which became the impetus for Kind.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Trinity University of San Antonio

did_you_know_facts: While in high school and college, Lubetzky purchased watches wholesale and sold them at a markup at flea markets and shopping mall kiosks.
Lubetzky wrote a 268-page senior thesis at Trinity University about achieving peace between Arabs and Israelis through business ventures.

name: J. Hyatt Brown
about: J. Hyatt Brown chairs New York Stock Exchange-traded Brown & Brown, the fourth largest insurance brokerage in the U.S.
His father, J. Adrian Brown, cofounded the company in Daytona Beach in 1939, and Hyatt became CEO in 1961.
Under Hyatt, Brown & Brown grew from a local, family-owned business into a firm with over 15,000 employees and 500 locations worldwide.
Hyatt's son J. Powell Brown took over as CEO in 2009; the elder Brown remains chairman.
J. Hyatt Brown owns 15% of Brown & Brown, which trades on the New York stock exchange.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Florida

did_you_know_facts: Brown was elected to the Florida House of Representatives in 1972 and served as the Speaker of the House in Florida from 1978 to 1980.
The Cici and Hyatt Brown museum in Daytona Beach, Florida, is home to the largest collection of Florida art in the world.

name: Karin Sartorius-Herbst
about: Karin Sartorius-Herbst inherited a stake in Sartorius AG, which makes pharmaceutical an laboratory equipment.
Her great-grandfather Florenz Sartorius founded what become Sartorius AG in 1870 to make analytical balances to measure small mass in laboratories.
Her father, Horst Sartorius, died in 1998 and left a 50% stake to his daughters Karin, Christine Franken and Ulrike Baro.
An executor oversees their inheritance until 2028.
Today, the company has more than 15,000 employees and annual revenue exceeding $5 billion. It went public in 1990.
did_you_know_facts: Sartorius-Herbst has had roles in various voluntary endeavors and charitable entities throughout her life.
She studied economics at the University of Goettingen.

name: Nerio Alessandri
about: Nerio Alessandri is the founder and president of the Italian gym and fitness equipment manufacturer Technogym.
Alessandri founded the company in Cesena, Italy in 1983 at age 22.
Alessandri took the company public on the Milan Stock Exchange in 2016.
When he started Technogym, Alessandri designed and built the first pieces of equipment in his garage.
Technogym has been the official supplier at eight Olympic Games, from Sydney 2000 to Tokyo 2020.
did_you_know_facts: Alessandri has written several books on the concept of wellness, with his latest book "Born to Move" published in 2014.

name: Steven Witkoff & family
about: Steven Witkoff is the founder and chairman of Witkoff Group, a real estate development firm he founded in New York in 1997.
Witkoff Group's developments include luxury condos, hotels, golf courses and apartment buildings in New York, Los Angeles and Florida.
Friends with Donald Trump since the early 1990s, Witkoff was appointed as Trump's special envoy to the Middle East in November 2024.
As Middle East envoy, Witkoff helped negotiate a peace deal in Gaza between Israel and Hamas in October 2025.
In 2025, he was also tasked with negotiations to end the war in Ukraine and reach an agreement with Iran over its nuclear program.
Witkoff was a real estate lawyer and then started buying apartments and offices with his former colleague Larry Gluck before going it alone in 1997.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts, Hofstra University; JD, Hofstra University

did_you_know_facts: Witkoff and his family own an estimated 6.4% interest Trump's crypto project World Liberty Financial.
Witkoff and Trump first met when Witkoff was a real estate lawyer in the late 1980s and Trump was a client; Witkoff bought him a sandwich.

name: Tibor Veres
about: Veres Tibor is one of Hungary's most reclusive business leaders.
Through holding companies, he controls interests in automobiles, real estate development, retail and manufacturing.
Founded in 1987 Wallis Group operates in real estate development, automotive, retail, logistics and manufacturing.
Wallis's Dayton-Invest is majority owner of WING, a real estate business with interests in Hungary, Poland and Germany.
Veres also controls AutoWallis, a leading automotive and mobility service provider 23 brands operating across Central and Eastern Europe.
did_you_know_facts: He graduated from the University of Moscow in 1986 and returned to Hungary where he founded Wallis Group with his father and another co-founder.
Veres is a member of the UNICEF Hungary Board of Trustees.

name: Liu Zhenfeng
about: Liu Zhenfeng is a director of Yantai Jereh Oilfield Services Group, a supplier of oilfield equipment.
The company won a US$100 million order for generator sets from a North American data center in November 2025.
Yantai Jereh Oilfield Services Group listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2010.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts / Science, University of Science and Technology Beijing; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Science and Technology Beijing

name: Edward Lampert
about: After a stint at Goldman Sachs' risk arbitrage department, Edward Lampert founded hedge fund ESL Investments in 1988, betting on undervalued stocks.
He took over as CEO of struggling retail giant Sears Holdings (Sears, Kmart, Kenmore) in 2013 with hopes of a turnaround, but failed miserably.
Lampert's ESL Investments promised Sears nearly $1 billion in loans in the first 10 months of 2017.
In October 2018, Sears Holdings filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and announced that it would close 142 Sears and Kmart stores.
In January 2019 Lampert won an auction to keep the company, with a reported bid of more than $5 billion.
did_you_know_facts: Lampert survived a kidnapping in 2003; his captors released him after two days.
A graduate of Yale University, he was a part of the secret society Skull and Bones, whose alumni include former presidents George H.W. Bush and George W. Bush.

name: Carlos March Delgado
about: Carlos March Delgado was president of $2.5 billion (net assets) Banca March, Spain's only 100% family-owned bank, for four decades until 2015.
Carlos and his billionaire brother Juan March Delgado are grandchildren of Banca March's founder, Juan March (d. 1962), who started the business in Palma de Mallorca in 1926.
After stepping down as a director of Banca March in 2024, Carlos remains chairman of $5 billion (net assets) investment company Corporación Financiera Alba, which is also nearly 100% family-owned.
Carlos and Juan March Delgado own 69% of Banca March and 42% of Corporación Financiera Alba combined (excluding Banca March's 15% stake in Corporación Financiera Alba).

name: Michael Hsing
about: Michael Hsing is chairman and CEO of semiconductor company Monolithic Power Systems.
Hsing founded the company in 1997 and took it public on the Nasdaq in 2004.
He owns 2% of the company.
Before founding MPS, Hsing was a senior silicon technology developer at several analog integrated circuits companies.
He is an inventor on numerous patents related to the process development of bipolar mixed-signal semiconductor manufacturing.

name: Thomas Dundon
about: Thomas Dundon founded subprime auto lender Drive Financial in 1997, sold it to Santander and exited with $700 million in 2015.
He acquired a majority stake in the NHL's Carolina Hurricanes in 2018.
In 2019 Dundon invested $70 million into the now-defunct Alliance of American Football.
Dundon in 2025 put together a consortium of investors to acquire the NBA's Portland Trail Blazers for $4.2 billion.
Dundon's pickleball empire includes control over the United Pickleball Association, the PPA Tour and gear seller Pickleball Central.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Economics, Southern Methodist University

did_you_know_facts: Dundon was president of the Phi Gamma Delta frat at Southern Methodist University, where he studied economics and graduated 1993.

name: Alexander Ponomarenko
about: Alexander Ponomarenko was chairman of the board of Sheremetyevo, the biggest airport in Russia.
Ponomarenko was sanctioned by the EU. the U.K. and the U.S. in 2022; he has disputed the sanctions.
Ponomarenko and partner Alexander Skorobogatko started out with sea ports and banking and then moved into airport construction.
In 2013 the two, with Arkady Rotenberg, a judo partner of President Vladimir Putin, won a tender to develop Sheremetyevo, the state-owned airport.
The partners and Rotenberg also founded TPS Real Estate, which owns more than half of the real estate in Ocean Plaza, Kiev's biggest shopping center.
In 2023 the center was seized by the Ukrainian government.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Russian State Academy of Management; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Simferopol State University

did_you_know_facts: In 2011 Ponomarenko paid $350 million for a complex of buildings and land near the Black Sea known as Putin's Palace. He later sold it to Arkady Rotenberg.
The two Alexanders first set up a small perfume factory in the Ukraine and then founded a bank in Moscow.

name: Ho Hung Anh
about: Ho Hung Anh is chairman of Techcombank, a large commercial bank in Vietnam that went public in 2018.
Ho and fellow billionaire Nguyen Dang Quang, whom he met while studying in Russia, are two close business partners whose interests are intertwined.
Ho started investing in Techcombank, in which Nguyen was already an investor, in 1995. They took control in 2006.
Together they control two big listed companies, Masan Group and Techcombank, a commercial bank, through Masan JSC, a holding company that they co-own.

Techcom Securities, the brokerage arm of Techcombank, went public on the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange in October 2025. Masan Consumer, the group's consumer goods unit, listed on the bourse two months later.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, Kiev Polytechnic Institute

did_you_know_facts: Ho started out trading goods between Eastern Europe and Vietnam in the 1990s.

name: Guo Guangchang
about: Guo Guangchang is the chairman of Fosun International, an investment group whose interests cover pharmaceuticals, insurance, tourism and mining.
Fosun was set up in Shanghai in 1992. Today the group has nearly 110,000 employees across the globe.
Fosun purchased a 74% stake in Indian pharmaceuticals company Gland Pharma in 2017.
It is reportedly in talks to sell a minority stake in luxury resort chain Club Med to Singapore's CapitaLand Investment.
Fosun cofounder Liang Xinjun is also a billionaire.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Fudan University; Master of Business Administration, Fudan University

name: Ryan Horton
about: Ryan Horton's late father Donald Horton (d. 2024) founded homebuilder D.R. Horton in 1978.
He inherited a share of the family's more than 10% stake in the business, which is America's largest builder.
D.R. Horton has built more than 1 million homes across 126 markets in 36 states. It did $36.8 billion in fiscal 2024 sales.

name: David Grain
about: David Grain is the CEO of Grain Management, a private equity firm he founded in 2007.
Grain Management is focused on broadband and communication infrastructure investments.
Before founding Grain Management, he led wireless infrastructure company Global Signal from bankruptcy to IPO.
Grain Management purchased 15 megahertz of spectrum in T-Mobile's 800 MHz band in 2025 and Quintillion, an Alaskan fiber-optic network, in 2024.
Grain and his wife founded the Grain Fellows Program in 2004, funding SAT and college prep, application fees and mentorship for low-income students at Booker High School in Sarasota, Florida.
did_you_know_facts: He is a lifetime member of the Council on Foreign Relations.
Grain was appointed by President Barack Obama to the National Infrastructure Advisory Council at the U.S. Department of Homeland Security.

name: Kevin Systrom
about: Kevin Systrom launched photo-sharing mobile phone app Instagram in 2010 with Mike Krieger.
Facebook bought Instagram for $1 billion in cash and stock in 2012, and Systrom stayed on to continue running it. He left Facebook in 2018.
Systrom, who owned 40% of Instagram going into the deal, mostly got Facebook stock.
Under Systrom as CEO, Instagram became a fast growing app, with roughly 1 billion monthly users.
In 2021, Systrom became a backer and director of the Ajax I SPAC, which took online car marketplace Cazoo public a year later.
Systrom and Krieger launched a personalized news feed app, Artifact, in 2023, which was acquired by Yahoo in 2024.
did_you_know_facts: Systrom convinced well known public figures to join Instagram, including Pope Francis and singer Selena Gomez.
Systrom, known for wearing stylish suits, was a regular at fashion and cultural events, from the Met Gala to the Oscars, while he was CEO of Instagram.

name: Heikki Kyostila
about: Heikki Kyostila is president of Planmeca, one of the world's largest dental equipment manufacturers, headquartered in Helsinki, Finland.
Kyostila founded Planmeca in 1971 in Helsinki as a small dental-stools and -cabinets manufacturer.
The company has expanded to making 2D and 3D imaging X-ray devices and software for dentists.
did_you_know_facts: Kyostila was the on the cover of the first edition of FORBES Finland, in April 2017.

name: Reagan Horton
about: Reagan Horton's late father Donald Horton (d. 2024) founded homebuilder D.R. Horton in 1978.
He inherited a share of the family's more than 10% stake in the business, which is America's largest builder.
D.R. Horton has built more than 1 million homes across 126 markets in 36 states. It did $36.8 billion in fiscal 2024 sales.

name: Rishad Naoroji
about: Rishad Naoroji is the low-profile cousin of billionaires Adi Godrej, Nadir Godrej, Jamshyd Godrej and Smita Crishna-Godrej.
Naoroji had a one-fifth share of the Godrej family assets until 2024 when their storied Godrej group was split into two factions.
After the split, stock exchange filings show that Naoroji sold his stakes in group companies to his cousins.
The wildlife enthusiast and photographer has never been involved in the business.
He founded the Raptor Research and Conservation Foundation to focus on the conservation of Asian birds of prey.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Associate in Arts/Science, University of Mumbai

name: Scott Nuttall
about: Scott Nuttall is the co-CEO of storied private equity giant KKR.
He and Joseph Bae were appointed as chief executives in October 2021 when KKR co-founders Henry Kravis and George Roberts stepped down.
Nuttall first joined KKR in his early 20s, in 1996, following a brief stint at Blackstone.
He spearheaded KKR's capital markets, fundraising, insurance, credit and hedge fund initiatives, and helped take the company public in 2010.
KKR has about $638 billion in total assets under management.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: Nuttall and his billionaire co-CEO Joseph Bae began as KKR analysts together when they were 24.

name: Shi Yonghong & family
about: Shi Yonghong cofounded Sichuan hot pot chain Haidilao in 1994 with Zhang Yong, also a billionaire, and two friends who became their wives.
The company, which had about $4.4 billion in sales from almost 1,300 locations in 2020, went public in Hong Kong in September 2018.
Known for offering special services such as free manicures for waiting customers, Haidilao has expanded to the U.S., Japan, South Korea and Singapore.
Shi, who owns his stake in Haidilao with wife Li Haiyan, has a stake in Yihai International, hot pot condiment maker that was spun off from Haidilao.
Shi sits on the board of both companies.

name: Lyu Yixiong
about: Lyu Yixiong is the CEO of Shanghai Chicmax Cosmetic, a cosmetics supplier in China.
Chicmax went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in December 2022.
Lyu completed executive management training at the Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.

name: Jerry Reinsdorf
about: Jerry Reinsdorf made a fortune in sports, buying Chicago teams in the 1980s and watching values skyrocket over the next three decades.
Reinsdorf led a group that bought the Chicago White Sox baseball team in 1981 for $19 million. He still owns an estimated 19% stake.
He and investors bought a controlling stake in the NBA's Chicago Bulls for $9.2 million in 1985, one year after the team drafted Michael Jordan.
Four decades and 33 years later, the Bulls are worth $5 billion; Reinsdorf owns an estimated 40%.
He made his first fortune in real estate, cofounding Balcor Company in 1973 and selling it nine years later to American Express.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, George Washington University; Law Degree, Northwestern University

did_you_know_facts: Reinsdorf reportedly got his start as a tax attorney for the IRS.

name: Rita Tong Liu
about: Rita Tong Liu's Gale Well Group owns prime office buildings and hotels in Hong Kong.
She entered the real estate business in 1976, wading into luxury homes and later parking spaces.
She was married to a high school sweetheart, the eighth of nine sons of Liu Po Shan, founder of Chong Hing Bank.
After her husband died in 2003, she transitioned into grade A offices, capitalizing on the then-soaring prices in Hong Kong's financial district.
did_you_know_facts: Her grandmother worked in the family business selling groceries and brewing rice wine in Macau. Then her widowed mother built houses with imported timber.
Liu is assisted by her two younger brothers, Jacinto and Luis Tong. Jacinto is the CEO and is in charge of investments, while Luis oversees the firm's logistics.

name: Sergei Sudarikov
about: Sergei Sudarikov is the main shareholder of Region Group, which includes banking, pension fund, insurance, brokerage and asset management companies.
Sudarikov began at Region in 1995 as a trader. In 2011, he and a group of partners bought the business from its founder.
Region bought several asset management businesses from state-owned oil firm Rosneft in 2011, helping it become one of Russia's largest investment groups.
In 2019, Sudarikov agreed to merge his assets with billionaire Roman Avdeev's Rossium concern, active in finance, real estate development and oil.
He bought Avdeev's stake and became owner of 93% of Rossium in 2024.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Moscow State University

did_you_know_facts: Sudarikov's main hobby is wild fishing. He caught his first fish at the age of three.
According to Sudarikov, his first business was selling books in the early 1990s.

name: Salil Singhal
about: Salil Singhal is the chairman emeritus of PI Industries, a maker of plant protection and nutrient products.
The company was founded by his father, P.P.Singhal, in 1946 to manufacture edible oils.
Singhal's son, Mayank, is the CEO and has been involved with PI Industries since 1996.
did_you_know_facts: PI Industries started as Mewar Oil & General Mills in India's lake city of Udaipur.
The company has a network of more than 10,000 distributors and 70,000 retailers across India.

name: Christopher Rokos
about: Chris Rokos is the founder of hedge fund firm Rokos Capital Management.
Rokos is a macro investor who trades currencies, interest rates and commodities, as well as equities.
Rokos founded his London-based firm in 2015 and it now manages some $12 billion and employs more than 200 people.
A founding partner of Brevan Howard Asset Management, Rokos left the hedge fund firm after having a falling out with his partner, Alan Howard.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master, Oxford University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Oxford University

name: Ramesh Jaisinghani
about: Ramesh Jaisinghani gets his fortune from his stake in Polycab India, which makes electrical wires and cables.
Polycab was started by his older brother Inder as a trading firm in 1986.
It supplies everything from power cables to solar cables to optical fibre cables to the power, oil and gas and renewable energy industries.
In 2014, Polycab expanded into making products such as electric fans, LED lighting, switches and switchgear. It went public in 2019.
His son Nikhil Jaisinghani sits on the board of Polycab.

name: David Paul
about: David C. Paul is the founder and executive chairman of spine implant manufacturer Globus Medical.
A mechanical engineer by training, Paul moved to the U.S. from India to get his master's degree at Temple University.
Paul worked as an engineer for medical device giant Synthes before leaving in 2003 to start Globus.
Paul took Globus public in 2012.
In 2017 Paul stepped down as CEO due to a "health condition," according to a company press release.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Temple University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Madras

did_you_know_facts: Globus makes the Excelsius GPS, one of the only spinal surgery robots on the market today.

name: Tim Draper
about: A scion of a Silicon Valley investing dynasty, Tim Draper is a founding partner of venture capital firm Draper Fisher Jurvetson.
Draper has made hundreds of VC investments in companies including Tesla and Theranos, and has made a fortune investing in cryptocurrencies.
In 2014, he bought 29,656 bitcoins confiscated by U.S. Marshals from the shuttered Silk Road black market for $18.7 million, or just $632 per coin.

name: Matthew Pritzker
about: Matthew Pritzker and his sister Liesel Pritzker Simmons sued their family for a chunk of its Hyatt Hotels fortune and received around $500 million apiece in 2005.
Their uncle Jay Pritzker (d. 1999) founded the hotel chain and their uncle Donald Pritzker (d. 1972) managed and developed it.
Their father Robert Pritzker (d. 2011) ran the family's industrial conglomerate Marmon Group, which was acquired by Berkshire Hathaway in a series of transactions beginning in 2008.
Three of Matthew and Liesel's step-siblings, seven cousins and their father's cousin Nick Pritzker are also billionaires.
Matthew invests his fortune through the Chicago-based Matthew Pritzker Company.

name: Yinon Costica
about: Yinon Costica cofounded Israeli cloud security business Wiz and owned a 10% stake in the company.
Google's parent company Alphabet acquired Wiz for $32 billion in cash in March 2026.
Wiz software scans storage providers such as Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure to flag and prioritize security risks.
The company's revenue surpassed $100 million in 2023, when the founders began their "suicide plan" of hiring fast, raising funds and targeting top-of-market corporations.
Wiz customers include Fox, Morgan Stanley and LVMH, whose billionaire CEO wrote the unicorn a personal check.

Wiz software scans storage providers such as Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure to flag and prioritize security risks.

name: Ajay Jaisinghani
about: Ajay Jaisinghani gets his wealth from a minority stake in Polycab India, which makes electrical wires and cables.
Polycab was started as a trading firm in 1986 by his brother Inder Jaisinghani.
The company makes everything from power cables to solar cables to optical fibre cables for the the power, oil and gas and renewable energy industries.
In 2014, Polycab expanded into products such as electric fans, LED lighting, switches and switchgear.
did_you_know_facts: The company, which went public in 2019, got a boost in 2022 from increasing electrification and an uptick in spending in the power sector.
Son Bharat sits on Polycab's board.

name: Acharya Balkrishna
about: Acharya Balkrishna derives his fortune from consumer goods giant Patanjali Ayurved.
Balkrishna owns the bulk of the privately held company, which he cofounded with politically well-connected yoga guru Baba Ramdev.
Patanjali sells everything from herbal toothpastes and cosmetics to noodles and jams.
To push online sales, Patanjali has agreements with several e-commerce giants, such as Amazon and BigBasket.
Edible oils maker Ruchi Soya, which he acquired in 2019, was renamed as Patanjali Foods and he was installed as chairman.
did_you_know_facts: Balkrishna is often dressed in an all-white traditional dhoti.
Balkrishna's parents hail from Nepal.
In 2024, he apologised to India's Supreme Court for Patanjali's ads that allegedly make misleading claims about the medicinal benefits of its products.
quote: We want to use this wealth to serve others and not ourselves.

name: Wei Ying-Chiao
about: Wei Ying-Chiao and his three brothers, Ing-Chou, Yin-Chun and Yin-Heng, started Tingyi in 1991.
Tingyi is now one of the largest producers of ready-to-drink tea and bottled water in China. It is also a major supplier to the country's instant-noodle market.
The family also controls the Dicos fried-chicken chain.
The family's private company, Ting Hsin, sold its 37.17% stake in Taipei 101, Taiwan's tallest building, to Itochu for $665 million in 2018.
did_you_know_facts: Wei graduated from a local high school in Changhua County, central Taiwan, but didn't go to college.

name: Wei Ing-Chou
about: Wei Ing-Chou and his three younger brothers, Ying-Chiao, Yin-Chun and Yin-Heng, started Tingyi in 1991.
Tingyi is now one of the largest producers of ready-to-drink tea and bottled water in China. It is also a major supplier to the country's instant-noodle market.
As of 2019, Ing-Chou is no longer a director of Tingyi (Cayman Islands) Holding, but he remains a senior consultant to the company.
His eldest son, Wei Hong-Ming, born in 1978, is now the chairman. His third son, Wei Hong-Chen, born in 1982, is an executive director.
The family's private company, Ting Hsin, sold its 37.17% stake in Taipei 101, Taiwan's tallest building, to Itochu for $665 million in 2018.
did_you_know_facts: Ing-Chou's second son, Wei Hong-Fan, started his own bicycle business in 2011.
The senior Wei graduated from a local middle school in Changhua County, central Taiwan, and never went to high school or college.
The family also controls the Dicos fried-chicken chain.

name: Wei Yin-Chun
about: Wei Yin-Chun and his three brothers founded Tingyi, one of the largest producers of ready-to-drink tea and bottled water in China.
Tingyi is also a major supplier of instant noodles in the country.
The family also controls the Dicos fried-chicken chain.
The family's private company, Ting Hsin, sold its 37.17% stake in Taipei 101, Taiwan's tallest building, to Itochu for $665 million in 2018.
Yin-Chun was sentenced in 2018 to 15 years in prison for his part in a tainted-cooking-oil scandal.
did_you_know_facts: Yin-Chun graduated from a local high school in Changhua County, central Taiwan, and never went to college.

name: Wei Yin-Heng
about: Wei Yin-Heng and his three brothers, Ing-Chou, Yin-Chun and Ying-Chiao, started Tingyi in 1991.
Tingyi is now one of the largest producers of ready-to-drink tea and bottled water in China. It is also a major supplier to the country's instant-noodle market.
The family also controls the Dicos fried-chicken chain.
The family's private company, Ting Hsin, sold its 37.17% stake in Taipei 101, Taiwan's tallest building, to Itochu for $665 million in July 2018.
did_you_know_facts: Wei graduated from a local high school in Changhua County, central Taiwan, and never went to college.

name: Jyoti Bansal
about: Jyoti Bansal is the founder and CEO of software delivery company Harness, which uses AI agents to automate the manual labor of making sure code is secure and compliant with regulations.
Bansal grew up helping his dad with his farming machinery business in a small town in India's Rajasthan state, before testing into Delhi's Indian Institute of Technology for computer engineering.
He immigrated to the U.S. at age 21 and worked as an engineer at a handful of startups in Silicon Valley for seven years on an H1-B visa before getting his green card.
Bansal sold his first company, AppDynamics, which diagnoses and troubleshoots software anomalies, to Cisco for $3.7 billion in 2017. He founded Harness soon after.
Harness raised a $240 million Series E funding round from Goldman Sachs Alternatives, Institutional Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures at a $5.5 billion valuation in late 2025.
did_you_know_facts: Bansal fell in love with entrepreneurship after he met billionaire Bill Gates, who visited Delhi's Indian Institute of Technology when Bansal was a student.
Bansal has hiked Machu Picchu, trekked the Himalayas and gone on multiple African safaris.
quote: I strongly believe to build a company you have to spend a lot of time on it. Ten years at least.

name: Stefan Soloviev
about: Stefan Soloviev is the chairman of the Soloviev Group, which has interests in agriculture, ranching, real estate, railroads and hospitality.
He formed the group in April 2021, merging his agriculture company with his late father Sheldon's (d. 2020) real estate firm Solow Building Co.
The Soloviev Group owns 700,000 acres of farm and ranch land in Kansas, Colorado and New Mexico, as well as two railroads in Colorado and Kansas.
The group sold several apartment buildings in New York for $1.75 billion in 2022; its properties include the iconic 9 West 57th St office tower.
Soloviev started working for his father as a teenager but the two fell out when he was 21; he then moved to Phoenix to trade commodities and grain.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Drop Out, University of Rhode Island

did_you_know_facts: Soloviev uses the older Russian spelling of the family's name.
In 2023, the group bid for a New York City casino license, with plans to build a complex with a Ferris wheel, hotel, residential towers and a democracy museum.

name: Edwin Leong
about: Edwin Leong is the sixth son of Henry G. Leong, a comprador of British trading house Jardine Matheson, who died when Edwin was just nine years old.
Leong earned the moniker "King of Shops" from amassing an immense portfolio of retail and commercial properties through Tai Hung Fai Enterprise.
Leong also ventured into the mass residential market during the pandemic.
He is the founder of the Tai Hung Fai Charitable Foundation, which focuses on helping needy children and the elderly.

name: Zheng Jianjiang & family
about: Zheng Jianjiang is founder and chairman of Aux Group, a conglomerate and controlling shareholder of Ningbo Sanxing Medical Electric.
Zheng cofounded Ninbo Sanxing Medical Electric in 2007 and took it public in Shanghai in 2011.
Ninbo Sanxing supplies power distribution equipment such as smart meters and transformers.
Prior to Aux, Zheng worked at a bankrupt watch parts factory in 1986 with seven other people.

name: Katsumi Tada
about: Katsumi Tada is the founder of property developer Daito Trust Construction, which specializes in building rental apartments.
In 2011, Tada stepped down as chairman and sold his stake back to the publicly traded company.
He switched his focus to Australia, where he develops and owns office buildings, malls and hotels through his privately held Daisho Co.
Daisho has a portfolio of 10 properties in Japan and overseas, including in Tokyo, Okinawa, Sydney, Brisbane, Melbourne and Singapore.
Tada also owns seven hotels in Japan.

name: Wu Cheng
about: Wu Cheng is chairman of Guocheng Mining, a Beijing-based miner of metals.
His Guocheng Co, a holding company, has interests in chemical, logistics and hotels.
Guocheng employs a staff of 7,000 and has operations across China, including Beijing, Inner Mongolia, Sichuan and Tibet, among others.

name: Bahaa Hariri
about: Bahaa Hariri is the eldest son of slain Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik Hariri (d. 2005); he inherited his fortune from his father, who was a billionaire.
In 2008, Bahaa Hariri sold his stake in Saudi Oger, the family construction business, to his brother Saad Hariri, also a former prime minister of Lebanon.
Bahaa Hariri founded and chairs Horizon Group, a real estate holding company with investments in Amman, Jordan and Beirut, Lebanon.
He helped revitalize an area of Amman, called Abdali, in partnership with the Jordanian government.
He's the majority owner of Globe Express Services, a logistics company with a presence in more than 100 countries.
did_you_know_facts: Hariri is a graduate of Boston University; he pledged $15 million to its Rafik Hariri Institute for Computing and Computational Science and Engineering.
Hariri is also an advisory board member of the Atlantic Council, a Washington, D.C. think tank that promotes international cooperation.
quote: My dream job: CEO of Apple. And what job would I hate to have? Well, what comes to mind is being the president of the U.S.

name: Chin Jong Hwa
about: Chin Jong Hwa is the largest shareholder of Hong Kong-listed auto-parts supplier Minth Group, which he started in 1997.
In 2016, Minth became the first auto-parts maker to receive a permit from China to make electric cars.
Chin stepped down from Minth in 2019. His wife Wei Ching Lien has taken over as chairman and CEO.
Their daughter, Chin Chien Ya, is a non-executive director at Minth. Son William is chief strategy officer and executive director.
Minth owns more than 70 factories globally, and is building new facilities in India and Serbia.
did_you_know_facts: Chin once worked as a counselor at China Youth Corps, a youth organization in Taiwan.

name: Daniel Hirschfeld
about: Daniel Hirschfeld is chairman of Nebraska-based casual clothing retailer The Buckle; he owns about a third of the company.
The Buckle has 440 stores in 42 U.S. states and sells clothing online as well.
Hirschfeld's grandfather opened a men's clothing store in the early 1900s and his dad started the current business in 1948.
Under Hirschfeld, the retailer turned its attention to denim and added women's clothing in the 1970s.
Hirschfeld stepped down as CEO in 1991, a year before the company went public.

name: Doug Ostrover
about: Doug Ostrover is a cofounder and co-CEO of Blue Owl, an investment firm specializing in private credit with $250 billion in assets under management.
Ostrover started credit firm Owl Rock Capital in 2016. A merger with Dyal Capital as part of a SPAC deal formed Blue Owl and took it public in 2021.
Previously, Ostrover cofounded credit firm GSO Capital Partners, which Blackstone acquired for up to $945 million in cash and stock in 2008.
He stayed at Blackstone until 2015, helping GSO grow to $75 billion in assets under management by the time he left.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, New York University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pennsylvania

name: Ron Sim
about: Ron Sim is the founder of OSIM International, maker of high-end massage chairs.
He took the company private in 2016 when its shares had dropped steeply from their 2014 high.
In both 2018 and 2022, V3 Brands Asia, part of his V3 Group, filed for an IPO in Hong Kong but shelved it due to market volatility.
He owns a majority stake in the popular Bacha Coffee, a more than century-old Moroccan cafe chain, in Singapore.
Sim also has a sizable property portfolio that includes a stake in Perennial Holdings, which was taken private in 2020.
did_you_know_facts: At age 20, he started a company that sold knife sharpeners and other household goods.
Sim has founded R3 Asset Management to back fast-growing companies.
His Futuristic brand supplies wooden and metal store fixtures to a range of retailers from Levi's to Gap to Bath & Body Works.
His fortune also includes stakes in listed companies such as GHY Media (a film production and distribution company) and Jumbo (a seafood restaurant chain).
In April 2025 Bahca opened its first European flagship in Paris.
quote: The key for us is to continue designing new products that people need.

name: Leonard Abess
about: Leonard Abess made headlines for gifting $60 million to more than 450 current and former employees of his City National Bank of Florida after selling it for more than $1 billion duringthe financial crisis.
His father, Leonard Abess Sr., cofounded the bank in 1946, but sold it in the 1980s. Abess bought it out of bankruptcy a few years later and grew it to nearly $3 billion inassets.
Since selling the bank, Abess has bought up nearly 4,000 acres of land across Miami and Vermont, some of which he's using to grow limes.
His company, ThinkLab Ventures, provides capital and financing for commercial real estate development projects.
It also owns a stake in Jersey Jack Pinball, a leading maker of ?artisanal pinball machines? and previously owned a private jet center near Miami.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, The Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: Abess bought Sylvester Stallone's former Miami home for $16.2 million in 1999.
Abess is on the board of trustees of the University of Miami.

name: Alicia Koplowitz
about: In the early 1960s, Alicia Koplowitz inherited a stake in Spanish construction company Fomento de Construcciones y Contratas after her father died.
She sold her stake to sister Esther for $800 million in 1997 and put the money into diverse investments.
Over the years she's invested in steelmaker Acerinox, electric utility Iberdrola, and Banco Sabadell.
Koplowitz owns hotels in Italy and Miami, real estate in Washington, D.C. and Chicago, as well as a stake in Hospes, a Spanish luxury hotel chain.
Her charitable foundation sends Spanish fellows to study child psychiatry in England and the U.S. at Columbia University, Stanford and others.
did_you_know_facts: In 1969 when she was a teenager she married Alberto Cortina, six months after her sister Esther married Cortina's cousin, Alberto Alcocer.
Koplowitz owns property in Madrid with Amancio Ortega, the Spanish billionaire known for fashion giant Zara.

name: Shu Ping
about: Shu Ping is a cofounder of Chinese hot pot chain Haidilao International Holding.
Shu and three friends, including Zhang Yong who became her husband and is now chairman and CEO of the company, set up their first restaurant with personal savings in 1994.
Haidilao has nearly 1,400 restaurants in Greater China. It is renowned for its spicy dishes and attentive customer service, including free manicures for waiting customers.
It spun off its overseas business Super Hi, which went public in Hong Kong in 2022 and had a dual listing on Nasdaq in 2024. Super Hi has over 120 restaurants in international markets.
Shu became chairman of Super Hi in 2023.

name: Ed Craven
about: Ed Craven and Bijan Tehrani founded and run Stake.com, believed to be the largest crypto-backed online casino in the world.
Stake.com generated $4.7 billion of gross revenue in 2024, despite crypto gambling being unavailable in the United States, United Kingdom and much of Europe.
The founders have reinvested its profits into aggressive marketing, putting Stake's name on Formula 1 cars, English Premier League jerseys, UFC octagons and a new livestreaming service.

During the pandemic, Stake started paying content creators on Twitch millions to livestream themselves gambling, transforming the business from $100 million in revenue to over $2 billion in two years.
After Twitch banned Stake from advertising on its platform due to a lack of consumer protections, Craven and Tehrani launched their own competing livestream service, Kick.
did_you_know_facts: Craven and Tehrani first met online as teenagers, playing the videogame "Runescape." The name Stake comes from the controversial "Runescape" game mechanic called "staking."
quote: We've taken two of the most controversial technologies and industries and combined them. So it's always been an uphill battle for us to beat public perception of what the company may stand for.

name: Helena Dassault
about: Helena Dassault is the daughter of Olivier Dassault, an heir to the Dassault aerospace and software fortune.
Olivier Dassault's grandfather founded Dassault Aviation, a French aerospace company that started out making propellers in World War I.
Her father Olivier, a prominent French politician who served as a representative in France's National Assembly, died in a helicopter crash in 2021.
The Dassault family also own the country's daily newspaper Le Figaro, several vineyards and a private aeronautic company.
Her brother Remi is also a billionaire.
did_you_know_facts: She studied acting and theatre at the Actors Factory and is following an acting career.

name: Remi Dassault
about: Remi Dassault is the son of Olivier Dassault, an heir to the Dassault aerospace and software fortune.
Olivier Dassault's grandfather founded Dassault Aviation, a French aerospace company that started out making propellers in World War I.
His father Olivier, a prominent French politician who served as a representative in France's National Assembly, died in a helicopter crash in 2021.
The Dassault family also own the country's daily newspaper Le Figaro, several vineyards and a private aeronautic company.
did_you_know_facts: His sister Helena is also a billionaire.

name: Constantinos Martinos & family
about: Constantinos Martinos is the owner of Greek shipping firm Thenamaris, which has a fleet of 87 tankers, bulk carriers, container ships and LNG carriers.
He cofounded the company in 1972 with his mother and two brothers. His brothers, Athanasios and Andreas, split off in 1990 and 1998, respectively, leaving him with Thenamaris.
Collectively, Constantinos and his brothers own the largest shipping fleet in Greece, the largest shipowning nation in the world.
Thenamaris is now run by his son, Nikolas. His other son Ioannis runs shipping services firm Signal Group.

name: Marcelo Claure
about: Marcelo Claure is a Bolivian and American entrepreneur who served as chief operating officer of Japanese firm SoftBank.
After selling his first company, a regional phone chain, Claure founded Brightstar, a wireless distributor targeting Latin America.
Claure sold Brightstar to SoftBank in 2014, then joined the firm to run Sprint, a SoftBank investment, as CEO.
Much of his fortune is now tied up in shares of T-Mobile, which merged with Sprint in 2020. Claure sits on T-Mobile's board.
He's now making investments through his family office Claure Group, which owns stakes in fast fashion giant SHEIN and private equity firm Brightstar Capital Partners.
did_you_know_facts: Claure was born in Guatemala and lived in Europe before returning to his parents? home country of Bolivia.
Claure's father was a geologist for the United Nations.

name: Joaquin del Pino y Calvo-Sotelo
about: Joaquin del Pino y Calvo-Sotelo inherited his stake in Spain's Ferrovial S.A., one of the country's largest builders, founded by his late father Rafael del Pino Moreno.

Ferrovial, which means railway in Spanish, was started in an attic in central Madrid and got its big break when it built the railway between the cities of Las Rozas and Chamartín, laying out 18 miles of track in 30 days.
Its business now spans airports, highways, construction and energy.
Formerly an owner of London's Heathrow Airport, Ferrovial built its third runway, two terminals and an integrated baggage system.
Del Pino y Calvo-Sotelo sat on the company's board from 2010 to 2021.
His brother Rafael chairs the company and his sister Maria is president of the family's charitable foundation; both of them are also billionaires.

name: Li Zhongchu
about: Li Zhongchu chairs Shenzhen-listed software firm Beijing Shiji Information Technology.
He quit his first job as a government employee and started the business out of his apartment in 1998.
A Shiji service focus is hotel information management systems..

name: Clayton Zekelman
about: Clayton Zekelman owns a stake in his family's steel business, Zekelman Industries.
The $3.3 billion (revenues) company is one of North America's largest steel pipe and tube makers.
The company has also pumped more than $1 billion into Z Modular, a division that is developing modular apartment complexes in places such as Texas, Arizona and Canada.
Clayton and his brothers, fellow billionaires Barry Zekelman and Alan Zekelman, split 100% ownership of Zekelman Industries.
They sold the company to the Carlyle Group in 2006 for some $1.2 billion, but bought the business back in 2011.
did_you_know_facts: One of Zekelman Industries' subsidiaries, Atlas Tube, produced steel for stretches of the Mexican border wall in Arizona.

name: Phongthep Chiaravanont
about: Phongthep Chiaravanont is a cousin of Thai billionaire Dhanin Chearavanont.
He has been a director on the board of Charoen Pokphand Foods, part of the family's Charoen Pokphand conglomerate, since 1994.
Phongthep studied avian sciences at the University of California, Davis.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, University of California, Davis

name: Christian Birkenstock
about: Christian Birkenstock is an heir to German footwear company Birkenstock, which traces its roots back to 1774.
The company began making its trademark sandals in the 1960s, under the leadership of Christian's father, Karl Birkenstock.
In 2002, Christian and his two brothers, Alex and Stephan, were given control of the company.
Stephan Birkenstock sold his stake to his two brothers in 2013 for an undisclosed amount.
In 2021, the brothers sold Birkenstock to L Catterton and Bernard Arnault's holding company for more than $4.5 billion. Christian rolled forward a stake then worth $300 million.

name: Du Jinhao
about: Du Jinhao chairs Shanghai Allist Pharmaceuticals, a drug supplier based in Shanghai.
Co-founded by Du in 2004, Shanghai Allist specializes in tumor treatment and employs 130 scientists and researchers.
Du, who took the company public in Shanghai in 2020, is a tenured scientist at the National Institutes of Health (NIH) in the U.S.

name: Jim Thompson & family
about: Jim Thompson started his moving company, Crown Worldwide Group, in Japan in 1965, with $1,000.

Crown Worldwide is now one of the world's largest privately held relocation companies, with operations in 45 countries and more than 3,000 employees. It is also involved in document storage and fine-arts transportation.
Thompson moved the company's headquarters to Hong Kong in 1978. He is a permanent resident of Hong Kong.
A citizen of Ireland, he is a native of the state of New Jersey and owns a country estate in Ireland, near the home of his ancestors.
He resigned as chairman in 2025 and is now chairman emeritus; his daughter, Jennifer Harvey, is the group's CEO.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, San Jose State University

did_you_know_facts: In his adopted home, Hong Kong, Thompson served as chairman of the American Chamber of Commerce in Hong Kong.
Thompson celebrates his birthday with an annual tradition of doing a push-up for every year of his life.
quote: I didn't have a vision. Because when you're small, there are so many things that you have to accomplish that the vision is: can I make my payroll next week? You can't think too far beyond that.

name: Zeng Chaolin
about: Zeng Chaolin chairs Shenzhen-listed Tianshan Aluminum Group, a Chinese supplier of aluminum products.
Tianshan's shares trade at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange; it's headquartered in Xinjiang.
Shimge Pump Industry Group acquired Tianshan Aluminum Group in 2020 in a backdoor listing and changed its own name to Tianshan Aluminum Group.
Brother Zeng Chaolin's brother Zeng Chaoyi is a director of the listed company.

name: Cynthia Helena Grossman Fleishman
about: In 1964 Cynthia Grossman's father, Burton Grossman, founded Grupo Continental, a soft drink producing and distributing company.
Grupo Continental merged with Embotelladoras Arca in 2011 to create Arca Continental, the second-largest Coca-Cola bottler in Latin America.
Along with her brother Bruce, Cynthia owns around 10% of the company shares.
Arca Continental has over 45 plants and 345 distribution centers across America.

name: Rafique Malik
about: Rafique Malik's Metro Brands is a popular multi-brand footwear retailer with hundreds of stores across India.
The company is known for its brands such as Mochi, Metro and Walkway.
Farah Malik Bhanji, the second of his five daughters, runs the company as managing director.
Malik took the company public in 2021.
did_you_know_facts: The late billionaire investor Rakesh Jhunjhunwala's wife Rekha has a minority stake in Metro Brands.
Metro was founded in 1955 as a single shoe store in Mumbai by his father Malik Tejani.

name: Dennis Gillings
about: Dennis Gillings is the founder and former CEO and chairman of clinical research firm Quintiles Transnational, which changed its name to IQVIA in 2017.
Gillings, a former biostatistics professor, launched Quintiles in 1982 with the goal of making clinical trials for drugs faster and more efficient.
Gillings retired from the board of IQVIA in 2018.
Quintiles reached annual revenues of $5.7 billion before merging with healthcare data firm IMS Health in 2016.
did_you_know_facts: Gillings received a Commander of the Order of the British Empire from Queen Elizabeth in 2004 for his work in the pharmaceutical industry.

name: Liang Qin & family
about: Liang Qin chairs Yangzhou Yangjie Electronic Technology, a microchip supplier.
The company went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2014.
Yangjie is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Yangzhou.

name: Sergei Studennikov & family
about: Sergei Studennikov is founder of the Krasnoye & Beloye (Red & White) chain of self-service liquor stores, the largest liquor retailer in Russia.
In 2019, he merged it with the Dixy supermarket chain owned by billionaires Igor Kesaev and Sergei Katsiev to form Mercury Retail Group Limited.
Mercury Retail, in which he and his wife have a 49% stake, is the leading alcohol retailer in Russia with 15,000 stores.
Mercury postponed its much anticipated IPO after Putin invaded Ukraine.
In the 1990s, Studennikov founded a company that distributed vodka, beer and tobacco. He opened his first Red & White store in Kopeysk in 2006.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Technology, Satka Mining and Ceramics College

quote: Why Red & White? For the elder generation, red is wine, white is vodka. But now it means red and white wine.

name: Sabrina Benetton
about: Sabrina Benetton is a daughter of Gilberto (d. 2018), one of four siblings who founded clothing retailer Benetton in 1965.
She and her sister Barbara each inherited part of their father's fortune after he died.
Initially Giuliana knitted sweaters, Luciano and Gilberto took care of sales and financials, and Carlo acted as the product manager.
Benetton's colorful sweaters soon won over Italy, and the siblings expanded abroad with their first store in Paris in 1969.
The family later diversified their portfolio and invested in other sectors, including infrastructure and finance.
did_you_know_facts: Sabrina studied at the exclusive Swiss boarding school Le Rosey.
In March 2021, Sabrina stepped down from the board of Atlantia, the infrastructure company controlled by the Benetton family.

name: Yoon Dae-in
about: Yoon Dae-in is the chairman of South Korean biotechnology company Sam Chun Dang Pharm (SCD).
SCD develops active pharmaceutical ingredients used in treatments for dry-eye disease and high blood pressure.
The company also develops novel drug delivery systems, such as S-Pass, which turns injectable medicines into easy-to-take pills.
In January 2026, SCD signed an agreement with Japanese big pharma Daiichi Sankyo to jointly develop and commercialize SCD's weight-loss pill, which was developed using S-Pass, in Japan.
SCD was established in 1943 during the Japanese occupation under the name Chosun Sam Chun Dang. In 1986, after completing his M.B.A. studies, Yoon used family funds to acquire Chosun Sam Chun Dang.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Business Administration, Seoul National University; Master of Business Administration, Long Island University

name: Abdullah Al Othaim
about: Abdullah Saleh Al Othaim chairs the board of Saudi-listed supermarket chain Abdullah Al-Othaim Markets.
The chain has more than 400 stores in Saudi Arabia and some 50 stores in Egypt; 2024 revenue grew to nearly $2.9 billion.
He also chairs Al Othaim Holding Company, a private company that owns and runs shopping malls and restaurants in Saudi Arabia.
Abdullah's father, Sheik Saleh Al Othaim (d. 1979), founded Saleh Al Othaim Trading Establishment in 1956, predecessor of Al-Othaim Markets.
Abdullah Al-Othaim Markets went public in 2008; Abdullah owns a 36% stake.

name: Irving Grousbeck & family
about: Irving Grousbeck is a co-owner of the NBA's Boston Celtics. His son, Wycliffe, is the franchise's lead owner and governor.
He cofounded Continental Cablevision in 1963, which merged with US West in 1996.
In 2002, Grousbeck, his son and a group of investors bought the Celtics for $360 million. The team is now worth $6 billion.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard University; Bachelor of Arts, Amherst College

name: Benjamin Otto
about: Benjamin Otto inherited a 15.1% stake in Otto Group, which his grandfather, Werner, started as a mail-order business in 1949.
His father, Michael Otto, he ran the business for 26 years until 2007. He is now chairman of its supervisory board.
With revenues exceeding $15 billion, Otto Group has more than 40 companies in retail (including Crate and Barrel), real estate and financial services.
Benjamin joined the family company as an executive director in 2012.
did_you_know_facts: Benjamin Otto and his wife are active in philanthropic organizations focused on healing through alternative treatment methods.

name: Chen Jinxia
about: Chen Jinxia is the widow of entrepreneur Wei Dong, who committed suicide in 2008.
Chen inherited a controlling interest in Hunan Yongjin Group, which was founded by her late husband and owns shares in drug makers.
Chen graduated from Shanghai University of Finance & Economics

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

name: Huang Jiangji
about: Huang Jiangji is cofounder and vice president of Chinese smartphone maker Xiaomi.
He worked for Microsoft from 1997 to 2010, serving as the director of development at Microsoft's China Academy of Engineering.
Huang is a graduate of Purdue University.

name: Dong Wei
about: Dong Wei chairs Liangyungang Hengchuang Pharmaceutical Technology.
He chairs the supervisory committee of Shanghai-listed Jiangsu Hengrui Medicine.
Liangyungang Hengchuang holds a stake in Hengrui.
Dong graduated from China Pharmaceutical University in 1993.
He worked for the predecessor of Jiangsu Hengrui Medicine after his graduation.

name: Drorit Wertheim
about: David and Drorit Wertheim are the children of the late Moshe Wertheim (d. 2016) who founded the Central Bottling Company, Israel's only Coca Cola bottler.
Before he died, Moshe Wertheim gave his children ownership over the company, as well as his shares in Mizrahi Tefahot Bank and Alony Hetz.
In 2018, David purchased all of his sister's shares in Alony Hetz, then sold them because of Israeli anti-monopoly rules.
In 2019, the siblings became majority shareholders in Mizrahi Tefahot bank.
David controls 67% of the Central Bottling Company and manages the business while Drorit owns the remaining shares.

name: Lee Chae-yoon
about: Lee Chae-yoon is the founder and CEO of Leeno Industrial, a manufacturer of semiconductor-testing equipment in South Korea.
The company's main products are IC Test Socket, which helps test chips to ensure they work, and Leeno Pin, a pin that helps check for defects in chips and printed circuit boards.
Leeno claims to have more than 1,000 customers globally, including Nvidia, Samsung Electronics and memory chip giant SK Hynix.
Lee founded Leeno in 1978, nine years after graduating from Kwangsung Engineering High School in Busan.
The company listed on Korea's technology-rich Kosdaq stock exchange in 2001.
did_you_know_facts: The company's name is a combination of Lee's surname and that of his wife.

name: Ales Zavoral
about: Ales Zavoral is a Czech billionaire who, in 1994, founded Alza.cz, the e-commerce giant based in Czechia that operates in Germany, Austria, Hungary, Slovakia and other parts of central Europe.
According to recently published book, Ales Zavoral started as a collector of cigarettes butts and sold them to drunken punk club goers.
Ales Zavoral started to make computers in college sold them out of his dorm.
did_you_know_facts: Zavoral is an avid basketball lover and experienced pilot, and he owns a small bio farm in Bohemia, Czechia.

name: Noam Gottesman
about: Noam Gottesman cofounded hedge fund GLG Partners in 1995, which started out as a subsidiary of Lehman Brothers.
GLG went public in 2007 and was sold to Man Group for $1.6 billion in 2010. Gottesman stepped down as CEO at the time of the sale.
In 2014, Gottesman cofounded Nomad Foods, which is today Europe's largest frozen food company.
Gottesman's art collection has hundreds of works including pieces by Andy Warhol, Francis Bacon and Lucian Freud.
did_you_know_facts: Gottesman invested in Eleven Madison Park in 2011; six years later it was named the best restaurant in the world by one publication.
Gottesman also owns 200 Burger King franchises.

name: Somsri Lamsam
about: Somsri Lamsam draws her wealth from a 4.21% stake in the holding outfit of the Charoen Pokphand Group, one of the world's largest producers of animal feed and livestock.
Her late father Montri Jiaravanont was the son of Chia Ek Chor, who along with his brother Choncharoen Chiaravanont, opened a shop selling seeds imported from China in 1921.
CP's other assets include stakes in Chinese insurer Ping An, Hong Kong conglomerate CITIC and telecom unit True Corp. It also owns Tesco's operations in Thailand and Malaysia.

name: Roberto Hernandez Ramirez
about: Roberto Hernández Ramirez made a fortune in banking, beginning with the establishment of brokerage firm Acciones y Valores, also known as Accival.
Accival purchased Mexican bank Banamex in 1991, becoming Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival, which Hernández chaired.
In 2001 Citigroup purchased Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival for $12 billion in cash and stock.

name: Manas Chiaravanond
about: Manas Chiaravanond is part of the clan behind Thai conglomerate Charoen Pokphand Group.
He derives his wealth from his 4.2% stake in holding outfit CP Group.
Manas is the CEO of the family's food outfit Chia Tai.
He's a cousin of CP group head, Dhanin Chearavanont.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, California State University, Sacramento; B.Com, Eastern Kentucky University

name: Alberto Cortina
about: Alberto Cortina's fortune stems largely from construction company ACS, which is headed by fellow billionaire Florentino Pérez.
Alberto Cortina was married to Alicia Koplowitz, a billionaire who was a significant shareholder of the FCC construction group; they divorced in the nineties
Along with his billionaire cousin Alberto Alcocer, Cortina also had interests in banking, running Banco Zaragozano. They sold their combined 40% stake to Barclays in 2004.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctor of Jurisprudence, Universidad Complutense de Madrid

did_you_know_facts: Cortina owns several ranches in Toledo, Spain, along with houses in Mallorca and Madrid.
The Panama Papers revealed that Cortina and his cousin Alcocer had offshore accounts in the Central American tax haven country.

name: Jerry Speyer & family
about: Real estate baron Jerry Speyer redeveloped landmarks like Rockefeller Center and the Chrysler Building in Manhattan.
Jerry is the chairman of Tishman Speyer and his son Rob is CEO. Until 2015, they held co-CEO titles.
Tishman Speyer has developed over 152 million square feet, including skyscrapers in New York, Chicago, Berlin, London, Frankfurt and Paris.
Speyer started the firm with his late father-in-law, Robert Tishman, in 1978. The marriage ended in divorce, but the company survived.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Columbia Business School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Columbia University

did_you_know_facts: Speyer was chairman of the Museum of Modern Art's board of trustees for 11 years and was elected chairman of New York Presbyterian Hospital in 2018.
Speyer has hundreds of art works in his personal collection, which skews contemporary and includes pieces by Damien Hirst and Andy Warhol.

name: Zhang Bangxin
about: Zhang Bangxin is the cofounder and chairman of education services firm TAL Education.
TAL went public on the New York Stock Exchange in October 2010.
Zhang holds degrees from Sichuan University and the China Europe International Business School.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: EMBA, China Europe International Business School

name: Howard Marks
about: Howard Marks is the cofounder and co-chairman of Oaktree Capital Management, a Los Angeles-based distressed debt investor with over $220 billion in assets.
Marks began his career at Citibank, where he started a portfolio of high-yield bonds after meeting with junk bond king Michael Milken.
He became an asset manager at TCW, where he met Oaktree cofounder Bruce Karsh. The duo left with four colleagues in 1995 to found their own shop.
In September 2019, Brookfield Asset Management acquired 61% of Oaktree for about $4.9 billion in cash and stock. It agreed to buy the rest for $3 billion in 2025.
He and Karsh still head up Oaktree, which continues to operate independently of Brookfield. His stake in the firm is now about 7.5%.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School

did_you_know_facts: Marks is known for his highly detailed investment memos, which cover everything from cryptocurrency to index investing.
The Wharton and UChicago alum minored in Japanese studies, which he became interested in after signing up for a mandatory literature class.

name: Natacha Nikolajevic
about: Natacha Nikolajevic is the widow of Olivier Dassault, an heir to the Dassault aerospace and software fortune.
Olivier Dassault's grandfather founded Dassault Aviation, a French aerospace company that started out making propellers in World War I.
Nikolajevic's husband Olivier, a prominent French politician who served as a representative in France's National Assembly, died in a helicopter crash in 2021.
The Dassault family also own the country's daily newspaper Le Figaro, several vineyards and a private aeronautic company.
did_you_know_facts: She met her late billionaire husband Olivier during an auction where they competed for the same item.

name: Sandor Csanyi
about: Sandor Csanyi is the most powerful banker in Hungary and CEO of OTP Bank, one of the largest financial services firms in Central and Eastern Europe.
When he took over OTP in 1992, he did the unthinkable in a formerly socialist country and fired a number of managers and introduced new technology.
Csanyi is also one of Hungary's biggest investors in agriculture, whose Bonafarm operates the second biggest slaughterhouse in the nation.
He also sits on the board of regional oil giant MOL.
From 1983 to 1986, he was a departmental head at the Ministry of Agriculture and Food Industry.
did_you_know_facts: Csnyi is the President of the Hungarian Football Association.

name: Vivek Chand Burman
about: Chairman emeritus of Indian consumer goods outfit Dabur, Vivek Chand Burman, is the oldest member of the founding Burman clan.
Dabur was started by his great-grandfather in 1884 to sell ayurvedic medicines.
He joined the company in 1954 and became chairman in 1998 holding that post for close to a decade.
In 2007, he handed over charge to nephew Anand Burman, who is also a billionaire. His son, Mohit, was appointed chairman of Dabur in 2022.
Burman has a stake in Kolkata-based battery maker Eveready Industries.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Miami

did_you_know_facts: Burman's sons Mohit and Gaurav are involved in a slew of privately-held ventures ranging from sports and healthcare to financial services and real estate.
Gaurav owns the franchise for Taco Bell in India.

name: Kim Nam-goo
about: Kim Nam-goo is the chief executive and largest shareholder of Korea Investment Holdings, the country's only non-bank financial holding company.
The eldest son of Dongwon founder Kim Jae-chul, Kim started at Dongwon Securities (precursor to Korea Investment Holdings) in 1991.
His brother, Kim Nam-jung, is chairman of packaged seafood producer Dongwon.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Korea University; Master of Business Administration, Tsinghua University; Master of Business Administration, Keio University

did_you_know_facts: When Kim was young, his father had him spend four months at sea on a deep-sea fishing vessel (Dongwon started as a tuna-processing and distribution company).

name: Gordon Wu
about: Gordon Wu is the chairman of Hopewell Holdings, one of the largest commercial landlords in Hong Kong's Wan Chai business district.
The Princeton University-educated tycoon also boasts interests in power and transportation infrastructure projects in mainland China.
Son Thomas Jefferson was deputy chairman and managing director of Hopewell until 2019. He sits on the board of Asian casino giant Melco Resorts & Entertainment.
In 2019, Wu took Hopewell private from the Hong Kong stock exchange in a HK$21 billion ($2.7 billion) deal.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Princeton University; Master, Princeton University

did_you_know_facts: The Queen of England conferred upon Wu the title of Knight Commander of the Order of St. Michael and St. George in 1997 for his contribution to Asian infrastructure.

name: Pawel Marchewka
about: Pawel Marchewka is the founder and CEO of Polish videogame company, Techland.
Founded in 1991, Techland is the publisher of zombie-themed titles including the Dead Island and Dying Light franchises.
Techland was sold to Chinese technology giant Tencent in 2024 for a reporrted 6.9 billion zloty ($1.7 billion).
The sale to Tencent came on the heels of news about internal struggles and layoffs at the gaming company.

name: Li Jianli
about: Li Jianli chairs Shenzhen Kedali Industry, a supplier of lithium battery components.
Kedali went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2017.
The company's customers include CATL, BYD, CALB, EVE Energy, Panasonic and LG.

name: Juan March Delgado
about: Juan March Delgado is one of the two largest shareholders of $2.5 billion (net assets) Banca March, Spain's only 100% family-owned bank.
Juan and his billionaire brother Carlos March Delgado are grandchildren of Banca March's founder, Juan March (d. 1962), who started the business in Palma de Mallorca in 1926.
Until 2018, Juan was co-chairman of the $5 billion (net assets) investment company Corporación Financiera Alba, which is also nearly 100% family-owned.
Juan and Carlos March Delgado own 69% of Banca March and 42% of Corporación Financiera Alba combined (excluding Banca March's 15% stake in Corporación Financiera Alba).
Juan is president of the family's philanthropic foundation, Fundación Juan March, which focuses on the arts.

name: Jupally Rameshwar Rao
about: Jupally Rameshwar Rao founded My Home Constructions, a residential and commercial property developer, in 1981.
The privately held My Home is a prominent real estate player in the southern Indian city of Hyderabad.
The company's projects span the gamut from apartments to villa communities to office buildings.
The My Home Group also has interests in cement and education.
did_you_know_facts: Rao was reportedly among the donors for the construction of the 216-foot tall Statue of Equality depicting Ramanuja, an 11th century Hindu philosopher, in Hyderabad.

name: Prem Kumar Arora
about: Prem Kumar Arora gets the bulk of his wealth from his stake in Indian generics maker Mankind Pharma.
The company was founded by his wife's brothers Ramesh and Rajeev Juneja in 1995.
