Mankind Pharma sells generic drugs including antibiotics and treatments for cardiovascular diseases in over two dozen markets worldwide.
The company went public in India in May 2023, raising 43.3 billion rupees ($529 million).

name: Hamdi Akin & family
about: Hamdi Akin is the founder of Akfen Holding, a conglomerate with investments in energy, real estate development and infrastructure.
During college, he produced heating boilers and water and fuel tanks in his father's workshop. After graduating, he started Akfen as a contractor.
Winning tenders for operating the Istanbul Ataturk Airport and Ankara Esenboga Airport led him to establish TAV Airports Holding.
In 2012, he sold 38% of TAV to Aeroports de Paris Group for $874 million. In 2017, he sold his remaining 8% to Aeroports de Paris for $160 million.
Today, Afken is mainly focused on renewable energy, building hospitals and developing and renting apartments to students.
did_you_know_facts: Akin has transferred ownership of Akfen to daughter Pelin and son Selim. They both serve on its board.
In December 2015, he donated six flats he owned in a compound in Istanbul Beylikduzu to Syrian refugees.
quote: Companies grow when they are sold, when they get new partners. If you don't sell, if shares don't change hands, they don't become immortal but die with their owners.

name: Alexandra Burt
about: Alexandra Burt sold a stake In February 2025 in there family's Rhodes Ridge iron ore project to Japanese investment company Mitsui.
Her sister Leonie Baldock and her aunt Angela Bennett had stakes in the the same project and are fellow billionaires.
Burt's grandfather Peter Wright established a mining partnership with mining magnate Gina Rinehart's father Lang Hancock in the 1950s.
Part of her wealth comes from a stake in Wright Prospecting, a privately owned mining firm based in Perth.

name: Liu Chengyu & family
about: Liu Chengyu chairs Shenzhen Kstar Science and Technology, a maker of uninterruptible power supply equipment, inverters and storage for the solar power industry.
KStar went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2010.
Kstar is headquartered in Shenzhen, China.
He joined the company, which is also based in Shenzhen, in 1993 before rising through the ranks.
His first job out of college was a high school teacher.

name: Fiona Geminder
about: Fiona Geminder owns a substantial stake in listed plastics-packaging business Pact Group, with her husband Raphael Geminder.
She also holds a large stake in her family's paper packaging and recycling business, Visy Asia-Pacific.
She holds the Visy Asia-Pacific stake with her brother Anthony Pratt and sister Heloise Pratt, who are both also billionaires.
Pact Group was delisted in 2025 after Raphael Geminder's holding company, Bennamon Industries, launched a takeover bid in 2023.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: LLB, Monash University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Monash University

name: Prathip Chiravanond
about: Prathip Chiravanond is part of the clan behind Thai conglomerate Charoen Pokphand Group.
Prathip studied at the University of California, Davis from where he earned degrees in plant sciences, including a doctorate in plant physiology.
He sits on the board of trustees of the International School Bangkok.

name: Vlad Yatsenko
about: Vlad Yatsenko is cofounder of digital bank Revolut, which was valued by private investors at $75 billion in November 2025.
The dual British-Ukrainian citizen called Vladimir Putin "one of the most brazen liars in history" on February 24, the day Russia invaded Ukraine.
Revolut, which he runs with Nik Storonsky, who grew up in Russia but left at age 20, helped raise more than $11 million in donations for the Ukrainian Red Cross.
Yatsenko is Revolut's chief technology officer; he previously built software at UBS, Deutsche Bank and Credit Suisse.
Yatsenko owns a bit less than 3% of Revolut.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Diploma, National University of Kyiv-Mohyla Academy

name: Liang Rubo
about: Liang Rubo is the chairman of the board of ByteDance, the China internet giant that owns TikTok.
Liang was a cofounder along with Zhang Yiming, who stepped down as CEO in 2021.
The two reportedly were college roommates at Nankai University in China.
ByteDance is best known for its hugely popular social video app TikTok, which is now in danger of being banned in the U.S. It also operates news app Toutiao.

name: Adarsh Hiremath
about: Adarsh Hiremath is a cofounder of Mercor, a recruiting startup that helps Silicon Valley's biggest AI labs train their models.

Hiremath and his cofounders Brendan Foody and Surya Midha became the world's three youngest self-made billionaires in October 2025, when private investors valued Mercor at $10 billion. All three were 22 at the time, but Midha is the youngest by roughly two months.
Foody serves as CEO of Mercor, while Hiremath serves as chief technology officer. Midha transitioned from his role as chief operating officer to become the company's chairman in October 2025.
Foody, Hiremath and Midha founded Mercor in 2023. Each cofounder owns an estimated 22% stake in the company.
In September 2025, Mercor announced the company had hit $500 million in annualized revenue, up from $100 million in March.

name: Brendan Foody
about: Brendan Foody is a cofounder of Mercor, a recruiting startup that helps Silicon Valley's biggest AI labs train their models.

Foody and his cofounders Surya Midha and Adarsh Hiremath became the world's three youngest self-made billionaires in October 2025, when private investors valued Mercor at $10 billion. All three were 22 at the time, but Midha is the youngest by roughly two months.
Foody serves as CEO of Mercor, while Hiremath serves as chief technology officer. Midha transitioned from his role as chief operating officer to become the company's chairman in October 2025.
Foody, Hiremath and Midha founded Mercor in 2023. Each cofounder owns an estimated 22% stake in the company.
In September 2025, Mercor announced the company had hit $500 million in annualized revenue, up from $100 million in March.

name: Surya Midha
about: Surya Midha is a cofounder of Mercor, a recruiting startup that helps Silicon Valley's biggest AI labs train their models.

Midha and his cofounders Brendan Foody and Adarsh Hiremath became the world's three youngest self-made billionaires in October 2025, when private investors valued Mercor at $10 billion. All three were 22 at the time, but Midha is the youngest by roughly two months.
Foody serves as CEO of Mercor, while Hiremath serves as chief technology officer. Midha transitioned from his role as chief operating officer to become the company's chairman in October 2025.
Foody, Hiremath and Midha founded Mercor in 2023. Each cofounder owns an estimated 22% stake in the company.
In September 2025, Mercor announced the company had hit $500 million in annualized revenue, up from $100 million in March.

name: Basudeo Singh
about: Basudeo Singh is the executive chairman of Indian generics firm Alkem Laboratories.
The company has 18 factories including one in California to make pharmaceutical ingredients.
Basudeo Singh is the cousin of Alkem's late billionaire cofounder Samprada Singh.
His son Dhananjay Kumar Singh, Alkem's joint managing director, who was named to succeed him as executive chairman, passed away in 2021.

name: Bijan Tehrani
about: Ed Craven and Bijan Tehrani founded and run Stake.com, believed to be the largest crypto-backed online casino in the world.
Stake.com generated $4.7 billion of gross revenue in 2024, despite crypto gambling being unavailable in the United States, United Kingdom and much of Europe.
The founders have reinvested its profits into aggressive marketing, putting Stake's name on Formula 1 cars, English Premier League jerseys, UFC octagons and a new livestreaming service.
During the pandemic, Stake started paying content creators on Twitch to livestream themselves gambling, transforming the business from $100 million in revenue to $2 billion in just two years.
After Twitch banned Stake from advertising on its platform due to a lack of consumer protections, Craven and Tehrani launched their own competing livestream service, Kick.
did_you_know_facts: Craven and Tehrani first met online as teenagers, playing the videogame "Runescape." The name Stake comes from its controversial game mechanic called "staking."
quote: When you have people's attention, you should invest everything you can to hold onto that.

name: Sanjeev Bikhchandani
about: Indian internet pioneer, Sanjeev Bikhchandani, draws his wealth from listed Info Edge (India).
Info Edge owns portals for job search (naukri.com), matrimony (jeevansathi.com); real estate (99acres.com) and education (shiksha.com).
It also owns stakes in online food delivery outfit Zomato and insurance marketplace, policybazaar.com. Both companies went public in 2021.
Bikhchandani, who studied at the premier Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad, is founder and executive vice-chairman of Info Edge.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad; Bachelor of Arts/Economics, St Stephen's College (India)

did_you_know_facts: He cofounded and funded Ashoka University, a liberal arts institution, which is located in the north Indian state of Haryana.

name: Pavel Baudis
about: In 1988 software engineer Pavel Baudis wrote his first antivirus program after a friend sent him a floppy disk containing the "Vienna" computer virus.
In April that year, he and Eduard Kucera, with whom he'd worked at Research Institute of Mathematical Machines, cofounded ALWIL to sell the software.
Following the fall of Communism in 1989, the pair broke off to establish what would become Avast.
Now run by an outside CEO, Avast, which secures online activities for more than 435 million users, went public in 2018.
Its goals for the future are loftier: to protect all things in your home connected to the internet, from thermostats to webcams.

name: Steven Tisch
about: Steven Tisch is chairman and executive vice president of NFL's NY Giants. His late father Bob paid $75 million in 1991 for a 50% stake in the team.
Bob Tisch (d. 2005) cofounded Loews Corp. with his brother Laurence (d. 2003) as a New Jersey hotel venture in 1946.
Today, Loews Corp., a publicly traded company, is active in insurance, drilling rigs, natural gas pipelines and hotels.
Steven's mother Joan (d. 2017) was the largest individual shareholder of Loews with a 6% stake. His brother Jonathan is co-chairman.
Steven, Jonathan and sister Laurie Tisch, inherited their mother's fortune.
did_you_know_facts: Steven is the only known person to have won both an Academy Award and a Super Bowl ring: he won an Oscar for producing Forrest Gump, and the Giants won two Super Bowls.
Steven has been a movie producer for decades, working on hit films including Risky Business, American History X, and The Pursuit of Happyness.

name: Laurie Tisch
about: Laurie Tisch's late father Bob (d. 2005) started Loews Corporation with his brother Laurence (d. 2003) as a New Jersey hotel venture in 1946.
Today, Loews is active in insurance, drilling rigs, natural gas pipelines, and hotels.
Laurie's mother Joan Tisch (d. 2017) was the largest individual Loews shareholder with a 6% stake. Laurie and her two siblings inherited her mother's stake.
In 1991, her father Bob bought a 50% stake in the New York Giants for $75 million.
Laurie's brother Steve Tisch is chairman and executive vice president of the NFL team, which FORBES values at $6.3 billion (net of debt).
did_you_know_facts: An avid art collector, Laurie Tisch is a trustee at the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York City.
In 2008, Tisch worked with then-New York Mayor Michael Bloomberg to launch NYC Green Carts, which provides fresh produce to "food deserts" throughout the city.

name: Lisa Su
about: Lisa Su, the CEO of semiconductor firm Advanced Micro Devices, has led one of the greatest recent turnarounds in the technology sector.
In 2025 the company announced a partnership with OpenAI (the creator of ChatGPT), highlighting the use of AMD chips for computing power.
Next, she's preparing for battle against Nvidia in the AI revolution, and expects to keep winning; Nvidia is run by her distant relative Jensen Huang.
The daughter of a mathematician and a bookkeeper turned entrepreneur, Su was born in Tainan, Taiwan, in 1969, and immigrated to New York City at age 3.
After graduating from the Bronx High School of Science, Su went to MIT, where she earned a bachelor's (and later a Ph.D.) in electrical engineering because it seemed to be the most difficult major.
She did stints at Texas Instruments, IBM and Freescale, then joined AMD in 2012 and became CEO two years later.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Ph.D, Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Bachelor of Engineering, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

did_you_know_facts: During her time at IBM, Su worked directly with highly respected CEO Lou Gerstner.

name: John Armitage
about: John Armitage is the cofounder and chief investment officer of Egerton Capital, a hedge fund firm with $19.9 billion under management.
Armitage was born in the U.K., but in 2018 he changed his citizenship to Ireland.
Egerton Capital has generated $30.9 billion of net gains since inception in 1995, according to Edmond de Rothschild research.

name: Linda Pritzker
about: A scion of the billionaire Pritzker family, Linda Pritzker devotes herself to Tibetan Buddhism rather than her family's enterprises.
She is building a spiritual retreat center in Montana dedicated to Tibetan Buddhist practice; she offers online courses and annual coastal retreats in the interim.
Her father Robert Pritzker and his brother Jay Pritzker built up manufacturing business Marmon Holdings and sold it to Berkshire Hathaway in 2008.
Pritzker goes by Lama Tsomo in her teaching and professional capacities.
The Pritzker family also built the Hyatt hotel empire.
did_you_know_facts: Pritzker published a Westerner's guide to Tibetan Buddhist meditation that included an introductory letter from H.H. Dalai Lama.
Pritzker was one of the first American women to be ordained as a Lama in the Tibetan Buddhist tradition.
quote: As long as you have the basics in life - basic food, shelter, clothing - after that, a lot of it is dependent on what's going on in the inside. Because where you experience happiness is in the inside.

name: Gustavo Denegri & family
about: Gustavo Denegri is the chairman of biotech company DiaSorin SpA; the bulk of his fortune is a 45% stake in the publicly-traded company.
In 2000, his private equity firm acquired the distressed DiaSorin from American Standard Companies and built it into a global player in diagnostics.
His first breakthrough came when his Gruppo Pro-Ind, a components firm, merged with Piaggio, owner of motor scooters Vespa and Aprilia.
He is one of few Italian businessmen to have built billion-dollar companies in more than one sector.
His firm Investimenti is run by his son Michele and has a diverse portfolio, including medical technology, real estate and TV production.
did_you_know_facts: Gustavo Denegri was trained as a chemist.

name: Wong Luen Hei
about: Wong Luen Hei chairs Hong Kong-listed China Lesso, a supplier of building materials and interior decorations products like pipes and windows.
Wong's wife Zuo Xiaoping and brother-in-law Zuo Manlun sit on Lesso's board.
Lesso is headquartered in the southern Chinese city of Foshan.

name: Alberto Bombassei
about: Alberto Bombassei chairs Brembo, a global leader in high-performance braking technology.
Brembo's brakes can be found in Ferraris, Corvettes and Harley-Davidsons around the world.
Founded by Alberto's father Emilio, Brembo broke into the big leagues in 1975, when Enzo Ferrari asked Emilio to outfit his race cars.
Alberto became general manager of the company in 1976, managing director in 1984 and was chairman from 1993 to 2021.
He has transferred his shares in the publicly traded company to his children, Luca and Cristina, but maintains control over their 53.5% stake.

name: Petter Stordalen & family
about: Petter Stordalen and his three children own Scandinavia's largest hotel chain, Nordic Choice Hotels, which has 180 high-end hotels in five countries.
In 2018 he signed over almost all ownership, but none of the control, of the hotel chain to his kids; he has vowed to keep control until his death.
Stordalen got his start working at his father's grocery store at age 10, and later helped found one of Norway's largest commercial real estate firms.
He married model-turned-physician Gunhild Stordalen in a lavish $5 million affair officiated by Irish singer Bob Geldof in 2010.
did_you_know_facts: A committed environmentalist, Stordalen chained himself to the U.K.'s Sellafield nuclear reprocessing plant in protest in 2002.
A former Ironman triathlete, Stordalen runs 6 miles a day.

name: Cheng Yixiao
about: Cheng is the cofounder of Kuaishou, a short video platform headquartered in Beijing.
The company went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in February 2021.
Pre-IPO strategic investors included funds managed by Fidelity and BlackRock.
Kuaishou cofounder Su Hua is also a billionaire.
Cheng, the CEO, succeeded Su and added the role of chairman in October 2023.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, Northeastern University Engineering; Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Northeastern University

name: Akio Nitori
about: Akio Nitori founded discount home furnishings chain Nitori Holdings; its shares trade on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
The company has expanded in urban markets like Tokyo and has more than 1,000 stores mostly in Japan.
Nitori, the firm's chairman, opened the first store in 1967. He stepped down as president in 2016.
The chain has stores outside Japan in China, Taiwan, South Korea, India and several Southeast Asia countries.
did_you_know_facts: To earn money for college tuition and expenses, he worked collecting unpaid bar tabs and hustling pool, among other jobs.
In 2020, the company acquired home-improvement chain Shimachu in a nearly $2 billion deal.

name: Jerry Moyes & family
about: Jerry Moyes and his father founded Swift Transportation in 1966 with one truck, moving cotton and imported steel between Arizona and California
Swift grew to nearly 20,000 trucks and some $4 billion in annual revenue before it merged with Knight Transportation in 2017.
Moyes sold much of his stake in Knight-Swift prior to 2022. Now concentrates on SME Industries, a steel fabricator and construction company in Utah.
Moyes owned the Phoenix Coyotes hockey team, with minority partner Wayne Gretzky, until the team filed for bankruptcy in 2009 and was sold to the NHL.
did_you_know_facts: Moyes resigned as Swift CEO in 2005 after an insider-trading case (he did not admit to wrongdoing). Two years later, he took Swift private in a leveraged buyout.
Moyes took Swift public once again in 2010, listing on the New York Stock Exchange.

name: Dragos Paval
about: Dragos Paval and his brother, Adrian, own Dedeman, a leading Romanian construction materials and do-it-yourself home products retailer.
The $2 billion (sales) company's 57 stores stock some 60,000 products, ranging from tools and building supplies to furniture and appliances.
The brothers founded the business in 1992 with a single location in Bacau, Romania.
They also own shares of several publicly traded Romanian companies and a portfolio of real estate in Bucharest and the northern city of Cluj.

name: Marc Lasry
about: Marc Lasry and his sister Sonia founded Avenue Capital Management in 1995 with $7 million in funding from friends and family.
The firm manages about $13 billion in assets and focuses on distressed and undervalued securities.
Lasry was born in Morocco and moved to the U.S. at age 7 with his family, sharing a bedroom with his 2 siblings for a decade.
He is a major supporter of the Democratic Party, having raised funds for President Obama and candidate Hilary Clinton in the past.
Lasry reportedly sold a 25% stake in the Milwaukee Bucks in 2023, when the team was valued at $3.5 billion.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Clark University; Doctor of Jurisprudence, New York Law School

did_you_know_facts: In 2017, his daughter Sophie married Alex Swieca, the son of a cofounder of hedge fund Highbridge Capital.
A comic book collector, Lasry sold a Wonder Woman #1 comic at auction for a record $291,000 in 2016.

name: Matthew Roszak
about: Matthew Roszak is a cryptocurrency investor and cofounder and chairman of Bloq, a blockchain startup that consults on projects such as helping banks store digital assets.
Bloq also helps companies that are trying to process transactions for "stablecoins," or cryptocurrencies pegged to the value of a fiat currency.
In the 1990s and early 2000s, Roszak worked in venture capital and as an entrepreneur before amassing a crypto portfolio starting in 2012.
He settled insider trading charges in 2006 related to stock purchases of Blue Rhino, a propane tank exchange business.
Roszak co-led an initiative to give each member of Congress $50 worth of digital assets; some accepted, but not all.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Economics, Lake Forest College

name: Alberto Alcocer
about: Alberto Cortina derives his wealth largely from shares in construction company ACS, led by billionaire Florentino Pérez.
He and his billionaire cousin Alberto Cortina ran their wives' Construcciones y Contratas firm from the early 1970s until 1989, when both marriages fell apart.
Alcocer and Cortina then moved into banking, running Banco Zaragozano. They sold their combined 40% stake to Barclays in 2004
The cousins were married to sisters Esther and Alicia Koplowitz, who were previously significant shareholders of the FCC construction group.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctor of Jurisprudence, Universidad Complutense de Madrid

did_you_know_facts: Alcocer owns several ranches in Cadiz and Toledo, Spain, along with houses in Paris and Madrid.
The Panama Papers revealed that Alcocer and his cousin Cortina had offshore accounts in the Central American tax haven country.

name: Mario Gabelli
about: Mario Gabelli runs Gamco, a mutual fund and investment firm he founded in 1977.
Gabelli's reputation for stock-picking took off in the 1980s, when he found success betting on the media and telecom sectors.
A first-generation college student, Gabelli graduated from Fordham University's business school, now named for him, in 1965.
He is a big donor to higher education and a signatory of the Giving Pledge.
He also serves as executive chairman of Associated Capital Group, an investment management business that spun off from Gamco in 2015.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Columbia Business School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Fordham University

did_you_know_facts: A life-long contrarian, even as a schoolboy Gabelli refused to hide with classmates during air raid drills.
Around age five, Gabelli set up a shoe-shine box at a Bronx subway station to make money. He bought his first stocks at 13 years old.
quote: That's my approach to life: Go where others fear to tread. Hell, I bought a Cadillac in the middle of the oil embargo.

name: Jian Jun
about: Jian Jun is the chairwoman of biomedical supplier Imeik Technology Development, which makes products like skin fillers and facial implant threads.
Imeik listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2020, in an IPO that raised more than $530 million.
Best known for its Hearty filler that treats neck wrinkles, the company has also branched into segments such as skincare products amid heightened competition.
Jian worked for the state-owned China National Cereals Oils and Foodstuffs Import and Export early in her career.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Tsinghua University

name: Chen Qixing
about: Chen Qixing is the chairman of Shenzhen Everwin Precision Technology, a Shenzhen-listed electronics component manufacturer.
Chen was a government official in Anhui Province before becoming an entrepreneur.

name: Strive Masiyiwa
about: Strive Masiyiwa overcame protracted government opposition to launch mobile phone network Econet Wireless Zimbabwe in his country of birth in 1998.
He owns 38% of publicly-traded Econet Wireless Zimbabwe, which is one part of his larger Econet Group, as well as roughly 33% of mobile phone-based money transfer firm EcoCash.
Masiyiwa also owns a stake in private company Liquid Intelligent Technologies, which provides fiber optic and and cloud-based services to telecom firms across Africa.
His other assets include investments in fintech and power distribution firms in Africa plus stock options in Netflix, where he has served on the board since December 2020.
He and his wife Tsitsi founded the Higherlife Foundation, which supports orphaned and poor children in Zimbabwe, South Africa, Burundi and Lesotho.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, University of Wales

did_you_know_facts: After studying at university in Britain, Masiyiwa worked at ZPTC, Zimbabwe's phone company.
He left ZPTC to start an engineering services firm, then sold it and founded Econet Wireless Zimbabwe, but had to battle the government in court for years.

name: Larry Robbins
about: Larry Robbins is founder and CEO of Glenview Capital Management, a New York hedge fund that oversees $2.6 billion in assets.
Robbins is known for his hot and cold streaks, with his returns swinging wildly from one year to the next.
Through his Robbins Family Foundation, he is an active supporter of education reform both in New York City and on the national level.
In 2017, Robbins began serving as chairman of the Robin Hood Foundation, which fights poverty in New York City.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School

did_you_know_facts: Robbins named his firm Glenview after the town outside Chicago where his childhood hockey team practiced.
Robbins, who played hockey at the University of Pennsylvania, built an indoor hockey rink next to his house in New Jersey.

name: J. Frank Harrison III & family
about: J. Frank Harrison, III is the long-time chairman and CEO of Coca-Cola Consolidated, the largest independent Coca-Cola bottler in the U.S.
He owns 15% of the publicly traded company, which his great-grandfather J.B. Harrison founded in 1902, but has majority voting control.
He succeeded his father J. Frank Harrison, Jr. (d. 2002) as CEO in 1994 and chairman in 1996.
A graduate of the University of North Carolina and Duke MBA, he joined the Charlotte-based company in 1977 and got his start running routes and operating bottling lines.
A devout Christian, he cofounded a missionary organization called Open Eyes with his son James Harrison IV, who died while doing relief work in Kenya in 2010.

name: Renato dos Santos
about: Renato Monteiro dos Santos is one of the partners of BTG Pactual Holding, the holding company of BTG bank, with about 2/3 of its assets.
Banco BTG Pactual is a Brazilian investment bank and asset and wealth manager that was founded in 1983 and now has with more than 1 billion reais ($200 million) under management.
He began his career at BTG Pactual in 1997 as a trader and now serves as senior vice president of the bank, responsible for its Latin America Treasury Department.
dos Santos is a member of BTG's managers group -- the 'Top Seven Partners' -- together with fellow billionaire Roberto Balls.

name: Aneel Bhusri
about: Aneel Bhusri cofounded the business software firm Workday together with Dave Duffield, the founder of PeopleSoft.
Bhusri stepped down from his role as co-chief executive in 2024, taking on an advisory position.
Bhusri started his career in the early 1990s at business software firm PeopleSoft, where he rose to become vice chairman.
He's a former Intel board member and managing partner at venture capital firm Greylock Partners; he's been on the Forbes Midas List six times since 2008.
He studied electrical engineering at Brown University and has an MBA from Stanford.

forbes_list.list: The Midas List: Top Tech Investors (2017)

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Stanford Graduate School of Business; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Brown University

did_you_know_facts: Bhusri joined the Giving Pledge, a commitment by the world's wealthiest people to dedicate the majority of their wealth to philanthropy, in 2018.

name: Jaroslav Hascak & family
about: Jaroslav Hascak is cofounder of Penta Investments, which has investments in the healthcare, banking, real estate and aeronautical industries.
Penta, which he controls with Mark Dospiva, has controlling stakes in Privatbanka, pharmacy chain Dr. Max and sports betting operator Fortuna.
Hascak and Dospiva (a Czech national) were both studying in Beijing and got started by importing Chinese textiles to chain stores in then-Czechoslovakia.
During Slovakia's 1996 privatization, Penta gained control over the nation's biggest fund paying only 20 percent of its real market value.
A very hands-on manager, he has created very competitive culture within the company, called System Up or Out, designed to get rid of weak performers.
did_you_know_facts: Hascak spent one-tenth of his early earnings to buy his first car, a Fiat Uno; the rest he invested into the stock brokerage business.
Hascak typically works 12 hours a day, six days a week.

name: Koh Wee Meng
about: Hotelier and property magnate Koh Wee Meng controls Fragrance Group with interests extending to Australia and the U.K. He took the Singapore-listed company private in 2021.
Son of a jeweler and schoolteacher, Koh broke away from Aspial, his family's jewelry business, to start his own property venture in the 1990s.
He was once known as the Geylang King for Fragrance's beginnings in Singapore's red light district.
His younger sibling Koh Wee Seng runs Aspial and has his own property interests.
did_you_know_facts: In the early years, he named his hotels after precious stones, such as Ruby, Sapphire and Emerald, inspired by his days as a jeweler.
In 2017, Fragrance Group entered the U.K. hotel property market, where it has since made 12 acquisitions.
quote: Only buy and hold what you are able to afford.

name: Karl Scheufele III & family
about: Karl Scheufele III and his family control Swiss jewelry and watchmaker Chopard, one of the best-known luxury accessory lines in the world.
A goldsmith and watchmaker by training, the German-born Scheufele bought the Geneva-based company in 1963 and transformed it into a global brand.
More than 50 years later, Scheufele remains active in the company, though his children Karl-Friedrich and Caroline lead the business.
Chopard's jewelry is a regular on the red carpet, with 11 Oscar winners having won while wearing Chopard, including Kate Winslet and Julianne Moore.
did_you_know_facts: Scheufele was born in Pforzheim, Germany, nicknamed the "Golden City" due to its longstanding tradition in jewelry and watchmaking.
For five generations, his family has been naming sons Karl. His own son is Karl IV and his grandson is Karl V.
quote: When I visited the workshops in Geneva and saw the venerable Mr. Chopard at his workbench, I immediately saw that our companies would be a good fit. We talked for half an hour and then I knew that this was the right choice.

name: Jeremy Allaire
about: Jeremy Allaire is the cofounder and CEO of Circle, issuer of USDC, the second-largest stablecoin by market capitalization.
A serial entrepreneur, Allaire previously founded and took public two internet companies: Allaire Corp., which helped web developers build sites, and Brightcove, a pioneer in online video publishing.
He pivoted to crypto in 2012, driven by an interest in creating a more robust international monetary system after the 2008 financial crisis, and cofounded Circle with Sean Neville.
The company initially focused on bitcoin payments before launching USDC in 2018 in partnership with crypto exchange Coinbase.
He took Circle public in June 2025 in a high-profile IPO, the first ever for a stablecoin issuer.

name: Koo Kwang-mo
about: Koo Kwang-mo is the chairman and chief executive of LG, one of South Korea's top five conglomerates.
He inherited shares of his late father and former LG chairman Koo Bon-Moo after his death in 2018.
He is an adopted son of the former chairman, who lost his biological son in 1994; Kwang-mo was born as a nephew to Bon-Moo.
In 2018, at age 40, he became the youngest chairman of a major Korean conglomerate.
LG has diversified into AI, biotech and cleantech.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Rochester Institute of Technology

name: Kabir Mulchandani
about: Kabir Mulchandani is the owner of Dubai-based real estate firm FIVE Holdings, which owns luxury party hotels and resorts in the Middle East, Spain and Switzerland.
He founded the firm in 2011 and plans to take it public on the Dubai stock exchange in 2025.
Born and raised in Mumbai, India, Mulchandani worked for his family's consumer electronics business before moving to Dubai in the early 2000s and investing in real estate.
After Dubai's property market collapsed in 2008, Mulchandani was charged with fraud and embezzlement in 2009 and spent 140 days in jail before being cleared in 2010.
FIVE Holdings acquired Pacha Group, which owns hotels and nightclubs in Ibiza, Spain, for $330 million in November 2023.

name: Bruce Toll
about: Bruce Toll cofounded homebuilding giant Toll Brothers in 1967 with his late brother, Bob (d. 2022).
Toll is the son of a multimillionaire investor who lost it all in the 1929 stock market crash and supported his family through the Depression by delivering laundry.
He and his brother built their first home in Chester County, Pennsylvania, then built Toll Brothers into one of America's leading luxury builders.
They took the $11 billion (fiscal 2025 sales) company public in 1986. It builds in more than 60 markets across the United States.
His BET Investments owns, manages, develops and leases mid-rise office buildings, office parks, retail complexes, apartment buildings and industrial space across the U.S.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts, University of Miami

name: Vladislav Filev & family
about: Vladislav Filev is the founder of S7 Group, which owns S7 (Sibir) Airlines, the largest private airline in Russia.
Filev and his wife Natalia Filev successfully managed the business, turning a small airline into the country's largest private air carrier.
S7 Group also owns aircraft maintenance provider S7 Technics and cargo operator S7 Cargo, among other businesses related to the transportation industry.
In 2019 his wife Natalia died in a plane crash in Germany, leading his daughter, Tatyana, to become chief executive of the group.
Filev became chairman of Sibir Airlines 1997; the company rebranded as S7 Airlines in 2006.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Mozhaisky Military Space Academy

did_you_know_facts: Vladislav Filev was a military engineer in the Strategic Missile Forces of the Russian Federation.

name: Beda Diethelm
about: Beda Diethelm is Swiss hearing aid manufacturer Sonova's largest individual shareholder, with a 10% stake.
Diethelm joined what would become Sonova in 1965, receiving a chunk of equity from the former owner in 1980.
Sonova has sales of roughly $2.8 billion and is based in Stafa, Switzerland and has production facilities in Vietnam and China.
Born in the tiny village of Galgenen, Switzerland, Diethelm first dabbled in electronics as an apprentice for a radio and TV technician in Zurich.
By 1962, Diethelm had become the head of production and technical director of Bommer, a Zurich company that was a global supplier of hearing aids.

name: Marek Dospiva
about: Marek Dospiva is cofounder of Penta Investments, which has investments in the healthcare, banking, real estate and aeronautical industries.
Penta has controlling stakes in Privatbanka, pharmacy chain Dr. Max and sports betting operator Fortuna.
Dospiva and Slovak Jaroslav Hascak, who were both studying in Beijing, got started importing Chinese textiles to chain stores in Czechoslovakia.
During Slovakia's 1996 privatization, Penta gained control over the nation's biggest fund, paying only 20 percent of its real market value.
Dospiva and Hascak are still both partners and the largest shareholders of Penta Investments.
did_you_know_facts: Dospiva is developing an office building complex in Prague that was the last project of famous British architect Zaha Hadid, who died in 2016.
Dospiva, who speaks Chinese and likes sports car, is co-owner of Ferrari and Maserati dealerships in the Czech Republic.

name: Richard Saghian
about: Richard Saghian is the founder and CEO of fast fashion company Fashion Nova, which generates some $2 billion in annual sales.
The son of Iranian immigrants, Saghian started the company in 2006 after dropping out of college.
He offered hundreds of new clothing styles a week, promoted on Instagram by influencers and celebrities like Cardi B.
In 2018, Fashion Nova was the most Googled fashion brand, beating out the likes of Louis Vuitton, Versace and Gucci.
Saghian owns several properties in Los Angeles, including a sprawling hilltop estate in Bel Air that he purchased for $141 million.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Drop Out, California State University Northridge

did_you_know_facts: Three men attempted to rob Saghian outside his home in 2021. A confrontation with a security guard led to gunfire, resulting in one fatality. Saghian was uninjured.
In 2022, Fashion Nova agreed to pay $4.2 million to settle allegations by the FTC that it suppressed negative reviews online. Fashion Nova denies the allegations.

name: Jason Murray
about: Jason Murray is the cofounder, chairman and CEO of Utah-based PACS Group, a publicly traded firm that operates skilled nursing facilities.
He cofounded PACS Group with fellow billionaire Mark Hancock in 2013 and the pair took the company public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2024.
PACS Group started with two skilled nursing facilities and has since expanded to 315 facilities in 17 states in the U.S.
Murray and Hancock each owned 50% of PACS Group before the IPO; Murray now owns nearly 35% of the company's shares.
Before starting PACS, Murray worked as a healthcare executive and licensed nursing home administrator.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master, Weber State University; Bachelor of Arts, Weber State University

name: Ibrahim Al Muhaidib
about: Ibrahim Al-Muhaidib is the chairman of HDB Group, which owns several hotels and towers, most notably the heritage Tuwaiq Tower in Riyadh.
He is the founder of Safwat Al-Muhaidib Dental Company, which operates more than 70 branches across Saudi Arabia.
He holds a broad real estate portfolio comprising numerous properties and investments throughout different regions of Saudi Arabia.
He also briefly served as president of Saudi soccer team Al-Nassr in 2024.

name: Xu Shugen
about: Xu Shugen is the founder and chairman of Shanghai-listed Zhejiang Dingli Machinery.
Founded in 2005, Dingli manufactures industrial lifts.
Xu's brother, Xu Zhilong, is a board member.

name: Zhao Ding
about: Zhao Ding is the deputy chairman and deputy general manager of Chinese snacks retailer Busy Ming Group.
The company went public in Hong Kong in January 2026, raising $470 million.
It sells under the Busy for You and Super Ming brands, offering products such as small-packaged biscuits and nuts across a network of about 20,000 stores in China.
The group was formed in 2023, when Zhao's Super Ming merged with fellow snacks retailer Busy for You.
Busy for You's founder, Yan Zhou, is also a billionaire.

name: Alex Birkenstock
about: Alex Birkenstock is an heir to German footwear company Birkenstock, which traces its roots back to 1774.
The company began making its trademark sandals in the 1960s, under the leadership of Alex's father, Karl Birkenstock.
In 2002, Alex and his two brothers, Christian and Stephan, were given control of the company.
Stephan Birkenstock sold his stake to his two brothers in 2013 for an undisclosed amount.
In 2021, the brothers sold Birkenstock to L Catterton and Bernard Arnault's holding company for more than $4.5 billion. Christian rolled forward a stake then worth $300 million.

name: Mark Hancock
about: Mark Hancock is the cofounder and executive vice chairman of Utah-based PACS Group, a publicly traded firm that operates skilled nursing facilities.
He cofounded PACS Group with fellow billionaire Jason Murray in 2013 and the pair took the company public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2024.
PACS Group started with two skilled nursing facilities and has since expanded to 315 facilities in 17 states in the U.S.
Hancock and Murray each owned 50% of PACS Group before the IPO; Hancock now owns nearly 35% of the company's shares.
Before starting PACS, Hancock worked as an analyst at Ford, as a director at a steel company and as treasurer of a financial services firm.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Brigham Young University; Master of Business Administration, Brigham Young University

did_you_know_facts: In 2024, Hancock's private investment firm PV3 acquired Utah-based bicycle manufacturer ENVE Composites for $20 million.

name: Nicholas Pritzker
about: Nicholas (Nick) Pritzker is a cousin of the late Jay Pritzker and his brothers Donald and Robert, who built the Hyatt hotel chain.
Pritzker spent many years leading Hyatt's hotel development efforts, but he has since sold most of his Hyatt stock.
He has shifted his attention and investment dollars to causes like clean energy, marijuana legalization and criminal justice reform.
He is cofounder and chairman emeritus of Evergreen Climate Innovations, which invests in clean energy companies in the Midwest.
Pritzker invested early in the e-cigarette maker Juul, Uber and Tesla through his investment firm, Tao Capital.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctor of Jurisprudence, University of Chicago; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Lake Forest College

did_you_know_facts: In the 2016 election, Pritzker donated to Proposition 64, a ballot initiative in California which successfully legalized marijuana in the Golden State.

name: John Liew
about: John Liew is co-founder of AQR, a money management firm that trades through a systematic, data-driven approach.
The firm focuses on factor-based investing and held $187 billion of assets under management as of March 2026.
Based in Greenwich, Connecticut, AQR operates globally with offices from London to Sydney and Hong Kong.
Before cofounding AQR, Liew worked at Goldman Sachs as a portfolio manager, where he developed and managed quantitative trading strategies.
He created the Liew College Fellows Fund to finance undergraduates who have unpaid research opportunities with the University of Chicago's faculty.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of Chicago; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Chicago; Ph.D, University of Chicago

name: Heikki Herlin
about: Heikki Herlin, born 1990, is an heir to the Kone fortune in Finland.
He is the great-great-grandson of Harald Herlin, who invested in Kone Elevators in 1924.
Heikki Herlin inherited shares in several Scandinavian companies from his father Niklas, who died in 2016.
His most valuable holdings are stakes in Kone and Cargotec, a producer of machinery for heavy duty cargo ships.
His two uncles and aunt, Ilkka, Antti and Iona Herlin, are all billionaires.
did_you_know_facts: Like his father, Herlin is a journalist and writer. In 2020, he published a memoir about his father's life.
He is the second largest shareholder of Finnish publishing company Alma Media.

name: Simon Nixon
about: Simon Nixon earned the bulk of his fortune from his price-comparison website MoneySuperMarket.
He cofounded the company in 1993, took it public in 2007, and sold all his shares in it by 2016.
Nixon has invested in dozens of private companies, including--before they went public--Airbnb, Robinhood and Wise (formerly called Transferwise).
He also owns luxury homes around the globe, including in Malibu and Barbados, which he lists for private holiday rentals on his site, SimonEscapes.
did_you_know_facts: In 2013, Nixon moved from Chester, England, to tax haven Jersey, where he owns a multi-million dollar home.
Nixon studied accounting at Nottingham University before dropping out at the age of 20.

name: Djoko Susanto
about: Djoko Susanto is the founder of Alfamart, which has more than 22,000 convenience stores across Indonesia and 2,000 stores in the Philippines.
The sixth of 10 siblings, he started managing his parents' modest food stall inside a traditional market in Jakarta at age 17.
He later partnered with clove cigarette tycoon Putera Sampoerna to open similar stalls and then a discount supermarket chain.
When Putera sold his cigarette business to Philip Morris in 2005, Susanto bought the retail business and developed it into the Alfamart chain.
In 2022, the company bought a $30 million stake in Bank Aladin Syariah, which provides sharia-compliant financial services.
did_you_know_facts: Susanto's daughter Feny and sons, Budiyanto and Harryanto, hold senior positions at Alfamart.
His property division Alfaland operates Omega Hotel Management throughout Indonesia.
His Bunda Mulia University in Jakarta, founded in 2003, offers programs in everything from digital business to visual communication to informatics.

name: Andres Santo Domingo
about: Andres Santo Domingo inherited a part of his father Julio Mario's multibillion dollar stake in the beer giant SABMiller when he died in 2011.
The bulk of his fortune is now in Anheuser-Busch InBev, following its $100 billion acquisition of SABMiller in 2016.
Santo Domingo is of Colombian heritage but has grown up and lived in the United States for years. He graduated from Brown University in 2000.
He sits on the boards of Conservation International and the New York Public Library.
His brother, Alejandro, is a director at Anheuser-Busch InBev. His mother, Beatriz Davila de Santo Domingo, is also a billionaire.
did_you_know_facts: Santo Domingo cofounded the vinyl-loving, rock-oriented record label Kemado Records, now called the Kemado Media Group, in 2002.
His wife, Lauren, began her career at Vogue and remains a contributing editor. She founded Moda Operandi, an online retailer that sells fresh-off-the-runway designs.

name: Lin Xiucheng & family
about: After making a fortune in scrap steel during the 1990s, Lin Xiucheng shifted into the light-emitting diode (LED) business.
He injected his LED business into a Shanghai-listed firm in exchange for a majority stake and changed its name to Sanan Optoelectronics in 2008.
Lin shares majority ownership of his main holding company, Fujian Sanan Group, with son Lin Zhiqiang.

name: Manuel Villar
about: Manuel Villar is the chairman of property developer Vista Land & Lifescapes run by his son Manuel Paolo.

Villar's biggest asset is his stake in Villar Land Holdings (formerly Golden MV Holdings), a property developer which is building Villar City, a 3,500-hectare master-planned community south of Manila.
He also has five other listed entities including mall operator Vistamalls, property landlord VistaREIT, home improvement chain AllHome, supermarket chain AllDay Marts and Premiere Island Power REIT.
Villar is diversifying his business with new investments in free-to-air TV and plans to build a casino and a theme park in southern Metro Manila.
His son Mark and daughter Camille are senators in the Philippines.
did_you_know_facts: Villar has been involved in politics and held positions including congressman, speaker of the house of representatives, senator and senate president.
As a child, Villar helped his mother sell seafood in a Manila market.

name: Vasily Anisimov
about: Vasily Anisimov is a Russian-born billionaire who made his first fortune in non-ferrous metals trading.
Later he became a partner of billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Andrei Skoch, before selling out to move into real estate. He also has interests in African uranium mining.
Anisimov was a head of the Russian Judo Federation for 12 years, until October 2022; its first vice president is Putin's friend Arkady Rotenberg.
He renounced his Russian citizenship in 2022 and now holds a Croatian passport.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Alma-Ata Institute of National Economy

did_you_know_facts: The 2024 Oligarch-themed Romantic Comedy, "Anora", was filmed in Anisimov's former mansion in Brooklyn, NY.

name: Mao Geping & family
about: Mao Geping is chairman of his eponymous company Mao Geping Cosmetics, based in Hangzhou, China.
He took the company public in Hong Kong in 2024, raising over $300 million in the IPO.
The cosmetics brand competes with international labels in China's premium market, offering products such as $50 foundations and $30 eye shadow palettes.
Mao initially studied Chinese opera performance but later went into cosmetics. He set up his own brand in 2000.
The mogul's wife, Wang Liqun, is the company's vice chairman. His two sisters are both directors.

name: Liu Weiping
about: Liu Weiping chairs snack food maker WL Delicious.
WL is headquartered in the central Chinese city of Luohe.
Liu is a graduate of Southwest University in Chongqing, China, where he was majored in management.

name: Zhao Lixin
about: Zhao Lixin is the CEO of semiconductor supplier GalaxyCore.
GalaxyCore went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2021.
GalaxyCore's customers include Oppo, Xiaomi, Samsung and Lenovo.
GalaxyCore was founded in 2003.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Tsinghua University

name: Ren Jinsheng & family
about: Ren is the founder and chairman of Simcere Pharmaceutical Group, a pharmaceuticals supplier. .
Simcere has research development centers in Nanjing, Shanghai and Boston.
Ren holds an undergraduate degree in traditional Chinese pharmacology from the Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine.
He also holds a master's degree in business administration from the Nanjing Normal University.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Nanjing Normal University; Diploma, Nanjing University of Chinese Medicine

name: Kishore Jain
about: Kishore Jain owns and runs Chennai-based Khazana Jewellery, which sells gold and diamond jewellery.
Khazana, which means treasure in Sanskrit, has more than 50 stores across India and two stores in Sharjah.
Jain took over the wholesale jewelry business founded by his late father, Bhoormal Sehsmalji, and set up his first retail store in Nellore, a city in the southern state of Andhra Pradesh in 1976.
He shifted base to Chennai city in 1989.
did_you_know_facts: His father founded the business as Jewellery House in Nellore in 1954.
His ancestors hail from a village in Rajasthan.

name: Leonie Baldock
about: Leonie Baldock sold her stake in the Rhodes Ridge iron ore project to Japanese trading and investment company Mitsui In February 2025.
Her sister Alexandra Burt and aunt Angela Bennett also had stakes in the same project and are billionaires.
Her grandfather Peter Wright established a mining partnership with mining magnate Gina Rinehart's father Lang Hancock in the 1950s.
Part of her wealth comes from a stake in Wright Prospecting, a privately owned mining firm based in Perth.
The sisters are embroiled in legal battles with other family members and with mining billionaire Gina Rinehart over royalties from other mines.

name: Archie Hwang
about: Archie Hwang founded HMI, formerly known as Hermes Microvision, in 1977, which specializes in optoelectronic devices, used in semiconductor manufacturing.
He sold the company to ASML of the Netherlands for $3.1 billion in 2016.
Hermes-Epitek, the parent company of HMI, has offices in mainland China, Malaysia, Singapore and Taiwan.
Hwang, who also goes by the name Hwang Min Qi, is the chairman of the group.
Heron Neutron Medical, a group subsidiary that has independently developed the boron neutron capture therapy cancer treatment system, went public on Taiwan's Emerging Stock Board in 2024.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, National Chiao Tung University

did_you_know_facts: In 2024, he gifted cancer care equipment worth $37 million, developed by Heron Neutron, to his alma mater, the National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University.

name: Athanasios Martinos & family
about: Athanasios Martinos is the owner of Greek shipping firm Eastern Mediterranean Maritime, which has a fleet of 75 tankers, bulk carriers and container vessels.
He founded the company in 1990, after splitting from the family shipping company Thenamaris, which he had cofounded with his mother and two brothers in 1972.
Collectively, Athanasios and his brothers Andreas and Constantinos own the largest shipping fleet in Greece, the largest shipowning nation in the world.
He also owns a Cyprus-based real estate investment firm which holds office and retail properties in London and Geneva.
He served as the civil administrator of the monastic community of Mount Athos, an autonomous region run by Orthodox monks in Greece, from 2019 to 2023.

name: Wilma Tisch
about: Wilma Tisch owes her fortune to her late husband Laurence (d. 2003) and his brother Bob, who started Loews Corp as a New Jersey hotel venture in 1946.
Wilma's son James is the president and CEO of publicly traded Loews, which now has interests in drilling, natural gas pipelines and insurance.
Her sister-in law Joan Tisch, also a billionaire, died in 2017; Wilma's son Andrew co-chairs Loews' board with Joan's son Jonathan.
At NYU, the Tisch family donated funds to support the Tisch School of the Arts and the Tisch Hospital at Langone Medical Center.
Wilma donates some of her Loews shares annually to her three children's charitable foundations.
did_you_know_facts: Tisch was the first woman to be elected president of the Federation of Jewish Philanthropies of New York.
Tisch is an honorary board member of WNYC Radio and holds an honorary doctorate from NYU.

name: Joseph Bae
about: Joseph Bae is co-CEO of storied private equity giant KKR, which has about $638 billion in assets under management.
He was appointed to the top job alongside Scott Nuttall after KKR cofounders Henry Kravis and George Roberts stepped down in October 2021.
Bae started his career at Goldman Sachs and joined KKR in 1996.
He led KKR's expansion into Asia and served on all its private market investment committees.
He cofounded The Asian American Foundation to build safety and inclusivity among AAPIs.
did_you_know_facts: Bae and his co-CEO Scott Nuttall began as KKR analysts together when they were 24.

name: John Bloor
about: John Bloor is one of the largest builders in the UK through his Bloor Homes and also owns Triumph Motorcycles, the iconic bike manufacturer.
He reportedly left school at age 15 and began an apprenticeship as a plasterer, then built his first house before turning 20.
Now the privately-held Bloor Homes puts up more than 3,500 homes every year.
In 1983 he bought the manufacturing rights for Triumph motorcycles.
He and son Nick have revamped the brand, which was made famous by riders like Marlon Brando, James Dean and Steve McQueen.

name: Bill Austin
about: Bill Austin owns Starkey Hearing Technologies, the largest hearing aid manufacturer in the U.S.
He bought a hearing aid parts shop, which was then called Starkey Labs, for $13,000 in 1970.
Austin fired several top executives of Starkey Hearing in 2015, a tumultuous time for the company.
That move unleashed a series of events that resulted in the former company president being found guilty of federal fraud charges in 2018.
Austin spends much of his time traveling to developing countries for his Starkey Hearing Foundation, distributing hearing aids.
did_you_know_facts: Starkey's customers have reportedly included five U.S. presidents, two popes and singer Dolly Parton.
The Starkey Hearing Foundation says it has donated over 1.5 million hearing aids around the world.

name: Mustafa Kucuk
about: Mustafa Kucuk is the biggest shareholder of LC Waikiki, a producer and retailer of ready-to-wear fashions and home items.
Designer Georges Amouyal and a partner founded LC Waikiki in France in 1985. Kucuk and partners including Sefik Yilmaz Dizdar acquired it in 1997.
LC Waikiki's first international store opened in Romania in 2009. In 2016, it expanded into home textile products under the brand name LCW Home.
The company prides itself on promoting women into its management ranks.
Today, LC Waikiki has over 1,000 locations in 47 countries; roughly half are outside of Turkey. Its motto: "Everyone deserves to dress well."
did_you_know_facts: The brand combines the name of the famous Hawaiian beach with "LC," as in "Les Copains" ("friends" in French).
Mustafa Kucuk avoids the media. His older brother, Vahap Kucuk, is the public face of the company, which pulls in revenue of around $2.5 billion annually.

name: Walter Wang
about: Walter Wang is chairman and CEO of JM Eagle Inc., one of the world's largest manufacturers of plastic pipe.
Wang is a son of Y.C. Wang, the former chairman of Taiwan's Formosa Plastics, who died in 2008 at age 91.
Headquartered in Los Angeles, JM Eagle has 2,000 employees globally and generates $2.3 billion of estimated annual revenue.
Wang's philanthropic interests include healthcare, education and missionary work.
Wang is the founder and owner of a Taiwanese basketball team, the New Taipei Kings. His daughter named the team after the family name Wang, which means king in Mandarin.
did_you_know_facts: Wang survived a battle with nasopharynx cancer in 2005, which he credits to his Christian faith.

name: Ishay Davidi
about: Ishay Davidi is the Chairman, CEO, and founder of FIMI Opportunity Funds, Israel's first and largest private equity firm in terms of assets under management.
Since 1996, FIMI has raised seven private equity funds (three of which are currently active), with over $4.3 billion in capital commitments.
It has also completed 108 investments and 76 exits, generating over $9 billion in transaction value.
FIMI specializes in acquiring and scaling mature Israeli and Israel-related companies across diverse sectors, including automotive, electronics, aviation, energy, and logistics.

name: Nihat Ozdemir
about: Nihat Ozdemir and his billionaire partner, Sezai Bacaksiz, met as students at Gazi University and founded Limak Construction in 1976.
Besides being contractor for some of the world's largest infrastructure projects, Limak has operations in energy, tourism, transportation and cement.
It's part of a consortium building Istanbul's new airport. When all phases are complete, it will be the world's largest based on passenger capacity.
Limak is a major builder and operator of hydroelectric power plants, ranking among Turkey's top ten electricity producers.
Besides Turkey, Limak operates in Kuwait, Egypt, Kosovo, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Eastern Europe, Africa, Pakistan, Ukraine and Russia.
did_you_know_facts: As an academic at what is now Gazi University, Ozdemir was for a short while assistant to Necmettin Erbakan, who went on to become minister of Turkey.
The future billionaire was on the faculty of the Engineering and Architecture department for four years, until 1980.

name: Sezai Bacaksiz
about: Sezai Bacaksiz and his billionaire partner, Nihat Ozdemir, met as students at Gazi University and founded Limak Construction in 1976.
Besides being contractor for some of the world's largest infrastructure projects, Limak has operations in energy, tourism, transportation and cement.
It's part of a consortium building Istanbul's new airport. When all phases are complete, it will be the world's largest based on passenger capacity.
Limak is a major builder and operator of hydroelectric power plants, ranking among Turkey's top ten electricity producers.
Besides Turkey, Limak operates in Kuwait, Egypt, Kosovo, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Eastern Europe, Africa, Pakistan, Ukraine and Russia.
did_you_know_facts: In partnership with Punj Lloyd, Limak built the Trans-Anatolian Natural Gas Pipeline, which transports natural gas produced in the Caspian Sea to Turkey and Europe.

name: Manuel Arango Arias
about: Manuel Arango and his brothers, Jeronimo (d. 2020) and Placido (d. 2020) are credited for building one of Mexico's first major retailers and helping establish Walmart's presence in the country.
In 1958, as sales of their father's clothing factory dwindled, the trio founded the bargain retail chain Central de Ropa, later renamed Grupo Cifra.
The company owned the Bodega Aurrera stores, selling everything from groceries to home appliances.
The Arango's took the company public on the Mexican Stock Exchange in 1977. Fourteen years later, they embarked on a 50/50 partnership with Walmart to expand across Mexico.
In 1997, Walmart bought a majority stake in Grupo Cifra for $1.8 billion and took over Walmex (Walmart de Mexico).
did_you_know_facts: Arango won two Oscars in 1971 for producing "Sentinels of Silence," a documentary short about ancient Mexican civilizations.

name: Michael Heine
about: Michael Heine started Netwealth in 1999 with his brother Leslie.
Michael worked with his father Walter in international financing, mortgage lending and property development, then started a fund management business in 1982.
He sold that business and launched Netwealth Group. It went public in 2017 and now has A$100 billion in funds under management.
Netwealth provides products and services to financial advisers and individuals.
Heine resigned as co-managing director of Netwealth in 2022 but remains a director. His son, Matt, is managing director and CEO.
did_you_know_facts: Michael's father, Walter, built a steel-trading business, Heine Bros., after fleeing Nazi Germany. It expanded into property and mortgage lending.

name: Robin Khuda
about: Robin Khuda is founder and CEO of AirTrunk, a leading data centre provider across the Asia- Pacific and the Middle East.
He founded AirTrunk in 2015. Since then it has established data centres in Australia, Hong Kong, Japan, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, and Singapore.
AirTrunk was acquired in 2024 in a $16 billion transaction by a consortium led by global asset manager Blackstone and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board. Khuda retains a small but valuable stake.
Before founding AirTrunk he held leadership roles at tech companies such as PIPE Networks, Fujitsu and SingTel Optus.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Business Administration, University of Technology Sydney; Master of Business Administration, University of Manchester

did_you_know_facts: Khuda founded Ondas, a luxury property developer. It has upscale projects in Sydney and Melbourne.
In 2025, he donated A$100 million ($66 million) to the University of Sydney to fund a 20-year STEM program for female students.
He has an MBA degree from the University of Manchester in the U.K.

name: Per Sandberg
about: Per Sandberg is a major shareholder in pharmaceutical company Camurus, which develops treatment for opiod dependency.
He inherited the stakes from his father, entrepreneur Gunnar Sandberg.
He is also the sole owner of Aimpoint ? the world leader in red dot sights for hunting, sport shooting, and military use.
Sandberg Development is his family-owned investment company, focusing on water technology, quality of life, and security.
Per Sandberg has three siblings, all of whom have been bought out of Sandberg Development. He now owns the company together with his three sons.

name: Gao Jifan & family
about: Gao Jifan is founder, chairman and CEO of Trina Solar, a Changzhou-based company specializing in solar panels.
Trina Solar, which supplies PV modules and smart energy solutions, listed on the New York Stock Exchange in 2006 before privatizing in 2017.
The company has manufacturing sites across China as well as in Vietnam and Thailand.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Jilin University; Bachelor of Science, Nanjing University

did_you_know_facts: Gao holds bachelor degree in chemistry from Nanjing University and a master degree from Jilin University.

name: Anthony Casalena
about: Anthony Casalena founded website building startup Squarespace in his University of Maryland dorm room in 2003.
Casalena founded Squarespace with a $30,000 loan from his parents.
Squarespace sells monthly or annual plans that range from a simple domain name and website to more advanced options for e-commerce.
He took Squarespace public in 2021, then took it private in October 2024 alongside UK private equity firm Permira.
Casalena owns more than 20% of Squarespace and remains CEO.

name: Wong Man Li
about: Wong Man Li is the chairman and CEO of Man Wah Holdings, one of the world's largest suppliers of recliner sofas best known for its high-end Cheers brand.
It also manufactures and sells mattresses.
In 2005, Man Wah went public in Singapore and became the first Chinese furniture enterprise on the Main Board of the Singapore Stock Exchange.
After delisting in 2009, the company re-listed in Hong Kong the following year.
did_you_know_facts: He got his start earning $4 a day as a factory worker after arriving in Hong Kong from the mainland's Fujian Province in 1990.
Before a recliner goes into production at Man Wah, it is tested by a machine that pokes it for the equivalent of 72 years of use to see if it stays firm.

name: Guillermo Rauch
about: Guillermo Rauch cofounded Vercel, which creates developer tools for hosting and deploying websites.
In September 2025, the company raised $300 million, co-led by venture firm Accel and GIC, one of Singapore's sovereign wealth funds, putting Vercel's valuation at $9 billion.
Rauch, an Argentine immigrant to the U.S., became famous in the developer community as a teen, after becoming a core contributor to MooTools, a popular Javascript library.
Vercel has become a crucial infrastructure vendor for some of the world's biggest brands, including Under Armour, Stripe and Sonos.
did_you_know_facts: One of the most popular ways to view the Epstein Files, an interface called Jmail that mimics a Gmail inbox, is hosted on Vercel.

name: Denis Yarats
about: Denis Yarats is the chief technology officer and cofounder of AI search startup Perplexity, which hit a $20 billion valuation in 2025.
Perplexity uses a mix of AI models to summarize information from different websites and provides footnote-style citations to the source.
The startup is backed by investors including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, AI pioneer Yann LeCun and Google's chief scientist Jeff Dean.
Originally from Belarus, Yarats cofounded Perplexity in August 2022 with Aravind Srinivas, Andy Konwinski and Johnny Ho.
Before starting Perplexity, Yarats was a research scientist at Meta's Facebook AI Research (FAIR) lab and helped create search engine Bing at Microsoft.

name: Andy Konwinski
about: Andy Konwinski is a cofounder of AI search startup Perplexity and Databricks, a platform that helps build and analyze datasets.
Perplexity hit a $20 billion valuation in 2025 and Databricks was valued at $134 billion in 2026.
Originally from rural Ohio, Konwinski cofounded Databricks in 2013 and later cofounded Perplexity in August 2022 with Aravind Srinivas, Denis Yarats and Johnny Ho.
He no longer holds active positions at Databricks or Perplexity.
In 2024, he launched Laude Ventures to back early stage tech startups. It started with a $150 million fund.
In 2025, he started the nonprofit Laude Institute with $100 million of his own money to back moonshot research ideas on fundamental human problems.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Ph.D, University of California, Berkeley; Bachelor of Science, University of Wisconsin, Madison

name: Johnny Ho
about: Johnny Ho is the cofounder and chief strategy officer of Perplexity, which hit a $20 billion valuation in 2025.
Perplexity uses a mix of AI models to summarize information from different websites and provides footnote-style citations to the source.
The startup is backed by investors including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, AI pioneer Yann LeCun and Google's chief scientist Jeff Dean.
He cofounded Perplexity in August 2022 with Aravind Srinivas, Andy Konwinski and Denis Yarats.
A former competitive programmer, Ho is a three-time gold medalist at the International Olympiad.

name: Aravind Srinivas
about: Aravind Srinivas is the CEO and cofounder of AI search startup Perplexity, which hit a $20 billion valuation in 2025.
Perplexity uses a mix of AI models to summarize information from different websites and provides footnote-style citations to the source.
The startup is backed by investors including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, AI pioneer Yann LeCun and Google's chief scientist Jeff Dean.
Originally from Chennai, India, Srinivas cofounded Perplexity in August 2022 with Andy Konwinski, Denis Yarats and Johnny Ho.
Before starting Perplexity in 2022, he worked as a researcher at companies like OpenAI and Google DeepMind.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Technology, Indian Institute of Technology Madras; Ph.D, University of California, Berkeley; Masters of Science in Technology, Indian Institute of Technology Madras

name: Farris Wilks
about: Farris and his brother Dan got a combined $3.5 billion (pretax) in 2011 selling their fracking company to a group led by Singapore-based firm Temasek.
The brothers have acquired more than 672,000 acres of land in six different states across the West, becoming America's 12th-largest landowners.
The brothers began their careers as stone masons, like their father, founding Wilks Masonry in 1995.
In 2002 they went into fracking, launching Frac Tech and growing it into an oil and natural gas giant before cashing out less than a decade later.
The brothers are also investing in oil and gas businesses, including fracking company U.S. Well Services and data provider Dawson Geophysical Company.
did_you_know_facts: Farris Wilks is the pastor of his own church, the Assembly of Yahweh Seventh Day Church, near Cisco, Texas.
Farris Wilks and his brother are active Republican donors.

name: Jane Lauder
about: Jane Lauder, granddaughter of cosmetics legend Estée Lauder, is a former executive vice president and chief data officer at her family's company.
Lauder joined Estée Lauder in 1996, a year after graduating from Stanford University. She previously managed the company's Clinique and Origins brands.
Estée Lauder, which her grandmother cofounded in 1946, now has over 20 brands and revenues of $14 billion.
Jane stepped down as an executive vice president at Estée Lauder in 2024. She has served on its board of directors since 2009.
In 2018, she joined the board of Eventbrite, the ticketing and event technology company.
did_you_know_facts: Lauder's husband, Kevin Warsh, also a Stanford grad, was the youngest-ever appointee to the Federal Reserve Board.

name: Paul Saville
about: Paul Saville leads Virginia-based NVR, one of the largest homebuilders in the United States, with $10.3 billion in annual revenue.
Saville joined Ryan Homes, now a subsidiary of NVR, in 1981. He became president and CEO in 2005 and was promoted to executive chairman in 2022, taking over for Dwight Schar.
NVR builds homes in 16 states, primarily in the Mid-Atlantic and Midwest.
In 2020, Saville and his wife, Linda, donated $20 million to open a new cancer screening and prevention center in Falls Church, Virginia.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, The University of Pittsburgh; Bachelor of Arts/Science, The College of William & Mary

did_you_know_facts: In 2017, Paul and Linda Saville sold their Palm Beach home to hedge fund billionaire Ken Griffin for $85 million.
The Savilles' current residence sits on land previously owned by Donald Trump and Russian oligarch Dmitry Rybolovlev.

name: Manuel Lao Hernández & family
about: Manuel Lao Hernandez founded Cirsa, a multinational casino company. He sold it to Blackstone for an estimated $2.6 billion (including debt) in 2018.
He started the business in 1978 and expanded it to nine countries in Latin America and Europe. He still owns Cirsa's Argentina operations.
His three children all worked for the family business, which was based just outside of Barcelona.
Today, through his Nortia investment firm, Lao Hernandez has interests in infrastructure, real estate and leisure and entertainment.
did_you_know_facts: As a hobby, Lao Hernandez grows bonsai trees.
He has a foundation named after him that has organized a poker tournament in which people with disabilities compete to have a wish fulfilled.

name: Mohammed Dewji
about: Mohammed Dewji is the CEO of METL, a Tanzanian conglomerate founded by his father in the 1970s.
METL is active in textile manufacturing, flour milling, beverages and edible oils in eastern, southern and central Africa.
In additional to Tanzania, METL operates in 10 African countries including Uganda, Ethiopia and Kenya.
Dewji, Tanzania's only billionaire, signed the Giving Pledge in 2016, promising to donate at least half his fortune to philanthropic causes.
Dewji was reportedly kidnapped at gunpoint in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania in October 2018 and released after nine days.
did_you_know_facts: Dewji retired from Tanzania's parliament in early 2015 after completing two terms.
Dewji, who is known as Mo (short for Mohammed), launched Mo Cola several years ago to compete with Coca Cola.

name: B. Wayne Hughes Jr
about: B. Wayne Hughes Jr. was born into the self-storage business; his father, B. Wayne Hughes (d. 2021), cofounded Public Storage in 1972.
Hughes Jr. worked at Public Storage for almost two decades, starting in 1983.
He was vice president of acquisitions from 1992 to 2002 and served on the board until late 2020.
In 2005 he launched American Commercial Equities, a real estate company that acquires and manages properties in Hawaii and California.
His Hughes Charitable Foundation focuses on issues such as education, at-risk youth and food and housing insecurity in his home state of Wyoming.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Southern California

did_you_know_facts: Hughes Jr. is the founder of Serving USA, a nonprofit that helps military families, victims of crime and former inmates rebuild their lives.
Hughes Jr.'s sister, Tamara Hughes Gustavson, is also a billionaire.

name: Larry Connor
about: Larry Connor is a real estate investor in Dayton, Ohio who founded and leads the Connor Group, which invests in luxury apartment buildings across the U.S.
The Connor Group currently owns and operates a $5 billion portfolio of 51 apartment buildings across 12 states from Colorado to Florida. The firm keeps properties for 5 and a half years on average.
Connor founded the firm in 1991 with two partners, which he later bought out in 2003. The firm's annual rate of return is 30.4% and it has sold more than $6 billion worth of properties since 1995.
He traveled to the Mariana Trench, the deepest point on Earth, on a research voyage in 2021 and took part in Axiom Space's Ax-1 mission to the International Space Station in 2022.
In 2024 he opened the Greater Dayton School, Ohio's first private non-religious elementary school dedicated to under-resourced students.
did_you_know_facts: In September 2023, he broke the world record for the highest HALO formation skydive at 38,139 feet alongside a team of four U.S. Air Force pararescue specialists.
His first jobs included painting houses, selling "damaged label" wines to college students and picking up dead bodies for $5 apiece to bring to a local funeral home.

name: Ruslan Rahimkulov
about: Ruslan Rahimkulov and his older brother, Timur, became billionaires after inheriting the fortune from their father, Megdet, who led the Hungarian office of Russian gas giant Gazprom in the early 1990s.
Megdet Rahimkulov became CEO and co-owner of a joint venture between Gazprom and Hungary's oil and gas concern MOL in the mid 1990s.
The elder Rahimkulov also headed AEB, a Hungarian bank that Gazprom bought to process payments from its local customers that he later bought from Gazprom.
At the same time, he started began buying shares of MOL and OTP, Hungary's largest bank.
The brothers, both of whom live in Hungary, inherited the wealth in 2020 and began diversifying into other assets, including real estate.
did_you_know_facts: Megdet Rahimkulov was the richest person in Hungary before his return to Russia in 2008.

name: Solomon Lew
about: Solomon Lew chairs Melbourne-based Premier Investments, an apparel retailer.
The company is the largest shareholder in Australian department store Myer and home appliance maker Breville.
Premier's brands also include the Smiggle stationery store franchise aimed at children, and sleepwear label Peter Alexander.
In 2025, Myer bought Premier's five apparel brands in exchange for new shares issued to Premier. This will create one of the largest retail and apparel companies across Australia and New Zealand.
Following five apparel brands acquisition, Lew will join the board of Myer in April 2026.
did_you_know_facts: Lew says he always had an entrepreneurial mindset, working in retail after school and during holidays before opening his first apparel business on his 18th birthday.
He was the first Australian to enter the World Retail Hall of Fame, in 2016, when he was inducted along with Jo Malone and Tommy Hilfiger.

name: Rubens Menin Teixeira de Souza
about: Rubens Menin founded MRV Engenharia in 1979, and turned it into Brazil's leading home builder; it trades on the Sao Paulo exchange.
The company started in his home state of Minas Gerais and eventually spread to Brazil's southern states.
He is also the founder of Banco Inter, a Brazilian bank that went public in 2018.
In January 2019, Menin announced the launch of CNN Brasil, a licensed brand, which began operations in late 2019.
A sports fan, Menin sponsors F1 racer Bruno Senna and years ago launched his own tennis tournament in Brazil.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais

name: Thomas Powell
about: Thomas Powell is the former chairman and CEO of Houston-based electrical engineering and manufacturing company Powell Industries.
His father, William E. Powell, founded the company in 1947 as a metal-working shop.
Thomas Powell started working at the company in 1964 and was named chairman and CEO in 1984.
He served three terms as CEO before retiring from the top job for good in 2016.
He retired as a chairman in 2019 and as a director in 2022. He still owns 19% of the Nasdaq-listed company.

name: Ruan Shuilong & family
