The original business, Dr. August Oetker, began in 1891 when his great-grandfather started selling non-perishable baking powder.
In September of 2024, he and his brother Carl Ferdinand bought out their sister Julia from Geschwister Oetker, assuming full control over the company.
When Alfred's father, Rudolf August, passed away in 2007, ownership of Dr. August Oetker was divided among his eight children from three marriages.
did_you_know_facts: Alfred has two sons with his wife, Princess Elvira Grimaldi, whose family is the Sicilian branch of the Grimaldis of Genoa and Monaco.
Alfred studied economics at the University of Passau and Oxford, and speaks six languages.

name: Alfons Doblinger
about: Alfons Doblinger is the founder and controlling shareholder of German real estate developer, Doblinger Gruppe.
Doblinger started the Munich-based business in 1962 at age 17.
The group, which designs, builds and manages properties, has more than 600 employees and annual revenue of about 600 million euros.

name: Li Rucheng
about: Li Rucheng chairs China's Youngor Group, which has branched out from garments into real estate and finance.
Li was assigned to work in a collective factory in Ningbo, the precursor to Youngor, in 1980; and became its factory chief in 1982.
Younger employs more than 50,000 people.

name: Monica Crippa
about: Monica Crippa is the daughter of Giuseppe Crippa (d. 2025), the late founder of Technoprobe, an Italian manufacturer of probe cards, small devices that test the functionality of microchips.
Her father founded Technoprobe in 1989 in his garage and attic alongside his son Cristiano, while still working at semiconductor firm ST.
Technoprobe went public on Euronext Milan in 2022; Monica owns a 12% stake.
Monica served on Technoprobe's board until stepping down for personal reasons in 2022.

name: P.V. Krishna Reddy
about: P.V. Krishna Reddy is the managing director of privately held Megha Engineering and Infrastructure.
He cofounded it with his uncle, P.P. Reddy, in 1989 to build small pipes for municipalities.
Megha soon expanded into building infrastructure projects such as dams, natural gas distribution networks, power plants and roads.
Megha also has projects overseas in Zambia, Tanzania, Bangladesh and Kuwait.

name: Gary Fegel
about: Gary Fegel ran the aluminum business for Glencore and left the commodities giant in 2013, when he begab building a diversified investment portfolio.
Through his family office GMF Capital, Fegel invests across public and private equity, including companies in media and technology, as well as real estate.
Fegel sold his real estate asset management firm, GMF RE, in 2022.
Fegel's recent deals include the merger of his SPAC with FlyExclusive, a U.S. aviation company, and the purchase of The Motorsport Network, a global media and technology company.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of St. Gallen

did_you_know_facts: GMF, the name of Fegel's business, stands for Gary Mischa Fegel.
He and his wife Yael, a lawyer from Britain, have been listed in ARTnet's list of the world's Top 200 collectors.

name: Zhong Ruonong & family
about: Zhong Ruonong chairs Shenzhen-ilsted Zhuzhou Hongda Electronics.
Zhuzhou Hongda Electronics makes electronic components including capacitors, inductors and resistors.
Husband Zeng Jijiang is general manager of the listed company.

name: Carmen Daurella Aguilera
about: Carmen Daurella owns nearly 4% of bottling company Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, the largest independent Coke bottler by revenue.
CCEP was formed in 2016 as a merger of Coke bottling companies from Spain, Germany and Coca-Cola Enterprises.
The company which is listed in London and New York, saw $22 billion in annual revenue in 2024; its brands also include Sprite, Fanta and Monster.
Coca-Cola partnered with the Daurella family of Spain in the early 1950s to create its first bottling plant in Barcelona.
Her cousin Sol Daurella, also a billionaire, is chair of CCEP.

name: Guilherme Benchimol
about: Guilherme Benchimol is the founder of XP Inc., a Brazilian financial services firm that went public in December 2019 in the U.S.
XP Inc. has grown popular by focusing its products and services on clients with little investing experience.
Benchimol founded XP in 2001 after being fired from a brokerage firm in southern Brazil, with initial capital of approximately $2,000.
Through the XP Institute, Benchimol aims to offer free education to 50 million Brazilians over the next 10 years.
In 2021, he stepped down from his position as the CEO of XP Inc.; he remains its chairman.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Economics, Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro

name: Raamdeo Agrawal
about: Raamdeo Agrawal cofounded Motilal Oswal Financial Services as a small securities firm with his pal Motilal Oswal in 1987.
The company now offers a range of services including investment banking and mutual funds.
Agrawal grew up in a village in Chattisgarh in central India and came to Mumbai for his accountancy studies.
In 2023, Agrawal made a pledge to donate 5% of his stake in Motilal Oswal to philanthropic causes, such as education, health and rural upliftment.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Chartered Accountant, Institute of Chartered Accountants of India; B.Com, University of Mumbai

did_you_know_facts: Agrawal and Oswal lived in the same hostel in Mumbai while studying accountancy but became friends much later.
An ardent Warren Buffet fan, he has been attending Berkshire Hathaway's annual general meetings since 1995.

name: Max Levchin
about: Levchin is cofounder and CEO of Affirm Holdings, a fintech lending company that helps people pay for items like cameras and dresses in installments.
Before Affirm launched in 2014, Levchin cofounded PayPal, gaming company Slide and fertility-tracking app Glow.
Levchin owns more than 8% of Affirm, which went public on the Nasdaq in January 2021.
In 1991, Levchin and his family emigrated from Ukraine to Chicago as Jewish refugees; they arrived with just $700.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, University of Illinois Urbana Champaign

name: Bianca Rinehart
about: Bianca Rinehart is the eldest daughter of Australian mining magnate Gina Rinehart and is a trustee of the Hope Margaret Hancock Trust.
She replaced her mother as trustee in 2015, after a lengthy court battle.
The trust owns nearly a quarter of Gina Rinehart's Hancock Prospecting, on behalf of her four children.
She has a degree in hospitality and hotel management from Flinders University in Adelaide.
Hancock disclosed that as of September 2023 it had provided A$5.44 billion for dividends that will be paid after the dispute between Bianca and her brother John against their mother is resolved.
did_you_know_facts: She worked briefly at global miner Rio Tinto. Her job included driving a huge haul truck.
She slept with a hammer under her mattress after her grandfather, Lang Hancock, married his housekeeper, generating huge publicity.
quote: I am pleased that as a result of this judgment, the trust he [grandfather Lang Hancock] set up will now be able to be managed in the best interests of its beneficiaries: my sisters, my brother and myself.

name: Hope Welker
about: Hope Welker is the third child of Australian mining billionaire Gina Rinehart.
Together with her three siblings, she is the beneficiary of a trust that owns a large stake in mining giant Hancock Prospecting.
She joined, then withdrew, from a court battle waged by her siblings to remove their mother as trustee.
Hancock disclosed that as of September 2023 it had provided A$5.44 billion for dividends that will be paid after the dispute between Bianca and her brother John against their mother is resolved.
did_you_know_facts: In 2011, she told her mother she was down to her last $60,000.
She went to boarding school at Switzerland's famous Insitut Le Rosey.
quote: I don't think you [Gina Rinehart] understand what it means now that the whole world thinks you're going to be wealthier than Bill Gates.

name: Tom Persson
about: Tom Persson is third generation of the family that made its fortune from global cheap chic retailer H&M.
His grandfather, Erling Persson, founded the chain in 1947.
Brother Karl-Johan is set to be appointed chairman at the annual shareholders meeting in 2020.
Tom's father, brother, sister Charlotte S'derstr?m, and aunt Lottie Tham are all billionaires.
He lives in Stockholm and works in movie production.
did_you_know_facts: Persson is a graduate of the Met Film School in London.
Persson's film company produced the award-winning Swedish movie Ravens (2017). Tom is credited as a producer.

name: Geoffrey Palmer
about: Geoffrey Palmer is one of the largest apartment developers in Los Angeles, with more than 13,000 units in the greater L.A. metro area.
Palmer got his start developing residential projects in Los Angeles in the 1970s before starting his own firm, G.H. Palmer Associates, in 1978.
His first projects were condos in the Santa Clarita valley in north Los Angeles county; he built his first apartment complex in Santa Clarita in 1985.
Palmer is a major financial backer of former president Donald Trump, donating nearly $20 million to his campaigns and PACs from 2016 to 2024.
Palmer gained notoriety for his lawsuits against the city of L.A., most famously by successfully suing to block its affordable housing policy in 2009.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Economics, University of Colorado at Boulder; Doctor of Jurisprudence, Pepperdine Caruso School of Law

did_you_know_facts: Palmer has spent millions of dollars to defeat rent control ballot initiatives in California in 2018 and 2020, plus a failed attempt to recall Gov. Gavin Newsom.
Palmer is a competitive polo player in France.
quote: Quite simply, I don't like paying taxes!

name: Alfred West Jr
about: Alfred West oversees SEI, the $2 billion (revenue) financial services firm he founded in 1968.
SEI, which stands for Simulated Environments Inc., first developed a computer program to train loan officers by simulating a lending environment.
West took SEI public in 1981 and branched out into investment advisory and money management.
He retired as CEO in 2022, after more than 50 years at the helm. He's now executive chairman.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Georgia Institute of Technology

did_you_know_facts: West dreamed of becoming a fighter pilot when he was younger and studied aerospace engineering at Georgia Tech.
He didn't qualify to fly due to poor eyesight, so he got an MBA at Wharton instead and then launched SEI.
quote: CEOs need to be shareholders ... They should have just as much at stake as their employees or their investors.

name: Evan Williams
about: Evan Williams, also referred to as "Ev," has started three digital publishing companies: Blogger, Twitter and Medium.
A University of Nebraska dropout, Williams grew up on his family's soybean and corn farm.
Williams' venture capital firm, Obvious Ventures, was one of the largest investors in Beyond Meat, which had a successful IPO in May 2019.
He cofounded Twitter and served as a member of its board of directors until February 2019. He was President and CEO from July 2009 to March 2010.
In July 2022, Williams announced he was stepping down as CEO of Medium, the online publishing platform he founded in 2012. He remains chairman.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Drop Out, University of Nebraska Lincoln

did_you_know_facts: Williams has been credited as the person who coined the term "blogger."
Williams sold tutorial videos aimed at helping people understand the Internet in the mid-1990s.
Williams' firm Obvious Ventures invests in "world positive" companies, focusing on sustainability, healthy living and democratizing tech.
quote: Maybe it was because I grew up on that farm with so many ideas in my head and so few people to share them with that I couldn't think of anything more exciting than a system with the potential to connect brains from all over the planet.

name: Ilona Herlin
about: Ilona Herlin is the great-granddaughter of Finnish business leader Harald Herlin, who invested in Kone Elevators in 1924.
After her father's death in 2003, Ilona and her siblings discovered the will had been rewritten leaving most of the ownership in Kone to brother Antti
Angered that they had never been informed, the siblings battled for control. The dispute ended in 2005, with Kone being split in two.
Antti maintained control over the elevator business while his siblings were given stakes in Cargotec, producer of machinery for heavy duty ship cargo.
Niklas, one of the siblings, passed away in 2017. Three of the siblings are billionaires.
did_you_know_facts: Ilona is a linguist by training and an associate professor at Helsinki University.
Her research, leading to calls for a simplification of the Finnish language, has sparked debate in academia.

name: William Koch
about: William "Bill" Koch, brother of Koch Industries chairman and co-CEO Charles Koch, is the founder of petroleum coke and sulphur products company Oxbow Carbon Corp.
The Kansas native formed his own company after selling his stake in Koch Industries to brothers Charles and David (d. 2019) for $470 million in 1983.
He battled his brothers for two decades over the payout amount. The case was settled for an undisclosed amount in 2001.
Bill's brother Frederick (d. 2020) also sold his stake in Koch Industries to Charles and David in 1983 and was involved in the ensuing legal battle.
Koch Industries was started in 1940 by Bill's father, Fred Koch, who improved a method of refining heavy oil into gasoline.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctorate, Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

did_you_know_facts: Bill and David were fraternal twins; the duo went to MIT together and played on the same basketball team.
The thrice married industrialist built a private Wild West-style town in Colorado, complete with saloons, a jail house and a train station.

name: Christopher Goldsbury
about: Christopher "Kit" Goldsbury's fortune comes from selling salsa maker Pace Foods to Campbell Soup for $1.1 billion in 1994.
Goldsbury worked on the assembly line at Pace in 1969, two years after marrying founder David Pace's daughter Linda. He became president in 1977.
After Goldsbury and Linda separated in 1987, Goldsbury purchased her half for $95 million, a fraction of what he sold it for seven years later.
The San Antonio billionaire is backing the revitalization of the downtown Pearl neighborhood through his private equity firm Silver Ventures.
quote: "I was raised in Mexico, so I had a lot of influence in that area, with the food, with the people, everything."

name: Koo Bon-sik
about: Koo Bon-sik is the chairman of LT group, which has interest in precious metals, advanced materials and electronics.
He owns a stake in Heesung Electronics, which is run by his brother, Koo Bon-neung, also one of the richest people in South Korea.
Bon-sik is the youngest of the four Koo brothers of the LG Group, cofounded in 1947 by their late grandfather Koo In-hwoi.
did_you_know_facts: LG, then called, Lak Hui Chemical Industrial, was set up with a popular face cream.

name: Sefik Yilmaz Dizdar
about: Sefik Yilmaz Dizdar is a partner in LC Waikiki, a producer and retailer of ready-to-wear fashions and home items.
Designer Georges Amouyal and a partner founded LC Waikiki in France in 1985. Dizdar and partners including Mustafa Kucuk acquired it in 1997.
LC Waikiki's first international store opened in Romania in 2009. In 2016, it expanded into home textile products under the brand name LCW Home.
The company prides itself on promoting women into its management ranks.
Today, LC Waikiki has over 1,000 locations in 47 countries; roughly half are outside of Turkey. Its motto: "Everyone deserves to dress well."
did_you_know_facts: LC Waikiki, with annual revenue of around $2.5 billion, is managed by Kucuk, also a billionaire, and his family.
The brand combines the name of the famous Hawaiian beach with "LC," as in "Les Copains" ("friends" in French).

name: Michael Arougheti
about: Michael Arougheti is the cofounder and CEO of credit-oriented alternative investment firm Ares Management, which manages $596 billion in assets.
Arougheti arrived at Ares in 2004 to help create and grow its private credit business and took over as CEO from cofounder Antony Ressler in 2018.
Ares' largest business is its direct lending segment, which makes loans to private middle-market companies in the U.S. and Europe.
The firm also has funds in several other asset classes, including private equity, real estate and infrastructure.
Arougheti graduated from Yale and worked at Kidder, Peabody & Co., Indosuez Capital and Royal Bank of Canada before joining Ares.

name: Ye Guofu
about: Ye Guofu is the founder and CEO of budget retail chain Miniso, known for its value-for-money goods such as $1.5 mascara and $6 headphones.
The company went public on the New York Stock Exchange in October 2020.
Once branded as Japan-inspired, Miniso apologized in 2022 for its marketing strategy amid consumer backlash at home. It has has since removed Japanese elements from its store and logo designs.
Banking on a franchise-heavy model for expansion, the company now has over 5,000 Miniso shops, including more than 2,000 overseas.
Ye holds a degree from Zhongnan University of Economics and Law.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Associate in Arts/Science, Zhongnan University of Economics and Law

name: Lee Jay-hyun
about: Lee Jay-hyun is chairman of the CJ Group, a conglomerate that operates the country's largest food and beverage company, CJ Cheiljedang.
He is the eldest grandson of the late Samsung founder Lee Byung-chull; CJ officially separated from Samsung in 1997.
In 2015, Lee Jay-hyun was convicted and sentenced to two and a half years in jail on embezzlement and tax evasion charges.
In 2016, he was pardoned by then president Park Geun-hye and returned to his post in 2017. He is facing a new tax evasion probe in 2025.
did_you_know_facts: His CJ Group began as a sugar mill and boosted domestic sugar production just after the end of the Korean War.
In 1995, CJ paid $300 million for an 11% stake in Steven Spielberg's production vehicle Dreamworks SKG.

name: Lillian Teh Li Ming
about: Lilian Teh Li Ming is the daughter of late banker Teh Hong Piow, who chaired Malaysian banking behemoth Public Bank for several decades
Teh Hong Piow founded the bank in 1966. He died in December 2022 at age 92.
In addition to Malaysia, the bank serves millions of customers across Cambodia, China, Hong Kong, Sri Lanka and Vietnam.
Teh had a substantial minority stake in the bank as well as in the listed insurance business, LPI Capital.

name: William Teh Lee Pang
about: William Teh Lee Pang is the son of late banker Teh Hong Piow, who founded Malaysian banking behemoth Public Bank and chaired it for several decades.
Teh Hong Piow founded the bank in 1966. He died in December 2022 at age 92.
n addition to Malaysia, the bank serves millions of customers across Cambodia, China, Hong Kong, Sri Lanka and Vietnam.
The late Teh owned a substantial minority stake in the bank as well as in the listed insurance business, LPI Capital.

name: Lillyn Teh Li Hua
about: Lillian Teh Li Hua is the daughter of late banker Teh Hong Piow, who chaired the Malaysian banking behemoth Public Bank for several decades.
Teh Hong Piow founded the bank in 1966. He died in December 2022 at age 92.
In addition to Malaysia, the bank serves millions of customers across Cambodia, China, Hong Kong, Sri Lanka and Vietnam.
Teh had a significant minority stake in the bank as well as in the listed insurance business, LPI Capital.

name: Diona Teh Li Shian
about: Diona Teh Li Shian is the daughter of late banker Teh Hong Piow, who chaired Malaysian banking behemoth Public Bank for several decades.
Her father founded the bank in 1966. Teh died in December 2022 at age 92.
Her father had a substantial minority stake in both Public Bank and insurance firm LPI Capital.

name: Holger Loclair
about: Holger Loclair, originally from the GDR (former socialist East Germany) started working in 1987 at an industrial company that was later named Orafol when capitalism took hold.
West German investor Klaus Schmidbaur owned Orafol until he gradually transferred 99% of it to Loclair during 2013-2016.
Orafol is the world market leader for self-adhesive reflective films and industrial tapes.
Loclair is the only billionaire form former East Germany. His son Christian Loclair invests in startups.

name: Sue Gross
about: Sue Gross is the ex-wife of PIMCO cofounder and billionaire Bill Gross. The two divorced in 2017 after 32 years of marriage.
Gross walked away with roughly $1.3 billion, including a $36 million house in Laguna Beach and half of the couple's art collection.
After the divorce, she sold a Picasso painting for $35 million and purchased a number of properties in Orange County.
In 2017, Sue Gross started her own charitable vehicle, Sue J. Gross Foundation.
Previously the couple had run the William and Sue Gross Family Foundation, which supported Doctors Without Borders, Columbia U. and Duke U.
did_you_know_facts: Gross apparently got custody of two of she and her ex-husband's three cats in their divorce settlement.

name: Andrew Bialecki
about: Andrew Bialecki is cofounder and CEO of Klaviyo, which sells marketing automation software.
Bialecki launched Klaviyo in 2012 and refused venture capital money for three years.
Klaviyo eventually raised $455 million from VCs, but Bialecki managed to retain sizable control: he owned 38% when he took the firm public in 2023.
Bialecki said he took cues on efficiency from the cultures at Microsoft and Oracle in the 1980s and 1990s.
Before Klaviyo, Bialecki studied physics, astronomy and astrophysics at Harvard, graduating in 2007, then worked as a software engineer for a few years.

name: Boris Zingarevich
about: In the early 1990s Boris Zingarevich and his business partner Zakhar Smuskhin got involved in barter trading with Russian pulp and paper mills.
Later that decade, during the country's privatization phase, they bought their first plant, the Kotlas pulp and paper mill.
The partners' Ilim Group formed a joint venture in 2007 with multinational firm International Paper; the venture operates in Russia as Ilim Group.
As part of the deal, International Paper purchased 50% of Ilim for approximately $650 million, most of which was cash.
In 2023 International Paper sold its 50% interest in Ilim Group to the Russian partners.
Zingarevich also controls Ilim Timber, a large Russian processed timber firm.

personal_stats.label: Source of Wealth
personal_stats.value: Pulp and paper, diversified, Self Made

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Leningrad Technological Institute of Pulp and Paper Industry

name: Zhou Yahui
about: Zhou Yahui is the founder and director of Beijing Kunlun Tech, a Beijing-headquartered operator of online games. He stepped down as chairman in April 2020 to focus on his African mobile payment business, Opay.
Zhou's former wife Li Qiong became a billionaire in 2016 following the couple's divorce settlement.
Zhou holds a master's degree from China's elite Tsinghua University.

name: Robert Fisher
about: Robert "Bob" Fisher is one of three sons of Gap founders Donald (d. 2009) and Doris Fisher.
He is managing director of the Fisher family's investment firm, Pisces, and chaired Gap's board until 2020.
Like his two billionaire brothers, he attended Princeton, where he played tennis and majored in English, before heading to Stanford's business school.
A philanthropist, Fisher cofounded the California Water Foundation, which focuses on improving California's water supply, in 2010.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Princeton University; Master of Business Administration, Stanford University

name: Airat Shaimiev
about: Airat Shaimiev made his fortune as a co-owner of the TAIF Group, a large regional holding company with assets in the Republic of Tatarstan.
In 2021, TAIF merged with petrochemical company Sibur. He and other TAIF shareholders got 15% of Sibur in exchange.
Shaimiev is also CEO of Tatautodor, the government-owned group that does road construction and repair in Tatarstan.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Moscow Power Engineering Institute, Kazan

did_you_know_facts: Airat's father, Mintimer Shaimiev, was Tatarstan's first president; his brother, Radik is also a billionaire.
Airat, his brother Radik and Airat's son Timur together own a small oil company, MNKT, in Tatarstan.

name: Li Xiaohua & family
about: Li Xiaohua is the vice chairman of Shenzhen-listed Yunnan Energy New Material, a supplier of paper packaging materials and polypropylene film.
Clients include Panasonic, LG Chemical and Comtemporary Amperex Technology.
Li graduated from the University of Massachusetts with a major in polymer materials in 1993.
He worked for World-Pak Corp. in the U.S. after graduation until 1996.
His brother Paul Xiaoming Lee, a U.S. citizen, is the chairman of Yunnan Energy New Material and is also a billionaire.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, University of Massachusetts

name: Drew Houston
about: Drew Houston is the CEO of Dropbox, a file storage and sharing service that has more than 700 million users.
Houston cofounded the company in 2007, when he was 24, with MIT classmate Arash Ferdowsi.
The cloud storage provider went public on the Nasdaq in 2018.
Houston, who owns more than 20% of the company, is Dropbox's largest individual shareholder.
Houston joined Meta's board of directors in 2020.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

did_you_know_facts: Houston worked at an industrial robotics startup when he was 15.
quote: Maximize your rate of learning. Pick opportunities that will push you and surround you with the most talented people.

name: Peter Lim
about: After cashing out of palm oil giant Wilmar more than a decade ago, former stockbroker Peter Lim focused on healthcare, property and sports.
Lim has consolidated his healthcare businesses in Singapore and Malaysia with his Singapore-listed Thomson Medical Group.
Son Kiat serves as executive vice chairman of Thomson Medical Group. In March 2025, he was appointed president of Spanish football club Valencia, which his father acquired in 2014.
In 2023, Thomson Medical Group acquired hospital operator Far East Medical Vietnam for $353 million.
Peter ventured into education in 2022, partnering with top British boarding school Wellington College to set up international schools across Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore in the next few years.
did_you_know_facts: Lim also owns Hotel Football in Manchester, located close to Old Trafford, a stadium that's the home of Manchester United.
Lim, who once made a failed bid to buy English football club Liverpool, owns a controlling stake in Spanish football club Valencia.
The son of a fishmonger, Lim held part-time jobs as a waiter and taxi driver to pay for his college tuition.
quote: At the end of the day the key component is the person. You may target the right company, but if you've chosen the wrong person, you'll get a headache.

name: Charlotte Soderstrom
about: Charlotte S'derstr?m is the daughter of Sweden's richest person, Stefan Persson, chairman of global cheap chic retailer H&M, where she holds a stake.
Her grandfather Erling Persson founded the chain in 1947.
Brother Karl-Johan is set to be appointed chairman at the annual shareholders meeting in 2020.
Brother Tom Persson and aunt Lottie Tham are also billionaires.
S'derstr?m works on H&M sponsorships and runs a stud farm.
did_you_know_facts: S'derstr?m is reportedly the owner of the horse H&M All In, which won a silver medal at the 2016 Olympics.

name: Sun Mengquan & family
about: Sun Mengquan chairs Shandong-based cooking oil company Luhua Group.
Sun began working for the predecessor of Luhua in 1983, when it was a nearly bankrupt metals trading collective with fewer than 10 workers.
Sun shifted the company's business to processing and exporting peanuts, and, later, into peanut oil.

name: Massimo Moratti
about: Massimo Moratti is the largest shareholder and former CEO of Saras, Italy's largest oil refinery.
His father, Angelo, founded the firm in 1962; Massimo and his late billionaire brother, Gian Marco (d.2018), took Saras public in 2006.
Massimo owns 20% of the company, which has a liquified fuel gasification plant, a wind farm in Sardinia and gas stations mainly in Spain.
Gian Marco controlled a similar stake as Massimo and passed it on to his two sons, Angelo and Gabriele, when he died.
did_you_know_facts: Moratti was an owner of soccer club Inter Milan for more than two decades before selling the last of his shares in mid-2016.
His 19-year tenure included five straight Italian titles and the elusive treble in 2010, which included Champions League and Club World Cup titles.

name: Wang Miaotong
about: Wang Miaotong is the chairman of Zhejiang Century Huatong Group, a supplier of auto parts that has diversified into the mobile gaming business.
His son Wang Yifeng is vice chairman of Zhejiang Century Huatong Group.

name: Asok Kumar Hiranandani
about: Asok Kumar Hiranandani is a cofounder of the erstwhile Royal Brothers property group.
He separated from his older brother Raj Kumar in 2011 after dividing their property empire.
His Royal Group, run by his son Bobby, owns the 215-room Sofitel Singapore Sentosa Resort.
Hiranandani opened Singapore's second Raffles hotel in Sentosa, consisting of 62 villas, in 2024.

In 2022 after selling his 134-room SO/Singapore hotel in the city's central business district for a record S$240 million, he paid a record price of S$172 million for the Ming Arcade near Orchard Road.
did_you_know_facts: In 2018, he bought the Darby Park Executive Suites, a serviced apartments complex close to Orchard Road, for $70 million but has sold it since.
In February 2025, his Royal Group bought a former bank building in London. He's looking to redevelop it into a luxury hotel with 50 suites.
quote: I'd rather give the business over when I'm alive.

name: Ralph Winterhalter
about: Ralph Winterhalter owns Winterhalter, a family-owned maker of commercial dishwashers based in Meckenbeuren, Germany.
Winterhalter was founded by Karl Winterhalter in 1947, and is now controlled by his grandson Ralph Winterhalter, who owns the majority stake, and son Jurgen, the CEO.
Winterhalter has 2,000 employees and revenue of 475 million euros in 2024.
The company blog features articles on Oktoberfest beer mug hygiene, avoiding glass corrosion and how to properly place glasses on a dining table.

name: Sandro Veronesi & family
about: Sandro Veronesi is the president of Oniverse (formerly Calzedonia), a hosiery and lingerie retail chain he founded in 1986 in Verona, Italy.
He got his start in the business by working for the Italian king of hosiery, Nerino Grassi, at the Golden Lady Company.
Today, his Oniverse group with subsidiary brands Intimissimi, Tezenis, and Falconeri, boasts more than 5,600 stores in 57 countries.
Veronesi is passionate about wine, and opened Signorvino, a chain of wine shops, cafes and restaurants across Italy.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Verona

did_you_know_facts: Veronesi started Calzedonia as a side business, while he was still working at the Golden Lady Company.

name: Raymond Kwok
about: Raymond Kwok is the youngest son of the late Kwok Tak-seng, cofounder of Sun Hung Kai Properties, one of the largest developers in Hong Kong.
Since 2011 he's served first as the developer's cochairman and now as the chairman.
The three Kwok brothers inherited the publicly traded company after the death of their father in 1990.
The brothers fought for a decade over the family's assets until Walter (d. 2018), the eldest brother, decided to drop his lawsuit.
Raymond's son Edward has been an alternate director and his other son, Christopher, has been an executive director. Both are also billionaires.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts, Cambridge University; Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School

did_you_know_facts: Both he and his brother Thomas are devout Christians. They built an evangelical theme park, Noah's Ark, on Ma Wan Island in Hong Kong.
quote: "I remain grateful for knowing you as my brother, you will remain my brother," Raymond wrote in the memorial booklet at Walter's funeral in 2018.

name: Lesley Bamberger
about: Lesley Bamberger is the owner of Kroonenberg Groep, a privately held real estate company in the Netherlands.
The group has a portfolio of retail, industrial and residential buildings in the Netherlands and the United States.
His grandfather, Jacob Kroonenberg, founded the company in 1956.
Bamberger joined the business in 1986 and inherited it in 1996 after his grandfather's death.

name: Zbigniew Juroszek & family
about: Zbigniew Juroszek is the founder of Atal S.A., a real estate developer listed in Warsaw, Poland.
Juroszek first founded Atal in 1990 as a supplier to clothing manufacturers, before investing in real estate.
He built his first residential projects in 2003; Atal now develops properties in Katowice, Warsaw, and other major Polish cities.
He now runs his business with his son Mateusz, who is the CEO of gambling company STS.
STS, which is owned by the father and son duo, provides betting services to over 1 million customers in Europe.

name: Daniel Chiu
about: Daniel Chiu chairs Fortune Oil, a Hong Kong-based oil and gas supplier that also operates infrastructure projects in mainland China.
Through Fortune, Chiu also owns a large stake in China Gas Holdings, a Hong Kong-listed distributor of natural gas and operator of gas pipelines.
Chiu is the founder of the Harrow International Schools, which has 12 locations in Bangkok, Beijing, Hong Kong, Shanghai and Japan's Appi.
Also known as Chiu Tat Jung, he broke into the billionaire ranks in 2019.

name: Lu Ruibo
about: Lu Ruibo is the founder and chairman of Impro Precision Industries, a manufacturer of casting and machined components.
Customers of the company include Bosch, Caterpillar, Cummins, Honeywell, HUSCO and Parker Hannifin.
The company has over 7,000 employees.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Yanshan University

name: Oleg Boyko
about: Oleg Boyko's private equity firm Finstar Financial currently manages and consults portfolio companies operating in 30+ countries.
After Russia invaded Ukraine, his mother who held all of his shares in fintech 4Finance gave 9.9% each to Ukrainian relatives and a nonprofit in Switzerland.
She sold the rest of the family's 4Finance stake to four new, non-Russian minority shareholders.
Boyko opened Moscow's first stores with credit card readers in the 1990s.
In 2002 Boyko invested in a Moscow chain of gambling venues and founded Ritzio Entertainment Group, which invested in casinos and gambling.
When gambling was banned, Boyko sold his Russian gambling assets and moved into gambling in the European Union.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Moscow Aviation University; Master of Business Administration, Russian National Academy of National Economy and Public Administration

did_you_know_facts: Boyko, who was injured in an accident in 1996 and often appears in a scooter-style wheelchair, is the main private sponsor of Russian Paralympics team.
He invests in movie-making. His projects include Roberto Rodriguez's Sin City II and Scarlett Johansson's Summer Crossing.

name: John Goff
about: John Goff made a fortune selling Crescent Real Estate to Morgan Stanley for $6.5 billion in 2007, then bought it back at a big discount after the financial crisis.
He is an owner of Greystone Castle Sporting Club in Mingus, Texas, a 6,000-acre ranch where you can hunt exotic game and stay in a castle.
Goff spearheaded the creation of publicly traded oil company Crescent Energy by rolling up numerous smaller operators.
He owns the Canyon Ranch chain of wellness spas, which is building a new location in Austin, Texas with financing from hotel giant VICI.
did_you_know_facts: Goff got his big break working for famed Fort Worth investing guru Richard Rainwater.

name: Zong Yanmin
about: Zong Yanmin chairs SICC, a supplier of silicon-carbon semiconductor materials.
Founded in 2010, SICC is headquartered in the eastern China city of Jinan.
SICC went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2022.

name: Thomas Eisert
about: Thomas Eisert is a shareholder of Phoenix Contact Group, a family-owned German electrical engineering company.
Phoenix was founded by Hugo Knumann merchant who started a distribution business for electrical products following the first world war.
Knumann died in 1953, but not before hiring an electrical engineer, Josef Eisert, who along with Ursula Lampmann took over and transformed the business into a manufacturer.
Five members of the Eisert family, including Josef's son Klaus, remain shareholders in the company, which has annual sales of more than 3 billion euros.

name: Girdhari Jaisinghani
about: The eldest of five siblings, Girdhari Jaisinghani owns a minority stake in listed Polycab India, which makes electrical wires and cables.
The company was started in 1986 by his younger brother Inder as a trading firm.
Today, Polycab gets the bulk of its revenues from wires and cables.
It supplies everything from power cables to solar cables to optical fiber cables. Its customers are largely in the oil and gas, power and renewable energy industries.
In 2014, Polycab expanded into products such as electric fans, LED lighting, switches and switchgear.
did_you_know_facts: He has no executive role in the company.
Polycab India went public in 2019.

name: Hiroshi Ishibashi
about: Hiroshi Ishibashi is a grandson of the founder of Bridgestone, the world's second-largest tire maker by revenue.
He owns a small but valuable stake in the Tokyo-listed company but does not hold any executive position.
Hiroshi heads the Ishibashi Foundation, which operates Tokyo's Bridgestone Museum of Art.

name: Xue Xiangdong & family
about: Xue Xiangdong chairs Shenzhen-listed DHC Software, which makes software for industrial applications.
Xue worked at a state-owned company after graduation but quit in 1992 to become a representative in China for a Canadian software firm.
DHC went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2006.

name: Pantas Sutardja
about: Pantas Sutardja cofounded semiconductor company Marvell Technologies in 1995 with his late billionaire brother, Sehat Sutardja (d. 2024), and his billionaire sister-in-law, Weili Dai.
Pantas Sutardja resigned as chief technology officer of Marvell in 2014. His brother and sister-in-law were pushed out in 2016 amid an accounting investigation, though they never faced any charges.
Pantas Sutardja invested in semiconductor company Credo Technology's Series A funding round in 2015 and joined its board that year. He owns 3% of Credo, which went public on the Nasdaq in 2022.
He is also CEO of LatticeWork, a consumer electronics company he founded in 2013.
He holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science and Electrical Engineering from the University of California, Berkeley.

name: Peter Jackson
about: Peter Jackson is best known for his "Lord of the Rings" and "The Hobbit" trilogies, which have grossed $6 billion worldwide.
The film director became a billionaire in 2021, after selling a chunk of his Weta digital film effects shop to Unity Software for $1.6 billion in cash and stock.
He made $10 million up front for each of the three "Lord of the Rings" films (2001-2003), with at least another 10% of profits earned from each film's box office receipts.
For the "Hobbit" movies, he likely made $20 million per film with 20% backend.
Jackson's Weta Digital used motion capture of the actor Andy Serkis to create the now-iconic on-screen visualization of the character Gollum.
did_you_know_facts: Sean Parker, the tech investor known for founding Napster and serving as Facebook's first president, had a 25% stake in Jackson's Weta Digital at the time of sale.

name: Miranda Qu
about: Miranda Qu is the president of Shanghai-based social and e-commerce company Xiaohongshu, which translates as "Little Red Book."
She cofounded the company in 2013 with Charlwin Mao, who is CEO. Xiaohongshu now has over 200 million monthly active users.
Qu and Mao each own an estimated 10% of the company.
Xiaohongshu was valued at $20 billion after a funding round in November 2021 that raised money from investors like Tencent and Alibaba.
Qu formerly worked in marketing for Bertelsmann.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Beijing Foreign Studies University

name: Charlwin Mao
about: Charlwin Mao is the CEO of Shanghai-headquartered social and e-commerce platform Xiaohongshu.
Mao co-founded the company with Miranda Qu in 2013.
Earlier in his career, he worked at Bain Consulting and Bain Capital.

name: Eric Glyman
about: Eric Glyman is the cofounder and CEO of fintech startup Ramp, which private investors valued at $32 billion in November 2025.
Glyman launched the company in 2019 with Karim Atiyeh and Gene Lee. Each cofounder owns an estimated 6% of Ramp.
Glyman and Atiyeh met as undergrads at Harvard and cofounded their first company, price tracking app Paribus, in 2014.
The pair enrolled Paribus in the elite startup incubator Y Combinator that year and then sold the company to Capital One for an undisclosed sum in 2016.
Glyman and Atiyah continued to run Paribus as part of Capital One for two and a half years before leaving to launch Ramp.
Before cofounding Paribus, Glyman worked for two years as a financial analyst at Millstein & Co. (now part of Guggenheim Partners).

name: Gene Lee
about: Gene Lee is a cofounder of fintech startup Ramp, which private investors valued at $32 billion in November 2025.
Lee launched the company in 2019 with Eric Glyman and Karim Atiyeh. Each cofounder owns an estimated 6% of Ramp.
Lee joined Paribus, a price tracking app cofounded by Glyman and Atiyeh, as a software engineer in 2015.
The trio went to work for Capital One for two and a half years after the credit card giant acquired Paribus for an undisclosed sum in 2016.
Lee and Glyman live in New York, where Ramp is headquartered, while Atiyeh lives in Miami.

name: Karim Atiyeh
about: Karim Atiyeh is the cofounder and chief technology officer of fintech startup Ramp, which private investors valued at $32 billion in November 2025.
Atiyeh launched the company in 2019 with Eric Glyman and Gene Lee. Each cofounder owns an estimated 6% of Ramp.
Atiyeh and Glyman met as undergrads at Harvard and cofounded their first company, price tracking app Paribus, in 2014.
The pair enrolled Paribus in the elite startup incubator Y Combinator that year and then sold the company to Capital One for an undisclosed sum in 2016.
Atiyeh and Glyman continued to run Paribus as part of Capital One for two and a half years before leaving to launch Ramp.
Before cofounding Paribus, Atiyeh worked for two years at consulting firm Oliver Wyman, doing what he describes as "PowerPoint and Excel".

name: Hisao Nagata
about: Hisao Nagata is the founder and chairman of Trial Holdings, a discount supermarket chain with interests in retail IT and developing AI systems. His son Hiroyuki is a director.

Nagata's father, Oumi, opened a thrift store called Asahiya in 1974 in Fukuoka, which Hisao took over in 1981. Three years later, he changed the name to Trial Company and also started a software developer focusing on retail.
Trial has developed technology to decrease labor costs and increase efficiency, including self-checkout shopping carts and AI-powered cameras to gather shopper behavior data and monitor inventory.
Trial has over 600 stores in Japan and posted $5.2 billion in revenue in the fiscal year ended in June 2025.
In March 2024, Trial was listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange's Growth bourse.
did_you_know_facts: The first Trial discount store opened in 1992.
Nagata has written books on retail AI and digitization, including one in 2022 titled 'How to Win the Retail Digital Transformation.'

name: Lalit Khaitan
about: Liquor baron Lalit Khaitan is chairman of publicly traded spirits maker Radico Khaitan.
The Delhi-based company started off as a bottler before expanding into making bulk alcohol and eventually branded spirits.
Radico Khaitan has a range of brands including 8 M whisky, Contessa rum and Magic Moments vodka.
Khaitan inherited the liquor business from his later father G.N.Khaitan in 1995 after a family division.
did_you_know_facts: Khaitan's son Abhishek runs Radico Khaitan as managing director.
The company used to be called Rampur Distillery and Chemical Company.

name: Cao Kejian
about: Cao Kejian chairs Zhejiang Kaishan Compressor, China's biggest manufacturer of air compressors and rock drilling equipment.
Cao owns 52% of Zhejiang Kaishan, which went public in 2011 and whose customers include giant GE.
Cao holds a degree from Zhejiang University of Technology, where he majored in chemical machinery.

name: Marc Andreessen
about: Andreessen runs influential Silicon Valley venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, whose successful bets include Instagram, Oculus VR and GitHub.
His first claim to fame was cofounding web browser firm Netscape, which AOL bought in 1998 for $4.2 billion in stock.
Andreessen's biggest score was as a seed investor in Facebook.
He also cofounded Loudcloud, which, renamed Opsware, sold to Hewlett-Packard for $1.6 billion in 2007.
In June 2018, a16z raised $300 million for its first crypto-focused fund, co-led then by fellow Midas Lister Chris Dixon and the firm's first female general partner, Katie Haun.

forbes_list.list: The Midas List: Top Tech Investors (2025)

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign

did_you_know_facts: His wife Laura is daughter of billionaire John Arrillaga, who built his fortune in Silicon Valley real estate.
While still at college, Andreessen co-created the highly influential Mosaic Internet browser.

name: Noubar Afeyan
about: Noubar Afeyan is the founder and CEO of Cambridge, Mass. life sciences innovation firm Flagship Pioneering.
He's also the chairman and cofounder of biotech firm Moderna, known for its Covid-19 vaccine which was authorized by the U.S. FDA in December 2020.
Afeyan has helped start more than 70 public and private healthcare and life sciences companies over the course of his career.
Born in Beirut, Lebanon, in 1962 to Armenian parents, he and his family fled the Lebanese Civil War to move to Montreal in 1975.
Beyond his stake in Moderna, he also owns shares in several publicly traded biotech companies in the U.S.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, McGill University; Ph.D, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

did_you_know_facts: Afeyan was a lecturer at Harvard Business School until 2020 and also taught at MIT's Sloan School of Management from 2000 to 2016.
In 2014 he helped launch UWC Dilijan, an international boarding school in the town of Dilijan in the mountains of northern Armenia.
quote: What keeps you from innovating is being comfortable. If you're an immigrant, then you're used to being out of your comfort zone.

name: Vladimir Ivanov
about: Vladimir Ivanov is one of the earliest employees at Yandex, a tech company best known for its search engine.
Yandex divested its Russia-based business and delisted its shares from the Moscow stock exchange in 2024.
Yandex was renamed Nebius Group; it now trades on the Nasdaq and builds and operates AI data centers.
Ivanov is one of the largest individual shareholders of Nebius; its shares more than quadrupled in its first year of trading.
Nebius has been able to finance its AI data center business model with $2.8 billion in cash from the Yandex split.

name: P.P. Reddy
about: Farmer's son P.P. Reddy founded Megha Engineering Enterprises to build small pipes for municipalities in 1989.
He soon expanded into building infrastructure such as dams, natural gas distribution networks, power plants and roads.
In 2006, he changed the company's name to Megha Engineering and Infrastructure.
His nephew P.V. Krishna Reddy runs the company.
did_you_know_facts: Megha also has projects in Bangladesh, Kuwait, Tanzania and Zambia.

name: Hui Wing Mau
about: Hui Wing Mau chairs Shimao Property Holdings, a Hong Kong-listed real estate developer with projects in dozens of Chinese cities.
Hui's son Jason is vice chairman at Shimao Property; daughter Carol is the chairman of Shanghai-traded Shanghai Shimao.
Shares in his flagship company were suspended into 2023 after bond defaults in 2022.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of South Australia

name: Alexander Ramlie
about: Alexander Ramlie is a commissioner of Amman Mineral Internasional, which operates one of the largest copper and gold mines in Indonesia.
Amman Mineral went public in 2023 in a $710 million IPO, the largest in the country in the year.
Ramlie started his career as an investment banker at Lazard Frères & Co., now Lazard, a world-leading financial advisory and asset management firm.
He is also the CEO of Dhilmar, a UK-based mining company which in 2025 acquired the Éléonore gold mine in Canada from U.S. gold giant Newmont for $795 million.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Economics, Boston University; Master of Arts, Boston University

name: Kim Kardashian
about: Kim Kardashian has parlayed reality TV stardom into a ten-figure fortune, the vast majority of which comes from her stake in Skims, her shapewear business.
Skims is worth $5 billion after a 2025 funding round. The company's investors include billionaires Stephen Mandel, Daniel Sundheim and Josh Kushner, who is Ivanka Trump's brother-in-law.
Skims began as an online, direct-to-consumer brand, but has grown to 20 stores in the U.S. and Mexico with plans to become a mainly brick-and-mortar business in the coming years.
Kardashian sold 20% of her KKW Beauty to French beauty giant Coty in 2021, but later shut down the business and launched SKKN By Kim. Coty divested its stake to Skims in March 2025.
Kardashian divorced musician Kanye West in 2022. They share custody of their four children, and Kardashian reportedly paid $23 million to keep their Axel Vervoordt-designed Hidden Hills mansion.
did_you_know_facts: Kardashian is an advocate for criminal justice reform, gun safety and cancer causes.
Kadashian has some of the most-followed social media pages in the world: 72 million on X and 354 million on Instagram.
quote: I do feel like success is the best revenge.

name: Bambang Sutantio
about: Bambang Sutantio founded Cisarua Mountain Dairy, better known as Cimory, a manufacturer and distributor of dairy products and processed foods in Jakarta.
Cimory is known for its range of dairy products such as milk and yogurt as well as processed meats.
Sutantio first set up meat processor Macroprima Panganutama in 1993. He started the dairy business in 2004 to support dairy farmers in East Java.
Sutantio took Cimory public in 2021, raising more than $200 million.
In 2023, private equity firm General Atlantic bought a 5.6% stake in the dairy firm for $130 million.
did_you_know_facts: Sutantio has a diploma in food technology from the Technical University of Berlin.
He started his career as a sales engineer at the Jakarta office of Fuehrmeister, a German maker of industrial equipment.

name: Joop van den Ende
about: Joop van den Ende is a Dutch entertainment mogul and theatrical producer who founded Amsterdam-based Stage Entertainment in 1998.
Advance Publications acquired Stage in 2018 for a reported price of about $1.1 billion.
Van den Ende was Stage's sole owner until 2015, when CVC Capital Partners reportedly bought a 60% stake for $550 million.
Stage's original productions have included Rocky, Sister Act and Ice Age Live.
In 2021, van den Ende sold his 50% stake in the venture capital firm he created in 2006 to its two other cofounders.
did_you_know_facts: Van den Ende partnered with John de Mol, also a billionaire, to create reality TV production company Endemol in 1994.
The duo scored big with worldwide hit Big Brother before selling Endemol to Spanish telecom company Telefonica in 2000 for $5.3 billion.

name: Martine Rothblatt
about: Martine Rothblatt cofounded Sirius Satellite Radio in 1990 but left soon after the company's 1993 IPO.
Rothblatt moved into biotech after her daughter was diagnosed with pulmonary arterial hypertension, a disease that was deadly at the time.
She founded United Therapeutics in 1996; it sells five FDA-approved drugs to help people with the disease.
The publicly-traded company is experimenting with pig cloning and genetic modification to create lung transplants the human body doesn't reject.
The company's pig 'pharm' in Blacksburg, Virginia is the world's largest cloner of pigs.
did_you_know_facts: Rothblatt is an activist for transgender rights. She and her wife Bina have been married for more than 30 years.
Rothblatt is working to develop the first electric helicopter.
quote: I'm a person who likes to hear why something can't be done and I'll whittle down every one of the can'ts one at a time.

name: Giovanni Arvedi
about: Giovanni Arvedi is the founder and owner of the Arvedi Group, a steelmaker based in the northern Italian city of Cremona.
Arvedi comes from a long line of metal workers: his ancestors owned a small copper mine in northern Italy in the 17th century.
He started two trading and manufacturing firms in 1963 and later opened a steel works in Cremona in 1970.
In January 2022, the Arvedi Group acquired an 85% stake in Italian steel mill AST from ThyssenKrupp for a reported price of roughly $700 million.
The AST acquisition brought the company's revenues to nearly $8 billion in 2022, making it one of Europe's largest steelmakers.
did_you_know_facts: Arvedi also owns his hometown soccer team, Cremonese, which plays in Italy's top division Serie A as of the 2022-23 season.
In 1984, Arvedi was awarded the title of Cavaliere del Lavoro, one of Italy's highest civilian honors.

name: Terry Taylor
about: Terry Taylor owns over 120 car dealerships in the U.S. through his majority stake Automotive Management Services Inc.
Taylor first got into the car business working at his dad's used Ford shop in Daytona Beach, Florida.
Taylor offers his dealership managers equity in his dealerships, usually around 25%.
He owns several high profile properties, including Tommy Hilfiger's former New York penthouse, and a private jet with his initials "TT" on the tail.
did_you_know_facts: He avoids most meetings, even with his own associates, and only shows up at conventions and conferences on condition that he's not introduced to anyone.

name: Abbas Sajwani
about: Abbas Sajwani is the founder and owner of AHS Properties, a Dubai-based luxury real estate developer.
The son of billionaire developer Hussain Sajwani, he founded AHS in 2021 and started buying and fixing up villas in Dubai's luxe Emirates Hills and Palm Jumeirah.
In 2022, he sold the villas and bought land along the Dubai Water Canal for luxury residential towers, which now make up most of the business.
In 2025, he bought the long-vacant "Big Ben" tower in Dubai for $120 million and is now transforming it into a luxury office tower.
Before real estate, he owned an internet café and a car wash business and made a small fortune trading Simon Property Group stock between 2020 and 2021.
did_you_know_facts: In 2025, he bought the superyacht Amadea at auction from the U.S. government, which had seized it three years earlier from Russian oligarch Suleiman Kerimov.

name: Itzhak Ezratti & family
about: Itzhak Ezratti cofounded GL Homes in 1976 with his father-in-law Joseph Hanin.
GL Homes, the initials of which stands for "Good Luck," is one of Florida's largest private home builders, having completed over 36,000 homes since its founding.
Originally from Israel, Ezratti immigrated to Washington, D.C., and worked as a bank teller before moving to Florida.
GL Homes gained momentum in 1992 after Hurricane Andrew hit south Florida. That year and the year following, the company sold about 1,000 homes.
Ezratti stepped down as president of the firm in 2016 but continues to serve as chairman. His son Misha now runs GL Homes as president.
did_you_know_facts: Ezratti and his father-in-law's first GL Homes project in 1976 was a single duplex in Hollywood, Florida.
GL Homes specializes in its housing communities for people aged 55 and over.

name: David Kaplan
about: David Kaplan is a cofounder of credit-focused alternative investment firm Ares Management, which manages $596 billion in assets.
Kaplan has been at Ares since 2003 and previously spent three years at venture firm Shelter Capital Partners and a decade at Apollo Global Management.
He currently serves as a director and partner of Ares and was previously co-chairman of its private equity business.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Business Administration, University of Michigan

name: Xu Yingzhuo
about: Xu Yingzhuo is cofounder and director of Guangdong Haid Group, a supplier of aquatic products.
Xu holds degrees from South China University and an MBA from HEC Paris.
Guangdong Haid Group went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2009.

name: K.C. Liu
about: Liu Ko-chen, also known as K.C. Liu, is the chairman of Advantech, a supplier of industrial computing devices and software.
Liu cofounded Advantech in 1983 at age 29 with two colleagues from HP Taiwan.
Advantech is the world's largest industrial PC maker with a 41% market share.
Liu's sons, Wesley and Tony, sit on the board.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, National Chiao Tung University

did_you_know_facts: An avid reader of management books, Liu enjoys sharing books with staff, including Built to Last and Blue Ocean Strategy.
Before Advantech he was an R&D engineer and later a sales engineer for HP Taiwan in the Instrument Department.

name: Xiang Guangming & family
about: Xiang Guangming chairs Shanghai-listed Zhejiang Weiming Environment Protection.
Weiming's main business is solid waste incineration disposal.
Xiang's wife, Wang Suqin, also holds shares in the company.

name: Zakhar Smushkin
about: In the early 1990s Zakhar Smuskhin and his business partner Boris Zingarevich were active in barter trading with Russian pulp and paper mills.
Later in the 1990s, during the privatization phase in Russia, they bought their first plant, the Kotlas pulp and paper mill.
The partners' Ilim Group formed a joint venture in 2007 with multinational firm International Paper; the venture operates in Russia as Ilim Group.
As part of the deal, International Paper purchased 50% of Ilim for approximately $650 million.
In 2023 International Paper sold its 50% interest in Ilim Group to the Russian partners.
Smushkin also owns some 3,500 acres of land near Saint Petersburg.

personal_stats.label: Source of Wealth
personal_stats.value: Pulp and paper, diversified, Self Made

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Leningrad Technological Institute of Pulp and Paper Industry

did_you_know_facts: Russia's prime minister and former president, Dmitry Medvedev, worked as general counsel of Ilim Holding in the mid 1990s.
Smuskhin collects Russian paintings, particularly works by Mikhail Vrubel.

name: Alex Shevchenko
about: Alex Shevchenko is the cofounder of popular grammar checking tool Grammarly and serves as product lead.
He launched the company in 2009 alongside fellow Ukrainian entrepreneurs Max Lytvyn and Dmytro Lider.
The trio had all worked together on Lytvyn and Shevchenko's previous startup, My Dropbox, a plagiarism detector.
Initially programmed as a service to help students with their grammar and spelling, Grammarly claims it is used by over 30 million people and 70,000 professional teams today.
In November 2021, it raised $200 million at a $13 billion valuation from investors including Baillie Gifford and BlackRock.
Forbes estimates that Shevchenko owns a 23% stake, which the company disputes, and that Grammarly is worth around $8 billion today.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of Toronto

did_you_know_facts: Shevchenko was raised in the Ukraine, attended graduate school in Toronto and obtained Canadian citizenship.

name: Max Lytvyn
about: Max Lytvyn cofounded popular grammar checking tool Grammarly in 2009 with Alex Shevchenko and Dmytro Lider; his current title is head of growth strategy.
The three Ukrainian-born entrepreneurs all worked together on Lytvyn and Shevchenko's previous startup, My Dropbox, a plagiarism detection service.
Initially programmed as a service to help students with their grammar and spelling, Grammarly claims it is used by over 30 million people and 70,000 professional teams today.
In November 2021, Grammarly raised $200 million at a $13 billion valuation from such investors as Baillie Gifford and BlackRock.
Forbes estimates that Lytvyn owns a 23% stake, which the company disputes, and that Grammarly is worth around $8 billion today.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Vanderbilt University

did_you_know_facts: Lytvyn was born and raised in Ukraine and later obtained Canadian citizenship.

name: Barbara Benetton
about: Barbara Benetton is one of two daughters of Gilberto Benetton, who founded the Benetton Group in 1965 with siblings Carlo, Gilberto and Giuliana.
In 2018, with the death of their father, Barbara and her sister Sabrina each inherited part of his fortune; Barbara is not involved in the business.
The Benetton family started knitting and selling colorful sweaters from their home in Treviso, Italy and opened their first store abroad in 1969.
The four siblings later diversified their portfolio, and now own investments in infrastructure, catering, and financial firms.
Each of their families owns a quarter of the main holding, Edizione. Currently, the second generation has taken over its board of directors.

name: Barbara Berlusconi
about: Barbara Berlusconi is the daughter of Silvio Berlusconi, the media mogul and longest-serving Italian prime minister in the post-war era, who died at age 86 in June 2023.
Barbara is one of five heirs to media group Fininvest, which her father started in the late 1970s and built into a national force, importing American shows like 'Baywatch' to Italy.
Her father Silvio, a three-time Italian prime minister, was convicted of tax fraud in 2014 and was initially banned from running for political office until 2019.
She was the CEO of Italian soccer team AC Milan from 2013 to 2017, when her father sold it to Chinese investors for $790 million.
She joined the board of directors of Fininvest in 2003.

name: Luigi Berlusconi
about: Luigi Berlusconi is the son of Silvio Berlusconi, the media mogul and the longest-serving Italian prime minister in the post-war era, who died at age 86 in June 2023.
Luigi is one of five heirs to media group Fininvest, which his father started in the late 1970s and built into a national force, importing American shows like 'Baywatch' to Italy.
His father Silvio, three-time Italian prime minister, was convicted of tax fraud in 2014 and was initially banned from running for political office until 2019.
He has served on the board of directors of Fininvest since 2012.

name: Eleonora Berlusconi
about: Eleonora Berlusconi is the daughter of Silvio Berlusconi, the media mogul and longest-serving Italian prime minister in the post-war era, who died at age 86 in June 2023.
Eleonora is one of five heirs to media group Fininvest, which her father started in the late 1970s and built into a national force, importing American shows like 'Baywatch' to Italy.
Her father Silvio, a three-time Italian prime minister, was convicted of tax fraud in 2014 and was initially banned from running for political office until 2019.
Eleonora is the only Berlusconi heir who doesn't sit on the board of Finivest.
She manages companies outside the family's empire, including jewelry design and and a fur and clothing business.

name: Yigal Dimri
about: Yigal Dimri is the CEO and owner of the real estate group Y.H. Dimri, a Tel Aviv-based real estate business.
Y.H. Dimri is one of the largest residential construction companies in Israel, operating in the residential, office, and commercial real estate sectors.
He began his career as a renovation contractor in 1980 together with his father and established Y.H. Dimri in 1989.
In 2004, the company went public, and its securities are traded on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange.

name: Satish Mehta
about: Pharma distributor's son Satish Mehta founded and runs generics maker Emcure Pharmaceuticals, headquartered in Pune city.
He started Emcure as a contract manufacturer for multinationals in 1981 then went on to sell his own branded generics.
After getting investors such as Bain Capital, he listed the company at a 31% premium in July 2024.
Daughter Namita, an MBA graduate from the Fuqua School of Business and a trained chartered accountant, has a board seat. She's a judge on the Indian version of Shark Tank.
Son Samit, who has an MBA from Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania, is also a director on Emcure's board.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Pune University; Master of Science, Pune University

did_you_know_facts: Mehta's son-in-law and nephew work with him.

name: Zhang Liguo
about: Zhang Liguo is the founder and chairman of Harbin Fuerjia Technology, a maker of skincare products best known for its beauty masks.
He took Fuerjia public in Shenzhen in August 2023, raising $306 million.
Zhang worked as a pharmacist in a local hospital before striking out on his own.

name: Cao Ji
about: Cao Ji chairs Zhejiang Hangke Technology, a supplier to the lithium battery industry.
Hangke went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2019.
Cao has more than a 60% stake in Hangke with his son Cao Zheng, a company director.
Hangke is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Hangzhou.

name: Brendan Blumer
about: Brendan Blumer is cofounder of Hong Kong-based crypto exchange Bullish.
Bullish was founded in 2020 and went public on the New York Stock Exchange in August 2025.
Blumer owns a 28% stake in the company and serves as a director. Another Bullish board member, Kokuei Yuan, owns 25% of the company and is also a billionaire.
Blumer is also CEO and sole owner of block.one, a digital asset investment firm he cofounded in 2016. Bullish was majority-owned by block.one until 2024.
Blumer grew up in Iowa and moved to Hong Kong in 2005. He gave up his U.S. citizenship in 2020.

name: Stephane Courbit
about: Stephane Courbit is the chairman of Banijay Group, an independent production and distribution firm.
Courbit owns a 45% stake in the publicly traded company, whose 170,000+ hours of programming including Survivor and Peaky Blinders.
He started his career at production studio Coyote and then in 1994 formed his own production company with TV host Arthur
Four years later, billionaire John de Mol's Endemol merged that outfit to form Endemol France, which Courbit ran as CEO.
After leaving in 2007, Courbit set up privately held LOV Group, through which he operates Airelles, a collection of 7 boutique hotels including 3 palaces.
Through LOV, he also owns 740 acres of vineyards and olive trees plus Macaron maker Laduree.

name: Samir Mane
about: Samir Mane is the founder and president of BALFIN Group, an investment conglomerate based in Tirana, Albania.
BALFIN owns shopping malls and electronics retail and toy stores in the western Balkans, plus a bank and luxury real estate developments in Albania.
Mane fled Albania's communist regime in 1991 and moved to Austria as a refugee; in 1993, he started selling domestic appliances to his native country.
He launched Neptun, a chain of electronics stores, in Albania in 1998 and moved back to Albania in 2005 to open the country's first shopping mall.
BALFIN also owns real estate in the U.S., Canada and Austria as well as logistics parks and a private university in Albania.
did_you_know_facts: Mane would sleep in trucks on the two-day journey from Vienna to Tirana when he sold appliances in the early 1990s.

name: Rubén Coppel Luken
about: Rubén Coppel Luken and his four brothers own the Coppel department stores, one of Mexico's largest retailers.
Coppel is chairman of BanCoppel and Afore Coppel, the group's banking and pension fund businesses
BanCoppel, founded in 2007, stemmed from the retailer's historical practice of financing items to their clients.
Because customers were low on cash after World War II, founder Enrique Coppel Tamayo started selling furniture on credit using weekly payments.
In mid-2023, Afore Coppel reported over $24 billion in assets under management.
did_you_know_facts: BanCoppel has over 1,000 offices across Mexico.

name: Scot French
about: Scot French is a founding partner of HPS Investment Partners, one of the world's biggest alternative credit managers with $149 billion in assets.
French cofounded HPS in 2007 with Scott Kapnick and Michael Patterson, who are both also billionaires.
HPS was sold to BlackRock in July 2025 for around $12 billion in BlackRock stock.
French previously managed a proprietary investment fund within Citigroup, and before that worked at Goldman Sachs and Salomon Brothers.
He began his career as an accountant at Price Waterhouse after graduating from the University of Illinois.

name: Michael Patterson
about: Michael Patterson is a founding partner of HPS Investment Partners, one of the world's biggest alternative credit managers with $149 billion in assets.
He oversees HPS' specialty lending, corporate lending and core senior lending funds, and previously worked at Silver Point Capital and Goldman Sachs.
HPS was sold to BlackRock in July 2025 for around $12 billion in BlackRock stock.
Prior to his investing career, he served as an officer in the United States Navy. He serves on the Dean's Advisory Council for the Radcliffe Institute of Advanced Studies at Harvard.
Patterson holds an AB in Applied Mathematics from Harvard College and an MBA from Stanford.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Stanford University Graduate School of Business; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Harvard University

name: Mario Moretti Polegato & family
about: Mario Moretti Polegato founded his comfort-focused shoe brand Geox in 1995 with his patented "breathable shoe technology."
Polegato worked at his family's wine business where he got itchy feet, but it was a hot trip to Nevada that inspired him to slice holes in his shoes.
He took his technology to Nike and other footwear giants, who were uninterested; he started his own company instead.
He took Geox public in 2004 while also running the family wine label, Villa Sandi.
did_you_know_facts: Polegato was named a Knight of the National Order of Romania in 2000, and was appointed Cavaliere del Lavoro, one of Italy's highest civilian honors, in 2005.
He developed his breathable shoe prototype in the mid-1990s with researchers at the University of Padua, a university established in 1222.
quote: What I recommend to my colleague entrepreneurs is that today it's impossible to have success in a business if you don't innovate.

name: Harvey Jones
about: Investor and entrepreneur Harvey Jones joined the board of Nvidia when it was founded in 1993 and has been a director ever since.
Jones cofounded two tech companies-Daisy Systems in 1981 and Tensilica in 1997.
In between, he was CEO and chairman of electronic design automation company Synopsys, which now has a market cap of more than $80 billion.
Jones is a billionaire almost entirely due to his Nvidia director's compensation. He owns 0.03% of the company.
He continues to invest as a venture capitalist through his firm Square Wave Ventures.

name: Scott Lin
about: Scott Lin cofounded lens supplier Largan Precision with Tony Chen in 1987.
The company is a leading smartphone lens maker and a major supplier to Apple, claiming a quarter of the global market.
Largan is now run by his sons, En-Ping and En-Chou.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, National Chung Hsing University

name: Alan Zekelman
about: Alan Zekelman owns a stake in his family's steel business, Zekelman Industries.
The $3.3 billion (revenues) company is one of North America's largest steel pipe and tube makers.
The company has also pumped more than $1 billion into Z Modular, a division that is developing modular apartment complexes in places such as Texas, Arizona and Canada.
Alan and his brothers, fellow billionaires Barry Zekelman and Clayton Zekelman, split 100% ownership of Zekelman Industries.
They sold the company to the Carlyle Group in 2006 for some $1.2 billion, but bought the business back in 2011.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Commerce, University of Toronto; Master of Science, University of Rochester

did_you_know_facts: One of Zekelman Industries' subsidiaries, Atlas Tube, produced steel for stretches of the Mexican border wall in Arizona.

name: Helena Revoredo & family
about: Helena Revoredo is chair of Prosegur, a Spanish private security company known for its fleet of 10,000 yellow armored trucks and 165,000 employees.
Her late husband, Herberto Gut, founded the company in 1976; Gut died in a car accident in 1997.
Her son, Christian, is Prosegur's CEO, and her daughter Chantal Gut sits on the board.
Prosegur, which went public in 1987, operates throughout Europe, Latin America and Asia.
Revoredo is involved in the Prosegur Foundation, which promotes education as well as inclusion for people with intellectual disabilities.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, IESE Business School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Catholic University of Buenos Aires

did_you_know_facts: Revoredo was the first woman to sit on the board of Endesa, Spain's largest electric utility company.
A patron of the arts, she serves as president of the International Council of Madrid's Royal Theatre.

name: Mark Attanasio
about: Mark Attanasio is a managing partner and cofounder of Crescent Capital Group, a Los Angeles-based debt-focused investment firm with $43 billion in assets under management.
He is also chairman and principal owner of the Milwaukee Brewers baseball team; he bought an estimated 45% stake in the team in 2004 for a reported $220 million.
Forbes now values the Brewers at $1.6 billion.
Attanasio is an investor in Strategic Sports Group, a group of sports team owners that in 2024 inked a deal to invest $3 billion in the PGA golf tour.
He first worked as a lawyer, then in the mid 1980s joined investment bank Drexel Burnham Lambert, a pioneer in junk-bond trading. He cofounded Crescent in 1991.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: JD, Columbia University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Brown University

did_you_know_facts: Attanasio is majority shareholder of Norwich City FC, a team that competes in the second tier of English professional soccer.
He was born and raised in the Bronx, New York, the son of actor Joe Attanasio (d. 2015) who sang the national anthem at home games for the Brewers.

Today Lippo group's interests include real estate, retail, healthcare, media and education.

He has mostly invested through his Medcare Investment Funds, which manages $1 billion in assets.

The Tokyo-listed company made its mark with its Final Fantasy franchise and its Dragon Quest series.

name: Philip O'Doherty

The Queen's University graduate worked as an engineer for DuPont out in Campsie, Ireland for five years before venturing out on his own.

name: Chang Jianming & family

The company was founded in Shanghai in 1994 and employs more than 3,000 people.

name: Alberto Prada
about: Alberto Prada and his sisters, Miuccia Prada and Marina Prada, inherited a share of Prada, the handbag and fashion empire founded by their grandfather in 1913.
Neither Marina nor Alberto is involved in running the business, but each owns an estimated 12% stake in the company.
