name: Carlie Irsay-Gordon
about: Irsay-Gordon is the granddaughter of Robert Irsay, who acquired the Indianapolis Colts in 1972, and the eldest daughter of Jim Irsay, who ran the team from 1997 until his death in May 2025.
She and her sisters, Casey Foyt and Kalen Jackson, inherited what Forbes estimates are equal 33.3% stakes in the franchise. They now rank among the richest female owners in sports.

Irsay-Gordon serves as the Colts' principal owner and CEO. Long seen as her father's likeliest successor, she got early experience leading the franchise when she stepped in for Irsay in 2014 after his legal troubles resulted in a six-game suspension.

Irsay-Gordon once served as a team intern and has been involved with the organization's inner workings for more than two decades, having represented the franchise at NFL owners' meetings as early as 2004. Four years later, she took on a vice president role.
She has demonstrated a hands-on approach, attending meetings with players and coaches and standing on the sideline during games listening to play calls over a headset.

name: Casey Foyt
about: Foyt is the granddaughter of Robert Irsay, who acquired the Indianapolis Colts in 1972, and the middle daughter of Jim Irsay, who ran the team from 1997 until his death in May 2025.
She and her sisters, Carlie Irsay-Gordon and Kalen Jackson, inherited what Forbes estimates are equal 33.3% stakes in the franchise. They now rank among the richest female owners in sports.

Long before the three sisters were publicly named Colts co-owners in 2012, their lives revolved around the NFL schedule. At an introductory press conference in June 2025, Foyt recalled answering the phones at the front desk while she was in high school.
Early in her career, Foyt worked for the NFL, where she helped plan the league's first regular-season game played outside North America, in London in 2007.
She returned to the Colts that year with a focus on marketing and community relationships.

name: Kalen Jackson
about: Jackson is the granddaughter of Robert Irsay, who acquired the Indianapolis Colts in 1972, and the youngest daughter of Jim Irsay, who ran the team from 1997 until his death in May 2025.
She and her sisters, Carlie Irsay-Gordon and Casey Foyt, inherited what Forbes estimates are equal 33.3% stakes in the franchise. They now rank among the richest female owners in sports.

Long before the three sisters were publicly named Colts co-owners in 2012, they had spent countless years around the organization, with their lives always revolving around the NFL schedule. Jackson, her sisters and their father all had matching horseshoe tattoos.

"He let us in on conversations at a very young age, and when I look back on it now, I'm kind of surprised," Jackson said of Irsay in June 2025. "But he trusted us, and he knew that we understood the seriousness of this job and the responsibility that we had. And I think we'll forever be grateful."

Jackson officially joined the organization in 2010 and currently leads its philanthropic arm, including mental health nonprofit Kicking The Stigma, while also holding the title of chief brand officer.

name: Pantaleo Dell'Orco

Dell'Orco is the managing director and a board member of Armani's namesake fashion firm and is set to lead the sale of between 15% and 70% of the company within five years, as specified in Armani's will.
He joined the company in 1977, two years after its founding, and led the menswear division for decades.
Under the terms of Armani's will, Dell'Orco is entitled to 32% of the net proceeds from the sale of 45% of the company, which may also IPO under the terms of Armani's will.
Dell'Orco also inherited some of Armani's shares in eyewear giant EssilorLuxottica as well as a stake in Armani's superyacht and his empire of luxury homes.

name: Sebastian Kulczyk
about: Sebastian Kulczyk and his sister Dominika Kulczyk inherited a fortune from their father Jan, who died in 2015 from complications of minor heart surgery.
In 2018, the siblings divvied up assets, with Sebastian getting a stake in Autostrada Eksploatacja, which maintains a major highway.
He also took over the chemical business Ciech and shares in mining companies, the latter of which he sold. He took Ciech private in 2024, renaming it Qemetica.
Sebastian also founded and runs VC tech fund Manta Ray.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: London School of Economics; Master, University of Poznan

did_you_know_facts: Sebastian Kulczyk worked in the digital media unit at Sony BMG in New York when he was 21.

name: Pawan Munjal
about: Pawan Munjal is the chairman and managing director of Hero MotoCorp,the world's largest producer of two-wheelers by volume having sold more than 120 million units to date.
He inherited a stake in the Hero group after his father Brijmohan Lall Munjal, who cofounded the enterprise with his brothers, died in 2015 at age 92.
A former partner of Honda, Hero MotoCorp parted ways with the Japanese company in 2011. Since then Pawan has led a global expansion with factories in Colombia and Bangladesh.
The group's renewable energy arm, Hero Future Energies, along with U.S. private equity firm KKR, is investing $450 million in expanding capacity.
did_you_know_facts: In 2022, Hero launched Vida, its first electric scooter.
In 2023, the Delhi High Court stayed a federal investigation into allegations that he took money out of the country illegally. He's denied any wrongdoing.

name: Marius Nacht
about: Marius Nacht wrote the original code for cybersecurity firm Check Point Software Technologies, which made him and cofounder Gil Shwed billionaires.
He served as non-executive chairman of the board at Check Point from 2015 until 2020. Prior to that he was vice chairman.
Nacht cofounded aMoon, an Israeli healthtech VC firm, in 2016.
Nacht has also invested in multiple early-stage security startups, including LightCyber, SafeDK, Cyber Secdo and Rapid API.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Hebrew University, Jerusalem

did_you_know_facts: Nacht is a veteran of Talpiot, an elite division of the Israeli army.
Nacht has degrees in physics and mathematics from Hebrew University of Jerusalem and in electric engineering and communications systems from Tel Aviv University.

name: Gan Zhongru
about: Gan is cofounder and chairman of Shanghai-listed Gan & Lee Pharmaceuticals.
Founded in 1998, the company produces insulin and injection pens and is publicly traded.
Gan graduated from Peking University and later became a teacher in the biology department.
Gan holds a PhD from Michigan State University and worked for Merck before starting Gan & Lee.

name: Sergei Katsiev
about: Sergei Katsiev, partner of billionaire Igor Kesaev, made his fortune in tobacco after the fall of the Soviet Union.
From 1991 to 1993, he worked in the government trade mission to the Netherlands.
When he returned to Russia, he headed Mercury Tobacco Corporation, an importer of tobacco products owned by Kesaev.
In 1998 Katsiev founded his own company, Megapolis, which also sold tobacco products.
In 2006 Katsiev and Kesaev merged their companies. Megapolis is now Russia's largest seller of tobacco products.
Philip Morris and Japan Tobacco International bought 40% of Megapolis for $1.5 billion in 2013.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master, Moscow Institute of International Relations

did_you_know_facts: Katsiev is now the owner of Nizhny Karmadon, a mineral water producer sourced from the Caucasus.

name: Bingkun Xie & family
about: Xie Bingkun chairs Fujian Kuncai Material Technology, a supplier of coating materials.
Fujian Kuncai Material Technology went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2017.
Xie founded the predecessor of Kuncai in 2005.

name: Alexander Tkachev
about: Alexander Tkachev is the co-founder and controlling shareholder of Agrocomplex, one of Russia's largest agricultural & food producers.
His father, Nickolay, was a managing director of feed mill in Krasnodar Krai, a rural region in the South of Russia, which Tkachev began managing in 1990 and later re-branded it as Agrocomplex.
He began expanding by buying land during the country's privatization era, building it into Russia's second-largest landholder, with 1.23 million hectares (about 3 million acres) of agricultural land.
Agrocomplex' enterprises produce meat (beef, pork, poultry) and sausage products, dairy products and cheese, canned goods, sunflower oil, flour, sugar, sauces, etc.
In 2015-2018 Alexander Tkachev served as Minister of Agriculture of Russia; previously he was Governor of Krasnodar Krai.

name: Anil Gupta
about: Anil Gupta is the chairman and managing director of Delhi-based power cables manufacturer KEI Industries.
The company's products include stainless steel wires as well as low, medium and high voltage cables.
KEI exports to more than 55 countries across the world.
The company was started in 1968 by his father to make rubber cables for home wiring.
It is also listed on the Luxembourg Stock Exchange.
did_you_know_facts: He plays table tennis.

name: Grigory Berezkin
about: Grigory Berezkin derives his fortune from Rusenergosbyt, a Russian energy trading company.
In 2006, Berezkin sold nearly half of Rusenergosbyt to Italy's energy conglomerate Enel for $105 million.
He got his start in the energy business in the 2000s; and controlled companies that supplied electricity to state-owned corporations Gazprom, Russian Railways and Transneft.
During the privatization of Russia in the 1990s, Berezkin purchased a mid-size oil company, which he later sold to Russian oil conglomerate Lukoil for $619 million.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Lomonosov Moscow State University

name: Timothy Dunn & family
about: Timothy Dunn is founder and CEO of Crownquest, a family-owned oil business based in Midland Texas.
In 2024 Occidental paid $12 billion for CrownRock, the Permian oil JV between CrownQuest and Lime Rock Resources.
Dunn also founded his own K-12 school, Midland Classical Academy, with 750 students; and regularly preaches at Midland Bible Church.
Dunn continues to manage oil and gas royalty holder CrownRock Minerals.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Texas Tech University

did_you_know_facts: The Dunn family owns the historic Green Acres minigolf park in Midland, Texas.

name: Timothée Lacroix
about: Timothée Lacroix cofounded Mistral AI in 2023 raising $113 million from investors in what was then Europe's largest ever seed round. He's the company's chief technology offier.
The Paris-based company builds open-weight large language models that compete with U.S. rivals like OpenAI, and raised $2 billion on a $14 billion valuation in September 2025.
The French AI researcher met his future cofounder Guillaume Lample while working for Meta in its AI Research Lab after studying at Paris' École Normale Supérieure.
The pair worked together on Meta's open source Llama large language model before resigning in 2023..

name: Gerry Cardinale
about: Gerry Cardinale is the founder, CEO and owner of RedBird Capital Partners, a private equity firm with $12 billion in assets.
RedBird targets investments in entertainment, sports and financial services. It invested $1.8 billion in Skydance Media's $8 billion purchase of Paramount.
Cardinale spent nearly two decades at Goldman Sachs, working in Hong Kong, Singapore and New York. He was made a partner in 2004.
At Goldman, Cardinale helped Yankees owner George Steinbrenner launch the YES regional sports network in 2001 and Legends Hospitality with Jerry Jones in 2008.
Cardinale founded RedBird in 2014. The firm has backed ventures of Ben Affleck, LeBron James, and Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, and bought A.C. Milan in 2022.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Philosophy, Oxford Univeristy; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Harvard

did_you_know_facts: Cardinale rowed heavyweight crew at Harvard as an undergrad and at Oxford as a Rhodes Scholar, where he rowed in the 1990 Oxford-Cambridge Boat Race.
quote: I wasn't one of these Wharton kids who knew I wanted to go to Wall Street from day one.

name: Guillaume Lample
about: Guillaume Lample cofounded Mistral AI in 2023 raising $113 million from investors in what was then Europe's largest ever seed round.
​​The Paris-based company builds open-weight large language models that compete with U.S. rivals like OpenAI, and raised $2 billion on a $14 billion valuation in September 2025.

The French AI researcher met his future cofounder Arthur Mensch while studying at Paris' elite college École Polytechnique. Lample would later complete a master's degree in artificial intelligence at Carnegie Mellon University.
Lample worked for Meta as part of the Facebook AI Research team responsible for launching its open source model Llama in 2024. There he work with his future Mistral cofounder Timothee Lacroix.

name: Arthur Mensch
about: Arthur Mensch cofounded Mistral AI in 2023 raising $113 million from investors in what was then Europe's largest ever seed round. He is chief executive.
​​The Paris-based company builds open-weight large language models that compete with U.S. rivals like OpenAI, and raised $2 billion on a $14 billion valuation in September 2025.
Mensch was born and grew up in a Paris suburb to a mother who taught physics, and a father who ran a tech company.

The French AI researcher met his future cofounder Guillaume Lample while studying at Paris' elite college École Polytechnique. Mensch would later complete a doctorate in machine learning at Université Paris-Saclay.
Mensch worked for DeepMind at its Paris office and helped work on an early version of Google's Gemini large language model before cofounding Mistral.

name: Brian Higgins
about: Brian Higgins is the cofounder of King Street Capital Management, a distressed-debt focused hedge fund.
He started King Street in 1995 with fellow billionaire O. Francis Biondi, whom he met on First Boston's high-yield desk in the late 1980's.
King Street Capital Management managed over $25 billion of assets in 2023.
did_you_know_facts: He and cofounder Francis Biondi manage the King Street Charitable Trust, which donates to medical research and Villanova, Higgins' alma mater, among others.
Higgins and Biondi are known for shying away from publicity and don't hold investor days, during which investors meet the firm's asset managers.

name: O. Francis Biondi
about: O. Francis Biondi cofounded hedge fund King Street Capital Management in 1995 with fellow First Boston alum Brian Higgins.
King Street Capital Management oversees over $25 billion in assets and focuses on out-of-favor investments in stocks and bonds.
Biondi retired from King Street in 2020, but kept his ownership stake in the firm.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Yale University

did_you_know_facts: Biondi and Higgins also run the King Street Charitable Trust, whose grant recipients include his alma mater Yale, Memorial Sloan Kettering and others.
He's married to Jamie Nicholls, a former Forstmann Little partner and alum of Amherst College.

name: Larry Culp
about: Larry Culp is chairman and CEO of GE Aerospace (formerly known as General Electric).

He took over GE in 2018 and has broken up the bloated conglomerate into three separate public companies after spinning off its healthcare business as GE HealthCare in 2023 and its energy business as GE Vernova in 2024.
Culp also serves as chairman of GE Healthcare.
Culp started his career at Danaher, the industrial conglomerate founded by billionaire brothers Mitchell and Steven Rales.
He joined Danaher in 1990 and served as president and CEO from 2001 to 2015.

name: JB Straubel
about: JB Straubel is the founder and CEO of Redwood Materials and the former chief technology officer of Tesla.
A Stanford-educated engineer, Straubel was working on battery-powered planes in 2003 when he met Elon Musk at a campus lecture.
He joined Tesla as employee No. 5 in 2004, and drove the development of its battery packs and electric motors as CTO. He left the C-suite in 2019 but remains on the board.
He now runs Redwood Materials, a Nevada-based electric vehicle battery recycling startup he founded in 2017.

He now runs Redwood Materials, a Nevada-based electric vehicle battery recycling startup he founded in 2017. It has since expanded to making battery materials from recovered metals. In 2025, Redwood also began building and selling battery storage systems for data centers..

name: Walter Kortschak
about: Walter Kortschak is an investor who joined growth equity firm Summit Partners in 1989. He spent 26 years there as an active partner.
At Summit, some of his biggest tech bets and buyouts were E-Tek Dynamics (a 40x return) and networking company Xylan (127x).
Kortschak now invests solo, with early bets on such outfits as The Trade Desk and Robinhood.
At first, Kortschak wanted to be a software engineer, but got into venture investing after business school at UCLA.
He also owns 2,800 acres in Kauai, Hawaii, including a ranch where Jurassic Park was filmed.

name: Alexander Knauf
about: Alexander Knauf is an heir to one of the world's leading producers of building materials and systems, Knauf Gips KG.
Based in Iphofen, Germany, the company employs more than 35,000 people around the world and has annual revenue of over $11 billion.
Its product line includes plasterboards, cement boards and insulating materials. Alexander has served as managing director since 2012.
Knauf Gips dates to 1932, when brothers and mining engineers Alfons and Karl Knauf obtained rights to gypsum deposits in Schengen, Germany.
Their original gypsum factory, on the Moselle River in the border region of Luxembourg, Germany and France, is still the company's production nucleus.
did_you_know_facts: Alexander began his professional career with an apprenticeship at Deutsche Bank before joining Knauf Gips.
The family's Knauf Museum, on the premises of a historical inn built in 1688 on Iphofen's market square, houses a renowned collection or ancient relief art.

name: Sam Pollock
about: Sam Pollock is the CEO of Brookfield Infrastructure, a spinoff of Toronto-based Brookfield which invests in industries like utilities and data storage.
Pollock has worked for Brookfield since 1994 in several senior roles, including leading its private equity business.
Brookfield raised $30 billion for its fifth flagship infrastructure fund in 2023, the largest such fund ever raised by an investment firm.
Brookfield Infrastructure Partners' publicly-traded stock has generated a 14% annualized return since inception in 2008.

name: Viren Doshi
about: Viren Doshi draws his wealth from a minority stake in Waaree Energies, India's largest manufacturer of solar panels by capacity.
Mumbai-based Waaree Energies listed on the Indian bourses in October 2024 at a 70% premium to its IPO price.
The listing made him and his three brothers instant billionaires.
The company has five solar module manufacturing plants in India.
Doshi is a director on the company's board and oversees engineering, procurement and construction.
did_you_know_facts: The company was originally founded in 1990 as a manufacturer of thermal and pressure gauges used in industrial boilers.

name: Charlotte Colket Weber
about: Campbell Soup Co. heir Charlotte Colket Weber served on the company's board from 1990 until 2014.
Her billionaire cousin, Mary Alice Dorrance Malone, is still a director. Her other billionaire cousin, Bennett Dorrance, stepped down from the board in 2022.
Their grandfather, John T. Dorrance, invented the condensed soup formula that turned the company into a global soup giant.
Weber is a devoted equestrian and owns the Live Oak Stud Farm, a 4,500-acre horse farm and commercial cattle operation near Ocala, Florida.
She is also an avid collector of Chinese art, a passion that reportedly began when her uncle gave her a rare porcelain K'ang-hsi frog in the 1970s.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Paris

did_you_know_facts: Weber is a trustee at New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art and provided funding for the Charlotte C. Weber Galleries for the Arts of Ancient China.
Weber races horses through her organization Live Oak Plantation.

name: Radik Shaimiev
about: Radik Shaimiev made his fortune as a co-owner of the TAIF Group, a large regional holding company with assets in the Republic of Tatarstan.
He and his cofounders bought up most of TAIF's assets during Russia's privatization era in the mid 1990s.
In 2021, TAIF merged with petrochemical company Sibur. He and other TAIF shareholders got 15% of Sibur in exchange.
His father, Mintimer Shaimiev, was Tatarstan's first president and his brother, Airat Shaimiev, is a fellow billionaire.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Kazan Institute of Civil Engineering

did_you_know_facts: TAIF was a sponsor of football club Rubin Kazan, which won the Russian Football Premier League In 2008 and 2009.
An avid race car driver, he won a European competition called Autocross in 2003.

name: Chen Yuantai
about: Chen Yuantai is secretary of the party committee at Contemporary Amperex Technology.
Contemporary Amperex Technology, also known as CATL, is a battery supplier to the EV industry.
CATL is headquartered in the southeastern China city of Ningde.

name: Shao Qinxiang
about: Shao Qinxiang chairs Zhejiang Garden Bio-chemical High-tech, a supplier of pharmaceuticals and animal nutrition products.
Shao is the controlling shareholder of parent Garden Group, which was founded in 2000.
Garden Group was founded as a candle factory and then a garment manufacturer. It has since diversified into pharmaceuticals, energy and other fields.

name: Yin Yee Lee
about: Lee Yin Yee is the founder and chairman of Xinyi Glass Holdings.
Xinyi Glass produces glass products for the automobile, construction and household good industries.
Early in his career, Lee was involved in auto-parts trading.

name: Huang Xu
about: Huang Xu is a director of Fuzhou Rockchip Electronics, a China semiconductor supplier.

name: John Oyler
about: John Oyler is the CEO, cofounder and chairman of global oncology company BeOne Medicines. He owns nearly 5% of the publicly traded company.
BeOne Medicines, which was formerly called BeiGene, was founded in 2010 as a research and development firm. It went public on the Nasdaq in 2016 and listed in Hong Kong two years later.
Before he cofounded BeOne, Oyler helped start and then sell two companies in the U.S. and China.
He sold Telephia, a consumer telecom research firm he founded in 1997, to The Nielsen Co. for $449 million in 2007.
Oyler's next success came with drug discovery outsourcing company BioDuro, which he founded in 2005 and sold to PPD Inc. for $77 million in 2010.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Master of Business Administration, Stanford Graduate School of Business

did_you_know_facts: BeOne has more than 40 drugs in its pipeline. Its blood cancer drug Brukinsa did more than $2 billion in U.S. sales in 2024.

name: Lai Guogui & family
about: Lai chairs Zhejiang CFMOTO Power, a supplier of transportation vehicles including motorcycles and all-terrain vehicles.
Lai founded CFMOTO in 1989; the business is headquartered in Hangzhou.

name: Chow Shing Yuk
about: Chow Shing Yuk is cofounder, chairman and CEO of logistics and delivery giant Lalatech Holdings.
It has a presence in 400 cities across Asia, Latin America and EMEA, operating under the brand Huolala in mainland China and as Lalamove outside the region.
Chow was a professional poker player and a consultant at Bain & Co. before he started Lalatech in 2013, betting his poker winnings of $3.8 million.
Lalatech disrupted the logistics industry by digitizing the booking of freight and trucking services, which were traditionally done through call centers.
Lalatech last filed for a Hong Kong IPO in October 2025 after failed attempts since 2023.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Economics, Chinese University of Hong Kong; Bachelor of Arts/Economics, Stanford University

did_you_know_facts: Lalatech's star-studded roster of investors includes HongShan, Hillhouse and Tencent.
Chow was born in mainland China but grew up in Hong Kong, where he lived in a dilapidated wooden house.
Chow scored straight A's in his high school exams and earned a scholarship to study in the U.S.

name: Banwari Lal Bawri
about: Banwari Lal Bawri is the joint managing director of privately held Macleods Pharmaceuticals, which is among India's top 10 pharma firms.
Bawri, whose family owned a pharmacy in Jaipur, set up Macleods Pharmaceuticals with two siblings in 1986 to make anti-TB medicines.
Macleods produces generics for a range of diseases including asthma, osteoporosis and diabetes.
Bawri's older brother Girdharilal Bawri is chairman, while younger brother, Rajendra Agarwal, is managing director.
did_you_know_facts: Bawri and his two brothers live together with their families in the same building in Mumbai.
The company was named after John Macleod, a Scottish doctor and author of medical textbooks.

name: Lai Shixian
about: Lai Shixian is an executive director and chief financial officer at Anta Sports, China's largest sportswear company.
Lai is the brother-in-law of fellow Anta billionaires and executive directors Ding Shizhong and Ding Shijia.
Lai holds an EMBA from the China Europe International Business School.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: EMBA, China Europe International Business School

name: Anna Maria Braun
about: Anna Maria Braun is CEO of medical device company B. Braun Melsungen, which began in 1839 as a small pharmacy that sold herbal remedies.
A sixth-generation family member, she owns 10% of the company and also serves as president of its Asian/Pacific operations.
Her father, Ludwig Georg Braun, took the reins in 1977, when the company had just $24 million in annual sales (now around $8 billion).
Today, with more than 64,000 employees globally, B. Braun manufactures products ranging from infusion and injection solutions to surgical instruments.
did_you_know_facts: Anna Maria is a member of the board of Dr. August Oetker KG, a $9 billion (sales) conglomerate with interests in food, beverages, financial services and hotels.
Her billionaire brother Otto Philipp Braun was responsible for the company's Iberian Peninsula and Latin American regions before stepping down in February 2017.

name: Johanna Braun
about: Johanna Braun owns 10% of the medical device company B. Braun Melsungen, which began in 1839 as a small pharmacy that sold herbal remedies.
Her father, Ludwig Georg Braun, took the reins in 1977, when the company had just $24 million in annual sales (now around $8 billion).
A sixth-generation family member, Johanna is the youngest daughter of Ludwig Georg. Her sister, Anna Maria, is CEO of B. Braun.
Today, with more than 64,000 employees globally, B. Braun manufactures products ranging from infusion and injection solutions to surgical instruments
did_you_know_facts: Johanna Braun is a member of the board of the B. Braun Foundation, which works in education, science and public health in the field of human medicine.
B. Braun has been operating in Africa for more than 60 years, and now has subsidiaries in Zambia, Algeria, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Kenya.

name: Karl Friedrich Braun
about: Karl Friedrich Braun owns 10% of the medical device company B. Braun Melsungen, which began in 1839 as a small pharmacy that sold herbal remedies.
His father, Ludwig Georg Braun, took the reins in 1977, when the company had just $24 million in annual sales (now around $8 billion).
A sixth-generation family member, Karl Friedrich is one of three sons of Ludwig Georg.His sister Anna Maria is CEO of B. Braun.
Today, with more than 64,000 employees globally, B. Braun manufactures products ranging from infusion and injection solutions to surgical instruments.
did_you_know_facts: Karl Friedrich is a doctor at Berlin's Charit?, with a focus on traumatology.
B. Braun has been operating in Africa for more than 60 years, and now has subsidiaries in Zambia, Algeria, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Kenya.

name: Maike Oberwelland-Height
about: Oberwelland-Height's great-grandfather, August Storck founded the business in the Westphalia town of Werther in 1903.
At the time, sweets typically were sold unpackaged and without branding. He packaged his individually and gave them snappy names.
Today, Storck employs over 7,000 people, sells products in more than 100 countries and generates almost $3 billion in estimated annual revenue.
Her brother, Axel, became the fourth generation of his family to lead the company after their father, Klaus, retired on Storck's 100th anniversary in 2003.

name: Wang Linxiang
about: Wang Linxiang is the cofounder of Inner Mongolia Erdos Resources, a supplier of cashmere.
Wang resigned as chairman in 2014. The position was succeeded by his daughter Wang Zhen.
Inner Mongolia Erdos Resources listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2001.

name: James France
about: James France inherited an estimated 36% of Nascar, the stock-car racing business founded in 1948 by his father, William France Sr.
He has sat on Nascar's board of directors since 2000.
Viewership is down, but the business remains afloat due to 7-year TV deals with Fox, NBC, Amazon Prime Video, and TNT, worth $7.7 billion in rights, that began in 2025.
France also serves as chairman of Nascar's sister company, International Speedway Corp, which operates 13 racetracks.
After Sprint's contracted ended in December 2016, Nascar signed a $20 million per year deal with Monster Energy that commenced in 2017.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Florida Southern College

did_you_know_facts: His niece Lesa France Kennedy is International Speedway's CEO, while nephew Brian France is Nascar's chief executive.
France raced in the U.S. Motorcycle Grand Prix in the late 1960s, raced dirt track competitions for nearly five years and has raced karts on both dirt and asphalt.

name: José Coppel Luken
about: José Coppel and his four brothers own Grupo Coppel, a Mexican conglomerate with over 1,700 department stores.
Their father and grandfather founded the first shop in 1941 selling radios and watches. Today, the stores sell everything from clothing to electronics.
The stores are known for providing credit to customers, allowing them to finance their purchases over multiple payments.
The group expanded into the banking sector with BanCoppel in 2007.
did_you_know_facts: The brothers also have two sisters who don't have active roles in the business.

name: Alberto Coppel Luken
about: Alberto Coppel Luken and his four brothers own the family's retailing and banking giant, Grupo Coppel.
Their father and grandfather started the company in 1941 as a small shop in Sinaloa called "El Regalo."
Coppel is the CEO and chairman of GC1 Holding; owner of sake producer Nami and software company ClickBalance.
GC1 Holding's venture capital arm had investments in Spotify, Uber and Pinterest before they went public.
Coppel, who was previously director of stores in the Coppel Group, is a civil engineer with a degree from the Monterrey Institute of Technology.
did_you_know_facts: He is the vice president of Pronatura Noroeste, a conservation organization in Northwest Mexico.

name: Gretel Packer
about: Gretel Packer is the elder sister of fellow billionaire James Packer.
She became a billionaire after James split their family estate 10 years after the 2005 death of their father, media mogul Kerry Packer.
Famously low-profile, she was the driving force behind the establishment of the $160 million National Philanthropic Fund in 2014.
The fund is supported by the Packer Family Foundation, which she chairs.
She is also an arts patron, who sits on the boards of the Art Gallery of New South Wales and the Sydney Theatre Company.

name: Lim Kok Thay
about: Lim Kok Thay is the executive chairman of Genting, a casino and resorts conglomerate with a global footprint. In February 2025, he stepped down as CEO, a role he had held for almost two decades.
In 2022, Lim's troubled cruise operator Genting Hong Kong, which was hit hard by the pandemic, filed a winding up petition. Lim stepped down as chairman.
Lim's assets include Empire Resorts, the parent company of loss-making Resorts World Catskills.
A long-drawn family feud over the empire's wealth and businesses, which include a palm-oil unit, was finally resolved in 2020.

As part of an ongoing S$6.8 billion ($5 billion) expansion, Genting Singapore is revamping its Resorts World Sentosa, which will include two new hotels, a four-storey retail and dining podium, and a waterfront promenade.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of London; Harvard Business School

did_you_know_facts: His late father, Lim Goh Tong, arrived in Malaysia from Fujian, China, in 1937 at age 19 with barely anything to his name.
Lim also has a stake in Singapore-listed luxury yatch company, Grand Banks Yatchs.

name: Li Qiong
about: Li Qiong is the former wife of online gaming tycoon Zhou Yahui.
Zhou is chairman of Beijing Kunlun Tech, one of China's most successful online game companies.
Li became a billionaire through her divorce settlement.
She holds a degree from Tianjin University.

name: Wang Wenmo
about: Wang Wenmois a non-executive director at Anta Sports, China's largest sportswear company.
Wang is a cousin of fellow Anta billionaires and directors Ding Shizhong and Ding Shijia.
Wang oversees Anta's apparel operations.

name: Amnon Shashua
about: Amnon Shashua is the cofounder and CEO of autonomous vehicle technology firm Mobileye.
A computer science professor at Hebrew University, Shashua launched the company in 1999 with fellow billionaire Ziv Aviram.
The pair took Mobileye public in 2014, then sold it to Intel in 2017 at a $15.3 billion valuation.
Aviram and Shashua also co-CEOs of Or-Cam, which makes portable, artificial vision devices for visually impaired people. They founded it in 2010.

name: Li Zhigang
about: Li Zhigang chairs Wuhan DR Laser Technology, a supplier of laser equipment.
Wuhan DR Laser listed at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2019.
Customers include LONGi, Canadian Solar, Tongwei Co. and Trina Solar -- leading Chinese solar cell and panel makers.

name: Aloke Lohia
about: Indian-born plastics tycoon, Aloke Lohia, is the younger brother of Sri Prakash Lohia, one of Indonesia's richest.
The Bangkok resident runs the $15.4 billion (2024 revenue) Indorama Ventures, the world's largest producer of PET resins by capacity.
To expand its global footprint, Indorama has been on an acquisition spree with a string of acquisitions since 2014.
Bullish on his country of origin, Lohia has a joint venture with India's Dhunseri Petrochem to make polyester resin in eastern India.
The family holding outfit Indorama Resources is investing $1.5 billion globally to expand recycling capacity and sustainable production.
did_you_know_facts: Lohia has lunch with his wife, Suchitra, who works with him nearly every day.
In 2022, the company completed the acquisition of Oxiteno, a Brazilian producer of surfactants, for $1.3 billion.
Indorama Ventures has recycled 50 billion PET beverage bottles since 2011 and aims to recycle 50 billion annually by 2025.
In February 2025, Indorama Ventures agreed to buy a 25% stake in Indian packaging company EPL from private equity giant Blackstone for 19 billion rupees.

name: Gary Michelson
about: Gary Michelson is a retired orthopedic and spinal surgeon who holds some 340 U.S. patents for orthopedic and spinal surgery instruments.
He became a billionaire in 2005 when he reached a $1.35 billion settlement with medical device giant Medtronic after years of litigation.
Michelson, who signed the Giving Pledge in 2016, has founded several nonprofits to give to medical research, animal welfare and education.

personal_stats.label: Education

did_you_know_facts: George Steinbrenner died during a one-year repeal of the federal estate tax, saving his kids an estimated $600 million.

name: Ivan Chrenko
about: Ivan Chrenko is Slovakia's first billionaire, who began building his real estate fortune in the early 1990s.
His company, HB Reavis, developed the first business centers in Bratislava and the top shopping mall, later sold.
In one of the earliest big post-Brexit real estate deals in London in 2016, HB Reavis sold 33 Central to Wells Fargo for a reported $400 million.
In Warsaw, it is constructing one of the tallest buildings in Europe.
He invested more than $10 million in e-commerce cloud startup Exponea, which was sold in 2022.
Chrenko served as CEO of the HB Reavis Group from 1994 to October 2013. He is now the board chairman.

name: Wang Zhenggen
about: Wang Zhenggen is a director and general manager of Suzhou Maxwell Technologies, a supplier of equipment used in the solar power industry.
Maxwell went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2018
The company holds 802 patents and has expanded into markets in Thailand, Turkey, and the United States.

name: Roland Duchatelet & family
about: Roland Duchatelet started automotive sensor company Melexis in 1989 with married couple Rudi De Winter Françoise Chombar.
Melexis and a sister company, X-Fab, are both publicly traded and jointly controlled by the two families.
Duchatelet is the founder of social-liberal political party Vivant in Belgium, which later merged with the VLD party. He was elected senator between 2007 and 2010.
did_you_know_facts: Roland Duchatelet has previoulsy invested in sports and once owned soccer teams Standard Liège (Belgium) and the Charlton Athletic (U.K.).

name: Lei Jufang
about: Lei Jufang chairs Tibet Cheezheng Tibetan Medicine, best known for its pain-relief patches and cream.
Lei discovered the business that made her a billionaire on a leisure trip to Tibet seeking peace of mind.
Lei holds an undergraduate degree from Xian Jiaotong University in vacuum physics.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Xi'an Jiaotong University

name: Fu Guangming & family
about: Fu Guangming is the chairman of Fujian Sunner Development, which supplies chicken to KFC in China.
He shares his fortune with daughter Fu Fenfang, a company director, and his wife.
Fu is a member of China's Communist Party.

name: Lai Jianfa
about: Lai Jianfa is a former director and executive vice president of express delivery firm ZTO Express; he resigned his positions in May 2022.
ZTO was founded in 2002.
ZTO's business partners include Alibaba and JD.com.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Fudan University

name: Sergey Shishkarev
about: Sergey Shishkarev is the founder Delo Group, one of Russia's largest transport and logistics companies, which he started in 1993.
Delo's core asset is DeloPorts, which owns several terminals in the Novorossiysk sea port.
In 2019, state-owned conglomerate Rosatom bought a 30% stake in Delo. Since then Shishkarev has made several mergers and acquisitions to expand the business.
Shishkarev started Delo as a logistics and port management company. It's since become a major domestic player in the transportation industry with interests in sea terminals, rail cars and ships.
In 2022 Delo acquired shipping company SASCO and a stake in Maersk's Global Ports, Russia's largest container operator.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Military Institute of Ministry of Defense of Russia

name: Lin Fanlian
about: Lin Fanlian is chairman of Order Group, whose interests include energy, real estate and finance.
Order is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Linyi in Shandong Province.
Lin Fanlian was reportedly born into a farming family in a small village of Shandong Province; he dropped out of school and worked as construction worker as a teen.

name: Madhusudan Agarwal
about: Madhusudan Agarwal, who was running Delhi-based Haldiram Foods, merged his company with his cousin's Nagpur-based Haldiram Foods International in 2023 to create Haldiram Snacks Food.
A consortium of investors led by Singapore's Temasek, acquired a 20% stake in the merged company in 2025 at an estimated valuation of $10 billion.
Agarwal is the grandson of founder Ganga Bishan Agarwal, who started selling snacks from a tiny shop in Bikaner in Rajasthan in 1937 and went on to create the popular Haldiram brand.
The business was eventually divided among the patriarch's grandsons into three separate companies, operating out of Nagpur, Delhi and Kolkata.

name: Paul Van Zuydam
about: Paul Van Zuydam is the owner and chairman of Le Creuset, a cookware company known for its colorful enameled cast-iron pots.
Van Zuydam acquired Le Creuset in 1988, quitting his job to buy the company himself after a deal he had championed for his then-employer fell through.
Le Creuset was founded in 1925 by two Belgians in Fresnoy-le-Grand, a small village in northern France.
Today, the company brings in more than $700 million in revenue and produces around 10,000 cast iron products a day in its France-based factory.
did_you_know_facts: Paul's son, Paulo Van Zuydam, is the director of the company.
Flame, a gradient red and orange color, is the original color of Le Creuset.

name: Ulrich Mommert & family
about: Ulrich Mommert took over Austrian lighting company ZKW In 1982, when it was on the brink of bankruptcy.
He refocused ZKW on lighting technology for high-end automobiles, with clients such as BMW, Mercedes, Porsche and Audi.
In 2018 Mommert sold the company to South Korean firm LG for $1.2 billion.
Mommert owns a horse racing team and a trotting track in Berlin-Mariendorf.
did_you_know_facts: He used to be an amateur horse racer, and won more than 160 races; he is believed to own around 100 horses.

name: Jitendra Mohan
about: Jitendra Mohan is cofounder and CEO of Astera Labs, an artificial intelligence-focused semiconductor networking firm.
He launched the company in 2017 with fellow billionaire Sanjay Gajendra and a third cofounder, Casey Morrison.
The trio decided to start their own company while working together at semiconductor firm Texas Instruments.
They took Astera Labs public on the Nasdaq in 2024.
Mohan and Gajendra, who serves as chief operating officer, each own an estimated 4% of Astera Labs. Morrison, who serves as chief product officer, has never had his stake disclosed.

name: Surjit Kumar Gupta
about: Surjit Kumar Gupta gets his fortune from his stake in Havells India, a company founded by his late brother-in-law, Qimat Rai Gupta.
Havells sells a range of electrical products such as fans and lights as well as consumer durables, such as air conditioners and water heaters.
Gupta used to work at the company but now has a board seat as a non-executive director.
His son, Ameet, is also a director and oversees new projects and new product roll-outs.
In 2024, Havells expanded its product range by launching built-in kitchen appliances such as cooking stoves and chimneys.

name: Helene Odfjell
about: Helene Odfjell is the largest shareholder of Odfjell Drilling, Norway's leading drilling and oil-services group.
The business was founded by her father Abraham Odfjell in 1973 during the early years of the country's oil boom.

She and her sister Marianne inherited Odfjell Drilling, while their brother Johan Odvar Odfjell took over the family's shipping operations in Jo Tankers. In 2015, Marianne exited the drilling company.
Helene Odfjell has been based in the U.K. for decades but relocated to Lugano, Switzerland in 2025.
She is a graduate of the Norwegian School of Economics (NHH) with an MBA from London Business School.
did_you_know_facts: The Odfjell fortune dates back to 1917, beginning with timber and dry-cargo transport before expanding into chemical tankers.

name: Ricardo Villela Marino
about: Ricardo Villela Marino is a member of a storied Brazilian banking dynasty.
He is grandson of Eudoro Libânio Villela, who cofounded Brazilian bank Itau in 1945; it merged with Unibanco in 2008.
Ricardo Villela Marino is a partner and vice chairman of Itaú Unibanco and chairman of the bank's Latin America Strategic Council.
His mother, Maria de Lourdes Egydio Villela, a former billionaire, transferred her shares of parent company Itausa to Ricardo and his brother Rodolfo.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Polytechnic School of the University of Sao Paulo; Master of Arts/Science, London School of Economics and Political Science; Master of Business Administration, MIT Sloan School of Management

name: Rodolfo Villela Marino
about: Rodolfo Villela Marino is a member of a storied Brazilian banking dynasty.
He is a grandson of Eudoro Libânio Villela, who cofounded Brazilian bank Itau in 1945; it merged with Unibanco in 2008.
Rodolfo Villela Marino sits on the board and serves executive vice president of Itausa, the parent of Itau Unibanco.
His mother, Maria de Lourdes Egydio Villela, a former billionaire, transferred her shares of Itausa to Rodolfo and his brother Ricardo.
He has a degree in business and a doctorate in management from the Getúlio Vargas Foundation (FGV) in São Paulo.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Business Administration, Fundacao Getulio Vargas; Master of Arts/Science, London School of Economics and Political Science; Ph.D, Fundacao Getulio Vargas

did_you_know_facts: Villela has a degree in business and a doctorate in management from the Getúlio Vargas Foundation (FGV) in São Paulo.

name: Winai Teawsomboonkij
about: Winai Teawsomboonkij founded his Thaifoods Group in 1987 with a chicken farm of 20,000 chickens.
He went on to expand into breeding pigs and producing animal feed, taking the company public in 2015.
Winai holds a majority stake with his family in Thaifoods.
It's one of the top three producers of chicken meat and live pigs in Thailand.
In 2022, the company set up a renewable energy subsidiary.

name: Dhruv Sawhney
about: Cambridge-educated engineer and Wharton grad, Dhruv Sawhney joined his uncle's floundering engineering and sugar firm and turned it around.
Eventually, he took charge of his father's sugar interests as well and merged the two businesses into Triveni Engineering and Industries.
Triveni produces sugar and liquor and also has a power transmission business. He also owns listed Triveni Turbine, which makes turbines for the power sector.
His older son Tarun runs Triveni Engineering while younger son Nikhil runs Triveni Turbine.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts/Science, The University of Cambridge; Master of Business Administration, The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: Chess buff, Sawhney was president of the All India Chess Federation for 12 years.
He lives in Dubai.

name: Koon Poh Ming
about: Koon Poh Ming is the executive vice chairman of aluminum company Press Metal while his brother Koon Poh Keong is group CEO.
They started Press Metal with their three brothers--Poh Tat, Poh Weng and Poh Kong--in the mid-1980s.
The brothers pooled $50,000 to start the aluminum-extruding company, at a time when Malaysia was in a recession.
Press Metal is Southeast Asia's largest integrated aluminum producer and competes with Rio Tinto, Russia's RUSAL and the Aluminum Corp of China.
Poh Ming and Poh Keong, the two biggest shareholders, made the list of Malaysia's richest for the first time in 2017. Poh Weng joined them in 2019.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, University of Wales

did_you_know_facts: Poh Ming launched the company with his brothers by renting a factory in Puchong, Selangor, on the west coast of peninsular Malaysia.

name: Ivan Savvidis & family
about: Ivan Savvidis, a Greek-Russian businessman, is the founder of Agrocom Group, whose assets included Russian tobacco firm Donskoy Tabak.
Savvidis sold Donskoy Tabak for $1.6 billion to Japan Tabacco in March 2018.
Seen as a Putin ally, Savvidis is a former member of the Russian parliament.
Through his Greek company Dimera, he owns a stake in soccer team FC PAOK in Thessaloniki, Greece, where he also operates a port.
He got his start as a worker at the Don State Tobacco Factory (now Donskoy Tabak) and was elected general director in 1993.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Rostov Institute of National Economy

did_you_know_facts: In 2022 Savvidis bid for the port of Alexandroupoli in northeastern Greece but in the long run the Greek government decided not to sell it.

name: Brandt Louie
about: Brandt Louie presides over grocery retailer H.Y. Louie and drug store chain London Drugs.
His Vancouver-based holding company H.Y. Louie is the third-largest private firm in British Columbia, with an estimated $4.2 billion in revenues.
His grandfather, Hok Yat Louie, immigrated to Vancouver from China in 1896 and worked as a farm laborer.
Hok Yat eventually saved enough money to open a small general store in the city's Chinatown in 1903.
Louie joined the family business in 1972 and became president in 1987.
did_you_know_facts: Prior to working for H.Y. Louie, Brandt was a chartered accountant.
Originally named the Kwong Chong Company, H.Y. Louie's first store sold seed, fertilizer and wholesale groceries.

name: Lloyd Blankfein
about: Lloyd Blankfein was chairman and CEO of financial behemoth Goldman Sachs from 2006 to 2018, when he was succeeded by David Solomon.
Before leading Goldman Sachs, he worked under then-CEO Henry Paulson as the company's president and chief operations officer from 2004 to 2006.
Blankfein first became a partner at the firm in 1988.
Blankfein grew up in the projects in Brooklyn, graduated as a valedictorian from Thomas Jefferson High School before getting history and law degrees from Harvard.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctor of Jurisprudence, Harvard University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Harvard University

did_you_know_facts: Blankfein was diagnosed with lymphoma late in 2015, and after months of chemotherapy, he said he was likely cured of the disease.

name: Christian Dreyer
about: Christian Dreyer is one of three family shareholders of Amazonen Werke, a German maker of Agricultural Machinery.
Dreyer owns about half of the Hasbergen, Germany based company, which has annual revenue of about $1 billion.
Amazonen was established in 1883 by his great-grandfather, Heinrich Dreyer, who sold his first plow in 1894 and first cultivator in 1904.
The company has paid shareholder dividends totaling of about 500 million euros since 2005.

name: Justus Dreyer
about: Justus Dreyer is one of three family shareholders of Amazonen Werke, a German maker of Agricultural Machinery.
Dreyer owns about half of the Hasbergen, Germany based company, which has annual revenue of about $1 billion.
Amazonen was established in 1883 by his great-grandfather, Heinrich Dreyer, who sold his first plow in 1894 and first cultivator in 1904.
The company has paid shareholder dividends totaling of about 500 million euros since 2005.

name: Lau Cho Kun
about: Lau Cho Kun is the largest shareholder in Hap Seng Consolidated, through holding company Gek Poh and investment arm Lei Shing Hong.
The diversified firm's interests include financial services, plantations and property.
Its plantation division is one of the largest producers of palm oil in Sabah, East Malaysia.
Hap Seng Consolidated has been operating Mercedes-Benz dealerships in Malaysia since 1969.
Privately held Hong Kong-based Lei Shing Hong runs Mercedes-Benz dealerships in Asia and Europe.
did_you_know_facts: Yaw Chee Ming, CEO of Samling Strategic, a fellow rich lister, is his son-in-law.
Lau is the nephew of Lau Gek Poh, the late founder of Gek Poh Holdings.

name: Nicole Shanahan
about: Nicole Shanahan is an attorney and entrepreneur who was married to Google cofounder Sergey Brin from 2018 to 2023.
Shanahan burst onto the national stage when Robert F. Kennedy Jr. picked her as his vice president during his 2024 presidential campaign.
Shanahan grew up in a family that relied on food stamps, and her career as a lawyer has largely been in Silicon Valley startups and nonprofits.
She owns much of her fortune to the estimated 5.3 million Google shares she got in her divorce from Brin.

She has donated a chunk of the stock to the nonprofit she heads, called the Bia-Echo Foundation, which provides grants in the areas of "longevity and equality, criminal justice reform and a healthy and livable planet."
did_you_know_facts: Shanahan's Bia-Echo Foundation had over $124 million in assets at the end of 2024.
Shanahan and Brin reportedly divorced after an alleged affair with Elon Musk that both Shanahan and Musk have denied.

name: Zhang Yin
about: Zhang Yin, also known as Cheung Yan, chairs Hong Kong-listed Nine Dragons Paper, one of Asia's largest packaging and paper producers.
Zhang's husband Liu Ming Chung, the CEO of Nine Dragons, is also a billionaire.
Her younger brother, Zhang Cheng Fei, is deputy CEO of Nine Dragons, and the third billionaire in the family.
Zhang Yin is vice chair of the Guangdong Federation of Industry and Commerce.

name: Wang Chaobin
about: Wang Chaobin chairs the Zhonglu Group, one of the largest non-government real estate owners in the central Chinese city of Zhengzhou.
Son George is heir apparent.
The Wang Chaobin Charitable Foundation in Zhengzhou provides financial support for disaster relief, cultural exchanges, education and other fields.

name: Ivan Zhao
about: Ivan Zhao is the CEO and original founder of productivity software company Notion, which was last valued at $10 billion.
Notion's software is a minimalistic competitor to Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace.
The software is popular among both business users and consumers. Zhao expects it to hit 100 million users in 2024.
Word-of-mouth growth has helped Zhao to keep Notion lean in employee count and profitable.
In turn, he has raised about $330 million at low dilution. He owns 30% of the company, Forbes estimates.
did_you_know_facts: Zhao is particular about the design and aesthetics of a space. Notion's first three offices had a no-shoes policy.
He also hand-selected every piece of furniture in Notion's San Francisco headquarters.
His favorite is the Artek Aalto Stool, designed in 1933, which retails for about $400.

name: Igor Tulchinsky
about: Igor Tulchinsky is founder and CEO of WorldQuant, a quantitative investment firm with $17 billion in assets under management.
WorldQuant specializes in stastical arbitrage and other quantitative-driven trading techniques.
Born in Belarus, Tulchinsky immigrated to the U.S. as a child and began his career at AT&T Bell Laboratories.
He spent two years at Interactive Brokers before moving to Millennium, the hedge fund run by billionaire investor Izzy Englander.
He founded WorldQuant in 2007 as a subadvisor of Millennium, and it still manages $7 billion on behalf of the larger hedge fund.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts, The University of Texas at Austin; Master of Business Administration, The Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: His nonprofit WorldQuant University provides free online masters-level courses in financial engineering.
He has written three books about investing and financial markets.
quote: We're getting to a place where you can kind of quant everything.

name: Vladimir Leshchikov
about: Vladimir Leschikov owns more than 370 acres of land near the border between Moscow and New Moscow territory.
That's where his shopping complex Slavyanskiy Mir (Slavic world), with a space of about 3 million square feet, is located.
Leschikov was born in Dagestan in the North Caucasus region.
Leschikov and his older brother moved to Moscow bought rooms in the center of Moscow to lease them.
Moscow's government plans to build two metro stations on Leschikov's land.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, Dagestan State University

name: Guy Laliberté
about: In 1984, Guy Lalibert?, a former street performer, cofounded Cirque du Soleil, which would become one of the world's biggest entertainment companies.
His empire began with a show, funded by $1 million from the Canadian government, put on for the 450th anniversary of the discovery of Canada.
The celebration went global, and the shows have been performed for more than 180 million spectators across more than 450 cities in 60 countries.
He sold much of his 90% stake to U.S. private equity firm TPG Capital and Chinese investment group Fosun in 2015, but kept 10% of the company.
In 2020, Lalibert? sold his remaining 10% stake in Cirque du Soleil to Quebec pension fund CDPQ.
He founded Lune Rouge in 2017, which develops and invests in projects in arts, technology and entertainment.
did_you_know_facts: Guy Lalibert? was the first private Canadian citizen to explore space as part of a 2009 mission to raise awareness on water issues facing humankind.
In 2007, Lalibert? founded One Drop, a foundation devoted to making clean and safe water accessible around the world.
In November 2019, Laliberte was briefly held in custody in Tahiti for growing cannabis at his French Polynesian residence.

name: Steven Sarowitz
about: Steven Sarowitz founded online payroll firm Paylocity in 1997 after working at several other payroll firms.
Sarowitz still sits on Paylocity's board but is no longer involved with its operations.
He now focuses on philanthropy and has contributed nearly $250 million to his family foundation Julian Grace and spiritually-inspired foundation Wayfarer.
Sarowitz also cofounded and co-chairs Wayfarer Studios, which produces films with inspirational messages. "It Ends with Us" starred Blake Lively and was one of the top-grossing films of 2024.
After legal controversy erupted around "It Ends with Us," Sarowitz closed his Wayfarer Foundation in 2025 to focus on private giving.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign

did_you_know_facts: Sarowitz is a convert to the Baha'i Faith.

name: Motilal Oswal
about: Chartered accountant Motilal Oswal cofounded and chairs Mumbai-headquartered Motilal Oswal Financial Services.
From a small stock brooking outfit, Oswal and his billionaire business partner Raamdeo Agrawal, grew it into a financial services firm.
In their early days, the duo would walk a mile from the Bombay Stock Exchange to the nearest payphone to take orders from clients.
Son of a grain trader, Oswal was the first person in his family to go to college.
In 2023, he and cofounder Agrawal pledged to donate 5% of their respective holdings in Motilal Oswal for philanthropic causes such as education, health and rural upliftment.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Chartered Accountant, Institute of Chartered Accountants of India

did_you_know_facts: When he was starting out, Oswal was turned down by 60 accountancy firms because he couldn't speak English fluently.
Oswal is the chairman of the Jain International Trade Organisation.

name: Stephen Rubin & family
about: Stephen Rubin is the chairman of Pentland Group, one of the U.K.'s largest sports apparel companies.
Rubin owns an estimated 49% of Pentland, which owns brands like Speedo and Berghaus and a majority stake in publicly-traded JD Sports Fashion.
His parents started Pentland in 1932 as a shoe wholesaler. In 1959, he joined the firm and a decade later, after his father died, took over as chair.
The company paid $77,500 for a 55% stake in Reebok USA in 1981, then offloaded the investment for $770 million in 1991.
did_you_know_facts: In 2002, Rubin was named an Officer of the British Empire for his services to business and to human rights. It is one of the highest honors in the country.

name: Melchior Oeri
about: Melchior Oeri is a descendant of Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche, founder of Switzerland-based pharma behemoth Roche.
Oeri joined the Forbes billionaires ranks in 2026 after his billionaire mother, Maja, split her inheritance of Roche shares with him.
The family pooled their shares together in 1948, which has allowed them to continue voting control of Roche, the maker of blockbuster drugs like Tamiflu and Valium.
His mother split away from the family voting block in 2019, which disclosed her individual holdings and diminished the family's majority control of the company.

name: Chey Ki-won
about: Chey Ki-won is the younger sister of SK Group chairman Chey Tae-Won.
Her stake in SK Holdings accounts for most of her wealth.
She chairs SK's Happiness Sharing Foundation, which conducts educational programs for poor children and sets up and runs social enterprises.
did_you_know_facts: Since 2006, her Happiness Sharing Foundation has provided more than 40 million lunch boxes to starving children.
The foundation also invests in social entrepreneurship.

name: Ingrid Wu
about: Ingrid Wu is a co-founder of Shenzhen-headquartered electronics manufacturer AAC Technologies; her husband Benjamin Pan is the CEO.
Wu is a non-executive director and not involved in the day-to-day operations, according to the company.
AAC went public at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2005.
Wu is a graduate of the Changzhou School of Public Health in China.
Wu is the mother of Kelvin Pan, an executive vice president at AAC and the company's chief innovation officer.

name: Xu Yingtong
about: Xu Yingtong is the chairman and CEO of Chinese energy storage firm Sigenergy Technology.
The Shanghai-based company went public in Hong Kong in April 2026, raising $562 million.
It makes energy storage hardware used by businesses and homes. The company's top markets include Australia, Vietnam, Germany and Sweden.
Prior to founding Sigenergy in 2022, Xu spent over two decades working for Chinese telecommunications giant Huawei.
His wife Yang Ting is a non-executive director at Sigenergy.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Nanjing University of Science and Technology; Master of Business Administration, Fudan University

name: Tian Ming
about: Tian Ming chairs Hefei Meiya Optoelectronic Technology, a supplier of detection equipment.
Tian made his fortune initially from optical sorters for grains and tea leaves, profiting from China's agricultural boom.
Hefei Meiya went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2014.

name: Gerald Schwartz
about: Gerald Schwartz is the founder and chairman of Onex, one of Canada's largest private equity firms, which he ran for 39 years before stepping down in May 2023.
He got his start working with buyout legends Jerome Kohlberg, Henry Kravis and George Roberts at Bear Stearns in the 1970s.
The Americans left to start KKR in 1976; Schwartz went home to Canada and cofounded the media company CanWest in 1977.
In 1984 he started Onex, which now has $50 billion in assets under management and offices in London, Toronto and the U.S.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard University

did_you_know_facts: Schwartz also serves as a director of bookstore chain Indigo Books & Music, which his wife, Heather Reisman, founded and runs.
The couple's HESEG Foundation provides full academic scholarships and living expenses to lone soldiers who travel to Israel to serve in the Israel Defense Forces.

name: Anita Zucker
about: Anita Zucker is chair and CEO of Charleston, South Carolina-based InterTech Group, a private, family-owned chemicals manufacturer.
InterTech was founded in 1982 by Zucker's late husband, Jerry, who died of a brain tumor in 2008 at age 58.
The company, which has estimated revenues of roughly $3 billion, also owns an aerospace engineering firm and extensive commercial real estate.
Jerry Zucker, an immigrant from Israel, was a prolific inventor who was granted numerous patents.

forbes_list.list: The Richest Person In Every State (2019)

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts, University of North Florida; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Florida

did_you_know_facts: The daughter of a holocaust survivor, Zucker is a former elementary school teacher.

name: Thomas Bruch
about: Thomas Bruch's retail fortune derives from Globus, with roots dating back to 1828.
Globus operates hypermarkets and DIY stores in Germany, Luxembourg, Russia and Czech Republic. It employs almost 47,000 worldwide.
Bruch owns about 38% of the holding company; the rest is distributed among other family members, a family foundation and a charitable foundation.
The charitable Globus Stiftung -- of which Bruch's wife, Graciela, is CEO -- holds about 26% and will receive Bruch's stake after his death.
In 2020, his son Matthias took over as managing director of Globus, representing the sixth generation of the family to run the firm. He also holds 10% of the company.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of Saarland

did_you_know_facts: Globus Stiftung has supported more than 400 social projects with $10.5 million. It focuses on supporting youth in their transition from school to work.
Globus offers its 18,500 employees the chance to invest in and profit from the performance of the company though silent partnerships.
Globus offers its employees the chance to invest in and profit from the performance of the company though silent partnerships.
quote: Globus should live as a company that is constantly renewing itself from within.

name: Wu Xiaoge
about: Wu Xiaoge was formerly a director and vice president at CNGR Advanced Material, a supplier of battery materials, before stepping down in 2023.
Her husband Deng Weimin is chairman and also a billionaire.
The company went public in Shenzhen in 2020 and five years later dual-listed in Hong Kong.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Tsinghua University

name: Farkhad Akhmedov
about: Farkhad Akhmedov got his start selling Russian sables at the London commodity exchange.
In 1987 he founded Tansley Trading, which supplied equipment to Russian gas producers.
Six years later, he became a minority shareholder in Nortgas, an oil and gas company in Siberia.
In 1998, he bought out the 44% stake of another investor, Bechtel Energy, and became chairman of Nortgas.
He sold that stake in 2012 for $1.4 billion.
In 2016, a U.K. High Court judge ordered Akhmedov to pay his ex-wife 454 million British pounds, but he refused. In 2021 Tatiana accepted cash and art and the divorce dispute was settled.
He is under EU and U.K. sanctions since April 2022. In June 2022 his yacht Luna, valued at about $500 million, was frozen in Germany; In September 2023 the EU removed its sanctions against Akhmedov.
did_you_know_facts: Akhmedov invested $55 million in a pomegranate juice factory in his native Azerbaijan, where his father worked during the Soviet era.
Akhmedov's helicopter was seized and sold for around $5.7 million on behalf of his ex-wife in December 2018 after the London court granted his assets be frozen.

name: Anand Burman
about: Anand Burman is the fifth-generation scion of the storied Burman clan.
After more than a decade, he stepped down as chairman of the family company Dabur, India's fourth-largest consumer goods company, in 2019.
His wealth is mostly derived from his stake in the Delhi-headquartered company, known for its hair oil, fruit juices and health supplements.
He also has stakes in Kolkata-based dry-cell battery maker Eveready and New Delhi-based financial services group Religare.
His cousin, Mohit, is now chairman of Dabur, while his son, Aditya, is a director.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Ph.D, University of Kansas; Master of Science, University of Kansas

did_you_know_facts: Burman has invested in his personal capacity in home healthcare services, cancer diagnostics and life sciences.
Burman enjoys playing the saxophone.
Falguni Nayar, the billionaire founder of beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa, sits on Dabur's board.

name: Song Fei
about: Song Fei chairs Shanghai-listed Yantai Eddie Precision Machinery, which produces and sells construction machinery.
Song shares his fortune with his wife Feng Xiaohong and son Song Yuxuan.
Song's sister-in-law Feng Xiaohua and his brother Song Ou are Eddie executives.

name: Wang Dong
about: Wang Dong is a cofounder of Chinese semiconductor maker Moore Threads Technology.
The company went public in Shanghai in December 2025, raising $1.1 billion.
Wang worked as a sales director for Nvidia for over a decade before cofounding Moore Threads in 2020.
The company's Chairman and CEO, Zhang Jianzhong, is also a billionaire.

name: Pacal Vanhalst & family
about: Pascal Vanhalst's fortune stems from Thermote & Vanhalst, also known as TVH Parts, a supplier of spare parts for industrial and agricultural equipment.
He inherited part of the company from his father, Paul Vanhalst, who started TVH with his friend Paul Thermote to repair and resell forklift trucks.
He's reinvested a significant part of his wealth by acquiring European companies through his investment vehicle Quva Invest.

name: R.G. Chandramogan
about: College dropout R.G. Chandramogan started a tiny venture in 1970 to make ice cream.
Today, his listed Hatsun Agro Product, which he chairs, is one of India's largest private dairy companies by sales.
Every day Hatsun gets milk directly from more than 400,000 farmers spread across 10,000 villages.
Hatsun also exports dairy ingredients to 42 countries.
His son, C.Sathyan, is the company's executive vice-chairman.
did_you_know_facts: Chandramogan's first ice creams were sold on pushcarts.

name: Lu Di
about: Lu Di was an early investor in Chinese drone maker DJI when it was founded in 2006.
Today the Shenzhen-headquartered business is one of the world's largest drone makers.
Lu has been called a "penny pincher" by DJI's CEO Frank Wang.

name: Phil Shawe
about: Phil Shawe is cofounder and co-CEO of translation, language services and AI company TransPerfect.
Shawe owns 99% of the firm, which generated $1.3 billion in 2025 revenue and counts Microsoft and various U.S. governmental entities as customers.
He and his one-time fiancee started the company out of an NYU dorm room in 1992; they initially split the company 50-50.
After a messy court battle, a judge ordered a public auction of the company and in 2018 approved Shawe buying her out for $770 million.
Shawe wants to reform the Delaware Court of Chancery, where the TransPerfect case happened; he's funded campaign ads and written op-eds.

name: Gloria Joseph
about: Gloria Joseph is the ex-wife of George Joseph, the billionaire founder of Los Angeles-based insurance company Mercury General Corporation.
She owns a 17% stake in Mercury, which she received when the couple divorced in 1985.
The couple married in 1946 after George served in the Air Force during World War II.
When George founded Mercury in 1961, Gloria was named vice president, and she served in that role until the couple divorced. She continued to sit on the company's board until 2003.

name: John Phillips
about: John Phillips is an angel investor who made an early bet on Shopify, a Canadian e-commerce software company.
He and his wife Catherine Phillips together own an estimated 2% of Shopify.
John served on Shopify's board of directors from 2010 to 2023.
The couple has invested in a slew of other early-stage companies that are lesser known, like Virtual Marine Technology and Sequence Bio.
John previously spent 25 years as a corporate lawyer, including as general counsel at telecom firm Clearnet Communications.
The Phillips' Northpine Foundation has donated hundreds of millions to organizations focused on climate, refugees and formerly incarcerated individuals.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Law Degree, University of Toronto; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Toronto (Trinity College)

name: Catherine Phillips
about: Catherine Phillips and her husband John Phillips were early investors in Canadian e-commerce firm Shopify.
The couple owns an estimated 2% of Shopify combined.
Now retired, Catherine worked as a psychologist specializing in helping cancer patients deal with stress.
She leads support groups and in 2013 published a book titled, Calm Your Mind, Warm Your Heart.
Her husband served on Shopify's board of directors from 2010 to 2023.
The Phillips' Northpine Foundation has donated hundreds of millions to organizations focused on climate, refugees and formerly incarcerated individuals.

name: Shyam Bhartia
about: Shyam Bhartia chairs the Jubilant Bhartia group with interests in energy, fast food, pharma and auto distribution.
The Jubilant group has four listed companies.
Jubilant Foodworks has hundreds of Domino's Pizza outlets across India.
Jubilant Life Sciences was split into two companies, Jubilant Pharmova and Jubilant Ingrevia. The latter was listed in March 2021.
His younger brother Hari, who is also a billionaire, is co-chairman.
did_you_know_facts: Bhartia's wife Shobhana has her separate media company, which publishes the Hindustan Times daily newspaper.
In February 2025, a police case was filed against him for allleged rape and criminal intiimdation of an aspiring Bollywood actress. Bhartia denied the allegations.
In December 2024, the Bhartia brothers acquired a 40% stake in Coca Cola's Indian bottler for 125 billion rupees ($1.5 billion).
In December 2024, the Bhartia brothers acquired a 40% stake in Coca Cola's Indian bottler for 125 billion rupees ($1.5 billion).

name: Hari Bhartia
about: Hari Bhartia co-chairs the Jubilant Bhartia group with interests in energy, fast food, pharma and auto distribution.
The Jubilant group includes four listed companies.
Jubilant Foodworks has hundreds of Domino's Pizza outlets across India.
Jubilant Life Sciences was split into two companies, Jubilant Pharmova and Jubilant Ingrevia. The latter was listed in March 2021.
His older brother Shyam, who is also a billionaire, is co-chairman.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology Delhi

did_you_know_facts: Hari has a chemical engineering degree from the Indian Institute of Technology, Delhi.
In December 2024, the Bhartia brothers acquired a 40% stake in Coca Cola's Indian bottler for 125 billion rupees ($1.5 billion).

name: Will Adderley
about: Will Adderley is the son of Bill and Jean Adderley, the founders of UK home furnishings retailer Dunelm.
The business was founded after the couple set up a market stall in Leicester, U.K. in 1979.
They took the company public on the London Stock Exchange in 2006.
The Adderleys own 43% of the business and Will serves as the company's deputy chairman.
There are now almost 200 Dunelm stores across the U.K.

name: Horst Wortmann & family
about: Horst Wortmann, Germany's shoe billionaire, established Wortmann KG in 1967, in the city of Detmold in North Rhine-Westphalia.
Considered the European market leader in women's fashionable shoes, its brands include Tamaris, Marco Tozzi, Caprice, Jana and s.Oliver.
Nephew Jens Beining developed "Agenda 2020" to prepare the company for future challenges, with special focus on online retail.
Heir apparent Beining, who assumed operational management control in 2016, owns 10% of the company.
The company, operating under the umbrella of Wortmann Schuh-Holding KG, has about 1,100 direct employees and an overall workforce of 30,000.
did_you_know_facts: Wortmann runs a real estate business on the side.

name: Chang Chung-Hsing
about: Chang Chung-Hsing is the chairman of Taichung-based Apex Dynamics.
He founded the company in 1987 as a maker of robotic arms, and has built it into one of the world's largest suppliers of high-precision gearboxes.
Apex listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in 2022.
It also owns Millennium Vee Hotel Taichung, operated in partnership with Singapore's Millennium Hotels & Resorts, one of the oldest international-brand hotels in central Taiwan.

name: Ludwig Theodor Braun
about: Ludwig Theodor Braun owns 10% of the medical device company B. Braun Melsungen, which began in 1839 as a small pharmacy that sold herbal remedies.
His father, Ludwig Georg Braun, took the reins in 1977, when the company had just $24 million in annual sales (now around $8 billion).
A sixth-generation family member, Ludwig Theodor is the youngest son of Ludwig Georg. His sister Anna Maria is CEO of B. Braun.
Today, with more than 64,000 employees globally, B. Braun manufactures products ranging from infusion and injection solutions to surgical instruments.
did_you_know_facts: B. Braun has been operating in Africa for more than 60 years, and now has subsidiaries in Zambia, Algeria, South Africa, Zimbabwe and Kenya.

name: Jahm Najafi
about: Jahm Najafi is a Phoenix-based private equity investor whose portfolio includes direct-to-consumer brands and minority stakes in sports teams.
An Iranian by birth, Najfi's family immigrated to the U.S. when he was a child.
After a stint on Wall Street and his older brother's Pivotal Group real estate firm, Najafi launched his own investment firm, Najafi Companies.
His most lucrative acquisition was a $100 million bet in 2003 on domain registrar Network Solutions, which he sold for $800 million in 2007.
Najafi acquired 10% of the Phoenix Suns in 2009 and rolled forward his stake when a group led by billionaire Mat Ishbia bought the team for $4 billion in 2023.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Economics, University of California Berkeley

did_you_know_facts: Najafi previously owned a minority stake in British Formula 1 team McLaren Racing, which he sold in a 2025 deal that valued McLaren at $4.5 billion.
Najafi's MSP Sports Capital has invested in several European football clubs alongside billionaire Blackstone executive David Blitzer.

name: Francisco Jose Riberas Mera
about: Francisco José Riberas Mera and his billionaire brother Juan Maria each own about 25% of listed autoparts firm Gestamp Automocion.
Francisco is executive chairman of Gestamp Automocion, which listed on the Madrid stock exchange in 2017.
The company operates in more than 20 countries and has 44,000 employees.
The brothers are the largest shareholders of Madrid-listed car components maker CIE Automotive.
did_you_know_facts: Francisco and Juan Maria's late father, Francisco Riberas Pampliega, founded a small steel trading company in 1958.

name: Diego Della Valle
about: Diego Della Valle took the small shoe factory his grandfather started and turned it into global shoe- and purse-maker Tod's S.p.A.
Della Valle, who is chairman, and his brother Andrea together own the majority of the company.
In 2024, the brothers teamed up with private equity firm L Catterton and LVMH to take Tod's private at a $1.5 billion valuation.
The brothers also hold stakes in Italian scooter-maker Piaggio and multimedia conglomerate RCS MediaGroup.
The brothers owned Florence-based soccer team AC Fiorentina from 2002 to 2019, when they sold it to fellow billionaire Rocco Commisso.
