He cofounded Italy's first private rail operator, Ntv-Italo, in 2006 and sold it 12 years later to an American investment firm for $2.2 billion.
did_you_know_facts: He has spearheaded a campaign to renovate the crumbling Roman Colosseum, committing millions of euros from Tod's for the project.
In 2017, Della Valle opened a new factory in the central Italian town of Arquata del Tronto as part of recovery efforts after a devastating 2016 earthquake.

name: Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani
about: Faisal Bin Qassim Al Thani is the chairman of Al Faisal Holding, one of Qatar's biggest conglomerates, which he founded in 1964.
It owns more than 20 hotels around the world, including the St. Regis in Washington, D.C. and Miami, and the W Hotel in London.
Al Faisal Holding also has a majority stake in publicly-traded Aamal, which owns real estate in Qatar and sells medical supplies and pharmaceuticals.
Al Thani started selling car parts in Doha at age 16. He became the sole distributor of Bridgestone tires in the 1960s.
did_you_know_facts: Al Thani is a distant relative of the Qatari royal family.
A museum in Doha houses his collection of more than 15,000 artifacts, including antique cars, ancient coins and Islamic art.

name: David Mindus
about: David Mindus is the founder and CEO of Swedish commercial real estate company Sagax AB.
Mindus and two partners began buying warehouses and light industrial properties around Stockholm in 2000 after identifying the sector as undervalued.
Mindus owns more than 17 percent of Sagax, which listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange in 2004.
Its portfolio consists of more than 37 million square feet across 673 properties.
Before Sagax, Mindus worked at GE Capital, where he helped found the company's Swedish real estate investment business.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Stockholm University

name: Li Weiwei
about: Li Weiwei is chairman and general manager of Sanqi Interactive Entertainment Network Technology Group.
Li holds an executive MBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business in Beijing.
Li worked for several IT companies including Sina before he founded Sanqi in 2011.

name: Samuel Chen
about: Samuel Chen was an early investor in Zoom and served as its director until 2018. He made the investment after playing football with founder Eric Yuan in San Francisco.
He also invested in a range of biotech and electronics companies in Taiwan through his Digital Mobile Venture and sits on the board of many.
His majority-owned cancer drug research firm Polaris Group went public in Taiwan in 2022.
Chen earned his initial wealth by trading ink.

name: Chen Xuehua
about: Chen Xuahua is founder and chairman of Zhejiang Huayou Cobalt, one of China's largest mining-related businesses.
Huayou is a supplier of cobalt and nickel products to the world's EV industry.
Huayou agreed in 2022 to join with Ford and Vale Indonesia in a nickel chemicals extraction project in Indonesia.

name: Nir Zuk
about: Nir Zuk founded the $91 billion (market cap) cyber security firm Palo Alto Networks in 2005.
He currently serves as the Chief Technology Officer of the company.
An Israeli native, Zuk and his family moved from California back to Israel during the pandemic.

Zuk started working with computers during his mandatory stint in the Israeli military in the early 90s, which led to his first job in cybersecurity working for Check Point, now a Palo Alto competitor.

name: Chen Yung-tai
about: Chen Yung-tai got his start selling office clocks in 1965. He later expanded into office equipment, furniture and electronics.
Today his listed Aurora Corp., chaired by wife Yuan Hui-Hua since 2018, sells electronics in over 1,500 locations in Taiwan and mainland China.
Aurora also owns real estate, including a 38-story tower, in Shanghai's Lujiazui financial district.
Chen studied economics in college. That department is now part of National Taipei University.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, National Chung Hsing University

did_you_know_facts: Chen was born into a well-off family but worked as a small trader and street merchant after his father died in his youth.
Chen founded the Aurora Museum in Shanghai, known for its Buddhist sculptures and jade.

name: Juan Maria Riberas Mera
about: Juan María Riberas Mera and his billionaire brother Francisco each own a bit more than 25% of listed autoparts firm Gestamp Automocion.
Their late father, Francisco Riberas Pampliega, founded a small steel trading company in 1958.
Over two decades the company became one of Spain's largest steel companies and diversified into auto parts in 1997.
Juan Maria, known as Jon, started at the company in a junior management position in 1992 after getting law and business degrees.

name: Othman Benjelloun & family
about: Othman Benjelloun is CEO of BMCE Bank of Africa, which has assets of more than $12 billion and a presence across West, Central and East Africa.
His father was a shareholder in RMA, a Moroccan insurance company; Benjelloun built it into a leading insurer.
Through his holding company FinanceCom, he has a stake in the Moroccan arm of French telecom firm Orange.
He inaugurated in 2014 a $500 million plan to build the 55-story Mohammed VI Tower in Rabat, one of the tallest buildings in Africa.
FinanceCom, which largely operates as O Capital Group, is part of a project to develop a multibillion-dollar tech city in Tangiers that is expected to host 200 Chinese companies.
did_you_know_facts: He co-owns Ranch Adarouch, one of the biggest cattle breeders in Africa.
Benjelloun and his wife received the David Rockefeller Bridging Leadership Award for building schools in rural Morocco in 2016.

name: Leonid Simanovsky
about: Leonid Simanovsky holds just under 2% of the gas company Novatek.
He met fellow billionaire Leonid Mikhelson, his partner in Novatek, in the late 1980s, when he worked at Mikhelson's construction company.
Since 2003 Simanovsky has been a State Duma deputy and a deputy chairman of the Duma's budget and tax committee.
Simanovsky was among the 336 members of Russia's parliament sanctioned by the EU on February 23.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Economics, Kuibyshev Planning Institute

did_you_know_facts: Simanovsky began his career as a fitter in a factory producing space rocket technology.
Simanovsky worked for Mikhail Khodorkovsky's Yukos many years ago.

name: Kenny Troutt
about: Kenny Troutt founded long-distance phone company Excel Communications in 1988 and took the company public in 1996.
In 1998, Troutt sold Excel Communications to Teleglobe in a $3.5 billion deal and reinvested the profits in stocks, bonds and horses.
An avid horse racing fan, Troutt owns WinStar Farm in Versailles, Kentucky, breeder of Thoroughbreds including a Kentucky Derby winner.
The son of a single mother who worked as a bartender, Troutt grew up in public housing in Mount Vernon, IL.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Southern Illinois University

did_you_know_facts: For years, Troutt sponsored his sons' nationally competitive basketball teams, providing jerseys, equipment and even rides on his private jet to tournaments.

name: Kokuei Yuan
about: Kokuei Yuan is a director of Hong Kong-based crypto exchange Bullish.
Bullish was founded in 2020 and went public on the New York Stock Exchange in August 2025.
Yuan owns a 25% stake in the company. Bullish cofounder Brendan Blumer owns 28% and is also a billionaire.
Yuan previously served as executive chairman of block.one, a digital asset investment firm that Blumer cofounded in 2016. Bullish was majority-owned by block.one until 2024.
Yuan, who studied economics and studio art at Tufts University, worked as an investment banker earlier in his career.

name: Torsten Toeller
about: Torsten Toeller encountered pet supply superstores during a visit to the U.S. in the late 1980s and decided the concept deserved a try in his native Germany.
When he opened his first Fressnapf store in 1990, in Erkelenz, customers were initially unimpressed with his selection and prices.
Toeller doubled down by selling his car to raise cash, invested in more inventory and went for broke with aggressive discounts.
The gamble paid off, and in 1992 Fressnapf Tiernahrungs GmbH began opening franchise stores, paving the way for rapid growth.
Today, with over 20,000 people working in approximately 2,600 stores in 15 countries, it is Europe's largest pet-focused chain.
did_you_know_facts: Toeller has invested in an office building project called Mercator One in Duisburg, close to the company's headquarters in Krefeld.
He is a car fanatic and former sailor.

name: Li Haiyan
about: Li Haiyan is a co-founder of hot-pot chain Haidilao International Holdings; she has been a company supervisor since 2009.
Li is the wife of billionaire Shi Yonghong, a director at Haidilao and chairman of hotpot seasonings supplier Yihai International.
Haidilao co-founders Li, Zhang Yong, Shu Ping and Shi Yonghong funded their first restaurant with personal savings in 1994.
Haidilao today is one of the most popular restaurant chains in China and has about 1,300 locations worldwide.

name: Wang Qiangxiang
about: Wang Qiangxiang chairs CoCreation Grass, or CCGrass, a leading global supplier of artificial grass.
CCGrass is used for athletic and landscape purposes.
The company supplies to sports organizations such as FIFA, FIH and World Rugby.
CCGrass was founded by Wang Qiangxiang and his brother Wang Qiangzhong in 2004 in Nanjing city.

name: Min-Liang Tan
about: Min-Liang Tan gave up a law career in Singapore to start gaming devices company Razer in 2005.

Its early backers include IDG-Accel, Temasek Holdings, Intel and Li Ka-shing's Horizon Ventures. The company has acquired a huge global following and sold millions of gaming laptops, mice, fitness bands and tablets.
Tan listed the firm in Hong Kong in 2017, raising $529 million.
Tan expanded Razer in Asia with the acquisition of Malaysian virtual currency firm MOL Global, and tie-ups with SingTel, Lazada and China's JD.com.
In 2022, Tan and Lim Kaling, who is a founding investor and director at Razer, took the company private in a deal that valued it at $3.2 billion.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Laws, National University of Singapore

did_you_know_facts: Diehard Razer fans sport tattoos of the brand's logo.
Razer acquired THX, the audio company founded by Star Wars director George Lucas, in 2016 and Android smartphone maker Nextbit in 2017.
Tan is a key investor in Lucence, a Singapore- and Palo Alto-headquartered biotech company that provides cancer blood tests, founded by his older Min-Han in 2016.
quote: I don't fire somebody because their design sucks, but I've fired some who have no passion for the product.

name: Edward Netylko
about: Edward Netylko founded Pulse Pharmaceutical company in 1996, which became one of Russia's top three drug distributors in 2015.
In 2023, Pulse won first place in a rating of Russian pharmaceutical distributors.
The company delivers drugs to more than 60,000 pharmacies and medical institutions in Russia and employs 3,000 people.
In the1990s Netylko worked at NPO Lavochkin, a Russian aerospace company; NPO was a key contractor of the Soviet space program, Venera, which ran from 1961 to 1984.
Netylko was born in Orsha, Belarus.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Moscow Aviation University

name: Xia Xinde
about: Xia Xinde chairs Guangzhou Great Power Energy and Technology, a supplier of lithium-ion batteries.
Guangzhou Great Power went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2015.
Founded in 2001, Great Power is headquartered in the southern Chinese city of Guangzhou.

name: Rolly van Rappard
about: Rolly van Rappard is a cofounder and non-executive chair of the board of Luxembourg-based private equity firm CVC Capital Partners.
The firm went public on the Amsterdam stock exchange in 2024 and van Rappard owns a nearly 7% stake.
CVC was established in 1981 as the European operations of Citicorp Venture Capital, the VC arm of Citigroup.
In 1993, van Rappard and seven cofounders acquired the business and spun it out as CVC. They raised their first fund in 1996 and shifted their focus to private equity.
CVC's investments include Petco, Swiss watchmaker Breitling and Spanish soccer league La Liga.
did_you_know_facts: Van Rappard has a family office in Luxembourg that invests in public and private firms in Europe.
Van Rappard co-owns a yacht, the 184-foot Blue II, with CVC cofounder Steve Koltes.

name: Chen Shiliang
about: Chen Shiliang is the chairman of Tongkun Group, a supplier of textile products under the "Golden Cock" brand.
Tongkun Group's predecessor business was a county-owned chemical fiber plant.
Chen took charge of the small collective chemical fiber business in 1991 when it went into bankruptcy.
Chen and other managers were granted shares of Tongkun in 1999 when the company reorganized.

name: Jeffrey Gundlach
about: Jeffrey Gundlach is the cofounder of mutual fund company, DoubleLine Capital, which manages $91 billion in assets.
The bond-trader extraordinaire is known for his bold calls and correctly predicted the housing crash in 2007.
He previously helped build the fixed-income business at TCW, before he was fired in 2009.
He is an avid modern art collector and owns works by artists including Warhol, Mondrian and de Kooning.
did_you_know_facts: Gundlach used to be the drummer in a punk rock band.
He became interested in the investments business after learning of the earnings potential in an episode of "Lifestyles of the Rich and Famous."

name: Yoshiaki Yoshida
about: Yoshiaki Yoshida is the founder of Japanese beauty brand DHC. He started the company in 1972 to provide translation services.
In 1980, he started the cosmetics business using organic olives. In 1983, he got into the mail order segment. It also sells nutritional supplements and health foods.
The privately held company sells both through retail stores and online.
In 2023, Yoshida sold his company to Japanese leasing giant Orix, which valued it at ¥300 billion.
did_you_know_facts: DHC stands for Daigaku Honyaku Center.
Yoshida is a supporter of conservative political causes and has his own TV production company providing online and broadcast content.
DHC sources its olive oil from organic olive groves in Spain.

name: Wang Xicheng & family
about: Wang Xicheng's fortune rose following the July 2016 IPO of his tire manufacturer, Shandong Linglong Tire, on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.
Its predecessor was a state-owned tire factory founded in 1975 in Shandong Province.
The company was on the verge of collapse in 1987 when Wang was named leader and shifted its focus to pricier tires.
The company is now a supplier to GM, Ford, Tata, Fiat and Hyundai.

name: Juan Domingo Beckmann Legorreta & family
about: Juan Domingo Beckmann Legorreta inherited a nearly 51% stake in tequila firm Becle S.A.B., maker of Jose Cuervo, from his father Juan Francisco Beckmann.
The company went public on the Mexican Stock Exchange in 2017 under Juan Domingo's leadership. He remains CEO.
Founded in 1758, Becle has remained family-owned for over 250 years.
His sister Karen Beckmann Legorreta inherited nearly 36% of the company from their father and is a billionaire as well.
did_you_know_facts: La Rojeña, built by the Cuervo family in 1812, is Latin America's oldest active distillery.
In 2022, Beckmann partnered with comedian Kevin Hart to create the Gran Coramino tequila brand.

name: Henry Engelhardt
about: The son of a Chicago meatpacker, Henry Engelhardt aspired to be a journalist before turning to entrepreneurship.
His insurance company Admiral Group, founded in 1993, offers car and home insurance and created the UK's first insurance price comparison website.
Based in Cardiff, Wales, Admiral also has operations in Spain, France, Italy and the U.S.
Its American brands include Elephant Auto Insurance and Compare.com.
Engelhardt stepped down as CEO in May 2016, but he's still a part-time employee, mentoring senior managers and taking part in MBA recruitment.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Michigan; Master of Business Administration, INSEAD

did_you_know_facts: Admiral's Ministry of Fun organizes events for its employees, such as dress-up days, rock band contests, and surfing trips.
He and his wife, Diane, started Moondance Foundation to support causes in Wales, education, healthcare, poverty, and the arts.
quote: How wealthy we've become is a recipe of three parts luck, one part smarts and one part determination.

name: Zhao Jianhui
about: Zhao jianhui is the chairman of Epiworld International, a maker of silicon carbide (SiC) epitaxial wafers used in power devices for sectors such as EV, renewable energy and AI.
It is the world's largest SiC epitaxial foundry by both revenue and sales volume, accounting for roughly a third of the global market in 2024.
Zhang founded the company in 2011 and took it public on the Hong Kong stock exchange in March 2026.
Zhang has over 35 years of research experience and is the first IEEE Fellow selected based on their contributions to SiC technologies.
He serves as chair professor at Xiamen University in China and worked with Rutgers University in the U.S.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Ph.D, Carnegie Mellon University; Bachelor of Science, Xiamen University

name: Ramesh Kunhikannan
about: Ramesh Kunhikannan is the founder and managing director of electronics manufacturer Kaynes Technology, headquartered in Mysore, a city in southern India.
Kaynes specialises in assembling printed circuit boards and has eight factories in India.
Kaynes supplies to clients across the globe in the auto, aerospace and medical industries.
An electrical engineer, Kunhikannan founded Kaynes in 1989 and took it public in 2022.
His wife Savitha Ramesh is chairman of the board.
did_you_know_facts: In December 2024, Kaynes acquired a 54% stake in Austria-based Sensonic which provides fiber-optics integrated with artificial intelligence to monitor railway infra.

name: Cai Jianyong
about: Cai Jianyong chairs China nickel supplier Lygend Resources & Technology, headquartered on the coast of the East China Sea.
He founded the company in 2009, after nearly a decade in the commodities trading business.
Lygend trades and produces nickel products, essential for stainless steel and electric vehicle batteries.
Lygend went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in November 2022, raising money to expand its operations in Indonesia, home to much of the world's nickel resources.
Cai graduated from the Shanghai Institute of Building Materials Industry.

name: Kishin RK
about: Kishin RK is among Singapore's leading developers with his Royal Holdings/RB Capital property empire, which he owns and runs together with his father Raj Kumar.
He's been on a dealmaking spree after a 2011 family settlement between his father and uncle Asok Kumar Hiranandani, who's also a billionaire.
Prize holdings include the 442-room Holiday Inn Express at Clarke Quay, Holiday Inn Little India and the hotel Intercontinental Singapore Robertson Quay.
He bought the Porcelain Hotel in Singapore's Chinatown, which was refurbished and reopened in 2023 as the 134-room Hotel 1900.
In 2025, they set up their RB Family Office in Abu Dhabi to tap investment opportunities in the Middle East.
did_you_know_facts: Kishin's RB Food Group owns a portfolio of brands, such as members' club 1880, cocktail bar Employees Only, Roia restaurant and cloud kitchen company TiffinLabs.
The name RB is derived from the erstwhile Royal Brothers, a 77-year-old property group with roots in textile trading.

name: Raj Kumar
about: Raj Kumar is among Singapore's leading landlords with his Royal Holdings/RB Capital property empire, owned and run together with his son Kishin RK.
After a 2011 family settlement between him and his younger sibling Asok Kumar Hiranandani, also a billionaire, he has been on a deal-making spree.
Prize holdings include the 442-room Holiday Inn Express at Clarke Quay, Holiday Inn Little India and the hotel Intercontinental Singapore Robertson Quay.
He bought the Porcelain Hotel in Singapore's Chinatown, which was refurbished and reopened in 2023 as the 134-room Hotel 1900.
In 2025, they set up their RB Family Office in Abu Dhabi to tap investment opportunities in the Middle East.
did_you_know_facts: The name RB is derived from the erstwhile Royal Brothers, a 77-year-old property group with roots in textile trading.
Son Kishin's RB Food Group owns a portfolio of brands, such as members' club 1880, cocktail bar Employees Only, Roia restaurant and cloud kitchen company TiffinLabs.
quote: When you've done hundreds of deals you develop an instinct. That becomes your Midas touch.

name: Vladimir Krupchak
about: Vladimir Krupchak's fortune stems from his stake in Arkhangelsk Pulp and Paper Mill (APPM), Russia's largest producer of cardboard and one of its biggest makers of market pulp.
Prior to 2022 Krupchak controlled the Russian and Ukrainian assets of Austria's Pulp Mill Holding.
In the 2000s he was involved in a corporate battle with billionaire Oleg Deripaska for control of APPM.
Krupchak is a former member of the State Duma of Russia, the country's parliament.
did_you_know_facts: His wife is a stakeholder of Titan Group, a leading company in Russia's sawn timber market.

name: William Fisher
about: William Fisher is one of the heirs to the Gap retail fortune. He sits on Gap's board alongside his brother Robert.
Known as "Bill," he was founder and president of the International Division for Gap Inc. and expanded the company into Canada, Japan and Europe.
He is CEO of Manzanita Capital, a London-based private equity firm he founded in 2001.
Bill's parents Doris and Don (d. 2009) founded retailer Gap in San Francisco in 1969.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Princeton University; Master of Business Administration, Stanford University

name: Alan Miller & family
about: Alan Miller founded Universal Health Services, a chain of hospitals and other health providers, in 1979.
The company has more than 400 facilities across the US and UK and brings in over $14 billion in annual revenue.
Miller stepped down as CEO in 2021 and his son Marc Miller now runs the company.
Miller remains the executive chairman of UHS' board of directors.
He is also the CEO of Universal Health Realty Trust, which invests in medical buildings.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Economics, College of William & Mary; Master of Business Administration, The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania

name: George Yancopoulos
about: George Yancopoulos is the chief scientific officer of biotech firm Regeneron.
He received his M.D. and Ph.D. from Columbia University and became a professor of biology by age 28.
Regeneron was cofounded by now-billionaire Leonard Schleifer in 1988. Yancopoulos joined the next year.
Yancopoulos led the invention of eleven FDA-approved drugs and a technology platform designed to invent more.
Yancopoulos owns about 1% of Regeneron stock.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Ph.D, Columbia University; Medical Doctor, Columbia University

did_you_know_facts: Yancopoulos was a finalist in the Westinghouse Science Talent Search in 1976. Today, it is called the Regeneron Science Talent Search and sponsored by his company.
quote: I think we do discovery differently and better. And I think part of it is we've really learned how to brainstorm and think inventively in a group.

name: Dmitry Alexeyev
about: Dmitry Alexeyev is a cofounder of DNS Retail, the largest consumer electronics retailer in Russia, which he started with fellow billionaire Yuri Karptsov.
The duo established its first store in 1998 and didn't open a second one until 2005.
Today DNS Retail has more than 2,700 stores and 39,000 employees.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Far Eastern State Technical University

did_you_know_facts: DNS stands for Digital Network Systems.

name: Manoj Upadhyay
about: Manoj Upadhyay is chairman of Gurgaon-based solar energy company Acme Solar Holdings, which develops and operates solar, wind and solar-wind hybrid power projects across India.
The company made a weak debut on the Indian bourses in November 2024, listing at a 13% discount to the issue price.
He founded ACME in 2003 to offer energy management solutions for mobile phone towers and pivoted to solar in 2008.
He is developing green energy projects in India, Oman and the U.S.

name: Jose Llorens Torra
about: José Llorens Torra founded EPSA Internacional, a subcontractor for mining and public-use projects, which grew into the core of his family holding, Llotor S.L.
He owns 62% of Llotor, with his five children holding the rest; the group controls nearly 100 companies in dozens of countries, and has more than 2.2 billion euros in assets.
Llotor has a real estate portfolio worth 770 million euros, with properties in Spain, Florida, Georgia and Ireland.
Llorens is among Spain's largest landowners, with at least 3,000 hectares, and is one of the top private beneficiaries of EU agricultural subsidies.
His group is developing Casmar, a 1 billion-euro logistics megaproject in Seseña (Toledo), expected to create 12,000 jobs.

name: Brad Keywell
about: Brad Keywell cofounded Groupon with Eric Lefkofsky and Andrew Mason in 2008.
Together with Lefkofsky, Keywell went on to launch VC firm Lightbank. The two men have been early investors in each others' ventures.
Keywell stepped back from Lightbank in early 2021, just before the firm announced it raised a $180 million fund.
In 2014, he founded predictive analytics company Uptake; in 2018, he launched immersive art organization WNDR Museum.
Keywell and his wife filed for divorce in December 2021, which may result in each of them owning an 11.7% stake in Tempus after the divorce is finalized.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Michigan; Doctor of Jurisprudence, University of Michigan

name: Teo Swee Ann
about: Teo Swee Ann is the founder and CEO of Shanghai-listed semiconductor firm Espressif Systems.
Teo has a master's degree and a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering from the National University of Singapore.
Teo worked with U.S. chipmakers Transilica and Marvell Technology Group and China's Montage Technology before founding his own firm in 2008.
The company's flagship ESP32 chips now power goods such as speakers, wearable devices and home appliances.
In 2019, Espressif sold 25% of its shares in an IPO that valued the company at $716 million.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, École Nationale Supérieure des Arts Décoratifs

did_you_know_facts: One of Teo's hobbies is Chinese chess, known as Go. He was the president of the National University of Singapore's Go club during his undergraduate years.

name: Vladimir Yevtushenkov
about: Vladimir Yevtushenkov is a cofounder of AFK Sistema, which has investments in Russia's largest cellular operator MTS, online retailer Ozon and healthcare chain Medsi.
Yevtushenkov was hit by sanctions in April 2022 and transferred 10% of his stake in AFK Sistema to his son; Forbes still credits him with his remaining 49% stake in the company.
In 2014, AFK Sistema was accused of illegally acquiring a controlling stake in oil firm Bashneft. The shares were returned and sold to state-owned Rosneft.
In 2023 the company, through its Cosmos Hotel Group, acquired ten Radisson and Park Inn hotels for just 200 million euros from Norway's Wenaas Hotel Russia, which left the Russian market.
AFK Sistema was founded in 1993.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Mendeleyev Chemical Engin; Master of Economics, Moscow State University

quote: Any state will always find a way to put you in your place.

name: Marc Lipschultz
about: Marc Lipschultz is a cofounder and co-CEO of Blue Owl, an investment firm specializing in private credit with $250 billion in assets under management.
Lipschultz spent more than 20 years at private equity giant KKR and was its head of energy and infrastructure investments when he left in 2016.
He cofounded Owl Rock Capital in 2016 with Doug Ostrover and Craig Packer, which merged with Dyal Capital to form Blue Owl in 2021.
Lipschultz was promoted from president to co-CEO of Blue Owl alongside Ostrover in May 2023.

name: Sanjay Agarwal
about: Sanjay Agarwal is managing director and CEO of the Jaipur-headquartered AU Small Finance Bank.
It serves retail customers as well as small and medium businesses
The chartered accountant set up a finance company in 1996 and converted it into a bank in 2017.
The bank has more than 1,000 branches across India and over four million customers.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Chartered Accountant, Institute of Chartered Accountants of India

name: Ye Xiaoping
about: Ye Xiaoping is the chairman of Hangzhou Tigermed Consulting, one of China's largest contract research organizations in the pharmaceutical industry.
Ye holds an EMBA from Peking University and a Ph.D. from Oxford University.
Ye was an executive at Swiss pharmaceutical giant Roche before becoming an entrepreneur.
Tigermed was founded in 2004.

name: Saroj Rani Gupta
about: Saroj Rani Gupta cofounded APL Apollo Tubes in 1986 with her late husband S.K. Gupta. It was initially called Bihar Tubes.
Delhi-based APL Apollo Tubes is a leading producer of a range of widely used, branded steel products.
Her son, Sanjay Gupta, runs the company as managing director.

name: Yi Dasheng
about: Yi Dasheng chairs Hunan Fortune Group, whose business interests include property development, auto-related services and trade.
Yi worked in a government office in the southern Chinese city of Yueyang before taking the plunge as an entrepreneur.
He made his early fortune in auto repair.

name: Andrew Tisch
about: Andrew Tisch's father Laurence (d. 2003) started Loews Corporation with his brother Bob (d. 2005) as a New Jersey hotel venture in 1946.
Andrew co-chairs Loews with his cousin Jonathan. His brother James is CEO.
Loews is active in insurance, drilling rigs, natural gas pipelines and hotels.
Andrew's mother Wilma is also a billionaire, as are his cousins Laurie and Steven.
The Tisch family donated funds to support NYU's Tisch School of the Arts and its Tisch Hospital at Langone Medical Center.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Cornell University; Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School

name: Andrew Tan
about: Andrew Tan is the chairman of Alliance Global, a holding company with interests in food and beverage, gaming, hospitality and real estate.
The son of a factory worker, Tan built his fortune developing large apartment complexes around Manila.
Alliance Global runs Emperador, the world's largest brandy company by sales volume.
Tan's son Kevin is chief executive of Alliance Global and chief strategy officer of property developer Megaworld.
Megaworld is investing 350 billion pesos ($6.3 billion) from 2023 to 2028 to build townships across the Philippines.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of the East

did_you_know_facts: Tan's father splurged on a bottle of brandy at Tan's graduation from the University of the East in 1974; that was Tan's first time trying brandy.

name: Gao Mingqing
about: Gao Mingqing is the chairman and CEO of Wanguo Gold Group, a China-based mining and processing company.

Wanguo acquired 77.78% of AXF Gold Ridge in the Solomon Islands for AUD39.215 million in April 2020 and another 20.22% for HK$732.6 million in October 2024, strengthening its global gold mining presence.
Wanguo Gold Group listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2012.

name: Olivia Holding
about: Olivia Holding is one of four sisters of Frank Holding, Chairman and CEO of First Citizens Bank, a commercial banking chain, since 2008.
Her grandfather, Robert Powell Holding, became an employee of the bank in 1918, and became president by 1935, before passing it down to her father, Lewis Holding.
Today Olivia Holding, her three sisters, and her brother Frank collectively own about 20% of the bank.

name: Tony Xu
about: Tony Xu cofounded restaurant delivery service DoorDash in 2013 and became a billionaire after its 2020 IPO. He owns 4.6% plus options.
Cofounders Andy Fang and Stanley Tang, who Xu met while they were all studying at Stanford, own about 4% each. Xu is the CEO.
DoorDash is America's largest food delivery service. It delivers meals and more from 390,000 restaurants and other merchants like CVS.
Xu was born in China and moved to the U.S. at age five. Growing up, his mom worked as a server at a Chinese restaurant.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Stanford Graduate School of Business; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of California, Berkeley

quote: DoorDash exists today to empower those like my Mom who came here with a dream to make it on their own. Fighting for the underdog is part of who I am and what we stand for as a company.

name: Aziz Akhannouch & family
about: Aziz Akhannouch is the majority owner of Akwa Group, a multibillion-dollar conglomerate founded by his father and a partner, Ahmed Wakrim, in 1932.
It has interests in petroleum, gas and chemicals through publicly-traded Afriquia Gaz and Maghreb Oxygene.
Akhannouch was appointed prime minister of Morocco in Sept 2021.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Universite de Sherbrooke

did_you_know_facts: His wife Salwa Idrissi runs her own company, which has franchises for Gap, Gucci and Ralph Lauren in Morocco.

name: S.D. Shibulal
about: Infosys cofounder S.D. Shibulal oversees his family office, Innovations Investment Management.
While he stepped down as the company's CEO in 2014, he continues to hold a small stake in the firm.
Shibulal cofounded business incubator Axilor Ventures together with former Infosys colleague Senapathy Gopalakrishnan.
He also chairs The Tamara, a boutique resort chain, which his daughter Shruti founded and runs.
did_you_know_facts: Along with wife, Kumari, he donates regularly to various causes through two family foundations.
From 1991 to 1996, Shibulal worked with Sun Microsystems in the US.

name: Hans-Ueli Rihs & family
about: Hans-Ueli Rihs is Swiss hearing aid manufacturer Sonova's second largest individual shareholder, with a 6% stake.

With fellow billionaire Beda Diethelm, Rihs and his brother Andy (d. 2018), grew Sonova into the world's largest hearing aid manufacturer, after their father Ernest (d. 1980) bought the company in 1965.
Sonova, which is publicly traded on the SIX Swiss Exchange, generated nearly $4 billion of revenue in fiscal 2024.
Rihs also owns privately-held Swiss Casinos AG, which operates four casinos in Switzerland, and Swiss soccer team BSC Young Boys.

name: D.V. Manjunatha
about: D.V.Manjunatha is the chairman and managing director of Bangalore-based solar panel and cell maker Em Vee Photovoltaic Power.
He listed the company on the Indian bourses in November 2025.
His older son Suhas is CEO while his younger son Sumanth heads business development.
He's planning a $625 million expansion to boost manufacturing capacity over the next two years.
He started Emm Vee Group in 1992 to manufacture thermal and photo voltaic products later moving into solar heaters.
did_you_know_facts: He started production of solar modules in 2007.

name: Patricia Angelini Rossi
about: Patricia Angelini Rossi inherited a stake in Grupo Empresas Angelini, the Chilean investment group headed by her brother, Roberto Angelini Rossi.
The group's largest holding is publicly-traded Antarchile, which distributes fuel, operates fishing and shipping businesses and invests in energy.
Antarchile's forestry subsidiary, Arauco, entered North America in 2012 with the purchase of Canada's Flakeboard, which manufactures wood panels.
The group was previously headed by Patricia's uncle, Anacleto Angelini, who died in 2007.

name: Shamsheer Vayalil
about: Shamsheer Vayalil is founder and chairman of Burjeel Holdings, a network of hospitals, clinics and pharmacies in the Middle East.
His net worth got a boost from the 2022 listing of Burjeel Holdings, which has used Bollywood superstar Shah Rukh Khan as its brand ambassador.
Born into a business family in Kerala state, he migrated to the Middle East after his medical studies and worked as a radiologist at a local hospital.
Backed initially by his father-in-law, Gulf retailing billionaire M.A. Yusuff Ali, Vayalil started with one hospital in Abu Dhabi in 2007. Burjeel now has 19 hospitals and 29 medical centres.
Vayalil was vice chairman of investment firm Amanat Holdings until 2022. He remains chairman of listed Response Plus Holdings, a provider of medical services.
did_you_know_facts: Egyptian national Eman Ahmed, once billed as 'the world's heaviest woman', was treated free of cost at Vayalil's Burjeel Hospital until her death in September 2017.
Vayalil has signed the Giving Pledge.
quote: We don't worry about cost. Our philosophy is that when we give, we grow.

name: Sze Man Bok
about: Sze Man Bok cofounded and chairs Hengan International, China's largest home-grown supplier of sanitary napkins.
Hengan International leads in industry sales in China over global giants such as Proctor & Gamble, Johnson & Johnson and Kimberly-Clark.
Sze's son Sze Wong Kim is a member of Hengan's board.
He cofounded the company with fellow billionaire Hui Lin Chit.

name: Shalom Meckenzie & family
about: Shalom Meckenzie is an Israeli entrepreneur who became the largest shareholder in daily fantasy and sports-betting firm Draft Kings in early 2020.
He secured an 11% stake in Draft Kings when it merged with his company, SBTech.
Meckenzie founded gambling-technology provider SBTech in 2007 and served as a director until May 2014.
DraftKings is an official daily fantasy and sports betting partner of the NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, PGA TOUR and UFC.
Meckenzie spent $11.8 million to acquire a rare CryptoPunk NFT in a June 2021 auction run by Sotheby's.

name: Dean Solon
about: Dean Solon founded Shoals Technologies in 1996; it makes electrical gear for some of the biggest U.S. solar installations.
Solon, who stepped down as CEO to join the board, owns 40% of Shoals Technologies Group, which had its IPO in January 2021.
Solon got his start at age 8 carrying his dad's toolbox to repair air conditioners; by 16 he had his own customers.
He dropped out of Purdue University and was soon designing and manufacturing automotive parts.
He is the author of two dozen patents pertaining to solar gear.
did_you_know_facts: Since the 1970s Solon has visited Disney World at least twice a year. His favorite movie is Beauty And The Beast.
Shoals makes all its solar gear at four factories in Tennessee and Alabama; the company charges more than most competitors, but its products are seen as safer, more reliable and easier to install.

name: Deniz Sahenk
about: Deniz Sahenk is the widow of Dogus Holding founder Ayhan Sahenk, who died of a heart attack in 2001. She has no active role in the conglomerate.
Dogus operates in sectors ranging from tourism, real estate and media to financial services, construction, autos and restaurants.
The family had controlled Garanti Bank, the cornerstone of its fortune, selling it last 10% to Spain's BBVA in 2017, bringing in $900 million.
Deniz's son, Ferit Sahenk, is CEO of Dogus Holding, and her daughter, Filiz Sahenk, manages its fashion and tourism components.
Both Ferit and Filiz are also billionaires.
did_you_know_facts: Dogus has been deleveraging. In 2020, it agreed to sell its 42% stake in high-end Istanbul shopping mail Istinye Park to Qatar Holding LLC.
Luxury hotel divestments include the Astir Palace and Athens Hilton in Greece, and the Capri Palace and Aldrovandi Villa Borghese in Italy.

name: Dmitry Nikolaev
about: Nikolaev controls coal producer Stroyservis.
In the early 1990s the company traded metals and pipes, then invested in coal mines.
Stroyservis is 6st coal producer in Russia. Company produces coking and thermal coke and coke chemistry.

Head office of Stroyservis is located in Kemerovo (Kuzbass, Siberia). Kuzbass or Kuznetsk Basin is one of the largest coal areas in the world. Overall coal deposits of Kuzbass are estimated at 700 billion tons.
Every year Stroyservis entered into agreement on social and economic cooperation with the administration of the Kemerovo region. Company supports local hospitals and schools.
did_you_know_facts: Stroyservis is the main sponsor of the Muay Thai Federation of Russia.
Stroyservis publishes on its website "world records" of production achievements of employees.?

name: Mohammad Abunayyan
about: Mohammad Abunayyan is the founder and chairman of ACWA Power, a Saudi power generation and water desalination firm.
He founded the company in 2004 and took it public on the Saudi stock exchange in 2021; he now owns 3.5% of the shares.
Abunayyan also chairs Vision Invest, a Saudi holding company that owns stakes in several publicly traded and privately held companies.
He also owns 8% of Abdullah Abunayyan Trading Company, a Saudi holding company that owns 50% of Vision Invest.
Vision Invest and Abunayyan Holding own shares in several Saudi publicly traded companies in wastewater treatment, logistics and flour milling.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

name: Zhou Jian
about: Zhou Jian is the founder and CEO of artificial intelligence and robotics firm UBTECH Robotics.
UBTECH Robotics investors include Tencent, one of China's largest Internet companies.
UBTECH listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in December 2023.

name: Agustín Coppel Luken
about: Agustín Coppel Luken is the chairman and CEO of Mexican retail and banking giant Grupo Coppel.
The Coppel family owns 100% of the $8 billion-plus (sales) company which their father founded in Sinaloa in 1941.
The stores, known for providing credit to customers, started allowing buyers to pay in weekly installments after World War II.
In 2024, the group announced it would invest over $700 million renovating existing retailers, reducing its carbon footprint and opening over 100 new stores.
The company was reportedly exploring a more than $1 billion IPO in 2018 but the plans were indefinitely postponed.
did_you_know_facts: Agustín and his wife are avid collectors of contemporary art.

name: Wang Xiaoshen
about: Wang is vice chairman of Jiangxi Ganfeng Lithium, a supplier of lithium products.
Earlier in his career, Wang worked for state-run China Nonferrous Metals.
Wang received an EMBA from China Europe International Business School in 2002.

name: Zeng Kaitian
about: Zeng Kaitian became a billionaire in 2015 when Sanqi Interactive Entertainment Shanghai Technology (cofounder) was bought by Wuhu Shunrong Auto Parts.
Sanqi Interactive owns web game platforms 37.com and 6711.com.
Earlier in his career, Zeng was media director at ad agency Shanghai Leo Burnett.
Zeng holds a bachelor's degree from Lanzhou University and an EMBA degree from China Europe International Business School.

name: Thaksin Shinawatra
about: Thaksin Shinawatra, the former prime minister of Thailand, had been living in self-imposed exile in Dubai for 15 years until he returned to his homeland in 2023.
On his return, he was taken into custody over previous convictions and was released six months later on a special parole after spending most of the time in hospital.
In September 2025, Thailand's Supreme Court sentenced him to prison for one year over previous convictions.Two months later the court imposed a tax demand of 17.6 billion baht on Thaksin.
His youngest daughter Paetongtarn became Thailand's prime minister in 2024 but was suspended by a Constitutional Court in July 2025 after senators filed a petition seeking her dismissal.
He owns a controlling stake in property firm SC Asset, among much else.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Eastern Kentucky University

did_you_know_facts: In 2017, the ruling military junta imposed a retrospective tax on Thaksin's sale of telecom firm Shin Corp's shares to Singapore's Temasek.
His sister Yingluck, also a former prime minister, fled the country in 2017 to escape arrest over a rice subsidy scheme. A Thai court acquitted her in 2024.
Thaksin has invested in two U.K.-based health tech startups, DNANudge and Owlstone Medical.

name: Hans Thomann
about: Hans Thomann is managing director of Thomann, one of Europe's largest music retailers with locations in Germany, France and Denmark, among others.
Thomann took over the business from his father, who started the company in 1954, and expanded it during the dot-com-era of the 1990s and 2000s.
Today Thommann employs more than 1,800 people who come from 55 countries.
The company is still headquartered in the small German town of Treppendorf.
The sole owner of the company, Thomann became involved in the business when he was 12 years of age.

name: Kwek Leng Keow
about: Kwek Leng Keow inherited a stake in Hong Leong Group from his father, Kwek Hong Leong, whose brother, Kwek Hong Png, founded the group in 1941.
Kwek Leng Keow is the brother of Kwek Leng Peck, who is the executive chairman of Singapore-listed Hong Leong Asia, which makes, trades and distributes cement and steel products.
He's the managing director of Hong Realty, a unit of Hong Leong Investment Holdings.

name: Kwek Leng Peck
about: Kwek Leng Peck is the executive chairman of Singapore-listed Hong Leong Asia, which makes, trades and distributes cement and steel products.
Singapore billionaires Kwek Leng Beng and Kwek Leng Kee are his cousins.
Kwek has a board seat in the family's Hong Leong Finance.
He inherited a stake in Hong Leong Group from his father, Kwek Hong Leong, who cofounded it with the fathers of Kwek Leng Beng and Kwek Leng Kee.
In 2020, Kwek caused a stir by resigning from the board of flagship City Developments, citing differences with the management, such as the company's investments in China.
did_you_know_facts: Kwek is a trained accountant.

name: Ke Xiping & family
about: Ke Xiping chairs Xiamen Hengxing Group, which has interests in real estate and minerals.
Raised in Fujian Province, Ke Xiping started out in business in the construction materials trade.
Ke's philanthropic donations exceed $30 million.

name: Kirill Minovalov
about: Kirill Minovalov is the founder of Bank Avangard, which he founded in 1994 with $400,000, a third of which he borrowed.
Bank Avangard grew following the 1998 Russian financial crisis; it now holds assets of about $1.5 billion.
Minovalov also started and now chairs Avangard-Agro, one of Russia's largest and most efficient agricultural manufacturers.
He also owns Avangard Malz, a leading malting company in Germany.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Moscow State University of Railway Engineering

did_you_know_facts: Minovalov founded a consulting company when he was a student in university.
Avangard-Agro's assets include more than 450,000 hectares of agricultural land in Russia.

name: Terence (Terry) Matthews
about: A dual U.K. and Canadian citizen, Terence (Terry) Matthews made his fortune with telecom firms Mitel and Newbridge Networks.
In 2018, he left his chairman role at Mitel, the company he co-founded with Michael Cowpland, after it was acquired for $2 billion.
In 1986, Matthews founded data networking business Newbridge Networks before selling it to Alcatel in 2000 for $7.1 billion.
He claims to have funded or founded more than 100 companies, many through his Ottawa-based investment firm Wesley Clover.
A resident of Canada, his U.K. property portfolio includes Celtic Manor Resort, which hosted the 2010 Ryder Cup and 2014 NATO Summit.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Wales; Doctorate, Carleton College

did_you_know_facts: Matthews was knighted by Queen Elizabeth in 2001; the honor created a diplomatic incident in Canada, which does not allow its citizens to accept foreign titles.

name: Wu Zhigang & family
about: Wu Zhigang is the founder of Shanghai-listed bakery chain Shenyang Toly Bread.
Wu was a teacher at an industrial school before founding the chain with his son Wu Xuequn in 1995; Xuequn is the company's general manager.
Wu Zhigang's wife, Sheng Yali, and sons Wu Xuedong, Wu Xuequn and Wu Xueliang hold shares in Toly.
Xuedong, Xuequn and Xueliang are board members.
Wu Zhigang retired as chairman in 2019 and was succeeded by Wu Xueliang.

name: Julia Oetker
about: Julia Oetker is an heir to the fortune of the Oetker Group, a now-divided German conglomerate with diverse holdings that included a popular range of food products.
In September of 2024, she gave up her ownership stake in Geschwister Oetker, a German holding company with brands spanning wine and spirits, chemicals and luxury hotels.
Geschwister Oetker was formed in 2021 after the eight Oetker siblings agreed to divide their $8 billion (sales) conglomerate into two separate groups.
The original business, Dr. August Oetker, began in 1891 when her great-grandfather started selling non-perishable baking powder.
Julia's brothers, Alfred and Carl Ferdinand, are co-CEOs and owners of Geschwister Oetker.
did_you_know_facts: When her father, Rudolf August, passed away in 2007, ownership of Dr. August Oetker was divided between his eight children from three marriages.

name: Richard Fairbank
about: Richard Fairbank is the chairman and CEO of Capital One Financial, a U.S. bank known for its credit cards.
He presided over the bank's creation in 1994, helping it branch out into credit card and loan services.
He owns just under 1% of the bank's shares and has sold hundreds of millions of dollars of the stock over the years.
He resides in the Washington D.C. area and is a part owner of the Washington Capitals professional ice hockey team.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Stanford Graduate School of Business; Bachelor of Arts/Economics, Stanford University

did_you_know_facts: Fairbank and his wife, Chris, have eight children.

name: Arvind Lal
about: Arvind Lal is executive chairman of diagnostics chain, Dr Lal PathLabs, in which he owns a majority stake.
The company is located in Gurgaon, a thriving township close to Delhi, and has clinical labs and collection centres across India.
The company offers a range of pathology, radiology and cardiology tests.
The business was founded by his father S.K. Lal, also a doctor, in 1949 in Delhi. Arvind Lal joined the business after studying medicine, at age 28.
His wife, Vandana Lal, who is a pathologist, is the technical director and heads clinical research services and the test development department.
did_you_know_facts: Lal is a published author whose book, 'Corporate Yogi: My Journey as a Spiritual Seeker and an Accidental Entrepreneur' was published in 2018.
Lal has an honorary brigadier's rank in the Armed Forces Medical Services.

name: Sidney Kimmel
about: Sidney Kimmel founded apparel company Jones Group more than four decades ago; it owned brands including Stuart Weitzman and Nine West.
In 2014, he sold the company for $2.2 billion to private equity firm Sycamore Partners.

His production company Sidney Kimmel Entertainment was responsible for movies including ?The Place Beyond The Pines? and ?Crazy Rich Asians,? before he sold a majority stake in 2022 to London-based investment firm Centricus.
Kimmel has donated more than $200 million to Thomas Jefferson University over the past two decades, much of which has gone to cancer research.

name: Georgios Peristeris
about: Georgios Peristeris is the chairman and CEO of GEK TERNA, an Athens. Greece-based conglomerate with operations in infrastructure, energy and construction.
Peristeris started working at TERNA in 1981 as a construction manager. He took over the top job in 1984 and took the company public on the Athens Stock Exchange in 1994.
In 1999, he merged TERNA with Athens-based GEK, combining two of the country's biggest construction companies.
Peristeris founded Terna Energy in 1997 as a subsidiary of the group and sold it to UAE-based Masdar for more than $2 billion in 2025.

name: Leopoldo Espinosa Abdalá
about: Leopoldo Espinosa Abdalá and his brother Fernando gets the bulk of their wealth from the 2016 sale of their drug manufacturer Rimsa, which it sold to Tel Aviv-based Teva Pharmaceuticals for $2.3 billion.
Leopoldo was the executive president of the privately-held Mexican company before the sale.
Their father founded the business in 1970 as a pharmaceutical distributor before expanding into manufacturing.
At the time of the sale Risma was known for a slew of patented products, most notably its fixed-dose drug combinations.
Following the sale, Teva sued Leopoldo and Fernando claiming fraud and a breach of contract. The charges were mostly dismissed; the parties eventually settled for less than $200 million.

name: Fernando Espinosa Abdalá
about: Fernando Espinosa Abdalá and his brother Leopoldo derive much of their fortune from the sale of their drug manufacturer Rimsa, which it sold to Tel Aviv-based Teva Pharmaceuticals for $2.3 billion.
Fernando was the operational president of the company before the sale in 2016.
Their father founded the business in 1970 as a pharmaceutical distributor before expanding into manufacturing.
Following the sale, Teva sued Fernando and Leopoldo claiming fraud and a breach of contract.
Most of the charges were dismissed; as for breach of contract, the parties eventually settled for less than $200 million.

name: Chaitanya Desai
about: Chaitanya Desai is the managing director of Mumbai-based Apar Industries.
The 68-year-old company manufactures conductors, electric cables, speciality oils, polymers and lubricants.
His older brother Kushal is chairman and managing director of Apar Industries.
Apar was originally called Power Cables when it was set up in 1958 by his late father Dharamsinh Desai.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, The University of Pennsylvania; Bachelor of Arts/Economics, The Wharton School at the University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: His mother Maithili Desai hails from the Mafatlal family, an old textile clan in Mumbai.

name: Kushal Desai
about: Kushal is chairman and managing director of Mumbai-based Apar Industries.
The 68-year-old company manufactures and supplies conductors, electrical cables, speciality oils, polymers and lubricants.
His younger brother Chaitanya is Apar's managing director.
Apar was originally called Power Cables when it was set up in 1958 by his late father Dharamsinh Desai.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: His mother Maithili Desai hails from the Mafatlal family, an old textile clan.

name: Lou Jing & family
about: Lou Jin is chairman and CEO of 3SBIO Inc, a biopharmaceutical company.
The company first went public on the Nasdaq in 2007 before privatizing in 2013. It listed again in Hong Kong in 2015.
The company's main research and development centers are in Shenyang, Shanghai, Shenzhen and Hangzhou.

name: Cheng Zhenghui
about: Cheng Zhenghui is the founder of APT Medical, a supplier of medical devices.
APT is headquartered in the southern Chinese business hub Shenzhen.
APT went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2021.
Cheng stepped down as chairman in April 2025.

name: Ben Ashkenazy
about: Ben Ashkenazy bought his first building at age 17, after he went to a Bronx shopping center to check out a site to open a fast food restaurant.
Then a recent high school grad, Ashkenazy realized the lease offered was below market value and decided to find a lender and buy the property instead.
Since then he's built a portfolio of stakes in more than 100 buildings via real estate firm Ashkenazy Acquisitions, which he founded and runs as CEO.
The company owns historical landmarks like Washington D.C.'s Union Station and Boston's Faneuil Hall.
Ashkenazy, who primarily invests in retail properties, is also a minority owner in New York's famed Plaza Hotel.
did_you_know_facts: In between his real estate ventures, Ashkenazy took night classes at Adelphi University but ended up six credits shy of graduating.

name: Alessandro Rosano
about: Alessandro Rosano is the founder of HeyDude, a line of comfort shoes.
He and his business partner and U.S. distributor, Daniele Guidi, sold the business to Crocs for $2.5 billion in 2022.

Before starting HeyDude, Rosano had launched a number of businesses, including a wooden watch brand called WeWood and a line of wooden clogs with springs in their heels that sold under the name Baldo.
He grew up in Pistoia, Italy, a medieval city not far from Florence, and moved to Hong Kong to run his businesses.
With comfort shoes having a moment, HeyDude sales soared from $20 million in 2018 to $581 million in 2021, when Crocs agreed to buy the brand. Revenue for the latest 12 months is now over $1 billion.
did_you_know_facts: Rosano built the HeyDude brand with no investment and minimal marketing.

name: Liang Yunchao
about: Liang Yunchao chairs Guandong By-health, one of China's largest producers of vitamins and health supplements.
Every few years he invites young leaders to join a "wildlife training" boot camp to test their stamina, he told Forbes Asia in an interview.
His favorite boot camp spots include Teklimakan Qumluqi in Xinjiang, the world's second largest desert, and Antarctica.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Sun Yat-sen University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Zhongnan University of Economics and Law

name: Thomas von Koch
about: Thomas von Koch joined publicly traded Swedish investment company EQT AB at its founding in 1994.
He ran EQT as CEO and managing partner from 2014 to 2019.
Von Koch owns 4% of EQT, which has roughly $62 billion (52 billion Euro) in assets under management.
EQT primarily invests in private equity, but has also put funds into venture capital, real estate and infrastructure.
EQT's portfolio include Nestl? Skin Health and open-source software company SUSE, which EQT acquired in 2019 for $2.5 billion.
did_you_know_facts: Thomas von Koch lives with his family in Hong Kong.

name: Allan Wong
about: Allan Wong cofounded electronic toymaker VTech Holdings, which is also one of the largest manufacturers of residential phones in the U.S.
The company is headquartered in Hong Kong with manufacturing facilities in mainland China, Malaysia and Mexico.
He is an independent non-executive director of the Bank of East Asia and deputy chairman of the board.
He's also an independent non-executive director of China-Hongkong Photo Products Holdings.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, University of Hong Kong; Master of Science, University of Wisconsin

name: Georg Haub
about: Georg Haub derives his fortune from Tengelmann Group, which began with a shop opened in Muelheim an der Ruhr in 1876. Georg holds 31.33% of the group.
Its operations include home-improvement chain OBI; clothing and non-food discounter KiK; online retailer babymarkt.de; and food production company No Meat Factor.
The group also invests in startups and is active in services (energy, plus audits and consulting), property management and real estate development.
Oldest brother Karl-Erivan and Christian had taken over as co-CEOs in 2000. In 2018, Karl-Erivan went missing while on a ski tour. In 2021, he was declared dead.
With Karl-Erivan presumed dead, Georg's younger brother, Christian, who had been overseeing Tengelmann's U.S. venture portfolio, took over as CEO.
did_you_know_facts: Erivan Haub had strong ties to Tacoma, WA, where his sons were born. He was a major contributor to UW-Tacoma, the Museum of Glass and the LeMay Automobile Museum

name: Mori Arkin
about: Mori Arkin got his start in business in 1972 helping his father run a small Israeli pharmaceutical distribution company.
The Arkins eventually moved into generic drug manufacturing, founding Agis Industries.
In 2004, they sold Agis to U.S. pharmaceutical company Perrigo for $818 million in cash and stock.
Still bullish on healthcare, he oversaw a January 2018 public offering on Nasdaq of Sol-Gel Technologies, a dermatology company. He owns over 62%.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Tel Aviv University

did_you_know_facts: His two sons are involved in the family business; his daughter is serving in the Israel Defense Forses.
Arkin is an art history buff and enjoys composing music as a hobby.

name: Fabian Hedin
about: Fabian Hedin is cofounder and chief technology officer of Swedish vibe coding startup Lovable.
Private investors valued Lovable at $6.6 billion in December 2025.
Forbes estimates that Hedin and his billionaire cofounder, Lovable CEO Anton Osika, each own 24% of the company.
Launched in November 2024, Lovable achieved $100 million in subscription revenue (on an annualized basis) in just eight months, making it the fastest-growing software startup in history.
The company uses AI to enable millions of non-coders to instantly turn their ideas into websites, apps and online side hustles.
Hedin and Osika have both pledged to give away 50% of their earnings from an eventual exit to charitable causes.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Drop Out, KTH Royal Institute of Technology

name: Anton Osika
about: Anton Osika is cofounder and CEO of Swedish vibe coding startup Lovable.
Private investors valued Lovable at $6.6 billion in December 2025.
Forbes estimates that Osika and his billionaire cofounder, Lovable chief technology officer Fabian Hedin, each own 24% of the company.
Launched in November 2024, Lovable achieved $100 million in subscription revenue (on an annualized basis) in just eight months, making it the fastest-growing software startup in history.
The company uses AI to enable millions of non-coders to instantly turn their ideas into websites, apps and online side hustles.
Osika and Hedin have both pledged to give away 50% of their earnings from an eventual exit to charitable causes.

name: Bruce Wilson
about: Bruce Wilson gets his wealth from a stake in Reece Group, Australia's biggest bathroom and plumbing supplies chain.
Reece also provides HVAC-R (heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration) to commercial and residential customers.
The company, which has more than 800 outlets across Australia, New Zealand and the U.S, celebrated its centennial in 2020.
His brothers, Alan and John, also have stakes in Reece and are billionaires.
The brothers' father, Leslie Wilson, was a plumber who joined the board of H.J. Reece, then a small listed plumbing supplies company in 1958.

name: Alan Wilson
about: Alan Wilson gets his wealth from a stake in Reece Group, Australia's biggest bathroom and plumbing supplies chain.
Reece also provides HVAC-R (heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration) to commercial and residential customers.
The company, which has more than 800 outlets across Australia, New Zealand and the U.S, celebrated its centennial in 2020.
Alan became Reece's chairman in 2008 and his son Peter became chief executive. In 2022, Alan stepped down as chairman but remains an executive director. Today Peter serves as chairman and CEO.
His brothers, John and Bruce, also have stakes in Reece and are billionaires.
did_you_know_facts: The brothers' father, Leslie Wilson, was a plumber who joined the board of H.J. Reece, then a small listed plumbing supplies company in 1958.

name: John Wilson
about: John Wilson gets his wealth from a stake in Reece Group, Australia's biggest bathroom and plumbing supplies chain.
Reece also provides HVAC-R (heating, ventilation, air conditioning and refrigeration) to commercial and residential customers.
The company, which has more than 800 outlets across Australia, New Zealand and the U.S, celebrated its centennial in 2020.
His brothers, Alan and Bruce, also have stakes in Reece and are billionaires.
The brothers' father, Leslie Wilson, was a plumber who joined the board of H.J. Reece, then a small listed plumbing supplies company in 1958.

name: Mariana Voigt Schwartz Gomes
about: Mariana Voigt Schwartz Gomes is one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, the largest manufacturer of electrical motors in Latin America.
The company was cofounded by her grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt along with the late Eggon Joao da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus, who were billionaires.
A publicly-traded multinational with factories in over ten countries, WEG has annual revenue of approximately $7 billion.
Mariana does not hold a board seat or any executive position at WEG; she works as an interior designer in Florianópolis, Brazil.

name: Eduardo Voigt Schwartz
about: Eduardo Voigt Schwartz is one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, the largest manufacturer of electrical motors in Latin America.
The company was cofounded by his grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt along with former billionaires Eggon Joao da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus (deceased).
A publicly-traded multinational with factories in over ten countries, WEG has annual revenue of approximately $7 billion.
Eduardo does not hold a board seat or any executive position at WEG; and performs and tours as a DJ.

name: Satyanarayana Chava
about: Satyanarayana Chava is the founder and CEO of Laurus Labs, a pharma and biotech company in Hyderabad, in southern India.
Chava worked in the pharma sector for two decades before starting Laurus Labs as an R&D firm in 2005.
Today, the $658 million (revenue) company supplies pharma ingredients for drugs to treat HIV, cancer, asthma and diabetes.
Chava remains passionate about research spending 25% of his time in the labs and getting involved with new products.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, Andhra University; Master of Science, Andhra University

did_you_know_facts: Chava is listed as an inventor, along with others, in 145 patents granted to his company.
In his spare time, Chava enjoys cooking Indian food and sweets.
quote: We believe we are a startup in our thinking, action and in our speed of execution.

name: Lim Chap Huat
about: Son of a rickshaw driver, Lim Chap Huat set up a small construction outfit with two partners in 1976 at age 22.
He expanded Soilbuild Group into property development and set up an REIT, eventually buying out his partners. His wife Leo Jee Lin and sons, Lim Han Feng and Lim Han Qin, work with him.
Soilbuild expanded into Myanmar in 2012 where it has multiple contracts, and into Vietnam in 2017.
In 2021, Lim, together with Blackstone Real Estate, privatized Soilbuild Business Space REIT, delisting it from the Singapore stock exchange.
In 2024, Lim and Blackstone sold their office and industrial properties in Singapore to New York-based private equity firm Warburg Pincus and Australian developer Lendlease for $1.2 billion.
did_you_know_facts: Lim taught part-time to pay fees for engineering school.
He is a firm believer in his school motto "Nothing Without Labour."
quote: If you are transparent, have no intention to cheat and treat people fairly, things will fall into place.

name: Ronald Perelman
about: Ronald Perelman is a dealmaker who built a fortune with a diverse array of holdings, from candy to cosmetics.
Perelman sold assets worth billions of dollars to pay off debt in late 2020 after the Covid-19 pandemic ravaged his businesses.
He was a longtime shareholder of cosmetics giant Revlon but lost his holdings during its 2023 bankruptcy proceedings. His daughter Debra was the firm's CEO from 2018 to 2023.
Perelman learned about business from his father. He attended board meetings with him while in elementary school.
He is a prolific art collector who has sold off much of his collection in recent years.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pennsylvania; Master of Business Administration, University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School

did_you_know_facts: Perelman's foundation pledged $65 million to Princeton in 2018 but did not follow through, prompting the school to remove his name in 2021 from a new dorm.
Perelman has eight children from five wives.
quote: As I grew, it became very clear to me that what I do, I am not doing alone. I am placed in situations with opportunities that others are not. I don't believe that that is happenstance. I believe that there is a God that has a plan for me.

name: Wang Shuifu
about: Wang Shuifu chairs equipment manufacturer Xizi Clean Energy Equipment.
Xizi Clean Energy was previously known as Hangzhou Boiler Group; Hangzhou Boiler went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2011.
Wang Shuifu started his career selling agricultural machinery in 1970.

name: Yu Qibing & family
about: Yu Qibing is a former chairman of the Kibing Group, a glass manufacturer.
Zhuzhou Kibing Group listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2011.
The Group is headquartered in Shenzhen, China.

name: Nie Tengyun & family
about: Nie Tengyun is the chairman and president of Yunda Holding, one of China's largest express delivery companies.
The company finished a backdoor listing in China in December 2016 and changed the listed company's name from Ningbo Xinhai Electric to Yunda Holding.
Nie established the company in 1999 with only 17 employees; today, it employs more than 9,000 people.

name: Evgeny (Eugene) Shvidler
about: Evgeny Shvidler, who became an American citizen in 1994, is the best friend and a partner of Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich.
His core asset is stake in Russian steelmaker Evraz.
Former Executive chairman of Highland Gold Mining, Shvidler sold his 12% stake in this company in 2020.
Shvidler was born in Moscow, Russia. He got an MBA from Fordham University in 1992 and worked for Deloitte & Touche in New York.

Shvidler, a dual British-American citizen, was sanctioned by the U.K. in March 2022. His two jets were detained by British authorities. He filed the claim in 2023 in London to challenge the sanctions.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Fordham University; Master of Science, Gubkin Institute of Petrochemicals and Natural Gas

did_you_know_facts: His 370-foot yacht, Le Grand Bleu, was a gift from Abramovich.
Shvidler was the primary funder for the rebuilding of a Jewish school in England that is now called Beit Shvidler Primary School.

name: Wang Shih-Chung
about: Wang Shih-Chung is the chairman of Taiwan's AirTAC International Group, a maker of pneumatic equipment for the automotive, electronics, medical and other sectors.
He worked at a factory upon graduating high school, and set up the company in 1988.
AirTAC is headquartered in Taipei with a strong foothold in mainland China, where it has two manufacturing sites.

name: Konstantin Goncharov & family
about: Konstantin Goncharov controls Novotrans, a closely held Russian railway, port and shipping business.
Goncharov bought Novotrans in 2015, when it was operating at a loss, and built it into a fleet of 25,000 railway cars and several wagon repair plants.
Prior to purchasing Novotrans, Goncahrov ran several logistics companies in the 2000s.
Novotrans is building a Lugaport marine terminal in the Baltic Sea with a capacity of over 24 million tons per year.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master, Magnitogorsk Mining and Metallurgical Institute

did_you_know_facts: Goncharov's wife is reportedly the daughter of Rashit Sharipov, who lost the fight against Victor Rashnikov for control over the MMK in the 1990s.

name: Yu Kai
about: Yu Kai is the chairman and CEO of Beijing-based Horizon Robotics, which develops both the software and hardware needed for self-driving cars.
The company listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in October 2024 in what was the bourse's largest IPO so far in the year, raising nearly $700 million.
Before it went public, Horizon has attracted investors including SAIC Motor, 5Y Capital, Hillhouse, HongShan and Volkswagen.
Horizon claims to be the largest Chinese provider of assisted and autonomous driving systems in the country by installation volume, counting Volkswagen, Hyundai Motor and BYD as its customers.
An AI scientist, Yu started an autonomous driving project at Baidu before cofounding Horizon Robotics in 2015 with other former Baidu employees.

name: Ronnie Screwvala
about: Ronnie Screwvala is the cofounder and chairperson of Mumbai-based edtech firm upGrad.
He set up the firm in 2015 after a successful career in the media business as the founder of the UTV group.
He sold his stake in UTV to the Walt Disney Company for over $450 million in 2012 and ran the India unit as managing director. He stepped down two years later.
Screwvala has other investments in startups such as eyewear firm Lenskart and also owns sports franchises.
Along with wife Zarina, he founded nonprofit Swades Foundation, which focuses on rural upliftment projects.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Commerce, University of Mumbai

name: Michael Steinhardt
about: A pioneer of the modern hedge fund, Michael Steinhardt closed his fund in 1995 after making a fortune in the 1990s from stellar returns.
He came out of retirement a decade later to help run WisdomTree Investments, where he is still a leading shareholder.
He retired as chairman of the board in October 2019.
WisdomTree is a publicly traded asset manager that focuses on ETF investing.
Steinhardt cofounded Birthright Israel, a foundation that provides funding for young Jewish Americans to take heritage trips to Israel.
did_you_know_facts: He maintains a zoo at his 57-acre Bedford, N.Y. estate -- complete with 90-year-old land tortoises, rare zonkies, camels and "oodles and oodles of berries."
quote: For me, running hedge funds was an art. It was something that I thought I did exceptionally well, and most of the world did not. But they didn't care the way I did.

name: Hitesh Doshi
about: Hitesh Doshi is chairman and managing director of Waaree Energies, India's largest manufacturer of solar panels by capacity.
Mumbai-based Waaree Energies was listed on the Indian bourses in October 2024 at a 70% premium to its IPO price.
The company has five solar module manufacturing plants in India.
He founded the business in 1990 as a manufacturer of thermal and pressure gauges used in industrial boilers.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Commerce, University of Mumbai

name: Bharat Desai
about: Bharat Desai founded IT consulting and outsourcing company Syntel with his wife Neerja Sethi from their apartment in Troy, Michigan in 1980.
In 2018 French IT firm Atos SE acquired Syntel for $3.4 billion in cash.
Atos sued Desai, accusing him of hiding liabilities ahead of the merger; the case was dismissed in 2023.
In its first year, Syntel generated just $30,000 in sales; before it was acquired, annual revenue grew to more than $900 million.
Desai, who was Syntel's chairman, was born in Kenya, raised in India and came to the U.S. in 1976 as a programmer for Tata.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay; Master of Business Administration, University of Michigan, Stephen M. Ross School of Business

did_you_know_facts: Desai and Sethi started the company with just $2,000.
The couple met in the U.S. while working for pioneering IT firm, Tata Consultancy Services, the company they went on to emulate.

name: Pankaj Doshi
about: Pankaj Doshi draws his wealth from a minority stake in Waaree Energies, India's largest manufacturer of solar panels by capacity.
Mumbai-based Waaree Energies listed on the Indian bourses in October 2024 at a 70% premium to its IPO price.
The stock market debut of the company made him and his three brothers billionaires.
It has five solar module manufacturing plants in India.
The company was originally founded in 1990 as a manufacturer of thermal and pressure gauges used in industrial boilers.

name: Bachtiar Karim
about: Bachtiar Karim or Lim Ek Tjioe is chairman and CEO of Musim Mas Holdings, a Singapore-based integrated palm oil firm that owns operations in Indonesia.
He runs Musim Mas together with his brothers Burhan and Bahari.
His late father Anwar founded Nam Cheong Soap Factory in 1932; the family run operation still makes soaps and margarine.
The family opened the first palm oil refinery in Indonesia in 1970. Musim Mas was formally set up two years later.

name: Filippo Ghirelli
about: Filippo Ghirelli is a Monaco-based Italian businessman with investments in infrastructure, real estate and energy.
In 2024 he launched Infracorp, an investment firm focused on energy, transportation, decentralized AI and commercial space flight, including orbital modules and data centers.
He also has significant investments in oil & gas infrastructure.
He founded and led Genera Group, an Italian energy efficiency firm, from 2009 until 2024, when he sold the company to Swiss investment manager SUSI Partners.
Through his family office, Sophrance Global, Ghirelli also invests in oil & gas, real estate and edtech startups.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, University of Rome, La Sapienza; Master of Business Administration, LUISS Business School

name: Magic Johnson
about: Earvin "Magic" Johnson is one of the greatest NBA players of all time. Forbes named him a billionaire in October 2023.
Johnson earned only around $40 million total as a Los Angeles Lakers player, mainly in the 1980s, and even at his peak only brought in between $2 million and $4 million per year in endorsements.
Instead he built his wealth through joint venture partnerships in everything from movie theaters, Starbucks franchises, real estate and healthcare.

The majority of his fortune comes from a 60% ownership stake in life insurance company Equitrust, which has grown from $16 billion in assets under management to $33 billion since he took over in 2015.
He also owns small ownership stakes in the NFL's Washington Commanders, MLB's Los Angeles Dodgers, WNBA's Los Angeles Sparks and MLS' LAFC.
did_you_know_facts: Johnson is just the fourth athlete billionaire Forbes has ever identified. The others are Michael Jordan, Tiger Woods and LeBron James.
Before the 1979 NBA Draft, Nike offered Johnson stock in the company and royalties on shoe sales. He declined in favor of $100,000 per year cash from Converse.

name: Yusaku Maezawa
about: Yusaku Maezawa founded Japan's largest online fashion mall, Zozotown, in 1998. Its parent company, Zozo, is listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
In 2019, Maezawa announced that he was resigning as CEO and selling most of his stake to Yahoo Japan in a deal worth more than $2.3 billion.
