Maezawa got his start selling CDs and records of his favorite bands by mail from his home.
He collects modern art and plans to build a museum to display it in Chiba, east of Tokyo.

In 2021, Maezawa flew on a Russian Soyuz rocket to the International Space Station for a 12-day trip. Maezawa's trip to the moon on Elon Musk's SpaceX, scheduled for 2023, was cancelled in 2024 due to delays in the rocket's development.
did_you_know_facts: In 2017, he paid over $110 million for Jean-Michel Basquiat's 1982 painting "Untitled," a new record for the artist.
Maezawa, who had advertised in January 2020 for a 'life partner' to accompany him on his moon trip, later sought eight people to go with him.

name: Robert Knauf & family
about: Robert Matthias Knauf is an heir to one of the world's leading producers of building materials and systems, Knauf Gips KG.
Based in Iphofen, Germany, the company employs more than 35,000 people around the world and has annual revenue of over $11 billion.
Its product line includes plasterboards, cement boards and insulating materials.
Knauf Gips dates to 1932, when brothers and mining engineers Alfons and Karl Knauf obtained rights to gypsum deposits in Schengen, Germany.
Their original gypsum factory, on the Moselle River in the border region of Luxembourg, Germany and France, is still the company's production nucleus.
did_you_know_facts: The family's Knauf Museum, on the premises of a historical inn built in 1688 on Iphofen's market square, houses a renowned collection or ancient relief art.

name: Ahmet Calik
about: Ahmet Calik built his fortune on denim, selling to Diesel, Levi's, Gap and other Western brands, but textiles are now ancillary in his group Calik Holding.
With a footprint stretching from Turkey and the Middle East to Eastern Europe and Central Asia, Calik is active in construction, banking, telecom and mining.
Calik Holding has a partnership with Mitsubishi Corp. dating back to 1990s, when the companies began collaborating on plant construction in Central Asia.
In 2015, Mitsubishi acquired 4.5% of Calik Energy, which serves five cities in Turkey and has projects in such places as Turkmenistan, Libya, Georgia and Yemen.
Besides providing services to energy plants, the company has electricity and gas distribution businesses and a portfolio of power generation assets.
did_you_know_facts: In terms of contract value, Calik Holding's pipeline of construction and energy projects amounts to around $7 billion.
quote: In a world of continuous change, our ways of doing business are constantly evolving. However, our values remain unchanged. We strive to achieve longevity through our human-centric values, and sustainable success through our innovative culture.

name: Chen Zhisong
about: Chen Zhisong is co-founder and chairman of Yealink Network Technology, a supplier of video conferencing solutions and Internet phones.
Yealink vice chairman Wu Zhongyi has also been a billionaire in recent years.
Yealink is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Xiamen.

name: Margarita Latsis Catsiapis & family
about: Margarita Latsis Catsiapis inherited the fortune of her late father, Greek shipping tycoon John S. Latsis (d. 2003) alongside siblings Marianna and Spiro.
The siblings split up the family fortune in 2019, with John and Margarita taking over the investments in banking and real estate.
With her brother, she own stakes in Zurich-based private banking group EFG International and Greek real estate developer Lamda Development.
The siblings also own shares in oil company Helleniq Energy and shipyard TALOS.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Geneva

did_you_know_facts: The Latsis siblings own a 300-passenger private cruise ship that is chartered out through their yacht services company, PrivatSea.

name: Robert Mouawad
about: Robert Mouawad inherited the family's eponymous high-end jewelry business that his grandfather founded in Beirut in 1890.
He turned over management of the business to his sons Fred, Alain and Pascal in 2010.
Mouawad boasts one of the world's most dazzling gem collections, including Dynasty, a 51.12 carat Russian diamond estimated at nearly $10 million.
Robert Mouawad also owns real estate, including hotels in Beirut. He developed luxury residences on Reef Island, a man-made island in Bahrain.
did_you_know_facts: Mouawad has a private museum in a 110 year-old Beirut palace displaying his collection of Roman and Phoenician antiquities.
In 2024, Mouawad announced a partnership with Dubai-based developer Dar Global to build a luxury residential development in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia.
quote: Success is a rare cocktail that requires a bottomless glass of passion, common sense as the basic ingredient, and a pinch of experience to make it delectable.

name: Premchand Godha
about: Premchand Godha is chairman of generics firm Ipca Labs, which manufactures formulations, bulk drugs and drug intermediates.
Godha acquired Ipca Labs together with the family of Bollywood superstar Amitabh Bachchan in 1975.
A qualified chartered accountant, he started his practice in 1971 before moving into pharma.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Chartered Accountant, Institute of Chartered Accountants of India; Bachelor of Commerce, University of Rajasthan

did_you_know_facts: Godha hails from a family of farmers.
He is a patron of the Jain International Trade Organization, which runs training centres for students preparing for the civil services.

name: Frank McCourt
about: Frank McCourt is an investor and entrepreneur with roots in his family's Boston-based construction business founded five generations ago.
In 2004, McCourt bought the Los Angeles Dodgers and sold the team for $2.2 billion eight years later, the largest sports sale at the time.
McCourt invested the proceeds into real estate, sports, tech and media through his company McCourt Global.
He stepped down as CEO of McCourt Global in 2023 to focus on Project Liberty, his $500 million commitment to fight for a safe, healthier internet.
McCourt has also pledged $200 million to his alma mater, Georgetown, helping establish the McCourt School of Public Policy.

name: Yuan Zhongxue
about: Yang Jianliang is a founder and honorary chairman of Sailun Group, a Chinese tire manufacturer. He stepped down as chairman in July 2021.
Sailun is headquartered in the eastern port city of Qingdao.
Sailun went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2011.

name: Tseng Cheng
about: Tseng Cheng inherited his Chang Chun Group stake from his father, Tseng Shin-yi, who died in 2016.
Shin-yi cofounded the business in 1949 with classmates M.K. Liao and Lin Shu-hong.
Chang Chun is now one of Asia's largest petrochemicals-and-plastics manufacturers, with plants in Taiwan, mainland China and Southeast Asia.

name: Christina Flügel
about: Christina Flügel is a fifth-generation member of the Mast-Jägermeister family fortune, best known for its green-bottled herbal liquor.
Her brother, Florian Rehm, a fellow German billionaire, chairs the company and serves as its spokesperson.
Mast-Jägermeister was founded in 1878 as a maker of vinegar; it shifted to producing wine and spirits in 1922 before creating the now-famous recipe for Jägermeister.

name: Alexander Sixt
about: Alexander Sixt, together with his brother, Konstantin, owns 56% of Sixt SE, one of the world's largest car rental companies. They are the co-CEOs.
Their grandfather Martin Sixt founded the firm in 1912. Their father, Erich, took over in 1969 when it was a local operation with just 200 vehicles.
Together with his wife, Regine, Erich turned the company into a global player. He stepped down as CEO in 2021; he is chair of the supervisory board.
Sixt SE, which went public in 1986, had 2021 revenues of around $2.5 billion, 7,000 employees and some 2,000 locations in over 100 countries.
Alexander joined Sixt in 2009; he and his brother Konstantin were appointed co-CEOs in 2021 after their father stepped down.
did_you_know_facts: In 2015, Alexander and his brother Konstantin joined Sixt's executive board.
His mom is still active in the company, in her role as Senior Executive Vice President of Marketing.

name: Konstantin Sixt
about: Konstantin Sixt, together with his brother, Alexander, owns 56% of Sixt SE, one of the world's largest car rental companies. They are the co-CEOs.
Their grandfather Martin Sixt founded the firm in 1912. Their father, Erich, took over in 1969 when it was a local operation with just 200 vehicles.
Together with his wife, Regine, Erich turned the company into a global player. He stepped down as CEO in 2021. He now chairs the supervisory board.
Sixt SE, which went public in 1986, had 2021 revenues of around $2.5 billion, with 7,000 employees and some 2000 locations in over 100 countries.
Konstantin and Alexander were appointed co-CEOs of Sixt in 2021 after their father stepped down; the brothers had been board members since 2015.
did_you_know_facts: In 2005, after receiving an MSc in International Accounting and Finance from Cass Business School in London, he assumed responsibility for Sixt's online operations.
His mom is still active in the company, in her role as Senior Executive Vice President of Marketing.

name: Peter Guber
about: Peter Guber, a longtime movie executive, owns stakes in several pro sports teams, most notably the NBA's Golden State Warriors.
Guber was part of a group led by Joe Lacob in 2010 that bought the Warriors for $450 million; Forbes now values the team at $8.8 billion.
Guber owns an estimated 15% of the Warriors and is co-executive chairman alongside Lacob.
He also owns an estimated 3% of the LA Dodgers baseball team and is executive chair and co-owner of the Major League Soccer team Los Angeles FC.
At Columbia Pictures and Polygram Entertainment, Guber oversaw production of hit movies including Rain Man, The Color Purple, Batman and more.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: LLM, New York University; JD, New York University; Bachelor of Arts, Syracuse University

did_you_know_facts: Guber is also an author whose book Shootout: Surviving Fame and (Mis)Fortune In Hollywood became a TV series on AMC.
Guber was recruited by Columbia Pictures while pursuing an MBA at New York University in the late 1960s.
quote: "My career has been fueled by curiosity and personal reinvention."

name: Gabriella Meister
about: Gabriella Meister and her daughter Franziska Wuerbser, who is also a billionaire, are among four family heirs who inherited 63% of kitchen appliance manufacturer Rational AG.
Gabriella's late husband, Siegfried Meister, founded the company in 1973 and died in 2017, at age 78.
Rational has more than a 50% share of the global market for multifunctional food preparation appliances used in large-scale and commercial kitchens.
The company's products include ovens, steamers and grills.
Rational, which went public in 2000, has grown consistently without acquisitions, and prides itself on innovative, energy-efficient technology.
did_you_know_facts: Siegfried Meister had the idea to cook using steam after disliking how food was prepared at restaurant chain Wienerwald, where he worked previously.
Rational employs over 250 professional chefs, and its products are used in the White House and Buckingham Palace.

name: Wu Chung-yi
about: Wu Chung-yi is the chairman of central Taiwan's auto parts maker Fine Blanking & Tool.
Most of his fortune comes from the 2007 sale of a stake he owned in Hong Kong-listed Tingyi, the maker of Master Kong beverages and instant noodles.
He is also known by his Western name Tony.

name: Nelson Peltz
about: Nelson Peltz, an activist investor, is a founder of investment firm Trian Fund Management.
Trian now has $8.5 billion in assets under management.
The firm has a highly concentrated portfolio that includes stakes in Bank of New York Mellon, DuPont and food conglomerate Mondelez International.
In early 2017, Peltz battled with Proctor & Gamble over a board seat the company didn't want to grant him. He ultimately won the seat.
Peltz's daughter, Nicola, married Brooklyn Beckham, son of soccer player David Beckham, in April 2022 at the family's mansion in Palm Beach, Florida.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Drop Out, University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School

name: Barry Bentley & family
about: Barry Bentley and his brother Keith founded infrastructure engineering software provider Bentley Systems in 1984.
The company, which went public in 2020, develops and sells computer-aided design (CAD) software for architects and engineers working on public and industrial infrastructure.
A third brother, Greg, served as CEO for more than two decades before transitioning into the role of executive chair and president in 2024.
A fourth brother, Raymond, serves as a director.
The $1.5 billion (2025 sales) company remains majority owned by the Bentley family.
did_you_know_facts: The Bentley brothers' mom, Bonnie, was a schoolteacher and would make them read for an hour after lunch every day during the summer.
The first program Barry ever wrote on a computer was a blackjack game.

name: Dick Wolf
about: Dick Wolf is best known as the creator of Law & Order, which is now the second-longest running network drama in television history, behind only its spin-off Law & Order: SVU.
.His Wolf Entertainment has had a profit participation deal with Universal Television since 2004, allowing him to retain nearly half of his shows? profits when they sell into syndication.
Wolf is one of the pioneers of the "linear binge," putting shows from a shared universe back-to-back on a single night of television
The company now oversees seven network shows and a streaming show on Amazon, producing nearly 150 episodes of television per year and overseeing more than 3,000 writers, actors and producers.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts, The University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: Dick Wolf began his career as a copywriter, and is credited with the slogan, "You can't beat Crest for fighting cavities."
Wolf's shows have employed more than 35,000 actors, serving as the launching pad for dozens of stars including Timothee Chalamet, Adam Driver and Chadwick Boseman.

name: Luo Yangyong & family
about: Luo Yangyong chairs mining company Sichuan Anning Iron and Titanium.
Luo holds an EMBA from the Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business.
Luo worked as a cashier and construction team leader before he started his own business in the late 1990s.

name: Wang Minwen
about: Wang Minwen chairs Hangzhou Lion Electronics, a supplier of semiconductor materials and chips.
Hangzhou Lion went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2020.
Wang and four siblings own 76.5% of paper manufacturer Xianhe Co. through their wholly owned Zhejiang Xianhe Holding Group.

name: Lu Zongjun
about: Lu Zongjun is a director of Shanghai Zhonggu Logistics, a container shipping company in China. He stepped down as chairman in November 2023.
Zhonggu went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2020.
Lu holds a graduate degree from the Wuhan University of Technology.

name: Lu Hongyan
about: Lu Hongyan chairs Shanghai-listed online games company G-bits Network Technology.
Its business benefited during the pandemic, when quarantined Chinese people turned to online gaming for fun.
Lu worked for telecom firms ZTE and Salira Optical Network Systems as a software engineer before he founded G-bits in 2004.

name: Ilson Mateus & family
about: A former gold miner, Ilson Mateus built up supermarket chain Grupo Mateus and took it public in October 2020.
The company is controlled by Mateus and his ex-wife, Maria Barros Pinheiro, who is a former billionaire.
Now Brazil's fourth-biggest food retailer, Grupo Mateus operates more than 200 stores throughout the country's northern and northeastern regions.
Grupo Mateus operates in 90 cities across Brazil and had revenues of $4.4 billion in 2023.
His fortune includes his two sons' stakes in Grupo Mateus.

name: Qiu Minxiu
about: Qiu Minxiu is a director at Zhejiang Jingsheng Mechanical & Electrical, a leading semiconductor material manufacturer.
Son He Jun is Jingsheng's president.
The company went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2015.

name: Ma Hong
about: Ma Hong chairs Raytron Technology, a supplier of infrared imaging and sensor in the eastern Chinese city of Yantai.
Ma Hong holds a doctorate from Huazhong University of Science & Technology.
Raytron Technology listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2019.

name: Vladimir Voronin
about: Vladimir Voronin is the founder of FSK Group, one of the largest housing developers in Russia.
Since 2022 Voronin has bought Russian assets of foreign companies at a discount, including Belgian mineral company Sibelco, Swedish residential developer Bonava and U.S. glass maker Guardian Glass.
In the 2000s, his father Alexander Voronin was a major shareholder of one of the largest construction groups in Moscow with revenue of about $1 billion.
In 2005 Alexander lost the construction assets in a corporate war with billionaire Suleiman Kerimov, who later sold the assets to Russian billionaire Oleg Deripaska.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master, Moscow State University of Civil Engineering

name: Alexander Evnevich & family
about: Alexander Evnevich cofounded Orimi, Russia's largest Russian producer of tea and roasted coffee.
Orimi was founded in 1994 as the Orimi Trade company, which ran wholesale trade of flour, sugar and tea.
The company would become a major player in the Russian tea market, eventually launching its own tea packaging production.
During the 1980s and 1990s, Evnevich worked in Vedeneev VNIIG, the largest scientific center of designing, construction and operation of hydraulic power plants in Russia.
Evnevich's family also controls Maxidom, a large Russian DIY retailer that in 2020 acquired the Russian subsidiary of Castorama, part of British company Kingfisher.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Saint Petersburg State University

name: Bulent Eczacibasi
about: Bulent Eczacibasi and brother Faruk are partners in a conglomerate that has 25 production facilities in Turkey and 16 abroad.
It is a global exporter of ceramic and wall tiles, plus bathroom fixtures and accessories (brands include VitrA, Villeroy & Boch and Engers Keramik).
Bulent and Faruk's father, Dr. Nejat F. Eczacibasi, focused on pharmaceuticals before expanding into personal health care and other businesses.
Eczacibasi Holding also operates in healthcare services and the production and distribution of medical products to hospitals.
Other key sectors are consumer products, finance, IT, mining and real estate development. Eczacibasi is Turkey's leading producer of toilet paper.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Imperial College London

did_you_know_facts: An avid collector, Bulent heads the Istanbul Foundation for Culture and Arts and the Istanbul Modern Art Foundation, which includes the Istanbul Modern Art Museum.
In Turkish, Eczacibasi means "chief pharmacist," an honorary title and surname given to Bulent's grandfather, Suleyman Ferit Eczacibasi.
quote: There are countless examples of how those who combine creativity and entrepreneurship succeed professionally. We cannot hope to become successful by repeating ourselves, keeping the status quo, and confining our hopes and dreams to our comfort zone.

name: Karin Schick
about: Karin Schick inherited a stake in Bechtle AG from her father, Gerhard, who co-founded the IT company in Heilbronn, Germany in 1983.
Bechtle covers the IT landscape, ranging from expert strategy advice to managed services that can take over complete operation of a company's systems.
The company has more than 12,000 employees and revenues exceeding $6.5 billion.
Bechtle's strong growth in the IT space has been fueled in part through an aggressive M&A strategy (more than 100 acquisitions since 1993).
did_you_know_facts: Karin Schick stepped down from Bechtle's advisory board in 2017 to focus on social projects through the Schick family foundation.
In 2012, her family founded the Community Knowledge Center (CKC) in Tanzania to provide internet access and computer courses to people of all ages.

name: Surin Upatkoon
about: Low-profile tycoon Surin Upatkoon made his fortune across sectors from insurance to telecom.
Most of his wealth comes from selling a 10% stake in Thai telecom company InTouch in 2013.
He owns stakes in listed gaming company Magnum, financial services outfit MPHB Capital and textile firm MWE.
He started his career as a manager at MWE Weaving Mills in 1971 and rose through the ranks.
His son, Krian, is on the boards of MWE and Magnum, while Ivevei, the older of his two daughters, is on the board of MPHB Capital.
did_you_know_facts: Upatkoon is a Thai national but moved to Penang for school, stayed for work and has been a Malaysia resident ever since.
He loves playing golf.
In January 2025 he launched a selective capital reduction exercise to privatise his financial services company MPHB Capital.

name: Antti Aarnio-Wihuri
about: Antti Aarnio-Wihuri heads Wihuri Group, a Finnish conglomerate that has been in his family for over 100 years.
The group has interests in the packaging, technical trade, food wholesale and aviation and operates Caterpillar construction equipment dealerships.
Wihuri Group, which employs 5,000 people, also runs Metro daily goods wholesale stores and a private jet charter and ambulance service.
He is the largest shareholder of Winpak, a Canadian company that specializes in producing packaging materials.

name: Andrei Komarov & family
about: In March 2021, Komarov sold his 87% stake in Chelyabinsk Tube Rolling Plant, also known as ChelPipe, one of Russia's leading steel pipe makers to the fellow billionaire Dmitry Pumpyansky for $1.13 bil
He managed Moscow's Satiricon Theater in the last years of communism.
He traded cars, metal products and steel pipes in the early 1990s.
In the mid-90s, in his hometown of Chelyabinsk, he teamed up with the manager of the town's pipe-making plant to private the business.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Moscow Institute of Chemical Engineering

did_you_know_facts: Komarov is a Harley-Davidson motorcycle fan.

name: Miguel Tomás Arrufat Pujol
about: Miguel Tomás Arrufat Pujol founded Spanish online education group Proeduca Altus, which provides accredited university courses online across Spain, Latin America, and the U.S.
Arrufat Pujol, who has led Proeduca Altus since its creation in 2007, owns more than 75% of the company, which went public in 2019.
Arrufat Pujol will sell around a third of his stake in Proeduca Altus for more than $300 million as part of a take private deal that is expected to close in the second quarter of 2025.
Arrufat Pujol was previously the CEO of a Spanish publishing house that focused on educational textbooks before founding Proeduca Altus.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts, Universitat Autonoma de Barcelona

name: Ulrike Meister
about: Ulrike Meister is one of four family heirs who inherited 63% of kitchen appliance manufacturer Rational AG.
Siegfried Meister founded the company in 1973 and died in 2017, at age 78. Its products include ovens, steamers and grills.
Rational has more than a 50% share of the global market for multifunctional food preparation appliances used in large-scale and commercial kitchens.
The company, which went public in 2000, has grown consistently without acquisitions, and prides itself on innovative, energy-efficient technology.
did_you_know_facts: Siegfried Meister had the idea to cook using steam after disliking how food was prepared at restaurant chain Wienerwald, where he worked previously.
Rational employs over 250 professional chefs, and its products are used in the White House and Buckingham Palace.

name: Eustasio Lopez Gonzalez
about: Eustasio López González is the owner of Invertur Helsan, a closely held Spanish hotel group.
He co-founded investment company, Hijos de Francisco López Sánchez in 1972, which was the seed of the family's Lopesan Group.

Originally focused on construction and real-estate, Lopez Gonzales pivoted the business into tourism in the 1990s, creating the hotel division that developed Meloneras in south Gran Canaria, including the flagship Lopesan Costa Meloneras, which opened in 2000.
He acquired a majority stake in Germany's IFA Hotels & Touristik in 1999, which became a platform for growth in Germany, Austria and Switzerland.
He remains chairman of the Lopesan Group and continues to oversee its international portfolio, including the 5-star Lopesan Costa Bávaro in Punta Cana.

name: Patrick Hanrahan
about: Patrick Hanrahan cofounded data analytics company Tableau in 2003.
Salesforce acquired Tableau in June 2019 in a $15.7 billion, all-stock deal.
Hanrahan is a computer graphics and electrical engineering professor at Stanford University.
Tableau was born out of research he and one of his cofounders were doing while analyzing and visualizing large databases of information at Stanford.
He and his cofounders raised $15 million in venture capital before taking Tableau public on the New York Stock Exchange in May 2013.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Ph.D, University of Wisconsin Madison; Bachelor of Science, University of Wisconsin Madison

did_you_know_facts: Hanrahan, who was an early employee of Pixar, won three Oscars for his engineering and technical work between 1993 and 2014.

name: Chen Kaichen
about: Chen Kaixuan is vice chairman of Guangzhou-headquartered Liby Group, a supplier of washing detergents and soap.
Chen co-founded Liby in 1994 with his brother Chen Kaixuan, who is also a billionaire.
His daughter Danxia chairs Cheerwin Group, a Hong Kong-listed consumer and pet products company invested by Chen Kaixuan.

name: George Christ & family
about: George Christ cofounded software company Altair Engineering with fellow billionaire James Scapa in 1985.
Christ retired before Altair went public in 2017 but remained the company's second largest individual shareholder until it was acquired by German tech giant Siemens in 2025.
Siemens paid nearly $10 billion in cash for Altair and Christ walked away with $1 billion before taxes.

name: Xiong Haitao
about: XiongHaitao is a director of Shanghai-listed Kingfa Sci.and Tech, a plastics supplier.
The company entered the markets for medical and protective gloves during the global pandemic in 2020.
Xiong is the wife of Yuan Zhimin, who founded Kingfa in 1993.

name: Jonas Kleberg
about: Jonas Kleberg is the Chairman and CEO of Soya Group, a multi-billion dollar Swedish family conglomerate.
He is the grandson of Olof Wallenius, who founded the group in 1934.
The family's wealth stems primarily from shipping, including a major stake in Wallenius Wilhelmsen, one of the world's largest car carriers.
Under Kleberg's leadership, the group has diversified into real estate, wind-propulsion technology, and forestry.
He and his sister, Annika Bootmans Kleberg, each own 50% of the Soya Group, which also includes a trotting horse breeding operation.
did_you_know_facts: The family company is named "Soya" because the founder's first vessels in the 1930s were converted to carry soybean oil, a pioneering move at the time.

name: Annika Bootsman Kleberg
about: Annika Bootsman Kleberg is a Swedish shipping heir and co-owner of Soya Group, a multi-billion dollar family conglomerate.
She is the granddaughter of Olof Wallenius, who founded the group in 1934.
The family's wealth stems primarily from shipping, including a major stake in Wallenius Wilhelmsen, one of the world's largest car carriers.
The group has diversified into real estate, wind-propulsion technology, forestry and horse breeding.
She owns 50% of the Soya Group, with the remaining stake held by her brother, Jonas Kleberg.
did_you_know_facts: The family company is named "Soya" because the founder's first vessels in the 1930s were converted to carry soybean oil, a pioneering move at the time.
Bootsman Kleberg has a passion for reining, the dressage discipline of Western riding.

name: Ren Jianhua
about: Ren Jianhua chairs Shenzhen-listed kitchen appliance maker Hangzhou Robam Appliances.
The company claims its products, which include range hoods, microwaves and gas stoves, are in over 35 million households.
It was founded in 1979 and its first generation range hood, created by Robam and the department of aeronautics and astronautics, came out in 1987.
Ren borrowed $5.4 million at the end of 1998 to take control of the company.
It now has 5,635 patents.

name: Lai Jianping
about: Lai's fortune comes from a minority stake in Foshan Haitian Flavouring and Food of China, which makes soy sauce and other condiments.
Lai left the company before it went public in China in 2014.
Haitian originated from an ancient sauce workshop in Foshan, where it produced its first batch of soy sauce more than 400 years ago.

name: Evangelos Mytilineos
about: Evangelos Mytilineos is the chairman and CEO of Athens-based, publicly traded metals and energy firm METLEN Energy & Metals.
METLEN's assets include aluminum plants, bauxite mines and solar energy projects, and the firm is Greece's largest independent electricity supplier.
METLEN grew out of a metallurgy business founded by Mytilineos' grandfather, also named Evangelos, in 1908.
Mytilineos founded the modern company, then named Mytilineos Energy & Metals, in 1990 and took it public on the Athens stock exchange in 1995.
He renamed the company METLEN in 2024 and completed a dual listing on the London stock exchange in 2025.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Athens University of Economics and Business; Master, London School of Economics

name: Franziska Wuerbser
about: Franziska Wuerbser is the daughter of Gabriella Meister, who is one of four family heirs who inherited 63% of kitchen appliance manufacturer Rational AG.
Rational has more than a 50% share of the global market for food preparation appliances used in large-scale and commercial kitchens.
The company, which went public in 2000, has grown without acquisitions, and prides itself on innovative, energy-efficient technology.
More than 2,200 employees work for Rational AG, which is headquartered just outside Munich, Germany.

name: Chirayu Amin
about: Pharma tycoon Chirayu Amin's Alembic Pharmaceuticals is one of India's oldest pharma companies.
Alembic was founded by Amin's grandfather in 1907 to make tincture and alcohol.
Today, Alembic gets more than a third of its annual revenue from the domestic market selling generic drugs, including popular cough syrup Glycodin.
While Amin is chairman and chief executive, his three sons work in different parts of the business.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Baroda University; Master of Business Administration, Seton Hall University

did_you_know_facts: Amin is the brother-in-law of consumer goods billionaire Harsh Mariwala.
Amin was head of the Indian Premier League for 17 months after its founder Lalit Modi was sacked in 2010.

name: Vladimir Fartushnyak
about: Vladimir Fartushnyak, his brother Nikolay and Alexander Mikhalskiy are cofounders of Russia's largest sports and fashion retailer Sportmaster.
The three also cofounded Ostin, a large Russian fast-fashion retailer.
Vladimir Fartushyak himself wholly owns Zolla, another fast-fashion chain in Russia.
He and his partners got their start with a distribution company in the early 1990s, which supplied French consumer goods to the Russian market.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

name: Karl Hedin
about: Karl Hedin is the owner of AB Karl Hedin, a Swedish timber group in sawmills, building materials and forestry.
The company was founded by Hedin's grandfather in 1937 and is now a leading player in Sweden's forest industry.
Hedin is known for his strong views on forest ownership and has criticized Swedish environmental policy.
In March 2025, Hedin announced plans to sell the group's sawmills and packaging division.

name: Marissa Mayer
about: Google's first female engineer and 20th employee, Marissa Mayer spent 13 years at the tech company, which is the source of much of her fortune.
Mayer took over as CEO of Yahoo in 2012, but was unable to keep web traffic and ad revenues from falling.
Mayer resigned as CEO of Yahoo in 2017, when it sold to Verizon for $4.5 billion, following Yahoo's disclosure of security breaches.
She then cofounded Sunshine, which launched AI apps to automate everyday tasks, in 2018.
Sunshine raised $17 million but is reportedly dissolving and selling its assets to Marissa's third act, AI firm Dazzle.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Stanford University; Master of Science, Stanford University

quote: Find the smartest people you can and surround yourself with them.

name: Kim Jung-youn
about: Jung-youn and her older sister, Jung-min, each own a stake in NXC, which is the largest shareholder in online gaming giant Nexon.
The sisters inherited the bulk of their stakes from their father Kim Jung-ju, who founded Nexon in 1994; he died in 2022 at age 54.
Neither Jung-youn nor her sister has been involved in Nexon's operation. Little is known about them.

name: Kim Jung-min
about: Jung-min and her younger sister, Jung-youn, each own a stake in NXC, which is the largest shareholder in online gaming giant Nexon.
The sisters inherited the bulk of their stakes from their father Kim Jung-ju, who founded Nexon in 1994; he died in 2022 at age 54.
Neither Jung-min nor her sister has been involved in Nexon's operation. Little is known about them.

name: Jeff Lawson
about: Jeff Lawson is a cofounder of Twilio, a cloud communications platform that adds messaging, voice and video to web and mobile apps.
Lawson launched his first Internet startup while he was at the University of Michigan and went on to become the first CTO of ticket reseller StubHub.
The serial entrepreneur went on to work at Amazon, where he helped build the technology behind Amazon Web Services.
Along with two friends, Lawson started Twilio in 2008 then took it public in 2016.
He stepped down as CEO and and left the company's board in 2024.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Michigan

did_you_know_facts: In 2024, Lawson acquired the satirical news site The Onion.
Twilio's first customer was PhoneMyPhone.com, which allowed people to type their numbers into a website to ring their own cellphones.

name: Michael Teel
about: Michael Teel is the owner and chairman of Raley's, a Sacramento-based supermarket chain with estimated revenues of $6 billion.
He is the third-generation owner. His grandfather, Tom Raley, founded the company in 1935.
He took over from his mother, Joyce Raley Teel (d. 2022), who ran Raley's from 1991 to 2015, when she transferred ownership to Michael.
Today Raley's has 235 stores in California, Nevada, Arizona, Washington, Alaska and Oregon.
The company also operates stores in several tribal nations in the Southwest.

name: George Marcus
about: San Francisco Bay Area real estate broker George Marcus has been in the business for over 40 years.
Most of his fortune lies in a 35% stake in Marcus & Millichap, the publicly-traded real estate brokerage he founded in 1971.
Marcus & Millichap specializes in commercial real estate in the U.S. and Canada, closing nearly 9,000 transactions valued at $42.3 billion in 2016.
Marcus also controls a 3% stake in Essex Property Trust, a REIT he founded that owns more than 60,000 apartments along the West Coast.
Marcus also has a stake in several private real-estate and investment companies, including SummerHill Housing Group and Pacific Urban Residential.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Economics, San Francisco State

did_you_know_facts: He graduated with a B.A. in economics from San Francisco State University and served on the Board of Regents of the University of California from 2000 to 2012.
Marcus was born on a Greek island, northeast of Athens, and immigrated to the United States when he was four with his poor parents.

name: Zheng Wei
about: Zheng derives his fortune from Haisco Pharmaceutical, which employs 4,000 people worldwide.
He stepped down from the company in 2024 but retains a substantial stake.
Prior to Haisco, Zheng was a director at a pharmaceutical group in Sichuan.

name: Arsen Kanokov
about: Arsen Kanokov's fortune stems from the Sindika Group, which has 35 shopping centers in southern Russia and eight hotels -- three of which are in Sochi, a prominent city known for its resorts.
Kanokov was born in Kabardino-Balkaria, in 2005-2013 he used to be a president of Kabardino-Balkaria, one of Russia southern regions.
He is a member of the Federation Council from Kabardino-Balkarian Republic.
Kanokov bought shares of Starbucks, OBI and McDonalds in Russia after the companies decided to exit the country amid the Russia-Ukraine war.
He is under E.U. and U.S. sanctions since 2022, and under U.K. sanctions since 2025.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctorate, Plekhanov Russian University of Economics

name: Hans Sy
about: Hans Sy is the fourth child of Henry Sy Sr., the late founder of SM Investments, one of the largest conglomerates in the Philippines.
He stepped down as president of subsidiary SM Prime, a property developer, in 2016 and remains a director.
His five siblings, Teresita, Elizabeth, Henry Jr., Harley and Herbert, are all involved in the business.
He also serves as an adviser of SM Investments, chairman of China Banking Corporation and chairman of National University.
In 2022, SM Investments agreed to acquire Philippine Geothermal Production in a $304 million, all-share deal in a bid to lower its carbon footprint.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, De La Salle University

did_you_know_facts: Han's father, Henry Sy, acquired Philippines' National University, a private institution, in 2009.
He is the only Filipino member on the ARISE International Board, a group under the United Nations for global business leaders on disaster risk reduction management.

name: Brian Roberts
about: Brian Roberts is chairman and CEO of media and technology company Comcast.
His father Ralph Roberts (d. 2015) was the founder of Comcast, where Brian Roberts did his first internship at age 15.
Brian Roberts became president in 1990 at age 31; seven years later, his father transferred the bulk of his Comcast voting shares to him.
He now controls nearly a third of the company's voting power thanks to his super voting shares.
Comcast acquired the NHL's Philadelphia Flyers in 2016 and UK-based media and telecom conglomerate Sky in 2018.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School

did_you_know_facts: A top ranked squash player, Roberts earned a gold medal with the U.S. team at the Maccabiah Games in Israel in 2005 and silver medals in 1981, 1985 and 1997.

name: G.V. Prasad
about: G.V.Prasad is the co-chairman and managing director of pharma company Dr Reddy's Laboratories.
The company was founded by his late father-in-law K.Anji Reddy in 1984.
Prasad runs the company with Satish Reddy, the late founder's son, who is also a billionaire.
In December 2023 Dr. Reddy's launched Nerivio, a wearable therapy device to treat migraines.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Illinois Institute of Technology; Master, Purdue University

did_you_know_facts: Prasad sits on the boards of the Indian School of Business and Ashoka University.
His father-in-law was the son of a turmeric farmer and founded the company with seed money of $45,000 to make pharma ingredients and generics.

name: Xu Zhenhua
about: Xu Zhenhua cofounded Moonton Games, a business bought by ByteDance for $4 billion in 2021.
Cofounder Justin Yuan is also a billionaire.
Xu worked at China online game leader Tencent before taking the plunge as an entrepreneur himself.

name: Justin Yuan
about: Justin Yuan is CEO of Moonton Games, best known for "Mobile Legends: Bang Bang."
China's ByteDance bought Moonton for approximately $4 billion in 2021.
Moonton is headquartered in Shanghai.

name: John Morgan
about: John Morgan founded and runs America's largest personal injury law firm, Morgan & Morgan.
Morgan launched the firm in 1988, after his younger brother Tim, who died in July 2024 at age 65, was paralyzed in a diving accident as a teenage lifeguard at a Disney resort.
Morgan and his family own about half of the $2 billion (2023 revenue) law firm, with around 139 equity partners owning the rest.
His wife and sons are lawyers and work at the family firm, which spends $350 million annually on billboard, cable and other ads, some featuring Morgan as everything from a UFC fighter to Santa.
Morgan has been a major Democratic donor since the 1980s and has often teased a run for Florida governor. He registered as an independent in 2017.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts, University of Florida; JD, University of Florida

name: Prasanna Sankar
about: Prasanna Sankar cofounded human resources software startup Rippling with fellow billionaire Parker Conrad in 2016.
Sankar owns an estimated 9% of the company, which private investors valued at $16.8 billion in May 2025.
Before cofounding Rippling, Sankar served as director of engineering at another human resources software startup Zenefits, which Conrad founded in 2013.
Sankar served as chief technology officer of Rippling until 2020, before leaving to found 0xPPL, which he describes as a decentralized social network for crypto natives, in 2023.
Born in India, Sankar studied computer science at the National Institute of Technology in Tiruchirappalli. He now lives in Singapore.

name: Thomas Crowley Jr & family
about: Thomas B. Crowley Jr. is the chairman and majority owner of Jacksonville, Florida-based shipping company Crowley Maritime.
He and his immediate family own some 80% of the $3.5 billion (revenue) company.
Crowley is the third generation to run the family firm, which his grandfather founded in 1892.
Crowley took over the company at the age of 27, when his dad died in 1994.
He has grown Crowley Maritime's fleet to 125 shipping vessels as of July 2025.

name: Peter Ludwig
about: Peter Ludwig is the cofounder and CTO of vehicle software startup Applied Intuition.
The company develops operating systems and simulation tools designed to power everything from planes and tanks to automobiles.
Ludwig and cofounder Qasar Younis initially focused on selling simulators and tools to self-driving car startups but expanded to work with major car makers like General Motors, Nissan and Volkswagen.
The Sunnyvale, California-based company was last valued at $15 billion when it raised a $600 million fund round in June 2025.
Ludwig grew up in Detroit, Michigan, where his father, and grandfather both worked for car-maker General Motors.
He studied engineering at the University of Michigan then took a job with Google, where he worked with future Younis on Google Maps, and later helped develop Android's automotive software.

name: Qasar Younis
about: Qasar Younis is the cofounder and CEO of vehicle software startup Applied Intuition.
The company develops operating systems and simulation tools designed to power everything from planes and tanks to automobiles.
Younis and cofounder Peter Ludwig initially focused on selling simulators and tools to self-driving car startups but expanded to work with major car makers like General Motors, Nissan and Volkswagen.
The Sunnyvale, California-based company was last valued at $15 billion when it raised a $600 million fund round in June 2025.
Younis was born in Punjab, Pakistan, and grew up in Detroit, Michigan, after his parents immigrated to the United States. He studied at the General Motors Institute and later Harvard Business School.
Before founding Applied Intuition, Younis had launched startup TalkBin, which was acquired by Google in 2011, then worked on Google Maps and later served as COO of startup accelerator Y Combinator.

name: Ignacio Torras
about: Ignacio "Nacho" Torras runs Tricon Energy, one of the world's biggest distributors and traders of chemicals and plastics.
Torras, who is a dual Spanish and American citizen, was born in Barcelona to a family that owned paper mills and newspapers.
As a teen, he moved with his family to Brazil after they lost everything in the 1970s recession. When his father was diagnosed with ALS, Torras took over his small chemicals trading business.
After a seven years in the chemicals industry, including a four-year stint at Houston-based Holland Chemical, he and three other traders launched Tricon in 1996.

Torras tried bringing in a CEO to run the day-to-day in 2016 so he could focus on trading. But the new guy told him he was too much of a control freak, so Torras took the job back: "After a year I realized I wasn't such a bad CEO."
did_you_know_facts: The Michelin Guide gave Torras' Spanish restaurant BCN Taste & Tradition a star in 2024.
In 2024 Torras launched a soccer tournament for neurodivergent players called the Genuine Cup.
Torras is a devout Catholic who attends daily mass and spends the first 45 minutes of each day praying the Rosary.

name: Seth Klarman
about: Seth Klarman runs Boston-based hedge fund Baupost, which has $27.4 billion under management as of March 2023.
Klarman's book "Margin of Safety," a cult classic among value investors, sells for about $1,700 on Amazon.
Once a major donor to the Republican Party, Klarman publicly denounced Trump in 2016, and has been contributing to the Democratic Party.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Cornell University

did_you_know_facts: In 2017, Klarman's horse, Cloud Computing, won the Preakness Stakes at Pimlico, the racetrack he grew up next to in Baltimore.
Klarman, whose philanthropic efforts focus on scientific research and promoting access to music learning, is also a major supporter of causes in Israel.

name: Stewart Butterfield
about: Stewart Butterfield is the cofounder and former CEO of team-based messaging software Slack.
In 2021, cloud software giant Salesforce acquired Slack for $27.7 billion in cash and stock.
Butterfield departed Salesforce in 2022, amid an exodus of executives at the company.
Butterfield and wife Jen Rubio, the founder of luggage startup Away, sold their San Francisco home and moved to Aspen in 2020.
Though he cofounded a tech company, Butterfield proudly majored in philosophy as an undergraduate at Canada's University of Victoria.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Victoria; Master of Philosophy, University of Cambridge

did_you_know_facts: Butterfield cofounded image hosting site Flickr in 2003; it was purchased by Yahoo for $35 million in 2005.

name: Joseph Steinberg
about: Joseph Steinberg is the chairman of Jefferies Financial Group, a New York-based financial services firm best known for investment banking.
He served as president of Leucadia National Corporation, an investment firm which was often compared to a mini-Berkshire Hathaway, from 1979 to 2013.
During his time at the helm, Leucadia purchased companies like National Beef and helped finance Bill Ackman's Pershing Square Capital Management.
In 2013, the firm merged with Jefferies and Steinberg became chairman. The combined company changed its name to Jefferies Financial Group in 2018.
Steinberg also serves as a director of Crimson Wine Group, which owns vineyards in California, Oregon and Washington.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, New York University; Master of Business Administration, Harvard University

did_you_know_facts: Since 2015, Joseph and wife Diane have donated over $15 million through their charitable trust to museums, colleges and community centers.

name: Sekar Vembu
about: Sekar Vembu get his wealth from his holding in privately held Zoho, which offers business software on the cloud.
He cofounded AdventNet, the precursor to Zoho, along with his two brothers as well as three other friends.
In 2002, he set up Vembu Technologies in Chennai, which offers data backup and disaster recovery solutions to small and medium firms.
His brother Sridhar, who was the face of the company, stepped down as CEO in February 2025 taking on a role as a chief scientist for company
His sister Radha Vembu is the largest shareholder in Zoho and also a billionaire.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Technology, Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras)

did_you_know_facts: Zoho is setting up a new campus which an house 2,000 people in the tier 3 city of Kumbakkonam in the southern Indian state of Tamil Nadu
Zoho is headquartered in Austin, Texas and Chennai, India.
Younger brother Mani is now Zoho's CEO.

name: Carmen Thyssen
about: Carmen Thyssen inherited her fortune from her husband, Baron Hans Heinrich Thyssen-Bornemisza, when he died in 2002.
She owns an art collection being exhibited at the Thyssen Museum in Madrid that is valued by the Spanish government at more than $1.4 billion.
Carmen Thyssen, a former Miss Spain, married Hans Thyssen-Bornemisza, heir to a German industrial fortune, in 1985; she was his fifth wife.
Hans and his son Georg, now both deceased, settled a 3-year court battle over control of the family's Monaco-based TBG Group months before the elder Thyssen died in 2002.
The Thyssen Museum exhibits the government-owned Thyssen Bornemisza collection as well as the private collection of Carmen Thyssen.

name: Satish Reddy
about: Satish Reddy is the chairman of listed pharma company Dr Reddy's Laboratories, in which he has a minority stake.
The company was founded by his late father K.Anji Reddy in 1984.
Reddy's brother-in-law G.V.Prasad, who is also a billionaire, is the co-chairman and managing director of the company.
In December 2023 it rolled out Nerivio, a wearable therapy device to treat migraines.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Osmania University; Master of Science, Purdue University

did_you_know_facts: He is a member of the board of governors at the Indian Institute of Management in Visakhapatnam.
His father was the son of a turmeric farmer and founded the company with seed money of $45,000 to make pharma ingredients and generics.

name: Alan Gerry
about: Alan Gerry started building a cable TV network in upstate New York in 1956.
It became Cablevision Industries, which at its peak had 64 cable systems in 18 states.
Gerry sold Cablevision Industries to Time Warner in 1996 for a reported $2.7 billion; he pocketed an estimated $900 million.
He used that money to start own venture capital firm, Granite Associates, in 1996 to invest in emerging communications technologies.
did_you_know_facts: Gerry bought the site of the 1969 Woodstock festival and a decade later turned the location into the Bethel Woods Center for the Arts, an 800-acre cultural center
Gerry initially got into cable to increase demand for TV sets--he owned a television repair shop.

name: Vitali Machitski & family
about: Vitali Machitski traded timber and oil in 1990s and now controls publicly traded Vimetco, which has stakes in aluminum producers Alro in Europe and Zhongfu Industrial in China.
Machitski lost out to billionaires Mikhail Fridman and Viktor Vekselberg in the 1997 privatization auction of Tyumen Oil Company, one of the largest Russian oil companies.
In early 2000s he sold some refinery assets to Mikhail Khodorkovsky' Yukos and other buyers.

Machitski, a friend of Sergey Chemezov, the head of Rostec State Corporation, one of the largest weapon manufacturers in the world, controls companies that developed the Rostec-City business complex in Moscow.

name: René Holecek
about: René Holecek is the majority owner of Prague-based firearm manufacturer Colt CZ Group.
The firm owns major firearms and ammunition brands including Colt, Sellier & Bellot and Dan Wesson.
He invested in the firm, then named Česká zbrojovka, in 2001 and took a majority stake in 2014 before taking it public on the Prague stock exchange in 2020.
In 2021, the firm acquired historic American gun manufacturer Colt in a $260 million deal and renamed itself Colt CZ.
In 2024, Colt CZ acquired Czech ammunition manufacturer Sellier & Bellot for $700 million.
did_you_know_facts: Holecek started out as a banker in the early 1990s.
In 1994, he played a key role in the privatization of Czech state-owned steelworks Třinecké ?elezárny.

name: Tan Yu Yeh
about: Tan Yu Yeh gets his wealth from his stake in Mr. D.I.Y, a home improvement retail chain, which he founded in 2005.
The company was listed on the Malaysian stock exchange in 2020 making him and his brother, Tan Yu Wei, both billionaires.
Mr. D.I.Y. has more than 4,000 stores across Asia and Europe.
D.I.Y stores are typically 10,000 square feet and carry products across ten categories including electrical items, stationery and toys.
Tan worked as an engineer and then as a remisier before setting up his home improvement venture.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, University of Malaya

did_you_know_facts: He listed the Indonesian subsidiary, Daya Intiguna Yasa, in December 2024 on the Indonesian stock exchange

name: Turgay Ciner
about: Turgay Ciner (pronounced "jin-ner"), who worked as an errand boy in tea shops during high school, presides over a fortune built on soda ash.
Soda ash is used in glass, detergents and various industrial products. Ciner's Eti Soda and Kazan Soda are among the world's top producers.
In 2025, Ciner's London-based WE Soda acquired U.S. producer Genesis Alkali for $1.4 billion, reinforcing its position as the world's largest natural soda ash producer.
Ciner sold his media empire -- including Habertürk, Show TV and Bloomberg HT -- at the end of 2024, ending a 22-year run as one of Turkey's most prominent media owners.
Ciner's Silopi Electric, in Turkey's Southeastern Anatolia region, generates power from thermal plants fueled by coal extracted from Ciner mines.
did_you_know_facts: Turgay Ciner and his brother imported autos from Germany and had a shop in Istanbul Talimhane, now site of the modern headquarters building of Ciner Publishing.

name: Douglas Rippel
about: Douglas Ripple founded American First Finance, a company that offers lease-to-won and retail installment plans to customers, in 2013.
He sold the company to FirstCash in 2021 for $1.17 billion in cash and stock.
Rippel owns a 9% stake in FirstCash, an international operator of pawn stores
He served on First Cash? board of directors until stepping down in 2024.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Wichita State University; Bachelor of Arts, Kansas State University

name: Wang Zhenghua
about: Wang Zhenghua is a director and the largest individual shareholder of Spring Airlines of China, one of the world's largest budget carriers.
Wang was a district government official in Shanghai before he set up his first company, Shanghai Spring Tour, in 1981.
Spring has a fleet of 122 aircraft, according to the company's website.

name: Tiger Woods
about: Tiger Woods has earned roughly $1.8 billion pretax in his pro golf career, including a PGA Tour-record $121 million in prize money. In 2022, Forbes certified him as a billionaire, making him only the second active athlete ever with that distinction, after LeBron James.

Woods reached that rarified air despite reportedly turning down a "mind-blowingly enormous" offer from the upstart LIV Golf tour, a deal that LIV CEO Greg Norman told the Washington Post would have been in the "high nine digits."
Woods has parlayed his golfing paychecks into investments that include two homes on Jupiter Island, a golf-course design business and high-end mini-golf chain Popstroke.
Woods and fellow golf star Rory McIlroy announced in 2022 that they had founded TMRW Sports, a tech-focused venture that launched a new golf league called TGL in 2025.
The superstar is also a partner with Justin Timberlake and British billionaire Joe Lewis in Nexxus, a luxury real-estate venture.

personal_stats.label: Agency
personal_stats.value: Excel Sports Management, Excel Sports Management

personal_stats.label: Sponsors
personal_stats.value: 2K Sports, Autograph, Bridgestone, Full Swing, Kowa Company Ltd., Monster Energy, Rolex, TaylorMade, Upper Deck

name: Paul Fireman
about: Paul Fireman bought the US distribution rights for a British company in 1979, turned it into Reebok and rode the sneakers & aerobics craze in the 80s.
Nike pulled ahead in the early 1990s, and shareholders demanded that Fireman step down in 1996, which he eventually did.
Fireman returned in 1999 and revived the business before selling it to Adidas for $3.8 billion in 2005, a deal that earned him $600 million.
Fireman owns Liberty National Golf Course, a $250 million country club built on a New Jersey landfill overlooking the Statue of Liberty.
did_you_know_facts: Liberty National Golf club is one of the most exclusive courses in the world, with members reportedly paying $500,000 to join.
Before creating Reebok, Fireman was an officer in an outdoor sports distributorship.

name: Yu Lili
about: Yu Lili is a director of electronic products maker Changsha Jingjia Microelectronics. She stepped down as vice chair in August 2024.
Changsha Jingjia Microelectronics went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2016.
Yu's husband Zeng Wanhui chairs Jingjia.

name: Philip Fayer
about: Philip Fayer is the founder, CEO and chairman of Canadian fintech firm Nuvei.
Nuvei in went public in 2020 at a $6 billion valuation and raised $700 million, the largest tech IPO on the Toronto Stock Exchange at the time.
The firm, based in Montreal but with staff across six continents, processes payments in more than 150 currencies and generates more than $1 billion in annual revenue.
Fayer, PE firm Advent International and others took Nuvei private in a $6.3 billion deal in 2024. Fayer owns around a quarter of the company.
A Canadian native, Fayer was reportedly raised in Israel and Belgium and is a pilot and race car driver.

name: Eric Hémar
about: Eric Hémar founded ID Logistics, a France-based international logistics and transport company. He still runs the company as chairman and CEO.
He launched the company in 2001 and took it public in 2012 on the NYSE Euronext in Paris.
Today, ID Logistics has a presence in 19 countries and generated $3.6 billion of revenue in 2024.
Hémar owns over 50% of the company's stock.
He's also served as president of the TLF Union, which represents French transport and logistics professionals, since 2019.
did_you_know_facts: Hémar started his career in the French government, first at its supreme audit court and then its transport ministry.

name: Li Ming
about: Li Ming is the largest investor in Jinhui Mining, a mining business that went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2022.
Li Ming is also an investor in Jinhui Liquor, a spirits supplier.
Li Ming's family runs firms in real estate, automotive, entertainment, agriculture, retail, and services.

name: Stephen Winn
about: Stephen Winn founded retail management software firm RealPage in 1998.
Its products help landlords manage finances and compliance requirements, and enable tenants to pay rent and file maintenance requests electronically.
An electrical engineer by training, Winn started his career working for his father's accounting software firm, Computer Language Research.
He eventually took over as CEO of the family business, and founded RealPage in 1998.
Winn took the Texas company public in 2010 and sold it to private equity firm Thoma Bravo in April 2021; he stepped down as CEO shortly after.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Stanford University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, The University of Texas at Austin

did_you_know_facts: RealPage's predecessor, Little Buddy, was a side venture of a tax software business Winn acquired to expand Computer Language Research.

name: Lin Chang Su-O
about: Lin is the widow of real estate mogul Lin Rong San. She resigned as chairman of the family's property developer Union Enterprise Construction in 2021.
Lin Rong San died in 2015 and left a $4.2 billion fortune built on real estate developments and investments in northern Taiwan.
Eldest son Jeff Lin runs the publicly traded Union Bank of Taiwan, which was started by his father.
Second son Andy Lin runs the group's media outlets, including Chinese-language newspaper Liberty Times and its sister English-language Taipei Times.
Youngest son Kevin works with another family-owned developer, RSL, which builds upscale residential projects and operates hotels.
did_you_know_facts: Lin Chang Su-O also chairs her late husband's Lin Rong San Foundation of Culture and Social Welfare.
In 2018 the Lins ended Marriott's franchise agreement for its Taipei hotel to protest the chain's caving in to Chinese pressure by listing Taiwan as part of China.

name: Jose Isaac Peres & family
about: Jose Isaac Peres founded Multiplan, a company that develops, owns and manages shopping malls in Brazil.
At age 22 while an economics student, he founded his first company, real estate developer Vepan, which he turned into publicly-traded Multiplan.
He and his wife together own about a quarter of Multiplan's stock.
In 2014 Peres' Village Mall property in Rio de Janeiro became the site of Brazil's first official Apple store.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Universidade do Brasil

did_you_know_facts: Peres, a Rio de Janeiro native, is passionate about his hometown and refuses to move Multiplan's headquarters to Sao Paulo, Brazil's main financial main center.

name: Richard Warke
about: Richard Warke is a Canadian investor with holdings in gold, zinc and copper mining in Canada, Mexico, the U.S. and South America.
He sold Ventana Gold, which discovered the La Bodega gold deposit in Colombia, for $1.6 billion in 2011.
His Augusta Resource advanced one of the largest copper deposits in the U.S.; Warke sold the firm for $600 million in 2014.
His Arizona Mining discovered the largest zinc deposit in the U.S. in Arizona; he sold the firm for $1.3 billion in 2018.
In 2025 he sold Augusta Gold to AngloGold Ashanti for $200 million.
did_you_know_facts: Warke is also a minority partner in Fenway Sports Group, which owns the Boston Red Sox and Liverpool F.C.

name: Lu Lili
about: Lu Lili derives her fortune from a minority stake in East Money Information and a 8.5% stake in Wanda Film Holding.
Lu is the wife of Qi Shi, who founded and chairs East Money Information, a provider of IT and software for the financial services industry in China.
She previously worked at the company's general manager's office.
Lu bought just over 8% of Wanda Film Holding for $306 million in 2023.

name: Chi Fung Cheng
about: Chi Fung "Lawrence" Cheng cofounded semiconductor firm Credo Technology in 2008. He owns a 4% stake in the company and serves as its chief technology officer.
The Cayman Islands-based company went public on the Nasdaq in 2022.
Prior to cofounding Credo, Cheng worked as an engineering director at semiconductor giant Marvell Technology.
Marvell's cofounder Pantas Sutardja was an early investor in Credo Technology and now owns 3% of the company.
Cheng received a master's degree in electrical engineering from Purdue University.

name: Fumio Sakiya
about: Fumio Sakiya founded Rorze, a manufacturer of production equipment for semiconductor and flat-panel display makers, in 1985.
Sakiya was CEO of the Hiroshima Prefecture-based company.until 2015 and chairman for two years after that. He's now a board member and advisor.
Rorze listed on the JASDAQ bourse for startups in 2013 and is now listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
The firm has manufacturing operations in Japan, the U.S., China, Taiwan, South Korea and Vietnam
Santa Clara-based chip-equipment giant Applied Materials is Rorze's biggest customer, accounting for nearly one-fourth of sales.

name: Liu Ming Chung
about: Liu Ming Chung leads Nine Dragons Paper, one of Asia's largest paper producers.
Hong Kong-listed Nine Dragons started out as a supplier of packaging for exporters in China, and now also benefits from consumer demand inside China.
Liu is CEO and deputy chairman of Nine Dragons, while his wife Cheung Yan, also a billionaire, is the chairlady. They are both cofounders of the company, which was established in 1995.
Liu was born in Taiwan and grew up in Brazil. He holds a bachelor's degree in dental surgery from the University of Santo Amaro, in Brazil.
His son Ken Liu joined Nine Dragons' board of directors in 2018, after graduating from Harvard University and working as a consultant for PwC.
did_you_know_facts: His wife Cheung has been dubbed by Chinese media as the country's "wastepaper queen." Liu and Cheung met in Hong Kong and married in the US.

name: Filip Balcaen & family
about: Filip Balcaen derives his fortune from his holding company Enterhold, which invests in a slew of private companies and real estate across Belgium, the Netherlands, China and the U.S., among other countries.
Prior to Enterhold, he led the Balta group, one of Belgium's largest carpet makers, which was founded by his father Paul Balcaen in 1964.
In 2004 Filip sold Balta and soon after started IVC, a manufacturer of vinyl tiles, which he sold to U.S.-based Mohawk Industries in 2015.
He has a controlling stake in Brussels-based Recticel, a company that specializes in insulation boards and panels.
did_you_know_facts: Balcaen lives in an 18th century castle and owns a collection of vintage cars.
In 2023 he bought a 154-feet super yacht called Nilaya.

name: Jenny Lindén Urnes
about: Jenny Lind?n Urnes is the chairman and owner of $1.9 billion (sales) Lind?ngruppen, which she inherited from her father in 2009.
The industrial group owns 50% of H?gan's AB, a leading maker of powdered metal, and Beckers, which produces industrial coatings.
Her father, Ulf G. Lind?n, a former Volvo executive, built up a private stake in H?gan's AB, and took it private in 1987.
Beckers, a former subsidiary of Volvo, came into the family's hands in 1985, when Ulf bought the company from his employer.
In 2013, under Jenny's command, Lind?ngruppen, together with a foundation linked to the Wallenberg family, took H?gan's AB private once again.
did_you_know_facts: H?gan's AB has a one third market share of the world's powdered metals, a product used in construction of metal parts and to remove contaminants from drinking water.
Lind?n Urnes earned a B.A. with a major in philosophy from the University of London; she breeds horses in her free time.

name: Pan Laican
about: Pan Laican derives his fortune from his holdings in soy sauce supplier Foshan Haitian Flavouring and Food.
Pan is now retired from the company.
Haitian was originally known as Foshan Sauce Shop flourishing during the Qianlong years in the mid-Qing Dynasty,

name: Dan Gertler
about: Dan Gertler built a fortune through mining ventures in Africa, primarily in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
In February 2017, he sold his stake in two mines in the Congo to commodities giant Glencore for $960 million; Gertler made an estimated $400 million.
In December 2017, the U.S. government placed Gertler on its sanctions list for his alleged corrupt business deals in the Congo. Sanctions have been eased in recent years.
In June 2018, the U.S. levied sanctions against 14 additional companies of his, including Fleurette Africa Resources and Ventora Development Sasu.
A spokesman for Gertler declined to comment on the U.S. government's allegations.
did_you_know_facts: Gertler's grandfather, Moshe Schnitzer, cofounded the Israel Diamond Exchange in 1947.
He bought his first mine in the Democratic Republic of Congo in 1997 and soon became friends with DRC President Joseph Kabila.

name: Charles Liang
about: Charles Liang and his wife Sara Liu founded AI server and storage maker Super Micro Computer Inc. (commonly known as Supermicro) in 1993.
Liang has served as CEO, president and chairman of the board at Supermicro since the company's founding; Liu is senior vice president.
Headquartered in San Jose, California, Supermicro is a major supplier of Nvidia for AI server design outsourcing.
Liang was born in the southern city of Chiayi, Taiwan.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, University Of Texas At Arlington; Bachelor of Science in Engineering, National Taiwan University

did_you_know_facts: Liang holds several patents for his server technologies.
Liang is the founder and CEO of the Green Earth Foundation, which aims to combat deforestation.
quote: The key to success in technology is designing a company around people committed to work that they love.

name: Neide Helena de Moraes
about: Neide Helena de Moraes is an heir to a stake in Grupo Votorantim, a Brazilian industrial conglomerate.
She is a granddaughter of Jose Ermirio de Moraes, who founded Grupo Votorantim in 1918; she previously appeared on Forbes? billionaires list in 2014.
The company does business in more than 20 countries in the aluminum, pulp and paper, energy, banking and cement industries.
Neide Helena inherited an 8% stake in the family-owned company after the death of her father, Jose Ermirio de Moraes Filho, in 2001.
Her two siblings, Jose Ermirio de Moraes Neto and Jose Roberto Ermirio de Moraes, also inherited Votorantim stakes from their father.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Universidade Presbiteriana Mackenzie

name: Jose Ermirio de Moraes Neto
about: Jose Ermirio de Moraes Neto is an heir to Grupo Votorantim, a Brazilian family-owned industrial conglomerate.
His grandfather and namesake, Jose Ermirio de Moraes, founded Grupo Votorantim in 1918.
The company does business in more than 20 countries in the aluminum, pulp and paper, energy, banking and cement industries.
Jose Ermirio inherited an 8% stake in the company after his father, Jose Ermirio de Moraes Filho, died in 2001.
He previously appeared on Forbes' billionaires list in 2014; his siblings Jose Roberto Ermirio de Moraes and Neide Helena de Moraes also inherited stakes.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Fundacao Getulio Vargas

name: Jose Roberto Ermirio de Moraes
about: Jose Roberto Ermirio de Moraes is an heir to a stake in Brazilian industrial conglomerate Votorantim.
His grandfather, Jose Ermirio de Moraes, founded Grupo Votorantim in 1918; in 2021 the group had revenues of about $7 billion.
The group does business in more than 20 countries in the aluminum, pulp and paper, energy, banking, and cement industries.
Jose Roberto inherited an 8% stake in the family-owned company after the death of his father, Jose Ermirio de Moraes Filho, in 2001.
Jose Roberto Ermirio de Moraes previously appeared on Forbes? list of the World's Billionaires in 2014.
did_you_know_facts: His two siblings, Jose Ermirio de Moraes Neto and Neide Helena de Moraes also inherited stakes in the family company.

name: Huang Yi
about: Huang Yi chairs Zhongsheng Group, one of China's largest national car dealerships.
Zhongsheng focuses on luxury and mid-to-high-end brands such as Mercedes-Benz, Lexus, Porsche and Land Rover.
Huang and Li Guoqiang, Zhongsheng's CEO, established Zhongsheng Group in 1998.
Huang received an undergraduate degree in economics from Xiamen University in 1983.

name: Yang Yuanqing
about: Yang Yuanqing is chairman and CEO of Lenovo, one of China's largest makers of computer hardware.
He joined the company in 1989 and became its CEO twenty years later.
An engaging leader, Yang speaks frequently at conferences (lately on A.I.) and posts often about his business activities on social media.
He sits on the board of Chinese search giant Baidu as an independent director, a post he's held since 2015.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Masters of Science in Technology, University of Science and Technology of China

name: Herbert Sy
about: Herbert Sy is an adviser of SM Investments, a major conglomerate, and a director of SM Prime, the group's property developer.
He is a son of the late SM founder, Henry Sy Sr., and the second-youngest of six children.
His three brothers and two sisters all hold posts in the business, which spans banking, retail, real estate, mining, and hotels.
He is actively involved in the group's supermarket operations, which includes an investment arm.
He has an undergrad degree in management from De La Salle University.
In 2022, SM Investments agreed to acquire Philippine Geothermal Production in a $304 million, all-share deal in a bid to lower its carbon footprint.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Business Administration, De La Salle University

name: Itamar Locks & family
about: Itamar Locks is the son-in-law of Lucia Maggi, who cofounded Andre Maggi Group with her late husband, Andre Maggi.
Amaggi is one of Brazil's largest producers of soybeans and other commodities.
Lucia Maggi cofounded the business with her husband in 1977 and took over as majority shareholder after he died in 2001.
After Andre Maggi died in 2001, his son Blairo Maggi took over as the chief executive of the company.
Locks is one of the controlling shareholders of Amaggi, along with Blairo Maggi, and Hugo de C. Ribeiro.
did_you_know_facts: Locks previously served as the president of the agricultural division of Amaggi.
Amaggi produces approximately 1.2 million tons of soy, corn, and cotton in Brazil each year.

name: Blairo Maggi
about: Blairo Maggi is the son of Andre Maggi and Lucia Maggi, cofounders of Brazil's Andre Maggi Group.
Amaggi is one of Brazil's largest producers of soybeans and other commodities.
He took over as the chief executive of Amaggi after his father's death in 2001. Although he no longer holds the position, he remains a controlling shareholder.
Maggi has previously served as Brazil's minister of agriculture and the governor of the state of Mato Grasso.
did_you_know_facts: Maggi was referred to as the "King of Soy" by Brazilian media during his time leading the business.
Amaggi produces approximately 1.2 million tons of soy, corn, and cotton in Brazil each year.

name: Soegiarto Adikoesoemo
about: Soegiarto Adikoesoemo founded AKR Corporindo as a chemicals trader in 1960 and listed it on the Indonesian Stock Exchange in 1994.
AKR Corporindo is now engaged in petroleum trading and distribution, logistics services, chemical manufacturing and industrial estate.
AKR Corporindo and British oil and gas firm BP's joint venture distributes aviation fuel and operates jointly branded service stations in Indonesia.
Soegiarto is AKR's president commissioner. His son Haryanto is president director.
In September 2024, AKR's East Java industrial estate JIIPE inaugurated the world's largest single line copper smelter by capacity, run by Indonesia-U.S. joint venture Freeport Indonesia.
did_you_know_facts: His son Haryanto Adikoesoemo started collecting art over 25 years ago and has accumulated 800 pieces, including works by Andy Warhol and Mark Rothko.
Haryanto opened a museum dedicated entirely to modern and contemporary art, Museum MACAN, in November 2017.

name: Qin Hua
about: Qin Hua is chairman and CEO of Gambol Pet Group, a pet food company based in China's Shandong province.
Qin became a billionaire after the company went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in August 2023.
Gambol was founded in 2006 and exports to more than 30 countries across Europe, the U.S., Japan and South Korea.
Gambol investors include private equity giant KKR.

name: He Zhenggang
about: He is the second largest shareholder of Leshan Giantstar Farming & Husbandry, a supplier of leather products.
He stepped down as the company's chairman in August 2023.
He is also a director and the majority shareholder of Shanghai-listed chemicals supplier Sichuan Hebang Biotechnology.
He worked for a city government commercial bureau in Leshan, China from 1971 to 1993 and founded Hebang's predecessor company in 1993.
The company listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange on Dec. 18, 2017.

name: Forrest Preston
about: Forrest Preston founded Life Care Centers of America in 1970 and has since made a fortune with facilities that house and care for the elderly.
The private firm operates over 200 nursing homes, assisted living facilities and retirement living communities in 27 states.
Preston is the CEO and sole owner of the company, which is based in Cleveland, Tennessee.
In 2016, the company agreed to pay $145 million to settle a government lawsuit alleging that the firm had over-billed federal healthcare programs.
In February 2020, an LCCA facility in Seattle became the epicenter of Washington's Covid-19 outbreak as nursing homes across the country struggled.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Walla Walla College; Oregon State University

did_you_know_facts: Before founding the company, Preston sold vacuum cleaners, worked as an X-ray technician and ran a printing business with his brother.
His first facility, formerly called Garden Terrace Convalescent Center, is still open today in Cleveland, Tennessee.

name: Sylvia Wedemeyer
about: Sylvia Wedemeyer is a shareholder of Cordes & Graefe, the parent company of the GC Group, a wholesaler that covers a wide range of products for plumbing and HVAC systems.
Founded in 1921 as a pipe and tube trading company, Cordes & Graefe formed the GC Group in 1975 through a series of acquisitions.
Today the company is one of the largest wholesalers in the industry with $17 billion in sales (2023).
The company is 100% owned by the Hollweg family. Sylvia Wedemeyer is the daughter of longtime company leader Uwe Hollweg who died in December 2024.

name: Lu Yiwen
about: Lu Yiwen is a cofounder of jewelry supplier DR Corp.
DR went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2021.
The company is headquartered in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.

name: Jimmy Rane
about: Jimmy Rane is founder and chairman of Great Southern Wood Preserving, which makes decks, fences and other treated lumber products.
Rane is better known as "the Yella Fella," his cowboy alter-ego who appeared in his company's TV commercials.
He and his brother transformed the family's $22,000 (1971 sales) backyard treating plant into a company with nearly $2 billion in annual sales.
Rane served as CEO for more than half a century before retiring from the top job in 2025.

forbes_list.list: The Richest Person In Every State (2025)

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Auburn University; Doctor of Jurisprudence, Samford University

did_you_know_facts: Rane came up with the idea to advertise via short western films after reading about how Frank Perdue branded his chicken.
