He ran the company as a small side business for years while working as a lawyer, before eventually turning to it full-time.
quote: I will hire somebody with character and integrity every single time over somebody who is brilliant.

name: Lu Bin
about: Lu Bin is a director of Neway Valve (Suzhou).
Lu co-founded the company in 1997 with Wang Baoqing, Cheng Zhangwen and Xi Chao.
The company went public in 2014.

name: Wang Baoqing
about: Wang Baoqing is the chairman of Neway Valve (Suzhou).
Wang co-founded the company in 1997 with Lu Bin, Cheng Zhangwen and Xi Chao.
The company went public in 2014.

name: William Lauder
about: William Lauder is a grandson of Estée Lauder, who founded the cosmetics firm, and eldest son of Leonard Lauder, who was CEO and chairman for 17 years.
A member of the family's third generation, he was Estée Lauder's CEO from 2004 to 2009.
In January 2025, he stepped down as executive chairman of the company, a position he'd held since 2009.
He now serves as chairman of Estée Lauder's board of directors.
He lives in a Park Avenue co-op, and has homes in New York's Westchester County and in Aspen, Colorado.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: Lauder graduated from the University of Pennsylvania and now sits on the institution's board. He started lecturing Penn MBA students in 2012.
Lauder joined family's cosmetics company Estee Lauder in 1986 as regional marketing director of Clinique USA. He created the Origins brand in 1990.

name: Martin Herrenknecht
about: Martin Herrenknecht founded tunnel construction machine-maker Herrenknecht AG, in 1977.
He owns almost 96% of the business, with the remaining shares held by his brother.
Herrenknecht had sales of 1.2 billion euros in 2023, its most recent financial disclosure.
Projects built using Herrenknecht machines include the Doha Metro in Qatar, the New York City subway 7-line extension the 18-mile Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel in Virginia.

name: Jeff Tangney
about: Jeff Tangney cofounded Doximity, known as a "LinkedIn for Doctors," in 2010.
Tangney, who is not a doctor, owns over 28% of the $475.4 million (2024 revenue) social media and telehealth network.
More than 80% of U.S. doctors are verified members of Doximity -- the name is a mashup of doctor and proximity -- for professional networking.
Tangney took his first company, mobile medical reference app Epocrates, public in 2011 and later sold it to Athenahealth for $293 million.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, University of Wisconsin Madison; Master of Business Administration, Stanford Graduate School of Business

did_you_know_facts: Tangney's first job was a dishwasher at Pizza Hut.
Tangney started his first company Epocrates in his business school dorm room.

name: Zhang Jianhui
about: Zhang Jianhui is the chairman and CEO of energy storage firm Beijing HyperStrong Technology.
He took the firm public in Shanghai in January 2025, raising 860 million yuan ($121 million).
Before founding HyperStrong in 2011, Zhang worked for the National Semiconductor Corporation in the U.S. and Siemens in China.
His wife, Xu Rui, is a company vice manager.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctorate, University of California at Berkeley; Bachelor of Science, Tsinghua Univeristy; Master of Science, Tsinghua Univeristy

name: Xiang Wenbo
about: Xiang Wenbo is chairman of Sany Group, a heavy equipment manufacturer.
Xiang is one of three billionaires from Sany Group, along with Liang Wengen and Mao Zhongwu.
Xiang is a graduate of Dalian University of Technology with a master's degree in molding.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Dalian University of Technology

name: Vadim Vikulov
about: Vadim Vikulov controls Aston, a Russian agricultural exporter founded by his father in 1992.
Vikulov worked for Sovfracht, a logistic company of USSR's foreign trade, until 1992, when he established a freight and trading company in Germany.
His father, Ivan, was a former KGB officer, founded Aston as a sea- and river- transport business, later expanding to agricultural exports.

Vikulov now sole owner of Aston, one of the largest Russian grain and sunflower oil traders, as well as operator of grain stores, vegetable oil tankers and bulk carries, sunflower oil plants and a marine terminal.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master, Admiral Makarov State University of Maritime and Inland Shipping

name: Tang Xiuguo
about: Tang Xiuguo is one of four founders of Sany Group, one of China's largest suppliers of construction equipment.
He has been the director and president of Sany Group since 2002.
Sany's holding company was founded in Hunan Province in 1989 as a small welding material factory.
Tang holds a bachelor degree in metallic materials from Central South University in 1983.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Central South University

name: Shrikant Badve
about: Shrikant Badve is the founder and managing director of Pune-based automotive parts supplier Belrise Industries, which makes everything from shock absorbers to rearview mirrors for motorcycles, cars and commercial vehicles.
The company's marquee clients include motorbike manufacturers Eicher, Hero Motocorp and TVS, as well as auto companies Jaguar Land Rover and Mahindra and Mahindra.
Badve started out making fasteners in 1988 in a 150-square-foot shed with three machines and two workers.
Belrise shares were listed in May 2025 at an 11% premium to the issue price.
His wife Supriya sits on the board and his sons, Sumedh (a Harvard MBA) and Swastid (a Wharton graduate), lead business development and strategy respectively.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University

name: Chris Wallin
about: Armed with a geology degree, Chris Wallin was the Queensland government's chief coal geologist before starting his company, QCoal, in 1989.
He was a billionaire in 2011 and 2012, before plunging coal prices hammered his fortune. He reappeared on the list of Australia's 50 richest in 2019 after a five-year absence.
He rejoined the billionaire ranks after QCoal posted a five-fold increase in net profit in 2022 and paid him A$300 million in dividends.
In 2025, QGold launched a takeover bid for shares it did not own in Venus Metals Corp for A$0.21 per share, ending up with a nearly 32% stake after the bid closed in January 2026.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, University of Queensland

did_you_know_facts: He's lived in the same house in the suburban Brisbane neighborhood of The Gap for reportedly 30 years.
Wallin also owns a clutch of smaller mining stakes.
In 2024, QCoal's philanthropic arm QCoal Foundation established the Christopher Wallin Prize for Excellence in Geology to support educational opportunities in Queens

name: Alexander Savelyev & family
about: Alexander Savelyev is the controlling shareholder Bank of Saint Petersburg, which is among the 20 largest banks in Russia.
He was named CEO of the bank in 2001 and now owns about 27%, while his daughter and top managers control another 28%.
In 2022, while most Russian banks suffered losses, Bank of Saint Petersburg remained profitable.
Prior to entering the banking industry, Savelyev worked in several transport enterprises during the 1980s and 1990s.
The Bank of Saint Petersburg was sanctioned by U.S. Department of Treasury in 2023.
did_you_know_facts: Russian president Vladimir Putin owns 230 shares of Bank of Saint Petersburg, according to his tax statement.

name: George Raymond Zage III
about: George Raymond Zage III is the founder and CEO of Singapore-based investment firm Tiga Investments.
The bulk of his wealth comes from a stake in LGBTQ social networking app Grindr, where he sits on the board.
Grindr went public on the New York Stock Exchange through a SPAC merger in 2022.
Zage worked with U.S. hedge fund Farallon Capital Management for 18 years before setting up Tiga Investments in 2017.
He also has interests in Indonesia's property developer Lippo Karawaci and Australia's mining company Whitehaven Coal.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, University of Illinois

name: Rubens Ometto Silveira Mello
about: Rubens Ometto Silveira Mello became the world's first ethanol billionaire in 2007. Cosan, his sugar giant, is listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
The company's origins date to 1936, when Ometto's grandparents established a sugarcane mill in Sao Paulo.
After several takeovers, Cosan became one of the world's largest growers and processors of sugarcane and one of the largest producers of ethanol.
Besides his Cosan shares, Ometto also holds a portfolio of real estate investments.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, Polytechnic School of the University of Sao Paulo

did_you_know_facts: His combativeness earned him the moniker "the tractor," in part because of the long legal fights in order to gain control of Cosan.
quote: We have to recognize merits where they are, and stop complaining about what could have been better.

name: Lee Hae-jin
about: Lee Hae-jin is a cofounder of Naver, South Korea's No. 1 search engine.
In 2018, he stepped down from Naver's board but remained its global investment officer, focusing on the company's expansion. In 2025, he returned as chairman to drive the company's AI business.
In 2021, Naver and SoftBank agreed to a joint venture, taking control of their respective subsidiaries Line and Yahoo Japan.
In November 2025, Naver said its payment arm, Naver Financial, will acquire crypto exchange operator Dunamu in a stock swap that values the combined entity at $13.6 billion.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Seoul National University

did_you_know_facts: He started Naver while working at Samsung SDS in the late 1990s.
In 2016 his messaging app, Line, went public and raised $1 billion during its dual listing in New York and Tokyo.
Lee's son, Seung-joo, is a singer-songwriter and producer, who goes by the stage name Loren (stylized as LØREN).

name: He Zhaoxi
about: He Zhaoxi is the chairman of Sangfor Technologies, a supplier of IT infrastructure solutions.
The company went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2018.
He graduated from China University of Science and Technology in 1998 with a degree in automatic control and economic management.
After graduating, He worked for Huawei Technologies from 1998 to 2000.
He cofounded Sangfor Technologies in 2000.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, Huazhong University of Science and Technology

name: Adrian Paval
about: Adrian Paval and his brother, Dragos, own Dedeman, a leading Romanian construction materials and do-it-yourself home products retailer.
The $2 billion (sales) company's 57 stores stock some 60,000 products, ranging from tools and building supplies to furniture and appliances.
The brothers founded the business in 1992 with a single location in Bacau, Romania.
They also own shares of several publicly traded Romanian companies and a portfolio of real estate in Bucharest and the northern city of Cluj.

name: Liu Shengjun
about: Liu Shengjun is the second-largest shareholder of Himile Mechanical Science and Technology, a manufacturer of tire molds and rubber machinery, large mechanical components, and CNC machine tools. He was formerly the supervisor of the company.
The company went public in 2011.
The company has subsidiaries in the United States, Europe, India, and Brazil.

name: Yuan Jiandong & family
about: Yuan Jiandong chairs Shanghai-listed BrightGene Bio-Medical Technology, a pharmaceutical supplier.
Following university, he worked for U.S.-based Enzo Biochem from 1998 to 2001 before returning to China to start BrightGene.
He holds an undergraduate degree in chemistry from Peking University and a Ph.D. in chemistry from the State University of New York.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctorate, State University of New York at Albany; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Peking University

name: Eduard Kucera
about: Eduard Kučera is the cofounder of Prague-based internet security company Avast Software.
In 1988, he and Pavel Baudis, with whom he'd worked at Research Institute of Mathematical Machines, cofounded ALWIL to sell an antivirus software.
Following the fall of Communism in 1989, the pair broke off to establish what would become Avast.
Now run by an outside CEO, Avast, which secures online activities for more than 435 million users, went public in 2018.
In 2021, Avast, which Kučera chaired Avast from 2006 to 2014, agreed to merge with cybersecurity firm NortonLifeLock.
did_you_know_facts: Kučera is one of the biggest watch collectors in Czechia; he also owns a significant vintage car collection with his son.

name: Li Jiaquan
about: Li Jiaquan chairs Lomon Group, a chemical supplier.
Li founded the predecessor company of Lomon in Sichuan Province in 1985.
Li sold Lomon's titanium dioxide business to Shenzhen-listed Henan Billions Chemicals for $1.3 billion in 2016.

name: Lucy Guo
about: Lucy Guo cofounded data labeling giant Scale AI, and founded and runs creator platform Passes.
Guo ranked as the world's youngest self-made woman billionaire from April 2025 to December 2025.
The daughter of electrical engineers who emigrated from China, Guo taught herself to code in elementary school so that she could adopt virtual pets in a game called Neopets.
She studied computer science and human-computer interactions at Carnegie Mellon University but dropped out before graduating to become a Thiel Fellow.
Guo launched Scale AI in 2016 but left in 2018 amid a falling out with her cofounder, Alexandr Wang. She still owns roughly 3% of the company, which is the source of most of her fortune.
In June 2025, Meta bought 49% of Scale AI for about $14 billion and Scale paid its shareholders a hefty dividend.
She founded Passes, a platform for creators and celebrities to connect with fans that's similar to Patreon and OnlyFans, in 2022; she is CEO and has raised $50 million from investors.

name: Cai Zaihua
about: Cai Zaihua is the chairman of Hubei Zhenhua Chemical, a producer of chromium salts and Vitamin K3.
The company markets its products in more than 60 countries and regions.
The company went public in 2016.

name: Aditya Khemka
about: Aditya Khemka is the founder and managing director of Aditya Infotech, which provides security surveillance products like CCTVs and security cameras.
The Delhi-based company sells its products under the CP Plus brand.
Aditya Infotech has a wide range of offerings, from smart home IoT cameras to thermal cameras and AI solutions.
His father Hari Khemka is company chairman and the older of his two sons, Ananmay, has a board seat.
Khemka listed the company in August 2025 at a 50% premium to the issue price.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Commerce, Shri Ram College of Commerce

name: Anas Sefrioui & family
about: Anas Sefrioui is the founder and CEO of listed homebuilder Groupe Addoha, which has prospered thanks to government contracts.
He made his fortune developing low-cost housing in Morocco.
His daughter Kenza is the company's deputy chairman.

name: Cheng Zhangwen
about: Cheng Zhangwen is a director of Neway Valve (Suzhou).
Cheng co-founded the company in 1997 with Wang Baoqing, Lu Bin and Xi Chao.
The company went public in 2014.
The company has subsidiaries in the United States, Dubai, the Netherlands, Italy, Singapore and Nigeria.

name: Peter Salanki
about: Peter Salanki is cofounder and chief technology officer of data center giant CoreWeave.
Originally from Sweden, he was granted the title of cofounder despite joining the company in 2019, two years after it was founded (originally as a crypto outfit).
His fellow cofounders Brannin McBee, Brian Venturo, and Michael Intrator are also billionaires, as is early investor and director Jack Cogen.
CoreWeave went public in March 2025 at an approximately $23 billion valuation.
The company sells computing power mostly to AI companies.

name: Mao Zhongwu
about: Mao Zhongwu is a founder of the Sany Group, a construction equipment manufacturer.
Mao is one of three billionaires from Sany Group including Liang Wengen and Xiang Wenbo.
Mao resigned as a director at Sany International in October 2019.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, National University of Singapore

name: Markus Persson
about: Markus "Notch" Persson made his fortune selling the rights to his game Minecraft to Microsoft.
In September 2014, after selling 15 million copies of Minecraft across gaming consoles, Persson sold out to Microsoft in a $2.5 billion cash deal.
Persson has since been jetting around the world while programming new games in his spare time.
An avid social media user, Persson has been open about the downsides of instant success as he used Reddit to express loneliness.
Persson has said he mostly spends money on computer gear and traveling, though he bought a $70 million home in Beverly Hill in December 2014.
did_you_know_facts: Persson created Minecraft as a hobby project, and released the boxy designed game in indie-game forums, which won immediate popularity.
Persson is a member of high IQ society Mensa.
quote: Partying is not a sane way to spend money, but it's fun. When we were young we did not have a lot of money at all, so I thought, if I ever get rich, I'm not going to become one of those boring rich people that doesn't spend money.

name: Aerin Lauder
about: Aerin Lauder, the eldest daughter of billionaire Ronald Lauder, serves as style and image director at beauty company Estée Lauder.
Lauder has worked for Estée Lauder, founded by her grandmother, since 1992. She served as a board member from 2004 to 2016.
In 2012, she founded luxury lifestyle brand AERIN, which sells everything from lamps to handbags. The line is sold in 45 countries.
Her sister, Jane Lauder, a former executive vice president at Estée Lauder, also sits on the board.
In July 2019, Aerin launched a hotel amenity line featuring bath and body products.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pennsylvania

did_you_know_facts: Aerin inherited her grandmother's East Hampton home and still lives there in the summer with her family.
Eric Zinterhofer, Aerin's husband, cofounded private equity firm Searchlight Capital in 2010.

name: Lucio Co
about: Lucio Co and his wife Susan control and run Puregold Price Club, a chain of hypermarkets and supermarkets they cofounded in 1998.
Starting with a location in Mandaluyong City, the chain now boasts more than 640 stores across the Philippines.
Susan is chairman and Lucio a director of Puregold. Their son, Ferdinand Vincent, helps them run the company as president.
The Cos also head listed Cosco Capital, which has stakes in liquor distribution and real estate businesses.
They have interests in gaming and hotels as well.

name: Wang Mingwang
about: Wang Mingwang is the co-founder of China electronics maker Sunwoda, a supplier of lithium-ion battery modules.
Wang Wei, his brother and co-founder, chairs the Shenzhen-headquartered company.
Sunwoda's customers include Apple and Huawei.

name: Swift Xie
about: Swift Xie heads up marketing at Dajiang Innovation Technology Co. (DJI), the world's largest consumer drone manufacturer.
Xie is the high school best friend of DJI founder and CEO Frank Wang, who nicknamed him "fat-headed fish."
Xie owns an estimated 12% stake in DJI.

name: Yao Hsiao Tung
about: Yao Hsiao Tung is the executive chairman and CEO of Hi-P International, which the former DuPont executive acquired as a small tool maker in 1983.
Today it is one of Singapore's largest contract manufacturers of smartphones, tablet computers and consumer electronics with customers such as Apple.
In 2017, he acquired the stake of longtime partner Molex, a manufacturer of electrical connectors owned by U.S. billionaire Charles Koch.
He delisted the company from the Singapore Stock Exchange at a valuation of $1.2 billion in 2021, with the aim of securing greater flexibility in running the business. He plans to relist it by 2030.
In 2024, Temasek-backed 65 Equity Partners invested S$100 million ($74 million) in the company.
did_you_know_facts: Yao was born in mainland China but moved to Taiwan as a child; he's now a Singaporean citizen.

name: Mark Pincus
about: Mark Pincus cofounded Zynga, an online social game maker known for Words With Friends, Mafia Wars and FarmVille.
A serial entrepreneur who made early investments in Facebook and Twitter, Pincus launched several successful businesses before creating Zynga in 2007.
Pincus served as CEO of Zynga for seven years. The company, which went public in 2011, was acquired by gaming company Take-Two Interactive in 2022 for $12.7 billion.
In 2018 he founded investment firm Reinvent Capital, which has put money into SpaceX, health insurance firm Oscar and rideshare firm Lyft.
He has launched three SPACs, including one that took electric air taxi firm Joby Aviation public and one that took insurance firm Hippo Technologies public.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pennsylvania; Master of Business Administration, Harvard University

did_you_know_facts: Zynga is named after Pincus' late dog, Zinga, an American Bulldog. The company's red and white logo is a rendering of the bulldog.

name: Alexander Linnik
about: Alexander Linnik co-founded Miratorg, the leading Russian pork and beef producer, with his brother Victor, in 1995.
Miratorg is the largest owner of agricultural lands in Russia. Company controls about 1.4 million hectares, equivalent to 3.4 million acres.
Miratorg produces more than 400 products, including pork, Black Angus and Wagyu beef, pink veal, lamb ribs, sausages, poultry, frozen vegetables, dumplings and ready to eat meals.
Miratorg owns supermarket chain under brand Miratorg and restaurant chain Steak & Burger.
In 1990s Alexander and Victor Linnik earned first capital by organizing leisure activities for foreign tourists in Moscow. Then brothers started to import beef and pork from South America.

Miratorg produces more than 400 products, including pork, Black Angus and Wagyu beef, pink veal, lamb ribs, sausages, poultry, frozen vegetables, dumplings and ready to eat meals.

name: Mofatraj Munot
about: Mumbai real estate magnate Mofatraj Munot started developing property in 1969 after working with his uncle.
Munot snatched lucrative construction contracts during the 1970s in the Middle East oil boom, where he built the palace of the ruler of Sharjah.
Today, his Kalpataru, run by son Parag, has completed more than 110 projects in nine cities.
In July 2025, he listed the property development arm, Kalpataru. Engineering contractor Kalpataru Projects International, is Munot's other listed asset.
did_you_know_facts: The name Kalpataru is derived from Kalpavruksha, a mythological tree of wish fulfillment.
Munot is fond of Urdu poetry.

name: Michael Cagney
about: Mike Cagney is cofounder of blockchain technology company Figure Technology Solutions.
Cagney cofounded Figure with his wife June Ou in 2018 and took the company public on the Nasdaq in September 2025.
Cagney served as CEO of Figure until 2024, while Ou served as chief operating officer until 2022. Both still sit on the company's board.
Before Figure, Cagney cofounded fintech company SoFi in 2011 and ran it as chairman and CEO until 2017. Ou served as SoFi's chief technology officer from 2012 to 2017.
Cagney started his career at Wells Fargo and went on to found wealth management software company Finaplex and hedge fund Cabezon Investment Group.

name: Ge Tairong
about: Ge Tairong derives his wealth from a stake in Zhengjiang Rongtai Electric Material, a producer of temperature-resistant mica tapes.
His wife, Cao Meisheng, is the company's chairman and CTO.
Zhejiang Rongtai supplies to sectors including robotics and new energy vehicles.
It went public in Shanghai in 2023, raising $151 million.

name: Chua Thian Poh
about: High school dropout Chua Thian Poh got his start making hooks and spikes for the logging industry.
In 1987 Chua founded luxury property developer Ho Bee Land, known for building high-end condos in Sentosa, Singapore's island resort.
The company has a diversified portfolio that includes commercial property overseas, notably in London and Munich.
Since 2020 it has bought five sites in suburban Australia where it plans to build master-planned residential communities.
In 2022, Ho Bee acquired the Scalpel office tower in London's financial district for $961 million.
did_you_know_facts: Chua was once Singapore's non-resident ambassador to the Republic of Maldives.
He's set up a family office called One Hill Capital.
In 2018, Ho Bee purchased a London office block for $850 million.
His son, Nicholas, is Ho Bee Land's CEO.
quote: We learned from the Asian financial crisis. Spread the risk. Don't rely on a single market. Diversify.

name: Andrei Filatov
about: Andrei Filatov made his first money selling imported goods while taking part in international chess tournaments.
In 1996 together with Konstantin Nikolaev and Nikita Mishin, he founded a transport joint venture with Alexei Mordashov. They later bought him.
The trio previously owned more than a third of Globaltrans, the biggest private rail transport operator in Russia.
In December of 2017 all three withdrew from port business, selling their stakes in Global Ports.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Belarusian Academy of Physical Culture and Sports

did_you_know_facts: Filatov is the president of Russian Chess Federation.
Filatov owns wine production farm La Grace Dieu Des Prieurs in France, founded in 1885. The vineyard produces 35,000 bottles of wine a year.

name: Ma Fei
about: Ma Fei is the chairman of Shenzhen FRD Science and Technology, a supplier of electronics materials.
Ma Fei founded Shenzhen FRD in 2014.
FRD listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2014.

name: Yang Yunchun
about: Yang Yunchun is the chairman and general manager of Sai MicroElectronics, a producer of micro sensors.
The company is headquartered in Beijing.
The company went public in 2015.

name: Rajeev Gulati
about: Third generation scion Rajeev Gulati runs Delhi-based spice manufacturer MDH, which makes a range of Indian spices, including curry powders.
Gulati became chairman after the death of his father Dharampal Gulati, who was the face of brand appearing on all the packs and in TV commercials.
MDH has a factory in Sharjah to supply to the Middle Eastern market.
The business was founded by Gulati's grandfather in 1919 as Mahashian Di Hatti, a Punjabi phrase that translates into gentleman's shop.
did_you_know_facts: MDH's flagship product is Kitchen King, a mix of different spices.
In 2024, Hong Kong recalled specific MDH products saying they contained an excessive amount of ethylene oxide, a carcinogen. But tests by India's food regulator.

name: Suh Kyung-bae
about: Suh Kyung-bae is the chairman of Amorepacific, South Korea's largest cosmetic and skincare maker by revenue.
He's capitalized on the Hallyu wave, a keen interest in Korean pop culture that has swept Asia and the U.S.
The only one out of six children interested in the business, Suh joined the company in the 1980s and became CEO in 1997.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Yonsei University; Master of Business Administration, Samuel Curtis Johnson Graduate School of Management

did_you_know_facts: Amorepacific traces its roots to Suh's grandmother, who sold camellia oil as a hair treatment across the Korean peninsula.
In the 1960s Amorepacific hired women who went from door to door selling products on commission; some of them had lost their husbands in the Korean War.

name: Yang Xuegang
about: Yang Xuegang is the chairman and CEO of China Risun Group, a supplier of coke and chemicals.
Founded in 1995, China Risunis headquartered in Beijing.
Yang Xuegangworked at the Dongwushi Reservoir Management Center-- under a government water bureau -- earlier in his career.
Yang Xuegang holds an executive master's degree in business administration from Hebei University of Technology in Tianjin.

name: David Xueling Li
about: David Xueling Li is cofounder and director of JOYY, a Nasdaq-listed, Singapore-headquartered live streaming and social media platform.
Before cofounding JOYY, Li was the chief editor at Chinese news portal Netease.com.
Earlier in his career, Li founded CFP.cn, a copyright trading platform for journalists and amateur photographers.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts, Renmin University of China

name: Michael Wisser
about: Michael Wisser controls Wisag, a family-owned German facilities and logistics business.
The company, which was founded by his father, Claus, provides services that include aircraft loading and unloading, freight services and passenger transfers, and commercial cleaning.
Wisag has annual revenue of reported more than 3 billion euros, according to its most recent financial filings.
The company's motto is ?Let's end the impossible.?

name: Cao Yuhua & family
about: Cao Yuhua is chairman of Wuxi Best Precision Machinery, a manufacturer of precision components, intelligent equipment and fixtures for auto parts.
The company's products are widely used in new energy vehicles, industrial machinery and robots.
More than one-third of its revenue comes from overseas markets in Asia, Europe and the Americas.
Before founding the company in 1997, Cao worked at a machinery factory in Wuxi.
His daughter Cao Yi serves as vice chairman.

name: Adriaan Mol
about: Mol is the founder, CEO, and a large shareholder of Dutch payment service provider Mollie.
The unicorn raised an $800 million Series C round in 2021 at a valuation of $6.5 billion.
But it was valued at just over $2 billion in late 2025 after it agreed to acquire fintech company GoCardless in an all-stock deal.
Mol was never interested in school and began programming at the age of 14.
He is also the cofounder of cloud communications company MessageBird, and runs a family investment office called Spacetime.
did_you_know_facts: Mol comes from a family of artists and his father, Pieter Laurens Mol, has been represented in numerous collections around the world, including the MoMA in New York.
Mol once accidentally hacked into a South African telecom operator that allowed him to send text messages to his friends for free.

name: Li Xuhui
about: Li Xuhui was a director and vice president of Foshan Haitian Flavouring and Food before she left in 2016.
Li managed Haitian's oyster sauce factory from 1999 to 2010.
Pang Kang and Cheng Xue, chairman and vice chairman of Haitian, are also billionaires.

name: Carson Brice
about: Carson Brice is one of four sisters of Frank Holding Jr., who has been chairman and CEO of First Citizens Bank, a publicly-traded commercial bank, since 2008.
Brice's grandfather, Robert Powell Holding, became an employee of the bank in 1918, and became president by 1935, before passing it down to Frank's father, Lewis Holding.
Today, Brice, her three sisters, and her brother Frank collectively own about 20% of the bank.

name: LeBron James
about: LeBron James is the first active NBA player to become a billionaire.
Born to a 16-year-old single mother, he lived with an assortment of family members, friends and neighbors, plus his youth football coach, before being drafted by the Cleveland Cavaliers in 2003.
James has since gone on to earn upwards of $500 million in pretax salary from stints with the Cavaliers, the Miami Heat and his current team, the Los Angeles Lakers.
He has raked in more than $1 billion (pretax) off the court, according to Forbes estimates, from his business ventures and endorsement deals with brands including Nike.
Key to his billionaire status: James has been more than a pitchman, taking equity in brands he works with, including Beats by Dre.
His LeBron James Family Foundation opened its first elementary school in 2018 and has pledged to spend more than $40 million to send kids to college.

personal_stats.label: Agent
personal_stats.value: Rich Paul, Brad Slater, Josh Pyatt, Rich Paul

personal_stats.label: Agency
personal_stats.value: Klutch Sports Group, WME, WME, Klutch Sports Group

personal_stats.label: Sponsors
personal_stats.value: Amazon, Beats Electronics, DraftKings, Fanatics, LVMH Louis Vuitton Moet Hennessy, Mattel, Nike, Taco Bell, Richard Mille

did_you_know_facts: James has publicly dreamed about one day owning an NBA team. As an investor in Fenway Sports Group, he already owns stakes in pro baseball, soccer and hockey teams.
In 2021, James sold a minority stake in his movie and TV production business, the SpringHill Company, to a handful of investors at a $725 million valuation.

name: Xu Xudong & family
about: Xu Xudong chairs Ningbo Xusheng Auto Technology.
Xusheng is a supplier of gear boxes and battery protection shells to Tesla.
Other customers include Eaton, BMW and Bosch.

name: Claire Bristow
about: Claire Bristow is one of four sisters of Frank Holding, Chairman and CEO of First Citizens Bank, a $31 billion (market cap) commercial banking chain, since 2008.
Bristow's grandfather, Robert Powell Holding, became an employee of the bank in 1918, and became president by 1935, before passing it down to Frank's father, Lewis Holding.
Today, Bristow, her three sisters, and her brother Frank collectively own about 20% of the bank.

name: Jared Smith
about: Jared Smith cofounded the software company Qualtrics in Provo, Utah in 2002 with his brother, Ryan, and father, Scott; Ryan was the CEO, Jared was president.
Three days before its scheduled IPO in January 2019, Qualtrics was acquired by German software firm SAP for $8 billion in cash.
Jared owned about 14% of the company at the time of the sale.
Qualtrics sold a second time in March 2023 to Silver Lake and CPP Investments at $12.5 billion valuation.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, London School of Economics

name: Andy Fang
about: Andy Fang is a cofounder of food delivery app DoorDash and serves as its head of consumer engineering.
He owns about a 4% stake in DoorDash, which listed its shares on the New York Stock Exchange in early December 2020.

name: Lee Kar Whatt
about: Lee Kar Whatt is cofounder and managing director of Eco-Shop Marketing, a dollar store chain with more than 400 outlets across Malaysia.
Lee started his career with construction and renovation jobs before setting up his own company in 1994.
He ventured into retail in 2002, and a year later opened the first discount store with his brother Lee Tiong Bin and two other partners.
Creador, a South and Southeast Asia-focused private equity firm, which acquired a 10% stake in Eco-Shop in 2019 for an undisclosed amount, has since sold its shares.
Eco-Shop debuted on Bursa Malaysia in May 2025 after raising RM974 million ($245 million) in the country's largest IPO that year.

name: Rajju Shroff
about: Rajju Shroff is the founder of BSE-listed crop protection company UPL.
After its $4.2 billion acquisition of Arysta LifeSciences in 2018, UPL became one of the top agrochemical companies in the world.
UPL's product range includes insecticides, fungicides and seeds.
Shroff's older son Jai is the company's chief executive officer and vice chairman.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Mumbai

did_you_know_facts: The company was started in 1969 to produce red phosphorus for industrial chemicals.
UPL debuted on Forbes Asia's prestigious Fab 50 list in 2017.
quote: What India's farmers need is training in modern farm practices.

name: Brad Kelley
about: Brad Kelley, a Kentucky native and a farmer's son, built a fortune from discount cigarettes.
He built Commonwealth Brands, maker of USA Gold and Malibu cigarettes, and sold it for $1 billion in 2001.
Kelley has since used that cash to become one of the largest landowners in the U.S., with over 500,000 acres from Hawaii to Florida.
Kelley owns historic stud farm Calumet in Kentucky, which had three starters in the 2017 Kentucky Derby.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Diploma, High School; Drop Out, Western Kentucky University

did_you_know_facts: In 2020, Kelley sold travel guide Lonely Planet, which he had bought seven years earlier from the BBC for $75 million.
His horse English Channel has sired offspring that have nabbed over $57 million in prize money.

name: Wu Xushun & family
about: Wu Xushun is a cofounder of Wuhu Shunrong Sanqi Interactive Entertainment Network Technology in China.
Wuhu Shunrong Auto Parts, which is listed on the Shenzhen stock exchange, acquired 60% of Sanqi Interactive Entertainment Shanghai Technology in 2014.
Following the acquisition, Wuhu Shunrong Auto Parts was rebranded as Wuhu Shunrong Sanqi Interactive Entertainment Network Technology.
Wu dropped out of school after he finished middle high school in 1963. He was once a government official in Xitan in Nanling County in Anhui Province.

name: Jordi Rubiralta
about: Jordi Rubiralta derives his fortune from Werfen, a diagnostics company based in Madrid.
Founded by his late father Josep María Rubiralta and uncle Francisco in 1966, today the company covers diagnostics in hemostasis, acute care, transfusion, autoimmunity and transplants.
Rubiralta chaired the company until 2019 but remains on the board.
He led the expansion of Werfen in Germany and the U.S. with the acquisition of Tem and Accriva Diagnostics.
Rubiralta's family office, Yukon Capital, has carried out some of the most high-profile real estate transactions in Spain in recent years.

name: Nikesh Arora
about: Nikesh Arora has been chairman and CEO of cybersecurity company Palo Alto Networks since 2018.
The firm's stock has soared under Arora's leadership, making both him and the company's founder, Nir Zuk, billionaires.
Arora has netted nearly $800 million (before taxes) exercising options and selling shares since 2023.
He previously worked at Google for nearly a decade, where he rose to chief business officer, before leaving for Japanese investment giant SoftBank in 2014.
Arora was promoted to president and chief operating officer of SoftBank in 2015 and touted as the likely successor to the firm's billionaire founder Masayoshi Son.
Things didn't go as planned, and Arora resigned from SoftBank in 2016. He ended up cashing out at least $360 million (before taxes) during his short stint at the company.

name: Vladimir Bogdanov
about: Vladimir Bogdanov made his fortune in oil drilling. He was appointed chief executive of Surgutneftegas when he was 33.
In the early 1990s he and fellow managers privatized the company, which is famous for its thrift and avoiding expensive purchases.
In 2016, he was awarded Hero of Labour of the Russian Federation by Vladimir Putin "for special labor service for the country and people".
In 2018, Bogdanov was sanctioned by the U.S. and in 2022 he was sanctioned by the European Union.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Tyumen Industrial Institute

did_you_know_facts: Bogdanov is often called the "Siberian hermit," because he rarely leaves the remote town of Surgut and avoids public attention.
His Surgutneftegas managed to accumulate a huge cash pile of $56 billion at 2021, much more than the company's market capitalization.

name: Yves-Loic Martin
about: Yves-Loic Martin is the former chief technology officer of Eurofins Scientific, a laboratory testing company listed on the French stock exchange.
Martin owns about 10% of the company, which went public in 1997.
He joined Eurofins in 1992 and became chief technology officer in 1998. He stepped down in 2015 but remains a board member.
Eurofins has 400 labs in 41 countries and is prominent in food and pharmaceutical products testing.
Martin's billionaire brother, Gilles, founded the lab in 1987 and remains CEO.

name: Binny Bansal
about: Former Amazon executive Binny Bansal teamed up with pal Sachin Bansal in 2007 to found Flipkart as an online seller of books, and later grew it into an e-commerce giant.
The duo, who share the same surname but are not related, pooled $6,000 of their combined savings and started operating out of their apartment.
In 2018, Walmart bought a 77% stake in India-based Flipkart for $16 billion in what was reportedly then the world's biggest deal for an internet firm.
In 2023, Bansal sold his remaining 1.8% stake to Walmart in a deal that reportedly valued Flipkart at $35 billion.
He's now chairman of xto10X, an Indian firm that he cofounded with two former Flipkart colleagues, which helps startups scale up their operations.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Technology, Indian Institute of Technology

name: Daniel Calugar
about: Dan Calugar is a private investor based in Las Vegas, Nevada.
Calugar worked as a tax lawyer in Atlanta the late 1970s and 1980s before switching to investing in mutual funds.
He has invested using data-driven strategies across mutual funds, stocks, hedge funds, structured fixed income, volatility and managed futures.
He now primarily invests in an externally managed energy strategy and an in-house algorithmic stock trading program he developed internally.
In 2003, he settled alleged charges of fraud through improper late trading and market timing with the SEC for $225 million. He did not admit or deny the charges.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Business Administration, University of North Florida; LLM, University of Florida; JD, University of Florida

did_you_know_facts: Calugar attended the Air Force Academy and is a commercial pilot with more than 3,500 hours.
Calugar has flown over 200 Angel Flight missions, providing free air transport for passengers in need of medical treatment and for community service.

name: Peng Qian
about: Peng Qian is the founder and chairman of Wuhan Jingce Electronic Group, a manufacturer of testing equipment in the semiconductor, display and new energy industries.
Before founding the company, Peng worked in market sales at Guangzhou ASPEC Environmental Instruments, a Chinese environmental testing equipment manufacturer.
Wuhan Jingce Electronic Group listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2016.

name: Jan-Hendrik Goldbeck
about: Jan-Hendrik Goldbeck is co-CEO of the eponymous construction giant founded by his father Ortwin Goldbeck in 1969.
Goldbeck's projects include factories, warehouses, schools, offices and residential properties.
The company, which employs 12,500 people, works on more than 500 projects annually.
Goldbeck and his brothers, Jörg-Uwe and Joachim, each own about a third of the company.

name: Jörg-Uwe Goldbeck
about: Jörg-Uwe Goldbeck is co-CEO of the eponymous construction company, which his father, Ortwin Goldbeck, started in 1969 with just seven employees.
One of Germany's largest builders, Goldbeck's projects include factories, warehouses, schools, offices, parking lots and residential properties.
With more than 100 locations worldwide, the builder employs 12,500 people and manages more than 500 projects annually.
Goldbeck was one of the main developers for the Telsa factory in Germany.
He and his brothers, Jan-Hendrik (co-CEO) and Jörg-Uwe, each own about a third of the company.

name: Joachim Goldbeck
about: Joachim Goldbeck derives his fortune from the eponymous construction company founded by his father, Ortwin Goldbeck, in 1969.
His two brothers are co-CEOs of the German builder, which has 12,500 employees and 100 locations worldwide.
One of its country's largest developers, Goldbeck completes more than 500 projects annually; its services include factories, warehouses, offices, schools, parking lots and residential buildings.
He and his brothers each own about a third of the company.

name: Elly Reisman
about: Elly Reisman cofounded Toronto-based homebuilder Great Gulf Homes in 1975.
Great Gulf has built more than 80,000 homes across North America.
He and members of his family are also major shareholders in Ashton Woods Homes, an Atlanta-based builder also active in Austin, Charleston, Dallas, Houston, Orlando, Phoenix, Raleigh and San Antonio.

name: Mu Rongjun
about: Mu Rongjun is a cofounder, an executive director and a senior vice president of Meituan Dianping, the Yelp equivalent in China.
Before cofounding the company, Mu worked as a senior software engineer and project manager at Baidu, China's dominant search engine, for two years.
Mu also cofounded fanfou.com, a social media company specializing in microblogging, where he worked as an engineering director for two years.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master, Tsinghua University; Bachelor of Engineering, Tsinghua University

name: Yan Zhi
about: A former advertising executive, Yan Zhi chairs Hong Kong-listed Zall Smart Commerce Group, previously called Zall Group.
The firm started with shopping mall development and then got into e-commerce as well as wholesale trading, logistics and warehousing.
Yan holds an EMBA from the Cheung Kong Graduate School.
Yan holds 30% of Z-Bank, a Wuhan-based bank that specializes in lending to small businesses involved in supply chain transactions.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Wuhan University

name: Alexander Rakshin & family
about: Alexander Rakshin is the founder and owner of Maria-Ra, a Russian retail chain.
He founded his first Maria-Ra store in 1993 in Barnaul and has built the business into Siberia's largest retail chain with more than 1,300 locations.
Rakshin has 25% in the most operational companies. His family members (wife, son and daughter) own the same stakes.
The family also invests in commercial real estate, including shopping malls and markets, as well as office buildings in Siberia, Moscow and Saint Petersburg.
Rakshin got his start in business in 1990 when he and his partners established fur farm with silver foxes and minks to produce fur hats. He left the venture to start Maria-Ra three years later.
did_you_know_facts: Rashkin finished won second-place in the 1973 USSR junior in cross-country skiing championship and worked as physical education teacher in Barnaul, Siberia.
His retail business is named after his mother, Maria Rakshina.

name: Ronald Clarke
about: Ronald Clarke is the CEO and chairman of Corpay, a $3.9 billion (sales) digital payments company.
The Atlanta-based company offers businesses credit cards geared to travel expenses like gas, tolls and lodging.
Clarke joined the company in 2000. Ten years later, he took it public on the New York Stock Exchange under its previous name, FleetCor.
Corpay has some 800,000 customers and operates in more than 100 countries worldwide.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Colby College; Master of Business Administration, Cornell University

name: Philip Green
about: Philip Green and his wife Cristina Green once sat atop the British retail empire Arcadia Group.
The business was forced to sell its best-known brands ? including Topshop, Top Man and Dorothy Perkins ? after it fell into bankruptcy in 2020.
The Greens have been vilified in Britain for their role in letting home retailer BHS collapse, which put pensions for 19,000 workers at risk in 2016.
Parliament voted to strip Green of his knighthood over the pension deficit scandal. However, he is still a knight; the vote was symbolic.
Parliament voted to strip Green of his knighthood over a pension deficit scandal. However, he is still a knight; the vote was symbolic.
did_you_know_facts: A college dropout, Philip Green started his first business at age 21, importing jeans from Asia with a $30,000 loan from his family.

name: Cristina Green
about: Cristina Green and her husband Philip Green own the embattled retail empire Arcadia Group, which fell into bankruptcy during the Covid-19 pandemic.
The business was subsequently forced to sell its best-known brands, including Topshop, Top Man and Dorothy Perkins.
Outside of Arcadia, the Greens own three yachts worth about $140 million and nearly $40 million of real estate that Cristina was found to have bought through offshore firms.
The Greens have been vilified in Britain for their role in letting home retailer BHS collapse, which put pensions for 19,000 workers at risk in 2016.

name: Sergei Kolesnikov
about: Sergei Kolesnikov owns 50% of Technonicol, a global producer of roofing, waterproofing and thermal insulation materials.
He is a managing partner of Technonicol, which owns 72 companies and factories in seven countries in Europe and Asia.
Kolesnikov founded the company with his classmate Igor Rybakov in 1992.
Kolesnikov financed an ecopark near Ryazan with an area of more than 500,000 square meters with a hotel complex and biathlon track.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

did_you_know_facts: Kolesnikov finances biathlon schools and built two biathlon stadiums.
Together with colleagues from Technonicol, Kolesnikov participates in sailing competitions.
quote: I am engaged in biathlon, I go to competitions. Why? I like experiencing the stress that appears at the start, and the euphoria at the finish. Business, like sports, is a test of yourself.

name: Ed Park
about: Ed Park cofounded Devoted Health, a healthcare company for older Americans, with his brother Todd in 2017.
Investors last valued Devoted Health, where Park is CEO, at $12.9 billion in 2024.
Park was previously chief technology officer and chief operating officer at health tech company Athenahealth.
Park and his brother are both Harvard alums; Ed Park holds a bachelor's degree in computer science from the university.

name: Todd Park
about: Todd Park cofounded Devoted Health, a healthcare company for older Americans, with his brother Ed in 2017.
Investors last valued Devoted Health, where Park is executive chairman, at $12.9 billion in 2024.
Park previously worked in government, serving as White House technology advisor from 2014 to 2017 and U.S. chief technology officer from 2012 to 2014.
In 1997, Park cofounded health tech company Athenahealth.
A Harvard alum, Park also serves on the university's board.

name: Luca Ferrari
about: Luca Ferrari cofounded Italian app developer Bending Spoons in 2013 with his three cofounders Matteo Danieli, Francesco Patarnello and Luca Querella. He is CEO.
The four friends launched Bending Spoons after working together on an unsuccessful, earlier startup Evertale, a note-taking app.
The Bending Spoons cofounders met while studying in Copenhagen, Denmark, and would later relocate to Milan, Italy, as their new startup took off.
The Milan, Italy-based startup struck on the strategy of buying apps and companies with a loyal audience where it sees the potential to overhaul its features and pricing.
Bending Spoons was largely bootstrapped until it raised its first major funding round in 2022 and made its first takeover of Evernote in 2023.

The company last raised $270 on a $11 billion in October 2025 to help fund its takeover of AOL and Vimeo. Bending Spoons is now Italy's most valuable startup and has bought, or taken private, a string of apps and startups like Meetup, Eventbrite, and WeTransfer.

name: Ayman Hariri
about: Ayman Hariri is a son of the late Rafik Hariri, Lebanon's prime minister, who was assassinated while in office in 2005.
He inherited a stake in his father's Saudi-based construction company Saudi Oger, and sold it to his brother Saad in 2014.
In 2017, he sold his 42% stake in family holding company GroupeMed, which has interests in banking and real estate, for $535 million.
He invests in startups through New York-based firm Red Sea Ventures; among its investments was smart thermostat Nest, now part of Google.
He's a cofounder and CEO of Vero, an ad-free social media platform that lets users share music, videos and photos.
did_you_know_facts: His brother Saad Hariri also served as the prime minister of Lebanon.

name: Shirley Kao
about: Shirley Kao owns stakes in Uni-President Enterprises, the food and beverage conglomerate cofounded by her father, Kao Chin-Yen, in 1967.
She was the sole inheritor of her father's fortune after he died in 2016.
She has been a board member at Uni-President since 2013 and heads the group's health and beauty-related subsidiaries.
Her husband, Alex Lo, was promoted to CEO of the group in 2007 and doubled as its chairman after his father-in-law retired in 2013.
Before Lo turned 60 and stepped down from the CEO post in 2016, he had more than doubled the company's market cap to over $10 billion. He continues to lead the group as chairman.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Marymount California University

did_you_know_facts: Kao and her husband, Alex Lo, were high school sweethearts, but had a second chance at love only after her first marriage failed.
By that time her father was no longer opposed to her marrying a mainland Chinese descendant.

name: Mirwais Azizi
about: Mirwais Azizi is an Afghan-born real estate developer based in Dubai.
His firm Azizi Developments has delivered more than 45,000 homes since he founded it in 2007 and is currently developing more than 150,000 units in Dubai.
Azizi Developments is building Burj Azizi in Dubai, set to become the second-tallest tower in the world at 2,379 feet.
Azizi fled his native Afghanistan for the Soviet Union in 1988 with just $500. He moved to Dubai in 1994 trading cigarettes, later expanding to oil packaging and exporting and real estate.
Azizi is a major philanthropist in the UAE and Afghanistan, focusing on hospitals, housing and education.

name: Harald Link
about: Harald Link is the third-generation head of Thailand's storied B.Grimm group, with interests that include energy, real estate, transport and healthcare.
Founded in 1878 as Siam Dispensary, it was acquired by Link's grandfather Adolf Link in 1914.
After studying in Switzerland and Germany, where he grew up, Link arrived in Bangkok in 1978 to join his uncle in the family firm.
Chief executive since 1987, Link is grooming daughter Caroline to succeed him.
In 2017, Link listed the group's power unit in what was the first ever IPO of a group company. It does business in nine countries.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of St Gallen

did_you_know_facts: Link is an avid polo player.
His wife is a titled princess of Liechtenstein.
B.Grimm has sponsored the Royal Bangkok Symphony Orchestra.

name: Gleb Fetisov
about: Gleb Fetisov joined Mikhail Fridman's Alfa Group in 1995. He later led the group's takeover of an aluminum plant in Siberia.
Fetisov sold all of his business interests in 2014, including a stake in telecom outfit Vimpelcom, for approximately $1.4 billion in cash.
Soon after cashing out, he was arrested and accused of embezzling assets of now-bankrupt My Bank in Moscow.
In February 2015, he paid $200 million to creditors and was soon after released from prison.
He got Cyprus citizenship in June 2022.
did_you_know_facts: Fetisov was a member of the Federation Council, the upper house of Russia's parliament, from 2001 to 2009.
Fetisov invested $4 million and was one of the co-producers of the Oscar nominated film Loveless, first released in 2017.

name: Wang Jilei
about: Wang Jilei is a director of express delivery firm ZTO Express.
He has served as its vice president of infrastructure management since October 2012.
From October 2009 to March 2012, Wang was a deputy general manager of Beijing ZTO Daying Logistics, a ZTO Express network partner.

name: Andrei Kosogov
about: Andrei Kosogov is a member of Russian conglomerate Alfa Group's supervisory board and is in charge of its investment units.
Kosogov cofounded international investment company LetterOne in 2013. He stepped down from the board in March 2022 after his partners were sanctioned by the EU and the U.K.
LetterOne has invested in oil and gas firm Wintershall Dea, cellular companies Vimpelcom and Turkcell, and health food chain Holland & Barrett.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Moscow Power Engineering Institute

did_you_know_facts: Born in Estonia when it was part of the Soviet Union, Kosogov graduated from Moscow Power Engineering Institute.
In 1992, Mikhail Fridman hired Kosogov to oversee the establishment of a privatization investment fund. Months later he became chief executive of Alfa Capital.

name: Xu Yuejuan
about: Xu Yuejuan is a supervisor of Zhejiang Rongsheng Holding Group, a petrochemicals supplier.
Xu Yuejuan is a sister-in-law of Li Shuirong, the chairman and cofounder of Rongsheng's publicly traded Rongsheng Petro Chemical.
Zhejiang Rongsheng Holding is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Hangzhou.

name: Trevor Burgess
about: Trevor Burgess is chairman and CEO of flood insurance company Neptune Insurance Holdings.
Burgess owns nearly a third of the company, which went public on the New York Stock Exchange in October 2025.
Neptune Insurance Holdings is the largest private flood insurance company in the US. Burgess joined the company as its controlling shareholder and a director in 2018 and was named CEO in 2019.
Burgess previously served as CEO of a publicly-traded bank called C1 Financial, which was acquired by Bank of the Ozarks in 2016. At C1, he became the first openly gay CEO of a publicly traded bank.
Before joining C1 in 2012, Burgess worked as an investment banker at Morgan Stanley for nearly a decade.

name: Vincent Lo
about: Vincent Lo is the chairman of Hong Kong-listed Shui On Land, best known for developing Shanghai's Xintiandi, an upscale shopping and entertainment district turned from a rundown area.
His daughter and heir apparent Stephanie is vice chairman of Shui On Land. Son Adrian is deputy CEO of Socam Development, the Hong Kong construction arm of Shui On.
Vincent is a son of late property tycoon Lo Ying-Shek, who cofounded Great Eagle Holdings. The clan has been embroiled in a feud over a family trust fund.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Economics, University of New South Wales

did_you_know_facts: Vincent Lo was sued by Donald Trump in 2005, who claimed former partners Lo and Henry Cheng had not consulted him and closed on a deal for less than he would have.
Trump lost the $1 billion case but was granted proceeds from another deal with the partners.

name: Kapil Bhatia
about: Kapil Bhatia is the executive chairman of InterGlobe Enterprises, whose biggest asset is a stake in IndiGo, India's largest airline by market share.
IndiGo was set cofounded by his son Rahul Bhatia and started operations in 2006.
IndiGo has a fleet over 350 aircraft and flies to 118 destinations, including 32 overseas.
The other interests of InterGlobe include hospitality, aircraft maintenance and logistics.
Bhatia got his start in the travel business as a sales manager before he set up his own venture called Delhi Express Travels.

name: Frank Laukien
about: Frank Laukien is the chairman and CEO of Bruker Corp., a scientific instruments manufacturer headquartered in Billerica, Massachusetts.
His father, physics professor Gunther Laukien, founded the company in 1960.
The firm initially specialized in magnets and power supplies; now it produces a variety of imaging machines and microscopes, among others.
Bruker is publicly traded; Laukien owns about a quarter of the company.
Laukien's brother, Joerg Laukien, served on Bruker's board but retired in 2018.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Doctorate, Harvard University

name: Stelios Haji-Ioannou
about: The son of a Greek Cypriot shipping magnate, Stelios Haji-Ioannou founded the budget airline easyJet in 1995 after leaving his father's company.
Stelios owns an estimated 4% of the airline; his siblings Clelia and Polys both have large stakes as well.
Stelios maintains ownership of the easy brand through his private company, easyGroup.
Through easyGroup, Stelios has licensed the easy name to such businesses as easyHotel, easyCar and easyCoffee.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, City University of London; Bachelor of Arts/Science, London School of Economics

did_you_know_facts: His Stelios Philanthropic Foundation supports food distribution centers in Greece and Cyprus and funds an award for disabled entrepreneurs.
Stelios funds scholarships at his alma maters the London School of Economics and City, University of London.

name: Dong Fan
about: Dong Fan chairs Jafron Biomedical, which went public in August 2016 on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange.
Dong, who holds a 48% stake in Jafron, is a graduate of Shanghai University of Finance and Sun Yet-Sen University in China.
Jafron was founded in 1989.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics; Master of Business Administration, Sun Yat-sen University

name: A. Jayson Adair
about: A. Jayson "Jay" Adair is the executive chairman of Dallas-based Copart, a leader in online auctions for used and totaled cars.
He joined the company in 1989 at age 19 as a manager; Copart's founder, Willis Johnson, is Adair's father-in-law.
Adair pioneered Copart's move into online auctions in 1998, and by 2003, the company eliminated in-person bids and put auctions 100% online.
He became Copart's CEO in 2010, expanded Copart's physical footprint to more than 200 locations in 11 countries. He stepped down as co-CEO in April 2024.
As CEO, Adair expanded Copart's physical footprint to more than 200 locations in 11 countries.
did_you_know_facts: Adair owns a vineyard in Suisun Valley wine country in northern California.
In 1996, Adair and Johnson bought the Internet domain name Copart.com -- they also tried to buy IAA.com as a joke on their biggest rival, but it was taken.

name: Paul Sciarra
about: Since 2014, he has served as executive chairman of electric air taxi maker Joby Aviation. He owns a 6% stake in the company.
Sciarra held onto a roughly 5% slice of Pinterest, which went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2019.
Since 2014, he has served as executive chairman of electric air taxi maker Joby Aviation. He owns a 6% stake in the company.
Joby went public in 2021 through a reverse merger with Reinvent Technology Partners, Mark Pincus and Reid Hoffman's SPAC.
Sciarra and his wife Jennifer signed on to the Giving Pledge in 2019, promising to donate at least half their wealth to charitable causes.
did_you_know_facts: Sciarra still owns 5% of Pinterest, which went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2019.

name: Ziv Aviram
about: Ziv Aviram is the cofounder of autonomous vehicle technology firm Mobileye.
He launched the company in 1999 with fellow billionaire Amnon Shashua, a computer science professor at Hebrew University.
The pair took Mobileye public in 2014, then sold it to Intel in 2017 at a $15.3 billion valuation.
Aviram and Shashua also co-CEOs of Or-Cam, which makes portable, artificial vision devices for visually impaired people. They founded the company in 2010.

name: Sergey Dmitriev
about: Sergey Dmitriev cofounded software company JetBrains in 2000.
JetBrains' tools are used by more than 10 million software developers and project managers around the world.
Dmitriev serves as president of the Prague-based business.
His partner, Valentin Kipyatkov, is also a billionaire.
Dmitriev renounced Russian citizenship in 2023. He has Cyprus passport and lives in Cyprus.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Saint Petersburg State University

did_you_know_facts: JetBrains was among the biggest employers of programmers in St. Petersburg. It closed all Russian business in 2022.

name: Wu Bo
about: Wu Bo chairs Estun Automation, a Chinese supplier of components for artificial intelligence equipment and industrial robots.
Nanjing Estun Automation went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2015.
Wu Bo received his bachelor's degree and master's degree in mechanical engineering from Southeast Universtiy in Nanjing.

name: Jim Koch
about: Jim Koch created Samuel Adams beer in 1984. Now chairman, he's known as a founding father of the American craft brewery movement.
A Harvard graduate, Koch quit his consulting job and began brewing beer in his kitchen, using his great-great grandfather's 1870s recipe.
The first batch Koch brewed was Boston Lager. He started selling the beer door-to-door at Boston bars and restaurants.
He took Samuel Adams' parent company, Boston Beer, public in 1995 and owns an 18.5% stake.
Boston Beer's brands include Dogfish Head, Twisted Tea, Angry Orchard and Truly Hard Seltzer.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Harvard University; Master of Business Administration, Harvard University; Doctor of Jurisprudence, Harvard University

did_you_know_facts: Koch still taste tests every batch of beer himself.
Koch's favorite fall beer is Sam Adams Octoberfest. The company has been making it for more than 20 years.

name: Lin Por-Fong
about: Lin Por-Fong has been serving as the chairman of Taiwan Glass, one of Asia's largest glass suppliers, since 2009.
The company was founded in 1964 by his late father, Lin Yu-Chia, who took it public nine years later.
It has five plants in Taiwan and 15 in mainland China after expanding into the region in 1993.
Por-Fong's brother Por-Shih is the company's president and CEO; another brother Por-Chun is its executive director.

name: Zhang Wenzhong
about: Zhang Wenzhong is the controlling shareholding of Wumart Holdings Inc.
Wumart is a multi-brand retailer with supermarkets and department stores, among other businesses.
He was sentenced to 18 years in prison for financial violations in 2008 and released in 2013.
Zhang's earlier convictions were overturned by China's high court in 2018, clearing his record.

name: Andrei Rappoport
about: Andrei Rappoport worked for two billionaires, Mikhail Fridman and Mikhail Khodorkovsky, before becoming one himself.
Rappoport worked at Fridman's Alfa-Bank for four years, then joined Khodorkovsky's YUKOS-Rosprom before moving to RAO Unified Energy System.
After RAO UES, he bought Georgian Global Utilities and a Georgian water and power company that he then sold to BGEO Group in 2016.
These days he is an investor in more than 50 PE and VC funds. He was an early investor in Datadog and Delivery Hero.
Rappaport has Russian, Israeli, Cyprus and Portuguese citizenship.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Donetsk National University

did_you_know_facts: Rappoport is a master of sports in high-speed pistol shooting.
Rappoport decided to start a bank when he was 28 years old, but had no money. Instead he joined Alfa Bank after seeing an ad in the newspaper.

name: Hans-Otto Kromberg
about: Hans-Otto Kromberg owns Kromberg & Schubert, a family-owned German maker of cable and wiring.
The company was founded in 1902 by Paul Kromberg and Enrst Schubert, with Kromberg becoming sole owner 12 years later.
Hans-Otto Kromberg took control of his grandfather's company business at age 30 with the goal of expanding into international markets.
Kromberg & Schubert had revenue of 2.7 billion euros, according to its most recent financial filings.

name: Aluru Jagadish Prasad
about: Aluru Jagdish Prasad is chairman and managing director of Hyderabad-based HBL Power Systems, which makes everything from industrial batteries to energy saving motors.
Its batteries are used in aircraft, data centres, submarines, missiles and battle tanks.
It also makes train collision avoidance systems for the Indian Railways.
He founded the business in 1977.
He started off by making aircraft batteries for the Indian Air Force.

name: Igor Rybakov
about: Igor Rybakov owns 50% of Technonicol, a global producer of roofing, waterproofing and thermal insulation materials.
Technonicol owns 72 companies and factories in seven countries in Europe and Asia.
Rybakov founded the company with classmate Sergei Kolesnikov in 1992, at age 20.
He ran the business until 2015, when he cofounded technology company Prytek.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

did_you_know_facts: Rybakov and his wife Ekaterina started a foundation in 2015 that sets up programs to support education.
Rybakov got his start selling ice cream near one of the Moscow railway stations.
quote: Entrepreneurs paradoxically combine ultimate idealism, even romanticism, with extreme pragmatism and selfishness.

name: Heloise Pratt
about: Heloise Pratt is the sister of fellow billionaires Anthony Pratt and Fiona Geminder.
The three siblings hold stakes in the Melbourne family's Visy Asia-Pacific packaging business.
Heloise reached a settlement with ex-husband Alex Waislitz in 2025, receiving A$325 million in cash.
She also built Thorney Investments with her ex-husband and later divested her shares following the settlement.
She also owns a stake in listed investment company Thorney Opportunities and has a property portfolio.
did_you_know_facts: Pratt oversees the Pratt Foundation's $1 billion fund, which distributes around $20 million annually.

name: Weng Xianding
about: Weng is the majority shareholder of Shenzhen New Industries Biomedical Engineering, a supplier of clinical instruments.
Weng was the first person to be appointed as representative of China's securities watchdog in the city of Shenzhen back in 1992.
The company was founded in 1995 and is based in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.

name: John Coustas
about: John Coustas is the chairman and CEO of Athens, Greece-based shipping firm Danaos Corporation.
His father Dimitris Coustas (d. 2013) founded the company in 1972.
John Coustas succeeded his father as CEO in 1987 and took Danaos public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2006.
He owns just over 50% of the company's stock.
He also serves as deputy chairman of the board of international marine insurance company The Swedish Club.

name: Li Zhen & family
about: Li Zhen chairs Gotion High-Tech, a lithium battery supplier.
Gotion operates eight global R&D centers across Asia and North America.
The company went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2006.
The company raised $685 million in a secondary listing on the SIX Swiss Exchange in 2022.
Founded in 1996, Gotion went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2015 and became the first publicly-traded power battery company in China.

name: Michel Litvak
about: Michel Litvak derives his fortune from OTEKO, a Moscow-based investor with interests in port and industrial infrastructure in southern Russia.
He started out trading consumer goods between Russia and China in 1991, following the collapse of the Soviet Union.
In 1992 he entered the oil railroad business and founded OTEKO, then a major railroad operator.
In 2018 Litvak sold the railroad business, and has focused on expanding his port and infrastructure companies.
Through his business Litvak owns two seaport terminals on the Black Sea coast: LPG Transshipment Complex and Taman Bulk Cargo Terminal.
Born in Leningrad, Litvak's parents were Russian Jews. In the 1960s his family left the Soviet Union and immigrated to Belgium; he now holds dual citizenship in Russia and Belgium.
did_you_know_facts: Litvak has produced films, including Whiplash, Drive, Nightcrawler and Shot Caller.
Litvak was granted Russian citizenship in 2019.

name: Ben Silbermann
about: Ben Silbermann is cofounder and chairman of the photo bookmarking site Pinterest.
Silbermann grew up in Iowa and collected dried insects which he then would pin on cardboard.
He and cofounders Evan Sharp and Paul Sciarra, launched the first desktop version of Pinterest in March 2010.
Pinterest lets its 570 million users save and share image collections from recipes to hairstyles to crafts and home decor through their mobile phones or computers.
Prior to cofounding Pinterest, Silbermann graduated from Yale, spent three years as a consultant and worked for Google before quitting to focus on a startup, Cold Brew Labs.

name: Josef Boquoi & family
about: Frozen-food king Josef Boquoi presides over bofrost, which has approximately 11,000 employees, four million customers and $1.4 billion in revenue.
He joined his father's small coffee- and grain-roasting firm in 1953, after receiving a business degree and completing an apprenticeship in Hamburg.
He founded bofrost in 1966, and its first refrigerated vans hit the streets of Germany in 1969.
He introduced new items and developed a business model based on freezing and packaging a variety of fresh food, and delivering direct to households.
Today, bofrost, based in Straelen, offers upwards of 1,000 different foods in Europe, delivered by a fleet of 5,500 sales vehicles.
did_you_know_facts: In Venice, customer orders are brought by boat, while in Madrid small vehicles are deployed to be able to navigate through the narrowest of alleys.
Boquoi unsuccessfully sued Germany's Manager Magazine for including him on its list of richest Germans, claiming it was a violation of his privacy.

name: Greg Brown
about: Greg Brown has been CEO of Motorola Solutions since 2008 and chairman since 2011.
He is the longest-serving chief executive of the company formerly known as Motorola, Inc. after the firm's cofounder Paul Galvin (d. 1959) and his son Bob Galvin (d. 2011).
Brown spun off Motorola's struggling legacy smartphone business in 2011, and the Razr maker was acquired by Google for $12.5 billion a year later. (It's now part of Lenovo.)

Through more than 50 acquisitions, Brown has transformed Motorola Solutions into a $10.8 billion (2024 revenue) behemoth in the market for mission-critical public safety communications, 911 command center solutions and video security.
Brown has netted more than $700 million (before taxes) exercising options and selling shares of Motorola Solutions. He owns 1% of the company between his remaining stock and options.

name: Zhong Sheng Jian
about: Zhong Sheng Jian is the chairman of Singapore-listed Yanlord Land, one of the largest non-government-owned real estate developers in China.
Zhong, a mainland native, moved to Singapore in 1988.
Yanlord's prominent China partners include Ping An Insurance, China Merchants Property Development and Poly Real Estate Group.
His son Zhong Ming is Yanlord's executive deputy chairman; younger son Zhong Iek Ka and nephew Zhong Siliang both sit on the board.

name: Samih Sawiris
about: Samih Sawiris is the middle son of Egypt's wealthiest family, and founder and chairman of Orascom Development Holding, which builds and operates resorts in Egypt, Montenegro and Switzerland.
His brothers, Nassef and Naguib, are also billionaires and his son, Naguib Samih, is chairman of the board at Orascom Development.
He and his brothers all own stakes in publicly-traded Orascom Construction, the company established by their father in 1950.
Sawiris is also a founder and board member of the Sawiris Foundation for Social Development (SFSD), which seeks to create sustainable job opportunities for Egyptians.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts / Science, Technical University of Berlin; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Technical University of Berlin

name: Alexander Lutsenko & family
about: Former Soviet army officer Alexander Lutsenko and his wife Natalia founded Sodrugestvo Group in 1994.
The company processes soybeans and oilseed, manufactures fishmeal and composite animal protein mix, and imports corn gluten and lysine.
The group has its own terminals in the Baltic Sea port of Kaliningrad, and has railcar stocks and processing plants in Russia, Brazil and Denmark.
The couple sold 10% of Sodruzhestvo to Japanese firm Mitsui & Co. at a $2 billion valuation in 2012; they bought the shares back in 2016.
In 2023 Sodrugestvo Group, now Sodru, underwent a restructuring and sold off its Russian and Belorussian businesses to Lutsenko and his wife. Lutsenko sold the group's foreign assets to top managers.

name: Kimbal Musk
about: Kimbal Musk is the younger brother of the world's richest person, Elon Musk.
Kimbal is a billionaire thanks to his small stakes in Elon's giant companies, Tesla and SpaceX.
He has served as a director of Tesla since 2004. He owns 0.03% of the company and has netted more than $300 million (before taxes) exercising options and selling shares.
He previously served on the board of SpaceX and owns an estimated 0.05% of the $1.25 trillion company.

name: Nanu Gupta
about: Nanu Gupta is the founder and chairman of retailer Vijay Sales, which sells a range of electronics and appliances including televisions, air conditioners and refrigerators across 160 stores in India.
Gupta started out in 1967 with a small store selling sewing machines and radios in a Mumbai suburb.
Vijay Sales started selling black and white TVs in 1972 and color TVs in 1982.
His sons Nilesh and Ashish as well as his grandson Karan are directors on the company's board.
did_you_know_facts: Gupta started his career as a distributor for sewing machine company Usha International.

name: Deepinder Goyal
about: Deepinder Goyal cofounded food delivery service Zomato in 2008 which became Eternal in 2024.
Zomato's IPO in 2021 was oversubscribed 35 times and it listed at a valuation of $12 billion.
In 2022, Zomato acquired quick commerce platform Blinkit. It competes with rival Swiggy's Instamart.
In January 2026 he resigned as CEO of flagship Eternal and became vice chairman. He said in a letter to the stock exchange that it was to pursue new ideas.

In February 2026, Goyal's startup Temple, which is developing a wearable device for measuring cerebral blood flow, got a $54 million investment from investors including Peak XV Partners and Steadview Capital.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Indian Institute of Technology Delhi

did_you_know_facts: Goyal has a math and computing degree from the premier Indian Institute of Technology in Delhi.
Goyal was working with Bain & Company as a management consultant before he struck out on his own.
In late 2025, he made a series of social media statements defending the gig economy even as delivery personnel went on a nationwide strike on New Year's eve.

name: Michael Spencer
about: Spencer founded inter-broker dealer NEX Group (formerly ICAP), which was acquired by CME Group in 2018 for $5.4 billion.
After the half stock, half cash deal, Spencer was granted 3 million shares of CME.
He now owns and runs private IPGL Group, which has more than ?1 billion in assets.
A loyal Tory, Spencer served as the Conservative Party's treasurer from 2006 to 2010.
Spencer was granted peerage by UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson, and now sits in the House of Lords.

name: Li Guoqing
