about: Li Guoqing is a supervisor of Rongsheng Petrochemical, a company specialized in the production and marketing of petrochemical and chemical fiber.
Brother Li Yongqing a director of the listed company, is also a billionaire.
Rongsheng is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Hangzhou.

name: Gao Shuhua
about: Gao Shuhua is a cofounder of Hebei Changshan Biochemical Pharmaceutical, known primarily for its heparin products.
Gao was the chairman and CEO of the company from 2000 to 2016.
His son Gao Xiaodong took over as chairman and president in 2019.

name: Huang Chulong
about: Huang Chulong chairs Galaxy Group, a privately held business based in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen.
Huang's business interests span hotels, shopping malls, office leasing, parking-lot operation and real estate development.
Huang holds a controlling stake in Hong Kong-listed real estate management company E-Star Commercial Management.

name: Yasseen Mansour
about: Yasseen Mansour is a shareholder in family-owned conglomerate Mansour Group, which was founded by his father Loutfy (d. 1976) in 1952.
Mansour Group is the exclusive distributor of GM vehicles and Caterpillar equipment in Egypt and several other countries.
His brothers Mohamed and Youssef are also billionaires and part owners of Mansour Group.
He's chairman of Palm Hills Developments, one of Egypt's biggest real estate developers.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, George Washington University

did_you_know_facts: Mansour Group is the sole franchisee of McDonald's in Egypt, as well as the distributor of Gauloises cigarettes.

name: Smagulov Nurlan
about: Nurlan Smagulov is the founder and president of Astana Group, a Kazahkstani business with interests in car dealerships and shopping malls.

The group was founded in 1992 as Astana Motors, a car dealership, which now operates as a distributor and dealer for over a dozen automobile brands, as well as a manufacturer of passenger and commercial vehicles.
Smagulov launched one of the country's first modern shopping and entertainment center formats, MEGA, in 2006.
In 2025, he built Kazakhstan's first private museum of contemporary art, the Almaty Museum of Arts, investing more than $120 million in the project.
The museum will include works by Richard Serra, Anselm Kiefer, Yayoi Kusama, and Bill Viola, as well as art by Yinka Shonibare, Jaume Plensa, and Alicja Kwade created specifically for the museum.
did_you_know_facts: Astana Motors Manufacturing produces the Chinese car brands Chery, Changan, Haval, and Tank.

name: Femi Otedola
about: Femi Otedola is a Nigerian billionaire who made his first fortune in commodities before selling his shares in Forte Oil to invest in the energy business.
In 2025, Otedola sold his majority stake in Geregu Power, a power generation business, pocketing roughly $750 million.
He had previously sold down his stake in Geregu, which once exceeded 95%, to bring on institutional investors.
He retains a 5% stake in the Lagos-based company.
He also owns properties in Lagos, Dubai, London and Monaco, and holds shares in Zenith Bank and FBN Holdings.
did_you_know_facts: His daughter is a professional DJ who goes by the stage name DJ Cuppy.

name: Irfan Razack
about: Irfan Razack is the chairman and managing director of listed Bangalore real estate developer Prestige Estates Projects.
Prestige's portfolio includes 300 completed projects across residential,commercial, retail and hospitality segments.
Razack started out working in the family's textile and apparel retailing business before venturing into real estate.
Younger brothers Rezwan and Noaman, both billionaires, work with him.
Razack has a passion for adventure sports.

name: Rezwan Razack
about: Rezwan Razack cofounded Bangalore real estate outfit Prestige Estates Projects with his brother Irfan, also a billionaire.
He's the joint managing director of Prestige.
Razack started out working in the family's textile and apparel business.
Today, Prestige's portfolio includes 300 completed projects across residential, commercial, retail and hospitality segments.
He works together with older brother Irfan and younger brother Noaman.
did_you_know_facts: Razack is a numismatist and an authority on Indian paper money with two books published on that subject.

name: Noaman Razack
about: Noaman Razack is a executive director at Bangalore real estate developer Prestige Estates Projects in which he has a stake.
Prestige's portfolio includes 300 completed projects across residential, commercial, retail and hospitality segments.
He oversees retail operations at Prestige, where he works with his older brothers Irfan and Rezwan.
He enjoys playing golf and hockey.

name: Jose Ignacio Comenge
about: José Ignacio Comenge is a Spanish investor with holdings in beverage, food, and agribusiness sectors.
He inherited and later expanded interests in Coca-Cola bottling businesses and now holds almost 2% and is board member of Coca-Cola Europacific Partners, his most valuable asset.
Comenge, who is an influential figure in the Madrid business community, prefers leveraged, long-term equity positions rather than High-profile business ventures.
Through his investment vehicle, Mendibea 2002, he owns significant but minority stakes in listed companies such as Prim, Ebro Foods, and Cvne.

name: Wang Wenyin
about: Wang Wenyin is the founder of copper and cable conglomerate Amer.
Headquartered in Shenzhen, Amer has 30,000 employees globally with offices in Asia, the U.S. and Europe.
Wang's roots to Shenzhen trace back to 1993, when he moved to the city with the equivalent of about just fifty dollars.
Wang continues to face court-imposed high-spending restrictions, after his Amer shares were frozen by a Qingdao court due to contractual disputes.
He stepped down as chairman of Shenzhen Amer, a main subsidiary of the group, in October 2023.

name: Ni Yongpei & family
about: Ni Yongpei chairs spirits maker Anhui Yingjia Distillery.
Anhui Yingjia Distillery listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in May 2015.
Ni is also Chairman and CEO of Yingjia Group, the parent company of Yingjia Distillery.

name: Yu Peidi
about: Yu Peidi chairs Shanghai-listed real estate developer Greattown Holdings.
Yu left his hometown Fuzhou in 1976 and got his start in the home appliances trade in Indonesia.
Yu began to invest in Fuzhou in the 1980s, starting with minerals and later real estate.

name: Zhou Zongwen & family
about: Zhou Zongwen chairs Chow Tai Seng Jewelry, which listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2017.
Zhou is a graduate of the China University of Geosciences.
Zhou opened the first Chow Tai Seng jewelry store in Beijing in 1999.

name: Gary Magness
about: Gary Magness's late father, Bob, started cable giant TCI, then merged with AT&T in 1999 in a $48 billion deal.
He inherited half of the fortune (his late brother, Kim, got the rest) and now focuses on off-road racing, movie producing and philanthropy.
He collects vintage cars, owns cattle ranches in Colorado and invests in oil, gas and real estate.
His wife, Sarah Siegel-Magness, runs the couple's film company, Smokewood Entertainment, which produced the Oscar winning "Precious."

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Drop Out, Western State College of Colorado

name: Zhao Hongfei
about: Zhao Hongfei chairs Shenzhen-listed software firm Thunder Software Technology.
Zhao holds a master's degree from the Beijing Institute of Technology.
Zhao worked for a joint venture of Japan's NEC and the Chinese Academy of Science's Institute of Software before founding Thunder in 2008.

name: Erik Must
about: Erik Must is one of the largest private investors in the Norwegian stock market.
He got his start as a stock broker at the firm Hans P. Jeppesen, where he met Kjell Christian Ulrichsen.
The duo formed the brokerage firm Fondfinans and dominated Norwegian capital markets in the 70's and 80's thanks to savvy salesmanship.
In 1996, Must bought out Ulrichsen, and have used profits from Fondfinans to build up a large private stock portfolio.
Investments include large stakes in hydroelectric power company Arendals Fossekompani and Børregaard, a pulp and paper company.
did_you_know_facts: Despite being the largest owner of some of Norway's largest newspapers, Must shuns the press and has only agreed to a handful of interviews over the years.

name: Ashwin Desai
about: Ashwin Desai founded Surat-based speciality chemicals maker Aether Industries in 2013.
Aether supplies chemicals to the agrochemical, pharmaceutical and oil and gas industries.
Aether has two factories in the western Indian state of Gujarat.
Desai took Aether public in June 2022, raising $103 million. The company's shares listed at a 10% premium making him a billionaire
His son Rohan manages the company's business operations and son Aman manages the technical side. Desai's wife Purnima has a board seat.
did_you_know_facts: Desai's first entrepreneurial venture was a specialty chemicals business he cofounded with his brother-in-law in 1976.
He is an avid swimmer, nature enthusiast, and writes poetry.
Aether has bought a site in Surat in the western state of Gujarat for a new factory.

name: Tyler Perry
about: A director, actor, producer and writer, Tyler Perry is best known for his "Madea" franchise, which has grossed more than $660 million.
Perry started out in live theater in the 1990s and became extremely popular before transitioning to film and television in the 2000s.
Perry's wealth comes both from his cut as a producer and from a library dating back to the early 1990s: he owns 100% of the content he's created.
In 2019, he opened Tyler Perry Studios, a 330-acre property in Atlanta with 12 sound stages and custom sets that include a to-scale White House.
After seven years creating content for Oprah Winfrey's OWN, Perry struck a similar deal with Viacom in 2019, getting 25% of streaming service BET+.

name: Harley Sy
about: Harley Sy is the executive director of SM Investments, one of the country's largest conglomerates, which was founded by his late father Henry Sy.
SM Investments has interests in everything from retail and banking to property and equity.
He is the youngest of Henry Sy's six children and the fourth son.
He also serves as a director of China Banking and as an adviser of BDO Private Bank.
He is the co-vice chairman of SM Retail, which has retail chains such as Ace Hardware and Toy Kingdom.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, De La Salle University

did_you_know_facts: All of Henry Sy Sr.'s four sons, including Harley, are graduates of De La Salle University.
He joined the board of SM Investment during his early thirties.
In 2022, SM Investments acquired Philippine Geothermal Production in a $304 million, all-share deal in a bid to lower its carbon footprint.

name: Christopher Stolte
about: Christopher Stolte cofounded data analytics company Tableau in 2003.
Salesforce acquired Tableau in June 2019 in a $15.7 billion, all-stock deal.
Stolte left Tableau that year and now runs his family foundation?which focuses on climate, education and civic engagement causes.
Tableau was born out of Stolte's Stanford thesis, analyzing and visualizing databases under his then-advisor, later-cofounder Pat Hanrahan.
He and his cofounders raised just $15 million in venture capital before taking Tableau public in May 2013.

name: Tianqiao Chen
about: Chen Tianqiao is the founder, chairman and CEO of Shanda Investment Group, founded in 1999 by Chen and his family.
Chen is credited with having pioneered and built the online game industry and the online literature industry in China.
Chen stepped down as CEO of Shanda Interactive Entertainment in 2012 and then took the company private.
Chen and his wife Chrissy are active philanthropists, supporting research programs on brain science. Chen commits $1 billion to support global research on the human brain.
Chen cofounded Gestala, China's First Ultrasonic Brain Computer Interface Company in January 2026.

name: Lin Por-Chun
about: Lin Por-Chun is an executive director of Taiwan Glass, one of Asia's largest glass suppliers.
The company was founded in 1964 by his late father, Lin Yu-Chia, who took it public nine years later.
It has five plants in Taiwan and 15 in mainland China after expanding into the region in 1993.
Por-Chun's brother Por-Fong serves as the company's chairman; another brother Por-Shih is its president and CEO.

name: Habil Khorakiwala
about: Pharma tycoon Habil Khorakiwala chairs Wockhardt, one of India's top makers of generic drugs.
He founded Wockhardt in 1967 after breaking away from his family's storied retailing empire.
His son Murtaza runs the Mumbai company which counts the U.K. as one of its top markets.
did_you_know_facts: His daughter Zahabiya oversees the hospital arm while another son heads the charitable foundation.
Khorakiwala has served as the honorary consul general of Sweden in India.

name: Ravi Modi
about: Ravi Modi started Vedant Fashions, named after his only son, in Kolkata city in 2002 to manufacture traditional Indian garments.
Vedant's popular brand Manyavar is best known for its men's kurtas, sherwanis and jackets and women's lehengas, sarees and gowns, aimed at the Indian wedding market.
Modi's wife Shilpi has a board seat, while his son Vedant is the company's chief revenue officer.
The Kolkata company has more than 670 stores across 245 cities and 14 international stores.
Modi sold 10% of his stake in 2023 to increase the public holding in the company to 25% as required by the stock market regulator.
did_you_know_facts: Modi opened the first international Manyavar store in Dubai in 2011.
In 2022, Modi took Vedant Fashions public.
Media-shy Modi did not attend his company's listing ceremony at the National Stock Exchange.

name: Kirit Doshi
about: Kirit Doshi draws his wealth from a minority stake in Waaree Energies, India's largest manufacturer of solar panels by capacity.
Mumbai-based Waaree Energies was listed on the Indian bourses in October 2024 at a 70% premium to its IPO price.
The company has five solar module manufacturing plants in India.
It has five solar module manufacturing plants in India.
The company was originally founded in 1990 by his brother Hitesh as a manufacturer of thermal and pressure gauges used in industrial boilers.

name: Antonio Gallardo Ballart
about: Antonio Gallardo Ballart's father founded pharmaceutical company Almirall in 1943 in Barcelona.
When their father died in 1988, Antonio and his brother Jorge took over running Almirall.
The company listed its shares in Madrid in 2007; Antonio and his brother Jorge control the company.
Antonio Gallardo Ballart served as vice president and advisor until 2014, when he retired.
Members of the third generation of the Gallardo family now work at the company.

name: Adam Norwitt
about: Adam Norwitt is the president and CEO of Amphenol, one of the world's largest providers of high-technology interconnect, sensor and antenna solutions.
He joined Amphenol in 1998 after working as a corporate lawyer.
He was promoted to president in 2007 and CEO in 2009.
He owns just 0.2% of the company plus options to acquire another 0.4%.
He has netted nearly $600 million (before taxes) exercising options and selling the underlying shares.

name: Zhong Huaijun
about: Zhang Huaijun chairs Shanghai Ziyan Food, a supplier of chicken and other food.
Ziyan went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2022.

name: Susan Co
about: Susan Co is the chairman of Puregold Price Club, a chain of hypermarkets and supermarkets she cofounded with her husband Lucio in 1998.
Starting with a location in Mandaluyong City, the chain now boasts more than 640 stores across the Philippines.
Their son, Ferdinand Vincent, helps them run the company as president.
The Cos also head listed Cosco Capital, which has stakes in liquor distribution and real estate businesses.

name: Tope Awotona
about: Tope Awotona is the founder and CEO of scheduling software company Calendly.
Awotona, a former salesman for tech firms including EMC (now Dell EMC), founded Calendly out of his own frustration with the back-and-forth emails required to schedule meetings.
He bootstrapped Calendly for years before taking on a $350 million investment in 2021 that valued the firm at $3 billion.
Born in Lagos, Nigeria, Awotona immigrated to the United States as a teenager.
Before founding Calendly, he had started a few other businesses, including one that sold projectors and another that sold garden tools, that flopped.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Business Administration, The University Of Georgia

did_you_know_facts: To build its first product, Awotona hired a Ukrainian firm for programming help and was in Kyiv during anti-government protests in 2014.
quote: "In my life, I've benefited from not taking the conventional wisdom. It's benefited me personally, and I think it has benefited the business."

name: Sun Guangxin
about: Sun Guangxin leads Xinjiang Guanghui Industry Investment Group, a conglomerate which controls Guanghui Energy and China Grand Automotive Services.
Sun served in the army before he started his first business in Xinjiang province of China.
Founded in 1989, Xinjiang Guanghui today employs more than 100,000 people.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: EMBA, Tianjin University; Master of Arts, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences

name: Bina Chhabria
about: Bina Chhabria is chairperson of Allied Blenders and Distillers, India's third largest spirits company by sales volume.
The Mumbai-based company has 33 manufacturing plants and one distillery
Allied has 17 brands across whiskey, rum, gin and vodka. It's best-selling product is Officer's Choice whiskey
Her husband Kishore founded the company in 1988. Their daughter Resham is vice chairperson of Allied Blenders
did_you_know_facts: It is settling up a lithium ion phosphate plant in Odisha,

name: Simón Pedro Barceló Vadell
about: Simón Pedro Barceló Vadell is the co-chair and largest shareholder of the Barceló Group, one of Spain's largest hotel operators and tourism companies.
The group traces its roots to Simon Barceló, who founded the business in 1931 as a transportation company and expanded to tourism in 1954.
In 1962, the company opened its first hotel on the island of Majorca, and through a series of acquisitions expanded overseas, starting with the Caribbean, then Costa Rica and later the U.S.
Today Barceló has more than 300 4-star and 5-star hotels with 65,000 rooms in 30 countries.
Barceló Vadell's cousin, Simón Barceló Tous, is co-chair but is expected to step down in 2025, when he turns 65 years of age.

name: Cao Jianwei
about: Cao Jianwei chairs Zhejiang Jingsheng Mechanical and Electrical, a manufacturer of semiconductor and LED substrate material.
The company was founded in 2006 and is headquartered in Shaoxing in China's eastern Zhejiang Province.
Zhejiang Jingsheng went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2012.

name: Rick Smith
about: Rick Smith is the founder and CEO of taser maker Axon Enterprise.
He founded the company as TASER International in 1993 and took it public on the Nasdaq in 2001.
Smith is a billionaire thanks to a hefty performance-based stock option package (equaling an 8% stake in Axon) he was awarded in 2018.
He still owns 4% of the company after exercising and selling nearly half of those options for an estimated $200 million after-tax.
Axon had a market cap of more than $40 billion at the end of March 2025, up more than 600% from five years earlier.

name: Carsten Koerl
about: Carsten Koerl founded and runs sports data firm Sportradar, which he took public on the Nasdaq in 2021.
Sportradar, based in Switzerland, helps sports leagues compile data like in-game statistics and distribute it to media companies and betting operators.
He made his first entry into the sports data space in 1997 by founding Bwin (then called betandwin), later taking it public on Austria's Vienna Stock Exchange.
He earned a master's degree in electronic and microprocessor engineering from the University for Applied Sciences in Konstanz, Germany.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, University for Applied Sciences in Konstanz

did_you_know_facts: Koerl developed a love for sports and competition during his youth and was an avid fan of German soccer club Bayern Munich.
Michael Jordan, Mark Cuban, Washington Capitals owner Ted Leonsis and Los Angeles Dodgers part-owner Todd Boehly all own minority stakes in Sportradar.
quote: I'll smash myself to beat you in whatever you choose. Tennis, table tennis, you can jump from a helicopter, I will try this with you.

name: Daniela Grogg
about: Daniela Grogg is the daughter of Peter Grogg, founder of Swiss biochemical company Bachem Holding AG.
Peter Grogg, who died in 2025, started the business in 1971 and served as CEO until 2002, and chairman until 2012.
Grogg, along with her billionaire sister and mother, all serve on the board of the family's asset management firm Ingro Finanz AG.
Bachem AG develops and manufactures active pharmaceutical ingredients, including peptides, amino acid derivatives and other organic molecules.
The family controls about 58% of Bachem as well as shares in Swiss electrical engineering company Burkhalter Holding and chemical maker Dottikon.
did_you_know_facts: In 1971, Grogg started Bachem with 50,000 Swiss Francs.

name: Nicole Grogg-Hotzer & family
about: Nicole Grogg-Hotzer is the daughter of Peter Grogg, founder of Swiss biochemical company Bachem Holding AG.
Peter Grogg, who died in 2025, started the business in 1971 and served as CEO until 2002, and chairman until 2012.
Grogg, along with her billionaire sister and mother, all serve on the board of the family's asset management firm Ingro Finanz AG.
Bachem AG develops and manufactures active pharmaceutical ingredients, including peptides, amino acid derivatives and other organic molecules.
The family controls about 58% of Bachem as well as shares in Swiss electrical engineering company Burkhalter Holding and chemical maker Dottikon.
did_you_know_facts: In 1971, Grogg started Bachem with 50,000 Swiss Francs.

name: Zhou Chengjian
about: Zhou Chengjian is the founder of Shanghai Metersbonwe, one of China's largest home-grown apparel chains.
Daughter Hu Jiajia became Metersbonwe chairman in November 2016.
Zhou Chengjian began his career as a tailor.

name: Hans Schmid
about: Han Schmid controls Printus Group, a German mail order business for office supplies.
Schmid took control Printus in 1982 and now owns 100% of the Offenburg, Germany-based business.
Printus had sales of more than 1.2 billion euros in 2023, according to its latest reported financials.

name: Zhao Tongtong
about: Zhao Tongtong is a co-founder of H World Group, the operator of one of the largest hotel chains in China.
Ji Qi, H World's other co-founder, is also a billionaire and chairs the company.
She's also a board member of China Education & Technology Group.
Zhao holds an MBA from McGill University.and M.S. degree from Shanghai Jiao Tong University.
H World shares trade on both the Nasdaq and the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, McGill Univeristy

name: Helly Nahmad
about: Helly Nahmad is one of three sons of the late art billionaire Ezra Nahmad, who died in 2023.
Ezra Nahmad, along with his billionaire brother David, was an international megadealer of modern and impressionist art.
At the time of his death, the brothers' art inventory, which is stored in a duty-free warehouse in Geneva, Switzerland, was worth almost $7 billion.
Ezra's half of the collection - which includes works by more than 30 blue chip artists, from Monet and Matisse to Renoir and Rothko - was split evenly among his three sons after his death.
The family also owns 300 Picassos worth at least $1 billion and real estate in London, Monaco and the U.S.

name: Joseph Nahmad
about: Joseph Nahmad is one of three sons of the late art billionaire Ezra Nahmad, who died in 2023.
Ezra Nahmad, along with his billionaire brother David, was an international megadealer of modern and impressionist art.
At the time of his death, the brother' art inventory, which is stored in a duty-free warehouse in Geneva, Switzerland, was worth almost $7 billion.
Ezra's half of the collection - which includes works by more than 30 blue chip artists, from Monet and Matisse to Renoir and Rothko - was split evenly among his three sons after his death.
The family also owns 300 Picassos worth at least $1 billion and real estate in London, Monaco and the U.S.

name: Faruk Eczacibasi
about: Faruk Eczacibasi and brother Bulent are partners in a conglomerate that has 25 production facilities in Turkey and 16 abroad.
It is a global exporter of ceramic and wall tiles, plus bathroom fixtures and accessories (brands include VitrA, Villeroy & Boch and Engers Keramik).
Faruk and Bulent's father, Dr. Nejat F. Eczacibasi, focused on pharmaceuticals before expanding into personal health care and other businesses.
Eczacibasi Holding also operate in healthcare services and the production and distribution of medical products to hospitals.
Other key sectors are consumer products, finance, IT, mining and real estate development. Eczacibasi is Turkey's leading producer of toilet paper.
did_you_know_facts: Faruk has an extensive modern art collection (assembled with his wife, Fusun), loves jazz and lives in Istanbul's historic peninsula of Galata.
He is president of the Eczacibasi Sports Club, whose women's volleyball team won the Women's Club World Championship in 2015 and 2016.
quote: The most essential difference in the thought process of the post-internet generation is thinking exponentially. Whether positive or negative, the increasing speed of developments force us all to a new way of thinking, whether we want to or not.

name: Taavet Hinrikus
about: Taavet Hinrikus cofounded cross-border payments startup Transferwise in 2011 and took it public as Wise in July 2021 on the London Stock Exchange.
Wise offers low cost money transfers across 56 different currencies, allowing users to avoid big banking fees for moving money abroad.
Hinrikus and cofounder Kristo Käärmann are Estonia's first two billionaires. The pair met while working in London.
Käärmann and Hinrikus started Wise after having become "sick of losing money" to banks in fees for sending money to Estonia.
Billionaires Peter Thiel and Richard Branson were early investors, followed by VC firm Andreessen Horowitz and money manager Baillie Gifford.

name: Vinod Saraf
about: An MBA from BITS Pilani, Vinod Saraf started his career working for Aditya Birla, billionaire Kumar Birla's late father.
In 1989, he set up his own venture to manufacture isobutyl benzene, the key raw material used for making ibuprofen, a popular painkiller.
His listed Vinati Organics is now among the world's largest producers (by volume) of ibuprofen.
His older daughter Vinati Mutreja, a Wharton grad after whom the company is named, now runs the company as CEO and managing director.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Birla Institute of Technology and Science (BITS) - Pilani

name: Antonio Percassi
about: Antonio Percassi is a real estate and retail mogul with properties in Italy and the United States.
Percassi's older brothers founded a real estate company in the 1960s, and he branched out into commercial real estate in the 1980s.
Percassi got his start in retail when he met fellow billionaire Luciano Benetton in 1976, and went on to manage stores for the Benetton fashion brand.
Percassi brought Zara to Italy in 2001 and opened the first Starbucks store in Milan in 2018.
He also owns a 52% stake in KIKO Milano, an Italian cosmetics brand he founded in 1997.
did_you_know_facts: Percassi owns a stake in his hometown soccer club, Atalanta Calcio, and played for the team from age 17 to 23.
He sold a majority stake in Atalanta to Stephen Pagliuca, co-chair of Bain Capital, in 2022.

name: Yao Runhao
about: Yao Runhao is the chairman and CEO of Shanghai-based Paper Games.
The company has developed Love and Deepspace, one of the most popular dating simulation games in China.
Launched in 2024, Love and Deepspace lets players build a virtual romance with five AI-powered characters.
Paper Games also develops other female-oriented mobile games such as Love and Producer, a dating simulation game as well.
Yao established Paper Games in 2013 after returning to China from Japan's Waseda University.
did_you_know_facts: Tim Cook visited Paper Games' Shanghai office in 2024, and discussed introducing its dating simulation games to the Apple Vision Pro device.

name: Hou Juncheng
about: Hou Juncheng chairs Shanghai-listed Proya Cosmetics, a supplier of moisturizing and whitening skincare products.
Most of the company's sales come from its "Proya" brand, which are popular among Chinese women between the age of 18 to 24 who reside in small and medium cities.
Hou founded Proya in 2006 as a distributor of local brands such as "Yue Sai" before starting his own product lines.

name: Zhang Shengwei
about: Zhang Shengwei is the founder and majority owner of Shenzhen iMiracle Technology, a Shenzhen-based electronic cigarette manufacturer.
Shenzhen iMiracle Technology produces brands including Elf Bar and Lost Mary; Shengwei also owns stakes in the firms behind Air Bar and Geekvape.
Zhang sold kitchenware and clothing on eBay before turning to vaping devices.

name: Réal Plourde
about: Réal Plourde is a cofounder and board member of Alimentation Couche-Tard, the Canadian convenience store giant that owns the Circle K chain.
Couche-Tard does $73 billion in annual revenue across more than 17,000 stores.
The chain has made three other cofounders billionaires: former CEO Alain Bouchard, Richard Fortin and Jacques D'Amours.
Couche-Tard has ballooned by snatching up competitors, including Minnesota-based Holiday Stationstores for $1.6 billion in 2017.
Plourde held a number of roles at the business, including chief operating officer and manager of technical services. From 2011 to 2014, he was chairman.

name: Ryan Graves
about: Ryan Graves was the first employee hired at ride-hailing service Uber in 2010.
Graves was CEO for a brief period in 2010, then president and most recently SVP of Global Operations, working as a "resident entrepreneur and builder."
He announced he was resigning as an Uber exec in August 2017, two months after cofounder Travis Kalanick was forced to resign as CEO.
Graves left Uber's board in May 2019, a few weeks after its initial public offering; at the time he owned about 2% of the company's shares.
Now, Graves runs private investment firm Saltwater, which acquires small, profitable companies.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Miami University of Ohio

did_you_know_facts: Graves got his job by tweeting at Uber cofounder Travis Kalanick: "here's a tip. email me :)" when Kalanick was looking for a product manager.
Before Uber, Graves worked at GE and was an unpaid intern at Foursquare.

name: Stefan Kaluzny
about: Stefan Kaluzny founded Sycamore Partners in 2011. The private equity firm now manages more than $13 billion in assets
Sycamore has invested in consumer and retail brands including department store chain Belk, office supply retailer Staples and fast-fashion chain Hot Topic.
Sycamore led the acquisition of drugstore giant Walgreens in a $10 billion transaction in 2025.
The son of a pianist and a teacher, Kaluzny grew up on the Lower East Side of Manhattan and earned a bachelor's degree from Yale and an MBA from Harvard.
He worked as a consultant at Bain & Co. but in 1994 left to cofound Delray Farms, a chain of fresh grocery stores serving low-income Hispanic communities in Chicago.

name: Andrei Molchanov
about: Andrey Molchanov and his family owns a controlling stake in LSR Group, the biggest producer of construction materials (sand, brick, broken stone) in Russia.
LSR is also one of the leading real estate developers, with a portfolio of 8.3 million square meters of space.
Molchanov is a native of St. Petersburg, where his stepfather worked as vice governor for 10 years.
Molchanov's son Egor is a member of the board at LSR Group.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts/Science, St Petersburg State University; Masters of Public Administration, Russian State Academy of Management

name: Nikolay Fartushnyak
about: Nikolay Fartushnyak, along with his older brother Vladimir and Alexander Mikhalskiy, cofounded Russia's largest sports and fashion retailer Sportmaster.
The Fartushnyak brothers and Mikhalskiy are also cofounders of Ostin, a Russian fast-fashion retailer.
In 2014 Fartushnyak and Igor Khudokormov, known as the "Russian sugar king," bought Swedish company Agrokultura, which owns about 200,000 hectares of agricultural land in Russia.
Fartushnyak and his partners started out with distribution business in the early 1990s and supplied French consumer goods to their home market.
His Sportmaster also has its own brands, such as Demix, which makes sports goods, apparel and shoes.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

name: Mike Speiser
about: Mike Speiser is a managing partner at venture capital firm Sutter Hill Ventures, which he joined in 2008.
Speiser was an initial investor in software firm Snowflake and served as its founding CEO from 2012 to 2014.
He became a billionaire after the company went public in September 2020 in what was the largest ever software IPO at the time.
He owns less than 1% of Snowflake's stock.
His other investments include startups Augment Computing, Reve AI, Sigma Computing, Sila Nano and Observe, Inc.

forbes_list.list: The Midas List: Top Tech Investors (2025)

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Arizona

name: Ibrahim Erdemoglu
about: Ibrahim Erdemoglu and his brother, Ali, together own over 75% of a top producer of materials used in carpet, SASA Polyester.
They initially acquired 51% of SASA in 2015 for $102 million, then added to their stake in the publicly traded company and watched it soar in value.
The brothers' Erdemoglu Holding also includes the two privately held companies, Merinos Carpet and Dinarsu Carpet.
In 1970, their father, Mehmet Erdemoglu, along with family members, started Merinos with two rug-weaving looms.
Today, Erdemoglu Holding is one of the world's largest carpet manufacturers, with production facilities in eight locations in Turkey and Russia.
did_you_know_facts: SASA has a $935 million licensing and technical service agreement with Invista, a subsidiary of Koch Industries that makes chemicals, polymers, fabrics and fibers.
While studying physics at university, Ibrahim Erdemoglu carried carpets on his back and sold them directly to customers.
quote: My biggest hobby is my job.

name: Onkar Kanwar
about: Onkar Kanwar is chairman of Apollo Tyres which makes tires for cars, trucks, farm vehicles and two-wheelers.
It sells under the Apollo and Vredestein brands in India, Europe and Asia.
He took control of the company in 2002 after a public battle with his father, the late Raunaq Singh, who started the company in 1976.
Neeraj Kanwar, the younger of his two sons, is vice-chairman and managing director.
did_you_know_facts: The company's Vredestein brand supplies tires for luxury cars.
He enjoys learning about modern management practices and applying them to his business

name: Mark Dixon
about: Mark Dixon is the founder and CEO of IWG (formerly Regus), a flexible workplace provider.
The son of a Ford engineer, Dixon dropped out of school at age 16 to start a business delivering sandwiches by bicycle.
He held jobs as a logger and an encyclopedia salesman before founding IWG in 1989, after spotting businesspeople meeting around coffee tables.
Now the company rents out meeting rooms, office space by the hour, virtual offices and space in co-working sites across more than 120 countries.
did_you_know_facts: Earlier in his career Dixon launched The Bread Roll Company to supply bread to food vendors after realizing it was hard to procure buns for hot dogs and hamburgers.
Dixon owns the 150-acre Kingscote Estate winery in West Sussex, an area he reportedly hopes will be "a new frontier for wine."
quote: It is worth remembering that money isn't everything. People don't work for financial reward alone. For the great majority, it's about being recognized for the work you do.

name: He Zuxun
about: He Zuxun chairs Yunnan Shennong Agriculture Industry, a pig farming and processing business in China.
He worked as a veterinarian early in his career in the late 1980s.
Shennong was founded in 1999.

name: Boris Rotenberg
about: Younger brother of Arkady Rotenberg, Boris was his partner in SMP Bank and several infrastructure constrictors.
The Rotenberg brothers were hit by U.S. sanctions and had assets frozen in 2014 because of their close ties to President Vladimir Putin.
The U.S. Treasury claimed that Putin had awarded the Rotenbergs billions of dollars in contracts with Gazprom and for the Sochi Olympics.
Unlike Arkady, Boris was not subject to European Union sanctions because he has Finnish citizenship. The U.K. sanctioned him in February 2022.
In recent years Boris Rotemberg sold almost all of his assets including stake in SMB Bank.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts/Science, Leningrad Institute of Physical Culture

did_you_know_facts: Boris is vice president of the Russian Judo Federation. He sponsors the SMP Racing Project, which supports young Russian drivers. He also owns Sochi football club.
In 2018 Finnish Defense Forces banned Rotenberg from building a guest house on his site because it is located near a military base.

name: Frank Holding Jr
about: Frank Holding is Chairman and CEO of First Citizens Bank, a $31 billion (market cap) commercial banking chain, since 2008.
Holding's grandfather, Robert Powell Holding, became an employee of the bank in 1918, and became president by 1935, before passing it down to Frank's father, Lewis Holding.
Today, Frank and his four sisters collectively own about 20% of the bank.
Holding also serves as a board member of Wake Forest University.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Business Administration, University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill; Master of Business Administration, University of Pennsylvania, Wharton

name: Hugo Ribeiro & family
about: Hugp Ribeiro is the son-in-law of Lucia Maggi, who cofounded Amaggi in 1997 with her late husband Andre Maggi.
Amaggi is one of Brazil's largest producers of soybeans and other commodities.
After Andre Maggi died in 2001, his son Blairo Maggi took over as the chief executive of the company.
Ribeiro is one of the controlling shareholders of Amaggi, along with Blairo Maggi, and Itamar Locks.
did_you_know_facts: Ribeiro previously served as president of the board at an Amaggi-linked research institute dedicated to developing more sustainable soybean varieties.
Amaggi produces approximately 1.2 million tons of soy, corn, and cotton in Brazil each year.

name: Vicente Boluda Fos
about: Vicente Boluda Fos is the owner of Boluda Corporacion Maritima, the second-largest towage company in the world, based in Valencia, Spain.
The firm was founded in 1837 and expanded to tugboats in 1920 under Boluda Fos' grandfather. Boluda Fos took over in 1982 and expanded internationally.
Boluda Corporacion Maritima now owns more than 400 tugboats operating in 100 ports in 18 countries in Europe, Africa, Asia and Latin America.
The company also owns divisions in freight logistics, maritime terminals, mooring services and maritime insurance.
Boluda Fos also owns a stake in Bodegas Fos, a winery in the Rioja Alavesa region of Spain's Basque Country.
did_you_know_facts: Boluda Fos served a brief stint as president of Spanish soccer team Real Madrid from January to May 2009.

name: Gregory Bentley & family
about: Gregory Bentley is chairman of infrastructure engineering software developer Bentley Systems. He was CEO from 2000 to 2024.
He joined the company in 1991 after selling a financial trading company he co-founded with brother Barry for $50 million.
His younger brothers Barry and Keith founded the software company in 1984.
Bentley Systems develops and sells computer-aided design (CAD) software for architects and engineers working on public and industrial infrastructure.
The $1.5 billion (sales) company remains majority owned by the Bentley family.
did_you_know_facts: Before starting their software ventures, the brothers sold Christmas trees to earn extra cash.
After the Space Shuttle Challenger exploded in 1986, NASA used Bentley Systems? software to create 3D models of the launch to help analyze what went wrong.

name: Bahari Karim
about: Bahari Karim or Lim Ek Tie is a director of Musim Mas Holdings, a Singapore-based integrated palm oil firm that owns operations in Indonesia.
He runs Musim Mas alongisde brothers Bachtiar and Burhan.
His late father Anwar founded Nam Cheong Soap Factory in 1932; the family-run operation still makes soaps and margarine.
The family opened the first palm oil refinery in Indonesia in 1970. Musim Mas was formally set up two years later.

name: Burhan Karim

Anurang Jain is a billionaire based on his holding in Endurance
Jain stepped down as chairman of both companies in 2020.
His wife Suman is the younger sister of late two-wheeler billionaire Rahul Bajaj.

name: Gina Vecchiarelli
about: Gina Vecchiarelli and her sister Terry Leprino inherited a 90% stake in $3.6 billion (estimated annual revenue) Leprino Foods after the death of their father James Leprino in June 2025.
James Leprino built the company his father founded in 1950 into the world's largest mozzarella cheese maker, after pioneering the technology for manufacturing pizza cheese at scale.
Leprino manufactures and sells more than 1 billion pounds of cheese annually and supplies cheese to Domino's, Pizza Hut, Papa John's and other pizza brands.
Vecchiarelli's husband Dan Vecchiarelli took over as chairman and CEO of Leprino Foods around 2023.

Gina Vecchiarelli has kept a low profile, but her father told Forbes in 2016 that she was "running a program for Make-A-Wish" and that she was focused on mothering her two daughters, who were about to graduate from college.

name: Terry Leprino

name: Ajlan bin Abdulaziz Al-Ajlan
about: Ajlan bin Abdulaziz Al-Ajlan is the chairman of Ajlan & Bros Group, a large Saudi conglomerate with investments in textiles, real estate, mining, energy, logistics, technology and tourism.
He founded Ajlan & Bros in 1979 as a shop specializing in fabric and garments, going on to open a factory in China in 1990 and move into real estate in the 2000s.
The company has operations in more than 25 countries on four continents, including the U.S. and China.
In 2000, Al-Ajlan launched Abdulaziz Alajlan Sons for Trading & Real Estate Investments, which owns residential projects in Saudi Arabia and more than 20,000 residential units under construction.
Al-Ajlan is also a member of the Saudi Shura Council, a 150-member body.

Hagstr?mer co-founded HQ AB, later HQ Bank, in 1990. The bank collapsed in 2010 because of an overvalued trading portfolio.
Creades was one of the first investors in Klarna, investing as early as 2007, but sold their stake in 2014.
Hagstr?mer was, for the first three seasons, one of the sharks in the Swedish version of Shark Tank.
Hagstr?mer cofounded the Raoul Wallenberg Academy, a non-profit foundation that supports and educates young people in human rights and self-leadership.

name: Elena Baturina

In 2010, Luzhkov was removed from the mayor's post; Baturina and their daughters left the country.
Baturina soon sold almost all of her assets in Russia including a construction company called Inteko and a cement factories.
The Russian government seized land she owned in an exclusive area of Moscow. She filed a lawsuit, unsuccessfully demanding $1 billion in compensation.
Baturina, who now lives in London, owns real estate in Europe and USA, and invests in renewable energy.

Baturina's charity fund BE OPEN supports young designers, architects, writers and scientists.

The $33 billion (assets under management) company is the largest investor in energy pipelines in the United States.
Kayne began his career as an analyst in New York in the mid 1960s then managed money at financial services firm Cantor Fitzgerald.
He launched Kayne Anderson in 1984 and remains its co-chairman.

It has five plants in Taiwan and 15 in mainland China after expanding into the region in 1993.
Por-Shih's older brother Por-Fong and younger brother Por-Chun serve as the company's chairman and executive director, respectively.

Por-Shih was indicted by Taipei's local authorities in December 2025 for filing fraudulent business documents in an equity transaction in 2020. Taiwan Glass subsequently made an announcement, claiming it has no impact on the company.

name: Satya Nadella
about: Satya Nadella joined Microsoft in 1992 and rose to CEO in 2014, when his billionaire predecessor, Steve Ballmer, retired that year.
Nadella was named chairman in 2021, replacing veteran tech exec and investor John Thompson, who had assumed the role from Microsoft's billionaire cofounder Bill Gates in 2014.
As CEO, Nadella has built Microsoft Azure into a leading cloud computing platform and overseen the acquisitions of LinkedIn for $26 billion in 2016 and Activision Blizzard for $69 billion 2023.
He has also made Microsoft a major player in the AI boom, investing billions in OpenAI since 2019 and leading the development of Microsoft's own suite of AI-powered tools called CoPilot.
He owns just 0.01% of the company's stock, but that's enough to make him a billionaire, when combined with his more than $700 million of share sales.
A native of India, Nadella came to the U.S. as a student, earning a master's in computer science from the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee and an MBA from the University of Chicago.

The company mines both iron ore and a mineral called spodumene, which contains lithium.
In 2021, Mineral Resources together with U.S. lithium giant Albemarle re-opened the Wodinga mine in the Pilbara, in north-west Australia. It holds 29% of the world's spodumene.
Ellison was appointed non-executive chairman of lithium explorer Delta Lithium in September 2023, after Mineral Resources increased its stake to 23%.
Ellison grew up in a poor family in rural New Zealand where his father was a pig farmer and later worked in a quarry.

Ellison bought fellow mining billionaire Angela Bennett's riverside home in 2009 for A$ 57.5 million.

Over the next course of about two decades, they built the venture into Sibirskiy Delovoy Soyuz (Siberian Business Union), with operations in coal mining, engineering, chemicals, transportation and construction.

In 2021, a fire in a ventilation shaft of SDS coal mine, Listvyazhnaya, caused the death of 46 miners and five rescuers. In 2025, Fedyaev was sentenced to 3.5 years of probation for technical violations at the mine.
Fedyaev's son Pavel became deputy of the State Duma, low chamber of the Russian parliament, in 2011.

A former educator with the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology of the Pirogov Russian National Research Medical University, he founded MD in 2006, which later opened the first private maternity hospital in Moscow.

Beal joined the firm in 1995, two years after graduating from Harvard. He rose to become the firm's president in 2012 and now manages the day-to-day development process.
In all, Related has developed or acquired more than $60 billion worth of properties of all kinds from California to Abu Dhabi to London.
Beal also owns a stake in the NFL's Miami Dolphins and is part of the group of investors that bought the NBA's Boston Celtics for $6.1 billion.
Beal's great-great-grandfather Abraham Beal founded Boston-based developer the Beal Companies in 1878. The firm merged with Related in 2013 to form Related Beal.

At the time, Luddy had just lost a nearly $35 million fortune when his previous employer, Peregrine Systems, filed for bankruptcy.
Advised by Sequoia Capital, Luddy turned down a $2.5 billion acquisition offer for ServiceNow in 2011 and took it public the next year.
Luddy stepped down as CEO in 2011 to serve as chief product officer, a role he held until 2017. He became chairman of the board in 2018.
ServiceNow generated $9 billion in revenue in 2023.

In 2004, he took over as majority owner of the AHL's Hamilton Bulldogs and oversaw the club's 2007 Calder Cup victory.
He bought a minority stake in the Montreal Canadiens NHL team in 2009 and served as the team's alternate governor until 2023, when he sold his share of the team.
Andlauer led a group that purchased 90% of the Ottawa Senators in 2023 at a $950 million valuation.

In 2017, Shaich sold Panera to JAB Holdings for $7.5 billion; he pocketed nearly $400 million (pre-tax) from the sale.
The next year, Shaich reinvested $300 million of the proceeds in Act III Ventures, a new fund he founded to back emerging restaurant chains.
The fund's first big bet was on Cava, which went public at a nearly $5 billion valuation in June 2023.
Shaich owned nearly 10% of Cava when the company IPO'd but has since sold more than half his shares for at least $600 million (pre-tax).

Grupo Bafar had net sales of more than $450 million in 2024.

The company's IPO in November 2025 raised $83 million and made Keshre a billionaire.

name: Francesco Patarnello

The four friends launched Bending Spoons after working together on an unsuccessful, earlier startup Evertale, a note-taking app.
The Bending Spoons cofounders met while studying in Copenhagen, Denmark, and would later relocate to Milan, Italy, as their new startup took off.
The Milan, Italy-based startup struck on the strategy of buying apps and companies with a loyal audience where it sees the potential to overhaul its features and pricing.
Bending Spoons was largely bootstrapped until it raised its first major funding round in 2022 and made its first takeover of Evernote in 2023.

The company last raised $270 on a $11 billion in October 2025 to help fund its takeover of AOL and Vimeo. Bending Spoons is now Italy's most valuable startup and has bought, or taken private, a string of apps and startups like Meetup, Eventbrite, and WeTransfer.

Kalshi received federal approval in 2020 to operate in the U.S., and made history in 2024 after receiving federal approval to allow users to bet on the presidential election, marking the first legal election contracts in the U.S. in over a century.
Mansour grew up in Lebanon and met his cofounder, Luana Lopes Lara, while studying computer science at MIT.
He owns an estimated 12% stake in Kalshi.
