name: Luca Querella
about: Luca Querella cofounded Italian app developer Bending Spoons in 2013 with his three cofounders Luca Ferrari, Matteo Danieli and Francesco Patarnello.
The four friends launched Bending Spoons after working together on an unsuccessful, earlier startup Evertale, a note-taking app.
The Bending Spoons cofounders met while studying in Copenhagen, Denmark, and would later relocate to Milan, Italy, as their new startup took off.
The Milan, Italy-based startup struck on the strategy of buying apps and companies with a loyal audience where it sees the potential to overhaul its features and pricing.
Bending Spoons was largely bootstrapped until it raised its first major funding round in 2022 and made its first takeover of Evernote in 2023.

The company last raised $270 on a $11 billion in October 2025 to help fund its takeover of AOL and Vimeo. Bending Spoons is now Italy's most valuable startup and has bought, or taken private, a string of apps and startups like Meetup, Eventbrite, and WeTransfer.

name: Kurt Krieger
about: Kurt Krieger purchased Hoeffner Group in 1967 and turned it into one of Germany's leading furniture retailers.
After the fall of the Berlin wall in 1989, he seized the opportunity to tap into new markets in eastern Germany.
Besides Hoeffner Group, Krieger owns real estate in his hometown Berlin, having acquired almost 100 acres in 2010.
He's planning a development project with schools, shopping centers and, of course, a furniture store in the northern part of the city.
did_you_know_facts: In his youth, Krieger wanted to become a musician. He still plays the piano today.
He flies his own helicopter and often uses this means of transportation to get to business meetings.

name: Christoph Zeller
about: Christopher Zeller controls Ivoclar Vivadent, a closely-held maker of dental products and systems based in Schaan, Principality of Liechtenstein.
ounded in 1923 focusing on the production of artificial teeth, the company was bought by Zeller's grandfather, Dr. Adolf Schneider, in 1948.
Zeller served as CEO from 1990 to 2003. He served on the company's supervisory board until 2025, after having stepped down as chairman in 2019.
Today, Ivoclar Vivadent has subsidiaries in more than 50 countries, employs around 3,600 people and generates annual revenue in excess of $900 million.
did_you_know_facts: Zeller's wife, Christina, also serves on the supervisory board.

name: Mustafa Latif Topbas
about: Mustafa Latif Topbas is CEO and cofounder of BIM, Turkey's largest chain of discount stores. He owns about 15% of its shares.
After BIM went public in 2005, Topbas owned around 26%.
Founded in 1995, BIM has more than 12,000 locations across Turkey, Morocco and Egypt.
The company, with annual revenues exceeding $5 billion, offers a popular mobile telecom service under the brand name Bimcell.
did_you_know_facts: Topbas, who doesn't give interviews, has a longstanding friendship with Turkey's president, Recep Tayyip Erdogan, and his family.
His daughter Fatma is married to Ali Ulker, nephew of food billionaire Murat Ulker. (The families also have business ties through their companies.)

name: Timothy Headington
about: Inspired by geologist father, Timothy Headington founded Headington Oil in 1978. He sold his North Dakota oilfields to XTO Energy in 2008.
He found a new passion in filmmaking and helped bankroll "Hugo," "Argo," "World War Z," and the 2018 reboot of "Lara Croft: Tomb Raider."
He has invested in downtown Dallas, where he owns the Joule Hotel and department store 4510 and is partnering on a Virgin Hotel with Richard Branson.
After Oklahoma University, Headington earned graduate degrees in theology and psychology at Fuller Theological Seminary.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Oklahoma

did_you_know_facts: Headington was inducted into the Oklahoma Hall of Fame in 2014.
Headington cofounded the Headington Institute, a nonprofit organization that provides psychological support for humanitarian workers and first responders.

name: Polys Haji-Ioannou
about: Polys Haji-Ioanno is the son of late Cypriot shipping magnate Loucas Haji-Ioannou (d. 2008), who once owned the world's largest private tanker fleet.
Much of his wealth derives from a large stake in easyJet, the discount airline founded by his younger brother, Stelios.
Polys continues the family's shipping legacy with his own 13-tanker fleet.
He has also invested heavily in both commercial and residential real estate, particularly in Cyprus, Greece, Monaco and London.
did_you_know_facts: Haji-Ioanno's yacht, "Esmeralda," is named after one of the world's largest tortoises.
Haji-Ioanno remains involved in the philanthropic foundation started by his father.

name: Peter Kelly
about: Peter Kelly founded IT infrastructure provider Softcat in 1993, spending a reported $44,400 and working out of his garden shed.
Kelly, a college dropout, started out in sales at Xerox Corp.
He took Softcat public in 2015 on the London Stock Exchange and owns just over 30% of the company.
Kelly is known to offer his staff free breakfast and a weekly shirt-ironing service.

name: J. Wayne Weaver
about: Wayne Weaver is the chairman of shoe retailer Shoe Carnival.
Weaver and his wife Delores are the largest individual shareholders of Shoe Carnival, with a nearly one-third stake combined.
He was the first owner of the NFL's Jacksonville Jaguars and owned a majority of the team for 18 years.
He sold his stake in the Jaguars to billionaire Shahid Khan in 2011 in a deal that valued the franchise at $770 million.
Weaver started his career as a shoe salesman and eventually became CEO of retailer Nine West in 1978.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, University of Florida

did_you_know_facts: Weaver grew up in public housing and did odd jobs like digging ditches and delivering mail. He never attended college.

name: Kamlesh Jain
about: Kamlesh Jain is chairman of Chennai-based Jain Resources Recyling, which recycles lead, copper and aluminum scrap.
The company has three recycling facilities in Chennai.
It gets raw materials from more than 120 countries and recycles them.
The company exports the finished products to more than 20 countries including Bangladesh, Malaysia and Indonesia.
The company was founded in 1953 by his father Shantilal Jain as Jain Metal Rolling Mills for making brass and copper. It pivoted into recycling in 2013.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Commerce, University of Madras

name: Nobutada Saji
about: Saji is chairman of drinks powerhouse Suntory Holdings, which bought Beam, purveyor of Jim Beam and Maker's Mark bourbon, for $16 billion in 2014.
He stepped down as president in 2014, turning the reins over to a non-family member for the first time since the business was founded in 1899.
Saji owns a minority stake in Suntory Holdings, a closely held company. Its Suntory Beverage & Food unit trades on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Saji's nephew Nobuhiro Torii, a great grandson of Suntory's founder, is the president and CEO of Suntory Holdings.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Anderson School of Management

did_you_know_facts: In 2023, Suntory, which was founded in 1899, celebrated a century since it began building its first whisky distillery, in Yamazaki near Kyoto.

name: Martin Moller Nielsen
about: Martin Moller Nielsen is a Danish aviation entrepreneur who founded aircraft leasing firm Nordic Aviation Capital in 1990.
A quarter of a century later, he sold a 66% stake in it to private equity firms EQT and Krikbi in a deal that valued the firm at $3.3 billion.
He later brought on Singaporean sovereign wealth fund GIC as an investor and, in 2022, sold the last of his shares in NAC.
Moller Nielsen now runs Axiom Group, his private family office that invests in areas such as renewable energy and real estate.
did_you_know_facts: Moller Nielsen, a certified pilot by the age of 18, reportedly bought a beaten up aircraft at 21, renovated it, and sold it for a large profit.
NAC initially leased aircraft for humanitarian aid organizations looking to fly into remote areas.

name: Marcus Pürner
about: Marcus Purner controls Pending System and a related group of German cycle parts companies that sell bicycles under the Cube brand.
The businesses combined entities have revenue of more than $4 billion.
Purner started Cube in 1993, when he was a student, operating the new operation out of his father's furniture factory in Waldershof, Germany.

name: Michael Krasny
about: Michael Krasny founded Computer Discount Warehouse (CDW) in 1984 as an online store for IT products.
In 2007, he sold the company to Madison Dearborn Partners for $7.3 billion and has maintained a low profile ever since.
Krasny is an active donor to Jewish causes and medical research through his Circle of Service Foundation.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign

did_you_know_facts: In March 2017, Krasny reportedly paid $4.35 million for a condominium on the 50th floor of Park Tower in Chicago.
Krasny was a 28-year-old, unemployed college grad when he, after placing a $3 ad for his IBM personal computer on the paper, came up with the idea for CDW.

name: Thomas Mueller
about: Raised in rural Idaho, Mueller joined SpaceX in 2002 as employee No. 1, with a master's in mechanical engineering and experience building experimental rockets.
He and Elon Musk outlined plans for SpaceX's first rocket, Falcon 1, shortly after Musk sold PayPal to eBay, laying the foundation for the company's launch vehicle program.
As head of propulsion engineering, Mueller led the design and development of rocket engines for the Falcon launch vehicles and the Dragon spacecraft.
He departed SpaceX in 2020 to found Impulse Space, an aerospace startup focused on in-space transportation and orbital logistics.
Impulse has signed contracts with satellite provider SES, SpaceX, and NASA.

name: Carolin Hachenberg
about: Carolin Hachenberg is the daughter of Erwin Hymer, founder of the Erwin Hymer Group, a German maker of motor homes.
Hymer owned about half of the company when it was acquired by Thor in 2018 for $1.7 billion.
Erwin Hymer entered the motorhome business in 1956 and sold his first travel trailer, the Weltbummler, a year later.
The company became publicly traded in 1990 and was take private again in 2013.

name: Christian Hymer
about: Christian Hymer is the son of Erwin Hymer, founder of the Erwin Hymer Group, a German maker of motor homes.
Hymer owned about half of the company when it was acquired by Thor in 2018 for $1.7 billion.
Erwin Hymer entered the motorhome business in 1956 and sold his first travel trailer, the Weltbummler, a year later.
The company became publicly traded in 1990 and was take private again in 2013.

name: Kim Taek-jin
about: Kim Taek-jin is the founder and chairman of NCSoft, South Korea's No. 2 online game company which he founded in 1997.
He took the company public in 2003, and still serves as CEO. In 2024, Byungmoo Park joined Kim as co-CEO; Park was previously CEO of South Korean private equity firm VIG Partners.
NCSoft now provides online game services to more than 60 countries.
He sold most of his NCSoft shares in 2012 and now holds just under 12% of the company.
An avid sports fan, Kim founded the Korean professional baseball team NC Dinos in 2011.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Seoul National University; Master of Science, Seoul National University

did_you_know_facts: While still a student at Seoul National University's College of Engineering, he developed software that helped users practice typing in Korean.
He worked for Hyundai Electronics' R&D Center in Boston and later became head of a division of Hyundai Electronics that launched South Korea's first Internet access.

name: Chang Kuo-Ming
about: Chang Kuo-Ming is the second son of shipping tycoon Chang Yung Fa, who died in 2016 at the age of 88.
In 1968 Yung Fa founded Evergreen Marine, now one of the world's largest transportation companies.
Brothers Kuo-Hua, Kuo-Ming and Kuo-Cheng also inherited stakes in EVA Airways and hotels in Taiwan, mainland China, Paris and Bangkok.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, University of Southern California

name: Chad Richison
about: Chad Richison is founder and CEO of Paycom, one of the first companies to process payroll completely online.
Richison, a former senior manager at payroll firm ADP, created Paycom in 1998.
He took Paycom public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2014 and owns about 12% of its shares.
The company provides payroll and human resource services and joined the S&P 500 in 2020.
Richison founded a nonprofit, the Green Shoe Foundation, which aims to improve people's mental health through counseling and therapy sessions.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Central Oklahoma

did_you_know_facts: Richison was a wrestler in high school and college, placing at the state championships as a high school senior in his hometown of Tuttle, Oklahoma.

name: Huang Jian
about: Huang Jian is a former president of Midea Group, the biggest manufacturer of home appliances in China.
Huang Jian departed Midea in 2013 when it competed a backdoor listing on the Shenzhen stock exchange.
Huang Jian still owned more than 1% of Midea Group in 2023.

name: Qian Ying
about: Qian is a co-founder and director of Shenzhen-listed pig breeder Muyuan Foods, one of the world's largest pig breeders.
She is married to Muyuan chairman Qin Yinglin, with whom she co-founded the company in 1992 at age 26.
The couple started out with 22 pigs.
Qian is a graduate of the Henan University of Animal Husbandry Economy.

name: Igor Yakovlev
about: Igor Yakovlev is the founder of Kari, a Russian retailer of shoes, accessories and household products, which he founded in 2012.
Kari boasts 1,200 locations across Russia, including Moscow, St. Petersburg, Novosibirsk, Krasnoyarsk and Yekaterinburg, among other cities.
He also has stake in Sulpak, a large consumer electronics retailer in Kazakhstan; the company makes up a small part of his fortune.
In 2008 Yakovlev bought a 50% stake in FC Anzhi Makhachkala, a professional soccer club in Russia. Three years later he sold it to fellow Russian billionaire Suleiman Kerimov.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Dagestan Polytechnic Institute

name: Thomas Bailey
about: Thomas Bailey's fortune comes from mutual fund giant Janus, which he founded in Denver in 1969.
Bailey sold his 12% stake in Janus to its parent, Stillwell Financial, for $1.2 billion (pretax) in 2001-2002.
Janus had two decades of remarkable returns, but its funds began losing money in the early 2000s.
He served as the CEO of Janus for 33 years until 2002 and as chairman through 2003.
A Michigan State graduate who worked on Wall Street before moving to Denver, he spends his time fly-fishing and breeding horses.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Michigan State University; Master of Business Administration, University of Western Ontario

quote: Too much money can ruin a good mutual fund.

name: Lev Kvetnoi
about: Lev Kvetnoi has invested in airports, airport services, banking and cement.
Kvetnoi was the largest shareholder in Moscow's Vnukovo Airport, owning 30% of the project, until he sold out in 2013 and quit its board.
In 2011 he expanded his cement holdings by acquiring one of billionaire Elena Baturina's factories in southern Russia.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Leningrad Institute of Physical Culture

did_you_know_facts: For a time Kvetnoi served as chief executive of a company in billionaire Alisher Usmanov's metals group, but he sold out his interests to Usmanov in 2006.
In the early 1990s, Kvetnoi traded computers with an army friend Andrei Skoch, who is now also billionaire.

name: Michelle Xia
about: Michelle Yu Xia is cofounder, chairwoman and CEO of China-based biotech firm Akeso, which has multiple approved drugs in China to treat cancer.
Akeso has captured attention in the biotech world because one of its drugs outperformed Merck's bestseller Keytruda in a head to head Phase 3 trial in 2024.
The success of that Akeso drug, ivonescimab, drove up the price of Akeso's shares; the company is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.
Prior to Akeso, Xia worked in research and at U.S. biotech firms for a dozen years starting in the mid 1990s and obtained U.S. citizenship while in America.
Akeso licensed its most promising cancer drug to Miami-based firm Summit Therapeutics in 2022 for markets including the U.S., Europe and Japan.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Ph.D, Newcastle University; Bachelor of Science, Sun Yat-sen University

quote: We focus on science and biology and the most advanced technology. I think that makes the difference.

name: Marc Rubiralta
about: Marc Rubiralta chairs Werfen, one of Spain's largest diagnostics company based in Barcelona.
He inherited his stake from his late father Josep María Rubiralta, who cofounded Werfen which later became a specialist in in vitro diagnostics.
Since becoming chairman in 2019, one of his notable deals include the $2 billion acquisition of U.S.-based Immucor.
His brothers Jordi, Luis and Xavier each own stakes in the company and are also billionaires.
Rubiralta is also president of Monterri, the investment company he owns with José Luis and Xavier.

name: Xavier Rubiralta
about: Xavier Rubiralta owes his fortune to Spain-based Werfen, a diagnostics company that specializes in hemostasis, acute care, transfusion, autoimmunity and transplants.
A member of Werfen's board since 2013, he inherited his stake in the company from his late father in 2012.
Werfen's roots stem from his father and uncle who founded the business in 1966 as a health products distributor; it went on to acquire U.S.-based Instrumentation Laboratory in 1991.
Each inheriting equal stakes from his father, his brother Jordi, Jose Luis and Marc are also billionaires.

name: Jose Luis Rubiralta
about: Jose Luis Rubiralta derives his fortune from Werfen, which he inherited from his late father Josep Maria Rubiralta, in 2012.
One of Spain's largest diagnostic companies, Werfen operates in 30 countries and employs 7,000 people.
The company traces its roots to his late father Josep Maria Rubiralta and uncle Francisco, who founded its predecessor Izasa in 1966.
Werfen's notable international acquisitions include Tem in Germany and Instrumentation Laboratory and Accriva Diagnostics in the U.S.
Rubiralta has been a member of the company's board since 2013. His brothers Jordi, Marc and Xavier, who are involved in the business, are also billionaires.

name: Yuan Zhimin & family
about: Yuan Zhimin is founder of Shanghai-listed Kingfa Sci & Tech, a supplier of modified plastics.
In 2020, due to the global pandemic, the company expanded into the production of medical and protective gloves.
Yuan, who holds a graduate degree from the Beijing Institute of Technology, founded the company in 1993.
Yuan's son, Yuan Changchang, was appointed vice chairman of Kingfa in 2024.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Bejing Insitute of Technology; Master of Science, Beijing Institute of Technology

name: Lin Zhixiong & family
about: Lin Zhixiong chairs Double Medical Technology.
Double Medical Technology's main products are trauma implant and spinal implant consumables.
Lin studied at Chiba University in Japan from April 2003 to June 2004.
Lin founded the predecessor of Double Medical Technology after he returned from Japan in 2004.

name: Jorge Gallardo Ballart
about: Jorge Gallardo Ballart's father founded pharmaceutical company Almirall in 1943 in Barcelona.
After their father died in 1988, Jorge and his brother Antonio took over running Almirall; the company is publicly traded.
Jorge is executive president of Almirall, which had about $900 million revenues in 2020.
In 2018, Almirall announced the acquisition of five products from the dermatology division of Allergan.
Ballart's son, Carlos Gallardo Piqué, was appointed chairman of Almirall in 2022.

name: Alexander Klyachin
about: Alexander Klyachin owns one of the biggest Russian hotel chains, Azimut, which operates more than 11,000 rooms.
Klyachin earned his fortune largely in Moscow's commercial real estate market and from buying land from collective farmers.
Klyachin lost his business centers in Moscow due to a decision by the Prosecutor General's Office; later he bought back some of them.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Moscow State University

did_you_know_facts: Klyachin owns the Metropol hotel, which served as the headquarters of the opposition to the Bolsheviks in 1917.

name: Tsao Ter-fung
about: Tsao Ter-fung is the chairman of food and beverage company Standard Foods.
He worked for Quaker Oats in the U.S. and became head of its Taiwan operations in 1981.
In 1986 Tsao bought Quaker's Taiwan assets and set up his own business.
His Ph.D. is in food-and-chemical engineering.
His son Arthur Tsao took over the reins as CEO in 2019.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Ph.D, Colorado State University; Master of Science, Colorado State University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, National Cheng Kung University

name: Xu Wanmao
about: Xu Wanmao chairs the Huamao Group, whose interests include education, real estate and investment.
Huamao Group is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Ningbo, where it ranks as one of the city's largest service industry businesses.
Huamao Group's investments include the Bank of Ningbo.

name: Cheng Lili
about: Cheng Lili chairs Jiangsu Lihua Animal Husbandry, a chicken breeder and supplier of poultry feed.
Lihua debuted at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange on Feb. 28, 2019, after raising $171 million in an IPO.
Lihua is headquarterd in the eastern Chinese city of Changzhou.

name: Howard Huang
about: Howard Huang is the founder, chairman and CEO of Orbbec, a developer of 3D vision cameras.
Its cameras allow machines to perceive depth like human eyes do, and enable them to better navigate the environment.
Backed by Chinese fintech giant Ant Group, the Shenzhen-based company supplies to Alipay for its facial recognition payment system.
It also sells to the robotics clients including Chinese service bot maker Pudu Robotics as well as humanoid developers such as state-backed X-Humanoid and Ant Group's Ant Lingbo Technology.
Huang took Orbbec public on Shanghai's Star market in a 1.2 billion yuan ($169 million) IPO in 2022.
did_you_know_facts: A trained engineer specializing in optical measurement, Huang founded Orbbec in 2013, hoping to turn his academic research into real-world applications.

name: Jeffrey Michael & family
about: Jeffrey Michael is a founding investor and board member of Corvel Corporation, a healthcare technology company.
He and family members hold a 38% stake in Corvel through Michael's investment vehicle, Corstar Holdings, Inc.
Michael helped start Corvel in 1987; originally named Fortis, it began as a small chain of vocational rehabilitation firms.
The company has since grown into a national provider of risk management solutions for payors and employers and generated $795 million of revenue in 2024.

name: Michael Dunlap & family
about: Michael Dunlap is the cofounder and executive chairman of Nelnet, a loan servicing and payment processing company based in Lincoln, Nebraska
He started the company in the late 1990s with Stephen Butterfield (d. 2018). The two took the company public in 2003.
Michael's son Matthew is the chief business development officer and serves on the board.
His nephew Jason Muhleisen is the president and CEO of Lincoln's Union Bank & Trust, owned by the Dunlap family.
A graduate of the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, Dunlap serves on the board of the Raikes School of Computer Science and Management.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Nebraska Lincoln; Doctor of Jurisprudence, University of Nebraska Lincoln

name: Vera Rechulski Santo Domingo
about: Vera Rechulski Santo Domingo is the widow of Julio Mario Santo Domingo Jr. (d. 2009), who was the son of Colombian beer baron Julio Mario Santo Domingo.
She controls about 11% of the Santo Domingo family's Luxembourg-based holding company, through which she owns shares in Anheuser-Busch InBev.
Her two children, Tatiana Casiraghi and Julio Mario Santo Domingo III, own smaller stakes of about 5% each.
The family also owns a stake in Château Pétrus, a French wine estate near Bordeaux that produces some of the world's most expensive wines.
The family's public holdings also include stakes in Keurig Dr. Pepper and Kraft Heinz, as well as closely-held companies in Colombia, including movie theaters, supermarkets and gas distribution.

name: Huang Yimeng
about: Huang is founder and chairman of online game platform XD Inc.
XD was founded in 2011 and is headquartered in Shanghai.
Huang, a veteran in the tech industry, oversees the company's management and operations.

name: Daniel Dines
about: Daniel Dines is cofounder and CEO of UiPath, a robotic process automation company that went public on the New York Stock Exchange in April 2021.
Dines started DeskOver in 2005 in Bucharest, Romania. He later renamed it UiPath and moved its headquarters to New York City in 2018.
Customers like Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui bank or Toyota North America can spend millions on UiPath's virtual "robot" that can automate complex, repetitive tasks.
An avid reader, Dines said in a 2019 Forbes cover story that he reads in the mornings, often not showing up to UiPath's office until 11 am.
UiPath recorded $1.4 billion in revenue and a net loss of $74 million in the fiscal year through January 2025.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, University of Bucharest; Master of Science, University of Bucharest

did_you_know_facts: In October 2019, after a period of rapid hiring at UiPath, the company laid off more than 300 employees, or about 11% of its workforce.

name: Su Qingcan
about: Su Qingnan chairs Huaxia Eye Hospital, a provider of healthcare services headquartered in China's southeastern city of Xiamen.
Huaxia also serves patients in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar, Nepal and Sri Lanka.
Su emerged as a billionaire after Huaxia went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in November 2022.

name: Tony Chen
about: Tony Chen cofounded Largan Precision, a lens supplier to Apple and other tech outfits, with fellow billionaire Scott Lin.
He stepped down as chairman in 2013 and sat on the board until 2022.
The company is a leading smartphone lens maker and a major supplier to Apple, claiming a quarter of the global market.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, National Cheng Kung University

name: Roman Avdeev
about: Avdeev's first business was selling radio components and decoders for TV sets in the late 1980s.
The source of his wealth is Credit Bank of Moscow, one of Russia's largest banks by assets, which Avdeev bought in 1994 responding to a newspaper ad.
In addition to the financial sector, Avdeev owns a pharmacy chain and has assets in construction, timber and oil industries.
He sold all his assets including Credit Bank of Moscow to his partner billionaire Sergei Sudarikov in 2024.
Avdeev founded the charitable foundation "Arithmetic of Good," which helps orphans.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Moscow International University of Business and Information Technologies

did_you_know_facts: Avdeev has 23 children, 19 of whom are adopted.
In 2009, Avdeev ascended Mount Wilson, Antartica's highest point.
Avdeev owns football club Torpedo, founded in the early 1920s on the basis of the sports department of the Red Army
quote: Banking is a rather boring business, but you have to go to work every day and work honestly.

name: Grigory Anikeev
about: Grigory Anikeev owns ABI Group, a Russian conglomerate with interests in food, retail and real estate.
ABI Product, the largest division of ABI Group, is the largest Russian producer of sausage products and frozen food with revenue of about $1 billion.
Anikeev has been deputy of The State Duma, the lower house of the Russian parliament, since 2007, and is a member of President Vladimir Putin's United Russia Party.
In 2020, Anikeev declared the highest annual income among State Duma deputies - 2.7 billion rubles ($38 million).
did_you_know_facts: ABI Group is an acronym for Anikeev Business Invest.

name: Xiong Wu
about: Xiong is a director at Sangfor Technologies, a supplier of IT infrastructure services.
Sangfor listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2018.
The Shenzhen-headquartered company has more than 9,500 employees.

name: Zhong Peifeng
about: Zhong Peifeng is chairman of Amlogic Shanghai, a microchip supplier.
Zhong holds a master's degree from Georgia Institute of Technology.

name: Lauren Leichtman
about: Lauren Leichtman cofounded the buyout firm Levine Leichtman Capital Partners with her husband Arthur Levine in 1984, five years after the couple got married.
LLCP has managed $16.4 billion of institutional capital across 15 funds since inception, and currently manages $11 billion in assets.
The firm's target sectors include business services, franchising, education and training, and engineered products and manufacturing.
Successful exits have included Tropical Smoothie Cafe, Wetzel's Pretzels and Nothing Bundt Cakes.
Prior to entering private equity, Leichtman worked as a lawyer, including with the enforcement division of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.
As a couple, Leichtman and Levine share a fortune worth an estimated $2.6 billion.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, California State University, Northridge; LLM, Columbia Law School; JD, Southwestern University School of Law

did_you_know_facts: In October 2024, Leichtman and Levine bought the National Women's Soccer League's San Diego Wave FC for $113 million.

name: Arthur Levine
about: Arthur Levine cofounded the buyout firm Levine Leichtman Capital Partners with his wife Lauren Leichtman in 1984, five years after the couple were married.
LLCP has managed $14.8 billion of institutional capital across 15 funds since inception, and currently manages $10.2 billion in assets.
The firm's target sectors include business services, franchising and multi-unit, education and training, and engineered products and manufacturing.
Successful exits have included Tropical Smoothie Cafe, Wetzel's Pretzels and Nothing Bundt Cakes.
Prior to entering private equity, Levine was president of Westwood One, a radio syndicate.
As a couple, Levine and Leichtman share a fortune worth an estimated $2.6 billion.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: JD, Columbia Law School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, UCLA; Master of Business Administration, UCLA Anderson School of Management

did_you_know_facts: In October 2024, Levine and Leichtman bought the National Women's Soccer League's San Diego Wave FC for $113 million.

name: Joe Kiani
about: Joe Kiani founded medical technology firm Masimo Corp., whose devices non-invasively measure oxygen levels in patients' blood in 1989.
Kiani was ousted from Masimo's board and resigned as CEO in September 2024 after activist shareholders won a proxy fight.
An immigrant from Iran who studied electrical engineering in the U.S., Kiani came up with a way to vastly improve the performance of pulse oximeters early in his career.
Following years of struggle to break into the U.S. hospital market, Masimo became the leader in pulse oximetry for hospitals.

Kiani now serves as executive chairman of Willow Labs, which is rolling out techn to nudge people to improve their metabolic health, and as chairman of Like Minded Labs, which launched a virtual collaboration platform.
Danaher agreed to buy Masimo for nearly $10 billion in February 2026.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, San Diego State University; Bachelor of Engineering, San Diego State University

did_you_know_facts: Kiani's family moved from Iran to Alabama in 1974 for his dad's engineering studies; for a year they lived in a housing project in Huntsville.
Kiani finished high school near San Diego at age 15 and graduated from San Diego State University with a master's degree in engineering at age 22.
quote: I wanted to be a doctor, but my grades weren't that good and chemistry was not my thing. Physics fortunately was. So I switched to engineering.

name: Lívia Voigt de Assis
about: Lívia Voigt de Assis, one of the world's youngest billionaires, is one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, the largest manufacturer of electrical motors in Latin America.
At twenty years old, she is the world's second-youngest billionaire, behind nineteen-year-old German pharmaceuticals heir Johannes von Baumbach.
WEG was cofounded by her grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt along with late billionaires Eggon Joao da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus.
A publicly-traded multinational with factories in over ten countries, WEG has annual revenue of approximately $7 billion.
Lívia does not hold a board seat or any executive position at WEG; she is currently attending university.
did_you_know_facts: Voigt de Assis was the world's youngest billionaire in 2025 before losing the spot to German pharmaceutical heir, Johannes von Baumbach, a year later.

name: Dora Voigt de Assis
about: Dora Voigt de Assis is one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, the largest manufacturer of electrical motors in Latin America.
The company was cofounded by her grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt along with late billionaires Eggon Joao da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus.
A publicly-traded multinational with factories in over ten countries, WEG has annual revenue of approximately $7 billion.
Dora does not hold a board seat or any executive position at WEG; she graduated from university with an architecture degree in 2020.

name: Benjamin Zhengmin Pan & family
about: Pan "Benjamin" Zhengmin is CEO of miniaturized electronics components firm AAC Technologies.
Pan and his wife Ingrid cofounded AAC in 1993. It now makes speakers, receivers, microphones and antennas, often used in smartphones.
AAC, whose customers include Apple, went public in Hong Kong in 2005.
Pan graduated from the Jiangsu Province Wujin Teacher School in 1987.

name: Dieter Müller
about: Dieter Muller is the co-founder of European budget hotel chain Motel One.
Muller and partner Philippe Weyland created the concept for the business in 1999 and opened their first property in Frankfurt-Offenbach one year later.
Motel One investors have included German software billionaire Dietmar Hopp and a Morgan Stanley real estate fund that acquired a 35% stake in 2007.
Muller signed an agreement to sell a majority stake in 2025 that valued the business at 3.5 billion euros. He Still owns 6% plus 40% of its real estate portfolio.

name: Michael Rees
about: Michael Rees is cofounder and co-president of Blue Owl, which manages $250 billion and formed in 2021 when his Dyal Capital merged with Owl Rock Capital.
Dyal, since renamed Blue Owl GP Strategic Capital, is known for buying minority stakes in more than 60 other private equity firms.
Rees' division also invests in professional sports, with a fund that owns pieces of the NBA's Phoenix Suns, Sacramento Kings and Atlanta Hawks.
Rees still heads Blue Owl GP Strategic Capital, which oversees $66 billion. The rest of the firm's assets are in private credit and real estate.
Rees spent seven years at Lehman Brothers and started Dyal as a subsidiary of Neuberger Berman, which bought out parts of the bankrupt Lehman in 2009.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts/Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology; Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Pittsburgh

name: Ruben Vardanyan & family
about: Ruben Vardanyan cofounded investment company Troika Dialog in the early 1990s and is known as the father of the Russian stock market.
In 2013, Vardanyan and his managers sold Troika Dialog to state-owned Sberbank for $1.4 billion.
Vardanyan founded investment boutique Vardanyan, Broitman and partners, which serves ultra high-net-worth individuals, in 2014.
In 2021 he obtained Armenian citizenship and later renounced his Russian citizenship and moved to Armenia.
In November 2022 Vardanyan was appointed the State Minister of Artsakh (Karabakh). He transferred his business assets to the family trust. In February 2023 he dismissed as State Minister.
Vardanyan was arrested by the Azerbaijani State Border Service in 2023 while attempting to enter Armenia; In December 2025, prosecutors requested a life sentence for him.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Moscow State University

name: Mohammed Ibrahim
about: Mohammed "Mo" Ibrahim founded Celtel International in 1998, one of the first mobile phone companies serving Africa and the Middle East.
He sold Celtel to Kuwait's Mobile Telecommunications Company for $3.4 billion in 2005 and pocketed $1.4 billion.
Since then, he's focused on fighting corrupt leadership in Africa through the Mo Ibrahim Foundation, directed by his daughter, Hadeel.
Ibrahim also chairs the board of Satya Capital, a private equity fund that invests in African businesses, education and healthcare.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Alexandria; Master, University of Bradford; Ph.D, University of Birmingham

did_you_know_facts: Ibrahim's foundation has awarded the Ibrahim Prize, $5 million plus $200,000 annually for the rest of a laureate's life, to presidents of seven African countries.
He was born in Sudan.

name: James Jannard
about: Jim Jannard founded sunglasses brand Oakley out of his car in 1975.
He took Oakley public in 1995 and sold it to Luxottica in 2007 for $2.1 billion in cash.
By then he was working on his next project, Red Digital, building high-resolution cameras used in movies like "Avatar" and "The Hobbit." He agreed to sell the business to Nikon in March 2024.
He launched Red Hydrogen One, a holographic smartphone that was plagued with issues, in 2018 but shut down the project in 2019.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Drop Out, University of Southern California

did_you_know_facts: The USC pharmacy student dropped out in the 1960s after clashing with professors over bringing his dog to class.
Jannard named Oakley after his beloved English Setter, Oakley Anne. He has funded a breeder in Washington for decades.

name: Ye Shanqun & family
about: Ye Shanqun built up Shuanghuan in the spring of 1980 with only 3000 yuan and five instrument lathes in Hangzhou, Zhejiang province.
Zhejiang Shuanghuan Driveline went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2010.
Customers include Cummins,and Caterpillar, as well as SAIC Motor, China's largest automaker.
For more than 40 years, the company has been mechanical transmission. It is a leading global manufacturer in the gear component industry.
Shuanghuan set up a company in Hungary to support its Europe market.

name: Nigel Austin
about: Nigel Austin is the founder and majority owner of the Cotton On clothing and stationery group. Its brands include Cotton On, Supre, Factorie and Typo.
His company has close to 1,300 stores in 17 countries with 2025 revenue of around $1.5 billion.
About half of these stores are in Australia, while the other half are spread across countries such as Singapore, South Africa and the U.S.
Founded in 1991, Austin started selling acid-washed denim jackets from the trunk of his car in his hometown southwest of Melbourne.
Now it sells inexpensive fashion basics, including T-shirts, leggings, sweatpants, shoes and underwear, as well as quirky stationery.
did_you_know_facts: Austin's late father, Grant Austin, ran a publicly traded clothing wholesale and import business called the Austin Group, where Austin would spend school holidays working.
In 1991 Austin set up his first store in a small space behind a butcher shop run by his grandfather and sourced merchandise from his father.
quote: There was plenty of tough love. My family had a very successful business, but I was limited with resources when I went to college. I was forced to go out there and have a strong work ethic.

name: Derek Stevens
about: Derek Stevens is the CEO and majority owner of three casinos in Downtown Las Vegas, The Golden Gate, The D and his crown jewel, Circa.
Stevens, who co-owns these properties with his brother, opened Circa in October 2020 at a cost of $1 billion. It was the first new casino in Downtown Las Vegas since the 1980s.
Born in Grosse Point, Michigan, Stevens is also the CEO of Cold Heading Co., a leading manufacturer and supplier of fasteners for the auto industry that his family started in the early 1900s.
Stevens first bought 50% of The Golden Gate on Fremont Street, which opened in 1906 as Sin City's first hotel and casino. A few years later, he bought the rest.
In 2011, Stevens bought Fitzgerald's, an Irish-themed casino, and completed a 36-story renovation and renamed it The D.
Stevens also owns Circa Sports, a sports betting company that is live across seven states.

name: Kenzo Tsujimoto
about: Kenzo Tsujimoto is the chairman and CEO of Osaka gaming company Capcom, which he founded in 1983.
Capcom is known for popular video games such as Resident Evil, Monster Hunter and Street Fighter.
His eldest son, Haruhiro Tsujimoto, is president and COO of Capcom while his youngest son, Ryozo Tsujimoto, oversees Monster Hunter.
Tsujimoto also owns the 3,800-acre Kenzo Estate in California's Napa Valley, of which 125 acres have been developed into vineyards.
did_you_know_facts: His wife Natsuko, who is COO of the winery, has set up five Kenzo Estate restaurants in Japan and an upscale restaurant in downtown Napa.
The Kenzo Estate site used to be the training ground for the U.S. equestrian team.

name: Deepak Mehta
about: Deepak Mehta is chairman of listed Indian chemicals firm Deepak Nitrite, in which he has a stake.
The company was founded in 1971 by his father Chimanlal Mehta, who died in July 2023.
With a portfolio of 100 products, Deepak Nitrite is a leading producer of phenol and acetone in India.
It has more than 700 customers across the globe.
His son Maulik Mehta, who has a masters degree in industrial and organizational psychology from Columbia University, is the CEO.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, University of Mumbai

name: Nancy Lerner
about: Nancy Lerner owes her riches to her billionaire dad, Al Lerner (d. 2002), and to his banking fortune.
Al started his career as a furniture salesman, invested in Cleveland-area real estate and bought control of Equitable Bancorp in 1981.
Equitable Bancorp and Maryland National formed the credit card giant MBNA, whose 2005 merger with Bank of America created a $35 billion enterprise.
The Lerners bought the Cleveland Browns in 1999 and sold the team to Jimmy Haslam for about $1 billion in 2012.

personal_stats.label: Education

name: Michael Kum
about: Hotel tycoon Michael Kum runs a hospitality empire spanning 21 hotels across Asia and Europe through his privately held M&L Hospitality.
His eldest daughter Jocelyn helps him run the hotel group, which includes brands such as Hilton and Hyatt.
The son of street hawkers, Kum got into hotels in 2009 after selling his offshore barges business to Macquarie Group.
In June 2025, he acquired Hotel Maria, a 116-room luxury hotel in Helsinki, Finland. It will be rebranded as Waldorf Astoria Helsinki and managed by Hilton.
did_you_know_facts: He cofounded Offshore Equipment in 1976, chartering vessels and barges to the oil and gas industry.
He also has a stake in Australian vessel operator, MMA Offshore.

name: Lim Kaling
about: Lim Kaling is an early investor and non-executive director of Razer, a gaming hardware maker that was set up in 2005.
The company has acquired a huge global following and sold millions of gaming laptops, mice, fitness bands and tablets. It went public in Hong Kong in 2017, raising $529 million.
Lim and Razer cofounder Min-Liang Tan took the company private in 2022 in a deal that valued it at $3.2 billion.
Lim also runs the Lim Teck Lee group, a family business with interests in real estate, manufacturing and trading.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Business Administration, University of California Berkeley

name: Tan Lili
about: Tan Lili's fortune stems from his stake in Haid Group, a supplier of aquatic products and livestock feed.
Haid is headquartered in Guangzhou, China.
Haid went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2009.

name: Ivan Müller Botelho
about: Ivan Muller Botelho is the chairman of the board of directors of the publicly traded Brazilian electricity utility Energisa.
Muller Botelho is the third-generation descendant of one of the founders of Energisa; the family has maintained control of the company since 1905.
Energisa serves over 20 million customers in Brazil, controlling nine regional electricity distribution companies.
Muller Botelho's elder son Ricardo Perez Botelho currently serves as chief executive officer of Energisa, while his younger son Mauricio Perez Botelho is its chief financial officer.
Muller Botelho received a degree in electrical engineering from the University of Miami.

personal_stats.label: Education

name: Randolph Lerner
about: Randy Lerner owes his riches to his billionaire dad, Al Lerner (d. 2002), who made a fortune in credit cards.
His father got his start as a furniture salesman then invested in Cleveland-area real estate. He later bought control of Equitable Bancorp in 1981.
Equitable Bancorp merged with Maryland National to form credit card giant MBNA, which was acquired by Bank of America for $35 billion in 2005.

Lerner and his family sold the English football club Aston Villa for $88 million to Chinese businessman Tony Xia in 2016 after a decade of ownership.

name: Holger Timm
about: Holger Timm is the founder and controlling shareholder of German investment company, Effektengesellschaft.
Timm founded the company as a stock brokerage in 1986 and owns about 88% of the publicly traded business.
The Berlin-based company offers financial services, including brokerage, financial advisory services, investment funds and venture capital.
Through a subsidiary, it launched an all-day trading platform call Tradegate in 2001, whose investors now include BNP Paribas.

name: Norma Lerner
about: Norma Lerner is the widow of Al Lerner (d. 2002), who made a fortune as founder of credit card giant MBNA.
Al started his career as a furniture salesman, invested in Cleveland-area real estate and bought control of Equitable Bancorp in 1981.
Equitable Bancorp and Maryland National formed the credit card giant MBNA, which was acquired by Bank of America for $35 billion in 2005.

They bought the Cleveland Browns in 1999 and brought pro football back to the city, but sold the team to billionaire Jimmy Haslam for about $1 billion in 2012.

name: Huang Shanbing & family
about: Huang Shanbing chairs Shenzhen-listed Jiangsu JieJie Microelectronics, a microchip maker.
Huang founded the predecessor of Jiejie Microelectronics in Qidong in Jiangsu province in 1995.
From 1974 to 1995, Huang worked in a transistor crystal valve factory in Jiangsu Province.

name: Ben Francis
about: Ben Francis is the founder and CEO of Solihull, England-based sportswear brand Gymshark.
Francis sold a 21% stake to private equity firm General Atlantic in August 2020, in a deal that valued the company at $1.45 billion; he owns 70%.
He cofounded the company with his friend Lewis Morgan in his parents' garage in 2012 at age 19, when he was still a college student delivering pizzas.
Gymshark grew thanks to partnerships with fitness influencers on social media, paying them small amounts to wear the company's gear in their videos.
The company also has an office in Denver and opened its first brick-and-mortar store on London's Regent Street in October 2022.
did_you_know_facts: Francis built two fitness apps when he was an 18-year-old college student.
Gymshark started out selling supplements, but Francis and Morgan quickly pivoted to selling fitness gear they made with a screen printer and sewing machine.

name: Nicholas Woodman
about: Nick Woodman, a surfer and outdoors enthusiast, founded wearable video-camera company GoPro in 2002 and took it public in 2014.
Shares of GoPro soared following its initial public offering but fell dramatically starting in 2015, knocking Woodman off Forbes? billionaires list in 2016.
Woodman, who still serves as CEO of GoPro, has sold more than $540 million worth of his shares since taking the company public.
Compounded investment returns on the cash from selling shares paved the way for Woodman's return to the billionaire ranks in 2024.
Woodman owns a 180-foot yacht, Driftwood, which he took delivery of in 2017.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of California, San Diego

did_you_know_facts: Woodman and his wife Jill donated nearly $500 million worth of GoPro shares in October 2014 to a charitable entity at the Silicon Valley Community Foundation.
In 2019, the Woodmans donated a reported $4 million to a new $20 million community center in Big Sky, Montana, where they live.

name: Zhu Weisong
about: Zhu Weisong is the chairman and CEO of Shanghai-based toy maker Bloks Group.
The company raised HK$1.7 billion ($215 million) in a frenzied Hong Kong IPO in January 2025. The retail portion in the offering was 6,000 times oversubscribed.
Bloks sells Lego-like building blocks and figurines including those based on Japan's Ultraman superhero characters.
Zhu previously cofounded Shanghai-listed games developer Yoozoo Information Technology. He left in 2016 to build Bloks.

name: Hyuntae Kim
about: Hyuntae Kim is CEO of South Korean biotechnology company Voronoi.
Voronoi's two most promising cancer drug candidates are VRN10 and VRN11. Both started Phase 1 clinical trials in 2025.
Voronoi was founded by Kim's younger brother, Hyun-seok, in 2015. The older Kim took over the company in 2016 and listed it on Korea's Kosdaq in 2022.
Previously, Kim did stints as head of asset management at eBest Investment & Securities, Hanwha Investment & Securities and KB Securities.

name: Clemens Toennies
about: Clemens Toennies owns 45% of German food industry giant Toennies Lebensmittel, with annual revenue of around $6 billion. His son Maximilian owns 5%.
Operating meat, convenience, ingredients and logistics divisions, the company specializes in pig, sow and beef cattle slaughtering and processing.
Clemens attended butchery college and, in 1971, cofounded the company with his brother, Bernd.
Bernd died in 1994, at age 42. His son, Robert, now owns 50% of the business, which employs more than 15,000 people in facilities in Germany and Denmark.
Clemens fought in court with Robert for several years. In 2017, they settled their dispute over ownership of stakes in the company.
did_you_know_facts: For many years, Clemens presided over pro soccer team FC Schalke 04. He resigned from his post as chairman in June 2020.
Pressure on him had been mounting after racist remarks in 2019, poor team performance on the field, and a Covid-19 outbreak at one of his company's slaughterhouses.

name: Robert Toennies
about: Robert Toennies owns 50% of German food industry giant Toennies Lebensmittel, with annual revenue of around $6 billion.
Operating meat, convenience, ingredients and logistics divisions, the company specializes in pig, sow and beef cattle slaughtering and processing.
Robert's father, Bernd, and uncle, Clemens, cofounded Toennies Lebensmittel in 1971. It employs more than 15,000 people in Germany and Denmark.
Bernd died in 1994, at age 42. Robert inherited his stake and now serves on the board of advisors of the holding company.
Clemens and his son Maximilian own the other 50% of Toennies Lebensmittel.
did_you_know_facts: Robert fought in court with Clemens for several years. In 2017, they settled their dispute over ownership of stakes in the company.
Toennies Lebensmittel is expanding into China in partnership with Dekon Group, a move that reportedly has contributed to renewed tensions between Robert and Clemens.

name: Philip & family Hager

The company is a leading provider of solutions and services for electrical installations, covering business fields such as energy distribution, cable management, and building automation.
Hager SE generates consolidated group revenues exceeding $3.5 billion annually.
Originally founded as a GmbH, the company has a history spanning over three decades and transitioned into a Societas Europaea (SE) in May 2007.
The group operates internationally with a workforce exceeding 13,000 employees and manages well-known brands such as Hager, Berker, and E3/DC.

name: Kazim Turker
about: Kazim Türker is the founder of Türkerler Holding, which operates in the construction, real estate, energy, and healthcare sectors.

With Italian firm Astaldi, Türkerler built the Etlik City Hospital through a partnership with the Turkish government and has a total investment of $1.3 billion. Türkerler has three city hospitals in Turkey with a total of 7,068 beds.
In energy, the company owns hydroelectric, wind and geothermal power plants with a total capacity of 534 megawatts. It also owns an electricity company serving 828,000 subscribers in four provinces.
In real estate, Türkerler's two major projects - Mahall Bomonti in İzmir and Mahall in Ankara - were completed with investments of $650 million and $450 million, respectively.

Türker started his entrepreneurial journey at age 19 and opened a small clothing store in Ankara before venturing into construction. One of his first projects was the Police Moral Education Center in Istanbul.

In 1993 his brother and junior partner Sergei wrote the accounting application for DOS operating system. A year later 1C developed the accounting software for Windows.
Now 1C Group is the conglomerate of software companies, which develop various business and education software and games.
1C has 8,000 franchise partners, which provide IT and consulting services to customers.

name: Kim Hyoung-nyon
about: Kim Hyoung-nyon is cofounder and vice chairman of Dunamu, which operates Upbit, South Korea's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volume.
In November 2025, South Korean search engine behemoth Naver said its payment arm, Naver Financial, will acquire Dunamu in a stock swap that values the combined entity at $13.6 billion.
Dunamu's previous investors include Kakao Ventures, Silicon Valley-based venture capital firm Altos Ventures and Hybe, the agency behind K-pop powerhouse BTS.
Before starting Dunamu with Song Chi-hyung, who is also a billionaire, Kim worked at local mobile payment company Danal.

Gen, who started the company in 1999, resigned as chairman in 2022.

name: J. Christopher Flowers
about: J. Christopher Flowers runs private equity firm J.C. Flowers & Co., which focuses on the financial services sector.
Flowers studied math at Harvard and then joined Goldman Sachs in 1979, becoming a partner in 1988.
He struck out on his own a decade later and in 2000 bought a beleaguered Japanese bank, Long Term Credit Bank, which had been nationalized in 1998.
He resold the business to the public under the moniker Shinsei Bank in 2004; the partners reaped $2.3 billion.
In 2008, he helped advise Bank of America and Merrill Lynch on their merger.

During his college years, Flowers wrote for the Harvard Crimson.

Snowflake went public in 2020 and raised $3.9 billion, in what was then the largest software IPO in U.S. history.
Cruanes and Dageville met while working at Oracle.

Zan investments over the years have ranged include financial services, spirits, dairy and software.
Zan holds an EMBA degree from Tsinghua University.

name: Cheah Cheng Hye
about: Cheah Cheng Hye is honorary chairman of Hong Kong-listed asset management firm Value Partners Group, which he cofounded in 1993 and took public in 2007.
He stepped down as cochairman in January 2025.
Born in Malaysia, he worked as a reporter, subeditor and writer at the Star newspaper in the country after leaving Penang Free School with a high school diploma.
In 1974, he traveled to Hong Kong, where he had stints in journalism at the Standard, HK-TVB News, the Asian Wall Street Journal and the Far Eastern Economic Review.
He worked at Morgan Grenfell Group in Hong Kong before starting Value Partners.

name: Li Jianguo
about: Li Jianguo is chairman of China's Runjian Communication, an IT company serving the telecommunications industry with $1.2 billion in sales (2023).
Founded by Li in 2003, today Runjian employs 1,700 engineers and covers 29 provinces, more than 200 cities and 1,200 counties across China.
Runjian, which has subsidiaries in Hong Kong, Myanmar, Indonesia and the Philippines, also provides its services to the renewable energy market.
Li served in the military before starting the company; he shares his fortune with his wife, Jiang Libei.

ENKA, which was cofounded in 1957 by Sarik Tara and his brother-in-law, Sadi Gulcelik, is Turkey's leading private electricity producer and also operates in real estate, tourism, transport and trade (construction equipment and machinery).
In Moscow, ENKA owns a hotel, shopping malls and approximately 370,000 square meters of net rentable Class A office space.
Sadi Gulcelik died in a plane accident in Saudi Arabia in 1980, and Mehmet Sinan Tara took over in 1984 at age 26. His son Agah Mehmet Tara became CEO in 2012, at age 29.

about: Tony Townley founded the chicken chain Zaxby's with Zach McLeroy, his best friend since the seventh grade.
Townley and McLeroy each put up $8,000 to open the first Zaxby's restaurant in Statesboro, Georgia in 1990.
In 2020, Townley sold his stake in the business to Goldman Sachs for nearly $1 billion (pre-tax).
McLeroy sold part of his stake and remained CEO after the sale before stepping down from the chief executive role in 2022.
Townley and his wife Elizabeth have poured a chunk of their earnings into buying at least 35,000 acres of timberland and farmland around Georgia.
did_you_know_facts: Before founding Zaxby's, Townley was CEO and president of Southern Mortgage & Lending Corporation in Athens, Georgia.
Townley and his wife Elizabeth personally tend to their farmland and timberland.

name: Jet Jie Li
about: Jet Jie Li is the chairman and CEO of package delivery company J&T Global Express.
Li set up J&T in Jakarta in 2015 after leading Chinese smartphone maker OPPO's expansion in Indonesia and other Asian countries.
Today the company counts China as its largest market, followed by Southeast Asia where it is the market leader by parcel volume.
J&T went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2023.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Economics, University of Science and Technology Beijing

name: Simona Giorgetta
about: Simona Giorgetta is the largest shareholder and on the board of MAPEI, a manufacturer of chemical products used in construction based in Milan, Italy.
She is the niece of Giorgio Squinzi, who led MAPEI from 1984 until his death in October 2019; Giorgio's father Rodolfo founded the company in 1937.
The company's products have been used in projects ranging from the Panama City metro to the restoration of the Coliseum in Rome.
Giorgetta shares ownership of the company with her cousins Marco and Veronica, Giorgio's two children, who serve as co-CEOs of MAPEI.
Together, Giorgetta and her cousins also own Italian soccer team Sassuolo Calcio, which Giorgio acquired in 2003.

name: Pat Neal
about: Pat Neal founded Neal Communities, a private Florida homebuilder, in 1970.
Since then, the company has built over 25,000 homes and lots in Southwest Florida.
Neal is currently developing Skysail, a planned 640-acre community amid 240 acres of lakes in Naples that will have some 1,800 homes.
He served in the Florida state legislature from 1974 to 1986 and was also on Governor Rick Scott's transition team.
did_you_know_facts: Neal currently serves on the Board of Trustees of Florida Tax Watch, a non-partisan government watchdog.
Neal attended the University of Pennsylvania's business school at the same time as Donald Trump in the 1960s.

name: Oleg Misevra
about: Oleg Misevra controls East Mining Company, a Russian thermal coal enterprise.
Misevra, who served the Internal Troops of USSR and Russia, became a top manager and minority partner of the MDM Group, A WHATKT in the early 2000s.
MDM was founded by Andrey Melnichenko and Sergey Popov, who both became billionaires buying industrial plants across Russia.
In 2002, Misevra was elected as president of the Siberian Coal Energy Company (SUEK), the largest Russian thermal coal producer.
He resigned as president of SUEK in 2004 and purchased the company's assets on Sakhalin Island.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, Siberian State Industrial University  ; Master, Moscow State Pedagogical University; Graduate, Kharkiv Higher Military School of the Rear of the Ministry of Internal Affairs of the USSR

name: Gary Tharaldson
about: Gary Tharaldson purchased his first Super 8 motel in 1982 in Valley City, North Dakota.
He has since built, owned and operated over 480 hotels, opening one new hotel per month on average over 40 years.
In 2006, he sold 130 hotels to Goldman Sachs for about $1.2 billion, which he reinvested into land and commercial and residential developments.
In 2008, he launched an ethanol facility near Fargo, North Dakota, which produces over 175 million gallons per year.

forbes_list.list: The Richest Person In Every State (2025)

did_you_know_facts: Tharaldson once worked as a physical education teacher and insurance salesman.
Tharaldson is the richest person in North Dakota.
quote: From my youth I always wanted to create something on a big scale. I wasn't sure what that would be, but I knew whatever it was, it was going to be big.

name: J.K. Rowling
about: Author J.K. Rowling was a single mother living on welfare when the first Harry Potter novel debuted in 1997.
The series has sold more than 600 million copies worldwide to-date, the primary source of Rowling's billion-dollar fortune.
The eight Harry Potter film adaptations grossed almost $7.7 billion at the global box office, at the time the highest-grossing franchise in movie history.
She previously dropped off the billionaires list in 2012 due to her substantial philanthropy. She has donated more than $200 million to charity over the past 20 years.
In the years since, the Harry Potter brand has only expanded, into theme parks, video games, art exhibitions and a stage play, all of which have set sales records.
When the first Wizarding World attraction opened in 2010, Universal's Orlando theme park saw a 36% jump in attendance. Universal has since added it to five other parks around the world.

name: Michael Tojner
about: Michael Tojner bought German microbattery maker Varta in 2007 for $40 million and floated the business on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in 2017.
A serial entrepreneur, he has run an online gambling website, invested in real estate and hotels and has investments in other industrial companies.
He sold his entire majority stake in Aluflexpack, a flexible packaging and barrier solution company, in 2024.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of Vienna; Master of Laws, University of Vienna

name: Zhao Dongping
about: Zhao Dongping is general manager of Anker Innovations Technology, a China supplier of power charging products.
Half of Anker's revenue comes from the U.S. market.
Zhao worked for Dell China's and Google China's sales departments before joining Anker.
Anker is headquartered in Shenzhen, one of China's main electronics industry hubs.

name: John Lim
about: John Lim cofounded real estate fund manager ARA Asset Management in 2002, at age 45, with the backing of Hong Kong billionaire Li Ka-shing.
In 2016, Lim, along with U.S. private equity firm Warburg Pincus and China's AVIC Trust, took ARA private from the Singapore Stock Exchange in a $1.3 billion buyout.
In 2022, Hong Kong-based real asset manager ESR Group acquired ARA for $5.2 billion in stock and cash.
In July 2025, a consortium led by Starwood Capital Group and other investors took ESR private from the Hong Kong stock exchange in a deal that valued it at $7.1 billion.
Lim, who sold out his small stake in ESR Group and resigned from the board, now is the chairman of his JL Family Office.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Engineering, National University of Singapore

did_you_know_facts: He has been the chairman of the Asia Pacific Real Assets Association since 2017.
quote: After so many years I still love my business.

name: Neerja Sethi
about: Neerja Sethi cofounded IT consulting and outsourcing firm Syntel with her husband Bharat Desai in 1980 and took it public in 1997.
French IT firm Atos SE bought Syntel for $3.4 billion in 2018. Sethi got an estimated $510 million for her stake.
Sethi served as an executive at Syntel from its founding until its sale in 2018.
Her husband Bharat Desai is also a billionaire; they met in the U.S. while working for IT firm Tata Consultancy Services.
The couple started Syntel in their apartment in Troy, Michigan with an initial investment of just $2,000.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, Oakland University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Delhi University; Master of Business Administration, Delhi University

did_you_know_facts: Sethi holds an undergraduate degree in mathematics and a masters degree in computer science.
She and her husband joined the Giving Pledge, a commitment to give at least half their fortune to charitable causes, in May 2025.

name: Huang Min
about: Huang Min is the founder and chairman of Jiangsu Goodwe Power Supply, a supplier of inverters for the solar power industry.
Goodwe went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2020.
Goodwe is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Suzhou.

name: Alexander Mamut & family
about: Alexander Mamut was trained as a lawyer but made his fortune as an investor.
Over the years he's had stakes in a few banks, an insurance company, fertilzer producer and mobile phone chain.
He was an owner of Rambler&Co, which unites several internet media projects including news site lenta.ru and politics and society site gazeta.ru.
Mamut bought two of Russia's biggest movie chains, Cinema Park and Formula Kino, in 2017.
He eventually sold off his stakes in Russian companies and bought shares in such American companies as Google and Apple.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Laws, Moscow State University

did_you_know_facts: In the 1990s, Mamut was close to Russian president Boris Yeltsin and was known as "the Yeltsin family banker."
Mamut owns the British bookstore chain Waterstones, founded by his friend Tim Waterstone, which merged with Barnes & Noble In 2019.
He got Israeli citizenship in 2022.
quote: I did not learn anything from other people's mistakes. I was able to learn from someone else's success.

name: Marina Caprotti
about: Marina Caprotti inherited most of her wealth from her late father, Bernardo Caprotti, who was the founder of Italian supermarket chain Esselunga.
Bernardo left his second wife Giuliana and daughter Marina a 67% stake in the company, and gave the remaining third to his other two children.
In 2020, Giuliana and Marina bought out the remaining stake for nearly 2 billion Euros.
Marina was named executive chair of Esselunga in 2020.

name: Giuliana Caprotti
about: Giuliana Caprotti inherited her fortune from her late husband Bernardo Caprotti, who was the founder of Italian supermarket chain Esselunga.
Bernardo left his second wife Giualiana and their daughter Marina a 67% stake in the company, and gave the remaining third to his other two children.
In 2020, Giuliana and Marina bought out the remaining stake of Esselunga for nearly 2 billion Euros.
Giuliana was named honorary chair of Esselunga in 2020.

name: Ahmed Afif Topbas
about: Ahmet Afif Topbaş derives his fortune from BİM Birleşik Mağazalar, Turkey's largest discount supermarket chain.
Founded in 1995, BIM has more than 12,000 locations across Turkey, Morocco and Egypt.
His brother Mustafa Latif Topbaş, also a billionaire, is CEO and cofounder of the company.
Ahmet owns about 12% of BİM, which also has locations in Morocco with 687 stores there and in Egypt with 356 stores.
He owns about 12% of the company which has annual revenues exceeding $5 billion and offers a popular mobile telecom service under the brand name Bimcell.

name: Peter Kamprad
about: Ingvar Kamprad, who died in 2018, transferred the bulk of his Ikea empire to foundations in the 80's, but kept enough to make his sons billionaires.
Peter and his brothers own Ikano Group, which was created to manage Ikea's real estate and financial service businesses, but was spun out in 1988.
Today Ikano Group is a $2.1 billion (sales) company with interests in banking, real estate and Asian shopping centers.
Peter, the eldest brother, ran Ikea's Belgian operations for 12 years; he now chairs the Ikano Group.
Early in his career, Peter worked three years at a different Swedish retail giant, fast-fashion company H&M.
did_you_know_facts: Ingvar Kamprad ranked among the top 10 richest people for years before lawyers produced documents proving that he had irrevocably transferred economic control.

name: Mathias Kamprad
about: Ingvar Kamprad, who died in 2018, transferred the bulk of his Ikea empire to foundations in the 80's, but kept enough to make his sons billionaires.
Mathias and his brothers own Ikano Group, which was created to manage Ikea's real estate and financial service businesses, but was spun out in 1988.
Today Ikano Group is a $2.1 billion (sales) company with interests in banking, real estate and Asian shopping centers.
Mathias, the youngest brother, is a board member of Inter Ikea Holding, the owner of the intellectual property assets.
He sits on the board of Ikano Group, and on the supervisory board of Interogo, a Liechtenstein-based foundation that is the ultimate owner of Ikea.
did_you_know_facts: Mathias put in two years as assistant to Ikea's founder, Ingvar Kamprad, ranked among the top 10 richest people in the world for five years.
Ingvar Kamprad's net worth took a slide in 2011 after his lawyers produced documents proving that he had irrevocably transferred economic control decades earlier.

name: Jonas Kamprad

Jonas, the middle child, studied industrial and furniture design in Switzerland and applied his skills in Ikea-run subsidiary Habitat.

did_you_know_facts: Ingvar Kamprad ranked among the top 10 richest people for years before lawyers produced documents proving that he had irrevocably transferred economic control.

name: Sheila Johnson
about: Sheila Johnson cofounded cable TV channel Black Entertainment Television in 1979 with her then-husband Robert Johnson. Viacom bought it for $3 billion in 2001.
After her divorce in 2002, she sold her BET shares and has since invested in a portfolio of hotels known as the Salamander Collection, as well as other real estate and horses.
Her Innisbrook resort in Palm Harbor, Florida, hosts an annual PGA Tour championship.
She was an executive producer of the critically-acclaimed 2013 film The Butler, which tells the story of a former slave turned White House employee.
Through her investment in Monumental Sports & Entertainment, she owns stakes in three Washington sports teams: the WNBA's Mystics, NBA's Wizards and NHL's Capitals.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign

did_you_know_facts: Johnson is the only black woman to own stakes in three professional sports teams.
Johnson's parents enrolled her in an all-white school in early 1950s Kentucky before desegregation was federally mandated.

name: Lin Zhijun
about: Lin Zhijun is the vice chairman of Double Medical Technology.
Double Medical Technology supplies trauma implant consumables and spinal implant consumables.
Lin's elder brother Lin Zhixiong is a member of the 2017 Forbes China Rich List.

name: Sarah Humphreys Atkins & family
about: Sarah Humphreys Atkins is an heiress to the Galena, Kansas-based Tamko roofing fortune.
Her grandfather E. L. Craig started the company in 1944 at the age of 69 in an old streetcar barn in Joplin, Missouri.
Today, Tamko is the fourth-largest manufacturer of roofing shingles in the United States. The company recorded $1.2 billion in 2023 revenue.
The Humphreys family sold a 25% stake in the business to the Carlyle Group, a $447 billion (assets under management) private equity firm, for an undisclosed sum in 2019.
Sarah and her brother David, and their respective families, split the remaining 75%.
Atkins is married to SEC commissioner Paul Atkins. Both she and Atkins are on Tamko's board of directors.
did_you_know_facts: Paul Atkins, who was nominated by Donald Trump, is serving his second stint as SEC commissioner; he previously served for six years under George W. Bush.

name: David Humphreys & family

David took over as president and CEO of Tamko in 1994 after his father's death; he and his wife Debra both serve on Tamko's board of directors.
The Humphreys family sold a 25% stake in the business to the Carlyle Group, a $447 billion (assets under management) private equity firm, for an undisclosed sum in 2019.

Humphreys' passions include tennis, rare books and history.

name: Donald Mackenzie
about: Donald Mackenzie is a cofounder and honorary co-chair of Luxembourg-based private equity firm CVC Capital Partners.
The firm went public on the Amsterdam stock exchange in 2024 and Mackenzie owns a nearly 6% stake.
CVC was established in 1981 as the European operations of Citicorp Venture Capital, the VC arm of Citigroup.
In 1993, Mackenzie and seven cofounders acquired the business and spun it out as CVC. They raised their first fund in 1996 and shifted their focus to private equity.
CVC's investments include Petco, Swiss watchmaker Breitling and Spanish soccer league La Liga.
did_you_know_facts: Mackenzie led CVC's buyout of racing series Formula One in 2006 and served as Formula One's chairman. CVC later sold Formula One to Liberty Media in 2016.

about: Maxim Tebar is a fourth-generation heir to the Stihl family fortune, founded by his great-grandfather Andreas Stihl in 1926.
A German maker of chainsaws, the company saw $5.8 billion in sales in 2023.
His mother Karen Tebar sits on Stihl's advisory board as vice chair.

name: Per Franzén
about: Per Franzén joined publicly traded Swedish investment company EQT AB in 2007.
Franzen owns about 3% of EQT, which has roughly $83 billion (73,4 billion Euro) in assets under management.
EQT primarily invests in private equity, but has also put funds into venture capital, real estate and infrastructure.
Franzen's partners at EQT include billionaires Conni Johnson, Harry Klagsburn and Lennart Blecher, and Christian SInding.

name: Fredrik Österberg
about: Fredrik 'sterberg cofounded Evolution AB with Jens von Bahr in 2006.
Evolution sells casino solutions to online gambling operators, primarily live-streamed tables of blackjack, poker, craps and roulette.
Evolution's first casino studio was set up in Riga, Lithuania in 2006. Today the company has live-casino studios in nine countries, including the U.S.
The company went public in Stockholm in 2015 and today provides its services to over 700 customers in 21 countries. Evolution's products are available globally for end users.
Prior to Evolution, he was CEO of Sportal Nordic.

name: David Feffer
about: David Feffer is the eldest son of Max Feffer, whose immigrant father Leon Feffer launched the family business.
His grandfather Leon Feffer founded Brazilian pulp and paper firm Suzano in 1924.
David and his three brothers - Daniel, Jorge and Ruben - each inherited shares in Suzano; David and Daniel are also board members of the company.
Suzano acquired Fibria in January 2019 for about $7.5 billion, creating Brazil's largest paper producer.
David is president of Suzano's board of directors and has headed the family's investment arm since 2003.

He became the chief executive of Suzano in 2001, but later decided to step down and give the position to a non-family member.

name: Lee Ho-jin
about: Lee Ho-jin is a former chairman of Taekwang Industrial, a manufacturer that became synonymous with Korea's textile and petrochemical prowess.
He rose to chairman after his oldest brother, Lee Sik-jin, died. He has now stepped down and is reportedly struggling against liver cancer.
In 2011, he was sentenced to 54 months in prison for embezzling $128 million from the company but has been out on bail due to his illness.
In 2019, Lee was sentenced to three years in prison on charges of embezzlement and breach of trust. He was pardoned in 2023.

personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Seoul National University; Master of Business Administration, Samuel Curtis Johnson Graduate School of Management
