His mother sold clothes in a Busan market and provided the seed money to start Taekwang, which began as a textile company.

name: Jean-Marc Chapus
about: Jean-Marc Chapus is a managing partner and cofounder of Crescent Capital Group, a Los Angeles-based debt-focused investment firm with $43 billion in assets under management.
He serves on the advisory board of the Milwaukee Brewers, where his Crescent cofounder Mark Attanasio is chairman and principal owner.
Chapus is reported to be a part of the ownership group of the Brewers.
Prior to cofounding Crescent Capital in 1991, Chapus worked at Drexel Burnham Lambert, a pioneer of junk-bond trading.
Chapus also worked as an investment banker at Lehman Brothers in the early 1980s.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Harvard University

did_you_know_facts: Chapus was a track star while he was a student at Harvard University and captain of the team his senior year.
Chapus has seven children, one of whom ran track at Stanford.

name: Sung Kyu-dong
about: Sung Kyu-dong is the founder and CEO of EO Technics, a manufacturer of laser-based equipment used in the production of memory chips in South Korea.
Its flagship product is the CSM, equipment that etches identification codes onto chips to provide traceability, allowing manufacturers to quickly isolate the source of any defects.
The company's other major product is LA, which uses a laser to finish the electrical pathways inside the chip, providing the targeted heat needed to make them functional.
Sung founded EO Technics in 1989 and listed it on the South Korea stock exchange in 2000.
Before starting EO Technics, Sung worked at Goldstar Central Research Center, Daewoo Heavy Industries and Korea Laser, which pioneered industrial laser technology in South Korea.

name: Gao Yi & family
about: Gao Yi is the chairman of Yifeng Pharmacy Chain, which has more than 4,000 stores across China.
Yifeng employs more than 40,000.
Yifeng, headquartered in the central China city of Changsha, was founded by Gao in 2001.

name: Bastian Nominacher
about: Bastian Nominacher is cofounder and co-CEO of enterprise software startup Celonis.
The Munich-based company was valued by private investors at $13 billion in 2022. Nominacher owns a 16% stake.
The company disputes Forbes' valuation, which accounts for the downturn in private markets since the company's last funding round.
Nominacher's cofounders Alexander Rinke and Martin Klenk are also billionaires. Rinke is co-CEO and Klenk is CTO.
Celonis' cofounders launched the company in 2011 after graduating from Technical University of Munich.

name: Axel Oberwelland & family
about: Axel Oberwelland is proprietor of the German candy company August Storck KG, whose brands include Werther's Original, Riesen and Toffifee.
Oberwelland's great-grandfather August Storck founded the business in the Westphalia town of Werther in 1903.
At the time, sweets typically were sold unpackaged and without branding. He packaged his individually and gave them snappy names.
Today, Storck employs over 5,000 people, sells products in more than 100 countries and generates around $2 billion in estimated annual revenue.
Axel became the fourth generation of his family to lead the company after his father, Klaus, retired on Storck's 100th anniversary in 2003.
did_you_know_facts: In 1992, Klaus Oberwelland established the Stork Foundation to preserve endangered stork populations.
The most successful new launch in 2017 for sweets was Storck's Knoppers nut bar.

name: James Truchard
about: James Truchard cofounded National Instruments, a supplier of testing and measurement equipment and software for scientists and engineers, in 1976.
A Texas native, he got a PhD in electrical engineering from the University of Texas, Austin in 1974.
He launched National Instruments while working as managing director of the acoustical measurements division at the university's applied research lab.
He retired as chairman in 2019. National Instruments was acquired by manufacturing giant Emerson Electric in 2023.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctorate, The University of Texas at Austin

did_you_know_facts: A gardening and photography enthusiast, Truchard published "Memories from a Hill Country Garden: Flowers, Stones, and Critters" in 2013.

name: Kochouseph Chittilappilly
about: In 1977, Kochouseph Chittilappilly borrowed $1,500 from his father to set up a small unit to make voltage stabilizers.
Over four decades he built it into Kochi-based V-Guard Industries. The company's portfolio now includes kitchen appliances, air coolers and solar water heaters.
Chittilappily expanded into amusement parks in 2000 with Wonderla Holidays.
These days, Chittilappily is busy with his property venture, Veegaland Developers and his charitable foundation.
did_you_know_facts: His two sons run V-Guard and Wonderla.
He donated one of his kidneys to a poor truck driver.

name: Richard Teets Jr
about: Richard Teets is a cofounder of Steel Dynamics, one of the largest steel producers and metals recyclers in the United States.
He cofounded the Fort Wayne, Indiana-based company in 1993 and helped take it public on the Nasdaq in 1996.
He retired as the company's executive vice president for steelmaking and president and chief operating officer of steel operations in 2016.
He owns 3% of the company.

name: Ken Kendrick
about: Ken Kendrick is the managing general partner and largest shareholder of the Arizona Diamondbacks baseball team.
Kendrick was a member of the group that brought the MLB expansion team to Arizona in 1995.
He built a fortune in software and banking, founding Datatel (later renamed Ellucian) and investing in Woodforest National Bank.
In 2021, Kendrick joined a group of investors, including Larry Fitzgerald, Kevin Durant and Andy Roddick, that purchased memorabilia authenticator Collectors for $850 million.
did_you_know_facts: Kendrick owns one of the world's most valuable baseball card collections, estimated to be worth nine figures; it includes a 1952 Topps Mickey Mantle card.
Kendrick is a prostate cancer survivor and endowed a research position in the space at the Cleveland Clinic.
quote: If you've been an entrepreneur, you have to have had failure or you haven't really done very much. And you don't spend a lot of time talking about your failures, but you spend a lot of time thinking about them.

name: Danilo Iervolino
about: Danilo Iervolino is an Italian entrepreneur who founded online university UniPegaso in 2006, one of the first to be established in Italy.
Iervolino started UniPegaso at age 28 and grew it to become the largest in Italy, serving more than 120,000 students.
He sold his company Multiversity, which includes UniPegaso, to private equity firm CVC Capital Partners for $1.3 billion in October 2021.
Since selling UniPegaso, Iervolino has purchased Italian soccer team Salernitana.
He also invests in Italian tech startups, both independently and through a startup accelerator and venture capital funds.
did_you_know_facts: Iervolino was inspired to launch an online university in Italy when he traveled to the U.S. after developing online master's programs at the University of Salerno.

name: Yu Jinkun & family
about: Yu is chairman of KTK Group, which provides electrical control systems for railroads.
KTK Group is headquartered in Changzhou, Jiangsu Province.
Yu's son, Ge Jianming, sits on the board of the company.

name: Christian Angermayer
about: Christian Angermayer invests in life sciences, fintech, AI, psychedelics and cryptocurrencies through his family office Apeiron Investment Group.
He made his first millions cofounding biotech firm Ribopharma with his college professors; he sold his stake when it merged with Alnylam in 2003.
His Malta-based Apeiron owns shares in several publicly traded firms and private companies in the U.S., Germany, Canada and Australia.
His holdings include psychedelics biopharma firm Atai Life Sciences and blockchain holding company Samara, alongside co-investor Mike Novogratz.
He owns an extensive art collection that includes ancient artifacts highlighting the role that psychedelics have played in human history.

name: Manny Stul
about: Manny Stul took over a struggling company named Moose Toys in 2000. Sales have soared since.
Its Shopkins collectibles, inspired by grocery and department store items, with names like Milk Bud and Kris P. Lettuce, are some of their best-known.
He made a fortune building and selling a giftwares company. He then dabbled in various ventures like organic farming before investing in Moose Toys.
Stul tackled a logistics crisis triggered by the pandemic by chartering an entire ship to transport products from China.
did_you_know_facts: Stul's parents were Polish Holocaust survivors. He was born in a German refugee camp before the family traveled to Australia after World War II.
Stul was named EY World Entrepreneur of the Year in 2016, Australia's first global winner.
quote: Everyone thinks we are a toy company. I keep telling our team we are not a toy company, we are a creative house, a creative hub. Innovation is in our DNA.

name: Liu Jianjun
about: Liu Jianjun is the founder of Tibet Huayu Mining, which engages in the exploration, mining, processing and selling of non-ferrous metals.
He got his start by working at a mining bureau in China's Hebei Province after finishing high school in 1977.
Liu took the company public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2016.
His son Liu Liangkun has been the chairing the company since 2021.

name: Michael Gans & family
about: Michael Jacques Gans is a Luxembourgish-American businessman who owns commercial real estate in Dublin, London, Luxembourg and Manchester.

He used to own 25% of logistics firm Supreme Group, with the rest held by his business partner Stephen Orenstein. Supreme Group was the primary supplier of food and water to the U.S. army in Afghanistan.
The firm was founded in 1957 to supply food to U.S. military bases in Germany by Orenstein's father Alfred, a former U.S. army soldier. Gans joined the company after Orenstein took over in 1985.

name: Edouard Carmignac
about: Edouard Carmignac founded Carmignac Gestion, one of Europe's largest asset managers, in 1989.
Carmignac owns 79% of the company, which now has about $40 billion in assets under management; employees and executives own the rest.
His daughter Maxime works at the company and is the heir apparent. His son directs Foundation Carmignac and another daughter, Lucrece, is an actress.
In 2019, Carmignac stepped back from managing Carmignac Patrimoine, which he had run since 1989. He is chairman and chief investment officer.
The Foundation Carmignac opened an exhibition space in 2018 to show nearly 300 art works on Porquerolles, an island off the South of France.
did_you_know_facts: Edouard Carmignac wanted to be a rock star but settled for finance after receiving a BA in economics from the University of Paris and an MBA from Columbia.
Carmignac is a keen polo player. His team reached the semi final of the prestigious Deauville Gold Cup in 2017.

name: Ceyda Lale Tara
about: Ceyda Lale Tara is one of more than a dozen family members who hold shares in ENKA, one of Turkey's largest construction and energy companies.

ENKA, which was cofounded in 1957 by Sarik Tara and his brother-in-law, Sadi Gulcelik, is Turkey's leading private electricity producer and also operates in real estate, tourism, transport and trade (construction equipment and machinery).
In Moscow, ENKA owns a hotel, shopping malls and approximately 370,000 square meters of net rentable Class A office space.
Sadi Gulcelik died in a plane accident in Saudi Arabia in 1980, and Mehmet Sinan Tara took over in 1984 at age 26. His son Agah Mehmet Tara became CEO in 2012, at age 29.
did_you_know_facts: Over the last 20 years or so, ENKA has been the biggest builder of U.S. consular and embassy buildings.
The Lale Tara Arts Scholarship, run by ENKA Sanat, helps young artists?especially in classical music?pursue undergraduate and graduate studies outside of Turkey.

name: Wen Pengcheng & family
about: Wen Pengcheng chairs Guangdong Wens Foodstuffs Group of China, which sells and breeds chicken.
More than 50,000 family farms work with Wen.
Wens went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2015.

name: Zhang Xin
about: Zhang Xin and her husband Pan Shiyi co-founded real estate developer Soho China.
Soho China is listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange and develops office towers in Shanghai and Beijing.
Prior to founding Soho China, Zhang worked on Wall Street for Goldman Sachs and Travelers Group.
In June 2021, U.S. private equity giant Blackstone said it would buy the majority of Soho China for as much as $3.05 billion; the purchase wasn't completed.
In 2022, Pan and Zhang stepped down from their leadership roles as chairman and CEO "in order to focus on supporting the arts and philanthropic pursuits" but remain on the board.

name: Emre Tezmen
about: Emre Tezmen is the founder and largest shareholder of Tera Yatırım Bankası, a Turkish investment company.

After earning an economic degree from Université Libre de Bruxelles and an MBA at Vrije Universiteit Brussel, Tezmen began a career in finance sector, working in research, institutional sales, and management.
He founded Tera in 2005, selling his house and car to finance it, later using all of his savings for the acquisition of brokerage firm Stok Menkul.
He added to his portfolio of finance assets with businesses focused on factoring (2015), and portfolio management and information technologies (2020).
did_you_know_facts: The name "Tera" originates from Terra, the earth goddess in Roman mythology who symbolizes fertility and prosperity.
His office features objects from ancient cultures collected from various parts of the world, notably ancient Egypt.

name: Caryn Seidman-Becker
about: Caryn Seidman-Becker is cofounder and CEO of Clear Secure, which uses identification technology for security checkpoints at airports and stadiums.
A former hedge fund manager, she and a colleague bought Clear's predecessor out of bankruptcy in 2010.
In 2023 she expanded the company's identity-confirming services into digital healthcare records. This plus strong travel demand helped revenue grow to $990 million in 2025.
After raising capital from investors including airlines Delta and United, she took the company public in June 2021 at a $4 billion valuation.
She joined Home Depot's board of directors in 2022 and, previously, sat on the board of fintech Lemonade.

name: Xiong Xiaochuan
about: Xiong Xiaochuan chairs Chinese medical device and personal protective equipment supplier MeHow Innovative.
MeHow went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in October 2022.
Xiong worked for Sichuan Changhong Electric early in his career, before earning an MBA from the University of Warwick.

name: Lia Maria Aguiar
about: Lia Maria Aguiar inherited a banking fortune from her late father, Amador Aguiar, the founder of Bradesco, one of Brazil's largest banks.
Lia Aguiar and her twin sister Lina were adopted by Bradesco founder Amador Aguiar after being abandoned in front of a Bradesco branch in Sao Paulo.
Aguiar fought a long court battle over her father's will with his second wife, whom he married less than five months before his death.
Aguiar also owns shares of Bradespar, the bank's non-financial arm, which is publicly traded and specializes in industrial investments.
did_you_know_facts: In 2008, Aguiar started her own foundation, Lia Maria Aguiar Foundation, to support the city of Campos do Jordao, where she has been living since the early 1990s.

name: Thomas Sandell
about: Former hedge fund manager and activist investor Thomas Sandell closed up shop in 2019, transforming his Sandell Asset Management into a family office.
Hit hard by the great recession, the Swedish credit market specialist has built up his fortune twice.
Sandell earned an MBA from Columbia University and landed a spot at Bear Stearns in 1988 before founding Sandell Asset Management a decade later.
Initially a risk arbitrage specialist, Sandell later shifted tactics and engaged in loud proxy battles with firms like Bob Evans Farms in 2013.
At Bear Stearns he worked with famed investment banker Ace Greenberg on such deals as Kirk Kerkorian's attempted buyout of Chrysler.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Columbia Business School; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Uppsala University

did_you_know_facts: Sandell is a former badminton champion in his native Sweden.
Sandell privately invests in modern art, and owns pieces by Lichtenstein and Basquiat.

name: Tang Ye
about: Tang Ye chairs Shanghai Friendess Electronic Technology, a supplier of laser-related software and hardware.
Friendess went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2019.
Tang holds a master's degree in engineering management from China's prestigious Shanghai Jiaotong University.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Engineering Management, Shanghai Jiao Tong University

name: Subbamma Jasti
about: Subbamma Jasti inherited the assets of her husband Subba Rao Jasti, who died in 2023.
The biggest chunk of her inheritance is derived from the sale of a substantial stake in listed Suven Pharmaceuticals in 2022 to global private equity firm Advent International.
Jasti's son Venkateswarlu Jasti cofounded Suven Pharmaceuticals in 1989.
The Hyderabad company was demerged in 2020 when Suven Life Sciences, which focuses on neuroscience therapies, was spun off and listed separately.
did_you_know_facts: Her son Venkateswarlu Jasti ran a chain six of community pharmacies in the states of New York and New Jersey in the U.S. in the 1970s and 1980s.

name: Liu Xiucai & family
about: Liu Xiucai chairs Cathay Biotech, a Shanghai-headquartered supplier of industrial chemicals.
Cathay went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2020.

name: Zhou Wen & family
about: Zhou Wen chairs Shanghai Pret Composites, a supplier of plastics and composites.
He worked as an engineer at SAIC Volkswagen Automotive, a Volkswagen joint venture, in China early in his career.
Shanghai Pret Composites listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2009.
Zhou holds an executive MBA degree from Fudan University.
In 2025 his son Zhenlun Zhou was appointed to vice chairman and vice general manager of the company.

name: Jeff Sprecher
about: Jeff Sprecher is the founder and CEO of global stock exchange operator Intercontinental Exchange, also known as ICE.
In 1997, Sprecher was working at a California power plant developer when he negotiated to buy a struggling Georgia company called Continental Power Exchange.
He had an idea to create a platform that would allow traders to buy and sell commodities online.
In 2000, Sprecher folded Continental into new firm ICE; he took that company public in 2005.
In 2013, ICE acquired the New York Stock Exchange for $10.9 billion; it owns 12 stock exchanges and 6 clearing houses globally.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Pepperdine University; Bachelor of Science, University of Wisconsin

did_you_know_facts: Sprecher is married to Kelly Loeffler, who was appointed U.S. Senator from Georgia in 2019 to fill an empty seat; she lost the special election in January 2021.
Sprecher reportedly collects vintage Porsches.

name: Alakh Pandey
about: College dropout Alakh Pandey cofounded edtech company Physicswallah in 2020 with his business partner Prateek Boob.
Physicswallah offers test prep courses to help students crack entrance exams for engineering and medical colleges.
The Noida-based edtech firm went public in November 2025 and got listed at a 33% premium to its IPO price.
Physicswallah also offers courses in subjects such as artificial intelligence, data analytics, software development and banking.
His "Physics Wallah-Alakh Pandey" YouTube channel has nearly 14 million subscribers.
did_you_know_facts: He dropped out of engineering college in the third year.
He started a Youtube channel called Physics Wallah in 2014 where he taught physics for free.

name: Prateek Boob
about: Prateek Boob cofounded edtech company Physicswallah as an e-learning app in 2020, together with Alakh Pandey.
Physicswallah started with prep courses for the entrance test to the Indian Institute of Technology as well as for medical college entrance exams.
It now provides learning modules for students from grades one to 12.
The cofounders became billionaires after taking the company public in November 2025.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Technology, Indian Institute of Technology, BHU

did_you_know_facts: Physicswallah also offers offline coaching through its network of Vidyapeeth centers.
Boob has a B.Tech degree in mechanical engineering from IIT (Benaras Hindu University).

name: Hajime Satomi
about: Hajime Satomi is the chairman of Sega Sammy, a Japanese pachinko machine and gaming software firm.
He founded pachinko machine maker Sammy, which got into the videogame business when it acquired Sega in 2004.
His son, Haruki, is CEO and chairman.
Sega Sammy has a 45% stake in South Korean gambling-and-entertainment resort Paradise City.
Satomi is also a top-ranked owner of thoroughbred horses.

name: Shen Jinhua
about: Shen Jinhua chairs Focus Technology, the parent company of InQbrands, which operates two of China's popular business-to-business e-commerce sites: Made-in-China.com, Abiz.com, xyz.cn and InQbrands.

Launched in 1998, Made-in-China.com connects 12 million buyers to suppliers who hail from 220 countries and regions and cover a slew of categories ranging from food and chemicals to medicine and transportation.
In 2015 Focus Technology acquired U.S.-based Doba Inc., a similar platform that connects buyers and suppliers.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Shanghai Jiaotong University; Master of Science, Southeast University

name: Martin Klenk
about: Martin Klenk is cofounder and CTO of enterprise software startup Celonis.
The Munich-based company was valued by private investors at $13 billion in 2022. Klenk owns a 16% stake.
The company disputes Forbes' valuation, which accounts for the downturn in private markets since the company's last funding round.
Klenk's cofounders Bastian Nominacher and Alexander Rinke are also billionaires. Nominacher and Rinke serve as co-CEOs.
Celonis' cofounders launched the company in 2011 after graduating from Technical University of Munich.

name: Elizabeth Sy
about: Elizabeth Sy is an advisor of SM Investments, a post she's held since 2012.
She is the second child of the late SM founder, Henry Sy.
She is president and chairman of SM Hotels and Conventions Corp., which oversees nine hotels including a slew of Radisson properties.
She started out as an assistant at her father's first hotel business, the Manila Royal Hotel.
She has a degree in business administration from Maryknoll College, now known as Miriam College.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Business Administration, Maryknoll College

name: Hartati Murdaya
about: Hartati Murdaya is the president director of Central Cipta Murdaya, which she cofounded with her late husband Murdaya Poo, who died in April 2025 at age 84.
Central Cipta Murdaya has investments in engineering, IT, palm oil and plywood.
Her Jakarta International Expo is one of the city's biggest convention centers.
She owns a substantial stake in listed property developer Metropolitan Kentjana where she and her four children have board seats.

name: Madeleine Olsson Eriksson
about: Madeleine Olsson-Eriksson is a part owner of Stena Sphere, a privately held Swedish conglomerate.
Interests include cruising, shipping, offshore drilling, property and metal recycling.
Madeleine's father, Sten, founded Stena in 1939 as a trading company.
Her brother Dan took over in 1983 and now owns 51% of the company. Madeleine and her brother Stefan Olsson own 12.5% and 24.5%, respectively.
Madeleine's children, Gustav and Marie, each own 6% and have seats on different boards in the company.
did_you_know_facts: She became the first of her family to go to college, earning a degree in medicine and pursuing a career as a gynecologist.
Aside from an 12.5% stake in Stena, she is also part owner of a clinic in Gothenburg.

name: Rodney Lewis
about: Rodney Lewis grew up on the border in Laredo, Texas. Started Lewis Petro Properties in 1983 with one natural gas well.
He eventually acquired 500,000 acres in the Eagle Ford shale and became the fourth-biggest gas producer in Texas.
He owns America's biggest fleet of air-worthy World War II fighter planes, including a P-38 dug out of a Greenland glacier and restored.
In 2004 Lewis was the first U.S. oilman to sign a contract to drill for Pemex in Mexico.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Texas A&M University

did_you_know_facts: Lewis beat esophageal cancer a decade ago, but lost his salivary glands.
quote: "I fly helicopters pretty routinely, like a pickup truck. I drive very little."

name: Pedro Grendene Bartelle
about: Pedro Grendene Bartelle cofounded Grendene, one of the world's largest sandal manufacturers, with his twin brother Alexandre Grendene Bartelle.
Pedro is vice chairman of the board of directors of Grendene and owns just under 14% of the Sao Paulo-listed company.
He invests in other businesses, including footwear company Vulcabras, a direct competitor to Grendene in which he holds a nearly 50% stake.
did_you_know_facts: Pedro is married to Tania Bulhoes, a Brazilian entrepreneur who owns Tania Bulhoes Perfumes Ltda., a well known retailer of perfumes, creams and soaps.

name: Yu De-Chao
about: Yu De-Chao, also known as Michael Yu, is the chairman and CEO of Innovent Biologics, a China-headquartered biotech company.
Innovent went public at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2018.
Yu holds a PhD in molecular genetics from the Chinese Academy of Sciences.
Yu had a postdoc position in pharmaceutical chemistry at the University of California San Francisco from 1993 to 1996.

name: Saket Burman
about: Saket Burman is the fifth-generation member of the storied Burman clan that founded Dabur, India's fourth-largest consumer goods company.
He inherited a minority stake and a board seat in Dabur from his father Siddharth Burman, who died in 2015.
Other assets he owns include property and financial investments.
Saket founded and sold several companies. He is currently focused on building his family office.
He was appointed vice chairman of Dabur in 2022.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Business Administration, University of Wisconsin, Madison

did_you_know_facts: He is a member of Mumbai Angels, a group that backs startups.
He shuttles between homes in Dubai, London and Delhi.

name: Yang Ying & family
about: Yang Ying is a director of Chinese drugmaker Xiamen Amoytop Biotech.
Founded in 1996, Amoytop supplies recombinant protein drugs.
Yang's husband Lan Chun is the company's chairman; the two are investors.

name: Ali Erdemoglu
about: Ali Erdemoglu and his brother, Ibrahim, together own over 75% of a top producer of materials used in carpet, SASA Polyester.
They initially acquired 51% of SASA in 2015 for $102 million, then added to their stake in the publicly traded company and watched it soar in value.
The brothers' Erdemoglu Holding also includes the two privately held companies, Merinos Carpet and Dinarsu Carpet.
In 1970, their father, Mehmet Erdemoglu, along with family members, started Merinos with two rug-weaving looms.
Today, Erdemoglu Holding is one of the world's largest carpet manufacturers, with production facilities in eight locations in Turkey and Russia.
did_you_know_facts: SASA has a $935 million licensing and technical service agreement with Invista, a subsidiary of Koch Industries that makes chemicals, polymers, fabrics and fibers.
Ali Erdemoglu started in the carpet trade with his father after graduating from primary school.

name: Sam Tarascio
about: Sam Tarascio owns a portfolio of real estate across Melbourne, including a business park, two distribution sites, a large shopping mall and a market.
Tarascio, who emigrated from Italy in the 1950s, also owns several inner-city apartment developments.
He started out in property development in the 1960s by building a warehouse for German pharmaceutical company Hoechst, where he had worked in sales.
That led him to establish logistics and industrial-development business Salta Properties, now run by his son Sam.
Sam Tarascio, founder of Salta Properties, will transition from his role as founding director to non-executive founding director, effective 1 January 2026.
did_you_know_facts: Tarascio imported an olive press in 2014 for his Taralinga Estate on the Mornington Peninsula, near Melbourne.
His Taralinga Estate olive oil has won two gold medals at the New York International World Olive Oil Competition.

name: Michaela Herz
about: Michaela Herz owns 45% of the private equity firm Mayfair SE, whose investments have included the sports apparel company Puma.
She is a granddaughter of Tchibo cofounder Max Herz, who built a fortune based on the import and sale of coffee.
Her father, Guenter, ran Tchibo for almost 35 years. The family also built a stake in skin-care company Beiersdorf, whose brands include Nivea.
Guenter and his sister, Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel, founded Mayfair after they sold their stake in the family business in 2003.
As one of Mayfair's managing directors, Michaela Herz is active in shaping investment decisions.
did_you_know_facts: Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel and her children have exited Mayfair, reportedly founding Bilton Holding AG to invest primarily in real estate.

name: Christian Herz
about: Christian Herz owns 45% of the private equity firm Mayfair SE, whose investments have included the sports apparel company Puma.
He is the grandson of Tchibo co-founder Max Herz, who built a fortune based on the importation and sale of coffee.
His father, Guenter, ran Tchibo for almost 35 years. The family also built a stake in skin-care company Beiersdorf, whose brands include Nivea.
Guenter and his sister, Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel, founded Mayfair after they were bought out of the family business in 2003.
As one of Mayfair's managing directors, Christian Herz is active in the shaping investment decisions.
did_you_know_facts: Italian restaurant operator Vapiano, in which Mayfair had a stake, filed for bankruptcy after all locations in several countries closed in response to the pandemic.
Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel and her children have exited Mayfair, reportedly founding Bilton Holding AG to invest primarily in real estate.

name: Bruce Springsteen
about: Bruce Springsteen, a.k.a. The Boss, spun his New Jersey, blue-collar upbringing into a substantial fortune from five decades of touring and recording.
Springsteen and his E Street Band met playing clubs along the Jersey Shore, most famously at Asbury Park's The Stone Pony.
He's sold over 140 million albums globally, with 21 studio albums, 10 live albums and seven EPs.
Accolades include 20 Grammys, an Oscar, two Golden Globes, a special Tony award and inductions in both the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame and the Songwriters Hall of Fame.
In 2021, Springsteen sold his music catalog--his life's work--to longtime label home Sony for a $500 million lump sum.

name: John Christodoulou
about: John Christodoulou is the founder and owner of the Yianis Group, a London-based real estate firm with properties in the U.K. and Europe.
Born in Cyprus, he fled the country with his family after the Turkish invasion of the island in 1974 and resettled in the U.K.
He dropped out of school at age 16 and worked as a diamond mounter, using his early profits to buy his first property: a studio apartment in London.
The Yianis Group's portfolio includes residential, retail, office and hotel properties, including two five-star hotels in London's Canary Wharf.
The Monaco resident still maintains close ties with his birth country and his Yianis Christodoulou Foundation supports children's education in Cyprus.
did_you_know_facts: John is a nickname; his full name is Yianakis Theophani Christodoulou.
He owns a 245-foot-yacht, Zeus, which features decks made of teak wood.

name: James Litinsky
about: James Litinsky is the founder and CEO of MP Materials, which owns and operates the only rare earths mine in the United States in California.
Litinsky, after receiving his J.D. and M.B.A., began his career at Fortress Investment Group before launching his own hedge fund JHL Capital Group in 2006 with $11 million in backing.
JHL acquired the mine out of bankruptcy in 2017, orchestrated a cleanup effort, and took the company public in 2020 by merging it with a SPAC
MP Materials began production at its own magnet manufacturing factory in Fort Worth, Texas in 2024, and is working to build a second factory.
The U.S. Department of Defense acquired a $400 million stake in MP Materials in June 2025 and announced a 10-year partnership for buying the company's output.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts/Science, Yale College; Master of Business Administration, Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management; JD, Northwestern University Pritzker School of Law

did_you_know_facts: Litinsky began trading stocks, and reading Forbes, as a teen.
quote: If you really believe you can do something and are naive enough to take on the challenge, start as early as you can.

name: Xiu Laigui
about: Xiu Laigui's privately owned Xiuzheng Pharmaceuticals is one of China's largest pharmaceutical firms.
Xiu worked as a policeman in China in the early 1990s.
Xiuzheng is located in Tonghua in northeastern China's Jilin province.

name: He Yamin & family
about: He Yamin chairs Chengdu Leejun Industrial, a supplier of equipment to the cement and mining industries.
He Yamin's daughter He Jia is being groomed as his successor; she and her father each hold about one-third of the company's shares.
Leejun was founded in 1999 in the central Chinese city of Chengdu.

name: Xie Yi
about: Xie Yi is the chairman and CEO of Suzhou Tianmai Thermal Technology, a maker of thermal management products including heat pipes and graphite films.
The company went public in Shenzhen in 2024, raising $87 million.
The mogul started his first job when he was only 16, working at a local factory that makes thermal management products.
Xie founded Suzhou Tianmai in 2007 with his wife Shen Fenghua, who is a director at the company.
Nowadays, Suzhou Tianmai supplies to customers including Contemporary Amperex Technology Company (CATL), Huawei and Samsung.

name: Myron Wentz
about: Myron Wentz is the founder of USANA, a multilevel marketing company that sells nutritional supplements and skincare products.
Wentz owns 40% of the $850 million (net sales) business, which trades on the NYSE. He took it public in 1996.
In December 2019, he retired as USANA's chairman.
Prior to USANA, he founded Gull Laboratories in 1974 to sell diagnostic tests to hospitals and labs; he sold his stake in 1994 for $22 million.
Wentz renounced his American citizenship in the mid-1990s. He now claims citizenship in tax haven St. Kitts & Nevis.
did_you_know_facts: Wentz spends most of his time at Sanoviv Medical Institute, a holistic care center he founded in 1998 in Rosarito, Mexico.
Wentz enjoys snorkeling and watching coral reef videos on YouTube.

name: Arnold Schwarzenegger
about: One of the highest paid actors in Hollywood history, Arnold Schwarzenegger has earned some $500 million (before taxes and fees) in paychecks and profit-sharing deals from his movies.
He's made even more from early bets on everything from California real estate to stakes in some of the world's most valuable brands.
One of his best bets: Buying a minority stake in fellow billionaire David Booth's Dimensional Fund Advisors when it was managing $12 billion in assets.
Founded in 1996, DFA now has $777 billion of assets under management.
Other valuable investments include a piece of Easton Town Center, the Columbus, Ohio mall created by billionaire Les Wexner, and equity in the Waldorf Astoria hotel in Los Angeles.
Today, Schwarzenegger continues to own several businesses: film and production company Oak Productions, Fitness Publications Inc and film and trademarking holding venture Pumping Iron America.
did_you_know_facts: Between 1970 and 2019, Schwarzenegger churned out around 50 films that made $5.5 billion at the box office.
Schwarzenegger had a costly divorce in 2021 from Kennedy family member Maria Shriver; he could be worth nearly double his current fortune if the pair had a prenup.
quote: I wanted big investments that were interesting, creative and different. Conservative bets--the kind that would generate 4 percent a year, say--didn't interest me.

name: Denise Prenosil
about: Denise Prenosil is the ex-wife of Ed Stack, whose father Richard "Dick" Stack founded Dick's Sporting Goods in 1948.
After the pair divorced in 2006, Prensoil received a nearly 5% stake in Dick's, which she still owns today.
She also received a similar number of Dick's stock options as part of the divorce, which she exercised and sold over the following decade.
Ed Stack and his four siblings bought out their father in 1984. Dick's had just two locations at the time.
Ed ran the company for 36 years before stepping down as CEO in 2021; he is still chairman of Dick's and remains its largest individual shareholder with a nearly 25% stake.
Dick's has more than 850 stores across the U.S. and reported $13.4 billion of revenue in fiscal 2024.

name: Azman Hashim
about: Azman Hashim is the former chairman of AmBank Group, Malaysia's sixth-largest lender by assets. He acquired it in 1982 as the Arab-Malaysian Development Bank.
His bank holding company AMMB Holdings is the listed flagship.
Azman retired in 2022, though he remains chairman emeritus.
Azman also has stakes in RCE Capital and Amcorp Properties, which his daughter Shalina is non-executive chairman.
Azman has been in the banking industry since 1960, when he joined Bank Negara Malaysia.
did_you_know_facts: Azman wears many other hats: He is the president of the Malaysia South-South Association, Malaysia-Japan Economic Association and the Malaysian Prison Friends Club.
One of Azman's three daughters, Shazrina, is a local artist who is known as Mizz Nina.
Azman has climbed Mount Kinabalu - which stands between Myanmar and Papua New Guinea - twice. The second time was in November 2023 at the age of 84.

name: Yvonne Lo
about: Yvonne Lo cofounded clothing manufacturer Crystal International Group with her husband Kenneth in 1970.
They have built a modest sweater factory into one of Asia's largest garment manufacturers, with 80,000 employees at 20 sites around the world.
Crystal's customers include Fast Retailing, Gap, Abercrombie & Fitch, Nike, Adidas and Puma.
Yvonne is vice chairman of Crystal. Kenneth is chairman while their son Andrew is CEO.
Kenneth is the eldest son of the late textile magnate Law Ting-pong.

name: Vadim Novinsky
about: Vadim Novinsky owns Ukraine's Smart Holding Group, which has a 24% stake in Rinat Akhmetov's iron ore producer Metinvest.
Novinsky started working in Ukraine in the mid 1990s with Russian oil producer Lukoil, then began buying Ukrainian metallurgy companies.
The Russian native got his Ukrainian citizenship in 2012; he has been a member of parliament since 2013.
Long seen as one of Ukraine's most Putin-friendly billionaires, he tried to jump-start negotiations with Russia before the invasion.
He visited Mariupol with Akhmetov in February 2022 and briefly returned to Kyiv but apparently took off hours before the invasion; he is now suspected to be in Estonia.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Academy of Civil Aviation (Leningrad)

did_you_know_facts: His wife and four children are all Russian citizens and live in St. Petersburg, Russia.

name: Phillippe Van de Vyvere
about: Philippe In 2017, he is the owner of SEA-Invest, a Luxembourg-based terminal operator.
SEA-invest operates more than 20 ports across two continents with 5.500 employees.
Van de Vyvere bought the 70-hectare French wine estate, Phélan Ségur in Saint Estèphe, in 2017.

name: Norman Asbjornson
about: Norman Asbjornson founded HVAC company AAON in 1988 and took it public three years later.
He served as CEO until 2020, when he transitioned to executive chairman. He retired from that role in 2022 but remains on the board of directors.
AAON reported revenue of $1.2 billion in 2024.
A Montana native, Asbjornson pledged $50 million to help fund a new College of Engineering at his alma mater, Montana State University, in 2014.
Asbjornson is a U.S. Army veteran who served in South Korea.

name: Qiao Zhiyong
about: Qiao chairs Sichuan Qiaoyuan Gas, a supplier of industrial gas.
Sichuan Qiaoyuan Gas went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2022.
Sichuan Qiaoyuan is headquartered in Chengdu, the business hub and capital of China's Sichuan Province.

name: Jeffrey Lorberbaum
about: Jeffrey Lorberbaum built Georgia-based Mohawk Industries into the largest flooring company in the world; he owns a nearly 15% stake.
His father Alan founded Aladdin Mills in 1957 as a maker of bathmats. Lorberbaum joined the company in 1976 and later became CEO.
In 1994, the family sold Aladdin to Mohawk Industries. Lorberbaum took charge of Mohawk in 2001 and expanded into hard-surface flooring.
The publicly traded flooring company is now in more than 170 countries and has completed 54 acquisitions since it went public in 1992.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Denver

did_you_know_facts: In 2022, Lorberbaum was given the honorary title of knight commander of the Order of the Crown by Her Royal Highness Princess Astrid of Belgium.
Lorberbaum is in the World Floor Covering Association's Hall of Fame.

name: Kenneth Lo
about: Kenneth Lo cofounded clothing manufacturer Crystal International Group with his wife Yvonne in 1970.
They have built a modest sweater factory into one of Asia's largest garment manufacturers, with 80,000 employees at 20 sites around the world.
Crystal's customers include Fast Retailing, Gap, Abercrombie & Fitch, Nike, Adidas and Puma.
Kenneth is chairman of Crystal. Yvonne is vice chairman while their son Andrew is CEO.
Kenneth is the eldest son of the late textile magnate Law Ting-pong. His brother is fellow billionaire Law Kar Po.

name: Ngo Chi Dung
about: Ngo Chi Dung is the chairman of VPBank, also known as Vietnam Prosperity Bank, one of the largest banks in Vietnam.
The banking veteran served as vice chairman of rival Techcombank before joining VPBank in 2010.
In 2021, VPBank sold a 49% stake in its consumer finance unit FE Credit to Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group for $1.4 billion.
He holds a doctoral degree in economics from the Institute of Socio-Political Research under Russian Academy of Sciences.
VPBank Securities, the bank's brokerage arm, went public in Ho Chi Minh City in 2025.

name: Junro Ito
about: Junro Ito is the executive chair of Seven & I Holding and the son of the company's late honorary chairman Masatoshi Ito.
Masatoshi Ito, who helped build 7-Eleven into a global giant, died in March 2023 at age 98.
The company is best known for its thousands of 7-Eleven convenience stores in Japan, the U.S. and China. Seven & i Holdings has 87,000 stores in 19 countries.
In 2024, Canadian retail giant, Alimentation Couche-Tard made a $47 billion takeover bid for the company but withdrew in July 2025 citing the retailer's lack of cooperation during negotiations.
Junro Ito joined the company in 1990 and holds a minority stake. His two siblings are also billionaires.
did_you_know_facts: The company also owns Denny's restaurants in Japan, supermarkets, and financial services firms.
Ito and his siblings were mulling making a $58 billion management buyout of the company but backed out in February 2025 citing financial issues.
In March 2025, the company announced a massive share buyback plan in a bid to bolster the share price.
In March 2025, Seven & I agreed to sell its York Holdings unit which includes major supermarket chains and specialty retailers, to Bain Capital for $5.4 billion.

name: Konstantin Nikolaev
about: Konstantin Nikolaev and his partners Nikita Mishin andAndrei Filatov formerly owned a third of Globaltrans, Russia's biggest private rail transport operator.
The trio sold their stakes in Global Ports, exiting the port business in December 2017.
He and his partners worked together at Petra, a railroad freight company.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Moscow State University

did_you_know_facts: Nikolaev is one of the co-founders of Moscow management school Skolkovo, the first business school in Russia.
In 1996 the partners agreed with one of Petra's clients, Alexei Mordashov's Severstal, to start a transport company. They later bought him out.

name: Nikita Mishin
about: Nikita Mishin and partners Konstantin Nikolaev and Andrei Filatov formerly owned roughly one third of Globaltrans, Russia's biggest private rail operator.
In December of 2017 the partners sold their stakes in Global Ports, exiting the port business.
He and his partners worked together at a railroad freight company.
Since 2024, he's held dual citizenship in the U.K., where he has resided for more than a decade.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts/Science, Moscow State University

did_you_know_facts: Mishin is the founder of charity fund Dar, which helps talented children, including ones from low-income families.

name: Shin Dong-joo
about: Shin Dong-joo is the eldest son of Shin Kyuk-Ho, the late founder of Lotte Group, one of South Korea's largest conglomerates.
The retail heavyweight has interests ranging from food and beverage to chemicals, construction and professional baseball.
In 2015, he was dismissed from his executive positions in the group after a bitter feud with his brother Dong-Bin.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Economics, Aoyama Gakuin University; Master of Business Administration, Columbia Business School

did_you_know_facts: Lotte started as a confectionery manufacturer in Japan in 1948 and expanded into South Korea in 1967.
At the start of his career, he worked for Mitsubishi in Japan in 1978.

name: Sanjeev Shah
about: Sanjeev Shah is the chairman of Mumbai-based Everest Food Products, which sells a range of spices, pastes and powders.
Everest was founded by his father Vadilal Shah in 1967 as a small shop selling milk and tea mixes.
Shah joined the business in 1981 when the company was setting up its first factory; he expanded the sales and distribution network.
His younger brother Rajeev joined the company in 1992.
In April 2024 the Singapore food regulator ordered a temporary ban on Everest's fish curry masala alleging the presence of a pesticide. Everest claimed it was safe.
did_you_know_facts: In 2021, Everest started offering herb seasonings as well as pastes such as ginger and garlic paste.
Today Everest exports to more than 80 countries.

name: Vitaly Orlov
about: Vitaly Orlov is the CEO and cofounder of Norebo Holding, the largest vertically integrated seafood company in Russia.
In the late 1990s, Orlov and two partners, who he later bought out, started a business buying used fishing trawlers then exchanged for fish in Russia.
Over the years, Norebo has spent $600 million to acquire fishing companies in the North and Far East of Russia.
Today Norebo, which operates 15 companies, catches 400,000 tons of cod, haddock and pollock a year in the Norwegian Sea, Barents Sea and the Far East.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Murmansk Higher Marine Engineering School

did_you_know_facts: Orlov moved to Norway in 1996 and lived there until 2014. He gave up his Norwegian citizenship when he moved back to Murmansk, Russia.

name: Clelia Haji-Ioannou
about: Clelia Haji-Ioannou is the daughter of Loucas Haji-Ioannou, the late Greek Cypriot shipping magnate (d. 2008).
She is a billionaire thanks to her stake in discount airline easyJet, founded by her brother Stelios.
She owns real estate across Europe, including properties in Monaco and Greece.
She also has a gallery outside of Athens featuring artwork by Picasso, Warhol and Dali.
did_you_know_facts: Haji-Ioannou oversaw the publication of a biography of her father, "Loucas Haji-Ioannou: The King of the Tankers."
Born in Athens, Clelia Haji-Ioannou holds both Cypriot and British citizenship and sits on the board of the Cyprus Marine Environment Protection Association.

name: Farhad Ebrahimi
about: Farhad Ebrahimi is the cofounder of Denver software-publishing giant Quark, Inc.
Quark was sold to Platinum Equity for an undsiclosed sum in 2011.
Ebrahimi began buying Hawiian assets around 2001 and by 2018 owned nearly 80% of nut producer Royal Hawaiian Orchards, which was later privatized.
Ebrahimi is also an investor in solar panel maker First Solar.

name: Zhu Jiangming
about: Zhu Jiangming is the founder of Zhejiang Leapmotor Technology, a Chinese electric vehicle maker.
Earlier in his career, he co-founded Dahua Technology, a supplier of surveillance equipment.
From 2008 to 2010, Zhu worked at Motorola's branch Hangzhou, China.
Zhu received a bachelor's degree in electronic engineering from China's Zhejiang University in 1990.

The Goh family draws the bulk of its wealth from a majority stake in Japan's Nippon Paint Holdings, one of the world's largest paint manufacturers.
Henrietta, together with her two sisters and three cousins, inherited the bulk of their grandfather's fortune.
Her father is Hup Jin, the eldest child of the late patriarch who started making paints in a small factory in Singapore before partnering with Nippon Paint in 1962.
Hup Jin is the chairman of Nippon Paint.

The company has built about 350 apartment buildings in three decades.

In 2025, Escalante acquired shares owned by minority shareholders in a deal valuing the company at over $2 billion.

Veronica shares ownership of MAPEI with Marco and her cousin Simona Giorgetta, who owns the largest stake in the company.

about: Ong Leong Huat is the executive chairman and majority shareholder of financial services company OSK Holdings.
He is also the executive chairman of its property arm, OSK Property Holdings.
He was appointed non-executive chairman of OSK Ventures International, the group's venture capital and private equity firm, in 2023.
OSK Holdings and OSK Ventures International are listed in Malaysia.
OSK Holdings has a minority stake in RHB Bank, one of Malaysia's largest banks by assets.

name: Brian Lawson
about: Brian Lawson is a vice chair of Brookfield, a Toronto-based alternative investment firm with $1 trillion in assets under management.
Lawson joined Brookfield in 1988, when it was called Brascan, and served as the firm's CFO from 2002 to 2020.
Lawson began his career as an accountant at Touche Ross, a predecessor to Deloitte.
His family's foundation supports nutrition research and established the University of Toronto's Joannah & Brian Lawson Centre for Child Nutrition.

name: Mehmet Kazanci
about: Mehmet Kazanci is a shareholder of family-owned Kazancı Holding, one of Turkey's largest energy companies.
The $3.6 billion (revenue) company operates across the energy industry, including electricity generation and distribution, natural gas distribution and generator production.
Kazanci started the energy business in 1968 with the Watt Electric Motor Factory.
Kazancı Holding expanded its tourism business in the city of Bodrum, in 2022, with the 5-star Mirada Exclusive Hotel. It currently owns four hotels.

name: Daniel Feffer
about: Daniel Feffer is one of four billionaire brothers who control of Suzano, a Brazilian pulp and paper firm founded in 1924 by their grandfather.
The second-eldest of the brothers, he is vice-chairman of Suzano, which in early 2019 acquired rival Brazilian pulp and paper firm Fibria.
An advocate of open markets, Daniel Feffer is the chairman of the Brazilian branch of the International Chamber of Commerce.
He also founded Intelligent Tech & Trade Initiative, a project exploring how new technologies such as AI and blockchain can improve international trade negotiations.
did_you_know_facts: Suzano is the world's largest producer of eucalyptus pulp.

name: Ma Xiuhui
about: Ma Xiuhui is the general manager of China lighting manufacturer Opple Lighting.
Ma and husband Wang Yaohui started out making traditional light bulbs in Guangdong Province in the 1990s, before moving the headquarters to Shanghai.
Wang is also a billionaire.

name: Charles Beauduin
about: Charles Beauduin controls the textile machinery company Vandewiele and 25% of listed company Barco, which specializes in high-end digital projection, imaging, and networking solutions.
The Beauduin family has its roots in the sugar industry and sold sugar factory Tiense Suiker to Germany's Südzucker in 1989.
In 1993 Beauduin took over Vandewiele group, which was founded in 1880 as a machinery servicing company and converted into a weaving machine manufacturer by Michel Van de Wiele in 1921.
The company produces textile machinery for flooring, home linen and fashion under brands that include Titan, Aros, Loepfe and Eutron.

name: Pan Shiyi
about: Pan Shiyi and wife Zhang Xin co-founded Beijing real estate developer Soho China.
Soho China is listed in Hong Kong and is best known for developing commercial real estate in Beijing and Shanghai.
Pan and Zhang stepped down from their leadership roles as chairman and CEO "in order to focus on supporting the arts and philanthropic pursuits" in 2022 but remain on the board.

name: Scott Smith
about: Scott Smith is one of three cofounders of Utah-based cloud computing company Qualtrics.
He cofounded the company in Provo, Utah in 2002 with his two sons, Ryan and Jared; Ryan is the CEO.
Three days before its scheduled IPO in January 2019, Qualtrics was acquired by German software firm SAP for $8 billion in cash.
Scott owned about 14% of the company at the time of the sale.
The company sold a second time in March 2023 to Silver Lake and CPP Investments at a $12.5 billion valuation.

about: Hua Xuande chairs Zhejiang ZoneBanner Jiuzhou Group, which controls Shanghai-listed pharmaceutical supplier Zhejiang Jiuzhou Pharmaceutical.
Hua's daughter, Hua Lirong, chairs Zhejiang Jiuzhou Pharmaceutical.
In September 2019, Jiuzhou Pharmaceutical acquired U.S. pharmaceutical ingredient firm PharmAgra Labs for a reported $16 million.
In 2019 Jiuzhou also took over a Chinese subsidiary of Swiss pharmaceutical maker Novartis to help expand its production.

name: Alfredo Harp Helu & family
about: Alfredo Harp Helú's fortune stems from Acciones y Valores de Mexico, also known as Accival, which he cofounded.
In 1991 Accival merged with Mexican bank Banamex to form Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival (Banacci). Harp Helú then became chairman of the group.
Citigroup acquired Grupo Financiero Banamex-Accival for $12 billion in stock and cash in 2001, and Harp Helú joined Citigroup's board.
He has a minority stake in publicly-traded tile producer Internacional de Ceramica.
He owns two Mexican baseball teams, Los Diablos Rojos of Mexico City and Los Guerreros of Oaxaca.
did_you_know_facts: A baseball enthusiast, he published an autobiography in 2003 titled, "To Live and Die Playing Baseball."
He was kidnapped in 1994 for 106 days and released, reportedly after a payment of $30 million.

name: Jens von Bahr
about: Jens von Bahr cofounded publicly traded casino supplier Evolution AB with Fredrik 'sterberg in 2006.
He was CEO of Evolutions until 2016 and is now chairman of the company, which primarily sells live-streamed tables of blackjack, poker, craps and roulette to online gambling operators.
The company went public in Stockholm in 2015 and now provides its services to over 700 customers in 21 countries. Evolution's products are available globally for end users.
Evolution's first casino studio was set up in Riga, Lithuania. Today the company has live-casino studios in nine countries, including the U.S.
Before starting Evolution, von Bahr headed the Sri Lankan operations of Oriflame, a Swiss-Swedish multi-level marketing company that sells beauty products.
did_you_know_facts: The land of Von Bahr's house is owned the king of Sweden; he was denied permission to build a pool on the property.

name: Antonio Luiz Seabra
about: Antonio Luiz Seabra founded Natura Cosmeticos in 1969 as Brazil's answer to Avon and built it into Brazil's largest beauty company.
Some 1.4 million "consultants" (mainly women) sell Natura products door-to-door across Brazil, six other Latin American countries and France.
Natura Cosmeticos, which went public in 2004, bought U.K. cosmetics chain The Body Shop from L'Oréal in 2017 for over $1 billion.
Seabra is co-chairman of the board of Natura and also owns Bresco, a Brazilian property-rental operation focused on warehouses, offices and hotels.
Media-shy Seabra reportedly owns an apartment on the banks of the river Seine in Paris as well as real estate in London.
did_you_know_facts: Seabra communicates directly to employees through motivational videos. He is known for quoting poetry and philosophy in business meetings.
quote: The impossible is only the beginning of all possibilities!

name: Mustafa Hamied
about: Mustafa Hamied was the non-executive vice chairman of Mumbai generics maker Cipla until September 2024, when he resigned citing his age and health.
Cipla was founded in 1935 by his father Khwaja Abdul Hamied, a disciple of Mahatma Gandhi.
After the patriarch passed away in 1972, Mustafa, a science graduate from Bombay University, inherited the business along with his older brother Yusuf Hamied, also a billionaire.
His daughter Samina, who was executive vice-chairperson of Cipla, stepped down in March 2024 but retains a board seat. His son Kamil was appointed to the board in September 2024.

name: Wang Xinyang
about: Wang Xinyang is the founder, chairman and CEO of state-backed Gpixel Changchun Microelectronics, a fabless maker of CMOS image sensors - chips that turn incoming light into digital images.
Before setting up Gpixel in 2012, UK- and Dutch-educated Wang worked with CMOSIS NV, a Belgian company in CMOS image sensor design.
He also worked as a researcher and Ph.D. supervisor at the Changchun Institute of Optics, Fine Mechanics and Physics.
Wang took Gpixel public on the Hong Kong stock exchange in April 2026, raising $332 million.
His wife, Zhang Yanxia, serves as Gpixel's deputy general manager.

name: Mary Alice Malone Jr

Mary Alice Jr. and her sister, Catherine Dorrance Malone, inherited an 18% combined stake in The Campbell's Company when their mother, Mary Alice Dorrance Malone Sr., died in June 2025.
Mary Alice Jr. replaced her mother on the company's board in July 2025. Her cousin, Bennett Dorrance Jr., and her mother's cousin, Archbold van Beuren, are also billionaire directors of the company.
Mary Alice Jr. and her sister grew up on their mother's horse breeding farm in Coatesville, Pa. An accomplished dressage rider, Mary Alice Jr. once made the U.S. Junior Olympic Equestrian Team.
She founded luxury footwear brand Malone Souliers in 2014 and relaunched the forty-year-old UK footwear brand Duo Boots in 2020 after buying the company out of bankruptcy.
Mary Alice Jr. lives in London, where she studied shoemaking at the London College of Fashion.

name: Krishna Kumar Bangur

name: Steven Schuurman

He also founded and chairs FutureNL, a non-profit that supports digital literacy in Dutch primary and secondary schools.

name: Oliver Samwer
about: Oliver Samwer and his brothers Alexander and Marc founded Berlin-based tech incubator Rocket Internet in 2007 and took it public in October 2014.
Oliver is the middle brother and the CEO of Rocket Internet, which delisted from the Frankfurt Stock Exchange in October 2020.
Together, the Samwers own around 45% of Rocket. The company was valued at more than $8 billion at the time of its IPO.
Inspired by the dot-com boom, they created a German auction site, Alando, in 1999 and sold it to eBay for $43 million after a few months.
That was followed by the creation of mobile phone content provider Jamba!, which they sold to Verisign in 2004 for $273 million.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management

did_you_know_facts: Oliver once said in an interview that he has no time for hobbies, preferring to spend his spare time with his children.
quote: My mother always wanted to me to work for Bertelsmann. Sometimes it's good not to tell your mother what you are working on.

name: Ruben Feffer
about: Ruben Feffer is one of four billionaire brothers who control Suzano, a Brazilian paper giant founded by their grandfather.
He has developed a career creating music for movies and TV shows.
Ruben, a pianist, is credited with the music for Boy and the World, a 2013 Brazilian film nominated for Academy Award for best animated feature.
Known as Binho, he is not a board member at Suzano.
did_you_know_facts: Feffer is the founder of the production studio Ultrassom Music Ideas.
He has served as the musical director for a number of animated children's TV shows in Brazil.

name: Eduard Chukhlebov
about: Eduard Chukhlebov has ties to the powerful founder of Ural Mining Metallurgical Company (UMMC) Iskander Makhmudov.
When Makhmudov reorganized his business, he gave Chukhlebov, one of his managers, a 7.5% stake in UMMC.
Chukhlebov also owns minority stakes in thermal coal producer Kuzbassrazrezugol and transportation company Ugol-Trans through UMMC.
UMMC, which is the biggest zinc, copper and coal producer in Russia, operates more than 300 companies in nine regions of Russia.

name: Catherine Malone
about: Catherine Dorrance Malone is a great-granddaughter of John T. Dorrance, who invented Campbell's Soup in 1897.
Catherine and her sister, Mary Alice Dorrance Malone Jr., inherited an 18% combined stake in The Campbell's Company when their mother, Mary Alice Dorrance Malone Sr., died in June 2025.
While Catherine doesn't have a role at the company, Mary Alice Jr. replaced their mother on the company's board in July 2025.
Their cousin, Bennett Dorrance Jr., and their mother's cousin, Archbold van Beuren, are also billionaire directors of the company.
Catherine and her sister grew up on their mother's horse breeding farm in Coatesville, Pa. Catherine, who inherited the farm, also owns a dressage equestrian facility in Wellington, Florida.

name: William Heinecke
about: U.S.-born hotelier William Heinecke came to Thailand as a child and started his first business before he turned 18, hence naming his company Minor.
A Thai citizen since 1991, his Minor International has more than 600 hotels and resorts, over 2,700 restaurants and nearly 200 retail stores spread across more than 60 countries.
He tripled the size of his hotel portfolio by acquiring Spain's NH Hotels for $2.6 billion in 2018, the year of Minor's golden anniversary.
Minor also has franchises for such brands as Swensens, Sizzler, Dairy Queen and Burger King.
Three resorts from Minor's Anantara hotel chain were featured in hit TV series The White Lotus.
did_you_know_facts: An auto enthusiast, Heinecke has a collection of 36 cars and motorcycles.
In 2020, Heinecke ceded the CEO's position to a Minor veteran. In 2021, Minor expanded into China, partnering with Funyard Hotels & Resorts.
quote: You learn through every crisis, every challenge.

name: Wang Chou-hsiong
about: Wang Chou-hsiong started athletic-footwear maker Feng Tay Enterprises in 1971. Eight years later it formed a partnership to make sports shoes for Nike.
Over the years the company has expanded into casual shoes, bags and sporting goods such as golf balls and ice hockey helmets.
Headquartered in the western Taiwan county of Yunlin, Feng Tay operates plants in mainland China, India, Indonesia and Vietnam, as well as Taiwan.
Wang's older son Richard took over from him as chairman in 2018. Younger son Kevin became vice chairman in 2017.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Arts/Science, National Central University; Bachelor of Business Administration, National Taiwan University

did_you_know_facts: Wang Chou-Hsiong was mentioned in the autobiography of Nike cofounder Phil Knight.

name: Gerald Engström
about: Gerald Engström is a Swedish industrialist and co-founder of Systemair, a publicly traded manufacturer of ventilation systems.
He served as CEO of Systemair from 1974 to 2015 before becoming chairman until 2025.
Today Systemair operates in 51 countries with 90 companies and over 6,700 employees.
Engström owns a large portfolio of listed stocks, valued at over $1 billion.
did_you_know_facts: His daughter, Frida Engström, is CEO of fashion retailer Indiska, while his son, Niklas Engström, is CEO of RVM Systems, both companies in his portfolio.

name: Yasuhide Uno
about: Yasuhide Uno runs U-Next Holdings, a company that's become a streaming services giant in Japan.It also provides payment and point-of-sales services to restaurants and stores, broadband services and energy to companies.
His father Mototada started the Osaka-based company providing background music via cable to retailers and restaurants. Yasuhide joined the firm in 1998, just before his father died.
In 2001, it listed on the Osaka Stock Exchange's bourse for startups and moved to the Tokyo Stock Exchange in 2013.
In June, the company announced a tie-up with Tokyo-based e-commerce giant Rakuten for a mobile package to enable unlimited U-Next videos and data usage.
The Tokyo-based company posted nearly $2.5 billion in revenue in the fiscal year through August 2025.

name: Sun Huaiqing & family
about: Sun Huaqing chairs Guangdong Marubi Biotechnology, a supplier of cosmetics and skin care products.
Sun worked for an electric machinery factory in Chongqing more than 20 years ago.
He founded the "Marubi" brand in Guangzhou in 2000.
Marubi investors include L Capital, an affiliate of LVMH.

name: Laurent Junique
about: Laurent Junique is the CEO and founder of Singapore-based call center and business process outsourcing firm TDCX.
TDCX went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2021. In 2024, Junique took the company private in a deal valuing it at around $1 billion.
Junique, a French citizen, founded TDCX as a 29-year-old in 1995 after a two-year stint at consumer goods giant Unilever.
TDCX counts Meta and Airbnb among its key clients.

name: Craig Abod
about: Craig Abod is the founder and owner of Carahsoft, a Virginia-based technology company that specializes in IT services for government agencies.
Abod founded Carahsoft in 2004 and has grown the business to revenue of more than $11 billion.
Carahsoft ranked No. 20 on Forbes's 202 l5ist of America's Largest Private Companies.

name: Christian Louboutin
about: Christian Louboutin is a French fashion designer who cofounded his self-named fashion brand, known for its signature red-soled heels.

He started the firm in Paris in 1991 with his friends Bruno Chambelland and Henri Seydoux. In 2021, they sold a 24% stake to Exor, the investment holding company of Italy's Agnelli family, for about $650 million.
His shoes became famous in the U.S. when they were featured by Sarah Jessica Parker's Carrie Bradshaw in Sex and the City and have been name-dropped by Cardi B and Drake.
Today, Louboutin has more than 160 boutiques in 32 countries across 4 continents and also makes men's shoes, bags and beauty products.
In 2023, both Taylor Swift and Beyoncé wore Louboutins in their record-breaking Eras and Renaissance tours.
did_you_know_facts: Louboutin owns the Vermelho Hotel, a five-star luxury resort in southern Portugal that he opened in 2023.
His homes include the13th-century Château de Champgillon in France, which he co-owns with Bruno Chambelland and where he reportedly keeps 8,000 pairs of shoes.

name: Shigefumi Wada
about: Shigefumi Wada is the president and founder of publicly traded software and IT firm Obic Business Consultants.
Obic Business Consultants is known for its cloud accounting services and its television ads featuring a kabuki actor.
Wada started the business in 1980; his wife Hiroko is vice president and a board member.
Together Wada and his wife own a significant stake in the company.
Obic, another IT services firm, is a major shareholder and its founder and CEO Masahiro Noda is chairman of Obic Business Consultants.

name: Manoj Punjabi
about: Manoj Punjabi, his wife Shania and his parents Dhamoo and Sunita in 2002 cofounded MD Media, the precursor of Indonesia-listed film studio company MD Entertainment.
He is president director of MD Entertainment, which went public in 2018 through a $19 million IPO.
China's technology and entertainment giant Tencent bought a 14.6% stake in 2021. It has since pared its stake to 11.5%.
Shania serves as president commissioner of MD Entertainment.
In 2024, MD Entertainment acquired an 80% stake in free-to-air broadcaster NET. TV for $105 million.
did_you_know_facts: The company takes its name from Manoj and his father Dhamoo. The business started by producing popular soap operas.

name: Shin Chang-jae
about: Shin Chang-Jae is the chairman and CEO of Kyobo Life Insurance, founded by his father in 1958 as Daehan Kyoyuk Insurance.
When Shin assumed the posts in 2000, Kyobo was reeling from investment portfolio losses in the aftermath of the Asian financial crisis.
He turned the company around, focusing on customer satisfaction and risk control.
With a network of agents and financial planners, the company now offers insurance and asset-management products to more than 5 million customers.
did_you_know_facts: He has a mischievous penchant for staging stunts to make a point, such as reportedly taking part in his own fake funeral.
In 2010, he received the 19th Montblanc de la Culture Arts Patronage Award for his support of Korean literature through the Daesan Foundation.

name: Fahed Hariri
about: Fahed Hariri is the youngest son of the late billionaire Rafik Hariri, the former prime minister of Lebanon who was assassinated in 2005.
In 2012, Fahed sold his shares in family construction firm Saudi Oger to his brother Saad Hariri, who was Lebanon's prime minister until January 2020.
He invested some of the proceeds in real estate in New York, Paris and Monte Carlo and in now beleaguered Lebanese banks.
He is also developing residential buildings in Beirut.
did_you_know_facts: Fahed Hariri is an avid collector of modern and contemporary European and American art. His collection includes works by Pablo Picasso and Louise Bourgeois.
While an architecture student, Hariri ran an interior design studio outside of Paris and sold furniture, some of which he designed, to clients in Saudi Arabia.

name: Jiang Xuefei & family
about: Jiang Xuefei is the chairman of Shenzhen Suntak Circuit Technology, one of China's largest makers of printed circuit boards.
He founded the company in May 1995 and also serves as its CEO.
Jiang holds an EMBA from Xiamen University.

name: Theresia Gouw
about: Theresia Gouw launched Acrew Capital, an early-stage venture capital firm in 2019; it now manages $1.7 billion in gross assets.
In 2014 she cofounded venture capital firm Aspect Ventures with Jennifer Fonstad; in 2019 the two women parted ways.
Gouw earned her stripes in the VC world at Accel, where she spent 15 years and was the firm's first female partner.
Successful investments she led while at Accel included bets on real estate site Trulia and cybersecurity firm Imperva.
She is chair of education nonprofit DonorsChoose and a board member at ONE, a nonprofit focused on ending poverty.

forbes_list.list: The Midas List: Top Tech Investors (2020)

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Stanford Graduate School of Business; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Brown University

did_you_know_facts: Gouw has appeared on the Forbes Midas List of the most successful venture capitalists, seven times.
An engineering major at Brown University, she considered switching to sociology but was persuaded not to by her father.
quote: I, like thousands of others who are called to the Valley everyday, have my parents to thank for showing me how to be an American dreamer.

name: Rafal Brzoska
about: Rafał Brzoska is the founder and CEO of InPost, a logistics company that operates over 11,000 parcel lockers in Poland.
Brzoska started out by founding Integer Group, which distributed leaflets, in 1999
Seven years later, he started InPost, which operates automated lockers that allow customers to drop off and collect packages at any time of the day.
The company went public in Amsterdam in 2021, raising over $3 billion in its IPO.

name: Hideyuki Busujima
about: Hideyuki Busujima is the son of Sankyo founder Kunio Busujima, who died in October 2016.
In 2023, Hideyuki stepped down as CEO of pachinko-machine maker Sankyo, but remains chairman.
Kunio transferred his shares of publicly-traded Sankyo to Hideyuki in 2014.
In 2020, Hideyuki sold 20 million shares back to the company, which cancelled them.

name: Peter-Alexander Wacker
about: Peter-Alexander Wacker owns around 10% of chemical company Wacker Chemie AG, founded by his great-grandfather Alexander Wacker in 1914.
He worked for BMW for ten years before joining Wacker Chemie in 1993 as a member of the board, when it was still a privately owned company.
When Wacker went public in November 2005, Peter-Alexander became CEO. In 2008, he stepped down and became chairman of the supervisory board.
Wacker Chemie has an annual revenue of more than $6 billion and sells its products in over 100 countries.
In 2016, the company began producing polysilicon (used for solar cells and semiconductors) at a new facility in Bradley County, Tennessee.
did_you_know_facts: Peter-Alexander Wacker was named family business man of the year in Germany in 2006.
He collects elephant figures from around the world, as elephants symbolize strength to him. His holding company is named Blue Elephant.

name: Jiang Long
about: Jiang Long is a senior advisor of Goertek Inc., a maker of electronic components; Goerek's customers include Apple.
Jiang, who joined Goertek in 2004, holds a doctorate from the University of Maryland.
Brother Jiang Bin, who founded Goertek in 2001, chairs the company.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Tsinghua University; Ph.D, University of Maryland; Master of Arts, Renmin University of China

name: Cyrus Madon
about: Cyrus Madon is the executive vice chair of Brookfield Asset Management, a Toronto-based spinoff of Brookfield Corp. which manages $1 trillion in assets.
Madon joined Brookfield in 1998 and was previously the CEO of its private equity business. He remains its executive chair of private equity.
He began his career working in corporate finance at PricewaterhouseCoopers and initially joined Brookfield as CFO of its real estate brokerage business.
Madon also serves on the board of the C.D. Howe Institute, an influential Canadian think tank.

name: Xu Jiangnan
about: Xu Jiangnan chairs Jiangxi Tianxin Pharmaceutical, a suppier of vitamins.
Jiangxi Tianxi went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2022.
Xu's daughter Xu Jing is a member of the board of directors.

name: Igor Kudryashkin
about: Igor Kudryashkin is the commerce director of Iskander Makhmudov's Ural Mining Metallurgical Company (UMMC), a top Russian producer of commodities such as copper, zinc, coal and gold.
Kudryashkin received shares in UMMC when Makhmudov reorganized the business in 2013.
Kudryashkin and his family hold more than two-thirds of European Media Group, which boasts 8 radio stations with about 35 million listeners each week.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Ph.D, Moscow Institute of Steel and Alloys

did_you_know_facts: Kudryashkin's daughter sings under the name Nastya Kudri; in 2015, she recorded a song called "Father."

name: Vildan Gulcelik
about: Vildan Gulcelik is one of more than a dozen family members who hold shares in ENKA, one of Turkey's largest construction and energy companies.

ENKA, which was cofounded in 1957 by Sarik Tara and his brother-in-law, Sadi Gulcelik, is Turkey's leading private electricity producer and also operates in real estate, tourism, transport and trade (construction equipment and machinery).
In Moscow, ENKA owns a hotel, shopping malls and approximately 370,000 square meters of net rentable Class A office space.
Sadi Gulcelik died in a plane accident in Saudi Arabia in 1980, and Mehmet Sinan Tara took over in 1984 at age 26. His son Agah Mehmet Tara became CEO in 2012, at age 29.
did_you_know_facts: Over the last 20 years or so, ENKA has been the biggest builder of U.S. consular and embassy buildings.
These government projects can be found in locations ranging from Turkey, Algeria and Nepal to Equatorial Guinea, the Dominican Republic and the Netherlands.

name: Christian Chabot
about: Christian Chabot cofounded Tableau, a data analytics and visualization company, in 2003.
He and his cofounders raised $15 million in venture capital before taking Tableau public on the New York Stock Exchange in May 2013.
Chabot was CEO of Tableau until 2016 and chairman of the board until 2019.
Salesforce acquired Tableau in 2019 in a $15.7 billion, all-stock deal.
Chabot now focuses most of his time on his two nonprofits: The Holocene Foundation and Washington Neurodiversity Project.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Stanford University Graduate School of Business; Bachelor of Science, Stanford University; Master of Science, University of Sussex

name: Zhu Zhaojiang
about: Zhu Zhaojiang chairs Shenzhen Transsion, a supplier of mobile phones global emerging markets.
Transsion is headquartered in Shenzhen.
Zhu founded Transsion Technology--the predecessor of the listed company -- in 2006.

name: Marty Horton
about: Marty Horton's late husband Donald Horton (d. 2024) founded homebuilder D.R. Horton in 1978.
She owns a share of the family's more than 10% stake in the business, which is America's largest builder.
D.R. Horton has built more than 1 million homes across 126 markets in 36 states. It did $36.8 billion in fiscal 2024 sales.

name: Sergey Kasyanenko & family
about: Sergey Kasyanenko cofounded Orimi, Russia's largest producer of tea and roasted coffee.
Orimi was founded in 1994 as the Orimi Trade company, which ran wholesale trade of flour, sugar and tea.
The company would become a major player in the Russian tea market, eventually launching its own tea packaging production.
Most of his fortune is cash, thanks to $1.5 billion of Orimi dividends paid over more than a decade.
did_you_know_facts: Kasyanenko has Ph.D. in Physics and Mathematics.

name: Lim Wee Chai
about: Lim Wee Chai started Top Glove with his wife Tong Siew Bee in 1991 and took the company public in 2001.
Top Glove is one of the world's largest producers of rubber gloves. It has 51 factories with an annual capacity of 95 billion gloves.
Lim, whose parents are rubber plantation owners and traders, also holds a stake in property developer Tropicana.
