In March 2022, Lim postponed plans for a Hong Kong listing amid a sharp drop in profits.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Malaya; Master of Business Administration, Sul Ross State University

name: Patokh Chodiev
about: Eurasian Resources Group (ERG), of which Patokh Chodiev is part owner, got its start investing natural resources in Kazakhstan in the mid-1990s.
With partners Alexander Machkevich and Alijan Ibragimov (both billionaires), he took Eurasian Natural Resources Corp. (ENRC) public in London in 2007.
They delisted ENRC in 2013, after its stock price deflated amid a market downturn, stalled growth and investigative inquiries.
Today, ERG is a diversified natural resources group with production assets and development projects in 14 countries across four continents.
Its activities range from mining and smelting to energy production, logistics and financial services (Kazakhstan's Eurasian Bank is a subsidiary).
did_you_know_facts: Belgian Chodiev and Israeli Machkevich along with Ibragimov, a native of Uzbekistan who is now a citizen of Kazakhstan, are sometimes referred to as "The Trio."

name: Catharina Mühleis
about: Catharina Mühleis is a fourth generation heir to the Stihl family fortune, founded in 1926 by Andreas Stihl.
Primarily known for its chainsaws, the company also manufactures power tools for forestry, agriculture and construction.
Stihl, which employs 19,805 people, has manufacturing facilities in Germany, USA, Brazil, Switzerland, Austria, China and the Philippines.

name: Caspar Callerström
about: Caspar Callerström joined Swedish investment company EQT AB in 1996.
Callerström is chief operating officer and partner at now publicly traded EQT, which has roughly $81 billion in assets under management.
EQT primarily invests in private equity, but has also put funds into venture capital, real estate and infrastructure.
EQT has minted seven billionaires, nearly as many as Google or Facebook.
Privately, Callerstrom is one of the founding members of a group of financial elites that backs the Swedish football club Djurgårdens IF.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Economics, Stockholm School of Economics

name: Amit Burman
about: Amit Burman is the fifth-generation scion of the storied Burman clan, which controls consumer goods company Dabur.
An MBA from Cambridge University, he started off in Dabur's industrial engineering department where he worked on mechanization and packaging.
He went on to lead Dabur's foray into processed foods spanning the gamut from cooking pastes to fruit juices.
He resigned as non executive chairman in August 2022 and is now a non-executive director on the board.
Falguni Nayar, the billionaire founder of beauty and fashion retailer Nykaa sits on Dabur's board.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Lehigh University; Master of Business Administration, Judge Business School; Master of Science, Columbia University

did_you_know_facts: Apart from a minority stake in Dabur, he also has stakes in other privately held businesses such as restaurant chain Lite Bite Foods.
In 2020, Burman acquired a stake in No Worry No Tension Healthcare, a startup that uses artificial intelligence to gauge emotional wellness.

name: K. Rai Sahi
about: K. Rai Sahi oversees $18.9 billion (assets) real estate firm Morguard Corp. as executive chairman.
His firm's 200-some commercial, residential and hotel properties extend from Ontario to Illinois.
Sahi also heads TWC Enterprises, the largest golf club owner and operator in Canada.
He immigrated to Canada from India when he was 24 and started by selling insurance door to door.
did_you_know_facts: Sahi was born in Pakistan before India was partitioned into two countries, and his family fled to India after the split.

name: Jorge Feffer & family
about: Jorge Feffer is one of four billionaire brothers who control Suzano, a Brazilian paper giant founded by their grandfather.
In January 2019, Suzano completed a roughly $7.5 billion acquisition of Brazilian pulp and paper maker Fibria.
He was the Deputy Chief Corporate Officer of Suzano from 2013 until 2015.
Jorge partnered with a Brazilian publisher on a book series known as Library of Social Critics, with works by authors like philosopher Leo Strauss.
His grandfather, a Ukrainian immigrant, founded the company in 1924.
did_you_know_facts: Feffer partnered with a Brazilian publisher on a book series known as Library of Social Criticism, with works by authors like philosopher Leo Strauss.
He previously served as Assistant Secretary of Culture, Science and Technology for the State of São Paulo.

name: Tatiana Volodina
about: Tatiana Volodina's fortune is derived from L'Etoile, a well-known perfume and cosmetics retail chain with 1,000 locations in 250 cities across Russia.
Volodina owns L'Etoile through Alkor, a holding company in which she has a controlling stake.
Alkor also owns Podruzhka, a smaller cosmetics chain.
L'Etoile and Podruzhka ( also know as "Girlfriend") saw combined sales of over $1 billion.
After earning a degree in economic cybernetics, Volodina worked for Shiseido and Estée Lauder Companies and helped build their businesses in Russia.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master, Plekhanov Russian University of Economics

name: Hary Tanoesoedibjo
about: Hary Tanoesoedibjo got his start building a media business soon after college.
He stepped down as CEO of his Media Nusantara Citra (MNC), which owns four national TV stations, in 2016 to focus on politics.
In 2023, he opened the Lido Music & Arts Center in Bogor as part of the Lido City project, which will feature a Trump-branded golf course and resort.
His listed MNC Tourism Indonesia, formerly MNC Land, in 2000. MNC Tourism is building another Trump-branded golf resort in Bali.
His daughter Angela, who used to serve as Indonesia's Deputy Tourism and Creative Economy Minister, became co-CEO of MNC Group in 2024.
did_you_know_facts: Hary, who attended Donald Trump's inauguration in 2017, is building a Trump Hotel luxury resort in Bali.
Hary is now actively involved in his political party Perindo, which he founded in 2014 after a brief run to be the country's vice president.

name: Ke Guihua
about: Ke Guihua chairs Shanghai-listed Keboda Technology, a supplier of electronic components for the auto industry.
Keboda's customers include Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Audi, and Volkswagen.
Ke is originally from the eastern China city of Wenzhou.

name: Ryan Israel
about: Ryan Israel is the chief investment officer of Pershing Square Capital Management, the hedge fund founded by Bill Ackman in 2004.
Pershing Square has $16 billion in assets under management and was valued at $10.5 billion when outside investors bought 10% of the firm in June 2024.
A University of Pennsylvania graduate, Israel joined Pershing Square early in his career in 2009 following two years in investment banking at Goldman Sachs.
Ackman named Israel his CIO and eventual successor in 2022.
did_you_know_facts: Israel was named to Forbes' 30 Under 30 list in the finance category in 2015.

name: Hiroyuki Inoue
about: Hiroyuki Inoue is chairperson of steel maker Yamato Kogyo, which his father Asaji founded in 1944.

The firm, based in the western Japan city of Himeji, is an electric arc furnace operator and maker of structural steel and rail and switches for railroads, including for Japan's famous Shinkansen bullet train.
The company posted over $1 billion in revenue in the fiscal year ended in March 2025.
Yamato Kogyo, which earns a majority of its sales from overseas, has plants or joint ventures in South Korea, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia and the U.S.
In 1962, it listed on the First Section of the Tokyo and Osaka stock exchanges.

name: Rajesh Sharma
about: Rajesh Sharma gets his wealth from a majority stake in non-banking finance company Capri Global Capital, which he runs.
Mumbai-based Capri offers home loans, construction loans as well as customized business loans for medium and small-scale enterprises.
It has more than 900 branches across India, with a substantial presence in northern and western India.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Chartered Accountant, Institute of Chartered Accountants of India

did_you_know_facts: Capri Global started as a construction finance company in 2011.
Capri Global forayed into housing finance in 2017.

name: Eiichi Kuriwada
about: Eiichi Kuriwada's father, Kiyoshi Sagawa, founded a package delivery firm in 1957; now called Sagawa Express, it's Japan's No. 2 delivery outfit.
Sagawa Express parent SG Holdings listed its shares on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in December 2017.
Kuriwada is chairman and CEO of SG Holdings
Shares of the company had soared on the back of a jump in online buying during the pandemic but have since declined.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: High School Graduate, Arai High School

did_you_know_facts: In the early 1990s, Sagawa Express was the focus of a scandal; an executive was convicted of paying off politicians.
Sagawa, a billionaire in 1992, resigned that year; neither he nor Kuriwada were charged as part of the scandal.

name: Christian Sinding
about: Christian Sinding is a private equity executive and former CEO of EQT, one of the world's largest PE firms.
He joined EQT in 1998 after working as a consultant at McKinsey & Company.
Sinding spent more than two decades helping build EQT into a global buyout powerhouse with investments across Europe, North America and Asia.
He became CEO in 2019, the same year EQT went public on the Stockholm Stock Exchange.
He stepped down as CEO in 2025, and was succeeded by fellow billionaire Per Franzén.

name: Zhang Xuansong
about: Zhang chairs Yonghui Superstores, an operator of hypermarkets and supermarkets.
His brother Zhang Xuanning is the vice chairman of Yonghui Superstores.
Yonghui Superstore listed on Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2010.

name: Hartley Rogers
about: Hartley Rogers is executive co-chairman and a managing director of Hamilton Lane, a publicly traded asset management firm.
Rogers owns more than 13% of the company, which listed on the Nasdaq in 2017.
Prior to joining Hamilton Lane in 2003, he spent two decades working in private equity at Morgan Stanley and Credit Suisse.
He is the Chairman of the Advisory Board of Harvard Online and a board member of the Council on Foreign Relations.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard Business School

did_you_know_facts: Rogers previously served on the board of the Metropolitan Opera.
Both of his parents were university professors, contributing to Rogers? passion for academia.

name: Giannis Alafouzos & family
about: Giannis Alafouzos is the founder and chairman of Okeanis Eco Tankers, an Athens-based shipping company that owns 15 oil tankers.
He founded the firm in 2018 and took it public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2023.
Alongside his brother Themistocles, he co-owns Kyklades Maritime Corporation, an Athens-based shipping firm with 24 vessels.
He's also the president and majority owner of Skai Group, a Greek media conglomerate with interests in TV, radio stations and news sites.
Alafouzos is also the president and majority owner of Greek soccer team Panathinaikos.

name: Regina Helena S. Velloso
about: Regina Helena S. Velloso derives her fortune from Votorantim, one of Brazil's largest conglomerates.
Votorantim traces its roots to Velloso's grandfather who bought a textile factory in Sao Paulo in 1918.
Velloso's mother, Maria Helena Moraes Scripilliti, held aobut 25% of the company following her husband's death and before splitting her stake to her four children.
Velloso's siblings, Carlos Eduardo Scripilliti and Clóvis Ermírio de Moraes are also billionaires. The four sibling, a step-sister, split her stake among her three children.
Velloso's father, Clovis Scripilliti, helped expand Votorantim throughout northeast Brazil in the 1960s and 1970s.

name: Carlos Eduardo M. Scripilliti
about: Carlos Eduardo M. Scripilliti is an heir to the Votorantim empire, one of Brazil's largest and oldest conglomerates with interests in aluminum, pulp and paper, energy, agriculture and cement.
He is the third generation member of the family business which was started by his grandfather, Jose Ermirio de Moraes, in 1918.
Today, the group, which traces its roots to a textile factory in Sao Paulo, operates in 20 countries.
Scripilliti's siblings, Clóvis Ermírio de Moraes and Regina Helena S. Velloso, are also billionaires; the trio inherited their fortune from their mother Maria Helena Moraes Scripilliti.
did_you_know_facts: Scripilliti's uncle, Antonio Ermirio ran to become governor of Sao Paulo, Brazil's richest state. He did not win. He died in 2014.

name: Clóvis Ermírio de Moraes
about: Clóvis Ermírio de Moraes, is an heir to the Brazilian industrial conglomerate Votorantim, which was founded by his grandfather Jose Ermirio de Moraes.
The Votorantim fortune dates back to 1918, when Jose bought a textile factory in Sao Paulo.
Clóvis' mother, Maria Helena Moraes Scripilliti, held 25% of the company before giving the stakes to her four children.
The Votorantim group operates in more than 20 countries and has interests in aluminum, pulp and paper, energy, cement and banking.
He has held positions in the group since 1980 and is a director at Hejoassu Administracao, the family's holding company.

name: Aidyn Rakhimbayev
about: Aidyn Rakhimbayev is the co-founder and major shareholder of BI Group, the largest real estate development and construction groups in Kazakhstan.
He founded BI in 1988, growing its opertations to include commercial real estate, education infrastructure, and multi-used urban development projects.
BI Group operates projects in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, the U.S., the UAE, and Azerbaijan.
Rakhimbayev also co-foudned the educational project IQanat, which was the subject of a Harvard Business School case study.

personal_stats.label: Source of Wealth
personal_stats.value: Real estate and construction, Self Made

did_you_know_facts: Rakhimbayev completed triathlons at the 2016 Ironman Barcelona and 2017 Ironman Copenhagen.

name: Eddy Sugianto
about: Eddy Sugianto is the founder of coal mining group Mandiri and president commissioner of its Indonesia-listed Prima Andalan Mandiri.
He took Prima Andalan Mandiri public in 2021, raising $32 million.
His coal services company Mandiri Herindo Adiperkasa, also known as Mandiri Services, raised $31 million through an IPO in 2023.
Eddy's brother Handy Glivirgo is the president director of Prima Andalan Mandiri and a director of Mandiri Services.

name: Nguyen Dang Quang
about: Nguyen Dang Quang invested in commercial bank Techcombank in 1993 and later founded Masan Group with business partner, Ho Hung Anh, in 2004.
Masan Group has interests in a wide range of consumer and food product businesses, ranging from animal feeds to food processing.
While Ho Hung Anh, who is chairman of Techcombank, is in charge of the bank, Nguyen is focused on building Masan Group as its chairman.
In 2023, Bain Capital led a $500 million funding round in Masan, the global private equity giant's first-ever investment in Vietnam.

Techcom Securities, the brokerage arm of Techcombank, went public on the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange in October 2025. Masan Consumer, the group's consumer goods unit, listed on the bourse two months later.
did_you_know_facts: Nguyen Dang Quang belongs to the wave of Vietnamese students who studied in Russia and Eastern Europe in the 1980s, after the Vietnam War.
He returned to Vietnam and worked for Vietnam's Academy of Sciences before joining the private sector in the 1990s.

name: Tseng Sing-ai
about: Tseng Sing-ai inherited her Chang Chun Group stake from her father, Tseng Shin-yi, who died in 2016.
Shin-yi cofounded the business in 1949 with classmates M.K. Liao and Lin Shu-hong.
Chang Chun is now one of Asia's largest petrochemicals-and-plastics manufacturers, with plants in Taiwan, mainland China and Southeast Asia.

name: Anton Fedun
about: Anton Fedun is the son of Russian billionaire Leonid Fedun, whose fortune is derived from Lukoil, Russia's second-largest oil producer.
His father became one of the controlling shareholders of the company in the 1990s, during the murky privatization of state-owned businesses.
In 2018 his father transferred part of his ownership in Lukoil to him and his sister Ekaterina, a fellow billionaire.
He also owns luxury hotels in London: The Ampersand Hotel and Vintry & Mercer.
Fedun holds dual citizenship in Russia and the U.K., and resides in London.
did_you_know_facts: His wife Alina Uspenskaya was a contestant in the country's beauty pageant Miss Russian Radio.

name: Valery Kustov
about: Valery Kustov is the founder of EFKO, one of the largest Russian food companies with annual sales about $4 billion.

Kustov, along with partners, took control of a small perfume and essential oil producer during privatization in Russia in the 1990s, later rebranding the business to produce sunflower oil and mayonnaise.
EFKO now produces industrial fats, egg products, sunflower oil, sauces, soap and biotechnology products like sweet proteins.
In 2025 EFKO bought former oil-seed assets of US food company Bunge in Russia.

name: Guillermo Fierro
about: Guillermo Fierro derives his fortune from a network of banks primarily in Latin America.
He is the son of Ignacio Fierro, a second-generation heir to a banking family who started its expansion in the region.
Fierro is an avid vintage car racing and competes in several races across Europe.

name: Markus Hannebauer
about: Markus Hannebauer co-founded think-cell, a German software company, along with his partner Arno Schodl.
The partners founded the business in 2002, growing to more than 50,000 users and winning the Berlin Startup award for that year.
Hannebauer holds a Phd with a specialization in artificial intelligence and shares a 30% stake in the company along with Shodl.
Think-cell, which sold a majority stake to PE firm Cinven in 2021, specializes data visualization tools for the creation of PowerPoint presentations.

name: Arno Schodl
about: Arno Schodl co-founded think-cell, a German software company, along with his partner Markus Hannebauer.
The partners founded the business in 2002, growing to more than 50,000 users and winning the Berlin Startup award for that year.
Schodl holds a Phd with a specialization in computer graphics and shares a 30% stake in the company along with Hannebauer.
Think-cell, which sold a majority stake to PE firm Cinven in 2021, specializes data visualization tools for the creation of PowerPoint presentations.

name: Hong Seok-joh
about: Hong Seok-joh heads BGF Retail, one of Korea's largest convenience store companies.
Operating under the brand name CU, BGF boasts more than 18,000 stores.
His sister, Hong Ra-hee, is the widow of the late Samsung Group chairman Lee Kun-hee.
Prior to his start in the business, Hong was a prosecutor.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Laws, Harvard University; Law Degree, Seoul National University

did_you_know_facts: The business got its start in 1989 via a franchise-licensing agreement between the Hong family's Bokwang Group and Japanese convenience store operator FamilyMart.
His late father was the chairman of JoongAng Ilbo, one of South Korea's largest newspapers.

name: Hua Shen
about: Hua Shen chairs semiconductor and power module supplier StarPower Semiconductor; its products are used in the energy and machinery industries.
Shen was an engineer at Infineon Technologies and a senior program manager at Xilinx before forming StarPower in 2005.
StarPower went public at the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2020.
Shen received a MS in applied science from Yale in 1992 and a PhD from the Massachusetts Institute of Technology in 1995.
did_you_know_facts: Shen's wife Hu Wei holds a graduate degree from Stanford and U.S. citizenship; she is also a StarPower board member.

name: Alexander Rinke
about: Alexander Rinke is cofounder and co-CEO of enterprise software startup Celonis.
The Munich-based company was valued by private investors at $13 billion in 2022. Rinke owns a 15% stake.
The company disputes Forbes' valuation, which accounts for the downturn in private markets since the company's last funding round.
Rinke's cofounders Bastian Nominacher and Martin Klenk are also billionaires. Nominacher is co-CEO and Klenk is CTO.
Celonis' cofounders launched the company in 2011 after graduating from Technical University of Munich.

name: Qin Long
about: Qin Long chairs Qingdao Sentury Tire, a supplier of motorsport and aircraft tires.
Qin founded Qingdao Sentury Tire in 2007.
Qingdao Sentury Tire went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2020.

name: Rui Chen
about: Chen Rui is the CEO of Bilibili, a Shanghai-headquartered online media company
Chen previously cofounded New York-listed Cheetah Mobile, a software firm.
Chen is a graduate of the Chengdu University of Information Technology.

name: Weijian Shan
about: Weijian Shan is the chairman of PAG, an Asia-focused private equity firm with $50 billion in assets under management.
Before founding PAG's private equity business in 2010, he worked for 12 years at TPG Capital and was the U.S. private equity giant's top China dealmaker.
At TPG, Shan spearheaded the first purchase of a state-owned Chinese bank by a foreign investor.
In 2022, Shan became an independent director of Alibaba. He also served on the boards of Wilmar International, Bank of China (Hong Kong), Baosteel and Lenovo.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of San Francisco; Master of Economics, University of California, Berkeley; Doctorate, University of California, Berkeley

did_you_know_facts: The Beijing-born grew up during the Cultural Revolution and labored in northern China's Gobi Desert.
His memoir, published in 2019, is called Out of the Gobi: My Story of China and America.
He earned a Ph.D. in business administration from UC Berkeley, where U.S. Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen was one of Shan's thesis advisors.

name: Jerry Seinfeld
about: Jerry Seinfeld is the co-creator and star of the 1990s-era sitcom, "Seinfeld", which was broadcast on NBC for nine seasons and is now airing in syndication.
Seinfeld and co-creator Larry David reportedly earn 15% of the show's syndication revenue, which includes sales to local television stations and streaming platforms.
His fortune comes form his share of the syndication revenue the show generates, as well as income from touring, films and other projects.
Seinfeld's work outside of "Seinfeld" includes Netflix comedy specials, Comedians In Cars Getting Coffee, Bee Movie and Unfrosted, a film about the Pop Tart.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, City University of New York Queens

name: James Cameron
about: James Cameron has directed three of the four highest-grossing movies of all time in 'Titanic,' 'Avatar' and 'Avatar: The Way of Water.' In total, his films have grossed almost $9 billion at the global box office.
Cameron's big break came with 1984's 'The Terminator,' a script he sold for $1 with the promise that he'd be allowed to direct.
At the 1998 Academy Awards, Cameron won Best Director, Best Editing and Best Picture for 'Titanic,' quoting his own movie from the stage: "I'm the king of the world!"

On the production of 'Avatar,' Cameron developed--often at his own expense--new film technology such as a 3D camera system, head rigs for facial capture technology and a simulcam system that allowed him to see his actors rendered in digital environments in real time.
When 'Avatar' earned nearly $3 billion at the box office, and millions more in DVD sales and streaming, Cameron earned an estimated $350 million before taxes and fees.
Cameron is also a renowned deep sea adventurer, making several dives to the real life Titanic crash site and becoming the first solo expeditioner to travel to the lowest point of the Mariana Trench.
did_you_know_facts: Dozens of UK celebrities, including David Beckham, Sacha Baron Cohen, Peter Gabriel and Guy Ritchie, collectively earned millions as investors in 'Avatar.'

name: Jane Goldman
about: Jane Goldman is America's only female billionaire running a real estate firm. She heads up Solil Management, which she owns with her three siblings.
The youngest daughter of Sol Goldman (d. 1987), once New York's biggest landlord, she oversees a portfolio that includes at least 400 properties.
Trophies include apartments on the Upper East Side and the block of land in Midtown Manhattan that includes the Olympic Tower and the Cartier Mansion.
The family also owns a 17% stake in the World Trade Center developments in lower Manhattan.
Her brother Allan is co-chair but has taken a back seat in recent years. Her sisters Amy and Diane Kemper are senior advisers.
did_you_know_facts: The New York City resident paid $31 million in 2015 for a Palm Beach estate originally owned by the Kennedys; she sold it for $70 million in June 2020.
The Goldman family name is all over Yale University, from the law library named after Jane's mother, Lilian, to a $10 million endowed professorship.

name: Wu Jinzi
about: Jinzi Wu is the founder, chairman and CEO of Ascletis Pharma
Wu served as vice president at GSK R&D in USA before founding the company.
Ascletis Pharma listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2018.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctorate, University of Arizona; Master, Nanjing University

name: Zuo Jing
about: Zuo Jing is vice chairman of Leader Harmonious Drive Systems, which makes harmonic reducers - the "joints" of robots.
Known also as Leaderdrive, the Suzhou-based company is China's largest manufacturer of harmonic reducers by market cap, with customers such as domestic humanoid company UBTech Robotics.
In February 2026, Leaderdrive agreed to set up a joint venture with Taiwan's auto-parts supplier Minth Group in the U.S. to develop joint modules for humanoids.
Jing joined Leaderdrive in 2014, three years after his younger brother Yuyu, now chairman, founded the company.
Prior to Leaderdrive, Jing worked at several government taxation bureaus.

name: Zuo Yuyu
about: Zuo Yuyu is founder and chairman of Leader Harmonious Drive Systems, which makes harmonic reducers - the "joints" of robots.
Known also as Leaderdrive, the Suzhou-based company is China's largest manufacturer of harmonic reducers by market cap, with customers such as domestic humanoid company UBTech Robotics.
In February 2026, Leaderdrive agreed to set up a joint venture with Taiwan's auto-parts supplier Minth Group in the U.S. to develop joint modules for humanoids.
Yuyu founded Leaderdrive in 2011 with the aim of making more affordable robotics components.
His brother Jing serves as Leaderdrive's vice chairman.

name: Lou Guoqiang
about: Lou Guoqiang derives his fortune from Ningbo Jintian Copper, a supplier of copper rod and other copper products.
Lou formerly chaired the company before his son Lou Cheng took over the role in 2022.
The company, which was founded in 1986, provides integrated copper solutions for rail transit, power IoT and smart-city development. Its business spans more than 100 countries and regions.

name: Prayudh Mahagitsiri
about: Thai coffee magnate Prayudh Mahagitsiri's Quality Coffee Products was a long-standing joint venture with Nestle, which was terminated n December 2024.

In a case filed by Prayudh, a Thai civil court ordered Nestlé in April 2025 to suspend production, distribution and import of Nescafé instant coffee in Thailand. The order was reversed by a ruling of a specialized court.
Prayudh also has interests in steel, copper, shipping, offshore drilling and property development.
His son Chalermchai, a Boston University grad, is CEO of holding outfit PM Group.
His daughter Ausana is the chief operating officer of the PM Group and founder of Coffee Gallery, a chain of cafes.
did_you_know_facts: Prayudh's grandfather emigrated from southern China to Thailand, where he began trading foodstuffs and later imported Japanese-made tuk-tuks.
Prayudh sells and markets P80, a food supplement that's made from the Longan fruit.
The Mahagitsiri family has various franchises in Thailand including Pizza Hut, Taco Bell and Krispy Kreme.
In May 2025 he was given a 24-year sentence by a Thai court in an alleged land-grabbing case. He said he will file an appeal .
quote: When you have stake in a company it's your baby. You have to take more care of your baby. It's your blood in it.

name: Dylan Field
about: Dylan Field is cofounder and CEO of design software company Figma, which went public on the New York Stock Exchange in July 2025.
Figma listed its shares at a fully diluted valuation (including outstanding equity awards) of nearly $20 billion. Its stock price more than tripled on its first trading day.
Figma had previously agreed to be acquired by Adobe for $20 billion in September 2022, but the deal was scrapped in December 2023 over regulatory concerns.
Field launched Figma in 2012 with Brown University classmate Evan Wallace, after being awarded a Thiel Fellowship to drop out and work on the startup full-time.
Figma's largest investors include Index Ventures, Greylock Partners, Kleiner Perkins, and Sequoia Capital.

name: Colette Kress
about: Colette Kress is executive vice president and chief financial officer of Nvidia.
Kress first joined the company in 2013, reportedly after the endorsement of her two sons, who knew of Nvidia because of the chips in their favorite video games.
Before joining Nvidia, Kress spent three years as chief financial officer of a Cisco division; before that, she worked for 13 years at Microsoft.
Nvidia became the first ever company to achieve a market cap of $5 trillion in 2025.

name: Li San Yim
about: Li San Yim chairs Longkin Holdings, a construction equipment manufacturer in China.
Li holds an executive MBA from Fudan University in Shanghai.
Li's wife, Ngai Ngan Ying, is non-executive director of the company.

name: Anatoly Skurov
about: Anatoly Skurov's fortune stems from the sale of his stakes in coal producer Sibuglemet and fertilizer maker Uralkali, which is traded in Moscow.
He is a former designer of Soviet machine-building factories and worked for the state-owned coal producer Rosugol, where he took part in the reform of the Russian coal industry.
In 1995, with Vladimir Melnichenko and Valentin Bukhtoyarov, both former billionaires, he founded the coal producer Sibuglemet.
In 2017 Skurov started coal mining project Uvalnaya, which produces more than 6 million tons of coal annually.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Tula Polytechnical Institute

name: Joe Agresti
about: Joe Agresti sells 20,000 Mercedes-Benzes a year through Dream Motor Group, the dealership chain he owns alongside legendary football coach Nick Saban.
Agresti grew up in working-class New Jersey, studied accounting at Rutgers on a partial wrestling scholarship, then did stints at Big Six firm Arthur Andersen and auto dealer giant Asbury Automotive.
At age 31, he used his $200,000 life savings, a mortgage against his parents' house and a $500,000 loan to invest in his first car dealership, Mercedes-Benz of Baton Rouge.
He met Saban through Mercedes in 2013. They now runs nine Merecedes, Infiniti and Ferrari dealership locations in Alabama, Florida, Louisiana, Tennessee and Texas.
He splits his time traveling between homes he keeps near all his dealerships.
Agresti oversees the day-to-day operations and owns majority stakes in the dealerships, though Saban is a full minority partner. The two speak upwards of three times a day.
did_you_know_facts: Agresti has worked with Senator Bernie Moreno to help shape automotive policy and says he might one day run for federal office himself.
Agresti, Saban and their third partner, former Mercedes-Benz USA CEO Steve Cannon, own a fledgling Kentucky distillery, Slow Pass Bourbon.
quote: My mentality has always been, 'I've never done it, but I'm good at it.'

name: Paritosh Garg
about: Paritosh Garg is the chairman of Happy Forgings, which he founded in the northern Indian city of Ludhiana in 1979.
The company produces parts such as crankshafts and axles for a range of industries from automobiles to oil and gas to wind energy.
Happy Forgings got listed in December 2023 at an 18% premium to its IPO price.
His son Ashish Garg, an engineering graduate from the University of Warwick, is the company's managing director.

name: Tulay Kazanci
about: Tulay Kazanci is member of the board of directors at =family-owned Kazancı Holding, one of Turkey's largest energy companies.
The $3.6 billion (revenue) company operates across the energy industry, including electricity generation and distribution, natural gas distribution and generator production.
Kazanci started the energy business in 1968 with the Watt Electric Motor Factory.
Kazancı Holding expanded its tourism business in the city of Bodrum, in 2022, with the 5-star Mirada Exclusive Hotel. It currently owns four hotels.

name: Qi Xiangdong
about: Qi Xiangdong chairs Qi An Xin Technology Group, which supplies cybersecurity products and services to government and businesses.
Qi An Xin listed on China's STAR Market in July 2020.
He founded the company in 2014.
Earlier, Qi cofounded 360 Security Technology with fellow China billionaire Zhou Hongyi.
Qi Xiangdong was previously a vice president at Yahoo China.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Beijing University of Science and Technology; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Changchun College of Posts and Telecommunications

name: Naresh Trehan
about: Naresh Trehan, one of India's top cardiac surgeons, founded the Medanta hospital chain in 2007 with one hospital in Delhi.
He is chairman, managing director and chief cardiac surgeon at Medanta, which offers services across more than 30 specialties including cardiology, neurology and oncology.
Medanta has six hospitals across North India with more than 3,500 hospital beds
He listed Global Health, the parent company of Medanta, on the Indian bourses in 2022.
did_you_know_facts: Trehan is a recipient of the Padma Bhushan and the Padma Shri, among India's highest civilian honours.
Medanta is building four hospitals including a 400-bed super specialty hospital in south Delhi.

name: Sachin Agarwal
about: Sachin Agarwal is the chairman of PTC Industries, which makes precision stainless steel castings for the power, aerospace and oil and gas sectors.
The business has its roots in an engineering foundry started by his father Sateesh Agarwal in 1963.
Agarwal has a master's degree in finance from Boston College and an MBA from the University of Tulsa in Oklahoma.
His wife Smita is the company's chief financial officer.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, University of Tulsa; Masters in Finance, Boston College

did_you_know_facts: The original name of the company was Precision Tools and Castings.
PTC Industries uses robots and 3D printing in its manufacturing processes.

name: Kanjibhai Virani
about: Kanjibhai Virani is the cofounder of Indian snacks maker Balaji Wafers, which sells a range of items including packaged snacks, noodles and confectionery.

Virani and his two brothers Bhikhabhai and Chandubhai, who help him run the company, entered the three comma club after selling a minority stake to private equity giant General Atlantic in January 2026.
Before starting Balaji Wafers, the brothers were doing odd jobs at Astron Cinemas in the town of Rajkot in the western Indian state of Gujarat.
The name "Balaji" was inspired by a temple in their hometown.

name: Chandubhai Virani
about: Chandubhai Virani is the cofounder of Indian snacks maker Balaji Wafers, which sells a range of items including packaged snacks, noodles and confectionery.

Virani and his two brothers Bhikhabhai and Kanjibhai, who help him run the company, entered the three comma club after selling a minority stake to private equity giant General Atlantic in January 2026.
Before starting Balaji Wafers, the brothers were doing odd jobs at Astron Cinemas in the town of Rajkot in the western Indian state of Gujarat.
The name "Balaji" was inspired by a temple in their hometown.

name: Ekaterina Fedun
about: Ekaterina Fedun is the daughter of Russian billionaire Leonid Fedun, whose fortune stems from Russia's second-largest oil company.
Her father became a controlling shareholder of Lukoil during the 1990s when state-owned companies were being privatized.
In 2018 the elder Fedun transferred part of his stake to Ekaterina and her brother Anton, a fellow billionaire.
Ekaterina is not involved in the business; Anton manages a fund that owns Lukoil.
In 2014 she married the manager of the Spartak Moscow football club, which is owned by the company.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master, Moscow State Institute of International Relations

name: Vijay Shekhar Sharma
about: Son of a schoolteacher from a small city in north India, Vijay Shekhar Sharma founded mobile wallet Paytm in 2011.
One of the biggest beneficiaries of India's 2016 demonetization, Paytm has notched up more than 540 million users with 46 million daily active users.
Sharma made a splash in August 2018 by getting Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway to invest $300 million in Paytm.
In August 2025, Antfin (Netherlands), an affiliate of China's Alibaba Group, sold its entire stake in Paytm.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Delhi University

did_you_know_facts: Sharma dreams of starting a band that sings in Sanskrit, a language he studied in school.
Paytm is an acronym for "pay through mobile."

name: Qian Jinghong
about: Qian is co-founder and vice chairman of Yadea Group, a maker of electric scooters and bicycles.
Her husband, Yadea co-founder and vice chairman Dong Jinggui, is also a billionaire.
Yadea went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2016.

name: Andrii Verevskyi
about: Andrii Verevskyi is chairman and founder of Kernel Holding, an agricultural group based in Kyiv, Ukraine.
In 2010, Kernel became the biggest producer and exporter of sunflower oil in the country. In 2012, it accounted for 12% of world's sunflower oil exports.
Verevskyi took the company public in Warsaw in 2007. Since then, Verevskyi has been buying back shares, going from 38.05% to over a 95% stake in 2025, initiating a de-listing process.
In 2002, Verevskyi was elected to Ukraine's Parliament; he changed 4 party factions and acted as an advisor to the prime minister before leaving politics in 2013.
Kernel was founded in 2004 by combining several agricultural companies. At the outset, the company was in the grain exports business; it gradually grew into an agricultural and food processing group.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, National Agricultural University

name: Ana Maria Marcondes Penido Sant'Anna
about: Ana Maria Marcondes Penido Sant'Anna is vice president of the board of directors of CCR, a Brazilian toll road builder and operator.
CCR was founded by her late father Pelerson Soares Penido, and became one of Latin America's largest infrastructure concession companies.
CCR also owns a stake in STP, an electronic payment system for toll operators similar to E-Z Pass in the United States.
The company trades on Brazil's Bovespa exchange; she owns about 10% of the shares.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Universidade Presbiteriana Mackenzie

did_you_know_facts: The low profile billionaire lives in Sao Paulo, Brazil's largest city, and is a member of the board of ITACI, the Child Cancer Treatment Institute.

name: Eugene MIkhaylov
about: Eugene Mikhaylov inherited his fortune from his father, Igor Babaev, former managing director Cherkizovsky, a formerly state-owned meat-packing plant in Moscow.
Babaev became controlling shareholder of Cherkizovsky during Russia's privatization era in the 1990s, later adding pig and poultry farms, feed mills and other meat-packing plants.
Cherkizovo is now the largest meat producer in Russia, with 360,000 hectares (about 900,000 acres) of agricultural land.
Babaev retired from business in 2015 and gifted the shares to his two sons and ex-wife, who relinquished her shares in 2022.
Mikhaylov was elected the Chairman of Cherkizovo Group in 2016.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Economics, University of California at Los Angeles

name: Sergey Mikhaylov
about: Sergey Mikhaylov inherited his fortune from his father, Igor Babaev, former managing director Cherkizovsky, a formerly state-owned meat-packing plant in Moscow.
Babaev became controlling shareholder of Cherkizovsky during Russia's privatization era in the 1990s, later adding pig and poultry farms, feed mills and other meat-packing plants.
Cherkizovo is now the largest meat producer in Russia, with 360,000 hectares (about 900,000 acres) of agricultural land.
Babaev retired from business in 2015 and gifted the shares to his two sons and ex-wife, who relinquished her shares in 2022.
Mikhaylov had internships with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley (USA) in the early 2000s.

name: Dou Zhenggang
about: Dou Zhenggang chairs Hangzhou Jinjiang Group, a company whose businesses include environmental protection and energy.
Other Jinjiang businesses span trade, logistics and non-ferrous metals.
Dou made his early fortune in textiles, starting his first business in 1983 in Zhejiang Province.

name: Cho Hyun-sang
about: Cho Hyun-sang is the youngest son of Cho Seok-rae, the late former chairman of Hyosung, who stepped down in 2016 and passed away in 2024.
He is vice chairman of the industrial conglomerate, while his brother Hyun-joon is chairman.
Hyun-sang worked with global consulting firm Bain & Co. before joining Hyosung in 2000.

name: Nutchamai Thanombooncharoen
about: Nutchamai Thanombooncharoen is cofounder and chairman of SET-listed Carabao Group, maker of energy drink Carabao Dang.
Nutchamai branched out from her family's financial services business to team up with Sathien Sathientham for a property venture before jointly setting up Carabao.
In 2002, they partnered with popular folk singer Aed Carabao for a foray into energy drinks.
Top international markets for Carabao include Cambodia, China, Myanmar, Vietnam and Afghanistan.
In 2023, she got into beer brewing through Tawandang Brewery in partnership with Sathien.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Economics, Silpakorn University; Master of Arts, Thammasat University

did_you_know_facts: She also has a stake in Tawandang Distillery, which makes rice whisky.
In 2020, Carabao launched a new vitamin C-infused drink called Woody C+ Lock in orange and lemon flavors.

name: Cai Hongbin
about: Cai Hongbin's fortune comes from his stake in Jiangsu Hengrui Medicine.
Jiangsu Hengrui is one of China's largest pharmaceutical companies, employing more than 20,000 people.
Fellow Chinese billionaire Sun Piaoyang is Hengrui's chairman.

name: Lee Sang-hoon
about: Lee Sang-hoon is the founder, chairman, CEO and chief research officer of South Korean biotechnology company ABL Bio.
ABL Bio develops bispecific antibodies, which target two molecules simultaneously to improve treatment outcomes for cancer and neurodegenerative diseases.
In November 2025, it signed a $2.6 billion technology-transfer deal with Eli Lilly related to ABL Bio's Grabody-B blood-brain-barrier-penetrating bispecific antibody technology.
Lee founded ABL Bio in 2016 and listed it on Korea's Kosdaq stock exchange two years later.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science, Seoul National University; Master of Science, Seoul National University; Ph.D, Ohio State University

name: Cai Wensheng
about: Cai Wensheng is the founder and chairman of Meitu, a Chinese photo-touch-up app created to improve selfies.
Meitu also sells smartphones with large pixel cameras.
Cai is an angel investor in Chinese startups.

name: Wang Jinhua
about: Wang Junmin chairs China Kings Resources, which sells fluorite products and develops fluorite mines.
Wang is a member of China's Communist Party.
China Kings is headquartered in the eastern Chinese city of Hangzhou.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science, China University of Mining and Technology; Bachelor of Science, University of Science and Technology Beijing

name: Tsai Cheng-Chiu
about: Tsai Cheng-chiu is a director of Cathay Financial Holdings, a leading financial services company in Taiwan.
The company made his father, Tsai Wan-lin, Taiwan's wealthiest man before he died in 2004.
Half-brothers Cheng-ta and Hong-tu are billionaires, as are their cousins Richard and Daniel Tsai.

name: William Fung
about: William Fung and his older brother Victor own a significant stake in Li & Fung, which operates as a middleman between global manufacturers and retailers in the U.S. and Europe.
William stepped down as chairman of Li & Fung in 2020 when Victor's son, Spencer, took the helm.
In 2020 Li & Fung was privatized through a deal worth $930 million.
In 2022, Danish shipping giant A.P. Moller-Maersk acquired the brothers' logistics business, LF Logistics, for $3.4 billion.
Their grandfather, Fung Pak-liu, founded Li & Fung with partner Li To-ming in 1906, exporting porcelain and silk.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Harvard University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Princeton University

name: Michael Novogratz
about: Mike Novogratz is the founder, CEO and majority shareholder of Galaxy Digital Holdings, a crypto investment firm that trades on the Toronto Stock Exchange.
He began his career at Goldman Sachs in 1989, where he spent a decade and became a partner while the firm was still privately held.
Novogratz went on to work at private equity firm Fortress Investment Group, becoming its president.
He first bought bitcoin in 2013, and has since invested in a range of startups and tokens within the cryptocurrency industry.
His most notorious failure was betting big on Luna, a token tied to stablecoin TerraUSD, which blew up in 2022. Novogratz had tattooed its logo on his arm.

name: Bruce Mathieson
about: Bruce Mathieson operates his poker machine and pub empire Australian Liquor and Hospitality in a joint venture with supermarket giant Woolworths.
Mathieson is now a minority shareholder in the listed Endeavour Group, which holds both the Australian Liquor assets and Woolworth's extensive liquor retailing business.
In a board shakeup in 2024, Endeavour's chairman resigned as well as Mathieson's son, Bruce Mathieson Jr., who had a board seat.
He has a fondness for racehorses and part-owned a horse that ran in the Melbourne Cup.
He is battling a rare form of blood cancer.
did_you_know_facts: Bruce Mathieson has partnered with U.S. gambling giant Bally's to rescue financially-challenged Australian casino operator, The Star Entertainment Group.

name: Carl-Anton Kunz
about: Carl Kunz is a shareholder of Cordes & Graefe, the parent company of the GC Group, a wholesaler that covers a wide range of products for plumbing and HVAC systems.
Founded in 1921 as a pipe and tube trading company, Cordes & Graefe formed the GC Group in 1975 through a series of acquisitions.
Today the company is one of the largest wholesalers in the industry with $17 billion in sales (2023).
The company is 100% owned by the Hollweg family. Carl Kunz is the grandson of longtime company leader Uwe Hollweg who died in December 2024.

name: Bhaskara Rao Bollineni
about: Cardiothoracic surgeon Bhaskara Rao Bollineni founded KIMS Hospitals in 2000 with a 200-bed hospital in his home town of Nellore in southern India.
The company owns and operates 25 hospitals with a total of 8,300 beds across the states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Kerala.
The older of his two sons, Abhinay, who's also a doctor, is chief executive while the younger son Adwik is has a board seat.
Its flagship hospital in the southern city of Secundraabad has 1,000 beds.
Bollineni has performed more than 30,000 surgeries over a career spanning nearly three decades.

name: Hans Langer
about: Hans Langer is the world's first 3-D printing billionaire.
Langer founded EOS, one of the earliest and most successful 3-D printing companies, more than 30 years ago.
Daughter Marie Langer took over as CEO of the largest operating business, EOS GmbH, which makes 3D printers for polymers and metals, in October 2019.
While others focused on consumers and 3-D printing, Langer always believed that the technology's true value was in industrial applications.
Venture capital firms have plowed funds into American 3D printing startups, but the Langer family has turned down investments and sales offers.
did_you_know_facts: Langer's first customer was BMW, which bet on EOS before it even had a product available.
He has turned down multiple, multi-billion-dollar acquisition offers, insistent that the business stay in the family so that he can run it as he wishes.

name: Li Xuechun
about: Li Xuechun is chairman and executive director of Fufeng Group, primarily a supplier of bio-fermentation products, with other interests including mining, real estate and finance.
His son, Li Guangyu, serves as executive director of the company.
Li took the company public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2007.

name: Quek Leng Chye
about: Quek Leng Chye is managing director of Hong Leong Holdings, a property development and investment arm of diversified conglomerate Hong Leong Group.
His brother, Malaysian billionaire Quek Leng Chan, is the executive chairman of Hong Leong Co. (Malaysia), which has interests in finance, food and property.
His cousin, Kwek Leng Beng, serves as chairman of Hong Leong Group in Singapore and is also a billionaire.

name: Xie Juhua & family
about: Xie Juhua is a director and the largest individual shareholder at Kingfriend, a pharmaceuticals supplier.
Kingfriend's main products include cardiovascular and anti-tumor drugs.
Xie's son Tang Yongqun chairs Kingfriend.

name: Ryuji Arai
about: Ryuji Arai started Bic Camera, the electronics and appliances retailing giant, in 1978.
The company posted over $6 billion in revenue in the fiscal year through August 2025.
Arai also owns stakes in temporary staffing firm Hit Communications Holdings and contact lens-maker Seed.
did_you_know_facts: Bic Camera owns a majority stake in listed satellite TV network Nippon BS Broadcasting.

name: Chen Huwen
about: Chen Huwen is the chairman and a co-founder of Shanghai M&G Stationary Inc.
M&G Stationary was founded in 1996.
Chen holds an EMBA degree and has been involved in stationery manufacturing since 1997.

name: Keiko Erikawa
about: Keiko Erikawa cofounded videogame developer Koei in 1978 with her husband Yoichi Erikawa.
The company, now called Koei Tecmo Holdings, trades on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
The founders are stepping away from executive roles. Starting April, Yoichi, who is now CEO, will become chairman; and Keiko, who is now chairman, will become chairman emeritus.
The company is known for its Samurai Warrior games.
In 2021, Keiko Erikawa was appointed as an independent director of SoftBank Group. She's the only woman to sit on the company's board.

name: Alexander Mikhalskiy
about: Alexander Mikhalskiy is a cofounder of Sportmaster, Russia's largest sports and fashion retailer, which he started with brothers Nikolay and Vladimir Fartushnyak.
He also cofounded Ostin, a Russian fast-fashion retailer, with the brothers, both of whom are billionaires.
In the early 1990s Mikhalskiy and his partners had a distribution business that supplied French consumer goods to the Russian market.
They later became the exclusive distributor for German sports retailer Kettler and opened the first Sportmaster store in 1997.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Science in Engineering, Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology

name: Fritz Draexlmaier
about: Fritz Draexlmaier's eponymous auto parts maker counts among its customers Audi, BMW, Cadillac, Land Rover, Maserati, Mercedes-Benz, Porsche and Tesla.
Founded by his parents, Draexlmaier Group began in 1958 with an order for wiring harnesses for the Goggomobil, a microcar produced by Hans Glas GmbH.
A company speciality, wiring harnesses run throughout the entire vehicle connecting electrical components and relaying data and electrical power.
It has diversified into the manufacture of electronic components, consoles, door and instrument panels and exclusive interiors for specific model
Although he stepped down as CEO in early 2019, Fritz continues to serve as chairman and shareholder representative.
Draexlmaier has more than 65,000 employees and 60 business sites across 20 countries.
did_you_know_facts: Fritz is an only child. His father, Fritz Sr., died in 1995 at age 80, and his mom, Lisa, died in 2018 at age 100.
In 2017, Draexlmaier Group opened its first U.S. manufacturing site in Livermore, California, with 230 employees.

name: Lu Zhongfang
about: Lu Zhongfang retired from a pesticides factory in northern China's Jilin Province in 1993 and invested in test preparation firm Offcn in 1999.
Lu's son Liu Yongxin chairs Offcn and is also a billionaire.
Offcn Education Technology completed a backdoor listing at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2019.

name: Yang Min & family
about: Yang Min is the founder and former chairman of China Hanking Holdings, an iron ore mining and processing company.
Yang took China Hanking public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in 2011.
Yang's son, Yang Jiye, is chairman, CEO and president of the company.

name: Yoichi Erikawa
about: Yoichi Erikawa cofounded videogame developer Koei more than four decades ago with his wife Keiko Erikawa.
The company, now called Koei Tecmo Holdings, trades on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
The founders are stepping away from executive roles. Starting April, Yoichi, who is now CEO, will become chairman; and Keiko, who is now chairman, will become chairman emeritus.
The company is known for its Samurai Warrior games.
Hisashi Koinuma, currently executive vice president, is set to become president and CEO in June.

name: Diamantis Diamantides & family
about: Diamantis Diamantides owns Greek shipping firms Delta Tankers and Marmaras Navigation.
He founded Marmaras Navigation in 1976 and started Delta Tankers in 2006. Together, the firms own 55 tankers and bulk carriers.
His son Paschalis founded his own firm, Velos, in 2019. Velos owns 14 tankers and dry cargo ships.
Diamantides also owns large land holdings in the Astir peninsula, a wealthy enclave south of Athens on the Aegean coast.

name: Chang Kuo-Cheng
about: Chang Kuo-Cheng is the third son of shipping tycoon Chang Yung Fa, who died in 2016 at the age of 88.
In 1968 Yung Fa founded Evergreen Marine, now one of the world's largest transportation companies.
Brothers Kuo-Hua, Kuo-Ming and Kuo-Cheng also inherited stakes in EVA Airways and hotels in Taiwan, mainland China, Paris and Bangkok.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Business Administration, Boston University

name: Michele Kang
about: Michele Kang founded healthcare information technology firm Cognosante in 2008, which she sold to Accenture in 2024.
Born in South Korea, Kang moved to the United States for college and earned a bachelor's degree in economics from The University of Chicago and a master's degree from Yale.
She owns majority stakes in the NWSL's Washington Spirit, France's OL Lyonnes and England's London City Lionesses, which recently earned promotion to the Women's Super League.
She also has a stake in John Textor's Eagle Football Holdings, which controls three other European clubs, one in Florida and one in Brazil.
In 2024, Kang launched Kynisca, the world's first multi-team global organization focused on professionalizing women's football, and proving its commercial potential and cultural impact.
did_you_know_facts: Kang is the first woman of color to be the majority owner of a National Women's Soccer League team.
Kang convinced her parents to use her wedding fund to finance her first year of college in the U.S.

name: Wu Jianbin
about: Wu Jianbin is chairman of Ningbo Shuanglin Auto Parts, which manufactures auto parts, including automobile accessories, bearings and electronic control modules.
His father Wu Yonglin founded the company in 1987 and stepped down from management in 2006 due to health reasons.
Wu Jianbin's sister Wu Weijing is a director of the company.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business

name: Wee Wei Chi
about: Wee Wei Chi is the younger daughter of late patriarch Wee Cho Yaw, cofounder of United Overseas Bank, one of Singapore's largest banks.
She sits on the board of Kheng Leong, the family's commercial property development and investment outfit.
Her husband, David Eu, is from the family that founded Eu Yan Sang, a traditional Chinese medicine company in Singapore.
She has a bachelor's degree in fine arts from Moravian University in Pennsylvania.

name: Wee Wei Ling
about: Wee Wei Ling is the eldest child of late patriarch Wee Cho Yaw, cofounder of United Overseas Bank, one of Singapore's largest banks.
She sits on the board of Kheng Leong, the family's commercial property development and investment outfit.
She is the executive director of asset, lifestyle and sustainable partnerships at Pan Pacific Hotels Group, the luxury hotel arm of the family's real estate heavyweight UOL Group.
She also manages Pan Pacific's lifestyle brands such as St. Gregory and Si Chuan Dou Hua.
She is a director of the family's philanthropic Wee Foundation.

name: Petr Bely
about: Peter Bely is the founder of Russian biopharmaceutical company Promomed.
Promomed sold shares on the Moscow Stock Exchange in July 2024, raising 6 billion rubles.
Promomed produces Kvinsenta, generic analogue to Novo Nordisk' anti-diabetic drug Ozempic.
Bely graduated from the Russian University of Medicine in 2008.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Medical Doctor, Russian University of Medicine

name: Fu Kwan
about: Born in China's Hunan Province, Fu Kwan leads Macrolink Group, which has interests in real estate, mining, petroleum, finance and more.
Fu holds a MBA from Hunan University and an EMBA from Tsinghua University.
Fu enjoys wine.
Fu started Macrolink with $1,000 after leaving a job in government.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Hunan University; EMBA, Tsinghua University

name: Andrea Della Valle
about: Andrea Della Valle and his brother, Diego, are billionaires thanks to their majority ownership of Italian luxury goods maker Tod's S.p.A.
He is the vice chairman of the global shoe- and purse-maker that his grandfather founded in the early 1900s as a small shoe factory.
In 2024, the brothers teamed up with private equity firm L Catterton and LVMH to take Tod's private at a $1.5 billion valuation.
The brothers also own stakes in Vespa-maker Piaggio and media conglomerate RCS MediaGroup.
Andrea was chairman of soccer team ACF Fiorentina until 2009, helping turn the club around after its previous owner drove it into bankruptcy.

name: Herald Chen
about: Herald Chen is a former president and chief financial officer of AI-powered advertising technology company AppLovin.
Chen became a billionaire thanks to stock options he was awarded when he joined the Palo Alto, California-based company in 2019.
As AppLovin's CFO, Chen helped the company prepare for its 2021 initial public offering on the Nasdaq.
In 2024, Chen transitioned into a new role as advisor to AppLovin's billionaire cofounder and CEO Adam Foroughi, while remaining on the company's board.
Chen previously led KKR's technology, media and telecom division for 12 years, overseeing the private equity firm's investments in AppLovin, WebMD, Eastman Kodak and more.

personal_stats.label: Source of Wealth
personal_stats.value: Marketing software, mobile games, Self Made

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Stanford University; Bachelor of Science, The University of Pennsylvania

name: Takaya Awata
about: Takaya Awata is president and CEO of Tokyo-listed Toridoll Holdings, Japan's largest operator of udon noodle restaurants.
Awata opened his first yakitori grilled-chicken restaurant in 1985, after dropping out of the Kobe City University of Foreign Studies.
Toridoll has over 2,000 restaurants in Japan, China, Singapore, Europe. and the U.S.
In 2021, the firm listed its Tam Jai International, an operator of Chinese noodle restaurants that it acquired in 2018, on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange but took it private in August 2025.
The company posted $1.9 billion in revenue in the fiscal year through March 2025, a 16% jump from the previous year.
did_you_know_facts: In February 2025, Toridoll proposed delisting Tam Jai to make it a wholly-owned subsidiary.

name: Victor Fung
about: Victor Fung and his younger brother William own a significant stake in Li & Fung, which operates as a middleman between global manufacturers and retailers in the U.S. and Europe.
Victor chaired Li & Fung until William took over in 2012. Victor's son, Spencer, became executive chairman in 2020.
In 2020 Li & Fung was privatized through a deal worth $930 million.
In 2022, Danish shipping giant A.P. Moller-Maersk acquired the brothers' logistics business, LF Logistics, for $3.4 billion.
Their grandfather, Fung Pak-liu, founded Li & Fung with partner Li To-ming in 1906 by exporting porcelain and silk.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Doctorate, Harvard University; Bachelor of Arts/Science, Massachusetts Institute of Technology

name: Xu Zhihan
about: Xu Zhihan chairs Maxscend Microelectronics, an electrical components supplier that produces products like smart phone radio frequency switches.
Maxscend was founded in 2012 by a group of Silicon Valley alums.
Xu holds master's and bachelor's degrees in computer science and technology from Tsinghua University.
He also holds master's degree in electrical engineering from Santa Clara University.

name: Rajinder Gupta
about: Rajinder Gupta is the founder of Trident, a company known for its home textiles, paper and chemicals.
The Ludhiana-based company makes bath and bed linen such as towels, duvets and fitted sheets.
Two-thirds of Trident's annual revenue is from exports to more than 150 countries.
Trident has factories in the Indian states of Punjab and Madhya Pradesh.
He resigned as chairman in 2022 citing health reasons and family issues.
did_you_know_facts: He founded it in 1990 as a yarn manufacturer.
Trident is among the top five terry towel makers in the world.

name: Luigi Cremonini & family
about: Luigi Cremonini supplies hamburger meat to McDonald's and Burger King in Italy and other countries through his privately-held Inalca SpA.
Born to poor farmers in an Italian village near Modena, Cremonini got his start by opening a small butcher shop in 1963.
Beginning in the late 1970s he diversified into cured meats, distribution and catering and within a decade expanded the business internationally.
Today Cremonini Group employs more than 19,500 workers all over the globe and generated $5.6 billion in revenues in 2022.
Its catering arm Chef Express sells food on trains in Europe, Turkey and Russia, including the Eurostar service between London and Paris.
did_you_know_facts: In 1994 the University of Bologna awarded Cremonini an honorary degree in Veterinary Medicine.
An art lover, Cremonini has a vast collection of paintings and contributed to the restoration of an archaeological area near the Trevi fountain in Rome.
quote: Flying low but always flying.

name: Bang Si-hyuk
about: Bang Si-hyuk is the founder and chairman of Hybe (formerly Big Hit Entertainment), one of Korea's largest music labels and entertainment agencies.
He took the company public in 2020 in what was South Korea's largest IPO in three years, which made him a billionaire.
Hybe's success is attributed to its seven-member boy band, BTS, which scored six No. 1 albums on the U.S. Billboard 200.
Bang worked as a composer for JYP Entertainment, one of Korea's "Big Three" music agencies, before venturing out on his own.
In 2021, Hybe acquired Ithaca Holdings, which manages Justin Bieber and Ariana Grande, for over $1 billion.

name: Abigail Bennett
about: Abigail Bennett's grandfather, Marvin Sands, founded a humble wine business in 1945 at age 21.
That small operation has mushroomed into a publicly-traded behemoth now called Constellation Brands, which generates nearly $10 billion in annual revenue.
The company is known for its relentless streak of acquisitions. Subsidiaries include Robert Mondavi wine and Svedka Vodka.
Constellation also holds the rights to Grupo Modelo's U.S. beer business, including its Modelo and Corona labels.
Bennett's uncles, Robert and Richard Sands, are former executives and current board members. Her brother, Zachary Stern, is also a billionaire.
The family received $1.5 billion (pre-tax) of cash to convert its enhanced voting shares to ordinary shares in 2022.

name: Xu Guozhong & family
about: Xu Guozhong chairs Jiangsu Guomao Reducer, a Chinese motor manufacturer.
Xu founded the processor of Guomao in Jiangsu Province in 1993.
Son Xu Bin, 32, is Guomao's general manager.

name: Yuriy Kosiuk
about: Yuriy Kosiuk heads MHP, Ukraine's biggest producer of poultry.
He studied food process engineering at Kiev Food Industry Institute, and got his start importing furniture and gas from Turkmenistan.
He then began trading grain after the collapse of the Soviet Union, and eventually moved into poultry in 1998 with 10 employees.
Kosiuk took MHP public in 2008; he owns about 60% of the company, which trades in London.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Kiev Food Industry Institute

did_you_know_facts: Kosiuk pays himself handsomely through dividends and has used the cash to buy airplanes, a yacht and several cars, including a Lamborghini.
quote: If you know how to play the game, you can succeed.

name: Orion Hindawi
about: Orion Hindawi cofounded cybersecurity firm Tanium with his father David in 2007; private investors valued the firm at $9 billion in June 2020.
In February 2016, Orion took over as CEO of Tanium from his father, who serves as executive chairman.
The father-son team previously worked together on BigFix, an IT software patching system that they sold to IBM for $400 million in 2010.
Orion's father David was born in Baghdad, grew up in Israel, and went to UC Berkeley to earn a Ph.D.
Orion also ended up at UC Berkeley in 1997, but dropped out before graduating to work with his father.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Drop Out, University of California, Berkeley

name: Lee Su-jin
about: Lee Su-jin is the founder and CEO of South Korean travel superapp Yanolja.
SoftBank's Vision Fund 2 invested $1.7 billion in the company in 2021.
Orphaned as a child, Lee worked as a janitor at love hotels before starting Yanolja in 2005.
did_you_know_facts: Yanolja means "Hey, let's play" in Korean.

name: Shang Xiaobo & family
about: Shang Xiaobo is a general manager and director at Anhui Honglu Steel Construction Group, a supplier of steel buildings.
Honglu is headquartered in Hefei, the capital of Anhui Province.
Honglu was founded in 2002.

name: Bart van Malderen
about: Bart van Malderen is the founder and CEO of Drylock Technologies, a maker of baby diapers, feminine hygiene products, and incontinence diapers.
Drylock Technologies produces a billion diapers per month from nine factories, and had revenue of 1.2 billion euros in 2022.
Van Malderen has spent a career in diapers and other consumer products, working for 30 years at Belgian diaper producer Ontex, the family business founded by his father in 1979.
Van Malderen sold Ontex in 2002 and left in 2007 with a non-compete agreement. He founded Drylock when the agreement ended in 2012 to sell ultra-thin, cellulose-free diapers.
He is also the biggest shareholder of German diaper webshop Lillydoo.
did_you_know_facts: Drylock Technologies launched the world's first compostable diaper in February 2024.
quote: We're in a patent business. We register hundreds of patents every year. That's the only way we can make a difference.

name: Laszlo Szijj
about: László Szíjj is the cofounder and owner of Duna Aszfalt, a leading construction company for roads and bridges in Hungary.
Szijj bought out his former Duna partner and childhood friend, Károly Varga, to become sole owner of the business in 2019.

The business, which grew rapidly beginning in the mid 2000s on government contracts, has more recently looked outside of Hungary for growth, acquiring peer companies in Romania, the Czech Republic and Poland.
Szijj is also a business partner of Lőrinc Mészáros, Hungary's richest person, and owns two yachts where he has hosted several members of the Hungarian political and economic elite.
quote: As an entrepreneur, I can say that, in my experience, the economy has never been healthier in recent decades than it is now. So, naturally, I am optimistic.

name: Zhang Tianyu
about: Zhang Tianyu chairs Fibocom Wireless, a supplier of wireless communication modules and solutions.
Fibocom Wireless went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2017.

name: Tan Eng Kee
about: Tan Eng Kee is cofounder and CEO of Malaysia-listed Greatech Technology, a maker of factory automation equipment.
He set up the company in 1997 with his school buddy, Khor Lean Heng, who's the company's COO.
Greatech's customers include EV makers, solar energy producers and semiconductor companies.
The company, which listed in 2019, has eight factories in Malaysia and a testing facility in the U.S., one of its biggest markets.
did_you_know_facts: At age 16, Tan worked part-time at a bakery after school hours to supplement his family's income.
Greatech was part of Forbes Asia's Best Under a Billion list in 2022 and 2023.
quote: I have a simple life. I come to the office, do my job and I go home.

name: Shyam Sankar
about: Palantir's chief technology officer, Sankar has worked with the company in various positions since 2006. When he joined the company, he was its 13th employee.
In June 2025, Sankar was one of four tech executives to join the U.S. Army Reserves' Executive Innovation Corps.
Sankar serves on the board of Gingko Bioworks, a biotech company working on genetically engineered bacteria.
He is also a trustee of the Hudson Institute, a right-leaning think tank based in Washington, D.C.
Sankar's wife, Pooja, worked as a software developer at Oracle, Kosmix and Facebook, before starting Piazza, a classroom discussion software.

name: Maria Frias
about: Maria Cristina Frias is a journalist who inherited a third of Brazilian media giant Folha de Sao Paulo from her father Octávio Frias in 2007.
Her brother Luiz Frias, also a billionaire, runs the conglomerate and owns the remaining bulk of the company.
The siblings' late father acquired the precursor to Folha de Sao Paulo in the 1960s, which was already one of Brazil's most popular daily newspapers.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Master of Business Administration, Universidade de Sao Paulo

name: Kostyantin Zhevago
about: Kostyantin Zhevago, a member of Ukraine's parliament from 1998 to 2019, stepped down as the firm's CEO in late 2019 amid an investigation by Ukraine's state prosecutor office.

Zhevago was wanted for allegedly embezzling and money-laundering linked to the disappearance of $113 million from Finance & Credit, his former bank that went bankrupt. With the case pending since 2015, he claims it is political persecution.
He was detained in December 2022 at the French ski resort Courchevel at Ukraine's request and then released on bail. A French court ruled against extradition to Ukraine.
A Ukraine court has also ordered the seizure of his sares in iron pellet producer Ferrexpo, which account for roughly $400 million of his of fortune. He is fighting the charges.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Kiev State Economic University

name: Susan Carol Holland
about: Susan Carol Holland is the chair of the board of Milan-based Amplifon, the world's largest retailer of hearing aids.
Amplifon was founded in 1950 by her father, British-born Algernon Charles Holland, to provide hearing care for people injured in World War II.
Her father served in the British Special Operations Executive during the war, receiving the honor of Member of the Order of the British Empire.
Amplifon developed digital hearing aids in the 1990s and entered the North American market with the acquisition of Miracle-Ear in 1999.
Algernon died in 2001, the same year Amplifon went public on the Italian Stock Exchange; Susan took over as chair in 2011.

name: Gyorgy Gattyan
about: Gyorgy Gattyan made the bulk of his fortune from porn site LiveJasmin.com. He is also a cofounder of the International Teqball Federation
He founded the political party Megoldás Mozgalom (Solution Movement) prior the 2022 Hungarian Election but failed to win any seats in Parliament.
He co-founded the Hungarian Prima Primissima Award to celebrate achievements in Hungarian Culture and supports causes related to children in need.
did_you_know_facts: He is an active movie and TV producer whose work includes the last 11 episodes of the Hungarian Cult-classic animation series, Hungarian Folk Tales.

name: Aydin Dogan
about: Aydin Dogan owns 29% of Dogan Holding, a public company active in oil distribution, electricity production, real estate, tourism and e-commerce.
He was once Turkey's biggest media boss but came into conflict with the policies of the Turkish government.
In 2018, he sold his portfolio (including TV channels Kanal D and CNN Turk, and the newspapers Hurriyet, Posta and Fanatik) for around $1.1 billion.
In 2012, he entered into a licensing deal with Donald Trump for an office tower and shopping mall project in Instanbul.
In 2019, he sold Trump Towers to publicly traded Dogan Holding for around $150 million.
did_you_know_facts: In 2009, Dogan handed over management of the Dogan companies to his four daughters.
In 2019, he brought out a book titled "Aydın Sozler" ("Enlightened Words" - a pun on his name), consisting of aphorisms from his work life.
quote: First honor, then health, then wealth.

name: Wei Lidong & family
about: Wei Lidong chairs Shanghai-headquartered Weaver Network, which provides digital collaboration and workflow software to more than 80,000 clients.
Weaver went public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2017.
In 2019, the company added a regional headquarter in Singapore to expand its footprint in the Asia-Pacific region.
Wei holds a bachelor's degree from Zhejiang University.

name: Lee Hwa-kyung
about: Lee Hwa-kyung is vice chairwoman of Orion Corp., one of the country's oldest and most popular confectionery businesses.
The company's most famous product is Choco Pie, which consists of a combination of biscuit, chocolate and marshmallow filling.
The bulk of Lee's wealth is derived from a stake in Orion Holdings, the group's listed holding company that also has interests in biopharma and entertainment.
Lee is the second daughter of Lee Yang-gu, founder of Dongyang, precursor to the group.
Her husband, Dam Chul-gon, is the chairman of Orion Corp. Her son, Dam Seo-won, serves as its vice president.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, Ewha Womans University

did_you_know_facts: In 2017, she was sentenced to eight months in prison with a two-year suspension for embezzling $356,000 through moving company-owned artworks to her home.
Dam Chul-gon was acquitted in 2016 after being charged with embezzlement in a separate case.
Lee also runs the group's entertainment business Showbox.

name: Shintaro Yamada
about: Shintaro Yamada founded the online used-goods marketplace, Mercari, in 2013 and is the company's CEO.
Yamada launched the online marketplace focusing on smartphone users. It had achieved unicorn status by 2016.
Mercari's shares have more than doubled since 2020 on an online-buying boom during the pandemic.
The company gave each employee a grant of $550 to cover the cost of working from home during the coronavirus pandemic.
did_you_know_facts: Yamada is a big fan of retired Japanese pitcher Hideo Nomo, who played Nippon Professional Baseball and Major League Baseball.
In July 2019, Mercari bought a 62% stake in Japan's top-scoring soccer team, the Kashima Antlers, for $15 million.
quote: Never be afraid of failure:Go bold.

name: Jeffrey Soffer
about: Jeffrey Soffer is one of seven children of Donald Soffer, who developed the Florida city of Aventura.
Alongside his sister Jackie, Soffer helmed the family real estate firm, Turnberry Associates, for over two decades.
In 2019, Soffer set out on his own, bringing his interests under new company Fontainebleau Development.
Soffer's real estate holdings include the historic Fontainebleau Miami Beach luxury hotel.

name: Kevin Plank
about: Under Armour founder Kevin Plank built the popular sportswear brand as the underdog competitor to Nike.
Noticing his football teammates' sweat-soaked shirts, Plank came up with a lightweight, sweat-wicking shirt using fabrics from women's undergarments.
In the mid-1990s he sold his first shirts from his grandmother's basement, exaggerating to early customers to make the company sound bigger.
Plank, who stepped down as Under Armour's CEO in 2019 but returned to the role in 2024, took the company public in 2005.

personal_stats.label: Education
personal_stats.value: Bachelor of Arts/Science, University of Maryland; Master of Business Administration, Robert H. Smith School of Business

did_you_know_facts: Plank got kicked out of his high school after an alcohol-fueled brawl with Georgetown U football players; he later walked onto the U. of Maryland's football team.
Plank served on President Trump's manufacturing council but resigned in 2017 after the president lightly criticized neo-Nazi protestors in Charlottesville, Virginia.
quote: We were always smart enough to be naive enough to not know what we could accomplish.

name: Chen Xueli
about: Chen Xueli is the chairman of Weigao Holding Company, a supplier to the healthcare industry.
Chen co-founded his first disposable infusion business in an old warehouse in China in 1988.
His main publicly listed business is Shangdong Weigao Group Medical Polymer, which trades at the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

name: Chen Qingzhou & family
about: Chen Qingzhou chairs Hytera Communications, a manufacturer of radio communications equipment.
Early in his career, Chen worked at a mobile radio communications factory as a sales manager in Fujian Province.

name: Beyoncé Knowles-Carter
about: The majority of pop star Beyoncé Knowles' net worth comes from her roughly three decades as a solo performer and a member of the girl-group Destiny's Child.
